opportunities.title: MEAL Officer
opportunities.description:
English

  1. Projects overview and context

Expertise France is the French public agency for international technical cooperation, and a subsidiary of the French Development Agency (AFD Group). It designs and implements projects that sustainably strengthen public policies in developing and emerging countries. The agency operates in key development sectors such as governance, sustainable development, security, health, and education, and works alongside its partners to help achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

In this context, Expertise France is recruiting a Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer to support two Governance EU-funded projects (50% each project) within the Country Office and may evolve to support additional projects depending on the development of Expertise France’s portfolio in Lebanon.

  1. Support to Public Administration in Lebanon (PAR) (48 months: 11/2023 – 11/2027)

The project aims to support progress in key areas of public administration reform in Lebanon through enhancing the integrity, transparency and accountability of its public administration aligned with the principles of a modern public administration. It consists of three outcomes:

  1. Safeguarding integrity of the public administration, mainly in the area of public human resources management;
  2. Enhancing transparency in public administration systems, mainly in the area of public procurement at central and local level and access to public information;
  3. Strengthening accountability of the administration by reinforcing the role of the main oversight bodies (i.e., Central Inspection Board, Court of Audits and National Anti-Corruption Commission) in implementing reform, fighting and preventing corruption.

The project beneficiaries are the Civil Service Board, the Public Procurement Authority, the Court of Accounts, the Central Inspection, the National Anti-Corruption Commission and OMSAR, with the Institute of Finances and the National School of Administration (ENA) as key stakeholders.

The project aims to strengthen the capacity of Lebanon’s oversight institutions by improving their processes, thereby enhancing the legality, transparency, and efficiency of public administration.

  1. Support anti-corruption efforts through processes' reforms and digitalisation of high-impact public services (e-Services) (starting September/October 2026, contingent upon the signature of the project.)

A new EU Action, starting in September/October 2026 (to be confirmed) (duration 36 months) will be implemented to support anti-corruption efforts through processes' reforms and digitalisation of high-impact public services.

The Action is implemented by a consortium led by Expertise France, acting as the pillar-assessed entity and the e-Governance Academy (eGA) is the consortium partner responsible for leading the trust services component.

The action is structured around four complementary outputs, each led by one of the two consortium partners with cross-contributions where the complementarity of expertise adds operational value:

  1. Output 1 (EF lead). Accessible, user-centered and integrity-enhancing digital public services developed and deployed.
  2. Output 2 (EF lead). Pilot administrations' capacities strengthened for transparent and integrity-driven service delivery.
  3. Output 3 (eGA lead). Cybersecurity frameworks, European trust services and integrity standards implemented for digital public services.
  4. Output 4 (EF lead). Lebanese GovTech ecosystem strengthened and mobilised in support of public services digitalisation, towards the long-term financial sustainability of digitalised services.

The main beneficiaries of this project is OMSITAI which has developed Lebanon’s Digital and AI Roadmap and identified a portfolio of priority e-services to be digitalised in pilot administrations.

  1. Mission Description

The Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning (MEAL) Officer is a key position supporting the implementation of the two projects, PAR and e-Services. S/He will contribute to the operationalization of the projects’ MEAL frameworks and support the effective implementation of MEAL activities across the interventions.

The MEAL Officer will support the implementation of routine monitoring and data collection activities, including field visits, stakeholders follow-up, Means of Verification (MoVs), and the collection and analysis of quantitative and qualitative data related to projects outputs and outcomes. S/He will contribute to tracking progress against project indicators, ensuring data quality and consistency, and supporting timely reporting processes, including updates required for donor reporting platforms (OPSYS) and internal EF monitoring systems.

In coordination with the Governance portfolio manager, the project teams and the Country Direction MEAL function, the MEAL Officer will support the development and adaptation of MEAL tools, methodologies, databases, and data collection instruments, while ensuring compliance with EF MEAL standards, donor guidelines, and accountability requirements. The position will also contribute to strengthening data management, documentation, archiving, and learning processes, including the use of automated systems to support efficient data analysis, visualization, knowledge management, and evidence-based decision-making throughout projects implementation.

Essential Responsibilities:

Monitoring and Evaluation

  • Develop and implement comprehensive intervention MEAL plans for assigned interventions, ensuring alignment with donor, EF, and global MEAL standards.
  • Develop the e-Services monitoring and evaluation strategy and plan during the Inception phase and revise the logical framework.
  • Draft the ToRs for the recruitment of external evaluation firms (midterm review, final evaluation and capitalisation)
  • Ensure timely and high-quality implementation of MEAL activities, including qualitative and quantitative data collection, based on the established MEL System and MEAL Calendars.
  • Ensure proper MEL documentation in accordance to EF standards, including maintaining MAEL folders, raw and analytic datasets, evidence, tools, analysis workbooks, and all related documentation.
  • Ensure a comprehensive and updated database for the projects.
  • Lead the implementation of data collection activities in close coordination with the project expert and technical team.
  • Lead the preparation of the MEAL narrative components of donor and internal reports, ensuring clear presentation of results, rigorous analysis of outputs and outcomes, proper interpretation of findings, and evidence-based reporting aligned with indicators’ results.
  • Organize and lead data collection activities especially for qualitative data, this will include the design and implementation of outcome measurement exercises to capture behavioral, organizational, and institutional changes resulting from the intervention. Particular attention will be given to stakeholder consultation and accountability mechanisms, fostering meaningful engagement, transparency, and continuous learning throughout the project cycle and across EF country portfolio.
  • Adapt and strengthen data collection tools as needed to ensure accurate measurement of EF internal and country-level indicators, and guarantee the availability of reliable data to inform evidence-based decision-making at the Country Direction level.
  • Support the implementation of internal project quarterly and annual reviews in line with Expertise France MEAL guidelines, ensuring the use, adaptation, and updating of relevant EF tools and templates to facilitate structured reflection and indicators assessment.
  • Maintain a chronological record of progress against targets, and contributing to the design and structuring of the two projects database to guarantee data accuracy, traceability, and availability for donor reporting and audit purposes.
  • Rolling out and put in place the monitoring and evaluation MEAL tools, software licenses, communication methods, collection and analysis using KOBO, ODK, dashboard, etc).
  • Support the preparation and submission of regular reporting for EUD platform OPSYS.

Accountability and Learning

  • For the relevant project(s), develop tools and methodologies to implement the accountability and learning components of the MEAL Plan, including stakeholder feedback, consultation, and recommendations tracking mechanisms.
  • Lead the implementation of Key Informant Interviews (KIIs), Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), and stakeholder consultation sessions, and ensure proper analysis and reporting of the findings.
  • Follow up on the recommendations and action plans resulting from accountability and learning activities to support their effective implementation.
  • Ensure proper planning and follow-up of the projects’ capitalization and learning exercises to support knowledge management and adaptive implementation.

Cross-Cutting Activities

  • Ensure effective coordination with project teams, partners, and external stakeholders to support effective MEAL implementation.
  • Participate in the MEAL workshops, seminars and capacity building activities organized at HQ and country direction level.
  • Support EF communication and visibility efforts by adapting and organizing relevant data within MEAL tools and systems.
  • Ensure the availability of accurate data for communication materials, dashboards, visualizations, events, and Steering Committee meetings

The position is primarily dedicated to the above-mentioned projects; however, the successful candidate may be assigned responsibilities or provide support to other projects managed by Expertise France, according to operational needs.

  1. Required Profile

  2. Education

  • Graduate degree in social` sciences, international cooperation, project management, applied statistics, development economics, or any other relevant field. Advanced certificate in MEAL is preferred.
  • Experience in designing, implementing, and operating project MEAL systems from project initiation to closeout stages
  • At least 5 years’ professional experience in monitoring, information management, data collection and/or evaluation for international projects/donors/organizations, development projects, preferably in the field of humanitarian/social development/education or refugees, aid to displaced persons;
  • Good command of data collection software (Kobo Tool Box, Survey CTO, ODK, etc.), data analysis and visualization software (PowerBI), and good knowledge of more comprehensive monitoring software;
  • Experience in database design and management;
  • Experience in designing, facilitating and evaluating training for adults in the field of MEAL will be considered favorably;
  • Excellent understanding of results frameworks and indicators as well as international MEAL standards and applications, particularly on projects funded by EU and AFD;
  • Experience managing consultants and external service providers would be an asset.
  • Good command of project management tools and practices (theory of change, logical framework, programming, reporting, etc.) and knowledge of donor practices.
  • Proven experience in monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning for governance, public administration, and institutional reform projects,
  • Fluency in English and Arabic, ability to work in French will be an asset.

  1. Interpersonal and Soft Skills

  • Strong organizational skills, accuracy, and attention to detail.
  • Availability, flexibility, and autonomy.
  • Proactive, with a strong sense of initiative and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with a wide range of stakeholders, including public authorities, security institutions, and high-level counterparts.
  • Ability to work under pressure in a multicultural environment.

  1. Practical Information

  2. Application Documents

  • Resume
  • Cover letter
  • Contract details of 3 relevant professional references

  1. Additional Information

  • Location: Beirut, Lebanon
  • Preferred start date: As soon as possible
  • Contract Type: Full time
  • Salary: Based on profile and according to the salary scale of Expertise France

The selection process will consist of two phases:

  • In the first phase, a shortlist of candidates will be created at the discretion of Expertise France.
  • In the second phase, shortlisted candidates may be invited for a technical test followed by an interview.

If you do not receive a response within 5 weeks, please consider that your application has not been successful. Interested candidates are encouraged to submit their applications as soon as possible, as Expertise France reserves the right to conduct the preselection before the application deadline.

French

  1. Aperçu des projets et contexte

Expertise France est l’agence publique française de coopération technique internationale, filiale de l’Agence Française de Développement (Groupe AFD). Elle conçoit et met en œuvre des projets qui renforcent durablement les politiques publiques dans les pays en développement et émergents. L’agence intervient dans des secteurs clés du développement tels que la gouvernance, le développement durable, la sécurité, la santé et l’éducation, et œuvre aux côtés de ses partenaires pour contribuer à l’atteinte des Objectifs de Développement Durable (ODD).

Dans ce contexte, Expertise France recrute un(e) Chargé(e) de Suivi, Évaluation, Redevabilité et Apprentissage (SERA) pour appuyer deux projets Gouvernance financés par l’UE (50 % pour chaque projet) au sein du bureau Liban de la Direction Pays Jordanie-Liban, avec une possible évolution vers l’appui à des projets supplémentaires selon le développement du portefeuille d’Expertise France au Liban.

  1. Appui à la Réforme de l’Administration Publique au Liban (RAP) (48 mois : 11/2023 – 11/2027)

Le projet vise à soutenir les progrès dans des domaines clés de la réforme de l’administration publique au Liban, en renforçant l’intégrité, la transparence et la redevabilité de son administration publique, conformément aux principes d’une administration publique moderne. Il comprend trois effets :

  1. Préserver l’intégrité de l’administration publique, principalement dans le domaine de la gestion des ressources humaines publiques ;
  2. Renforcer la transparence des systèmes de l’administration publique, principalement dans le domaine de la commande publique aux niveaux central et local ainsi que l’accès à l’information publique ;
  3. Renforcer la redevabilité de l’administration en consolidant le rôle des principaux organes de contrôle (à savoir l’Inspection Centrale, la Cour des Comptes et la Commission Nationale Anti-Corruption) dans la mise en œuvre de la réforme, la lutte contre la corruption et sa prévention.

Les bénéficiaires du projet sont le Conseil de la Fonction Publique, l’Autorité de la Commande Publique, la Cour des Comptes, l’Inspection Centrale, la Commission Nationale Anti-Corruption et l’OMSAR, avec l’Institut des Finances et l’École Nationale d’Administration (ENA) comme parties prenantes clés.

Le projet vise à renforcer la capacité des institutions de contrôle du Liban en améliorant leurs processus, renforçant ainsi la légalité, la transparence et l’efficacité de l’administration publique.

  1. Soutien aux efforts de lutte contre la corruption à travers la réforme des processus et la digitalisation de services publics à fort impact (e-Services) (démarrage septembre/octobre 2026, sous réserve de la signature du projet)

Un nouveau projet d’une durée de 36 mois, débutant en septembre/octobre 2026 (à confirmer), sera mise en œuvre pour soutenir les efforts de lutte contre la corruption à travers la réforme des processus et la digitalisation de services publics à fort impact.

Le projet est mis en œuvre par un consortium mené par Expertise France, agissant en tant qu’entité accréditée par l’UE, l’e-Governance Academy (eGA - Estonie) étant le partenaire du consortium chargé de la composante services de confiance.

L’action s’articule autour de quatre produits complémentaires, chacun piloté par l’un des deux partenaires du consortium, avec des contributions croisées lorsque la complémentarité des expertises apporte une valeur opérationnelle :

  1. Produit 1 (piloté par EF). Des services publics numériques accessibles, centrés sur l’usager et renforçant l’intégrité sont développés et déployés.
  2. Produit 2 (piloté par EF). Les capacités des administrations pilotes sont renforcées pour une prestation de services transparente et fondée sur l’intégrité.
  3. Produit 3 (piloté par l’eGA). Des cadres de cybersécurité, des services de confiance européens et des normes d’intégrité sont mis en œuvre pour les services publics numériques.
  4. Produit 4 (piloté par EF). L’écosystème GovTech libanais est renforcé et mobilisé à l’appui de la digitalisation des services publics, en vue de la pérennité financière à long terme des services digitalisés.

Le principal bénéficiaire de ce projet est l’OMSITAI, qui a élaboré la feuille de route numérique et IA du Liban et identifié un portefeuille de services numériques prioritaires à digitaliser au sein d’administrations pilotes.

  1. Description de la mission

Le/la Chargé(e) de Suivi, Évaluation, Redevabilité et Apprentissage (SERA) occupera un poste clé dans l’appui à la mise en œuvre des deux projets, RAP et e-Services. Il/elle contribuera à l’opérationnalisation des cadres SERA des projets et à la mise en œuvre effective des activités SERA dans l’ensemble des interventions.

Le/la Chargé(e) SERA appuiera la mise en œuvre des activités courantes de suivi et de collecte de données, notamment les visites de terrain, le suivi des parties prenantes, les Moyens de Vérification (MoV), ainsi que la collecte et l’analyse de données quantitatives et qualitatives relatives aux produits et effets des projets. Il/elle contribuera au suivi de l’avancement par rapport aux indicateurs des projets, veillera à la qualité et à la cohérence des données, et appuiera les processus de reporting dans les délais, y compris les mises à jour requises pour les plateformes de reporting des bailleurs (OPSYS) et les systèmes internes de suivi d’EF.

En coordination avec le/la Responsable de Portefeuille Gouvernance, les équipes projets et la Coordinatrice SERA de la Direction Pays Jordanie-Liban, le/la Chargé(e) SERA appuiera le développement et l’adaptation des outils, méthodologies, bases de données et instruments de collecte de données SERA, tout en assurant la conformité aux normes SERA d’EF, aux directives des bailleurs et aux exigences de redevabilité. Le poste contribuera également au renforcement de la gestion des données, de la documentation, de l’archivage et des processus d’apprentissage, y compris l’utilisation de systèmes automatisés pour appuyer une analyse et une visualisation efficaces des données, la gestion des connaissances et la prise de décision fondée sur des données probantes tout au long de la mise en œuvre des projets.

Responsabilités essentielles :

Suivi et évaluation

  • Élaborer et mettre en œuvre des plans SERA complets pour les interventions assignées, en assurant leur cohérence avec les normes SERA des bailleurs, d’EF et les normes internationales.
  • Élaborer la stratégie et le plan de suivi-évaluation du projet e-Services pendant la phase de démarrage et réviser le cadre logique.
  • Rédiger les termes de référence pour le recrutement des cabinets d’évaluation externes (revue à mi-parcours, évaluation finale et capitalisation)
  • Assurer la mise en œuvre en temps utile et de haute qualité des activités SERA, y compris la collecte de données qualitatives et quantitatives, sur la base du Système SERA et des calendriers SERA établis.
  • Assurer une documentation SERA adéquate conformément aux normes d’EF, notamment le maintien des dossiers SERA, des jeux de données brutes et analytiques, des preuves, outils, classeurs d’analyse et de toute documentation connexe.
  • Assurer une base de données complète et à jour pour les projets.
  • Piloter la mise en œuvre des activités de collecte de données en coordination étroite avec l’expert projet et l’équipe technique.
  • Piloter la préparation des composantes narratives SERA des rapports aux bailleurs et des rapports internes, en assurant une présentation claire des résultats, une analyse rigoureuse des produits et effets, une interprétation appropriée des constats, et un reporting fondé sur des données probantes aligné avec les résultats des indicateurs.
  • Organiser et piloter les activités de collecte de données, en particulier pour les données qualitatives, notamment la conception et la mise en œuvre d’exercices de mesure des effets visant à saisir les changements comportementaux, organisationnels et institutionnels résultant de l’intervention. Une attention particulière sera accordée à la consultation des parties prenantes et aux mécanismes de redevabilité, favorisant un engagement significatif, la transparence et un apprentissage continu tout au long du cycle du projet et à l’échelle du portefeuille pays d’EF.
  • Adapter et renforcer les outils de collecte de données selon les besoins afin d’assurer une mesure précise des indicateurs internes d’EF et des indicateurs pays, et garantir la disponibilité de données fiables pour éclairer la prise de décision fondée sur des données probantes au niveau de la Direction Pays.
  • Appuyer la mise en œuvre des revues internes trimestrielles et annuelles des projets conformément aux lignes directrices SERA d’Expertise France, en veillant à l’utilisation, l’adaptation et la mise à jour des outils et modèles EF pertinents pour faciliter une réflexion structurée et l’évaluation des indicateurs.
  • Tenir un registre chronologique de l’avancement par rapport aux cibles, et contribuer à la conception et à la structuration de la base de données des deux projets afin de garantir l’exactitude, la traçabilité et la disponibilité des données à des fins de reporting aux bailleurs et d’audit.
  • Déployer et mettre en place les outils SERA, les licences logicielles et les méthodes de communication, de collecte et d’analyse (KOBO, ODK, tableaux de bord, etc.).

Redevabilité et apprentissage

  • Appuyer la préparation et la soumission du reporting régulier pour la plateforme OPSYS de l’UE.
  • Pour le(s) projet(s) concerné(s), élaborer des outils et méthodologies pour mettre en œuvre les composantes redevabilité et apprentissage du plan SERA, y compris les mécanismes de retour d’information, de consultation et de suivi des recommandations des parties prenantes.
  • Piloter la conduite d’entretiens avec des informateurs clés (KII), de groupes de discussion (FGD) et de sessions de consultation des parties prenantes, et assurer une analyse et un reporting appropriés des constats.
  • Assurer le suivi des recommandations et plans d’action issus des activités de redevabilité et d’apprentissage afin d’appuyer leur mise en œuvre effective.
  • Assurer une planification et un suivi appropriés des exercices de capitalisation et d’apprentissage des projets afin d’appuyer la gestion des connaissances et une mise en œuvre adaptative.

Activités transversales

  • Assurer une coordination efficace avec les équipes projets, les partenaires et les parties prenantes externes afin d’appuyer une mise en œuvre efficace du SERA.
  • Participer aux ateliers, séminaires et activités de renforcement des capacités SERA organisés au siège et au niveau de la Direction Pays.
  • Appuyer les efforts de communication et de visibilité d’EF en adaptant et en organisant les données pertinentes au sein des outils et systèmes SERA.
  • Assurer la disponibilité de données précises pour les supports de communication, les tableaux de bord, les visualisations, les événements et les réunions du Comité de Pilotage.

Le poste est principalement dédié aux projets susmentionnés ; toutefois, le/la candidat(e) retenu(e) pourra se voir confier des responsabilités ou apporter un appui à d’autres projets gérés par Expertise France, selon les besoins opérationnels.

  1. Profil recherché

  2. Formation

  • Diplôme d’études supérieures en sciences sociales, coopération internationale, gestion de projet, statistiques appliquées, économie du développement, ou tout autre domaine pertinent. Un certificat de formation avancée en SERA est un atout.
  • Expérience dans la conception, la mise en œuvre et le pilotage de systèmes SERA de projet, de leur lancement à leur clôture
  • Au moins 5 ans d’expérience professionnelle en suivi, gestion de l’information, collecte de données et/ou évaluation pour des projets/bailleurs/organisations internationaux, de préférence dans le domaine humanitaire, du développement social, de l’éducation ou des réfugiés et de l’aide aux personnes déplacées ;
  • Bonne maîtrise des logiciels de collecte de données (Kobo Tool Box, Survey CTO, ODK, etc.), des logiciels d’analyse et de visualisation de données (PowerBI), et bonne connaissance de logiciels de suivi plus complets ;
  • Expérience en conception et gestion de bases de données ;
  • Une expérience dans la conception, l’animation et l’évaluation de formations pour adultes dans le domaine du SERA sera considérée comme un atout ;
  • Excellente compréhension des cadres de résultats et des indicateurs, ainsi que des normes et applications internationales du SERA, en particulier sur les projets financés par l’UE et l’AFD ;
  • Une expérience en gestion de consultants et de prestataires de services externes serait un atout.
  • Bonne maîtrise des outils et pratiques de gestion de projet (théorie du changement, cadre logique, programmation, reporting, etc.) et connaissance des pratiques des bailleurs.
  • Expérience avérée en suivi, évaluation, redevabilité et apprentissage pour des projets de gouvernance, d’administration publique et de réforme institutionnelle,
  • La préférence est donnée aux candidats trilingues (arabe, anglais et français).

  • Solides compétences organisationnelles, rigueur et souci du détail.
  • Disponibilité, flexibilité et autonomie.
  • Esprit proactif, fort sens de l’initiative et capacités de résolution de problèmes.
  • Capacité à communiquer efficacement, à l’oral comme à l’écrit, avec un large éventail de parties prenantes, y compris des autorités publiques, des institutions sécuritaires et des interlocuteurs de haut niveau.
  • Capacité à travailler sous pression dans un environnement multiculturel.

opportunities.title: Regional MEAL Officer — Middle East
opportunities.description:
HAMAP-Humanitaire https://hamap-humanitaire.org

Halte aux Mines AntiPersonnel (HAMAP)-Humanitaire is a French NGO, established in 1999 in order to contribute to the struggle against mines and the risks it presents to civilian population. HAMAP-Humanitaire is active in 13 countries and pursues a mission of support to local partners from the need assessment, through project conception and to its sustainable implementation. HAMAP-Humanitaire diversified its field of activity, to encompass two sectors: Engineering (WASH, construction, energy) and Mine Action.

Requirements and job status

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field
Minimum experience: 4 years with a Bachelor’s degree, or 2 years with a Master’s degree
Required travel: Yes
No of jobs: 1
Published date: 28 July 2026
Deadline date: 10 Aug 2026
Start date: ASAP
Job Description PDF - HAMAP Humanitaire LinkedIn page

Description

HAMAP-Humanitaire is seeking a Regional Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer to strengthen the quality, coherence, use and accountability of programme evidence across its Humanitarian Mine Action portfolio in Lebanon, Syria and Iraq.

Based in Beirut, the position will work across country programmes, projects and grants implemented directly byvHAMAP and, in line with HAMAP’s localisation approach, through local and national partners. The role combines hands-on project monitoring with regional system-building: it will help teams and partners produce reliable data, understand performance, meet reporting requirements, and use evidence to improve programme decisions.

A central purpose of the position is to create a consolidated view of HAMAP’s Middle East portfolio. The Regional MEAL Officer will develop practical tools that connect project-level information to country and regional analysis, including common indicator matrices, reporting calendars, dashboards, data-quality controls, grant and partner tracking, and structured review processes. These systems must make it possible to identify progress, gaps, overlaps, inconsistencies, emerging risks and learning across several grants without creating unnecessary parallel reporting burdens.

The position is intended for either a strong national candidate or a junior international candidate with solid MEAL fundamentals and the ability to grow into the specific information-management requirements of HMA. Mine action information-management experience is highly desirable, but the role remains primarily a programme-quality and partner-support function rather than a technical operations position.

Hierarchical and organizational links:
Reports to: Regional Coordinator for Middle East;
Coordinates with: Country and Project Coordinators, Regional HMA Technical Advisor, Regional Support Manager, HQ programme-quality and technical focal points, and local partner programme, MEAL and information-management staff.
Direct reports: None initially. The position may provide functional supervision to enumerators, consultants or temporary data-collection personnel when required.

Main responsibilities

  1. Regional MEAL systems and portfolio oversight
  • Develop and maintain a proportionate regional MEAL framework and workplan covering Lebanon, Syria and Iraq, aligned with country strategies, project commitments, organisational priorities and partner capacities.
  • Establish and maintain a consolidated portfolio-monitoring system linking projects’ MINE-MEAL tools, grants, partners, locations, activities, indicators, targets, results, reporting deadlines and supporting evidence.
  • Build practical dashboards and portfolio-review products that provide management with a clear macro view of progress, delivery trends, geographic and population coverage, grant performance, implementation bottlenecks and emerging risks.
  • Maintain a master indicator matrix and indicator reference sheets, harmonising definitions, calculations, disaggregation and evidence requirements wherever possible while preserving donor-specific and national requirements.
  • Identify and resolve inconsistencies between project tools and reports, including duplicate counting, incompatible indicator definitions, missing disaggregation, unsupported results and divergence between narrative and quantitative reporting.
  • Facilitate regular project, country and regional performance reviews and maintain an action tracker so that findings lead to documented management decisions and follow-up.

2. Project and grant monitoring, reporting and data quality

  • Support Country and Project Coordinators to develop and update theories of change, logical frameworks, monitoring plans, indicator performance tracking tables, data-flow maps, data-collection plans, reporting calendars and MEAL budgets.
  • Review routine project and partner submissions for completeness, internal consistency, plausibility, required disaggregation and traceability to source documentation before consolidation into HAMAP and donor reporting.
  • Liaise closely with the Regional HMA Technical Advisor and relevant Project Coordinators on partner reporting. The Regional MEAL Officer will verify data structure, evidence, calculations and reporting consistency, while technical validation of HMA methodologies and operational outputs remains with the appropriate technical function.
  • Plan and conduct proportionate data-quality assessments, monitoring visits, remote verifications and evidence-file reviews, and support teams and partners to implement corrective actions.
  • Develop and maintain auditable project evidence systems, including clear filing conventions, source-document registers, version control, validation status and links between reported results and supporting documentation.
  • Support the design and implementation of baselines, endlines, KAP studies, post-activity monitoring, training assessments, outcome monitoring and other internal or external data-collection exercises.
  • Promote timely reporting and early escalation of data limitations, underperformance, access constraints or methodological weaknesses rather than retrospective correction at donor-reporting stage.

3. Local partner support and localisation

  • Assess MEAL and information-management capacities jointly with local partners, recognising existing systems and priorities rather than assuming that HAMAP tools should automatically replace them.
  • Co-develop practical, time-bound capacity-strengthening plans for partner MEAL, reporting, data management, accountability and learning, with clear responsibilities and indicators of institutional progress.
  • Provide coaching, on-the-job accompaniment and training to partner programme, operations, MEAL and information-management staff on indicators, data collection, analysis, evidence management, reporting and learning.
  • Help partners adapt donor and HAMAP requirements into manageable internal workflows, with clear roles from field data collection through validation, analysis, approval and submission.
  • Support partner ownership of analysis and reporting by involving partner teams in data-review meetings, interpretation of findings, preparation of reports, presentation of results and definition of corrective measures.
  • Avoid unnecessary parallel systems and promote interoperability between partner databases, HAMAP portfolio tools, donor reporting formats and national mine-action information requirements where relevant.
  • Document the evolution of partner MEAL capacity and identify where additional organisational, technical or resourcing support is needed for sustainable localisation.

4. HMA information management and analytical products

  • Support coherent data architecture for HAMAP-supported HMA activities, including land release, survey, clearance, EORE/CPP, training, capacity strengthening and related community-level outcomes, while respecting national standards and authority reporting arrangements.
  • Work with technical colleagues and partners to ensure that data-collection forms, databases, maps, dashboards, task or activity records and narrative reports use consistent definitions and can be reconciled.
  • Develop or improve digital data-collection and reporting tools using appropriate platforms such as KoboToolbox, ODK, Survey123, Excel or comparable systems, taking account of connectivity, language, user capacity and data-protection constraints.
  • Apply routine data-cleaning, deduplication, validation, geospatial and logical checks, and maintain controlled datasets with clear ownership, backup and access arrangements.
  • Produce maps, dashboards, analytical briefs and visualisations that support operational planning, programme management, donor communication and strategic decision-making.
  • Support IMSMA-compatible or national-authority-compatible reporting where applicable, in coordination with the Regional HMA Technical Advisor and designated country or partner information-management focal points.
  • Strengthen staff and partner ability to interpret HMA data, not only enter it, including analysis of reach, relevance, efficiency, quality, outcome trends and gaps in coverage.

5. Accountability, participation and responsible data

  • Support country teams and partners to establish or strengthen accessible, safe and context-appropriate community feedback and complaints mechanisms, with clear referral, response, confidentiality and closure procedures.
  • Ensure that community feedback and monitoring findings are periodically analysed, discussed with programme teams and used to adjust implementation.
  • Promote meaningful participation of affected people and partner organisations in assessment design, monitoring, interpretation of findings and learning processes.
  • Apply appropriate sex, age, disability, displacement and other context-relevant disaggregation, and promote conflict-sensitive, inclusive and do-no-harm approaches to data collection and use.
  • Ensure compliance with HAMAP requirements on informed consent, confidentiality, safeguarding, data minimisation, and controlled sharing of personal or sensitive information.

6. Evaluation, learning and capitalisation

  • Develop an annual regional learning agenda linked to programme priorities, recurring implementation challenges, partner capacity development and strategic questions across Lebanon, Syria and Iraq.
  • Plan and facilitate after-action reviews, pause-and-reflect sessions, project reviews and structured lessons-learned workshops with HAMAP and partner staff.
  • Maintain a regional lessons and recommendations register, with assigned actions, deadlines and follow-up on whether learning has been incorporated into tools, procedures, project design or management decisions.
  • Coordinate internal reviews and support external evaluations, including preparation of terms of reference, data and documentation, stakeholder engagement, quality review of deliverables and management responses.
  • Produce concise learning notes, case studies and cross-country syntheses that capture both results and implementation experience, including what did not work and why.
  • Organise accessible knowledge repositories so that tools, evaluations, lessons, methods and evidence can be retrieved and reused across projects and by local partners.

7. Programme design, standardisation and organisational contribution

  • Contribute to needs assessments, context analyses, concept notes and proposals by strengthening theories of change, results frameworks, indicators, targets, monitoring methods, evaluation questions and MEAL budgets.
  • Develop and periodically update common regional templates, guidance notes, checklists and minimum standards for monitoring, reporting, data quality, accountability, learning and information management.
  • Promote standardisation where it improves comparability, quality and efficiency, while allowing justified adaptation to national standards, donor requirements, operational realities and partner systems.
  • Provide induction and refresher training to HAMAP and partner staff on the regional MEAL framework and relevant tools.
  • Contribute evidence and analysis to strategy development, donor engagement, coordination forums and organisational reporting when delegated by management.
  • Remain informed of relevant developments in humanitarian MEAL, localisation, responsible data and HMA information management, and translate useful practices into realistic improvements for HAMAP programmes.

Role boundaries and accountability

The Regional MEAL Officer is a support, assurance and systems-strengthening function. The role is expected to challenge weak evidence and facilitate corrective action, while preserving clear ownership by programme management, technical staff and local partners.

Unless specifically delegated and authorised, the Regional MEAL Officer shall not:

  • replace Country or Project Coordinators’ responsibility for implementation, grant management and final reporting;
  • independently certify the technical validity or completion of HMA operational outputs; such validation remains with the competent technical staff, partner management and national authorities as applicable;
  • impose new tools or parallel reporting systems without assessing their added value, sustainability and impact on partner workload;
  • alter partner or project data without a documented validation and correction process;
  • share personal, sensitive or restricted operational information outside approved data-protection and information-sharing procedures;
  • make formal donor, contractual, policy or budget commitments on behalf of HAMAP outside delegated authority.

Required competencies and qualifications

Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in monitoring and evaluation, statistics, economics, social sciences, development studies, public policy, information management, data science, GIS or another relevant field. A relevant Master’s degree is desirable.
  • At least four years of relevant professional experience with a Bachelor’s degree, or two years with a relevant Master’s degree, in MEAL, monitoring and evaluation, information management, programme quality or a closely related function.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and using logical frameworks, indicator reference sheets, monitoring plans, data-collection tools, databases, dashboards and reporting systems.
  • Experience supporting humanitarian or development programmes funded through multiple grants and reporting cycles.
  • Experience working with local or national partner organisations through accompaniment, capacity assessment, coaching and jointly owned systems development.
  • Experience conducting data-quality reviews, field monitoring, assessments, quantitative and qualitative analysis, learning exercises or evaluations.
  • Experience in a multi-country, regional or geographically dispersed role is desirable.
  • Professional experience in humanitarian mine action is highly desirable but not mandatory.
  • Experience with HMA information management, IMSMA-compatible reporting, GIS, spatial data, KoboToolbox/ODK, Survey123, Power BI or comparable platforms is highly desirable.
  • Familiarity with IMAS/NMAS, land-release and EORE/CPP data structures, national mine-action authority reporting, or comparable regulated operational data systems is an advantage.
  • Experience in Lebanon, Syria, Iraq or comparable Middle Eastern humanitarian contexts is an advantage.
  • Experience contributing to donor proposals and reports for institutional donors is desirable.

Required Skills

  • Advanced command of Microsoft Excel, including structured datasets, formulas, pivot tables, validation controls and clear analytical outputs.
  • Strong quantitative and qualitative analytical skills, with the ability to move between detailed data verification and portfolio-level interpretation.
  • Ability to design proportionate systems that are useful to programme teams and partners, not only compliant on paper.
  • Ability to translate donor, organisational and technical requirements into clear tools, workflows, roles and deadlines.
  • Strong facilitation, coaching and training skills, including the ability to support colleagues with different levels of MEAL and digital literacy.
  • Strong written communication and reporting skills, with the ability to present complex evidence in concise narrative, tabular, visual and dashboard formats.
  • Sound understanding of accountability to affected populations, participation, safeguarding, data protection and responsible data management.
  • Strong organisational skills and ability to manage several projects, grants, reporting calendars and follow-up processes simultaneously.
  • Diplomacy and constructive challenge: ability to identify weaknesses clearly while maintaining trust with partner and internal teams.
  • Ability to work independently, travel regularly, and provide effective remote support in access-constrained environments.

Languages

  • English: fluent written and spoken, mandatory.
  • Arabic: working proficiency strongly preferred.
  • French: working level desirable.

Personal Profile

HAMAP is looking for a practical and collaborative MEAL professional who combines methodological rigour with a strong service orientation. The successful candidate should be comfortable building systems from imperfect starting points, working through partners, and improving quality without creating excessive bureaucracy.

The position requires a systems-builder who is equally willing to examine source data, facilitate a partner workshop, challenge an indicator definition, prepare a management dashboard and help a project team turn findings into decisions. The candidate must be able to balance regional standardisation with country realities and respect partner ownership throughout the process.

The successful candidate will contribute to a Middle East portfolio that is more evidence-based, accountable, comparable across grants and progressively more sustainable through stronger local MEAL and information-management capacity.

Rules of conduct

While working for HAMAP-Humanitaire, completing entrusted tasks, or presenting themselves as working for the NGO, the employee is expected to:

  • Report systematically to their line manager on activities and seek approval before undertaking material unplanned activities.
  • Act in accordance with HAMAP-Humanitaire values and maintain respectful, non-discriminatory relations with all stakeholders.
  • Respect local customs, applicable laws, organisational policies, safeguarding requirements and professional standards.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality regarding HAMAP-Humanitaire documents, projects, future opportunities, partners, stakeholders, providers and sensitive programme data unless authorised otherwise.
  • Avoid any use of the position, organisational information or resources for personal purposes or benefit.

Conditions

  • The position may be recruited under a national or international contract, depending on the selected candidate’s profile, eligibility and agreed status.
  • The position is budgeted at a total monthly employer cost of EUR 2,900, inclusive of salary, applicable employer taxes or social contributions and any recurring per diem or expatriation component. The corresponding gross and net remuneration will depend on contract status and applicable taxation.
  • For an international candidate, accommodation in Beirut and approved international travel costs are covered separately from the above monthly employment budget, in accordance with HAMAP policy.
  • Costs of approved duty travel within the region are covered by HAMAP in accordance with applicable procedures.
  • Insurance, leave, R&R and other benefits are provided according to the applicable national or international contract and HAMAP policy.

We would like to draw your attention to the fact that this offer is intended exclusively for you. Hamap does not provide any services, compensation, support arrangements, or coverage for family members in connection with your expatriation assignment with Hamap.

Consequently, Hamap cannot be held liable for any incident, accident, or harm suffered by a member of your family in your country of assignment.

opportunities.title: Programme Advisor, Africa
opportunities.description:
Finn Church Aid (FCA) is seeking a Programme Advisor to lead the planning, implementation, and monitoring of projects at the Network for Religious and Traditional Peacemakers (NRTP) in Africa, including the Horn of Africa Traditional and Faith-Oriented Insider Mediators (TFIM) Platform. In addition, the Programme Advisor will be responsible for leading the planning, implementation, and monitoring of the global iDove project.

The position is contracted from our head office in Helsinki, Finland, and requires regular travel, including occasional periods of work in the programme countries.

Remote working may also be possible from Nairobi, Kampala, Addis Ababa, or another mutually agreed location, subject to operational and legal requirements.

This is not an expatriate position. The successful candidate will be employed under the applicable employment framework depending on their location. For candidates working remotely from outside Finland, employment arrangements may be facilitated through an Employer of Record (EOR), where required, in accordance with local legal requirements.

Key tasks and responsibilities

  • Plan and implement NRTP Africa regional strategy and annual plan, projects, and programmes in Africa inclusive of all stages of the programme cycle.
  • Plan and implement the MFA PBS project activities for Africa (HoA TFIM Platform) region including donor coordination, M&E, and reporting.
  • Lead the planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting of the iDove global project, including donor and partnership engagement and coordination.
  • Facilitate engagement of NRTP members, partners, and supporters in the Africa region, including regular sharing of information through newsletters and organizing quarterly online meetings.
  • Support NRTP fundraising through proposal development, donor engagement, and development of new partnerships.
  • Provide advisory and thematic expertise and support on peacebuilding and peace mediation for FCA country offices and other relevant stakeholders where needed.
  • Support global NRTP activities such as the annual Advisory Group Meeting (AGM), UN engagement, donor reporting, etc.

Skills and Experience

  • A relevant postgraduate university degree in fields such as peace and conflict studies, international relations, development studies, human rights, or another related area.
  • At least five years of relevant professional experience in the peacebuilding and/or development sector.
  • Strong thematic expertise in peacebuilding and conflict transformation.
  • Regional expertise and experience of working with/in countries of Sub-Saharan Africa, especially Horn of Africa/East Africa, Mozambique, Central African Republic and Sahel region.
  • Experience in programme and project planning, monitoring and evaluation (M&E), and reporting.
  • Experience in developing funding proposals, preparing budgets, and financial reporting.
  • Excellent analytical thinking and professional writing skills.
  • Fluency in written and spoken English. Working knowledge of French, Kiswahili, and/or Arabic is considered an asset.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with experience working in multicultural environments.
  • Excellent organisational skills and the ability to proactively manage and coordinate work.

The position will be filled as soon as possible, with the successful candidate expected to start no later than September. This is a fixed-term position until 31 December 2027 and includes a six-month probationary period. The compensation is based on the FCA salary scale and the candidate’s level of experience. The salary range at the beginning for this position is 3288,05 - 3663,83€ depending on experience.

For more information about the position, please contact to Senior Advisor, Africa Region and Global Partnerships Gina.Dias@kua.fi

Please apply using the link no later than 2nd August 2026. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

Finn Church Aid (FCA) is Finland’s largest development co-operation organisation and the second biggest organisation in Finland working in humanitarian aid. FCA is a founding member of the international aid alliance of churches, ACT Alliance. We seek positive change by supporting the most vulnerable people in fragile contexts. We specialize in supporting local communities’ right to peace, livelihoods and quality education. Qualified and interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, race, religion or ethnic affiliation are encouraged to apply for the vacancy.

FCA has zero tolerance concerning aid diversion and illegal actions and may screen applicants against international lists to ensure due diligence and compliance with Anti-money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism requirements.

FCA has a Safeguarding policy and zero tolerance against child abuse and sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEAH), and participates in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures. FCA is certified against the Core Humanitarian Standard on Quality and Accountability (CHS).

opportunities.title: Partnership Finance Manager
opportunities.description:
TITLE: Partnership Finance Manager
TEAM/PROGRAMME: Finance LOCATION: Syria
GRADE: National 2
CHILD SAFEGUARDING:
Level 3: the post holder will have contact with children and/or young people either frequently (e.g. once a week or more) or intensively (e.g. four days in one month or more or overnight) because they work country programs; or are visiting country programs; or because they are responsible for implementing the police checking/vetting process staff.

ROLE PURPOSE:
The Partnerships Finance Manager will be supporting setting and developing the partnership financial management of Syria Country Office. The position is primarily responsible for providing oversight and day-to-day financial management of the SCI Partnerships Department’s, review of partner budgets at the proposal stage, participate in pre-award due diligence processes, financial report review, providing guidance and training to partners in order to strengthen their capacity.
SCOPE OF ROLE:

Reports to: Head of Treasury and Financial Compliance

Staff reporting to this post:
• Partnership Finance Coordinator

Budget Responsibilities: None

KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:

Partnership Development and Management

• Act as the key strategic Finance Business Partner to the Head of Treasury and Program Implementation team to support the growing response in terms of partnership and build the capacity of the team.
• Undertaking capacity assessment of partners’ organisation in order to identify capacity gaps and areas of support that the partners will require for effective implementation of the programme financial management requirements. The finance folk for the localisation strategy and its implementation.
• Undertake regular support visits to the partners organizations to discuss financial and operational issues/progress and identify ways in which SCI can provide the needed support.
• Support the development of partners’ project budgets, work plan, cash transfer plans and procurement plans.
• Support partners external audit exercise and follow up to ensure that the auditors’ recommendations are followed up and implemented.
• Monitor and follow up the implementation of the agreed work plan and budget to ensure that the programme objectives are being realized in accordance to the programme and partnership agreement and take the necessary actions for any identified deviations.
• Ensuring best in class financial management at field office level – including leadership in respect to recruitment and succession planning; capacity building; implementing efficient & effective processes and accounting systems; improving and ensuring compliance with internal controls.

• Staff Leadership, Mentorship, and Development

• Ensure appropriate staffing and efficient & effective organisation design within the Budgeting & Reporting teams.
• Ensure that staff understand and are empowered to perform their role especially the budgeting and reporting team.
• Manage team; define expectations, provide leadership and technical support as needed, and evaluate direct reports regularly.
• Recruitment, training, and professional development of team as part of the wider staff development strategy.
• Performance Management :

- Effective use of the Performance Management System including the establishment of clear, measurable objectives; ongoing feedback; periodic reviews; and fair and unbiased evaluations.
-Coaching, mentoring and other developmental opportunities.
-Recognition and rewards for outstanding performance.
-Documentation of performance that is less than satisfactory, with appropriate performance improvements/ work plans

BEHAVIOURS (Values in Practice)
Accountability:
• Holds self-accountable for making decisions, managing resources efficiently, achieving and role modelling Save the Children values.
• Holds the team and partners accountable to deliver on their responsibilities - giving them the freedom to deliver in the best way they see fit, providing the necessary development to improve performance and applying appropriate consequences when results are not achieved.
Ambition:
• Sets ambitious and challenging goals for themselves and their team, takes responsibility for their own personal development and encourages their team to do the same.
• Widely shares their personal vision for Save the Children, engages and motivates others.
• Future orientated, thinks strategically and on a global scale.
Collaboration:
• Builds and maintains effective relationships, with their team, colleagues, Members and external partners and supporters.
• Values diversity, sees it as a source of competitive strength.
• Approachable, good listener, easy to talk to.

Creativity:
• Develops and encourages new and innovative solutions.
• Willing to take disciplined risks.

Integrity:
• Honest, encourages openness and transparency; demonstrates highest levels of integrity.
QUALIFICATIONS

• BA Degree in Finance and Accounting, Business Administration, or other relevant discipline.
• Chartered Accountant (CPA, ACMA, ACA, and ACCA) strongly recommended.

EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS
Essential
• Minimum of 5 years management experience in a corporate or an NGO environment, of which three at a management level within a finance department
• Strategic mindset with the ability to lead, inspire and achieve results in a challenging context
• Strong team player
• Excellent inter-personal skills and able to communicate with diverse set of stakeholders
• Strong analytical, decision making and strategic planning skills with the ability articulate complex information in an easy to understand manner
• Solutions focused with ability to identify weaknesses and drive continuous improvement
• Ability to prioritise, plan ahead, and manage a complex and diverse workload with tight deadlines
• Ability to coach, mentor, delegate appropriately and provide developmental guidance to supervised staff.
• Self starter who is willing to go the extra mile to get the job done
• Excellent understanding of business and financial planning including strategic modelling.
• Excellent understanding of budgeting and budget management.
• Excellent understanding of financial systems and procedures.
• Excellent understanding of computerised accounts packages, Excel, PowerPoint and Word
• A full appreciation of the value of co-operation, both internationally and within a team environment.
• Understanding of Save the Children’s vision and mission and a commitment to its objectives and values.
• Written and verbal fluency in English

Desirable
• 4 years within the NGO / charities sector
• Experience of working in an emergency context.
• Understanding of major donor compliance regulations.
Additional job responsibilities
The duties and responsibilities as set out above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to carry out additional duties within reasonableness of their level of skills and experience.
Equal Opportunities
The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with the SCI Equal Opportunities and Diversity policies and procedures.
Child Safeguarding:
We need to keep children safe so our selection process, which includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the protection of children from abuse.
Health and Safety
The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with SCI Health and Safety policies and procedures.

opportunities.title: Regional Grant Compliance Advisor (Open for Nationals only)
opportunities.description:
WHO WE ARE

Diakonia is an international rights-based and faith-based development organization recognized for its commitment to democracy, human rights, and gender justice with the objective to change unfair structures that generate poverty, inequality, oppression and violence. All work is based on feminist principles. Digitalization plays a key role in enabling efficient, transparent, and secure operations across global contexts.

OUR VALUES AND COMMITMENT TO SAFEGUARDING

Diakonia is committed to promoting equality, diversity, and inclusion in the workplace, and strives to be representative of all sections of society. We know that different perspectives, experiences, and competences are key for Diakonia to be a relevant, capable, and successful organization. Diakonia therefore strives to recruit staff with diverse backgrounds and lived experiences.

Diakonia is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behaviour at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and financial misconduct; and committed to promoting the welfare of children, young people, adults and beneficiaries with whom Diakonia engage.

Diakonia expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We place a high priority on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation. All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. Diakonia also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

PURPOSE OF THE POSITION

As a Regional Grant Compliance Advisor, you are responsible for supporting the financial and administrative capacity of partner organisations across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, ensuring they meet compliance standards and sustain their operations.

You will ensure compliance with Diakonia’s policies, procedures, donor requirements, and grant agreements throughout the grant cycle, from inception to closure. The role contributes to strengthening partner accountability, financial management systems, and organisational sustainability.

You are part of the MENA Gender Justice Programme and work closely with the Regional Program Director, Programme Managers, Finance Manager, Global Operational Support and Finance Teams, as well as with partners, donors, and relevant networks.

This position reports to the Regional Program Director (direct supervisor).

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Support PD in partner capacity development and compliance:

  • Support the Regional Programme Director in Partner Capacity Development and Compliance
  • Support partner organisational assessments and collaborate with partners to develop and implement capacity development plans.
  • Follow up on partner financial and administrative systems to ensure compliance.
  • Ensure partners are well informed about Diakonia’s financial policies, procedures, compliance standards, and grant requirements.
  • Provide technical support to partners on work plans, budgets, financial reporting, procurement procedures, audits, and grant management.
  • Facilitate and monitor grant disbursements to partners and follow up on grant utilisation and reporting requirements.
  • Conduct partner financial monitoring, including field visits, virtual meetings, compliance reviews, and follow-up actions.
  • Review and assess partner budgets, financial reports, audit reports, and management responses.
  • Support partners in addressing audit findings and strengthening internal control systems.
  • Promote learning and exchange of good practices among partners in financial management and compliance.

Support PD in managing donor compliance:

  • Support the Regional Programme Director in Managing Donor Compliance
  • Support programme staff in meeting donor financial and compliance requirements.
  • Ensure compliance with donor agreements, reporting obligations, grant conditions, and relevant policies.
  • Monitor compliance risks across the regional portfolio and recommend mitigation measures.
  • Support the preparation and review of donor financial reports and grant-related documentation.
  • Maintain compliance tracking systems and reporting calendars to ensure timely submissions.
  • Contribute to donor audits, compliance reviews, and due diligence processes

Support PD in managing program finance at the country office/programme entity:

  • Support the Regional Programme Director in Financial Oversight of the Regional Programme
  • Support budgeting, financial planning, financial follow-up, and grant monitoring across the regional programme portfolio.
  • Provide technical input to annual planning and budgeting processes.
  • Review programme and partner budgets and provide recommendations to strengthen financial planning and resource allocation.
  • Support financial analysis and monitoring of grants and programme expenditures.
  • Contribute to the preparation of consolidated programme budgets and financial forecasts.
  • Support resource mobilisation efforts through budget development and financial review of funding proposals.
  • Ensure that financial management practices are aligned with Diakonia policies and donor requirements.
  • Support coordination of internal and external audits in collaboration with the Finance Manager and relevant global teams.
  • Advise programme staff on financial, compliance, grant management, and risk-related matters.

Support PD in managing administrative and HR compliance matters:

  • Support with technical HR matters
  • Ensure that payroll is correctly administered
  • Ensure that labour law is considered in all staff matters.
  • Ensure that all insurance matters are adequately handled
  • Oversee computer maintenance and security

Technical Leadership and Regional Support:

  • Provide mentoring, coaching, and technical guidance to junior Grant Compliance Advisors and relevant colleagues across the region.
  • Support country offices with financial bookings, reconciliations, and other finance-related processes in relevant systems, as requested.

Support PDin Risk Management and Accountability:**
