opportunities.title: Enterprise Finance & Credit Manager (National Position)
opportunities.description:
Near East Foundation

Position Title: Enterprise Finance & Credit Manager
Location: Damascus, Syria
Reports To: Country Director
Type: Full-time.

About Near East Foundation

Since 1915, Near East Foundation (NEF) has worked across the Middle East, Africa, and the Caucasus to expand economic opportunity, strengthen resilience, and support recovery in underserved and crisis-affected markets. Working through local teams, country offices, and partners, NEF combines deep field presence with practical, broad network of long-term partners, scalable approaches that support enterprise growth, livelihoods, and locally led development.

For candidates coming from enterprise finance or investment backgrounds, NEF offers the opportunity to apply structuring, partnership, and financing skills in markets where well-designed capital can have outsized impact and where innovative models can influence how enterprise finance works in some of the world’s most challenging and dynamic environments.

Position Description:

The Credit Manager is responsible for leading credit operations and portfolio management across the organization’s enterprise financing programs in Syria. The role combines strategic and operational oversight of credit risk, fund liquidity, product performance, donor compliance, and cross-departmental coordination. The Credit Manager ensures the sustainability and impact of credit operations in line with organizational goals.

Key Responsibilities and Duties:

A. Fund & Portfolio Management

Financial Oversight & Risk Management

  • Track and analyze key portfolio performance indicators: repayment rates, portfolio at risk (PAR), default/write-off rates, client retention, and yield.
  • Ensure appropriate provisioning for loan losses and advise on risk diversification to mitigate over-concentration.

Fund Liquidity & Revolving Fund Health

  • Oversee cash flow modeling to ensure balanced disbursements and collections.
  • Maintain adequate liquidity buffers to support timely disbursements and financial obligations.

Portfolio Strategy & Optimization

  • Advise on portfolio composition, including sectoral and geographical diversification, and risk mitigation mechanisms.
  • Monitor trends and detect early warning signs (e.g., spikes in delinquency) to recommend responsive actions.

Portfolio Reporting

  • Develop and deliver periodic performance dashboards and analysis for internal leadership and external stakeholders.

B. Credit Operations & Loan Management

  • Oversee end-to-end credit operations across Syria, including loan origination, disbursement, repayment monitoring, restructuring, and compliance.
  • Review and approve loan applications in accordance with organizational policy and regulatory standards.
  • Identify gaps and enhance operational procedures to improve efficiency and reduce risk.
  • Coordinate with Finance for cash flow planning and financial reporting alignment.
  • Design and implement tailored loan envelopes aligned with program needs and donor expectations.

C. Enterprise Financing Services[3]

Product Oversight

  • Lead product design and periodic review to ensure relevance, impact, and risk alignment.
  • Work closely with program and finance teams to align loan products with programmatic goals and funding requirements.

D. Stakeholder Engagement & Strategic Partnerships

  • Strategic Partnerships & External Engagement
  • Establish and maintain strong working relationships with relevant governmental financial institutions, regulatory authorities, microfinance institutions (MFIs), banks, financial service providers, business support organizations, local implementing partners, and other key actors within Syria's financial ecosystem.
  • Represent NEF in technical coordination forums and financial sector working groups, identify partnership opportunities, facilitate referrals and co-financing arrangements where appropriate, and strengthen collaboration to expand access to sustainable enterprise finance.

E. Lending Management System (LMS) Oversight

  • Monitor and troubleshoot system issues, ensuring resolution in collaboration with technical teams.
  • Test and implement new system features to enhance credit workflow efficiency.
  • Manage user access, roles, and permissions to safeguard data integrity.

F. Capacity Building & Interdepartmental Coordination[4]

  • Provide ongoing training to credit teams on policy compliance, risk mitigation, and system use.
  • Develop manuals and training materials to support operational consistency.
  • Collaborate with MEAL, Program, and Finance teams to ensure alignment in planning, monitoring, and delivery.
  • Use MEAL insights to inform credit strategies and improve client outcomes.
  • Lead the capacity strengthening of local financial partners and implementing organizations through structured mentoring, coaching, and Training of Trainers approaches.
  • Develop practical guidance, standard operating procedures, and technical learning plans to enhance institutional capacity in credit management, risk assessment, portfolio management, and enterprise finance, ensuring long-term sustainability and localization of financial services.

G. Donor Reporting & Policy Compliance

  • Prepare and contribute to credit-related sections in donor reports and funding proposals.
  • Ensure credit activities meet donor guidelines and reporting standards.
  • Maintain strong relationships with donors and respond to compliance-related inquiries.

3. Qualifications & Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in finance, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field (Master’s preferred).
  • At least 7 years of progressive experience in credit management, loan operations, or financial services.
  • Proven leadership in managing credit teams and operations in complex settings.
  • Proficiency in financial analysis and Loan Management Systems.
  • Strong analytical, decision-making, and communication skills.
  • Experience in donor-funded programs and familiarity with Middle East contexts (especially Syria and Jordan) is an asset.

opportunities.title: Finance Tools Specialist
opportunities.description:
MSF Ubuntu is looking for a Finance Tools Specialist

Do your skills and experience not precisely match the requirements? At MSF EA, we strive to create a safe, diverse and inclusive workplace, recognizing the need to increase access to professional opportunities for historically underrepresented groups. If you're interested in this position but your experience doesn't align perfectly with the selection criteria, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the ideal candidate for this or other positions.

Firmly committed to safeguarding patients, community members, staff, and all those in contact with the organization from all forms of abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), we will take all necessary steps, through rigorous vetting processes, to ensure that confirmed perpetrators of abuse do not join the organization.

For this position, contact level with patients and children is categorized as Low risk and will be monitored with this in regard.

Introduction

Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) is an international independent medical humanitarian organisation that provides assistance to people affected by conflicts, epidemics, and natural or human-made disasters and excluded from healthcare. We provide this assistance without discrimination, irrespective of race, religion, creed or political affiliation.

About MSF Ubuntu

MSF Ubuntu is the newest Operational Directorate of Médecins Sans Frontières, grounded in the philosophy of Ubuntu – “I am because we are”. With a strong emphasis on interdependence, interoperability, and locally grounded action, MSF Ubuntu aims to strengthen medical humanitarian response by placing communities at the centre of decision-making.

Rationale/Objective for Position

The Finance Tools Support Officer is responsible for the administration, optimization, deployment, support, and continuous improvement of UniField, WeFin, and other finance tools across MSF Ubuntu. The role combines finance expertise, ERP systems knowledge, business process design, and user enablement to ensure finance systems effectively support operational and strategic objectives.

The position acts as a key liaison between Finance, HR, Supply, IT, and Country Program teams, translating business requirements into effective system configurations, standardized processes, practical solutions, and sustainable ways of working. The role also leads user training, capacity building, documentation, and adoption of finance systems across the organization.

This position will be hierarchically and functionally accountable to the Regional Head of Operational Finance and will closely collaborate with the HR, IT, Country Finance Coordinators, and Country Accounting Managers.

Tasks & Responsibilities

Finance System administration and governance

  • Acts as the finance functional focal point for UniField, WeFin, and related finance tools.
  • Maintains system configurations, master data, user access, and finance-related settings.
  • Monitors system performance, data quality, and compliance with MSF standards.
  • Represents MSF Ubuntu in relevant UniField and WeFin platforms and coordinates enhancement requests, testing, and issue resolution.
  • Provides recommendations on the effective use and optimization of finance systems.

Functional Support & Solution Design

  • Provides functional support to users and troubleshoot systems and process-related issues.
  • Analyzes root causes and coordinates resolution with IT, system referents, and external support teams.
  • Gathers business requirements and translates them into practical system solutions.
  • Supports user acceptance testing, system releases, upgrades, and new functionality implementation.
  • Ensures effective integration and data flows between finance tools and related systems.

Process improvement and Workflow management

  • Maps, documents, and improves finance processes and workflows across MSF Ubuntu.
  • Develops standardized and scalable ways of working supported by finance systems.
  • Ensures alignment between business processes, policies, controls, and system configurations.
  • Identifies opportunities for process optimization, automation, and harmonization across Country Programs.
  • Supports change management and adoption of new processes and system functionalities.

Deployment, training and capacity building

  • Supports the deployment, rollout, and expansion of finance tools within Country Programs.
  • Designs and delivers face-to-face, virtual, and on-the-job training for finance system users.
  • Coaches and support key users to strengthen local ownership and expertise.
  • Assesses training needs and develop learning plans to improve user competency.
  • Promotes knowledge sharing and best practices across MSF Ubuntu.

Documentation and Knowledge management

  • Develops and maintains procedures, guidelines, training materials, and user documentation.
  • Ensures documentation remains current, practical, accessible, and aligned with system and process changes.
  • Contributes to the development of knowledge resources and e-learning materials.
  • Maintains accurate records of deployments, training activities, and key system changes.

Coordination & Reporting

  • Collaborates closely with Finance, HR, Supply, IT, Country Programs, and intersection platform stakeholders.
  • Provides regular reporting and recommendations to the Head of Finance Operations.
  • Prepares deployment, training, and support reports and follow up on agreed action plans

Qualifications

Education

  • A degree in Finance, Accounting, Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related field.

Experience

  • Minimum 5 years of experience working with finance ERP systems in a support, administration, implementation, or optimization role.
  • Experience with international NGOs or complex multi-country organizations. Experience with MSF is an asset.
  • Proven experience in functional support of ERP systems and finance applications. Experience with UniField and/or WeFin is a strong asset.
  • Experience in business process analysis, workflow design, and process improvement.
  • Experience delivering training, coaching, and capacity-building initiatives.

Competencies

  • Technical competencies
    • Strong knowledge of finance ERP systems, configuration, master data management, and user support.
    • Solid understanding of system integrations, data flows, and interfaces between Finance, HR, Supply, and related systems.
    • Knowledge of system implementation lifecycles, UAT, release management, and post-go-live support.
    • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
    • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and good knowledge of Word, PowerPoint, and Power BI.
    • Ability to translate complex systems and finance concepts into clear, user-friendly guidance and solutions.
  • Behavioral/Core Competencies
    • Ability to work collaboratively in a multicultural environment.
    • Capacity to work independently with limited supervision.
    • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
    • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
    • Strong organizational and planning skills.
    • Flexibility, adaptability, and willingness to travel to field locations.

Languages

  • Working proficiency in English is mandatory (incl. delivering training / webinar in English).
  • Knowledge of French is a strong asset.
  • Additional languages are an advantage.

Conditions and Benefits:

  • The role requires regular travel to countries of operation and MSF Ubuntu hubs.
  • Travel at short notice may be required during emergencies, assessments or critical incidents.
  • The post-holder may be required to work extended or irregular hours during crises.
  • The role requires high levels of discretion, resilience, political judgement and emotional intelligence.
  • The position will operate in a growing Operational Directorate and will require adaptability as MSF Ubuntu’s structures, systems and portfolio evolve.
  • Job Location: The position will be based in either MSF Eastern Africa office in Nairobi (Kenya), or Johannesburg (South Africa).
  • Contract: 2-year renewable, full-time contract.
  • Start date: As Soon As Possible.

If based in Nairobi, the benefits below shall apply:

  • Salary: An annual salary of EUR 27,145 at HQ Grade 8 based on a full-time appointment with an annual increment of 2% every year up to a maximum of 10 years.
  • Work-life balance financial benefit:; ranging between EUR 620 to 1,159/month based on individual & administrative status. This amount may be used to cover accommodation and utilities, transportation, etc.
  • Other benefits include;
    • Annual Leave: 25 days of annual leave per year.
    • Other Holidays: sick leave, circumstantial leave, maternity leave (21 weeks), paternity leave (4 weeks), own affairs days off, etc.
    • Employer Pension contribution: 10% of basic salary:
    • International insurance for both medical and disability**.**
    • Relocation support; based on MSF EA terms/conditions.
    • Work-life balance: Daily flexi-hours and 2 days working from home possible.
    • School fees benefits: for eligible dependents, based on individual & administrative status.
    • Diverse team composition:; Collaborate with a global network of talented professionals, bringing diverse perspectives and expertise from around the world.
    • Career Development: MSF provides many learning resources (online learning resources, regular trainings – including language, Peer to peer learning.
    • Mobility: You will have opportunities to travel abroad for work, meetings, trainings and workshops; giving you a chance to experience different cultures and broaden your professional network.
    • Annual home leave ticket: To be taken once every year for both staff and eligible dependents back to their home country for vacation. Only applicable to non-Kenyans and based on individual & administrative status.
  • If based in Johannesburg, the salary and benefits will be In line with MSF reward policy, Subjected to local conditions.

opportunities.title: Technical Consultant for ASER studies - Data Management
opportunities.description:
Duty Station: remote work within Asia Time Zone, occasional field travel to Myanmar

Line Manager: Head of Programmes for Myanmar

Start Date: ASAP

Completion of work: 30 April 2027

Part-time position: 0.7 FTE

People in Need

People in Need (PIN) was established in 1992 by a group of Czech war correspondents who were no longer satisfied with merely reporting on humanitarian crises and began providing direct assistance to affected populations. Since then, PIN has evolved into an international humanitarian and development organization working in more than 20 countries to support vulnerable communities, promote human rights, and strengthen resilience in contexts affected by conflict, disasters, and poverty.

About the Myanmar Programme at People in Need

PIN has been operating in Myanmar since 1997, with an established country office since 2008. The organization delivers multisectoral humanitarian and development programming with a particular focus on Education in Emergencies (EiE), Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), Shelter, Livelihoods, DRR, local governance and Protection mainstreaming in hard-to-reach and conflict-affected areas. PIN’s approach to working with local civil society organizations is grounded in mutual trust, partnership development, capacity strengthening, and localization.

Background

Myanmar has one of the biggest education crisis. Years of conflict, covid, displacement, economic instability, and natural disasters have disrupted children's access to safe and quality education. Since 2021, the situation has deterioated with school closures, population displacement, fragmentation of education systems, and increasing learning losses. Across the country, millions of children are now accessing education through diverse modalities, including ethnic education systems, community-based schools, temporary learning spaces, monastic schools, and other alternative education arrangements.
In this context, reliable evidence on children's learning outcomes is critical to inform programming, strengthen accountability, and support evidence-based decision-making. During 2025–2026, PIN successfully conducted a nationwide literacy and numeracy assessment across Myanmar, measuring learning outcomes among students attending a wide range of learning spaces supported by Plan International Myanmar (PIM), Save the Children International (SCI), UNESCO, and UNICEF. The assessment generated important evidence on foundational learning outcomes across diverse education systems and contexts, contributing to a stronger understanding of learning achievement and disparities among crisis-affected children.

In this new consultancy we plan to expand the areas of assessment and adjust tools for different ethnic minorities. Building on this experience, the Education Programme seeks to conduct a sample learning assessment using the Annual Status of Education Report (ASER) methodology to generate new comparable evidence on new areas in literacy, numeracy, and social-emotional learning outcomes among children supported by partner education providers.

Position Summary

The objective of the consultancy is to provide technical leadership and advisory support for the design, implementation, analysis, visualization, and reporting of sample-based learning assessments using ASER tools across multiple education programmes and partners in Myanmar.

The consultant will ensure methodological rigor, statistical validity, comparability of assessment results, high-quality data management, and production of evidence that supports programme learning, accountability, adaptive management, and donor reporting.

The consultant will work closely with the Education Programme, MEAL teams and staff in the country including MEC focal points/implementing partners, and relevant stakeholders throughout all phases of the assessment process.

The consultant will lead on the following process:

  • Design the proportional sample.
  • Review and contextualize ASER literacy, numeracy, and Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) assessment tools together with EiE expert.
  • Ensure comparability of learning outcomes across timelines, partners, educational modalities, and geographic areas.
  • Strengthen the capacity of programme staff and partners on learning assessment methodologies, sampling procedures, data quality assurance, and interpretation of findings.
  • The person should have practical knowledge of digital platforms used for data collection and management, such as Kobotoolbox (that was used during ASER), or ActivityInfo
  • Lead the teams that will be doing data collection, data management, statistical analysis
  • Be the main lead in Data analysis.
  • Develop analytical products and dashboards (utilizing powerBI) for different types of audiences
  • Support the team and lead decision making in MEAL aspects

Logistics

  • The project team will provide logistical support for:
  • Coordination with partners and stakeholders
  • Organization of workshops and meetings
  • The consultant will be responsible for producing deliverables and reports according to the agreed workplan.

Methodology

The consultant will apply a participatory and technically rigorous approach combining technical advisory support, capacity building, and coordination with project teams and partners.

During the inception phase, the consultant will agree with the project team on a detailed workplan and priorities for technical support. The consultant will contribute to the design and implementation of hazard and stakeholder assessments, supporting the development of tools, guiding data collection, and assisting in the analysis and validation of findings.

The consultant will also deliver technical training and mentoring for staff and partners on MEAL aspects.

Finally, the consultant will support the technical implementation of all the stages of this project.

Duties & Responsibilities

Research Design and Assessment Methodology

  • Review previous ASER reports, partner education systems, baseline assessments, and existing learning assessment approaches together with EiE technical lead.
  • Develop an inception report detailing the methodology, sampling strategy, analytical framework, and quality assurance mechanisms in the MEAL sections and write individual reports from partners (11 reports in total togheter with the education in Emergencies lead).
  • Design an analytical framework aligned with programme indicators and donor reporting requirements.
  • Define key variables, indicators, and disaggregation categories for analysis.
  • Establish baseline-endline comparability methodologies and document associated limitations.
  • Participate In meetings with donor.

Sampling Design and Statistical Methodology

  • Design representative sampling for aprox 25 villages of different townships in Myanmar
  • Conduct sample size calculations and different scenarios based on the agreed parameters with donor
  • Develop sampling procedures considering accessibility constraints and organize MEAL implementing team to conduct field work (e.i: training enumerators)
  • Ensure representativeness across gender, age, displacement status, disability, language groups, educational modality, and geographic location, and or any other parameters discussed with donor.
  • Document all methodological assumptions, limitations, and deviations.

Assessment Tool Review and Contextualization

  • Review and adapt ASER literacy, numeracy, and SEL assessment tools to partner curricula, languages, and local contexts togheter with EiE advisor
  • Develop new/adjusted questionnaires for students, teachers, schools, and learning centres.
  • Conduct variable mapping and compatibility reviews between baseline and endline instruments where applicable.
  • Pilot assessment tools and revise instruments based on findings.
  • Develop assessment protocols and administration guidelines.

Capacity Building and Training

  • Support implementing team in producing evidence of the trainings and manuals.
  • Deliver Training of Trainers (ToT) sessions for partner organizations.
  • Support enumerator training on assessment administration, child-friendly approaches, safeguarding, informed consent, and quality assurance.
  • Provide ongoing mentoring and technical support throughout implementation to all the MEAL staff

Ethical Review and Safeguarding Compliance

  • Develop ethical review documentation regarding data, including study protocols, consent procedures, safeguarding measures, confidentiality procedures, and risk mitigation plans.
  • Lead and support the ethical review and approval process.
  • Ensure compliance with child safeguarding, Do No Harm, and data protection requirements (GDPR compliance) throughout implementation.

Data Collection Oversight and Quality Assurance

  • Support partners focal and enumerators/ PIN team during assessment implementation.
  • Establish quality control mechanisms.
  • Define protocols for non-response, inaccessible locations, and replacement sampling.
  • Monitor adherence to approved methodologies and ethical standards.
  • Document implementation challenges and corrective actions.

Data Management

  • Consolidate datasets from multiple sources.
  • Clean, validate, and harmonize data from different collection rounds
  • Develop protocols on data management documentation. Use activity info
  • Ensure secure storage and management of assessment datasets.
  • Establish procedures for version control and data traceability.
  • Make sure partners have their activity info accounts set up under PIN account

Statistical Analysis and Interpretation

  • Conduct descriptive and inferential statistical analyses as per request of EiE advisor
  • Analyse literacy, numeracy, and SEL outcomes using ASER proficiency scales.
  • Assess minimum proficiency achievement rates and programme outcome indicators.
  • Conduct disaggregated analyses by gender, age, disability, displacement status, language group, educational modality, and geography.
  • Explore relationships between learner characteristics, teacher characteristics, and learning outcomes.
  • Apply appropriate statistical techniques including non-parametric tests, correlation analysis, regression models, and subgroup analyses.

Data Visualization and Reporting

  • Develop analytical dashboards and interactive reporting products using Power BI.
  • Build data models linking learner, teacher, school, programme, and geographic data.
  • Create visualizations of learning outcomes, subgroup comparisons, programme performance, and geographic coverage.
  • Develop baseline-endline comparison dashboards where applicable.
  • Produce user-friendly outputs suitable for both technical and non-technical audiences.

Reporting

  • Prepare technical assessment reports and methodological annexes.
  • Produce reports and summary briefs.
  • Develop presentations and facilitate validation workshops.
  • Document lessons learned and recommendations for future assessments.
  • Support dissemination and use of findings for programme improvement and strategic decision-making.

Organizational Learning

  • Assess the applicability of methodologies across different education systems and contexts in other missions of PIN
  • Document transferable tools, templates, code, and analytical frameworks.
  • Produce recommendations to strengthen future learning assessment exercises within humanitarian and conflict-affected education programmes.
  • The consultant will participate in regular coordination meetings with the Education Programme lead, MEAL team, and implementing focal points/schools.
  • The consultant will provide technical recommendations throughout implementation and support the documentation of lessons learned, methodological challenges, and best practices.
  • The consultant will report directly to the Head of Programmes and will work with rthe Education Programme focal point and team in the country programme of Myanmar as well as work closely with relevant technical teams throughout the assignment.

Expected Deliverables

  • Inception Report (Due: 15 July 2026)
    • Approved assessment methodology
    • Approved implementation plan
  • Contextualized and Piloted ASER Tools (Due: July–August 2026)
    • Adapted and piloted ASER tools for:
      • Literacy
      • Numeracy
      • Social and Emotional Learning (SEL)
      • School assessment
      • Teacher assessment
      • Student assessment
  • Ethical Review Protocol and Approval Package (Due: August 2026)
    • Ethical review package completed
    • Ethical clearance obtained
  • Partner-Specific Sampling and Implementation Plans (Due: August 2026)
    • Sampling framework developed
    • Partner-specific implementation plans finalized
  • ToT Training, Enumerator Capacity Building and Assessment Protocols (Due: August–September 2026)
    • Training package developed
    • Assessment protocols finalized
    • Enumerators trained and deployed
  • Completed Surveys and Validated Dataset (Due: October–December 2026)
    • Survey data collected
    • Dataset cleaned, validated, and anonymized
    • Final assessment dataset prepared
  • Final ASER Assessment Reports and Presentations (Due: January–February 2027)
    • Comprehensive assessment report
    • Partner-specific reports
    • Presentation materials
    • Recommendations for future actions and improvements

A suitable candidate:

Should have:

  • University degree (Master's or PhD) in Statistics, Demography, Educational Measurement, Education, Economics, Social Sciences, Public Policy, Monitoring and Evaluation, or another relevant field.
  • At least 4 of professional experience in Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL), assessment, research, or quantitative analysis within humanitarian, development, or international NGO (INGO) settings.
  • Minimum 2 years of demonstrated experience designing and implementing sample-based quantitative surveys and statistically representative sampling methodologies.
  • Proved expertise in quantitative research methods, including survey design, sampling theory, statistical analysis, and interpretation of complex datasets.
  • Strong practical experience with digital data collection platforms, particularly KoboToolbox; experience with ActivityInfo is highly desirable.
  • Advanced proficiency in Power BI for dashboard development, data visualization, and interactive reporting.
  • Proficiency in statistical software such as R, Stata, SPSS, or Python for quantitative data analysis.
  • Excellent analytical, and organizational skills
  • Excellent written and spoken English

Preferred to have:

  • Experience leading large-scale learning assessments, preferably using ASER, EGRA, EGMA, MICS, PISA, or similar education assessment methodologies.
  • Based in Asia time zone
  • Proven experience conducting descriptive and inferential statistical analyses, including regression models, correlation analyses
  • Experience measuring skills in capacity-building programmes, including Training of Trainers (ToT).
  • Experience working in Education in Emergencies (EiE) sector or education systems, including government, community-based, ethnic, or alternative education systems.
  • Knowledge of Myanmar or other local languages would be an advantage.

We offer:

  • Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organization in a challenging context;
  • Salary: total contract amount: 2100 Eur/month for part-time (30hrs/week)
  • Equipment: Laptop provided for both professional and personal use;
  • When traveling abroad:
    • Reimbursement of travel expenses such as flights, visas and vaccinations; assistance with the visa application procedure;
    • Travel health insurance covering medical care, incl. the repatriation;
    • 24/7 Medical Support available online;
    • Free psychological consultations available online;
  • Professional Development:
    • Free access to e-learning platforms and PIN Learning Hub; PIN’s global Induction Training, and tailored capacity-building opportunities.

Welcome to this IUCN tender. You are invited to submit a proposal. Please read the information and instructions carefully, as failure to comply with the instructions may result in your proposal being disqualified from this tender.

1. REQUIREMENTS
1.1. A detailed description of the services and/or goods to be provided can be found in Annex 1.

2. CONTACT DETAILS
2.1. During the course of this procurement, i.e. from the publication of this RfP to the award of a contract, you may not discuss this procurement with any IUCN employee or representative other than the following contact. You must address all correspondence and questions to the contact, including your Proposal.
IUCN contact: TendersMozWaterProject@iucn.org

3. PROCUREMENT PROCESS TIMELINE
3.1. This timetable is indicative and may be changed by IUCN at any time. If IUCN decides that changes to any of the deadlines are necessary, we will publish this on our website and contact you directly if you have indicated your interest in this procurement (see Section 3.2).

July 09, 2026-Publication of the Request for Proposals
July 15, 2026-Deadline for expressions of interest

3.2. Please email the IUCN contact to express your interest in submitting a Proposal by the deadline stated above. This will help IUCN to keep you updated regarding the procurement.

4. COMPLETING AND SUBMITTING A PROPOSAL
4.1 Your Proposal must consist of the following four separate documents:
 Signed Declaration of Undertaking (see Attachment 2)
 Pre-Qualification Information (see Section 4.3 below)
 Technical Proposal (see Section 4.4 below)
 Financial Proposal (see Section 4.5 below)
Proposals must be prepared in English.

4.1. Your Proposal must be submitted by email to the IUCN Contact (see Section 2).
The subject heading of the email shall be [RfP Reference – bidder name]. The bidder name is the name of the company/organisation on whose behalf you are submitting the Proposal, or your own surname if you are bidding as a self employed consultant. Your
Proposal must be submitted in PDF format. You may submit multiple emails suitably annotated, e.g. Email 1 of 3, if attached files are too large to suit a single email transmission. You may not submit your Proposal by uploading it to a file-sharing tool.
IMPORTANT: Submitted documents must be password-protected so that they cannot be opened and read before the submission deadline. Please use the same password for all submitted documents. After the deadline has passed and within 12 hours, please send the password to the IUCN Contact. This will ensure a secure bid submission and opening process. Please DO NOT email the password before the deadline for Proposal submission.

4.2. Pre-Qualification Criteria
IUCN will use the following Pre-Qualification Criteria to determine whether you have the capacity to provide the required goods and/or services to IUCN. Please provide the necessary information in a single, separate document.
Pre-qualification criteria
1. 3 relevant references for similar work issued by reputable entities to whom you have provided similar services
2. All legal registrations required to carry out the work in the Republic of Mozambique
3. Please state your annual turnover for each of the last 3 years
4. How many employees does your organisation have who are qualified for this work?
5. Please confirm that your organisation holds the following qualifications (e.g. ISO certification)
6 Please confirm that your organisation meets the following donor eligibility criteria (e.g. the EC nationality rule)?
7. Please confirm that your organisation has formal policies and/or procedures in place for the following (e.g. procurement, health and safety, code of conduct, sustainability, accounting)?
4.3. Technical Proposal
The Technical Proposal must address each of the criteria stated below explicitly and separately, quoting the relevant criteria reference number (left-hand column).
Proposals in any other format will significantly increase the time it takes to evaluate, and such Proposals may therefore be rejected at IUCN’s discretion.

Where CVs are requested, these must be of the individuals who will actually carry out the work specified. The individuals you put forward may only be substituted with IUCN’s approval.

IUCN will evaluate Technical Proposals with regards to each of the following criteria and their relative importance:
No.-Description-Information to be provided-Relative weight
1. Approach and methods-30%
Information to be provided:
Clear understanding of the tasks and the quality of the solutions in meeting the terms of reference (15 points).
Well-defined and consistent technical approach and methodology to meet the requirements ofthe tasks, including innovative and practical
ideas and efficient solutions (15 points).

2. Work plan-10%
Information to be provided:
Detailed and in line with the ToR — all key activities indicated in the timetable (5 points).
Detailed and realistic plan and timetable to complete the activities on time (5 points).

4. Organisation and staff-10%

Correct allocation of time for essential and nonessential staff (5 points).
10%

Team leader

Engineering/Hydraulic Engineering (2 points).

the goods/services stated in the RfP in their entirety.

4.5.2. Prices include all costs

IUCN will not accept charges beyond those clearly stated in the Financial Proposal. This includes applicable withholding taxes and similar. It is your responsibility to determine whether such taxes apply to your organisation and to include them in your Financial Proposal.

4.5.3. Applicable Goods and Services Taxes
Proposal rates and prices shall be exclusive of Value Added Tax.

4.5.4. Currency of proposed rates and prices
All rates and prices submitted by Proposers shall be in USD.

4.5.5 Breakdown of rates and prices

Price

4.6. Additional information not requested by IUCN should not be included in your Proposal and will not be considered in the evaluation.

4.7. Your Proposal must remain valid and capable of acceptance by IUCN for a period of 90 calendar days following the submission deadline.
4.8. Withdrawals and Changes
You may freely withdraw or change your Proposal at any time prior to the submission deadline by written notice to the IUCN Contact. However, in order to reduce the risk of fraud, no changes or withdrawals will be accepted after the submission deadline.

5. EVALUATION OF PROPOSALS
5.1. Completeness
IUCN will firstly check your Proposal for completeness. Incomplete Proposals will not be considered further.

5.2. Pre-Qualification Criteria
Only Proposals that meet all of the pre-qualification criteria will be evaluated.

5.3. Technical Evaluation
5.3.1. Scoring Method
Your Proposal will be assigned a score from 0 to 10 for each of the technical
evaluation criteria, such that ‘0’ is low and ‘10’ is high.

5.3.2. Minimum Quality Thresholds
Proposals that receive a score of ‘0’ for any of the criteria will not be considered
further.

5.3.3. Technical Score
Your score for each technical evaluation criterion will be multiplied with the respective relative weight (see Section 4.4) and these weighted scores added together to give your Proposal’s overall technical score.

5.4. Financial Evaluation and Financial Scores
The financial evaluation will be based upon the full total price you submit. Your Financial Proposal will receive a score calculated by dividing the lowest Financial Proposal that has passed the minimum quality thresholds (see Section 5.3.2) by the total price of your Financial Proposal.

Thus, for example, if your Financial Proposal is for a total of CHF 100 and the lowest Financial Proposal is CHF 80, you will receive a financial score of 80/100 = 80%

5.5. Total Score
Your Proposal’s total score will be calculated as the weighted sum of your technical mscore and your financial score.
The relative weights will be:
Technical: 70%
Financial: 30%

Thus, for example, if your technical score is 83% and your financial score is 77%, you will receive a total score of 83 * 70% + 77 * 30% = 58.1% + 23.1% = 81.2%.

Subject to the requirements in Sections 4 and 7, IUCN will award the contract to the bidder whose Proposal achieves the highest total score.

6. EXPLANATION OF PROCUREMENT PROCEDURE
6.1. IUCN is using the Open Procedure for this procurement. This means that the contracting opportunity is published on IUCN’s website and open to all interested parties to take part, subject to the conditions in Section 7 below.

6.2. You are welcome to ask questions or seek clarification regarding this
procurement. Please email the IUCN Contact (see Section 2), taking note of the deadline for submission of questions in Section 3.1.

6.3. All Proposals must be received by the submission deadline in Section 3.1 above. Late Proposals will not be considered. All Proposals received by the submission deadline will be evaluated by a team of evaluators in accordance with the evaluation criteria stated in this RfP. No other criteria will be used to evaluate Proposals. The contract will be awarded to the bidder whose Proposal received the highest Total Score. IUCN does, however, reserve the right to cancel the procurement and not award a contract at all.

6.4. IUCN will contact the bidder with the highest-scoring Proposal to finalise the contract. We will contact unsuccessful bidders after the contract has been awarded and provide detailed feedback. The timetable in Section 3.1 gives an estimate of when we expect to have completed the contract award, but this date may change depending on how long the evaluation of Proposals takes.

7. CONDITIONS FOR PARTICIPATION IN THIS PROCUREMENT
7.1. To participate in this procurement, you are required to submit a Proposal, which fully complies with the instructions in this RfP and the Attachments.
7.1.1. It is your responsibility to ensure that you have submitted a complete
and fully compliant Proposal.
7.1.2. Any incomplete or incorrectly completed Proposal submission may be
deemed non-compliant, and as a result you may be unable to proceed further in the procurement process.
7.1.3. IUCN will query any obvious clerical errors in your Proposal and may, at IUCN’s sole discretion, allow you to correct these, but only if doing so could not be perceived as giving you an unfair advantage.
7.2. In order to participate in this procurement, you must meet the following conditions:
 Free of conflicts of interest
 Registered on the relevant professional or trade register of the country in which you are established (or resident, if self-employed)
 In full compliance with your obligations relating to payment of social security contributions and of all applicable taxes
 Not been convicted of failing to comply with environmental regulatory requirements or other legal requirements relating to sustainability and environmental protection
 Not bankrupt or being wound up
 Never been guilty of an offence concerning your professional conduct
 Not involved in fraud, corruption, a criminal organisation, money laundering, terrorism, or any other illegal activity.

7.3. You must complete and sign the Declaration of Undertaking (see Attachment 2).

7.4. If you are participating in this procurement as a member of a joint venture, or are using sub-contractors, submit a separate Declaration of Undertaking for each member of the joint venture and sub-contractor, and be clear in your Proposal which parts of the goods/services are provided by each partner or sub-contractor.

7.5. Each bidder shall submit only one Proposal, either individually or as a partner in a joint venture. In case of joint venture, one company shall not be allowed to participate in two different joint ventures in the same procurement nor shall a company be allowed to submit a Proposal both on its behalf and as part of a joint venture for the same procurement. A bidder who submits or participates in more than one Proposal (other than as a subcontractor or in cases of alternatives that have been permitted or requested) shall cause all the Proposals with the bidder’s participation to be disqualified.

7.6. By taking part in this procurement, you accept the conditions set out in this RfP, including the following:
 It is unacceptable to give or offer any gift or consideration to an employee or other representative of IUCN as a reward or inducement in relation to the awarding of a contract. Such action will give IUCN the right to exclude you from this and any future procurements, and to terminate any contract that may have been signed with you.
 Any attempt to obtain information from an employee or other representative of IUCN concerning another bidder will result in disqualification.
 Any price fixing or collusion with other bidders in relation to this procurement shall give IUCN the right to exclude you and any other involved bidder(s) from this and any future procurements and may constitute a criminal offence.

8. CONFIDENTIALITY AND DATA PROTECTION
8.1. IUCN follows the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation
(GDPR). The information you submit to IUCN as part of this procurement will be treated as confidential and shared only as required to evaluate your Proposal in line with the procedure explained in this RfP, and for the maintenance of a clear audit trail. For audit purposes, IUCN is required to retain your Proposal in its entirety for 10 years after then end of the resulting contract and make this available to internal and external auditors and donors as and when requested.

8.2. In the Declaration of Undertaking (Attachment 2) you need to give IUCN express permission to use the information you submit in this way, including personal data that forms part of your Proposal. Where you include personal data of your employees (e.g. CVs) in your Proposal, you need to have written permission from those individuals to share this information with IUCN, and for IUCN to use this information as indicated in 8.1. Without these permissions, IUCN will not be able to consider your Proposal.

9. COMPLAINTS PROCEDURE
If you have a complaint or concern regarding the propriety of how a competitive process is or has been executed, then please contact procurement@iucn.org.
Such complaints or concerns will be treated as confidential and are not considered in breach of the above restrictions on communication (Section 2.1).

10. CONTRACT
The contract will be based on IUCN’s template in Attachment 3, the terms of which are not negotiable. They may, however, be amended by IUCN to reflect particular requirements from the donor funding this particular procurement.

11. ABOUT IUCN
IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together.

Headquartered in Switzerland, IUCN Secretariat comprises around 1,000 staff
with offices in more than 50 countries.

Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,300 Member organisations and some 10,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards.

IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development.

Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well being.

About IUCN
IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together.

Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,400 Member organisations and around 15,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards.

IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development.

Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well-being.

About the Project
The approach to integrated water resources management for more resilient basins in Mozambique [MozWateR] is a project aimed at achieving water security by supporting Mozambique in developing its capacity to implement effective integrated water resources management (IWRM) in key basins within the northern and central water management regions of the country and to improve capacity at the national level. This project is a collaborative effort in which joint action on the ground will yield critical lessons from tested best practices that inform policies strengthening business approaches, institutions and regulations surrounding the sustainable use of land and water. MozWateR is being implemented in collaboration with the Northern Regional Water Authority (ARA-Norte), the Central Regional Water Authority (ARA-Centro) and the National Directorate for Water Resources Management (DNGRH) as the main implementing partners (IPs) to address various challenges in the national water sector.

Description of the Assignment
1. GENERAL DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTIVITY
Climate variability reduces the socio-economic development potential of rural populations in Mozambique. Floods and droughts represent the main climate threats faced by the country and are responsible for recurring economic losses that inhibit the country’s robust growth. The main objective of the dams is to provide water for supply and to irrigate fields. The availability of water for irrigation will certainly contribute to economic growth and improved health conditions. As the forests in the region where the Augusto Maponesse dam is to be built are still quite dense and intact, the implementation of this project could provide an opportunity to preserve them. Agricultural planning could minimise the rate of clearing new fields and the destruction of forests.

2. INFRASTRUCTURE DATA
2.1. Augusto Maponesse (Irrigation and consumption)
The Augusto Maponesse dam is located in central Mozambique, specifically in the province of Manica, Gondola district, along the Mudamba River, a tributary of the Messinge (lowermiddle Pungué sub-basin). The coordinates are: 18 52 19.7S 33 28 54.7E.

The area has abundant fertile soil. Local families are well organised within a traditional system. A willingness to form farmers’ associations has been demonstrated. However, intensified agriculture could slow down the rate at which new fields are opened up and the destruction of the untouched closed forests.

3. DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES TO BE PROVIDED BY THE CONSULTANT
3.1. Preliminary and feasibility studies
During the Preliminary Studies phase, the location alternatives for each of the dams should be preliminarily assessed, with particular emphasis on the nature of the valley, the availability of materials for the execution of the works, the geology of the valley and the reservoir area, and the extent of the dam body and its reservoir. A first-order estimate is made of the benefits, costs and implementation timelines for the works. The consultancy services include, but are not limited to, the following tasks:

a) Conducting a technical site visit with a multidisciplinary team to inspect and identify three alternative sites for technical studies of the dam’s location, indicating the most suitable position;
b) Define the best alternative for the dam axis and analyse the possible design options for the dam and spillway structures, presenting the one that proves most suitable in accordance with the site’s geotechnical characteristics and the availability of materials (soils, water availability, etc.);
c) Present written and drawn documents and other information, so as to enable an assessment of the recommended solutions, including safety aspects, and thus allow for their comparison and decision-making;
d) Prepare a technical report on the preliminary and feasibility studies.

3.2. Preparation of the Detailed Design and Final Design
3.2.1. Preliminary Design
During the Preliminary Design phase, work will be carried out using the data generated from the Preliminary Study, incorporating technical and construction aspects. The preliminary design must provide input for the preparation of the Basic Design and should, but is not limited to, the following:

3.2.1.1. Hydrological Studies
Hydrological studies of the dam catchment area must take into account the interference of upstream and downstream weirs/dams, where applicable, and must cover, at a minimum, the following items:
i. Delimitation of the dam’s catchment area on a suitable scale;
ii. Collection of data from existing rainfall and climatological stations within the catchment and its vicinity;
iii. Calculation of rainfall (IDF) – I (intensity), D (duration) and F (frequency) for stations located upstream of the dam;
iv. Determination of maximum flows (design flow) for the sizing of the dam’s spillways;
v. Determination of residual flows for the design of regulation structures, ensuring multiple uses downstream and the maintenance of the aquatic ecosystem;
vi. Definition of the reservoir’s characteristic curves (elevation x area x volume) based on a topographical survey at an appropriate scale;
vii. Determination of the maximum discharge flow
viii. Definition of measures to control seepage through the foundation and the dam body.

3.2.1.2. Geological and Geotechnical Studies
When preparing geological and geotechnical studies, the following aspects must be taken into
account:
i. Geological and geotechnical studies must be carried out at the dam site, water intake, spillway, along the dam axis to characterise the foundation, and also at locations of borrow pits (deposits or borrow sites for the dam’s embankment);
ii. When selecting the borrow pit location, the study must consider the transport distance, assessing the cost-effectiveness and the technical feasibility of obtaining a licence or consent for material extraction.
iii. Geotechnical boreholes shall provide the data for the preparation of representative geological and geotechnical profiles, containing a description of the materials in the different layers, penetration resistances and other information that may be relevant to the interpretation

3.2.1.3. Technical Study Report
The Technical Study Report must contain the Technical Specifications and Diagnosis and must present, but be limited to, the following items:
i. Technical Specifications, which must address all the specific features of the site where the dam is to be built, taking into account the need for river diversions, excavations, removal of obstructions (poles, power lines, structural elements, site clearance, etc.) and foundation treatment, as well as any and all services required for the future construction of the.
ii. Specify, for the river diversion, the structural or earthworks elements required in its various construction phases, whatever solution is adopted (whether using tunnels, galleries, channels, or whether the dam will be constructed in sections, with water flowing on one side of the river channel, or in areas of the channel).
iii. A report (work plan) describing the dam construction works, covering their specific features and relevant considerations, listing the technical personnel responsible, construction stages and measures to mitigate environmental impacts, as well as Permanent Preservation Areas (PPA) and the Degraded Area Recovery Project (PRAD).
iv. A technical data sheet containing the characteristics of the reservoir and the dam.

3.2.1.4. Diagnostic Report
The Diagnostic Report must include, but be limited to, the following items:
 A study to assess the safety and stability of the dam, to be carried out through tests or any other method deemed appropriate for this purpose, primarily to assess sliding forces, overturning forces, base pressures, shear forces and seepage, amongst other factors deemed necessary for a thorough diagnosis of the dam;
 A diagnosis must assess the future stability of the dam to be constructed and the necessary interventions aimed at modifications and/or increasing reserve capacity.

3.2.2. Basic Design
This is the intermediate stage between the Preliminary Design and the Detailed Design. It enables the execution of the works and the detailing of the Detailed Design. To this end, it must include, but is not limited to, the following items:
3.2.2.1. Reservoir sizing
The sizing of the reservoir must take into account, but is not limited to, the following:
i. Definition of the elevation–area–volume curves based on the survey of the catchment area to determine the optimum storage volume;
ii. Flooded areas and stored volumes;
iii. Secondary uses compatible with the main purposes of the reservoir and the conditions under which they may be carried out;
iv. Design of discharge structures, including sluice gates and bottom outlets (or bottom discharges);
v. Dam operating mechanisms, including water intakes, associated hydraulic circuits and their respective outlets.

3.2.2.2. Dimensioning of the dam body geometry
The design of the reservoir shall take into account, but not be limited to, the following:
 Studies of the stresses, loads and conditions to which it will be subjected after entering into operation, to verify its stability and safety beyond the factors considered for the calculation of overall dam stability;
 Structural design, using software to present calculations, reports, formwork drawings, reinforcement and details;
 Depending on the scale of the works and the complexity of the dam design, instrumentation plans must be drawn up for monitoring the dam body and foundations and for operational control, including reservoir monitoring equipment, water intake flow meters and detailed drawings of the structures for installing this equipment
 Consideration must be given to the compositions, loading equations, profile calculations (base width, maximum height of a dam) and reinforcement.

3.2.3. Detailed Design and Safety Plan
3.2.3.1. Detailed Design
The Detailed Design must consist of elements that are easy and unambiguous to interpret, enabling the construction of the works, and must include, among other things:
 General and Descriptive Report;
 Written Documents and Drawings;
 Reports on stability calculations and structural design;
 Report on topographical surveys and studies;
 Report on geological and geotechnical surveys and studies;
 Dam body design and foundation design
 Laboratory test report;
 Physical and financial schedule for the works;
 Construction work execution plan;
 List of Materials and Equipment;
 Technical Specifications for Materials and Services for the civil works;
 Technical Specifications for Materials and Services for the equipment; and
 Other documents providing the necessary details for the complete and proper implementation of the works, including dam instrumentation (type, characteristics, location of application, bill of quantities, manufacturer’s catalogues, etc.).

The Detailed Design consists of the execution of all project details necessary for the execution of the works and, amongst others, the following main items must also be addressed, but are not limited to:
(i) Access design, including geometric design, any retaining structures, drainage, paving, vertical and horizontal signage, and lighting (if necessary).
(ii) River diversion design, including definition of its stages, construction materials, dimensions, execution methodology and equipment (if necessary).
(iii) Geotechnical designs, including the definition of construction materials, dimensions and characteristics, execution methodology, equipment and instrumentation.
(iv) Structural and foundation design, including the definition of materials, drilling studies, finishes, joints, types and grades of concrete, support devices, steel reinforcement and other devices, instrumentation plan, etc.
(v) Development plans and details (developer’s site) covering paving and drainage.
(vi) Earthworks and soil compaction design.
(vii) Any other designs and studies necessary for the complete and proper execution of the works.

The Studies, Surveys, Boreholes, Investigations, Designs, Structural Calculations and Drawings, amongst others, that may be carried out must comply with current and updated Technical Standards in force in Mozambique and accepted internationally.

In providing the services, the Consultant shall submit the Detailed Design and a final report, which shall cover all relevant technical aspects of the preparation of the Detailed Design and include all data, such as field notes and observations, inspection reports, geological mapping, laboratory test results, photographs, all structural, hydraulic, geotechnical and geological data and calculations.

Deliver to the Client the Detailed Design, completed and ready for implementation, as well as the Bill of Quantities and Price Schedule, in both digital and physical formats, together with all relevant technical information.

3.2.3.2. Dam Safety Plan
i. Construction Supervision and Quality Assurance Plan
The Consultant shall prepare a Construction Supervision and Quality Assurance Plan specific to the project, reflecting the key aspects and elements relating to organisation, staffing levels, procedures, equipment and qualifications for supervising the construction of the project, in accordance with best practice recommendations regarding dam safety.

ii. Dam Instrumentation Plan
The Consultant shall prepare the instrumentation plan in accordance with best practice recommendations for dam safety.

iii. Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Plan
As part of this task, the consultant shall, without necessarily being limited to the following:
i. Specify the requirements for daily, monthly, annual and periodic safety inspections (frequency to be recommended by the consultant);
ii. Prepare a draft operation and maintenance plan in accordance with recommendations on good dam safety practices.
iii. Ensure the existence and institutionalisation of the sediment management plan, electronic flow management plan and ESMP (and other related plans);
iv. Develop and recommend the staffing levels, technical expertise, tools and equipment required for dam maintenance and operation procedures, including safety inspections, as well as the necessary training.

iv. Emergency Preparedness Plan (EPP)
The purpose of the EPP is to provide a pre-determined action plan that the dam operator must implement in the event of a dam safety emergency. This plan will be drawn up by the consultant in close collaboration with the contractor and the authorities responsible for emergency management.

As part of this task, the consultant will identify potential emergency situations, including a possible dam failure. The consultant will draw up a plan describing the roles of the parties (stakeholders) in dealing with these potential emergencies, including situations where dam failure is imminent.

In preparing the plan, the consultant’s activities will include the preparation of descriptions, atlases and associated flowcharts for the parties involved, but not necessarily limited to the following situations:
a. Abnormal behaviour of the dam.
b. Dam failure (structural failure).
c. Severe and extreme flooding.
d. Controlled release of water that may endanger human lives and property downstream
e. Seismic waves.
f. Cyclones.
g. Water contamination.
h. Terrorism and sabotage.

The preparation of the EPP framework will require simulations of severe/extreme floods and dam failure scenarios with induced propagation of flood waves downstream. Dam breach flood maps should show the flooded areas at scales sufficient to identify areas at risk and include flood tables showing the time of arrival of the peak discharge, water level, velocity, etc. at key locations.

The emergency preparedness framework plan and associated flood maps must be drawn up in accordance with the recommendations of Best Practices on dam safety.

3.3. The Environmental Pre-Feasibility Study and Scope Definition (EPDA)
The Environmental Pre-Feasibility and Scope Definition Study (EPDA) must be conducted for activities classified as having a significant environmental impact, with the aim of identifying and assessing the main impacts, analysing alternatives and mitigation measures, as well as defining the scope of the EIA by selecting the environmental components that may be affected by the activity under review and on which the EIAS should focus.
