A bidder who submits or participates in more than one Proposal (other than as a subcontractor or in cases of alternatives that have been permitted or requested) shall cause all the Proposals with the bidder’s participation to be disqualified.
7.6. By taking part in this procurement, you accept the conditions set out in this RfP, including the following:

Such action will give IUCN the right to exclude you from this and any future procurements, and to terminate any contract that may have been signed with you.

8. CONFIDENTIALITY AND DATA PROTECTION
8.1. IUCN follows the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Terms of Reference for IUCN Consultancy
Integrated Baseline Assessment and Development of the Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning Plan for the REPLAN Project
Overall Objective
To establish an integrated baseline and develop a practical Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) system for the REPLAN Project.
Specific Objectives
1. Establish baseline values for the REPLAN project results framework. The draft results framework is available.
2. To identify priority restoration landscapes and implementation sites to inform project implementation.
3. Review and strengthen the project Results Framework, Theory of Change, indicators and targets.
4. To develop a practical and integrated MEAL system, including the PMP, PIRS, DQA framework and reporting tools.
5. Embed cross-cutting principles into the project monitoring system by ensuring that gender equality, human rights, safeguards, Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC), grievance redress, conflict sensitivity, social inclusion, and stakeholder engagement are systematically integrated into monitoring, reporting, and learning processes.
6. To strengthen the capacity of the PMU and implementing partners to implement the MEAL system.

Background
The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) is implementing the project ‘Building Resilient Community Conservancies for Biodiversity Conservation, Resilience, Livelihood Improvement and Peace/Security in the Churo-Kirisia-Mukogodo-Oldonyiro-Ndoto-Mathews Ranges-Sabarwawa Ecosystems in Northern Kenya’, short form REPLAN. The project is funded by the European Union under the NaturAfrica programme and implemented by IUCN in partnership with WWF-Kenya, VSF-Suisse and the Regional Centre for Mapping Resources and Development (RCMRD), each of which has responsibility for specific technical workstreams.
REPLAN is a 4-year project (2026 – 2029) implemented in a connected dryland landscape covering parts of Laikipia, Samburu, Isiolo, Baringo and Marsabit counties. The project area includes community conservancies, rangelands, dryland forests, riparian systems, wetlands, wildlife corridors, water towers, pastoral mobility routes and nature-based livelihood systems. The landscape faces interlinked pressures, including biodiversity loss, rangeland degradation, invasive species, water scarcity, human-wildlife conflict, climate vulnerability, weak natural resource governance, unclear resource tenure, and recurring resource use conflict and mobility.
The project seeks to strengthen the resilience of communities and ecosystems by improving biodiversity conservation, restoring degraded landscapes, strengthening climate-resilient livelihoods, promoting alternative energy, improving water and rangeland governance, supporting inclusive community institutions, strengthening human rights-based approaches, and improving conflict-sensitive natural resource governance.

About IUCN
IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together.
Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,400 Member organisations and some 15,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards.
IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development.
Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well-being.
www.iucn.org
https://twitter.com/IUCN

About the Project
REPLAN has four main components:
Component 1: Improve biodiversity and ecosystem conservation in Northern Central Kenya. This includes degradation and invasive species mapping, restoration of degraded ecosystems, rangeland reseeding, invasive species management, water conservation measures, biodiversity monitoring, OECM-related work, safeguards screening, Human Rights Impact Assessments, Gender Analysis and human-wildlife coexistence measures.
Component 2: Improve livelihoods and resilience of communities, especially women and youth. This includes support to regenerative green and nature-based enterprises, sustainable enterprise plans, blended finance support, alternative energy solutions, predator-proof bomas, and resilient livestock market systems.
Component 3: Strengthen inclusive natural resource governance in project landscapes. This includes community land processes, grievance redress mechanisms, dispute-resolution frameworks, peacebuilding, IMET assessments, stakeholder learning and advocacy.
Component 4: Project management, coordination, monitoring, evaluation, learning and communication. This includes baseline, mid-term review, endline, project coordination, reporting, knowledge management, financial management and adaptive learning.
This Terms of Reference (ToR) provides the framework for an integrated baseline assessment that will consolidate these workstreams into a coherent project baseline. The baseline will provide the foundations for sex, age, vulnerability, and location disaggregated monitoring as well as for community resilience, socio-economic change, governance outcomes, private sector engagement and safeguards performance.
The consultancy will therefore support IUCN to develop an integrated baseline and Project Monitoring Plan that brings together project level Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) requirements and partner-led technical baseline inputs into one coherent monitoring system required for implementation, partner reporting, donor reporting and adaptive management.

Purpose of the Assignment
The purpose of the assignment is to establish credible baseline values, methods, tools and datasets for REPLAN’s logical framework, and develop the core project Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning Plan required for implementation, donor reporting, safeguards tracking and adaptive management.
The baseline will provide the reference point against which project outputs, outcomes, EU Common Indicators and NaturAfrica indicators will be monitored, evaluated and reported. It will also support site prioritisation, partner work planning, safeguards implementation and compliance, gender-responsive programming, accountability and stakeholder feedback mechanisms beneficiary targeting, risk management, and learning throughout project implementation.

Description of the Assignment
IUCN seeks the services of a consultant to provide REPLAN and its partners with a technically sound, practical and field-usable baseline and Monitoring Evaluation Accountability and Learning (MEAL) system that enables the project to measure progress, demonstrate results, manage risks, support learning, and report credibly to the European Union.
The specific tasks of the consultancy are:
1. Establish baseline values for all REPLAN project indicators
2. Review, refine and, where necessary propose changes to the project results framework, indicators, targets, means of verification review the project's Theory of Change (ToC) to ensure logical flow from activities to EU-level outcomes.
3. Develop a Project MEAL plan Plan that includes a) a monitoring plan which defines what will be measured, how, by whom, how often, using which tools, and with what quality controls; b) project Learning agenda to include learning questions, pause and reflect sessions and adaptive manage sessions; c) project knowledge management plan and d) and accountability plan to address grievance procedures
4. Develop a MEAL risk register
5. Prepare Performance Indicator Reference Sheets for all project indicators.
6. Develop a Data Quality Assurance framework, including data verification procedures, reporting responsibilities, evidence requirements and partner-level quality checks.
7. Co-design practical reporting templates and tools for IUCN, WWF-Kenya, VSF-Suisse, RCMRD and other relevant project actors.
8. Assess the status and drivers of ecosystem degradation and biodiversity loss and identify priority restoration landscapes and implementation sites using the Restoration Opportunities Assessment Methodology (ROAM) and a participatory Multi-Criteria Analysis (MCA).
9. Undertake a stocktake of existing restoration initiatives to document best practices, lessons learned, and what has worked and not worked in the target country, drawing on scientific evidence and local and Indigenous knowledge.
10. In consultation with the consortium members and applying the principles of NbS develop context-specific restoration action packages for the prioritized landscapes, defining the recommended restoration interventions, implementation approaches, indicative investment needs, expected outcomes, and monitoring indicators.
11. Stakeholder Mapping and Categorization; Identifying all relevant actors, their interests, and their operational scales (from local to national).
12. Establish existing coordination mechanisms and related gaps targeting gender and social inclusion in the coordination structures and policy-related bottlenecks.
13. Security and conflict dynamics mapping to identify the hotspots, frequency, root causes and potential impacts to vulnerable groups.
14. Establish a beneficiary tracking and disaggregation framework covering sex, age, location, vulnerability category and relevant stakeholder group.
15. Integrate gender, safeguards, human rights, Free Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC), stakeholder engagement, Grievance Redress Mechanisms (GRM), conflict sensitivity and inclusion requirements into the MEAL system.
16. Produce a final baseline report and MEAL package that can be used by the Project Management Unit and implementing partners.
The assignment will cover all REPLAN components, outputs, indicators and partner workstreams. It will include both quantitative and qualitative methods, and will draw on field-level, institutional, geospatial, ecological, socio-economic, governance, gender, safeguards and conflict-related data.
The consultant will work across the four REPLAN micro-landscapes and relevant counties, including the following broad landscape clusters: Churo-Kirisia / Ruko-Kaptuya-Mukutan landscape; Mukogodo-Oldonyiro / Naibunga-Shulmai landscape; Ndoto-Mathews landscape and Sabarwawa / Melako-Shurr landscape.
Final field sites will be confirmed during inception in consultation with IUCN and implementing partners.

Methodology
The baseline assessment will establish the starting position for REPLAN’s results framework and develop the core Monitoring Evaluation Accountability and Learning system required to track implementation, measure results, support adaptive management and meet donor reporting requirements. The consultant will apply a mixed-methods approach combining document review, indicator mapping, field-based quantitative and qualitative data collection, geospatial and biophysical data review, partner consultations, and validation with IUCN and implementing partners.
The consultant shall not duplicate technical assessments already planned under other project activities, such as detailed geospatial mapping by RCMRD or specialist ecological assessments by biodiversity partners. The consultant shall coordinate with these workstreams and integrate available data into the baseline assessment and Project Monitoring Plan (PMP). Where partner-generated data are not available during the assignment, the consultant shall document the resulting data gaps, use the best available evidence where appropriate, and recommend how and when the outstanding data should be incorporated into the baseline and PMP.
The following are some of the activities to be included in the methodology:
1. Desk review and inception: Review relevant project documents and prepare an inception report setting out the proposed methodology, sampling approach, fieldwork plan, tools, team composition, data quality approach, ethical and safeguards protocols, risk management measures and detailed workplan.
2. Results framework and indicator review: Review the REPLAN project results framework and assess whether each indicator is clear, measurable, attributable, feasible and aligned with available data sources. The assessment will develop a practical indicator measurement framework for all project outcomes and outputs.
3. Methodology, sampling and data collection tools: The consultant shall design a mixed-methods baseline methodology, including the proposed sampling approach, data collection methods and tools, quality assurance measures, and analytical framework. The proposed methodology shall be technically robust, practical and fit for the scope and objectives of the assignment, with a clear justification for the proposed approach.
4. Landscape Restoration Opportunity Assessment and Restoration Planning: Applying the Restoration Opportunities Assessment Methodology (ROAM) and a participatory Multi-Criteria Analysis (MCA), the firm will assess ecosystem degradation and biodiversity loss, identify priority restoration landscapes and implementation sites, undertake a stocktake of existing restoration initiatives, and develop context-specific Nature-based Solutions (NbS) restoration action packages, including recommended interventions, implementation approaches, indicative investment needs, and monitoring indicators.
5. Field data collection: Undertake field data collection in selected project landscapes and counties using a mixed-methods approach proposed by the consultant and approved during the inception phase. The proposed methodology shall be appropriate to the scope and objectives of the assignment and should capture ecological, livelihood, governance, gender, safeguards, conflict, grievance redress and inclusion dimensions of the project. The consultant shall ensure that data collection does not raise unrealistic expectations or create conflict over project benefits.
6. Establish baseline values and confirm targets: Analyse collected data and establish baseline values for each indicator. For indicators where a baseline cannot be fully established during the assignment due to unforeseen issues, the consultant shall clearly explain the limitation and propose the method, responsible party, and timeline for confirming the baseline. The consultant shall also review and recommend refinements to targets where current targets are incomplete or require clarification.
7. Develop the Project Monitoring Plan: The consultant shall develop a Project Monitoring Plan (PMP) for REPLAN. The PMP shall be practical, concise, and usable by the PMU and partners. The PMP shall clearly identify which indicators are reported by IUCN, WWF-Kenya, VSF-Suisse, RCMRD or other actors, and how data will be consolidated. The consultant shall also prepare Performance Indicator Reference (PIR) Sheets for each indicator. The contents of the PIR shall be agreed during the inception phase.
8. Develop the Data Quality Assurance (DQA) framework: The consultant shall develop a DQA framework to guide project monitoring and reporting. The framework shall cover elements discussed during the inception workshop and should also include a simple DQA checklist for use during partner reporting and supervision.
9. Develop partner reporting tools and beneficiary tracking system: The consultant shall prepare reporting templates aligned to the donor reporting requirement and monitoring tools for use by IUCN and partners. The beneficiary tracking system shall enable disaggregation by sex, age, county, micro-landscape, conservancy/community, vulnerability category, beneficiary type and intervention type, subject to data protection and informed consent requirements.
10. Integrate Gender, Safeguards, HRBA, GRM and Conflict Sensitivity into MEAL: The consultant shall also work with the IUCN and Partner Gender and Safeguards team to ensure that the MEAL system captures the implementation of safeguards, gender, human rights and conflict-sensitivity commitments. These should be embedded in indicator reporting, activity reporting, field supervision, and adaptive management.
11. Validation and Capacity Building: The consultant shall organise and facilitate a validation workshop with IUCN, WWF-Kenya, VSF-Suisse, RCMRD and relevant stakeholders. The consultant shall also provide practical orientation to the Project Management Unit (PMU) and implementing partners on the use of the MEAL system, including monitoring and reporting tools, data quality assurance procedures, and roles and responsibilities for data collection, reporting and quality control.
Duration of the Assignment
The assignment is expected to be completed within 10 to 12 weeks maximum from the date of contract signature. The final timeline will be agreed during contract negotiation and confirmed in the inception report.

Phase 2(Baseline Assessment)
Final data collection tools

The draft report based on the annotated outline developed during the inception phase, highlighting key findings on the indicator values, analysis by component/output, data limitations and target recommendations. Which should include priority landscapes and sites with maps.
Baseline Validation workshop
5 days after approval of the draft baseline report
Report presenting summary of stakeholder feedback and agreed revisions.

Phase 3 (MEAL System Development)

Included with baseline report
Full PMP including indicators, baselines, targets, methods, frequency, responsibilities and data flow. Learning agenda, knowledge management plan, accountability plan and a project risk register

Performance Indicator Reference Sheets for all project indicators.

Included with draft PMP
Data quality framework, verification procedures, evidence standards, DQA checklist and partner controls.

Payment Schedule
Milestone - Deliverable - Description - Payment (%)
Milestone 1 - Inception Phase - Approval of the Inception Report and Indicator Mapping Matrix - 15%
Milestone 2 - Baseline Assessment - Approval of the final data collection tools, field data collection and submission of the draft baseline report - 30%

Milestone 5 - Final Deliverables and Handover - Submission and approval of the Final Baseline Report and Final MEAL Package, including the finalized PMP, PIRS, DQA Framework, reporting tools, beneficiary tracking tools, all supporting annexes and datasets, and completion of the capacity-building workshop(s) - 20%

Skills and Experience
The assignment may be undertaken by a consulting firm or a team of consultants. The proposed team shall collectively demonstrate the required expertise outlined below. Bidders may determine the most appropriate team composition, provided all required competencies are adequately covered, demonstrated and clearly justified.
Team Leader: Natural Resources Management Specialist:
• At least 15 years' experience in natural resources management, biodiversity conservation, landscape restoration, rangeland management, ecosystem management or related fields.
• Advanced university/master’s degree in Natural Resources Management, Environmental Management, Conservation Biology, Forestry, Rangeland Management or related discipline.
• Demonstrated experience leading large multidisciplinary baseline assessments and coordinating technical teams in donor-funded programmes.
• Proven experience in landscape restoration, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem management, and integrated natural resource management.
• Ability to interpret ecological, geospatial, and biophysical data.
• Demonstrated experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams comprising monitoring and evaluation, governance, livelihoods and social safeguard specialists.
• Experience managing multi-partner programmes funded by the European Union or other international development partners will be an added advantage.
The team leader will be supported by experts in the following thematic areas Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Specialist:
• At least 15 years' experience in conducting baseline studies, designing MEAL systems, and implementing MEAL systems for donor-funded programmes.
• Strong experience developing Results Frameworks, Project Monitoring Plans (PMPs), Performance Indicator Reference Sheets (PIRS), Data Quality Assurance (DQA) frameworks, indicator tracking systems and reporting tools.
• Proven experience leading MEAL system development for multi-partner consortia, including harmonising diverse reporting requirements across implementing partners. Experience with EU-funded or other large multi-partner programmes is highly desirable.
• Experience in designing and implementing baseline assessments, indicator measurement methodologies, data quality systems and learning frameworks.
• Strong analytical, reporting and data management skills.
Governance Specialist:
• Demonstrated experience in natural resource governance, community conservancies, institutional strengthening, policy development and stakeholder engagement.
• Experience supporting governance assessments, community participation, conflict-sensitive programming and multi-stakeholder coordination.
• Familiarity with governance systems within ASAL and conservation landscapes will be an added advantage.
Livelihoods Specialist:
• Demonstrated experience in sustainable livelihoods, nature-based enterprises, pastoral production systems, value chain development, and community resilience programming.
• Experience assessing socio-economic conditions and designing livelihood interventions within dryland and conservation landscapes.
• Familiarity with gender-responsive and inclusive livelihood approaches.
Human Rights-Based Approach (HRBA) Specialist:
• Experience integrating gender, safeguards, HRBA, FPIC, GRM, conflict sensitivity and inclusion into monitoring systems.
• Knowledge of gender and social inclusion issues in ASAL, pastoralist or conservation landscapes.
Quantitative and Qualitative Data Specialist(s):
• Experience designing sampling frameworks, survey tools, databases, data quality controls and quantitative analysis.
• Experience conducting KIIs, FGDs, participatory methods and institutional assessments in rural or dryland contexts.
Requirement: The consulting firm or team of consultants must be physically located in Kenya, as the assignment requires travel to the project target areas for field data collection, stakeholder consultations, and validation activities.
Evaluation Criteria
Proposals will be evaluated based on technical and financial criteria.

opportunities.title: Finance Development Coordinator
opportunities.description:
The purpose of the Finance Development Coordinator is to ensure specialized, targeted, deliverable-based assistance to the Ukraine Red Cross (NS). This includes both ongoing and upcoming FD projects i nthe country. Working directly/closely with the NS, the mission of the Coordinator will be to support the NS in improving their financial management such that they may efficiently implement their humanitarian action and fulfil their humanitarian mandate. This shall be accomplished in close collaboration with Network partners under established and ad hoc agreements. Technical service delivery provided by the Coordinator should contribute to NS becoming more accountable, efficient, and effective. The assistance provided to NSs should be structured within international frameworks and standards e.g. (IFRS, IAS, McKenzie 7S, COSO Framework on Internal Controls and the COSO Framework on ERM).

The Coordinator may also be requested to assist outside her/his region based on their specialization in coordination with the Finance Development Manager for Europe.

Strategic Objectives:

  • Ensures that the support provided is in conformity with the global service delivery model and is deliverable based, such that it is designed and implemented in line with established technical standards and project management methodologies and support the operationalization of those standards.
  • Contribute to financial management in URCS which is grounded in a due diligence/needs assessment, improved accountability, transparency & governance as well as improved efficiency and effectiveness of Internal Controls.
  • Increased efficiency, reliability and relevance of financial reporting and departmental structure.
  • Contributes proactively with other technical personnel to Global FD Center global efforts to establish and operationalize technical approaches and standards in finance development.

Operational Objectives:

  • Enhance efficiency and effectiveness within the NS finance department.

  • Evaluate the Finance Department structure using the McKinsey 7S model and propose new structures for improved efficiency and effectiveness, including job description revisions and specialized trainings.

  • Adopt a risk-based approach by focusing on hinderances to the Finance Dept not achieving its operational, reporting and compliance goals.

  • Recommend new departmental structures focusing on efficiencies and renewed effectiveness. This includes revision and alignment of job descriptions and conducting specialized trainings in accounting, treasury, budgeting and grants plus compliance.

  • Provides technical trainings to NS Finance Dept staff on established technical standards.

  • Design and co-facilitate workshops for NS Finance Dept staff on objective settings, structural assessments etc.

  • Improve internal control processes by compiling, mapping, and analyzing existing processes, evaluating inherent and control risks, and designing new processes and controls.

  • Compile, map, and analyze processes within the Finance Department on an ‘As Is’ basis.

  • Design new processes, internal controls while focusing on efficiencies and operation, reporting and compliance objectives. This includes preparing “should be” process maps.

  • Supports the NSs in preparing or revising policies and procedures including Finance & Accounting manuals.

  • Analyse and recommend areas of improvement in financial oversight by governance.

  • Focus on assisting NS in terms of improving financial reporting (internal and external) insofar that efficiency, effectiveness and relevance increases.

  • Introducing capabilities in NS accounting software to ensure automated, customizable, transparent and reliable financial reports are produced.

  • Develop deliverable based project documents including concept notes, proposals, specific objectives, budgets, PoAs, LFAs, Project risk assessment, ITTs and monitoring plans (as per applicable Core Process).

  • If required, assist in designing and conduct evaluations of FD projects.

  • Contribute to the global FD service delivery in various technical capacities.

  • Ensure coordination and alignment between FD Officers’ support and Global FD Center's global FD strategies.

  • Consolidate regional inputs from Officers to inform planning, reporting, and learning.

  • Up to 50% travel to support other NS if and as requested.

    Key Performance Indicators:

  • ≥ 85% of deliverables achieved on the POA implementation

  • ≥ 4.0/5 NS satisfaction rating Quality of NS-facing technical support

    Collaboration.

  • Fosters good relationship and works closely together with the host NS, PNSs, IFRC and ICRC.

  • Work as a team within the region and globally, to assist NS’s in meeting their needs in FD.

  • Liaises, as needed, with Colleagues in the Country, Regional and National Office.

  • Works closely together and participates in technical networks (FD and NSD) with other colleagues within Global FD Centre at global, regional and country level.

  • Helps colleagues to understand and make use of available technical tools and standards. Promotes harmonization across delegations’ structures, as well as at regional and country level with other Network partners, by promoting use of common standards and tools, also contributing to learning events and sharing of best practices.

    Mission Specific Responsibilities:

  • Conduct needs assessments of national societies in line with Global FD Center’s Due Diligence methodology.

  • Prepare deliverable-based Plan of actions that are targeted in meeting NS needs.

    Formal Competence:

    Education:

  • CPA/CA/Registered Auditor any accounting designation is a must; however, MBAs are also encouraged to apply.

  • Members of an international professional accounting body are preferred.

    Experience:

  • Over 10 years’ experience in Financial Management (Accounting, Budgeting, Grants and Compliance and Treasury).

  • Minimum 5 years’ experience in developing implementing partner’s strength in financial management.

  • Minimum of 5 years’ experience of coaching, facilitating, managing and/or supporting staff.

  • Experience of working for a humanitarian aid organisation preferably in a developing/conflict country/context.

  • Good understanding of an ERP system.

  • Strong organizational development background (e.g. change management, HR, leadership, strategy development and implementation).

    Skills and Knowledge:

  • In-depth understanding of relevant technical financial standards and the operationalization of those standards in humanitarian projects.

  • Operational understanding of IFRS, IAS, COSO Framework on Internal Controls and their Framework on Enterprise Risk Management.

  • Proven experience from project management, including needs assessments project design, and reporting.

  • High degree of competencies in strategic thinking and design, knowledge sharing, advising and facilitating, management of self; coaching; mentoring and facilitation. Training and facilitating experience in international/ multicultural environment are an asset.

  • Proficiency required in English (knowledge of local language (s) will be an added advantage).

  • Advanced understanding of the use of innovative tools and approaches in relevant technical discipline is an asset.

  • Fully familiar with software applications- windows, spreadsheets, word processing, accounting packages.

    Personal Attributes:

  • Ability to take initiative and accept responsibility.

  • Ability to work towards achieving objectives and results.

  • Ability to cooperate in teams and share competency.

  • Ability to develop and coach others Commitment to RCRC Network principles and values

    Reporting to:

  • Regional Finance Development Manager - Europe

    Position is based in:

  • Kyiv, Ukraine

    Contract length:

  • 12 Months

    Why should you apply?

  • Meaningful: You`ll be a part of the world's largest humanitarian organization, reaching the most vulnerable people in their local community.

  • Impact: You will help National Societies in the region to become strong, self-sustained and accountable humanitarian actors.

  • Career: You will be connected to an international organization with staff based all over the world

  • A great place to work: You will work in a multicultural environment with hard-working, dedicated and fun colleagues with a strong culture of collaboration, continual improvement, and celebration of wins.

  • Norwegian Red Cross striving to build a working culture based on respect, honesty and generosity.
    We do a thorough background check on relevant candidate.

opportunities.description:
Request for Proposals (RfP)

Consultancy services to support the Development of Management Plans and bylaws for Collaboratives Fisheries Management Areas (CFMAs) within Mtwara Seascape (MNAMANA, MKINAI and MNASI)

IUCN Tanzania Country Office,

Tanzania RfP Reference: IUCN-2026-July-P04809-003

Welcome to this Procurement by IUCN. You are hereby invited to submit a Proposal. Please read the information and instructions carefully because non-compliance with the instructions may result in disqualification of your Proposal from this Procurement.

1. REQUIREMENTS
1.1. A detailed description of the services and/or goods to be provided can be found in Attachment 1.

2. CONTACT DETAILS
2.1. During the course of this procurement, i.e. from the publication of this RfP to the award of a contract, you may not discuss this procurement with any IUCN employee or representative other than the following contact. You must address all correspondence and questions to the contact, including your Proposal.

IUCN Contact : dennis.mugera@iucn.org

3. PROCUREMENT TIMETABLE
3.1. This timetable is indicative and may be changed by IUCN at any time. If IUCN decides that changes to any of the deadlines are necessary, we will publish this on our website and contact you directly if you have indicated your interest in this procurement (see Section 3.2).

DATE - ACTIVITY
July 30, 2026 - Publication of the Request for Proposals
August 2, 2026 - Deadline for expressions of interest
August 4, 2026 - Deadline for submission of questions
August 6, 2026 - Planned publication of responses to questions August 16, 2026 Deadline for submission of Proposals to IUCN (“Submission Deadline”)
August 18, 2026 - Clarification of Proposals
August 21, 2026 - Planned date for contract award
August 24, 2026 - Expected contract start date

3.2. Please email the IUCN contact to express your interest in submitting a Proposal by the deadline stated above. This will help IUCN to keep you updated regarding the procurement.

4. COMPLETING AND SUBMITTING A PROPOSAL
4.1. Your Proposal must consist of the following four separate documents:
• Signed Declaration of Undertaking (see Attachment 2)
• Pre-Qualification Information (see Section 4.3 below)
• Technical Proposal (see Section 4.4 below)
• Financial Proposal (see Section 4.5 below)
Proposals must be prepared in English.

4.2. Your Proposal must be submitted by email to the IUCN Contact (see Section 2). The subject heading of the email shall be [RfP Reference – bidder name]. The bidder’s name is the name of the company/organisation on whose behalf you are submitting the Proposal, or your own surname if you are bidding as a self-employed consultant. Your Proposal must be submitted in PDF format. You may submit multiple emails suitably annotated, e.g. Email 1 of 3, if attached files are too large to suit a single email transmission. You may not submit your Proposal by uploading it to a file-sharing tool.

IMPORTANT: Submitted documents must be password-protected so that they cannot be opened and read before the submission deadline. Please use the same password for all submitted documents. After the deadline has passed and within 12 hours, please send the password to the IUCN Contact. This will ensure a secure bid submission and opening process. Please DO NOT email the password before the deadline for Proposal submission.

4.3. Pre-Qualification Criteria
IUCN will use the following Pre-Qualification Criteria to determine whether you have the capacity to provide the required goods and/or services to IUCN. Please provide the necessary information in a single, separate document.

Pre-Qualification Criteria
1. 3 relevant references of clients similar to IUCN / similar work
2. Confirm that you have all the necessary legal registrations to perform the work
3. State your annual turnover for each of the past 3 years
4. How many employees does your organisation have who are qualified for this work?

4.4. Technical Proposal
The Technical Proposal must address each of the criteria stated below explicitly and separately, quoting the relevant criteria reference number (left-hand column).
Proposals in any other format will significantly increase the time it takes to evaluate, and such Proposals may therefore be rejected at IUCN’s discretion.
Where CVs are requested, these must be of the individuals who will actually carry out the work specified. The individuals you put forward may only be substituted with IUCN’s approval.
IUCN will evaluate Technical Proposals with regards to each of the following criteria and their relative importance:

Description Information to provide Relative weight

1. Team composition and qualifications (Multidisciplinary team): - 10

Bachelor or advanced degree in Marine Science, Fisheries Management, Environmental Governance, Natural Resources Management, Biodiversity Conservation or related field.
o Relevant technical expertise (4)
o Multidisciplinary skills (2)
o Stakeholders’ engagement skills (2)
o Project management skills (2)

2. Competences: - 20

At least ten (10) years of experience in marine/coastal resource management. demonstrated and proven experience in
o Collaborative Fisheries Management Associations design and governance (5)
o Participatory community engagement (5)
o Developing marine protected area management plans and local bylaws (5)
o Strong understanding of Tanzania’s fisheries legislation (5).

3. Methodology: - 30

Description of the methodology approach to be used to deliver the work
o Understanding of the assignment (5)
o Work approach (5)
o Implementation phases (5)
o Methods and tools to undertake the assignment (10)
o Assignment management (5)

4. Work plan: -20

Working program / working schedule for delivery of deliverables
o Activities and Tasks (5)
o Timelines and Milestones (5)
o Roles and Responsibilities (5)
o Clearly stated deliverables (5)

5. Understanding of the local context: - 20

Knowledge of the Tanzania’s coastal and marine sectors and deep understanding of the collaborative fisheries management aspects and dynamics in Tanzania Mainland.
o Coastal and marine sector knowledge (5)
o Fisheries governance understanding (5)
o Collaborative fisheries management dynamics (5)
o Local challenges and opportunities (5)

TOTAL 100%

4.5. Financial Proposal
4.5.1. The Financial Proposal must be a fixed and firm price for the provision of the goods/services stated in the RfP in their entirety.
4.5.2. Prices include all costs
Submitted rates and prices are deemed to include all costs, insurances, taxes (except VAT, see below), fees, expenses, liabilities, obligations, risk and other things necessary for the performance of the Terms of Reference or Specification of Requirements. IUCN will not accept charges beyond those clearly stated in the Financial Proposal. This includes applicable withholding taxes and similar. It is your responsibility to determine whether such taxes apply to your organisation and to include them in your Financial Proposal.
4.5.3. Applicable Goods and Services Taxes
Proposal rates and prices shall be exclusive of Value Added Tax.
4.5.4. Currency of proposed rates and prices
All rates and prices submitted by Proposers shall be in Tanzania Shillings only.
4.5.5. Breakdown of rates and prices
For information only, the price needs to be broken down as follows:
Description - Quantity - Unit Price - Total Price
1. Consultancy fees
2. Travel
3. Others
TOTAL

4.6. Additional information not requested by IUCN should not be included in your Proposal and will not be considered in the evaluation.
4.7. Your Proposal must remain valid and capable of acceptance by IUCN for a period of 90 calendar days following the submission deadline.
4.8. Withdrawals and Changes
You may freely withdraw or change your Proposal at any time prior to the submission deadline by written notice to the IUCN Contact. However, in order to reduce the risk of fraud, no changes or withdrawals will be accepted after the submission deadline.
5. EVALUATION OF PROPOSALS
5.1. Completeness
IUCN will firstly check your Proposal for completeness. Incomplete Proposals will not be considered further.
5.2. Pre-Qualification Criteria
Only Proposals that meet all of the pre-qualification criteria will be evaluated.
5.3. Technical Evaluation
5.3.1. Scoring Method
Your Proposal will be assigned a score from 0 to 10 for each of the technical evaluation criteria, such that ‘0’ is low and ‘10’ is high.
5.3.2. Minimum Quality Thresholds
Proposals that receive a score of ‘0’ for any of the criteria will not be considered further.
5.3.3. Technical Score
Your score for each technical evaluation criterion will be multiplied with the respective relative weight (see Section 4.4) and these weighted scores added together to give your Proposal’s overall technical score.
5.4. Financial Evaluation and Financial Scores
The financial evaluation will be based upon the full total price you submit. Your Financial Proposal will receive a score calculated by dividing the lowest Financial Proposal that has passed the minimum quality thresholds (see Section 5.3.2) by the total price of your Financial Proposal.
Thus, for example, if your Financial Proposal is for a total of CHF 100 and the lowest Financial Proposal is CHF 80, you will receive a financial score of 80/100 = 80%
5.5. Total Score
Your Proposal’s total score will be calculated as the weighted sum of your technical score and your financial score.
The relative weights will be:
Technical: 70%
Financial: 30%
Thus, for example, if your technical score is 83% and your financial score is 77%, you will receive a total score of 83 * 70% + 77 * 30% = 58.1% + 23.1% = 81.2%.
Subject to the requirements in Sections 4 and 7, IUCN will award the contract to the bidder whose Proposal achieves the highest total score.

6. EXPLANATION OF PROCUREMENT PROCEDURE
6.1. IUCN is using the Open Procedure for this procurement. This means that the contracting opportunity is published on IUCN’s website and open to all interested parties to take part, subject to the conditions in Section 7 below.
6.2. You are welcome to ask questions or seek clarification regarding this procurement. Please email the IUCN Contact (see Section 2), taking note of the deadline for submission of questions in Section 3.1.
6.3. All Proposals must be received by the submission deadline in Section 3.1 above. Late Proposals will not be considered. All Proposals received by the submission deadline will be evaluated by a team of three or more evaluators in accordance with the evaluation criteria stated in this RfP. No other criteria will be used to evaluate Proposals. The contract will be awarded to the bidder whose Proposal received the highest Total Score. IUCN does, however, reserve the right to cancel the procurement and not award a contract at all.
6.4. IUCN will contact the bidder with the highest-scoring Proposal to finalise the contract. We will contact unsuccessful bidders after the contract has been awarded and provide detailed feedback. The timetable in Section 3.1 gives an estimate of when we expect to have completed the contract award, but this date may change depending on how long the evaluation of Proposals takes.
7. CONDITIONS FOR PARTICIPATION IN THIS PROCUREMENT
7.1. To participate in this procurement, you are required to submit a Proposal, which fully complies with the instructions in this RfP and the Attachments.
7.1.1. It is your responsibility to ensure that you have submitted a complete and fully compliant Proposal.
7.1.2. Any incomplete or incorrectly completed Proposal submission may be deemed non-compliant, and as a result you may be unable to proceed further in the procurement process.
7.1.3. IUCN will query any obvious clerical errors in your Proposal and may, at IUCN’s sole discretion, allow you to correct these, but only if doing so could not be perceived as giving you an unfair advantage.
7.2. In order to participate in this procurement, you must meet the following conditions:
• Free of conflicts of interest
• Registered on the relevant professional or trade register of the country in which you are established (or resident, if self-employed)
• In full compliance with your obligations relating to payment of social security contributions and of all applicable taxes
• Not been convicted of failing to comply with environmental regulatory requirements or other legal requirements relating to sustainability and environmental protection
• Not bankrupt or being wound up
• Never been guilty of an offence concerning your professional conduct
• Not involved in fraud, corruption, a criminal organisation, money laundering, terrorism, or any other illegal activity.
7.3. You must complete and sign the Declaration of Undertaking (see Attachment 2).
7.4. If you are participating in this procurement as a member of a joint venture, or are using sub-contractors, submit a separate Declaration of Undertaking for each member of the joint venture and sub-contractor, and be clear in your Proposal which parts of the goods/services are provided by each partner or sub-contractor.
7.5. Each bidder shall submit only one Proposal, either individually or as a partner in a joint venture. In case of joint venture, one company shall not be allowed to participate in two different joint ventures in the same procurement, nor shall a company be allowed to submit a Proposal both on its behalf and as part of a joint venture for the same procurement. A bidder who submits or participates in more than one Proposal (other than as a subcontractor or in cases of alternatives that have been permitted or requested) shall cause all the Proposals with the bidder’s participation to be disqualified.
7.6. By taking part in this procurement, you accept the conditions set out in this RfP, including the following:
• It is unacceptable to give or offer any gift or consideration to an employee or other representative of IUCN as a reward or inducement in relation to the awarding of a contract. Such action will give IUCN the right to exclude you from this and any future procurements, and to terminate any contract that may have been signed with you.
• Any attempt to obtain information from an employee or other representative of IUCN concerning another bidder will result in disqualification.
• Any price fixing or collusion with other bidders in relation to this procurement shall give IUCN the right to exclude you and any other involved bidder(s) from this and any future procurements and may constitute a criminal offence.

8. CONFIDENTIALITY AND DATA PROTECTION
8.1. IUCN follows the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). The information you submit to IUCN as part of this procurement will be treated as confidential and shared only as required to evaluate your Proposal in line with the procedure explained in this RfP, and for the maintenance of a clear audit trail. For audit purposes, IUCN is required to retain your Proposal in its entirety for 10 years after then end of the resulting contract and make this available to internal and external auditors and donors as and when requested.
8.2. In the Declaration of Undertaking (Attachment 2) you need to give IUCN express permission to use the information you submit in this way, including personal data that forms part of your Proposal. Where you include personal data of your employees (e.g. CVs) in your Proposal, you need to have written permission from those individuals to share this information with IUCN, and for IUCN to use this information as indicated in 8.1. Without these permissions, IUCN will not be able to consider your Proposal.

9. COMPLAINTS PROCEDURE
If you have a complaint or concern regarding the propriety of how a competitive process is or has been executed, then please contact procurement@iucn.org. This consultancy has the following objective(s):

The main objective of this consultancy is to facilitate the development and/or revision of management plans, action plans and bylaws for three Collaborative Fisheries Management Areas (CFMAs) in the Mtwara Seascape through an inclusive, participatory, evidence-based, and legally compliant process.

  3. Develop or revise CFMA management plans and action plans that define conservation priorities, governance arrangements, zoning systems, resource-use regulations, monitoring mechanisms, and implementation frameworks.
  4. Develop or revise CFMA bylaws aligned with relevant fisheries legislation, local government procedures, and community management needs.

About the Project

Pamoja Tuhifadhi Bahari Yetu Project is a 4-year initiative (2024 – 2028) aiming to contribute to the improved environmental protection and biodiversity conservation of the coastal and marine ecosystems in Tanzania. Funded by the European Union through the Blue Economy for job creation and climate change adaptation, the project is implemented in parts of the Mtwara, Lindi, Coast and Dar es Salaam regions (Mainland) and Unguja Island in Zanzibar. The total project budget is 11.4M Euros. The initiative will contribute to a climate-resilient Blue Economy on the Tanzanian coastal cities and ecosystems. The project implementation is led by IUCN and partnering with WWF, WCS, TNC and ForumCC.

The rampant degradation of coastal and marine ecosystems, weak land-use systems, poor governance of marine and coastal resources, high dependence on marine resources, and climate change are the most significant problems threatening the long-term productivity of Tanzania’s coastal and marine natural capital. Critical issues include coastal development; mangrove destruction; marine pollution from surface runoff and plastic waste; overfishing, damaging fishing practices and weak resources governance; targeting of juvenile and undersize fish and invertebrates (lobsters, crabs and sea cucumber); an uncoordinated and piecemeal approach to biodiversity and ecosystem-based fisheries management at the local level; poor advocacy skills and limited knowledge on environmental legislation for community conservation efforts; and unsustainable financing of coastal and marine resources.

The Bahari Yetu project’s theory of change is that the stewardship of the marine biodiversity and blue economy will be improved if: 1) science based natural resource management and governance at a landscape and seascape scale is improved; 2) economic benefits from conservation-based enterprises are increased for women and youth; 3) new technologies and approaches for increased climate resilience measures by communities are introduced and adopted; 4) knowledge management and capacity building on marine and coastal resources management (including forests) is improved; and 5) natural resource policy development, institutions, evidence-based research and monitoring and implementation are enhanced.

The project will build on the foundation and opportunities established by current and previous programs and projects, increasing focus on the well-being of rural populations, biodiversity conservation and climate action while retaining blue economy strategy implementation as its core goal. The program rationale rests on the linkage between environment and economic growth and poverty alleviation and the challenge of sustainable management of Tanzania’s biodiversity assets.

The project will align management and conservation of marine and coastal resources and demonstrate that addressing conservation and development objectives simultaneously leads to better decisions and more sustainably managed ecosystems under the Blue Economy

Description of the Assignment

Under Work Package 1 of the Bahari Yetu Project, IUCN seeks to strengthen community-based fisheries governance and biodiversity conservation through support to Collaborative Fisheries Management Areas (CFMAs) in the Mtwara Seascape.

The assignment will focus on three target Collaborative Fisheries Management Areas (CFMAs) within the Mtwara Seascape, namely: MNAMANA CFMA, comprising BMUs from Mkungu, Naumbu, Majengo, and Naumbu Kusini villages; MKINAI CFMA, comprising BMUs from Mgao, Kisiwa, Namgogoli, and Imekuwa villages; and MNASI CFMA, comprising BMUs from Msangamkuu, Namela, and Sinde villages.

The target CFMAs require either development of new management plans, action plans and bylaws or revision of existing governance instruments to align with:

  • Current ecological conditions and biodiversity priorities.
  • Fisheries and resource-use dynamics.
  • Community development priorities.
  • Existing governance and institutional arrangements; and
  • National and local legal frameworks.

The consultant will facilitate a participatory process involving Beach Management Units (BMUs), fishing communities, village leadership, district authorities, Marine Parks and Reserves Unit (MPRU), fisheries institutions, and other stakeholders.

Headquartered in Switzerland, IUCN Secretariat comprises around 1,000 staff with offices in more than 50 countries.

Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,300 Member organisations and some 10,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository
of best practices, tools and international standards.

IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development.
Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well being.

Terms of Reference for IUCN Consultancy

Title: Provision of Consultancy Service to Support the Development of Management Plans and bylaws for Collaborative Management Areas (CMAs) within North-East Unguja Seascape (T4K, KIFUMAKI and KIFUPIMUPO)

Objective of the Consultancy

This consultancy has the following objective(s):

The main objective of this consultancy is to facilitate the development and/or revision of management plans, action plans and bylaws for three Collaborative Management Areas (CMAs) in the Northeast Unguja Seascape through an inclusive, participatory, evidence-based, and legally compliant process.

Specific Objectives

The consultancy shall:

  1. Assess existing governance and management frameworks for the target CMAs, including review of management plans, action plans, bylaws, governance structures, ecological information, and institutional arrangements.
  2. Facilitate participatory stakeholder consultations with communities, Shehia Fishermen Committee (SFCs), local government authorities, fisheries institutions, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure local priorities and knowledge are reflected.
  3. Develop or revise CMA management plans and action plans that define conservation priorities, governance arrangements, zoning systems, resource-use regulations, monitoring mechanisms, and implementation frameworks.
  4. Develop or revise CMA bylaws aligned with relevant fisheries legislation, local government procedures, and community management needs.
  5. Facilitate validation and endorsement processes for management plans and bylaws with relevant community institutions and government authorities

Background

Project Reference: 04809

Donor reference: DN00140

About IUCN

IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together.

Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,400 Member organisations and around 15,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards.

IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development.

Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well-being.

www.iucn.org

https://twitter.com/IUCN/

About the Project

Pamoja Tuhifadhi Bahari Yetu Project is a 4-year initiative (2024 – 2028) aiming to contribute to the improved environmental protection and biodiversity conservation of the coastal and marine ecosystems in Tanzania. Funded by the European Union through the Blue Economy for job creation and climate change adaptation, the project is implemented in parts of the Mtwara, Lindi, Coast and Dar es Salaam regions (Mainland) and Unguja Island in Zanzibar. The total project budget is 11.4M Euros. The initiative will contribute to a climate-resilient Blue Economy on the Tanzanian coastal cities and ecosystems. The project implementation is led by IUCN and partnering with WWF, WCS, TNC and ForumCC.

The rampant degradation of coastal and marine ecosystems, weak land-use systems, poor governance of marine and coastal resources, high dependence on marine resources, and climate change are the most significant problems threatening the long-term productivity of Tanzania’s coastal and marine natural capital. Critical issues include coastal development; mangrove destruction; marine pollution from surface runoff and plastic waste; overfishing, damaging fishing practices and weak resources governance; targeting of juvenile and undersize fish and invertebrates (lobsters, crabs and sea cucumber); an uncoordinated and piecemeal approach to biodiversity and ecosystem-based fisheries management at the local level; poor advocacy skills and limited knowledge on environmental legislation for community conservation efforts; and unsustainable financing of coastal and marine resources.

The Bahari Yetu project’s theory of change is that the stewardship of the marine biodiversity and blue economy will be improved if: 1) science based natural resource management and governance at a landscape and seascape scale is improved; 2) economic benefits from conservation-based enterprises are increased for women and youth; 3) new technologies and approaches for increased climate resilience measures by communities are introduced and adopted; 4) knowledge management and capacity building on marine and coastal resources management (including forests) is improved; and 5) natural resource policy development, institutions, evidence-based research and monitoring and implementation are enhanced.

The project will build on the foundation and opportunities established by current and previous programs and projects, increasing focus on the well-being of rural populations, biodiversity conservation and climate action while retaining blue economy strategy implementation as its core goal. The program rationale rests on the linkage between environment and economic growth and poverty alleviation and the challenge of sustainable management of Tanzania’s biodiversity assets.

The project will align management and conservation of marine and coastal resources and demonstrate that addressing conservation and development objectives simultaneously leads to better decisions and more sustainably managed ecosystems under the Blue Economy.

Description of the Assignment

Under Work Package 1 of the Bahari Yetu Project, IUCN seeks to strengthen community-based fisheries governance and biodiversity conservation through support to Collaborative Management Areas (CMAs) in the Northeast Unguja Seascape.

The assignment will focus on three target Collaborative Management Areas (CMAs) within the Northeast Unguja Seascape, namely: T4K CMA, comprising SFCs from Tazari, Kidoti, Kilimani, Kendwa and Kigunda villages; KIFUPIMUPO CMA, comprising SFCs from Kivunge, Fukuchani, Pita na Zako, Muwange and Potoa villages; and KIFUMAKI CMA, comprising SFCs from Kiombamvua, Fujoni, Mangapwani and Kidanzini villages.

The target CMAs require either development of new management plans, action plans and bylaws or revision of existing governance instruments to align with:

  • Current ecological conditions and biodiversity priorities.
  • Fisheries and resource-use dynamics.
  • Community development priorities.
  • Existing governance and institutional arrangements; and
  • National and local legal frameworks.

The consultant will facilitate a participatory consultative process involving Shehia Fishermen Committee (SFCs), fishing communities, village leadership, district authorities, Department of Marine Conservation Marine (DMC), fisheries institutions, and other stakeholders.

Duration of the Assignment

From 14th September 2026 to 21st November 2026

Deliverables and Activities

The consultant will provide the following deliverables and carry out the following activities:

Deliverable/Activity - Description - Deadline

Inception Report - September 17, 2026

The consultant shall:

  1. Conduct an inception meeting with IUCN, Department of Marine Conservation (DMC-TUMCA), district authorities, and relevant partners.
  2. Review project documents, existing management plans, action plans, bylaws, CMA guidelines, ecological information, fisheries management frameworks, and legal requirements.
  3. Prepare Inception Report outlining:
    • Detailed methodology.
    • Stakeholder engagement strategy.
    • Workplan and timeline.
    • Data collection methods.
    • Consultation approach.

Stakeholder Consultations and Field Assessments Report - September 28, 2026

The consultant shall conduct participatory consultations and field visits to the target CMAs.

Stakeholders shall include:

  1. Shehia Fisheries Committees (SFCs)
  2. Community fishers and resource users
  3. Village leadership
  4. District and local government authorities
  5. Fisheries departments
  6. Department of Marine Conservation (DMC)
  7. Civil society organizations and relevant stakeholders

Participatory methods may include:

  • Focus group discussions.

Gender, youth, and vulnerable groups shall be meaningfully represented during consultations.

Developed/Revised CMA Management Plans and action plans - October 5, 2026

The consultant shall prepare or revise three management plans.

Each plan shall include:

  1. Background and contextual analysis.
  2. Ecological and biodiversity profile.
  3. Fisheries and resource-use assessment.
  4. Threat and vulnerability analysis.
  5. Vision, goals, and management objectives.
  6. Governance structure and institutional roles.
  7. Zoning framework and allowable activities.
  8. Compliance and enforcement mechanisms.
  9. Monitoring, evaluation, and learning framework.
  10. Financing and sustainability mechanisms.
  11. Climate resilience considerations.
  12. Gender and social inclusion considerations.

Developed /Revised CMA Bylaws - October 15, 2026

The consultant shall:

  1. Review existing bylaws where applicable.
  2. Facilitate community consultations.
  3. Develop or revise bylaws aligned with:
    • Fisheries Act and related regulations.
    • Local Government laws.
    • District approval procedures.

Prepare legally compliant draft bylaws for submission to relevant authorities

Validation report - November 23, 2026

The consultant shall:

  1. Facilitate validation workshops.
  2. Incorporate stakeholder comments.
  3. Finalize management plans and bylaws.
  4. Provide technical support for endorsement procedures.

Payment Schedule

The Timetable below summarises the chronological order of deliverables and indicates milestones at which IUCN will pay the Consultant.

  1. Approved Inception Report - 20%
  2. Submission of Stakeholder Consultations and Field Assessments Report - 30%
  3. Development/Revision of CFMA Management Plans and action plans - 15%
  4. Development/Revision of CFMA Bylaws - 15%
  5. Validation and Submission of the approved final Management Plans and Bylaws - 20%

Skills and Experience

  1. Minimum of a master’s degree in marine science, Fisheries Management, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Governance, Biodiversity Conservation, or related discipline.
  2. A bachelor’s degree with substantial demonstrated experience may be considered.
  3. At least ten (10) years of relevant experience in coastal and marine resource management.
  4. Demonstrated experience in:
    • Collaborative fisheries governance.
    • Development of fisheries or marine protected area management plans.
    • Drafting local governance bylaws.
    • Participatory stakeholder engagement.
    • Community-based conservation planning.
  5. Strong knowledge of Tanzania Mainland Fisheries legislation.
  6. Understanding of district bylaw approval procedures.
  7. Excellent facilitation skills.
  8. Fluency in English and Kiswahili.

Supervision and coordination

The consultant will report to and work under the supervision of Chief of Party, Bahari Yetu Project – IUCN Tanzania.
