opportunities.title: HR Officer
opportunities.description:
Human Resources Officer

Full time

Kampala

On-Site

40% field travel

About Alight

Alight is a proximity-driven humanitarian organization that restores power and agency to people experiencing displacement. For nearly 50 years, we’ve walked alongside our customers – displaced communities – in some of the most challenging and complex places in the world. Regardless of role or responsibility in this organization, we center the choices, dignity, and lived experience of people we serve – even when it complicates the work. We live our values at each step of our shared journey. At our best, our commitment to displaced people is sustained, relational, and grounded in trust.

Enterprise Summary

Alight is a long-standing humanitarian response partner and has been operational in Uganda since 1994. Our operation in Uganda serves the displaced and host communities in three Operational Regions (South-West, Mid-West, West Nile). In July 2026, the Uganda and Rwanda Enterprises consolidated into one Enterprise with the focus on aligning the programming and continuing to provide consistent, high-quality support to refugee customers.

Role Purpose

The Human Resources Officer is responsible for the day-to-day running of the Human Resource department in the Uganda Enterprise under the guidance of the Enterprise Head of HR. The HR Officer provides general and routine HR support to staff in-country by ensuring all staff feel efficiently supported. They will also champion the organization's culture and values, helping staff understand what the values mean in day-to-day work The HR Officer is also part of the broader Office of the People team within Alight that ensure Alight attracts, develops, deploys, and sustains the talent it needs across complex and evolving contexts.

The Human Resource Officer performs the following duties/responsibilities:

Human Resources Administration

  • Proactively manage all HR correspondences such as recommendations, bank letters, certificate of service, etc.
  • Support staff with leave planning and make sure plans are completed and ifollowed.
  • Coordinate with IT to set up email accounts and mailing-list access for new staff, and to deactivate accounts for staff who leave.
  • Ensure up to date records management of all staff documentation
  • Manage staff clearance processes and ensure payment of terminal benefits within policy.
  • Preparing and track offer letters and employment contracts.
  • Walk staff through their benefits package and oversee its administration.
  • Update and share staff lists with OOP monthly.

Recruitment and Selection:

  • Initiate and coordinate with hiring managers all the recruitment requests and hiring procedures in line with Alight recruitment policy.
  • Prepare and post all job advertisements for all vacant positions in appropriate channels and ensure wide and appropriate distribution.
  • Maintain an organized recruitment resource database and share updates of the recruitment status
  • Conduct all mandatory recruitment checks and ensure that they are on file for example reference background checks, sam.bridger checks etc.

Payroll and statutory Compliance:

  • Ensure that the Uganda Country programme complies with all Standard Operating Procedures of HR best practices and in accordance with Uganda’s employment act, liaising with the Alight Uganda Labor Attorney and other government bodies as needed.
  • Work closely with all teams across the program to maintain compliance with organisation’s policies and procedures.
  • Timely collate and share monthly payroll updates with finance team for payroll processing
  • Support in resolving payroll-related queries while maintaining confidentiality.

Performance management

  • Support in coordinating timely performance appraisals and maintain an updated PME database for all staff in coordination with HR team.
  • Liaise with supervisors to ensure that performance evaluations for all staff are conducted on time and review all evaluations to ensure quality and consistency.
  • Collate training needs from the PME and ensure that they are captured in the Annual learning and development plan.

Health Insurance management

  • Coordinate the national staff health insurance scheme ensuring timely and accurate reports from the service provider.
  • Ensure all staff and eligible dependents are registered on to the medical insurance scheme, monitor staff medical coverage and ensure that the scheme is running smoothly.
  • Liaise with the health service provider to resolve any issues with the services.
  • Follow up on all medical insurance matters for staff including adding and deleting staff to/from the employer’s liability and the medical and hospitalization insurance policy schemes as well as follow up on payments and claims.

Exit Management

  • Process and track all termination paperwork including preparation of termination notice letters in relation to closing grants and restructuring.
  • Track staff clearance and terminal benefit payments through to completion.
  • Work with supervisors to offer exit interviews and capture the data to support a reflective, learning-oriented program.
  • Remove departing staff from the health, GPA, and life insurance schemes, and collect their IDs and insurance cards.

Employee Relations and Staff Wellbeing

  • Monitor and advise on disciplinary matters in accordance with established policies and procedures and Uganda Labor Law
  • Reinforce staff complaint mechanism system that instills staff confidence through ensuring fair, transparent, confidential, and independent investigation processes.
  • Mediate conflict, grievances, and other complaints in accordance with HR policies and procedures and withing Uganda Labor Law.
  • Proactively identify opportunities to enhance the employee experience and help develop and implement innovative solutions and policies

Perform any other duties as assigned.

Education & Experience

  • A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Human Resources Management or related field. A Post Graduate Diploma in HRM is an added advantage.
  • At least 5 years’ HR experience working in a generalist role.
  • Experience working in, and demonstrate comfort with a fast paced, changing environment with skill and ability to balancing and drive for results while remaining human centered.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities

  • Proven skills in the full range of general HR needs including data management, administration, recruitment, pay and employee relations
  • Good understanding of Uganda Employment laws, statutory and tax requirements.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • High level of accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Excellent planning, organizational, and time management skills.
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Strong leadership and coaching skills.
  • High level of integrity, accountability, and confidentiality.
  • Ability to initiate and drive efforts forward with little, to no daily oversight and a high degree of comfort with ambiguity and working in a fluid country context.

Values Alignment

You are curious and truly listen. You appreciate the complexities of human beings. You ask questions, seek information, and dig deeper into understanding a problem holistically before working to solve it. You enter a space with humility and an eagerness to learn.

You believe shared ownership creates better outcomes. You trust displaced customers to guide the way forward. You’re open to new and different possibilities, are motivated in what an abundant future could hold, and you generate ideas sparked from insight – and foster spaces that are safe for others to generate their ideas too. You bring others in, build ecosystems, and share power with those who care about this more than you do. You adapt your work to make space for others.

You embrace transformation. You recognize and honor that our work centers people – a constantly changing and complex customer within a constantly changing and complex world. And so too, we must constantly change. You believe in the abundance of human beings and you understand that to unleash that abundance, we must bravely enter a bold new chapter capable of transforming the future.

You value beauty. You believe a meaningful life includes joy, dignity, and connection. You place weight on the experience people have – of a place, a space, a person, a service. You strive to create things that are human-worthy and you believe quality should be determined by those experiencing it.

Benefits

  • Borderless Team of 2,500 staff worldwide that sees possibility, celebrates moments of abundance, shares new ideas, and strives to do a better thing every day.
  • Learning & Development – Access hundreds of free online learning courses to take at your own pace and tailor to your professional goals.
  • Flexible Leave Time – Between vacation days, personal leave days, and holidays, you have ample opportunities to take time off when you need it.

Applications accepted through August 5, 2026.

Alight is an Equal Opportunity Employer offering employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, citizenship, physical or mental disability, or protected veteran status. Alight complies with all applicable laws governing nondiscrimination in employment.

opportunities.title: Individual Consultant – Education Information Systems (ClassMap) Community of Practice and Learning Assessment Coordinator
opportunities.publisher: UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
opportunities.description:
Call for Consultancy

Individual Consultant – Education Information Systems (ClassMap) Community of Practice and Learning Assessment Coordinator

System Transformation Grant (STG)

Date Issued: 10 July 2026

Parent Sector: UNESCO Antenna Office in Yangon, Myanmar

Duty Station: Yangon, Myanmar

Job Family: Education

Type of Contract: Non Staff – Individual Consultant (Form HR 13-2)

Duration of Contract: 11 months

Recruitment Open To: External candidates

Application Deadline: 30 July 2026 17:00 Hours Yangon time

UNESCO Core Values: Commitment to the Organization, Integrity, Respect for Diversity, Professionalism

1. Background:

Under the Global Partnership for Education (GPE), System Transformation Grant (STG), UNESCO Myanmar is implementing activities towards the attainment of the overall objective of the programme: to ensure that children across Myanmar, including those facing barriers to learning, have access to quality, inclusive education in safe and protective learning spaces, supported by strong community and partner engagement as well as targeted evidence generation and dissemination. This programme is organized around three key drivers of learning:

1. Access: Ensuring safe and equitable access to learning for all children and youth;

2. Quality: Strengthening quality teaching and learning through improved resources and capacity building; and

3. System Strengthening: Enhancing education system management, coordination, and monitoring.

As part of this programme, UNESCO Myanmar developed ClassMap, a school management, school development plan submission, and attendance tracking platform currently mapping 296 community schools across 12 states and regions. To ensure the continued, active, and meaningful use of ClassMap by participating schools as well as additional schools to be onboarded under STG, UNESCO Myanmar has adopted the ClassMap Sustainability Plan, which establishes a structured framework for monitoring, peer engagement, recognition, technical support, and continuous communication between UNESCO, implementing partners, and schools.

A central pillar of the Sustainability Plan is the establishment of a ClassMap Community of Practice, connecting school heads, focal teachers, UNESCO, and project partners around thematic areas critical to school functioning and resilience, alongside a monitoring, analytics, and feedback framework to track platform usage and school-level learning outcomes. Additionally, UNESCO also aims to promote peer learning and communities of practices among schools sharing experience, challenges and good practices through community groups. In parallel, UNESCO continues to coordinate learning assessment activities initiated under the previous GPE programme to support evidence generation, monitoring, and continuous improvement of education quality. To support these complementary areas of work, UNESCO seeks a consultant to lead the implementation of the ClassMap Sustainability Plan while also providing technical support for the coordination of learning assessment activities under the GPE STG programme.

2. PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The Individual Consultant is sought to coordinate and facilitate the ClassMap Community of Practice, design and deliver bite-size learning packages across four thematic areas such as School Planning, Basic Data Literacy, Risk Management, Climate and Disaster Risk Reduction Preparedness and Digital Literacy, and support learning assessment and data monitoring functions under the ClassMap Sustainability Plan. Working closely with the UNESCO Education team and implementing partners, the Consultant will contribute to building an active, well-informed network of ClassMap schools and ensure that engagement translates into measurable improvements in school planning, disaster preparedness, and platform data quality. The consultant will also be responsible for supporting the coordination of baseline and endline learning assessments across 100 schools in Sagaing and Rakhine, working closely with the contracted partner.

3. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Supervisory arrangements:

Under the overall authority of the Regional Director of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) Regional Office in Bangkok and the Office for UN Coordination in Asia and the Pacific, the direct supervision of the Head of the UNESCO Antenna Project Office in Yangon, and in close collaboration with the GPE STG Project Officer, the Individual Consultant will be engaged to coordinate the ClassMap Community of Practice and support learning assessment activities through the implementation of the following tasks:

1. Community of Practice Design and Content Development

  • Discuss with the UNESCO Education team to map out topics, formats, and timelines for bite-size learning packages across the four thematic areas;
  • Conduct consultative meetings with school heads and focal teachers to understand priorities and learning needs;
  • Develop bite-size learning packages, short guides, and micro-learning content for each thematic area - School Planning, Risk Management, Climate and Disaster Risk Reduction Preparedness and Digital Literacy – drawing on content available from the Myanmar Teacher Platform and other relevant sources.

2. Facilitation and Engagement of the ClassMap Community of Practice

  • Coordinate the ClassMap Digital Community of Practice (Telegram/Viber and in-platform School Community Network), including thematic sub-groups and prioritizing the safety of participants engaged in these groups;
  • Moderate discussions, respond to queries, and share tips, reminders, and success stories in community groups;
  • Plan and facilitate learning events (in-person workshops, webinars, orientations, refresher trainings) aligned with the Sustainability Plan's capacity-building and engagement calendar;
  • Support delivery of engagement campaigns and challenges (e.g. school recognition, data quality, and improvement campaigns) in coordination with the UNESCO team;

3. Learning Assessment and Data Monitoring

  • Support the planning, preparation and coordination of learning assessment implementation, including developing schedules, performing quality control, document review and translation.
  • Liaise with UNESCO implementing partners, STG Grant Agents and the contractor to ensure smooth coordination of the learning assessment and monitoring activities. This includes attending relevant meetings with partners and contractors
  • Conduct data verification and provide feedback to the contractor; review draft learning assessment reports and collate UNESCO’s technical feedback.
  • Support monthly monitoring of ClassMap usage and school classification (Active, Partially Active, Non-active, Dormant) in line with the Sustainability Plan's monitoring timeline;
  • Contribute to routine data quality checks, identifying gaps in attendance records, activity reports, and school profiles.

4. Documentation and Reporting

  • Prepare monthly engagement report including participation, package delivery, and challenges, and learning assessment coordination report including assessment outcomes.
  • Compile and share user feedback with the UNESCO team to support continuous improvement of the Community of Practice and ClassMap platform;
  • Maintain up-to-date records of activities and deliverables, and participate in regular UNESCO team meetings to provide updates;

In line with UNESCO’s overall gender mainstreaming strategy, the individual specialist is expected to integrate a gender perspective in all activities and apply gender analysis and mainstreaming concepts whenever feasible.

Travel:

The Individual Specialist will be based in UNESCO Antenna Office in Yangon during the contract period. No travel outside Yangon is anticipated.

4. TIMETABLE AND DELIVERABLES

Deliverables

The individual specialist will submit the following deliverables within the designated timeline. All deliverables must be submitted with original, editable files, as well as high-resolution versions of final products (if applicable) to UNESCO. The assigned tasks must be submitted by the following deadlines.

  1. Submit an inception work plan mapping Community of Practice engagement activities across the contract period, including risk management approach by 31/8/2026
  2. Submit a draft outline of topics to be covered under each thematic area - School Planning, Basic Data Literacy, Risk Management, Climate and Disaster Risk Reduction Preparedness, and Digital Literacy- including proposed approaches for delivering bite-sized learning content by 30/9/2026
  3. Submit the engagement and coordination report for October 2026, including Community of Practice activities, and challenges by 30 /10/2026
  4. Submit the engagement and coordination report for November 2026, including Community of Practice activities, and challenges by 30/11/2026
  5. Submit the engagement and coordination report for December 2026, including Community of Practice activities, and challenges by 31/12/2026
  6. Submit a report mapping lessons learned, good practices, challenges and recommendations by 29/1/2027
  7. Submit the engagement and coordination report for February 2026, including Community of Practice activities, and challenges by 26/2/2027
  8. Submit the engagement and coordination report for March 2027, including Community of Practice activities, and challenges by 31/3/2027
  9. Submit the engagement and coordination report for April 2027, including Community of Practice activities, and challenges by 30/4/2027
  10. Submit the engagement and coordination report for May 2027, including Community of Practice activities, and challenges by 31/5/2027
  11. Submit a final report outlining the number of schools and educators reached, learning assessment outcomes, key achievements and challenges encountered during the contract period by 30/6/2027

COMPETENCIES (Core / Managerial)

Accountability (C)

Innovation (C)

Knowledge sharing and continuous improvement (C)

Planning and organizing (C)

Teamwork (C)

Results focus (C)

For detailed information, please consult the UNESCO Competency Framework

Education

  • Advanced university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in Education, Communication, Social Sciences, Development Studies, or a related field.
  • A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s) with an additional five years of relevant experience may be accepted in lieu of an advanced degree.

Work Experience

Skills/Competencies

opportunities.title: Terms of reference for a training on participatory public policy review
opportunities.country: Kenya, Uganda, United Republic of Tanzania
opportunities.description:
Background

horizont3000 is an Austrian non-governmental organisation for sustainable development cooperation. Constituted by 11 grassroots organisations of the Catholic Church, horizont3000’s core instruments are co-financing, advisory and knowledge management. We work with almost 100 partner organisations, most of them are in four focus regions/countries East Africa, Mozambique, Senegal and Central America. In our two sectors Human Rights & Civil Society and Sustainable Livelihoods, the focus is on Gender Equality, Climate Action and Policy Dialogue with over 2 million people participating in over 180 projects.

One of the projects being implemented in East Africa by horizont3000 is Policy Dialogue with support from Austrian Development Agency (ADA). The project goal is to enhance civil society organisations’ (CSOs’) Effectiveness in Policy Dialogue and in the long term realize inclusive, responsive, representative and effective policies that reflect the aspirations and will of the community affected by a particular policy problem across levels. This project has made significant contributions for the past 4 years by capacitating partner organisations to effectively engage in Policy Dialogue.

A major pillar of the Policy Dialogue East Africa project is enhancing capacity of partner organisations for effective participation in all the 4 phases of policy cycle namely; agenda setting, policy formation, policy implementation and policy review. This is being accomplished through physical and virtual mentorship and coaching, individual and joint trainings and a regional sharing event; where all Partners in the Policy Dialogue project discuss their activities and experiences within a previously set topic or area of work in order to learn and improve their practice.

The regional sharing event is planned for August 2026 on Tuesday 11th and Wednesday 12th in Dares salaam-Tanzania. This two (2) days event will be split into; one day dedicated for the session on policy review and experience sharing from policy experts and one day specifically dedicated for partners to share policy dialogue successes and challenges from 2023 to 2026 and how they have managed to over the challenges encountered.

Against this background, horizont3000 is seeking for services of a qualified service provider (consultant) to design and deliver training on participatory public policy review with a focus on participatory policy monitoring and evaluation and accountability.

Purpose of the training and follow up support

The main purpose of this training in to enhance the capacity of Policy Dialogue East Africa project partners in policy dialogue through increased knowledge and skills in policy review for participatory and gender responsive policies in East Africa.

Specific objectives of the training

  1. To strengthen participants knowledge and skills on participatory and gender responsive policy reviews to ensure that the targeted policy is dealing with the identified policy issues and that the tagged government budget and spending is effectively implemented as planned
  2. To guide participants and jointly develop participatory and gender-responsive policy review frameworks and tools for strategic planning and policy making by improving the links between policy interventions and their outcomes & impact

Focus of the consultancy

The consultant(s) shall deliver one training divided into sub-topics as outlined below:

  1. Understanding public policies
  • Introduction to public policy formation and implementation frameworks focusing on history, principles, concepts and institutions.
  • The roles that policies play in national development and types of public policies.
  1. Introduction to participatory public policy review
  • policy monitoring versus policy evaluation and accountability
  • objectives and practical tools and frameworks for participatory policy monitoring and evaluation.
  • rationale for public policy monitoring and evaluation
  1. Steps for conducting successful participatory public policy monitoring and evaluation
  • Determining the public policies to be implemented and monitored
  • Developing standards for implementing and monitoring public policies
  • Collecting and analysing data on public policies
  • Measuring performance of policy implementation
  • Comparing actual performance of policy implementation and set public policy performance standards
  • Detecting any public policy performance deviations.
  • Finding out reasons why there is such public policy performance deviations.
  • Doing public policy performance corrective action
  1. Monitoring of public resource acquisition and allocation and the tracking of performance resulting from such allocations.
  • Key parameters and commitments (Baseline)-key programmes and departments and what was promised vs. what was allocated.
  • Audit processes (Data Collection)-Routine source verification and reconciliation of commitments
  • Value proposition (Following the money)
  • Outputs (What happens on the ground & gaps)
  • Outcome (Who benefits and how)
  1. Joint reflection on the common challenges in policy review and developing joint actions to overcome those challenges.
  2. Joint development of practical tools and frameworks for participatory policy monitoring and evaluation and accountability.

Methodology and target participants

The training will be conducted in person with approximately 30-35 participants from civil society organizations operating in diverse political and environmental contexts.The consultant(s) must use participatory learning approaches, gender-responsive training methods outlined in the proposal, ensuring participants can relate the topics to their organizational realities and facilitate peer exchange.

Expectation from horizont3000

  • Providing and catering for all cost of the training venue
  • Provide technical and administrative support, including assistance in mobilizing relevant participants, ppt presentation and other presentation equipment
  • Provide all the necessary data and information required by the consultant(s) to ensure the training is successful

Deliverables

The following are some of the deliverables expected from the successful coach/consultant(s);

  • Develop needs-based training programs based on the East African civil society context – to be approved at least 2 weeks in advance of the training
  • Deliver in person training targeting about 30-35 participants from approx. 15 organisations with various backgrounds in policy dialogue
  • Practical tools and frameworks developed for participatory policy monitoring and evaluation and accountability.
  • Submit all the approved training materials, templates, recordings and related documents and reporting notes to horizont3000 for filing
  • Depending on the country of residence of the selected trainer, horizotn3000 will cater for accommodation and food at the venue.

Budget

Interested consultant(s) are invited to submit technical proposal demonstrating their understanding and delivery of the assignment and financial proposal that includes their fees, taxes, and any other relevant expenses associated with the consultancy. The total budget for this consultancy should not exceed One Thousand United States Dollars ($1000) inclusive of all taxes.

Skills and Qualification of the consultant(s)

The assignment will be awarded to an experienced trainer (coach) with clearly demonstrated knowledge and diverse experience in participatory monitoring and evaluation of gender policies.In terms of years of experience, the lead consultant/trainer must have a minimum of 5 years of experience in handling similar trainings for international and indigenous civil society organisations.

More specifically;

  • Deeper understanding of the concept of policy dialogue
  • Proven track record and experience in delivering training workshops for civil society organisations on the topics highlighted above in any of the East African countries where horizont3000 operates.
  • Proven experience and tangible results on the trainings delivered on the topics highlighted above.
  • Fluency in Swahili is an added advantage

Additional consideration

  • Applications without supporting documents may be treated as incomplete and may not be considered for further assessment.
  • horizont3000 is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. The organisation recruits’ consultants regardless of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, ability, national origin, or any other basis covered by appropriate law.
  • All consultancies at horizont3000 is decided on the basis of qualifications, competence, integrity and organizational need.
  • horizont3000 has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of horizont3000, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination. The selected consultant(s) will be expected to adhere to all horizont3000’s policies and standard operating procedures.
  • Female qualified candidates are highly encouraged to apply for this consultancy opportunity.

opportunities.title: Senior Assessment Officer - PHU for OPT, Based in Amman
opportunities.description:
BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis, GIS and remote sensing. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO with headquarters based in Paris and presence in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, which allows IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support in its fields of intervention.

We are currently looking for a Senior Assessment Officer to support our team in Amman

Position: Senior Assessment Officer (Public Health)

Contract duration: 6 months, pending funding confirmation

Starting Date: 1 August 2026

Location: Amman

COUNTRY PROFILE

The humanitarian situation in the occupied Palestinian territories (oPt) has reached dire levels, particularly in the Gaza Strip, where ongoing hostilities have resulted in mass displacement, the collapse of basic services, and a near-total breakdown of civilian infrastructure. With 2.2 million people affected, access to food, water, healthcare, and shelter remains critically limited. The scale of destruction and access constraints have created an environment where humanitarian needs far exceed available resources. At the same time, rising tensions and violence in the West Bank have severely impacted freedom of movement, livelihoods, and overall humanitarian conditions.

In response, IMPACT Initiatives is implementing a range of activities to support a needs-based, evidence-driven humanitarian response. This includes multi-sectoral household assessments, displacement site mapping, and market assessments across Gaza to inform coordination, operational planning, and strategic decision-making.

POSITION PROFILE

Under the supervision of the Research Manager, the Senior Assessment Officer (SAO) will support the implementation of IMPACT’s public health-focused research portfolio in the occupied Palestinian territory (oPt). This includes data collection, analysis, reporting, and dissemination across topics such as food security, WASH, nutrition, and health. The SAO will bring a public health background and contribute to sector-specific and multi-sectoral assessments, including household-level research, with a focus on producing timely and actionable analysis to inform the humanitarian response.

The SAO must demonstrate strong analytical skills, including the ability to critically assess complex datasets, identify key trends, draw meaningful conclusions, and translate findings into clear and compelling insights for humanitarian actors. Strong writing, visualization, and presentation skills are essential, as is the ability to tailor messaging for diverse audiences, and guiding team members in strengthening analytical approaches across research cycles.

The ideal candidate will combine strong technical assessment experience with a solid understanding of public health issues in crisis contexts, paired with creativity, independence, and critical thinking. They must also be highly adaptable and comfortable working in a fast-paced, unpredictable humanitarian environment, where flexibility and responsiveness are key to ensuring relevant and impactful research.

RESPONSIBILITIES

The Senior Assessment Officer’s responsibilities include:

RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS LEADERSHIP

  • Leading analytical workstreams related to public health, food security, WASH, and nutrition in Gaza, ensuring findings directly inform humanitarian planning and response.
  • Managing the full research cycle, including research design, tool development, data collection, in-depth analysis, and production of outputs (briefs, factsheets, reports).
  • Translating complex data into clear, meaningful, and actionable insights for diverse humanitarian audiences.
  • Ensuring research integrates both primary and secondary data and is methodologically sound, contextually relevant, and responsive to partner needs.

CONTEXTUAL UNDERSTANDING

  • Closely monitoring developments in Gaza to ensure research is adapted to the fast-evolving operational environment.
  • Maintaining a strong understanding of local humanitarian needs, access dynamics, and operational challenges to contextualize findings.

CAPACITY BUILDING AND TEAM MANAGEMENT

  • Supporting team members in strengthening analytical thinking and writing skills, including through mentoring, feedback, and trainings.
  • Directly supervising assessment staff working on public health and multi-sectoral research streams.
  • Fostering a collaborative, analytical culture within the team.

STRATEGIC COORDINATION

  • Liaising with HQ focal points and supporting coordination across units and thematic workstreams in oPt.
  • Supporting the Research Manager in strategic planning, proposal development, and the integration of analysis across the mission’s research portfolio.
  • Representing IMPACT/REACH in external coordination platforms and technical working groups (eg., health, nutrition, Food Security).
  • Leading on the presentation and dissemination of analytical findings to key stakeholders, ensuring engagement with evidence to inform decision-making.

The Senior Assessment Officer will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners, or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Years of work experience 3 years of relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as assessments, monitoring and evaluation, research design and analysis, etc.;
  • Research and analysis skills Strong quantitative and qualitative analysis skills, with experience interpreting complex data and producing clear insights. Proficient in statistical tools and thematic analysis, with the ability to identify trends, contextualize findings, and communicate them effectively to diverse humanitarian audiences;
  • Proven experience working on public health-related research, including topics such as food security, nutrition, WASH, health access, and communicable disease risks in humanitarian settings. Familiarity with public health indicators and needs assessments. Ability to interpret data through a public health lens;
  • Sound judgment and emotional intelligence in high-pressure or sensitive situations. Possesses strong interpersonal awareness and the ability to respond constructively to feedback and shifting priorities;
  • Familiarity with aid system Good understanding of the aid system and the research community. Prior experience with humanitarian coordination forums preferred;
  • Communication/reporting skills Excellent verbal and written communication and drafting skills for effective reporting required;
  • Academic qualifications Excellent academic qualifications, including a master’s degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline (e.g. international studies, development, humanitarian response, data science, political science, etc.);
  • Software skills Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software an asset
  • Experience in geographical region Past experience in the region is desirable;
  • Language skills Fluency in English required, competency in Arabic is an asset.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

  • For this position, salary between 2’580 CHF and 2’640 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
  • Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
  • Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance.
  • Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
  • Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
  • Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
  • Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training;
  • IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

opportunities.title: Community-based Protection Officer-Der Ezzor
opportunities.description:
Background/IRC Summary: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Job Overview/Summary: Community-based protection Officer oversees the day-to-day implementation of IRC’s Community-based protection interventions in Jazret Elbuhameed, through community dialogues, and social activities and the establishment of community-based committees for conflict resolution, negotiations, and mediation to promote peaceful coexistence and social cohesion. He/she ensures the meaningful participation of IDPs and Host communities in all aspects of community-based protection response by IRC. This includes ensuring effective community mobilization, enhancing community-based protection and promoting community development activities in line with set guidelines and standards and with due attention to the engagement or inclusion of persons with specific needs. He/she will provide day-to-day direct supervision to community-based protection mobilizers and community committees volunteers and ensure that close collaboration is maintained with staff involved in direct implementation of IRC’s programs. He/she will be responsible for providing direct support for the implementation of the protection outreach program. This will include capacity building and day-to-day supervision and support to the community engagement volunteers. The Community Engagement Officer will also coordinate the activities of the community engagement volunteers as well as the PSN focal points in the protection committees, providing information materials and holding meetings.

  • Major Responsibilities: Major responsibilities of the Community-based Protection Officer (not exhaustive) are listed below:
  1. Support the partner in following up on community-based protection committees and contribute to maintaining their functionality and sustainability.
  2. Participate in reviewing assessment findings conducted by the partner and contribute to contextual analysis of community needs, vulnerabilities, and conflict dynamics.
  3. Assist in the implementation and follow-up of social cohesion and peacebuilding activities carried out by the partner.
  4. Accompany and support partner-led dialogue and mediation activities, ensuring adherence to basic protection and do-no-harm principles.
  5. Coordinate on a regular basis with community representatives, local authorities, and stakeholders to facilitate smooth implementation of partner activities.
  6. Contribute to training and coaching provided to community members and committees, particularly in conflict resolution and community engagement.
  7. Follow up on referrals raised by community protection committees and support the partner in ensuring proper documentation and tracking.
  8. Support coordination with other sectors to promote integrated service delivery at community level.
  9. Assist in awareness-raising activities and ensure messaging aligns with protection and program priorities.
  10. Contribute to data collection, verification, and routine reporting on community dynamics, activities, and outcomes.
  11. Provide day-to-day technical support and on-the-job coaching to partner staff to strengthen the quality of implementation.
  12. Document success stories, best practices, and lessons learned through regular follow-up with the partner, and contribute to capturing program impact and learning.

Community Protection Systems Strengthening & Sustainability

  1. Shift from broad awareness activities to targeted follow-up and strengthening existing community-based protection systems.
  2. Support the sustainability of protection committees and community groups (especially women- and youth-led groups) and ensure their continued function beyond project completion.
  3. Establish and strengthen continuity mechanisms for vulnerable groups after the program ends.

Referral & Coordination Oversight

  1. Oversee referral pathways to ensure effectiveness, continuity, and proper coordination with partners and service providers.
  2. Work closely with the partner to ensure gradual handover of responsibilities and knowledge transfer.

Data Validation, Compliance & Reporting

  1. Verify beneficiary data and ensure its accuracy and reliability.
  2. Manage documentation and archiving in line with donor (BMZ) requirements.
  3. Prepare impact reports, closure reports, and ensure full compliance with donor regulations and requirements.

Program Closure & Transition Planning

  1. Support final evaluations and lessons learned exercises.
  2. Lead or contribute to closure planning, ensuring safe and structured transition of activities to partners or communities.
  3. Ensure protection mainstreaming is integrated across remaining program activities.

General

  • Perform any other duties as required by program needs or as requested by the supervisor.

Key Working Relationships:

  • Position Reports to: Child Protection Senior Manager.
  • Position directly supervises: Community-based Protection Mobilizer – local partner activities.
  • Indirect Reporting: RISE Manager
  • Other Internal and/or external contacts:
  • Internal: Protection Officers, Legal Snr. Officer, WPE, and CP teams, ERD team. IP senior managers, RISE manager
  • External: INGOs, local actors

Job Requirements:

Education:

  • A bachelor's degree in social work, international relations, human rights, community development, or any other university degree.

Work Experience:

  • Proven experience in community engagement, social cohesion, conflict resolution, community-based protection, protection activities, or humanitarian work.
  • 2-4 years experience.

opportunities.title: Terms of Reference for a consultant to conduct an online training on documenting stories of change for selected partner organisations under the ADA Fr
opportunities.description:
Background

horizont3000 is an Austrian non-governmental organisation working in sustainable development cooperation. Based in Vienna, with offices in the four focus areas East Africa, Central America, Senegal and Mozambique, we are backed by eleven Austrian Catholic grassroots organisations.

We support partner organisations (POs) and locally-led initiatives through co-financing based on grant schemes, medium to long-term advisory services and knowledge management to facilitate learning and sharing processes. Our projects and programmes are embedded in two main sectors, Human Rights & Civil Society and Sustainable Livelihoods, with a focus on Gender Equality, Climate Action and Policy Dialogue.

We work with communities who have been marginalised in claiming their rights and leading self-determined lives, foremost with smallholder farmers, disadvantaged women, children and youth, women’s and human rights groups as well as indigenous people.

The know-how3000 (kh3000) programme intervention is implemented by horizont3000 and its regional and country offices. It is part of the Austrian Development (ADA) framework programme 2023-2026 “Gender Equality 4 Sustainable Development.”

The ongoing horizont3000 ADA framework programme 2023-2026 is committed to proactively pursuing the goal of gender equality. Therefore, it is key to hold a training ondocumenting stories of change to capture, and communicate the project's most significant results, lessons, and impact, but also demonstrate the project's contribution to gender equality, women's empowerment, and positive social change in communities.

horizont3000 therefore seeks a qualified consultant to deliver a comprehensive online training session covering these three areas, followed by individual feedback and a follow-up session for additional guidance.

Objective of the Consultancy

The objective of this consultancy is to equip partner organizations with practical skills in:

  • Identifying, collecting, and documenting credible Stories of Change that demonstrate the outcomes and impact of the project on project participants and communities with a focus on stories of women’s empowerment, strengthening gender equality or engaging men and boys.
  • Conducting interviews, gathering evidence, and validating change stories using ethical and participatory approaches.
  • Writing and communicating compelling gender-responsive Stories of Change for organizational learning, advocacy, donor reporting, and knowledge sharing.

The consultant will deliver:

  • A 4-hour virtual training session covering topics named in the objectives and including practical exercises.
  • Individual feedback on stories drafted by the participants (1 story each for the expected 16 participating Partner Organizations (Pos))
  • A 2.5-hour follow-up session dedicated to providing further technical support based on the received stories.

Scope of Work

Under the supervision of the horizont3000 East Africa Gender Focal Point, the incumbent will be responsible for the following tasks:

  • Develop and share training methodology being cognisant of POs needs and expectations.
  • Prepare learning materials, practical exercises, and real-life case studies to ensure the content is relevant to the needs of the participants.
  • Customize content to reflect the NGO sector and the specific challenges faced by partner organizations in East Africa.
  • Provide technical support and practical recommendations to partner organizations (POs) during the workshop as well as feedback on stories drafted by the participants
  • Generate a training report including annex using the horizont3000 reporting template
  • Provide additional resources, including templates, guides, and best practices for documenting stories of change.

Expected deliverables

Expected outputs under this consultancy are as follows:

  1. Workshop design and substantial training materials such as PowerPoint presentations, handouts, etc.
  2. Facilitation of the 4-hour training as well as the 2.5-hour follow-up session, including review and feedback on assignments and group tasks.
  3. Workshop report including post- evaluations, learning and recommendations by latest two weeks after the follow-up session
  4. Recordings of the training and follow-up sessions (to be uploaded on MS Teams and other shared platforms).

Duration and Timeline

The consultancy will be conducted as follows;

  1. An inception meeting to discuss the training methodology and material
    1. A 4-hours online training session on Tuesday 28th July,2026
    2. A 2.5-hours follow-up session scheduled for 6th August 2026.

Budget

The consultant should propose a budget that covers their fees (based on an hourly or daily rate), communication costs, taxes, and any other relevant expenses. The budget should be submitted along with the technical proposal. The total budget for the scope of work outlined under 3.) should not exceed 6,000,000 Uganda Shillings including taxes.

Required Qualifications

The consultant should meet the following qualifications:

  • Expertise in documentation, storytelling and communication strategies for NGOs.
  • Demonstrated experience in developing and delivering gender trainings preferably in East Africa.
  • Experience facilitating online training and coaching for diverse audiences, particularly in the NGO or non-profit sector.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to simplify complex concepts for non-technical audiences.
  • Familiarity with virtual training platforms, including Zoom, MS Teams, and others.
  • Excellent command of English, working proficiency in spoken Kiswahili.
  • Previous experience working with NGOs or similar organizations is an added advantage.

opportunities.title: Senior Programme Manager [Senior Advisor]
opportunities.description:
Job Highlight

Under the supervision of the Director, the Senior Programme Manager [Senior Advisor] supports the ASG and the Climate Action Team by leading the strategic planning and coordination of transition activities related to the change in UN leadership. The role provides strategic advice on political engagement, Member State relations, and institutional continuity, while coordinating consultations with internal and external stakeholders, supporting engagement across the UN system, and ensuring continuity of climate priorities, partnerships, and initiatives throughout the transition process.

Job Specific Context

UNOPS has signed an agreement with the Executive Office of the Secretary-General (EOSG) of the United Nations to implement the activities of the Climate Action Team (CAT) Project.

Following COP26 in Glasgow and COP27 in Sharm el-Sheik, there is less than a decade to prevent a climate breakdown. Without deep emissions cuts, the world is heading towards 2.4-degrees Celsius of warming with catastrophic consequences. At current levels of warming the world is experiencing unprecedented climate impacts.

In increase in global average temperature above 1.5˚C would mean extreme weather and climate disasters increasing in frequency and intensity, putting billions of people at immediate risk with significant parts of Africa becoming unlivable and whole countries ceasing to exist. The Secretary-General’s call to all countries, cities, companies and institutions to go into emergency mode on climate is needed more than ever.

While climate change risks undermining the 2030 Agenda, as well as the social, economic, and environmental pillars of sustainable development, climate action also presents an opportunity. Green investments boost growth and jobs; just transitions are inclusive and help to eradicate poverty; and enhancing carbon sinks strengthen biodiversity and resilience. It will be essential to ensure that the transformation of economies and societies takes place to enable accelerated climate action in line with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

The objective of the Secretary-General’s climate action strategy throughout his second term will be to accelerate this decade, the transition towards a resilient, net zero world, that keeps the 1.5˚C goal alive, to secure the alignment of public and private finance, of technological transfers and capacity building to enable the necessary cooperation and support needed by developing countries, to significantly enhance the credibility and accountability of commitments taken by governments and non-state actors to reach the Paris Agreement goals.

The Secretary- General’s Climate Action Team will focus on the following:

Raising ambition levels and concrete mitigation commitments by the major emitters, particularly the G20.

Contributing to the reform of the international climate finance architecture and the multilateral development banks including through the design and operationalization of the Loss and Damage Fund decided at COP27.

Delivering tangible results to scale up adaptation and resilience finance and projects in developing countries including through cooperative initiatives.

Developing and implementing targeted strategies for fossil fuel phase-out and renewable energy scale-up including through the Just Energy Transition Partnerships and other cooperative initiatives.

Strengthening and verifying short-term and longer-term commitments made by non-state actors to reach net zero by 2050 through the implementation of the guidelines recommended to the Secretary-General at COP27 by the High-Level Group of Experts on Net Zero pledges

Enhancing UN system support to countries to deliver on the climate and environment-related Sustainable Development Goals this decade.

Providing up-to-date analytics and policy guidance for the Secretary-General, Deputy Secretary-General, UN leadership and Member States.

Designing and executing a cross-UN global communications campaign and movement focused on SG and UN leadership on climate action at all levels, and messaging and storytelling to build political will, elevate local solutions and mobilize individual actions.

Role Purpose

The effective and successful achievement of results by the incumbent directly impacts on the development and performance of the Climate Action Team, visibility and image of CAT, ensuring that the project is aligned with the overall priorities on the UN agenda.

Functions / Key Results Expected

Under the supervision of the Director, the Senior Programme Manager will be responsible for the following duties:

Strategic Transition Planning and Coordination

Advise the ASG on transition priorities, sequencing, and political sensitivities across the outgoing and incoming administrations.

Develop and execute a comprehensive transition strategy, informed by the CAT continuity plan and developed in consultation with relevant EOSG entities and key internal and external partners, to ensure continuity and an effective handover to the incoming Secretary-General and relevant UN entities.

Lead multi-stakeholder consultations in support of the transition strategy, through to the Secretary-General's approval.

Serve as an interlocutor with both transition teams on climate-related matters, ensuring coherent and consistent engagement.

UN System Coordination and Institutional Anchoring

Identify and coordinate the CAT's engagements with the broader UN system to ensure coherent, coordinated approaches to the transition.

Identify and pursue opportunities to formally anchor the CAT's work and partnerships within UN system structures, institutionalizing progress made under the current Secretary-General and minimizing the risk of losing momentum during leadership transition.

Political Engagement and Member State Relations

Support and advise on ASG on political engagements with Member States required for the transition, providing substantive analysis and strategic advice.

Perform other duties as may be required by the ASG.

opportunities.title: Junior Project Officer (Cybersecurity)
opportunities.publisher: Geneva Centre for Security Sector Governance
opportunities.description:
At DCAF, we envision a world where democratic sector governance advances sustainable peace and development and human dignity for all.

Our mission is to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices.

DCAF contributes to making peace and development more sustainable by assisting partner states and international actors supporting these states, to improve the governance of their security sector through inclusive and participatory reforms. It creates innovative knowledge products, promotes norms and good practices, provides legal and policy advice and supports capacity‐building of both state and non‐state security sector stakeholders.

DCAF’s Cybersecurity programme, implemented by the Europe and Asia Entity, aims to support good governance in cybersecurity. The programme contributes to making cybersecurity responsive and effective by working with cybersecurity actors from the public and private sector on improving law and policies, stakeholder cooperation and the effective provision and oversight of cybersecurity. To this end, the programme provides advice and research, organises technical trainings and workshops and organises stakeholder exchanges.

In particular, the incumbent will work with the Programme Managers for Albania and for Kosovo on implementing cybersecurity capacity building activities in Albania, Kosovo and in the Western Balkan region. The incumbent will also support activities related to gender and cybersecurity in the region.
