Deadline: 02/09/2026

Starting date: 01/11/2026

Family Duty Station: NO

R&R: YES

Contract Type: Expatriate (International)

Working context

The presence of WeWorld in Syria dates back to 2011, with an emergency education intervention in favour of Iraqi refugees in Aleppo. Since 2014, WeWorld has been providing humanitarian assistance to the vulnerable Syrian population with interventions in different sectors such as Education in Emergency, WASH, and Livelihoods. WeWorld currently operates in 4 governorates in Syria: Aleppo, Deir Ez Zor, Ar-Raqqa, and Daraa. At present, the main donors are EU (ECHO), Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), Syria Humanitarian Funds (SHF), ChildFund Alliance and other United Nations Agencies.

Job description

The Grants Officer works under the direct responsibility of the Head of Programs. Working in coordination with: Project Managers, Project Coordinators, Technical Coordinators, Area Managers, Finance Team and other field team members as necessary. The Grants Officer will support and contribute to:

1. Support the coordination of the development of high-quality concept notes and project proposals in close collaboration with program and finance teams

2. Coordinate the high quality and timely development and submission of donor due diligence, internal and external reporting

3. Support the Head of Programs and Program team in any other tasks related to project and grant management upon request.

The role operates under close technical guidance from the Head of Programs including structured support and shadowing. Moreover, the position includes a structured professional development pathway, with progressive increase in autonomy based on performance, technical capacity, and organizational needs.

Main tasks and responsibilities

Support the coordination of the development of high-quality concept notes and project proposals in close collaboration with program and finance teams

·Initiate the process of the development of CNs or PPs in line with the guidance of the Head of Programs and the requirements of HQ

·Develop, present, review, and follow up on the implementation of CNs or PPs development workplans in coordination with the Program & Support teams in Syria and HQ under the supervision of the Head of Programs

·Coordinate the preparation of all required grant documentation including narrative proposals or CN, assessment reports, as well as technical and administrative annexes

·Review the proposed logic of intervention as well as inputs provided by Technical Coordinators and other team members on any part of the CN or PP and ensure its overall coherence

·Review and ensure the consistency between the CN/PP and the budget to identify potential discrepancies and participate in the identification of solutions with the relevant focal points

·Submit finalized CNs/PPs documents to the donor through the appropriate channels (email, PEC, or dedicated platforms)

·Support the development of needs assessment, technical, and administrative annexes when requested

·Report any potential delays, quality concerns, discrepancies, or inefficiencies in the coordination of the CNs/PPs to the Head of Programs in due time and support in identifying solutions

·Archive the CNs/PPs documents on SharePoint and share with the relevant mission and HQ colleagues

Coordinate the high-quality and timely development and submission of donor due diligence, internal and external reporting

·Initiate the development of donors DD, internal and external reporting requirements establishing workplans, clear internal deadlines, and contribute to the onboarding of all the relevant colleagues involved

·Facilitate the collection of input from Project Coordinators and MEAL Officers for periodic non-contractual reports, consolidating the information and requesting clarifications as needed

·Share monthly non-contractual reports with Project Managers and Head of Programs for validation, finalization, and archiving

·Support Project Managers in drafting the contractual reports, adapting and contextualizing the inputs to the appropriate format

·Support Project Managers in reviewing and consolidating reports received from partners, provide comments against inconsistencies, provide constructive feedback, and ensure that the information is relevant and accurate

·Support the follow-up on all involved Program, MEAL, and Support colleagues and abidance by the agreed-on reporting deadlines

·Flag to the Head of Programs / Country Representative any issues that could potentially affect the timely or quality submission of internal and external reports in due time and support in identifying solutions

·Finalize and share contractual reports in a timely manner for validation to relevant supervisors (Head of Programs and Country Representative) and submit to the donor through the appropriate channels.

·Archive all due diligence documents as well as internal and external reports (both contractual and non-contractual) in a regular manner

Support the Head of Programs and Program Team for any other tasks related to project and grant management and communication based on need and upon request

·Develop and maintain a live donors contact list

·Support on the management and maintenance of Donor’s grants management platforms

·Support the Program Department on any relevant task related to project and grant management (e.g., project modifications), based on needs and requests

·Support the Program department with specific tasks handed over by the Project Managers during their planned leaves under guidance of the Head of Programs and relevant technical leads

The duties and responsibilities set forth above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to perform additional duties requested by the Line Manager.

Provides a proper handover before the end of the assignment.

Requisiti

ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS

Qualifications and Knowledge

·Master or equivalent in the international cooperation and other relevant field

·Good computer skills are required

·Fluency in English is mandatory

·Fluency in Italian is mandatory

Professional experiences

·At least 2 years of specific experience in the field of international cooperation

·Previous experience in producing proposals/CN/external reports for donors such as AICS, EU, OCHA, etc.

Skills and Abilities

·Leadership, planning, organization and teamwork skills

·Proactive and dynamic attitude

·Ability to adapt and work under constraint, under pressure and in complex and multicultural contexts

·Interpersonal skills and intercultural approach

·Good listening and communication skills

·Good negotiation and conflict resolution skills

·Strong commitment to the Mission of WeWorld, genuine interest in international cooperation development topics

·Demonstrates integrity with regards to NGO values and ethical standards

·Displays cultural, gender, religion, nationality and age sensitivity and adaptability

·Treats all people fairly without favouritism

DESIDERABLE REQUIREMENTS

·Knowledge of Arabic would be considered an asset

·Previous working experiences in Syria would be considered an asset

WHAT WE OFFER

Type of contract: a first 6 (six) months contract subject to verification (achievement of specific objectives); a second collaboration contract of 6 (six) months renewable, following the positive evaluation of the first period of collaboration and depending on available funding

Economic conditions: according to WeWorld Expatriates Compensation Policy

Base Salary (2.265,70 € - 2.390,70 € gross monthly) + Contributions reflecting role complexity and hardship level of the duty station

Accomodation: WeWorld Guesthouse

Annual leave: 2,5 days/month (working days)

Wellbeing & Inclusion: One day of paid menstrual leave per month. We promote a positive and inclusive work environment based on psychological safety, respect, and team empowerment

Flight ticket: One round-trip air ticket every 12 months of service (between country of residence and duty station)

Health insurance: covered

R&R Policy: 5 days every 12 weeks, allowance of 1.000€ is provided

Altre informazioni

The selection process may be closed earlier than planned should a candidate matching the required profile be identified.

Due to the high number of applications, we apologize in advance that only candidates deemed suitable for the role will be contacted.

opportunities.title: Conflict Transformation and Livelihood Project Assistant - Yumbe
opportunities.description:
HEKS/EPER (Swiss Church Aid) is a faith-based international development and humanitarian organization committed to justice, human dignity, and sustainable development. In Uganda and South Sudan, our work focuses on supporting marginalized communities and building resilience through a triple nexus approach that integrates humanitarian response, sustainable development, and peacebuilding. We promote a rights-based, participatory, and conflict-sensitive approach that upholds dignity, inclusion, and accountability to affected populations.

For further information about HEKS/EPER, please consult our website https://en.heks.ch/.

This is a national position based in Yumbe Distrcit (West Nile).

Description of main tasks
The project Assistant will provide technical support in the implementation of the Pads for All Project through strengthening integration of conflict transformation approaches in HEKS/EPER interventions, community mobilization and coordination, monitoring, evaluation and reporting, market access and linkages. The Project Assistant works closely with the community-based peace structures such as the neighborhoods assembles, peace fora, Bidi Pads Ltd, women's groups, schools, district authorities, refugee and host communities, and private sector to ensure quality and timely implementation of project activities in accordance with HEKS/EPER standards, policies, and donor requirements.

KEY RESPONSIBILITES

Project Implementation

  • Provide technical guidance and oversight to Bidi Pads Ltd to ensure quality, coherence, and timely implementation of project activities.
  • Organize age and gender-inclusive creative and community-driven conflict transformation and peace building interventions
  • Support HEKS/EPER supported social enterprises/groups, farmer groups, local partners, and other stakeholders with training in conflict sensitivity, alternative dispute resolution and promotion of inclusive dialogue processes.
  • Design and provide tailored Business Development Services (BDS) to Bidi Pads Ltd focusing on marketing, branding, quality assurance, Financial Literacy and Soft Skills (FLESS) to address production challenges, ensure efficiency and sustainability.
  • Support the Conflict Transformation Officer (CTO) to generate regular conflict sensitivity updates, conflict analysis and mitigation strategies to inform timely decision-making to ensure inclusive and peaceful communities.
  • Explore, strengthen and expand public-private partnerships to enhance the sustainability and expansion of Bidi Pads Ltd outreach within the regional and national markets/fora.
  • Strengthen institutional capacity of Bidi Pads Ltd through capacity enhancement on governance, strategic decision making, business management, and marketing.
  • Enhance the capacity of the Bidi Pads Centre Management Committee (CMC) to develop and implement a sustainable marketing strategy.
  • Develop and scale digital marketing initiatives for Bidi Pads Ltd to improve, visibility, market access and enhance competitiveness.
  • Strengthen the coordination and implementation of Menstrual Health and Hygiene (MHM) activities, including awareness sessions, skills development, and reusable sanitary pad production.
  • Build the capacity of the Raising Star Women's Group in production, enterprise development, and product marketing.
  • Mobilize and sensitize girls, women, youth, schools, refugee and host communities on menstrual health and hygiene, use of reusable sanitary pads, water use, and hygiene practices.
  • Provide technical leadership in the development of gender-inclusive MHM training modules focusing on MHM infrastructure, social behavior changes Communication (SBCC), information education and communication (IEC) materials and advocacy products.
  • Facilitate community participation and stakeholder engagement throughout project implementation.

Coordination and communication

  • Build and maintain effective collaboration with district local governments, implementing partners, UN agencies, community leaders, private sector actors, civil society organizations, and Refugee-Led Organizations (RLOs).
  • Liaise with the MEAL Officer and lead the preparation of program briefs, success stories, and case studies in compliance with HEKS/EPER and donor guidelines and requirements.
  • Coordinate with district leadership on the integration of Menstrual Health and Hygiene into district development plans with focus on dissemination of National Menstrual Health Guidelines and advocacy.

Qualifications and Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Community Development, Public Health, Social Sciences, Development Studies, Business Administration, or another relevant field.
  • Minimum of three (3) years' experience in community development, humanitarian, or development programming.
  • Experience implementing Menstrual Health and Hygiene (MHM), livelihoods, women's economic empowerment, or similar projects is an added advantage.
  • Experience working with refugee and host communities.
  • Experience working with NGOs or international development organizations.

Skills and Capabilities

  • Strong community mobilization and facilitation skills.
  • Excellent interpersonal, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Good report writing and documentation skills.
  • Knowledge of monitoring, data collection, and project reporting.
  • Good planning, coordination, and organizational skills.
  • Sound ICT skills, including Microsoft Office applications.
  • High level of integrity, professionalism, teamwork, and accountability.
  • Commitment to safeguarding and humanitarian principles.
  • Fluency in English; knowledge of local languages spoken in West Nile is an added advantage.
  • Willingness to travel frequently within project locations.

opportunities.title: Regional HMA Technical Advisor — Middle East
opportunities.description:
HAMAP-Humanitaire https://hamap-humanitaire.org

Halte aux Mines AntiPersonnel (HAMAP)-Humanitaire is a French NGO, established in 1999 in order to contribute to the struggle against mines and the risks it presents to civilian population. HAMAP-Humanitaire is active in 13 countries and pursues a mission of support to local partners from the need assessment, through project conception and to its sustainable implementation. HAMAP-Humanitaire diversified its field of activity, to encompass two sectors: Engineering (WASH, construction, energy) and Mine Action.

Requirements and job status

Minimum education: EOD Level 3+ qualification
Minimum experience: 10 Years
Required travel: Yes
No of jobs: 1
Job Description PDF - HAMAP Humanitaire LinkedIn page

Description

HAMAP-Humanitaire is seeking a qualified and experienced Regional HMA Technical Advisor to provide strategic, technical, and quality-management leadership for its Humanitarian Mine Action portfolio in the Middle East, currently covering Lebanon, Iraq, and Syria.

The position replaces the narrower Regional EOD Advisor framing with a broader Humanitarian Mine Action mandate. The role covers the full HMA technical toolbox, including Land Release, Non-Technical Survey, Technical Survey, Clearance and EOD, EORE/CPP technical integration, Quality Management, SOP and technical governance, training and competency frameworks, operational risk management, partner capacity strengthening, accident/incident investigations, information management, task management systems, and technical input to programme design.

The Regional HMA Technical Advisor operates at regional, strategic, and system-design level. The role provides technical direction, harmonisation, risk escalation, mentoring, and system assurance across country programmes and partners.

Where National Technical Advisors are present, the Regional HMA Technical Advisor provides line management, technical direction, mentoring, and quality control. National Technical Advisors remain responsible for routine country-level advisory support, frequent field QA, compliance follow-up, and day-to-day partner mentoring.

The Regional HMA Technical Advisor does not replace country management or partner operational command. Country-level operational decisions remain with the relevant country / programme management and partner management structures.

Hierarchical and organizational links:
Reports to: Regional Coordinator for Middle-East;
Coordinates with: Country Programme Coordinators, Partner Operations Staff, Regional Support Manager, HQ Technical focal-points

Main responsibilities

  • Provide regional technical direction for HAMAP-supported HMA activities across Lebanon, Iraq, and Syria.
  • Ensure technical coherence across countries while allowing adaptation to national standards, partner capacity, operational context, access constraints, and grant requirements.
  • Provide technical guidance on land release methodology, including NTS, TS, cancellation, reduction, clearance, BAC, EOD spot tasks, completion, and handover.
  • Review and advise on technical approaches for manual clearance, BAC, EOD, mechanical support to clearance, rubble removal, integrated assets, and complex or high-risk tasks.
  • Support country teams and partners in applying all reasonable effort, evidence-based decision-making, and risk-based prioritisation.
  • Provide technical input on EORE/CPP integration, EO threat interpretation, risk analysis, blast protection logic, and technical accuracy of risk-reduction messaging, in coordination with the Global EORE Advisor.
  • Coordinate with the Global EORE Advisor, who remains HAMAP’s organisational technical reference for EORE methodology, messaging, IEC/material standards, and global EORE guidance.
  • Design, review, and strengthen Quality Management systems, including internal QA/QC frameworks, performance indicators, corrective-action tracking, and partner-owned internal QA capacity.
  • Conduct targeted system audits, spot checks, high-risk task reviews, verification visits, and corrective-action effectiveness reviews.
  • Support the development and review of regional and country-level SOPs, technical annexes, emergency procedures, QA/QC tools, task dossier templates, operational checklists, and training annexes.
  • Design regional training architecture, competency frameworks, qualification thresholds, refresher cycles, and technical training priorities.
  • Review and approve technical training packages, Training Management Plans, lesson plans, assessment tools, training completion reports, and competency records.
  • Provide technical oversight of HMA information management systems, including task dossiers, IMSMA-compatible reporting, land release evidence, QA/QC dashboards, indicators, and donor reporting consistency.
  • Provide technical input to proposals, logframes, budgets, workplans, procurement plans, donor reports, and technical feasibility analysis.
  • Advise on technical specifications for detectors, PPE, demolition equipment, clearance tools, mechanical assets, communications, medical support, and other operational equipment.
  • Support specialised technical adaptation for project-specific contexts, including archaeological or heritage-sensitive clearance, Civil Defence capacity development, urban/rubble environments, or other complex post-conflict contamination contexts.
  • Assess partner technical capacity and support realistic capacity development plans linked to operational needs, safety, quality, and sustainability.
  • Mentor National Technical Advisors, country teams, partner operations managers, QA/QC staff, training focal points, and senior technical personnel.
  • Promote cross-country learning, technical harmonisation, capitalisation of lessons learned, and continuous improvement across HAMAP’s HMA portfolio.

Risk Management and Authority

The Regional HMA Technical Advisor supports the integration of risk management into HMA planning, implementation, QA/QC, and partner capacity strengthening.

The role includes authority to recommend immediate suspension, and where delegated require temporary suspension, of HAMAP-supported activities in cases of critical safety risk, major non-compliance, or systemic failure, pending management decision and corrective action.

The Regional HMA Technical Advisor provides technical direction, advisory oversight, system assurance, and risk escalation. The role does not replace national authorities, country management, partner management, or external QA/QC systems.

Limits of the Role

Unless specifically delegated and authorised, the Regional HMA Technical Advisor shall not:

  • assume direct operational command of partner teams;
  • override country management decisions outside approved escalation and risk-management processes;
  • make formal donor, contractual, or policy commitments on behalf of HAMAP;
  • approve expenditure or procurement outside delegated authority;
  • act as the national authority or replace national authority QA/QC;
  • certify land or task completion unless authorised by relevant SOPs and national requirements;
  • validate EORE methodology, IEC materials, or global EORE doctrine independently of the Global EORE Advisor where this falls under that function;
  • introduce new equipment, methodologies, or technical procedures without controlled risk assessment, SOP coverage, training, and approval process.

Required competencies and qualifications

Qualifications and Experience

  • Formally recognised EOD Level 3+ qualification or equivalent advanced military EOD qualification.
  • Demonstrated advanced explosive ordnance technical knowledge, including Advanced Explosive Theory as a minimum.
  • Proven competence in ADW and bulk demolitions.
  • IEDD qualification is highly desirable.
  • Strong knowledge of IMAS and land release principles.
  • Strong understanding of Quality Management in humanitarian mine action.
  • Demonstrated competence in SOP development, QA/QC, training design, and operational risk management.
  • Minimum 10 years of professional experience in humanitarian mine action or comparable explosive ordnance technical operations.
  • Substantial experience in EOD, clearance, BAC, and land release.
  • Minimum 5 years of senior technical advisory, programme operations, QA/QM, training, or capacity-strengthening experience.
  • Experience supporting local or national partners through capacity strengthening, mentoring, technical governance, and systems development.
  • Proven experience in SOP development, technical documentation, QA/QC systems, training architecture, competency assurance, and technical review.
  • Experience in proposal design, technical methodology development, logframe/KPI design, asset-staffing planning, and donor reporting is strongly desirable.
  • Experience in the Middle East, particularly Lebanon, Iraq, Syria, or comparable operational contexts, is highly desirable.
  • Experience with national mine action authorities, technical working groups, accreditation processes, and national standards is strongly desirable.
  • Experience with mechanical support to clearance, rubble clearance, heritage-sensitive clearance, or similar specialised contexts is desirable.
  • Experience with IMSMA-compatible reporting, GIS, Survey123, task dossiers, QA/QC dashboards, and HMA information management systems is desirable.

Required Skills

  • Strong understanding of the full HMA toolbox, including NTS, TS, clearance, BAC, EOD spot tasks, EORE/CPP integration, QA/QC, training, IM, and partner capacity strengthening.
  • Advanced technical credibility in EOD and clearance.
  • Strong understanding of land release methodology and evidence-based decision-making.
  • Ability to design systems, not only deliver activities.
  • Ability to translate IMAS, NMAS, and organisational SOPs into practical field systems.
  • Ability to provide strategic technical direction while respecting country management and partner ownership.
  • Ability to assess partner capacity and design realistic capacity development pathways.
  • Strong analytical skills and evidence-based judgement.
  • Strong report-writing, technical drafting, and SOP-writing skills.
  • Ability to design training architecture, competency frameworks, and technical assessment tools.
  • Ability to review operational data, task dossiers, QA/QC records, training records, and donor reporting for technical consistency.
  • Ability to advise on equipment, mechanical assets, procurement specifications, and technical suitability.
  • Ability to identify when external expertise is required and facilitate appropriate technical support.
  • Ability to work across cultures, countries, technical disciplines, and organisational levels.
  • Ability to manage sensitive operational, technical, and reputational risks.

Languages

  • English: fluent, mandatory.
  • French: working level desirable.
  • Arabic: strong asset.

English is mandatory because the role requires technical drafting, SOP review, IMAS/NMAS interpretation, donor inputs, proposal support, coordination with HQ, and high-level reporting.

Personal Profile

HAMAP is looking for a senior technical professional with high operational credibility, strong judgement, integrity, and the ability to work independently across several countries and technical disciplines.

The Regional HMA Technical Advisor must be able to balance safety, quality, compliance, operational efficiency, partner ownership, and donor expectations. The position requires a systems-builder: someone able to strengthen technical governance, improve partner capacity, support country teams, and translate operational lessons into better SOPs, training, QA/QC systems, task dossiers, and programme design.

The successful candidate will contribute to making HAMAP’s Middle East HMA portfolio technically coherent, risk-managed, quality-assured, and progressively more sustainable through stronger local and national partner capacity.

Rules of conduct

While working for HAMAP-Humanitaire, completing the entrusted tasks, or presenting his/herself as working for the NGO, the following is expected by the future employee:

  • Systematically reporting to in-line manager his/her activities and seeking approval before undertaking any unplanned activity.
  • Acting in a proper way, according to HAMAP-Humanitaire values, with all actors: this excludes any discrimination on basis of nationality, ethnicity, religion, class, gender, sexual orientation or political affiliation.
  • Respecting the various local habits and customs, as well as the country’s laws and rules, in order to preserve HAMAP-Humanitaire respectability.
  • Respecting strict confidentiality regarding HAMAP-Humanitaire documents, projects (ongoing and future), prospects of development, stakeholders and providers, unless instructed differently by the Country Director.
  • Avoiding any use of the job position in HAMAP-Humanitaire for personal purposes.

Conditions

  • Salary in line with HAMAP-Humanitaire’s salary grid and candidate’s experience.
  • Accommodation provided in Beirut.
  • Coverage of international travel costs.
  • Full health and repatriation insurance.
  • Annual leave and R&R according to HAMAP policy.

We would like to draw your attention to the fact that this offer is intended exclusively for you. Hamap does not provide any services, compensation, support arrangements, or coverage for family members in connection with your expatriation assignment with Hamap.

Consequently, Hamap cannot be held liable for any incident, accident, or harm suffered by a member of your family in your country of assignment.

opportunities.title: Regional Finance Officer
opportunities.description:
HAMAP-Humanitaire

https://hamap-humanitaire.org
Halte aux Mines AntiPersonnel (HAMAP)-Humanitaire is a French NGO, established in 1999 in order to
contribute to the struggle against mines and the risks it presents to civilian population. HAMAP-Humanitaire is active in 13 countries and pursues a mission of support to local partners from the need assessment, through project conception and to its sustainable implementation. HAMAP-Humanitaire diversified its field of activity, to encompass two sectors: Engineering (WASH, construction, energy) and Mine Action.

Requirements and job status

Minimum education: Bachelor or master degree
Minimum experience: 5 to 10 years
Required travel: Regular regional travel
(Lebanon, Iraq and Syria)
No of jobs: 1
Published date: 28th July 2026
Deadline date: 9th August 2026
Start date: As soon as possible
Job Description PDF - HAMAP Humanitaire LinkedIn page

Description

The Regional Finance Officer (RFO) – Middle East is responsible for supporting the sound financial management of HAMAP-Humanitaire’s programmes and operations across Lebanon, Iraq and Syria.

Under the supervision of the Regional Support Functions Manager – Middle East, the RFO ensures effective budget monitoring and financial analysis across the regional portfolio, supports budgeting and forecasting processes, oversees the quality and timeliness of financial information, and helps ensure compliance with HAMAP-Humanitaire’s internal policies, donor requirements and applicable financial procedures.

The RFO works closely with programme and support teams to monitor expenditure against budgets, analyse variances and burn rates, anticipate financial risks and underspending or overspending, update forecasts, and support timely management decisions.

The RFO provides direct supervision and technical support to designated country finance staff in the region. The position contributes to strengthening and harmonising financial systems, tools, procedures and controls across the three countries while ensuring that these remain adapted to operational realities and donor requirements.

The position acts as a key link between country operations, regional management and HAMAP-Humanitaire HQ Finance on financial matters.

Hierarchical and organizational links:
Reports to: Regional Support Manager – Middle East
Coordinates with: Budget holders and project teams, HQ Finance Department, HR, Procurement and Logistics staff.

Objective 1: Regional Financial Management and Oversight
To ensure effective financial management across HAMAP-Humanitaire’s programmes in Lebanon, Iraq and Syria through robust budget monitoring, financial analysis, forecasting, budgeting and reporting, enabling timely identification of financial risks and supporting informed decision-making and effective use of project resources.

Objective 2: Financial Compliance, Controls and Systems Strengthening
To ensure accurate, compliant and consistent financial management across HAMAP-Humanitaire’s operations in the region, in accordance with donor requirements and internal policies, through effective financial controls, oversight and risk management. Strengthen HAMAP-Humanitaire’s regional finance function through the development and harmonisation of financial policies, procedures, systems and tools, alongside the supervision, technical guidance and capacity building of finance staff across Lebanon, Iraq and Syria.

Objective 3: Partner Financial Oversight and Capacity Strengthening
To ensure sound financial management and compliance of HAMAP-Humanitaire’s local partners through effective financial monitoring, review of financial reporting and identification and follow-up of financial and compliance risks. Strengthen the organisational financial management systems and individual capacities of local partners through tailored capacity assessments, training, coaching, tools and ongoing technical support, promoting greater autonomy, accountability and sustainable financial management practices

Main responsibilities

Budget Management, Financial Monitoring and Forecasting

  • Lead the regular financial monitoring of HAMAP-Humanitaire projects and operations across Lebanon, Iraq and Syria.
  • Prepare, consolidate and maintain Budget Follow-Up (BFU), Budget versus Actual (BvA) and other financial monitoring tools for all active projects in the region.
  • Analyse expenditure, variances, burn rates, commitments and projected costs, and identify risks of underspending, overspending, funding gaps or incorrect allocations.
  • Work closely with Programme Coordinators and budget holders to review expenditure, implementation plans and forecasts and recommend corrective actions where required.
  • Monitor shared costs, staff allocations and other cross-project expenditures to ensure appropriate allocation across projects and funding sources.
  • Support the development of project spending plans, cash forecasts and funding requests based on realistic operational projections.

Budgeting, Reporting and Donor Compliance

  • Lead or support the preparation of project budgets for proposals, amendments, extensions and budget revisions, in coordination with programme and support teams.
  • Ensure budgets are realistic, adequately costed and compliant with donor requirements and HAMAP-Humanitaire rules.
  • Support budget reallocations and revisions by analysing financial implications, remaining balances and donor flexibility.
  • Prepare, review and consolidate financial reports for donors and HQ, ensuring accuracy, completeness and timely submission
  • Ensure expenditure and financial documentation comply with donor requirements, approved budgets and HAMAP-Humanitaire policies, including cost eligibility, supporting documentation and correct allocation of expenditure.
  • Provide financial input throughout the project cycle, including proposal development, project kick-off, implementation and closure.

Financial Control, Audit and Systems Strengthening

  • Oversee the quality of financial records, accounting entries, reconciliations, supporting documentation and financial filing across the region.
  • Review financial transactions and allocations to identify errors, unsupported expenditure, control weaknesses or compliance risks and ensure timely corrective action.
  • Support internal and external audits, donor verifications and other financial reviews, including preparation of documentation and follow-up of findings.
  • Conduct periodic financial compliance reviews and support missions to country offices to assess the application of financial procedures and internal controls.
  • Contribute to the development, revision and harmonisation of finance policies, procedures, tools and internal controls across Lebanon, Iraq and Syria.
  • Support the implementation of improved financial systems and processes adapted to organisational, operational, legal and donor requirements.

Local Partner Financial Management and Capacity Strengthening

  • Review financial reports, expenditure records and supporting documentation submitted by HAMAP-Humanitaire’s local partners to ensure accuracy, completeness and compliance with partnership agreements, approved budgets, donor requirements and HAMAP-Humanitaire procedures.
  • Monitor partner expenditure and budget implementation, identify financial or compliance issues, and follow up on required corrections and recommendations.
  • Assess the financial management capacity, systems, procedures and internal controls of local partners and identify organisational and individual capacity-building needs.
  • Develop and implement tailored capacity-strengthening plans for partner organisations and finance staff, including coaching, training, tools and practical guidance on budgeting, financial reporting, compliance, internal controls and financial documentation.
  • Conduct financial monitoring and capacity-building visits to partners and follow up on agreed improvement actions.

Team Management and Regional Coordination

  • Directly supervise designated finance staff within the region.
  • Set priorities and objectives, monitor performance and workload, and identify staff development and training needs.
  • Provide induction, coaching and training to finance and non-finance staff on budget management, financial procedures, donor compliance and internal controls.
  • Provide timely financial analysis and advice to the Regional Support Manager, regional management and relevant budget holders to support decision-making.
  • Coordinate with HQ Finance and relevant country and programme teams on financial matters and participate in regional, country and project meetings as required.
  • Undertake regular travel and support missions across Lebanon, Iraq and Syria according to operational needs.
  • Perform other finance-related duties reasonably assigned by the Regional Support Functions Manager.

Procurement and Logistics Support

  • Provide financial and compliance oversight and technical support to procurement and logistics processes across the region, while maintaining clear segregation of duties between finance, procurement and operational decision-making.
  • Review procurement and logistics documentation from a financial and compliance perspective, identifying potential gaps, financial risks or inconsistencies and advising relevant staff on corrective actions where required.
  • Provide guidance and support on procurement and logistics processes when required as delegated by the Regional Support Manager.
  • Support the Regional Support Manager in monitoring procurement and logistics processes and identifying areas where procedures, controls or coordination between functions may require strengthening.
  • Maintain appropriate functional independence and segregation of duties, with procurement and logistics management, approvals, supplier selection and operational decisions remaining outside the authority of the Regional Finance Officer.

Risk Management and Authority

The Regional Finance Officer supports the integration of financial risk management into budgeting, financial monitoring, reporting, internal controls, partner financial oversight, and regional decision-making.
The role may recommend corrective action and escalate significant financial, compliance, control, fraud, or funding risks to the Regional Support Manager and HQ Finance. Any suspension of expenditure, budget revision, donor notification, or formal management action remains subject to the applicable delegation of authority.
The Regional Finance Officer provides financial oversight, analysis, technical guidance, and risk escalation.
The role does not replace budget holders, country management, HQ Finance, partner management, procurement decision-makers, or formal approval mechanisms.

Limits of the Role

Unless specifically delegated and authorised, the Regional Finance Officer shall not:

  • approve expenditure, payment, procurement, budget revisions, or contractual commitments outside delegated authority;
  • select suppliers or assume responsibility for procurement and logistics management or operational decisions;
  • make formal donor, contractual, legal, or policy commitments on behalf of HAMAP-Humanitaire; override budget-holder, country-management, partner-management, or HQ Finance decisions outside established escalation processes;
  • perform incompatible duties that would undermine segregation of duties or independent financial control;
  • validate unsupported expenditure or waive documentary, donor, or internal compliance requirements.

Required competencies and qualifications

Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics,
    Management or another relevant field.
  • A professional qualification or certification in accounting, finance or audit would be an asset.

Experience

  • Minimum of five years of progressively responsible professional experience in finance, accounting, grants finance or financial management, preferably within an international NGO, humanitarian or development organisation.
  • Demonstrated experience in project budgeting, Budget versus Actual (BvA) analysis, financial monitoring, forecasting and financial reporting.
  • Experience managing the financial requirements of multiple projects and institutional donor funded programmes.
  • Experience with donor financial compliance, financial controls, audits and/or expenditure verifications.
  • Experience working with local partners, including reviewing partner financial reporting, monitoring financial compliance and/or strengthening partner financial management capacity, is highly desirable.
  • Experience setting-up an ERP system would be a strong asset.
  • Previous experience in a regional or multi-country role and/or working within the Middle East is an asset.
  • Experience contributing to the development or improvement of financial systems, policies, procedures and tools is an asset.

Required Skills

Behavioral

  • Demonstrates integrity, accountability and professionalism, taking responsibility for decisions and responding constructively to feedback.
  • Plans and prioritises work effectively, anticipates risks and takes initiative to achieve high-quality results within established deadlines.
  • Works collaboratively with colleagues, local partners and other stakeholders, contributing to a constructive and respectful working environment.
  • Communicates clearly and effectively and builds positive working relationships across different functions, cultures and operational contexts.
  • Promotes continuous learning, knowledge sharing and improvement, and supports the development and performance of others.
  • Demonstrates adaptability and sound judgement when working across multiple countries and in changing operational environments.
  • Promotes a working environment free from discrimination, harassment, retaliation, sexual exploitation and abuse, and upholds HAMAP-Humanitaire’s safeguarding and PSEA principles.
  • Promotes inclusion and equal participation and considers gender and diversity perspectives in the performance of responsibilities.

Technical

  • Demonstrates strong knowledge of financial management, accounting principles, budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting and internal controls.
  • Ability to analyse complex financial information, identify trends, variances and financial risks, and provide practical recommendations to support decision-making.
  • Demonstrated understanding of institutional donor financial requirements, cost eligibility, supporting documentation and financial compliance.
  • Ability to manage and monitor the finances of multiple projects and funding sources across different countries and operational contexts.
  • Maintains high standards of accuracy, completeness and consistency in financial data, documentation and reporting.
  • Ability to communicate and explain financial information clearly to finance and non-finance colleagues and provide effective guidance to budget holders.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and good working knowledge of financial monitoring, accounting and reporting tools.
  • Demonstrates appropriate judgement and confidentiality in handling sensitive financial and organisational information.
  • Experience or knowledge of procurement and logistics processes within an NGO, humanitarian, or development context would be an asset.

Languages

  • Fluency in English and Arabic, both written and spoken.
  • Knowledge of French and/or Kurdish is an asset.

Personal Profile

HAMAP-Humanitaire is looking for a rigorous and service-oriented finance professional with strong analytical judgement, integrity, and the ability to work independently across several countries, teams, partners, and funding streams.
The successful candidate must be able to combine control and compliance with practical operational support, communicate financial issues clearly to non-finance colleagues, strengthen local partner systems, and contribute to coherent and sustainable financial management across HAMAP-Humanitaire’s Middle
East portfolio.

Rules of conduct

While working for HAMAP-Humanitaire, carrying out entrusted tasks, or representing themselves as working for the NGO, all employees are expected to:

  • Systematically report their activities to their line manager and seek approval before undertaking any unplanned activity.
  • Act appropriately and in accordance with HAMAP-Humanitaire’s values in all interactions. This excludes any discrimination based on nationality, ethnicity, religion, class, gender, sexual orientation, or any other legal right.
  • Respect local customs and practices, as well as the laws and regulations of the country, in order to preserve HAMAP-Humanitaire’s reputation.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality regarding HAMAP-Humanitaire documents, projects (ongoing and future), development prospects, stakeholders, and service providers.
  • Refrain from using their position within HAMAP-Humanitaire for personal purposes.

To be a source of proposals and individual initiatives are welcomed, nonetheless any action undertaken in
the name or as an employee of HAMAP-Humanitaire must, first, be approved by the Coordinator for
Middle East.

Conditions

Conditions will be determined in accordance with HAMAP-Humanitaire’s salary and benefits framework,
selected duty station, and applicable national contractual status.

opportunities.title: Senior Advocacy Advisor – Economic Justice
opportunities.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
opportunities.description:
Starting Salary: £44,766 - £48,225 (including London weighting)

Contract: Permanent

Location: UK, Hybrid working with a minimum of 40% of your time in the London Office

Job Profile

This role will lead CAFOD’s policy and advocacy work aimed at building a fairer global financial system. The post holder will have a solid understanding of contemporary global economic issues, including the global debt crisis, development finance and the workings of international multilateral organisations. Working closely with CAFOD’s overseas partners and within UK and global networks, this role will hold policy expertise on behalf of the organisation. This will involve developing policy positions and representing the organisation externally. The role will work closely with CAFOD’s government relations and campaigns colleagues to lobby decision-makers and mobilise supporters as part of our economic justice work. Sitting within the Advocacy, Policy & Campaigns team, the role is managed by the head of department.

Key Responsibilities

  • Leading the development and delivery of CAFOD’s global economic justice advocacy strategy
  • Working in partnership with UK and global organisations to develop evidence‑based policy positions
  • Influencing UK, regional and global policy debates on the global debt crisis, and other economic justice issues
  • Representing CAFOD in coalitions, to decision makers, in church networks and at international forums
  • Writing policy briefings, reports and communication outputs
  • Building relationships with external stakeholders and decision makers and UK and global levels
  • Ensuring advocacy is grounded in strong analysis, partner experience and a commitment to social and environmental justice
  • Supporting advocacy work of partners and global networks on debt cancellation and financial system reform
  • Providing strategic and technical advice across the organisation
  • Any other relevant duties reasonably required

Safeguarding

All CAFOD staff share responsibility to promote and maintain a strong safeguarding culture, including identifying the key actions they should take given their role and responsibilities.

Job Specific Competencies

  1. Strong background working in international economic policy and/or international development policy
  2. Excellent analytic and research skills and an understanding of how to form strategic policy positions
  3. Experience of developing strategic advocacy plans
  4. Experience of lobbying decision makers
  5. Background working with partners and coalitions, both in the UK and overseas
  6. Excellent written and verbal communication skills

CAFOD is a welcoming, supportive workplace committed to a safe, inclusive culture where everyone is respected. CAFOD will make reasonable adjustments at every stage of the recruitment process to ensure candidates with disabilities or individual needs are fully supported.

Safeguarding for Children and Vulnerable Adults

CAFOD recognises the personal dignity and rights of children and vulnerable adults, towards whom it has a special responsibility and a duty of care and respect. CAFOD, and all its staff and volunteers, undertake to do all in our power to create a safe environment for children, young people and vulnerable adults and to prevent their physical, sexual or emotional abuse. CAFOD is committed to acting at all times in the best interests of children and vulnerable adults, seeing these interests as paramount. Any candidate offered a job with CAFOD will be expected to adhere to CAFOD’s Safeguarding policy and sign CAFOD’s Code of Behaviour as an appendix to their contract of employment and agree to conduct themselves in accordance with the provisions of these documents.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references, and appropriate screening checks can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. CAFOD also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

opportunities.title: Projects & Partnerships Support Intern for HQ, based in Geneva
opportunities.description:
ABOUT IMPACT AND REACH

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organization manages several initiatives, which includes i) the REACH Initiative aimed at facilitating the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts, ii) the PANDA Initiative aimed at directly supporting key aid actors in improving the effectiveness, efficiency, and efficacy of their programmes, and iii) the AGORA Initiative aimed at promoting localised and multi-sectoral aid action in support of the recovery and stabilisation of crisis-affected communities.

The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of Acted and the two organizations have a strong complementarity, formalized in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from Acted’s operational support on its fields of intervention.

We are looking for a PROJECTS AND PARTNERSHIPS SUPPORT INTERN to join our team in HQ.

Supervisor: IMPACT Head of Projects and Partnerships Support, with functional links with the 2 managers

Position: Projects and Partnership Support Intern

Contract duration: 6 months

Location: Geneva, Switzerland

Remuneration: 1’450 CHF gross per month

Starting Date: from 01/07/2026

FUNCTIONS

The PROJECTS AND PARTNERSHIPS SUPPORT INTERN will report to the Head of Projects and Partnerships Support but will work closely with the 2 managers composing the unit. Following the recent US freeze, the department has undergone a restructuring with several functions being decentralized at regional hub level, with which the intern will also closely interact.

Based on these terms of reference and initial briefings, the selected candidate will progressively take on more responsibilities during the internship period, based on performance.

The PROJECTS AND PARTNERSHIPS SUPPORT INTERN will be responsible for:

Follow-up of processes related to Project Cycle Management (PCM)

  • Support the unit in keeping the department’s knowledge management tools updated – most notably the PCM Database – on a continuous basis.
  • Support project-related tools and processes on a rolling basis, including but not limited to analysis of donor contracts and requirements, project codes, project cards, kick off meetings, follow up of performance / contractual indicators.
  • Support the formalisation of external partnerships (specifically review and follow-up of grant agreements with IMPACT’s global partner Acted)
  • Contribute to the development of internal guidance, tools, and templates.
  • Assist with review and validation of external documents, such as donor proposals and donor reports.

Support to fundraising

  • Monitor and track potential funding opportunities through IMPACT’s tender monitoring framework.
  • Analyse potential funding opportunities and liaise with HQ team and field missions to support the decision-making process on funding applications.
  • Support with the preparation of specific funding applications.
  • Support the preparation of due diligences and other vetting processes for donor registration.
  • Develop / consolidate project past performances.

Support to partnership management

  • Support to the development and review of unfunded partnerships, notably by contributing to updating the consolidated database.
  • Support the consolidation and review of due diligence exercises required by upstream partners
  • Support to the monitoring of due diligence of funded downstream partners.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Studies related to a relevant field such as International Relations, Political Sciences, Social Research, Economics, Development Studies, or similar.
  • Excellent written and spoken English, and ideally good working level in French.
  • Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office 365.
  • Proven experience of copywriting and editing articles, reports and presentations.
  • Academic exposure to Grant management, Project Cycle Management and/or monitoring and evaluation.
  • Attentive to detail, rigorous and organized.
  • Proactive team player with the ability to think and work independently.
  • Ability to work in a dynamic, multicultural environment, to work under stress and to meet tight deadlines.
  • Fast learner and resourceful individual, able to take on a challenge and try new approaches.
  • Previous experience in the non-profit sector and understanding of the humanitarian coordination system would be a plus.
  • Knowledge of donor/institutional funding mechanisms would be a plus.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

  • For this position, gross salary is 1’450 CHF monthly (before income tax). NB – IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education and experience of staff. A contribution to medical insurance of 489 CHF per month is already included in the salary figure.
  • Insurance covering professional and non-professional accidents throughout the period of employment with IMPACT
  • Health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance in case of field visits/temporary deployments
  • Enrolment in IMPACT Initiatives Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.
  • Up to 40% of remote work on a weekly basis.

opportunities.title: Grievance Mechanisms Research Consultant
opportunities.description:
Position Title : Grievance Mechanisms Research Consultant

Duty Station : IOM Philippines Country Office (Manila)

Classification: Consultant

Type of Appointment: Consultancy

Estimated Start Date: ASAP

Closing Date : 06 August 2026

Project Context and Scope

MBHR in Asia is a regional programme aimed at promoting corporate responsibility to respect migrant workers’ rights in line with the United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs), implemented in the Philippines, Viet Nam, Thailand, Cambodia, Indonesia, Nepal and Malaysia.

Through MBHR in Asia, IOM collaborates with governments, business and civil society to uphold the human and labour rights of migrant workers in key sectors and migration corridors. The programme recognizes the critical and central role civil society, including migrant networks, human rights defenders and trade unions, play in organizing migrant communities and ensuring that the voices of migrants as rights holders are included in the design and implementation of migration policies. The programme aims to enhance and expand regular labour migration pathways that ensure ethical recruitment, facilitate labour mobility and decent work.

Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing

The consultant will report to IOM Philippines’ Migration Management Unit in close coordination with the MBHR PH and regional team.

Responsibilities

Tasks to be performed under this contract

  • First deliverable – Approved research design, including the proposed methodology and outline of the report, and an initial identification of stakeholders to be engaged in the data-gathering process. - First instalment payment - Deliverable by 1 September 2026
  • Second deliverable – Approved first draft of the research output, based on completed data-gathering and analysis, and with revisions based on feedback from the project team – Deliverable by 16 November 2026
  • Third deliverable – Completion of the validation process with stakeholders, in accordance with the approved research design – Deliverable by 11 December 2026
  • Final deliverable – Finalized research report (maximum of 80 pages including any Annexes), including a set of concrete policy recommendations, with revisions based on feedback from the project team – Fourth and Final instalment payment - Deliverable by 31 January 2027

Performance indicators for the evaluation of results

  • Required deliverables are submitted within the agreed-upon deadlines.
  • Submitted output is based on comprehensive research and adheres to international standards on human and labour rights
  • Feedback from the majority of stakeholders consulted indicates that the output is clear, easy to use, and applicable to their operations and specific country contexts
  • Submitted output ensured that all writing and formatting are consistent and aligned with the IOM Style Manual.
  • Any issues raised during development are resolved amicably with outcomes accepted by all parties involved.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Minimum of a bachelor’s degree in public policy, law, social science, business management, labour relations, international relations, international development, migration studies or related courses with a minimum of seven years of relevant professional experience, or an advanced/ graduate degree with at least five years of relevant professional experience

Experience

  • Previous experience in grievance management and resolution and/or in conducting research on this topic, particularly in cases involving international labour migration, is preferred.
  • Advanced understanding of internationally recognized frameworks and standards on human and labour rights, particularly relevant principles on the right to remedy
  • Substantial understanding of internationally recognized frameworks on business and human rights, including human rights due diligence

Skills

  • In-depth knowledge of the laws, policies and cross-cutting issues in Philippine labour migration.
  • Strong communication skills
  • Excellent writing skills, with the ability to produce clear, concise, and structured outputs and documentation. Shortlisted candidates will be required to submit samples of previous written work, such as research output or technical manuals/guides developed or co-authored by the candidate.

Languages

For this consultancy, fluency in English is required. Fluency in Filipino is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Notes

IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

opportunities.title: CALL FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST: Study on the implementation of a community-based Cervical Cancer project in Pakistan
opportunities.description:
Study on the implementation of a community-based Cervical Cancer (CC) project in an increasingly privatized health system through Public – Private Partnerships (PPPs) in Pakistan

1_BACKGROUND

Médecins du Monde France (MdM-F) is an independent organisation of active militants providing care, bearing witness and supporting social change, both in France and internationally. For the past 40 years, we have been committed to working with the most vulnerable individuals and their communities to break down the barriers preventing them from having access to healthcare.

BRIEF PRESENTATION OF THE PROJECT

MdM has been active in Pakistan since 2009, responding to emergencies and supporting health facilities providing primary healthcare services to vulnerable communities. MdM France in Pakistan has been implementing a strategic focus centred on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR), aiming to strengthen access to quality, integrated, and rights-based SRHR services, particularly for women and adolescent girls in underserved and marginalized communities. The programme focuses on key areas including family planning (FP), safe abortion and post-abortion care (PAC), cervical cancer (CC) awareness and screening, Gender Based Violence (GBV) response, and quality antenatal and postnatal care.

MdM will continue developing this strategy in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) and Punjab through collaboration with public health authorities, health facilities, and community-based actors. The approach combines service delivery, health system strengthening, community engagement, and advocacy to address barriers to care and improve continuity of services.

In the context of Pakistan’s evolving mixed public–private health system, including increasing reliance on public–private partnerships (PPPs), social health protection models and healthcare outsourcing, MdM aims to conduct a consultancy to identify strategic and operational opportunities to strengthen access to healthcare. The study will analyse health system governance, financing mechanisms, PPP arrangements, and existing service delivery models, with a focus on their implications for vulnerable populations and SRHR service provision in KP and Punjab.

2_DEFINITION OF THE CONSULTANCY MISSION

OBJECTIVE

In the context of this project, MdM-F is looking for a consultancy team to carry out an assessment mission, the objective of which is to identify practical and strategic opportunities for MdM to strengthen equitable access to healthcare within Pakistan’s evolving mixed public–private health system, and to provide evidence-based and operational recommendations to guide MdM’s future programming, engagement with public and private actors, and strategic positioning within Pakistan’s health system.

The specific objectives are to:

  • Map Pakistan’s health system governance, financing arrangements, PPPs and outsourced service delivery models;
  • Identify service delivery gaps and unmet needs that are insufficiently addressed through existing PPP and insurance mechanisms with a specific focus on SRHR including FP, PAC and CC;
  • Assess gaps in access, equity, and service delivery, particularly for vulnerable populations and with a specific focus on SRHR including FP, PAC and CC;
  • Identify opportunities for MdM to engage with public and private actors and strengthen community-based healthcare;
  • Develop actionable, evidence-based recommendations for future programming, partnerships, and advocacy.

BUDGET

The total budget available for this mission is 8400 Euros (including VAT) maximum, inclusive of all costs including contingency costs (maximum 5%).

3_PROFILE SOUGHT

The skills required for the mission are:

  • Degree in Public Health, Health Economics, Health Policy, Health systems
  • Proven professional experience in health systems analysis and strategic recommendations
  • Strong technical expertise in health systems, governance, health financing, PPPs, and health policy
  • Proven knowledge and understanding of Pakistan's health sector
  • Direct experience supporting the design, implementation or evaluation of PPP models in KP and Punjab
  • Strong understanding of Pakistani’ SRHR landscape and technical expertise in Family Planning and cervical cancer prevention and screening is a strong asset
  • Previous experience conducting health system assessments
  • Previous and proven experience working with or supporting INGO
  • Strong analytical, report writing, and communication skills, with the ability to produce clear and actionable recommendations
  • Fluency in English and Urdu and Penjabi and/or Pashto

4_INDICATIVE TIMETABLE

Deadline for an expression of interest: 03/08/2026 at 12 noon (Paris time/CET)

Deadline for filing a complete proposal: 21/08/2026 at 12 noon (Paris time/CET)

Preferred mission launch date: 21/09/2025

Preferred date for the “field” phase: 28/09/2026

Preferred final report delivery date: 06/11/2026

This timetable is for information only and subject to modification.

opportunities.title: Information Management Officer
opportunities.publisher: International Association for Relief and Development
opportunities.description:
About ONSUR:

The International Association for Relief and Development (ONSUR) is a non-governmental organization established in early 2012 and registered in Syria. ONSUR is dedicated to implementing relief and development projects that empower local communities and promote a dignified life for vulnerable populations. , the organization operates through a network of execution offices in Syria, Lebanon, Iraq,Turkey, and Yemen. ONSUR delivers humanitarian assistance and sustainable development initiatives in conflict-affected regions, with a focus on transparency, community engagement, and long-term impact.

Location: Damascus

Contract Duration: Five (5) months, with the possibility of extension

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Shelter/NFI Sector Information Management Officer provides professional information-management support to the Sector's national and/or sub-national coordination architecture. The role manages data collection, cleaning, analysis, visualization, and dissemination so that partners, donors, and humanitarian leadership have access to timely, accurate, and actionable information on Shelter/NFI needs, response coverage, gaps, stocks, and operational trends.

The IMO works closely with the Sector Co-Coordinator and UNHCR Sector Coordinator and serves the wider Sector in a neutral, non-programmatic capacity. The position is administratively managed by ONSUR under its HR and administrative policies while maintaining functional accountability to Sector coordination leadership. A central focus is to strengthen evidence-based decision-making, strategic planning, partner reporting, knowledge management, and accountability through consistent information-management standards and products.

Duties and Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

1. Data Collection and Management

• Develop, maintain, and improve standardized Sector data-collection and reporting tools, including 4W matrices, stock tracking, activity monitoring, partner presence, and response-progress tools.
• Liaise with Sector partners to ensure regular, complete, timely, and high-quality submissions in accordance with agreed reporting schedules and definitions.
• Consolidate, clean, validate, de-duplicate, and document incoming datasets, maintaining clear data dictionaries, version control, and audit trails.
• Maintain secure, well-structured Sector databases and ensure that data can be efficiently retrieved, updated, and used for analysis and reporting.

2. Analysis and Visualization

• Analyze Sector data to identify geographic and thematic needs, response gaps, duplications, trends, partner coverage, stock availability, and progress against targets.
• Produce and regularly update dashboards, maps, charts, tables, infographics, and other user-friendly products that clearly communicate Sector performance and priorities.
• Apply appropriate analytical methods and quality checks to ensure that findings are accurate, transparent, and suitable for operational and strategic decision-making.
• Prepare concise analytical narratives and briefing materials for coordination meetings, situation reports, donor discussions, advocacy, and humanitarian leadership.

3. Needs Assessment and Response Tracking

• Contribute to the design, implementation, and data-management arrangements of joint and Sector-specific needs assessments.
• Compile, clean, and analyze assessment data and produce summary reports, datasets, maps, and evidence products for Sector planning and prioritization.
• Maintain and update needs mapping, response tracking, gap-analysis, stock, and activity-monitoring tools at national and/or sub-national level.
• Support the harmonization of indicators, geographic references, assessment methodologies, and partner reporting definitions to improve comparability and reduce duplication.

4. Reporting and Knowledge Management

• Compile and issue monthly consolidated 4W products and support submission to OCHA and other relevant humanitarian platforms in accordance with agreed timelines.
• Support preparation of monthly situation reports, operational updates, strategic documents, response-monitoring products, and ad hoc information requests.
• Maintain an organized and current Sector documentation library covering assessments, reports, meeting minutes, strategies, standards, guidance, dashboards, and datasets.
• Contribute to Humanitarian Programme Cycle products, including HNO analysis, HRP indicators, periodic monitoring reviews, and national or sub-national planning processes.

5. Capacity Building and Partner Support

• Provide training, coaching, and help-desk support to Sector partners on IM tools, reporting requirements, indicator definitions, data quality, and submission procedures.
• Develop user-friendly templates, reporting calendars, data dictionaries, guidance notes, and standard operating instructions for partner submissions.
• Support national and sub-national IM colleagues in applying consistent methods, naming conventions, geographic coding, quality controls, and visualization standards.
• Document common reporting challenges and propose practical improvements that reduce partner burden while strengthening data completeness and usability.

6. Coordination and Liaison

• Participate in Sector coordination meetings and provide clear information-management updates, analyses, visual products, and recommendations.
• Liaise with OCHA Information Management, other Sector IMOs, assessment actors, and relevant humanitarian data platforms to promote interoperability and coordinated analysis.
• Support inter-sector data sharing and analysis, ensuring that definitions, geographic units, timelines, and caveats are clearly communicated.
• Respond to approved information requests from Sector leadership, partners, donors, and humanitarian coordination bodies in a timely and service-oriented manner.

7. Data Responsibility, Safeguarding, and Compliance

• Apply responsible-data principles, confidentiality, informed consent, data minimization, access controls, and secure storage when handling partner or affected-population information.
• Operate impartially and transparently in a neutral Sector-serving role and avoid using privileged Sector information to advance ONSUR's programmatic interests.
• Do not double-hat the Sector IMO function with programmatic information-management responsibilities within ONSUR where this could create an actual or perceived conflict of interest.
• Ensure compliance with ONSUR's Code of Conduct, Child Safeguarding Policy, PSEA standards, applicable data-protection requirements, and established procedures for reporting misconduct or data incidents.

Note:

The above responsibilities are illustrative and not exhaustive. Additional tasks may be assigned by Sector coordination leadership in line with the approved Terms of Reference, evolving operational needs, and ONSUR administrative procedures.

Required Qualifications & Experience

Education:

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Management, Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Geographic Information Systems, Humanitarian Studies, or a closely related discipline.
    • Relevant postgraduate study or professional certification in data analytics, business intelligence, GIS, database management, or humanitarian information management is highly desirable.

Experience:

  • Minimum of 3 years of humanitarian experience with a substantial focus on information management, data analysis, reporting, or GIS.
    • Demonstrated experience managing 4W or similar response-monitoring systems, partner reporting processes, dashboards, databases, and humanitarian information products.
    • Previous experience in Shelter/NFI, sector or cluster coordination, needs assessments, OCHA reporting, or a complex emergency context such as Syria is highly desirable.

Technical Skills

  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and strong practical experience with Power BI or comparable data-visualization and business-intelligence tools.
    • Experience with KoBoToolbox or similar mobile data-collection platforms, data cleaning, database management, and automated reporting workflows.
    • Working knowledge of GIS tools such as QGIS or ArcGIS and the ability to produce accurate humanitarian maps and geographic analyses.
    • Familiarity with OCHA IM standards, 4W reporting, Humanitarian Programme Cycle products, HDX or equivalent data-sharing platforms, indicator design, and responsible-data practices.

Core Competencies

  • Strong analytical, communication, facilitation, time-management, and stakeholder-service skills with exceptional attention to detail.
    • Ability to manage competing deadlines, work independently, and maintain neutrality and discretion when handling sensitive coordination information.
    • Ability to travel within Syria or work from sub-national hubs as required, subject to operational and security arrangements.

Languages:

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in Arabic ; professional proficiency in English is highly desirable.

Child Protection Policy

ONSUR maintains a strict zero-tolerance policy toward all forms of child abuse and exploitation. The organization is fully committed to creating and maintaining a child-safe environment across all areas of its work. All employees are expected to uphold the highest standards of behavior to ensure the safety and well-being of children, and any breach of this policy will result in immediate disciplinary action.

Anti-Discrimination, Harassment, and Abuse Policy

ONSUR is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace for all. Discrimination, harassment, or abuse of any kind — whether based on race, ethnicity, religion, gender, age, disability, marital status, citizenship, or military status — is strictly prohibited and will not be tolerated.

All staff are expected to promote a culture of respect and integrity. Participation in any form of abuse, harassment (verbal, physical, or sexual), intimidation, or exploitation — whether inside or outside the workplace — is a violation of ONSUR’s core values and policies.

Diversity & Inclusion

ONSUR is strongly committed to gender equality and encourages qualified female candidates to apply for this position.

opportunities.title: Finance Officer, Caribbean Resilience Initiative (CRI), Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands, Jamaica, or Saint Lucia
opportunities.country: Jamaica, Puerto Rico (The United States of America), Saint Lucia, United States Virgin Islands
opportunities.description:
Location: Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands, Jamaica or Saint Lucia
Valid unrestricted work authorization in the country in which you will be based is required at the time of application for this position.
