opportunities.title: Regional Advisor for Humanitarian Access & Risk for Africa (F/M) - Nigeria or Ethiopia
opportunities.description:
For more than 40 years, Médecins du Monde (MdM), a campaigning medical organisation committed to international solidarity, has been caring for the most vulnerable populations here and abroad. It has continued to bear witness to obstacles that exist in accessing healthcare and has secured sustainable improvements in health-for-all policies.

Those working for this independent organisation do not solely dispense care and treatment but condemn violations of human dignity and rights and fight to improve matters for populations living in precarious situations.

MdM France currently works in 30 countries across all continents to facilitate access to healthcare through 6 political battles:

  • Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights
  • Migration, Exile, Human Rights and Health
  • Harm Reduction
  • Environment and Health
  • Humanitarian Space
  • Healthcare systems and rights

About the role

The main objective of the Regional Humanitarian Access and Risk Advisor (HARA) is to improve the analysis, support operational management and access, safety, security capacity building of the MdM team working in 9 countries (DRC, CAR, Ivory Coast, Burkina Faso, Nigeria, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Madagascar, Sudan).

You will establish regular remote relationships with MdM's key security managers in these countries and will work closely with the Desk officers.

You will conduct regular visits to the countries within your area of responsibility, support the facilitation of humanitarian access, and contribute to regional analysis.

What you'll do

Under the supervision of the head of security and safety unit (based at the HQ), your main responsibilities are the following:

  • Monitor and analyse the political and security context across the countries of responsibility, identify trends, assess risks, and produce timely alerts and recommendations
  • Maintain security monitoring tools, incident databases, and regional analysis to support informed decision-making
  • Develop and maintain a strong network of security and humanitarian stakeholders, representing MdM in coordination forums and strengthening information-sharing
  • Provide technical guidance to country missions on security risk management, humanitarian access, and security assessments for new operational areas
  • Review and validate security aspects of field missions, operational plans, and access management systems
  • Support incident and crisis management, ensuring effective communication, post-incident analysis, and implementation of lessons learned
  • Prepare high-quality security reports, regional analyses, and ensure accurate archiving and documentation in line with organisational standards
  • Deliver security briefings, debriefings, and training to staff and partners, promoting compliance with MdM security policies and procedures
  • Supervise and technically support Country Humanitarian Access & Risk Advisors (HARAs), contributing to their recruitment, performance management, and professional development
  • Assess mission security management, identify capacity-building needs, and contribute to the continuous improvement of security practices through annual action planning

Who you'll work with

Under the International Operations Department, the service supports our international and national programs and several members of the MdM network.

It is composed of 8 people:

  • 1 Head of Unit
  • 3 Regional HARAs dedicated to our International Programs (1 for Europ/Asia, 1 for Middle East, 1 for Latin America)
  • 1 HARA for the MdM Network
  • 1 HARA for our domestic programmes in France

You are the right match if you:

  • Hold a degree in humanitarian security, security management, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience)
  • Have solid experience in humanitarian security management, including field missions in high-risk or complex environments
  • Have worked in one or more countries within the region of responsibility
  • Can analyse complex political and security contexts, anticipate risks, and provide clear operational recommendations
  • Are confident managing security incidents and advising teams in dynamic and challenging environments
  • Have experience delivering security training and supporting the development of colleagues' security capacities
  • Build strong relationships with diverse stakeholders and communicate effectively across multicultural teams and networks
  • Are organised, adaptable, and able to perform under pressure
  • Are fluent in both English and French

This role may not suit you if you:

  • Prefer working in stable environments with limited exposure to operational security challenges
  • Are uncomfortable making decisions or providing guidance in fast-changing or high-pressure situations
  • Do not enjoy collaborating with diverse teams, partners, and external stakeholders
  • Prefer a role with limited travel or field engagement
  • Are not comfortable balancing strategic analysis with hands-on operational support
  • Are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

Recruitment process

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

Ready to apply?

We only need your CV and a cover letter.
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

Employment conditions

Contract & status:

  • Gross monthly salary: 3 663 €
  • Fixed-term contract (6 months), starting as soon as possible
  • Trial period : 2 weeks
  • Single posting

Work environment:

  • Position based in Nigeria at Abuja or in Ethiopia at Addis Ababa
  • Regular field visits (40% of the working time planned in the countries covered)

Benefits:

  • 13th month salary (paid in 2 installments after 6 months of service)
  • Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
  • Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
  • Guesthouse
  • Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
  • Repatriation insurance
  • MdM promotes training and internal mobility

Essentials:

  • 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
  • Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
  • More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/

Our commitment to diversity and inclusion

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

opportunities.title: Consultant for Development of Measles-Rubella Follow-Up Campaign Application
opportunities.description:
General Information

DevelopmentPeople is currently supporting the identification of a Consultant for the development of the Solomon Islands Measles-Rubella Follow-Up Campaign Application on behalf of a leading global health partnership. The Ministry of Health and Medical Services of Solomon Islands is preparing a national Measles Rubella Follow-Up Campaign as part of its immunization strategy. The campaign is expected to address immunity gaps among zero-dose, under-immunized and missed children, while strengthening routine immunization systems, particularly in remote and outer island populations.

This is a remote role. The consultant should be immediately available, for up to 2 months, and be open to the possibility of a 1–2-week onsite stay in the Solomon Islands.

Objective

The campaign application should demonstrate a clear public health rationale, operational feasibility, equity focus, realistic costing, and alignment with the donor requirements. It should also show how campaign investments will contribute to routine immunization strengthening, demand generation, surveillance improvement, and sustainable service delivery.

What are the key responsibilities of the role?

The consultant will work under the leadership of the Ministry of Health and Medical Services, National EPI, and in close coordination with WHO, UNICEF and other organizational focal points, provincial health authorities and other relevant partners. Regular coordination meetings should be held to review progress, resolve bottle-necks and ensure timely completion of deliverables. They will provide technical assistance to MHMS, WHO, UNICEF and Alliance partners for the development of a high-quality MR Follow-Up Campaign application and for campaign readiness planning, including operational planning, microplanning, monitoring, supervision, implementation support and reporting.

Key deliverables include:

  • Lead the development and submission of the MR Follow-Up Campaign application, including technical narratives, equity analyses, operational strategies, and monitoring frameworks.
  • Analyze immunization coverage, disease surveillance, epidemiological data, and campaign performance to inform planning and decision-making.
  • Support campaign planning, including target population analysis, risk prioritization, budgeting, work planning, and resource mobilization.
  • Strengthen national campaign coordination by supporting technical working groups, task forces, and partner collaboration.
  • Develop and review operational plans, microplans, vaccine logistics, cold chain, waste management, and AEFI preparedness plans.
  • Design campaign guidance materials, training resources, standard operating procedures, and monitoring tools for national and subnational implementation.
  • Provide technical support during campaign implementation, including supervision, performance monitoring, problem-solving, and support to outreach activities in remote and hard-to-reach communities.
  • Monitor campaign readiness and implementation through assessments, field supervision, data analysis, and rapid corrective actions.
  • Support post-campaign monitoring, coverage assessments, evaluations, lessons learned, and technical reporting.
  • Develop recommendations and follow-up action plans to strengthen routine immunization systems and sustain campaign achievements.

Professional Skills, Competencies and Experience

  • 8+ years demonstratable technical experience supporting immunization programmes, including Measles-Rubella (MR) campaigns, Supplementary Immunization Activities (SIAs), vaccine introduction, health systems strengthening, zero-dose programming, programme optimization, or immunization technical assistance.
  • Proven experience developing, managing, or supporting large-scale vaccination campaigns, including campaign planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation.
  • Experience preparing and/or reviewing funding applications, investment cases, grant proposals, national strategic plans, operational plans, and results frameworks, including narrative development, budgeting, costing, and monitoring frameworks.
  • Demonstrated experience with funding applications and processes, including successful development, submission, and approval of donor-funded proposals.
  • Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple workstreams, competing priorities, timelines, and deliverables in complex public health programmes.
  • Proven ability to coordinate and collaborate effectively with Ministries of Health, WHO, UNICEF, Gavi, development partners, technical working groups, consultants, and senior government stakeholders.
  • Experience facilitating multi-stakeholder planning, governance, and technical coordination for national or subnational health programmes.
  • Strong analytical skills with experience interpreting immunization coverage data, disease surveillance information, epidemiological trends, and programme performance indicators to inform planning and decision-making.
  • Excellent written communication skills with the ability to prepare high-quality technical reports, strategic documents, donor submissions, and policy or programme recommendations.

Desirable experience

Previous experience working in the Solomon Islands or a strong understanding of the Solomon Islands health system, government structures, and immunization programme context is highly desirable.

opportunities.title: Senior Compliance & Subgrants Advisor
opportunities.description:
Position:

Senior Compliance & Subgrants Advisor

Location:

Consultancy | Home-based with travel to Morocco and Tunisia

Application Deadline:

07 August 2026

Duration:

Approximately 60 - 75 working days during the programme inception phase (anticipated period: September–December 2026)

Start Date:

01 September 2026

Consultancy Fee:

Competitive daily consultancy fee to be agreed based on qualifications and relevant experience.

About SPARK

SPARK is an international non-governmental organisation dedicated to creating opportunities for young people in fragile and conflict-affected contexts through entrepreneurship development and higher education. By strengthening local ecosystems, supporting entrepreneurs, and building institutional capacities, SPARK contributes to inclusive economic growth and sustainable employment.

About the Programme

SPARK is implementing a programme that aims to strengthen women's entrepreneurship in Morocco and Tunisia by selecting, supporting and enabling In-Country implementing partners (IPs) through tailored financial and non-financial support.

IPs will drive impact, addressing barriers through co-designed interventions that will support women entrepreneurs and their enabling environment.

SPARK will build the capacity of these IPs to enhance gender-responsive and transformative business development services, including tailored skill-building for climate-vulnerable and informal women entrepreneurs in business management, financial literacy, and digital tools, alongside MHPSS and soft skills training. At the societal level, IPs will design and implement community sensitisation and norm-change dialogues; promote positive narrative campaigns on women’s economic participation; and establish structured networks to foster business linkages, resilience, and safety.

Assignment Objective

SPARK is seeking a Senior Compliance & Subgrants Advisor to provide strategic and technical guidance during the inception phase of the programme and beyond, specifically for the development of the programme's compliance and subgrant management approach, the selection and organisational assessment of implementing partners (IPs), the co-design of tailored compliance and fiduciary improvement plans, and the establishment of practical systems, tools and guidance that enable accountable, transparent and effective programme implementation.

Scope of Work

  • Advise on the programme's overall compliance, governance and subgrant management approach, ensuring that it is practical, risk-based and aligned with donor requirements, while reflecting the operational realities of implementing partners in Morocco and Tunisia.
  • Support the development and enhancement of implementing partner selection, due diligence, organisational assessment and compliance tools to assess institutional readiness, governance arrangements, fiduciary capacity and risk management systems.
  • Support the implementing partner selection process by providing technical guidance on governance, financial management, procurement, internal controls and organisational compliance.
  • Facilitate organisational compliance and fiduciary assessments and support selected implementing partners in analysing assessment findings and co-designing tailored Compliance Improvement Plans that strengthen institutional systems and readiness to manage programme funding.
  • Support the co-design of practical compliance, financial management and subgrant management procedures with selected implementing partners, ensuring local ownership while maintaining alignment with donor requirements and SPARK's partnership approach.
  • Develop practical guidance, templates and quality assurance mechanisms that support compliant implementation of partnership agreements, financial support mechanisms, procurement, financial reporting and risk management throughout programme implementation.
  • Support the preparation of in-country programme kick-off clinics and deliver training and coaching to SPARK staff and implementing partners on compliance, subgrant management, fiduciary responsibilities and good partnership practices.
  • Promote organisational learning and adaptive management by identifying lessons learned, documenting good practices and supporting the continuous refinement of compliance and partnership management approaches throughout programme implementation.
  • Work closely with the GESI, MEL and Capacity Strengthening Advisors to ensure that compliance, governance and fiduciary management are fully integrated into the programme's overall implementation methodology, including partner selection, capacity strengthening, co-design and learning processes.
  • Support the continuous strengthening of SPARK's overall partnership approach by contributing practical tools, guidance and recommendations that enhance partner due diligence, compliance systems, risk management and institutional capacity across SPARK's programmes.
  • Provide any other relevant technical guidance required to strengthen implementing partners' institutional capacity, accountability and long-term sustainability.

Expected Deliverables and Outputs

Expected deliverables and outputs will be refined and agreed at the onset of the assignment and will most likely include:

  • Inception Work Plan, to be designed in consultation with the other technical advisors and the Programme Lead at the onset of the assignment.
  • Compliance and Subgrant Management Framework, establishing the programme's overall approach to compliance, governance, fiduciary management and accountable partnership implementation.
  • Enhanced implementing partner selection, due diligence and organisational assessment tools, ensuring effective assessment of governance, institutional readiness, fiduciary capacity and compliance risks.
  • Compliance and fiduciary assessment methodology, including practical tools, guidance and risk assessment approaches for implementing partner assessments.
  • Tailored Compliance Improvement Plans, co-designed with selected implementing partners to strengthen governance, procurement, financial management, internal controls and institutional compliance systems.
  • Practical compliance and subgrant management toolkit, including templates, reporting formats, quality assurance mechanisms and guidance to support effective implementation of partnership agreements and financial support mechanisms.
  • Compliance, fiduciary management and partnership management training and coaching delivered to SPARK staff and selected implementing partners.
  • Programme kick-off clinics preparation supported.
  • Recommendations to strengthen SPARK's partnership approach, including practical improvements to partner selection, due diligence, compliance management and institutional capacity strengthening processes that can be applied across SPARK's wider partnership portfolio.
  • Final Consultancy Report, summarising activities undertaken, deliverables completed, key findings, recommendations and proposed next steps for programme implementation.

Requirements and Qualifications

The successful candidate should possess:

  • A Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Public Administration, Law, International Development or another relevant discipline.
  • At least 10 years of professional experience in donor compliance, grant management or institutional compliance.
  • Demonstrated experience designing compliance and subgrant management systems.
  • Proven experience conducting organisational due diligence and local partner compliance assessments.
  • Experience developing internal control frameworks and risk management systems.
  • Experience strengthening the financial and compliance capacities of NGOs, Business Support Organisations or similar institutions.
  • Experience working with international donors, preferably the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the European Union or comparable bilateral or multilateral organisations.
  • Experience in Morocco, Tunisia or the wider MENA region is highly desirable.
  • Excellent analytical, stakeholder engagement and report-writing skills.
  • Excellent written and spoken English. Knowledge of French and/or Arabic is considered a strong asset.

opportunities.title: Land Use Planning Expert with national experience
opportunities.description:
Ref: 002
Position Title: Land Use Planning Expert with national experience
Status: Consultant
Number of Days: 360 (over a period of 18 months)
Tanzania, Ruvuma

About Landesa

Grounded in the knowledge that having legal rights to land is a foundation for prosperity and opportunity, Landesa partners with governments and local organizations to ensure that those experiencing the most extreme forms of poverty have secure rights over the land they steward. Founded as the Rural Development Institute in 1967, Landesa has helped more than 100 million families living in poverty gain legal control over their land. With secure land rights, these families can eat better, earn more, educate their children, practice conservation, and achieve dignity for generations. For additional information, visit the Landesa website at www.landesa.org.

Landesa is seeking a highly qualified Land Use Planning Expert with national experience for an anticipated 18-months GIZ program that aims to improve the management of Human Wildlife Conflict by key actors in Tanzania. The project’s main geographical scope is the Ruvuma Landscape/ including 42 villages of the Districts of Liwale, Namtumbo, and Tunduru. The project also aims to strengthen the capacity for steering and coordination of the Wildlife Division of the Ministry for Natural Resources and Tourism, and the institutions involved in managing HWC, including the Tanzania Wildlife Management Authority (TAWA), Tanzania National Parks (TANAPA), Tanzania Forest Services Agency (TFS), Districts councils and Hotspot Villages. The contractor will be responsible for the implementation of one District land use plan, 15 village land use planning (LUP) and community action plans, developing the organizational structure, curricula and materials, as well as piloting 30 clubs, for the revival of the Malihai Club (environmental conservation clubs in schools and colleges) and strengthening the outreach programs of Tanzania Wildlife Management Authority and Tanzania National Parks Authority (concept development, materials and support to implementation of pilot in 30 villages) of the institutions involved in wildlife management.

The vacancy is limited to candidates living in Tanzania. The position is contingent upon receipt of donor funding.

Availability The Land Use Planning Expert with national experience should start work on November 1st 2026.

Tasks of the Expert:
•
Planning, management, and implementation of the activities related to LUP and CAP in the three Districts, under thesupervision of the team leader.
•
Implementation of the WP-1.
•
Regular reporting to GIZ in accordance with deadlines.
•
Regular delivery of communication products in accordance with deadlines.
•
Responsible to implement all data protection requirements.
•
Preparing and implementing land use or spatial plans at district and village levels.
o
Participatory rural planning and community engagement.
o
Working with local governments, traditional authorities, and/or civil society organizations.
o
Application of GIS/remote sensing tools for land use mapping and analysis.
•
Steer and facilitate the 15 LUP processes, up to final registration and distribution to the communities and Districts.
•
Steer and facilitate the 15 CAPs based on the LUPs.
•
Facilitate 1 District framework LUP- Master plan for Liwale.
•
Facilitate development, validation, approval and registration of 15 Villages LUPs.
•
Facilitate development of specific by laws after LUP processes for the implementation of 15 CAP (grazingmanagement, water resources management, block farming, beekeeping, value addition, linking to private sector, valuechain development, etc).
•
Steer and coordinate with the Districts CAP implementation.
•
Facilitate capacity building for CAP measures.
•
Capacity building at village level for CAP.

Qualifications of the Expert:
•
Education/training: University degree (Master's or equivalent) in either Land Use Planning, Urban and RegionalPlanning, Environmental Planning, Geography, Natural Resource Management or Agriculture with landmanagement focus.
•
Language: Knowledge of English C1, C1 in Swahili.
•
General professional experience: 7 years’ experience in preparation and implementation of land use planningand management.
•
Specific professional experience: 5 years’ experience in developing and implementing land use plans andCommunity Action Plans (CAP) at district and/or village level. 3 years of professional experience in use of one ormore of the following: Stakeholder participation and community engagement, Integration of sustainability or climateresilience and HWC approaches. 2 years of professional experience in use of GIS/remote sensing tools.
•
Leadership/management experience: 3 years’ experience leading or coordinating multidisciplinary planningteams or field-based participatory planning processes.
•
Professional experience in the country/ region of assignment: 9 years of professional experience in EastAfrica or Tanzania.
•
Other: 3 years’ experience working with either customary land tenure systems, advising local governmentinstitutions on land tenure, or working in conflict-sensitive land use contexts.

Soft Skills
•
A deep commitment to the mission of a better, safer future for the world’s poorest people through secure accessto land.
•
Strong problem-solving.
•
Strong oral presentation skills and an ability to think on one's feet when defending policy recommendations.
•
Familiarity with concepts that can be applied to rural development.
•
Ability to develop concrete work plans and manage elements so that work is performed according to agreed-upon budgets and plans.
•
Ability to manage documents and correspondence, track, and report on project labor, and carry out otheradministrative tasks efficiently, routinely, and in conformance with Landesa standards and procedures.
•
Ability to work collaboratively with a range of people at all levels, including those from host countrygovernmental and non-governmental organizations, and other counterparts, clients, and funders.
•
Ability to demonstrate cross-cultural sensitivity, tact, and poise.
•
Ability to lead and work collaboratively as a member of teams, regardless of role within the team, throughconsensus building, communication, and leadership.
•
Ability to make and use distinctions as to types, frequency, tenor, and levels of communication, dependingupon the circumstances and audience.
•
Legal right to work in the country of assignment.

Physical and Environmental Conditions
This position does not require unusual demands for physical effort. Work environment involves everyday risks or discomforts that require normal safety precautions typical of places such as offices, meeting or training rooms, residences, or commercial vehicles, e.g., use of safe workplace practices with office equipment, and/or avoidance of trips and falls, and observance of fire regulations and traffic signals.

Work Environment and Working Conditions for Travelers to Developing Countries
While performing the duties of this job, the employee may be exposed to working conditions and hazards that are prevalent for the location and/or country of assignment. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Work is primarily performed indoors, with some potential for exposure to safety and health hazards related to electronics work. The employee may be required to travel overseas and domestically. When traveling in a developing country, the employee may be exposed to: Physical Hazards (illnesses, noise, extreme temperatures, wet or humid climates, etc.) Road Hazards (unfinished/dirt roads, potholes, traffic-related accidents, etc.), and Atmospheric Conditions (odors, dust, fumes, smog, etc.).

Additional Comments
The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. Reasonable accommodation may be provided in appropriate circumstances to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this job.

opportunities.title: National Consultant to Lead the Drafting and Validation of the National Framework for Inclusive Education in Syria
opportunities.description:
1. Background

Terre des Hommes Italia (TDH Italy) has worked in Syria since 2013, supporting children, families, schools and communities through education, child protection, disability inclusion and social cohesion. Under the project “Building Resilience and Enhancing Education Quality in Syria”, TDH Italy is supporting the Ministry of Education and relevant stakeholders to develop a nationally owned Framework for Inclusive Education.

The Framework will adopt a system-wide approach to inclusive education while maintaining a specific and substantive focus on removing the legal, institutional, physical, educational and social barriers faced by learners with disabilities. It aims to enable them to access, participate in and benefit from safe, relevant and quality education on an equal basis with others. Its development is informed by national legislation and policies, consultations across Syria, selected international and comparative references, and engagement with government institutions, education practitioners, civil society organisations, organisations of persons with disabilities, families and other stakeholders.

TDH Italy seeks a qualified National Consultant to translate the available evidence, institutional knowledge and consultation findings into a coherent and implementable Framework. The Consultant will lead the drafting and validation process under the guidance of the Ministry of Education, coordinate with the international technical expert for quality assurance, and ensure that the final Framework reflects Syria’s context, legal framework and national priorities.

2. Purpose of the Consultancy

The purpose of the consultancy is to provide high-level national technical expertise to lead the analysis, drafting, consultation, revision and validation of the National Framework for Inclusive Education in Syria, in close coordination with the Ministry of Education, TDH Italy and the designated technical stakeholders.

The assignment will result in a rights-based, contextually grounded and operationally relevant Framework that will adopt a system-wide approach to inclusive education while maintaining a specific and substantive focus on the rights of learners with disabilities, in line with national legislation and the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities:

  • defines a national vision, principles, intended results and strategic directions for inclusive education;
  • clarifies the scope of inclusive education across relevant education levels and pathways;
  • identifies the policy, institutional, pedagogical, accessibility, support-service, data and financing reforms required;
  • sets out governance arrangements and responsibilities at national, sub-national and school levels;
  • provides a basis for phased implementation, monitoring, accountability and future technical guidance; and
  • reflects meaningful participation by persons with disabilities and their representative organisations, learners, families, education personnel and other relevant stakeholders.

3. Objectives

  • Consolidate and critically analyse available national legislation, policies, data, studies, consultation findings and relevant international standards.
  • Identify systemic barriers, institutional gaps, enabling factors and priority reform areas for inclusive education in Syria.
  • Develop an agreed structure, conceptual foundation, theory of change, strategic results and substantive content for the National Framework.
  • Draft successive versions of the Framework through a structured and documented review process.
  • Support inclusive technical consultation and national validation of the draft Framework.
  • Develop an initial implementation and results framework that supports translation of the Framework into phased national action.
  • Ensure coherence with any regional or international technical review subsequently provided, without weakening national ownership or contextual relevance.

4. Scope of Work and Key Tasks

4.1 Inception and methodological planning

  • Participate in an inception meeting with TDH Italy, the Ministry of Education and designated stakeholders, held online or in person according to need and agreement.
  • Review the assignment, available documentation, consultation processes completed or planned, decision-making arrangements and expected approval pathway.
  • Prepare a detailed inception report setting out the proposed methodology, workplan, document map, stakeholder engagement approach, quality-assurance arrangements and detailed outline of the Framework.
  • Identify information gaps, issues requiring policy decisions and any additional targeted consultations or technical inputs required.

4.2 Desk review and national situation analysis

  • Review relevant Syrian legislation, decrees, executive instructions, education policies, curricula, standards, strategies, plans, administrative procedures and available data related to education and disability.
  • Review the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Article 24; the Convention on the Rights of the Child; Sustainable Development Goal 4; and relevant international and regional technical guidance.
  • Review , in agreement with TDH Italy, relevant national inclusive education frameworks from comparable contexts to identify transferable lessons, while avoiding the direct replication of external models.
  • Analyse available consultation reports and distinguish between verified evidence, official data, stakeholder perceptions and issues requiring further validation.
  • Prepare a concise situation and gap analysis identifying systemic barriers, existing capacities, opportunities, risks and priority areas for reform.
  • Prepare a benchmarking matrix comparing selected international guidance and relevant frameworks from comparable contexts against the Syrian legal, institutional and educational context, identifying transferable practices, contextual limitations and implications for the National Framework.

4.3 Consultation consolidation and supplementary engagement

  • Review the methodology, tools, representation and findings of consultations already undertaken.
  • Consolidate overlapping, complementary and divergent findings into a traceable analytical framework.
  • Identify stakeholder groups, geographic areas or technical themes requiring supplementary consultation.
  • Prepare interview guides, discussion tools or technical questions for any agreed supplementary consultations.
  • Facilitate or technically support agreed meetings, interviews or working sessions, including engagement with organisations of persons with disabilities, education personnel, families and learners where feasible and appropriate.
  • Document how consultation findings have informed the Framework and how significant divergent views have been addressed.

4.4 Development of the Framework architecture and substantive content

  • Develop a clear conceptual and rights-based foundation for inclusive education, including definitions and distinctions between exclusion, segregation, integration and inclusion.
  • Clearly define the scope of the Framework as system-wide, while ensuring that the barriers, rights and support requirements of learners with disabilities remain a central and substantive focus across all strategic pillars.
  • Propose the national vision, overall goal, guiding principles, theory of change, strategic results and strategic pillars.
  • Define policy directions, priority actions, institutional responsibilities and expected results under each strategic pillar.
  • Develop a coherent model for the identification of barriers, provision of classroom support, reasonable accommodation, individualised planning where required, referral, follow-up and transition between education levels.
  • Propose governance, coordination, accountability, financing, implementation and monitoring arrangements.
  • Ensure that the Framework addresses cross-cutting issues, including gender, protection, conflict sensitivity, displacement, poverty, geographic inequality, data protection and education in emergencies.

4.5 Drafting, review and revision

  • Prepare a detailed annotated outline for approval before full drafting.
  • Prepare in Arabic the first draft of the National Framework, including references and agreed annexes.
  • Present the draft to the technical group and other designated stakeholders.
  • Maintain a comment-response matrix recording each substantive comment, its source, the action taken and the rationale.
  • Prepare a second draft that reflects consolidated and approved feedback and clearly flags outstanding issues requiring a policy decision.

4.6 National validation and finalisation

  • Prepare the technical materials required for national validation, including a presentation, discussion questions and structured feedback tools.
  • Present and technically facilitate the validation of the draft Framework in coordination with TDH Italy and the Ministry of Education through in-person workshop.
  • Consolidate and analyse validation feedback, distinguishing technical revisions from policy decisions.
  • Revise and finalise the Framework based on feedback approved through the agreed governance mechanism.
  • Coordinate, in agreement with TDH Italy, with any regional or international expert or another partner and address agreed quality-assurance comments through the comment-response matrix.
  • The validation process shall be Ministry-led and structured to distinguish matters requiring technical revision from those requiring formal policy or institutional decisions.

4.7 Transition to implementation

  • Develop an initial phased implementation plan identifying priority actions, sequencing, responsible and supporting actors, indicative timing, dependencies and resource considerations.
  • Develop a results and monitoring framework with proposed indicators, definitions, data sources, frequency and responsible actors.
  • Prepare a list of secondary policies, standards, guidelines, tools and capacity-development packages required to operationalise the Framework.
  • Prepare an executive summary, a short policy brief and a final presentation for decision-makers and partners.

5. Minimum Technical Coverage of the Framework

The final structure will be agreed during the inception phase. At a minimum, the Framework should address:

  • purpose, scope, methodology and relationship with relevant national policies and legislation;
  • national situation and barrier analysis;
  • legal, conceptual and rights-based foundations and definitions;
  • vision, overall goal, theory of change, national results and guiding principles;
  • legislation, policy, governance, accountability and inter-ministerial coordination;
  • access, admission, attendance, retention, progression and transition across education levels and pathways;
  • curriculum, teaching and learning, assessment, examinations and reasonable accommodation;
  • teachers, school leadership, resource-room personnel, specialised staff and multidisciplinary support;
  • physical, communication, information and digital accessibility;
  • identification of barriers, educational assessment, support planning, referral pathways, assistive technology and related services;
  • learner protection, psychosocial wellbeing, prevention of violence, bullying and discrimination, and safeguarding;
  • participation of learners, families, communities and organisations of persons with disabilities;
  • disability-inclusive education data, research, monitoring and data protection;
  • financing, resource allocation and sustainability;
  • phased implementation, risk management and education in emergencies; and
  • institutional roles, results framework, indicators and accountability mechanisms.

6. Expected Deliverables

  1. Inception report

Methodology; detailed workplan; proposed allocation of the 60 working days; document map; stakeholder engagement and quality-assurance approach; information gaps; decision points; and annotated outline of the Framework

Within 10 working days of contract signature

*2 .*Desk review and situation/gap analysis

Review of national and international references; synthesis of available evidence; analysis of legislation, policy, systems, institutional and workforce capacities and current practice; identification of capacity-development priorities; and initial reform priorities.

Within three months duration based on the consultant offer

3. Consultation synthesis report

Consolidated findings; representation and evidence gaps; divergent views; supplementary engagement completed; and traceability between findings and proposed Framework content.

4. Framework architecture and annotated outline

Agreed vision, theory of change, strategic results, pillars, proposed chapter structure, governance logic and initial results chain.

5. First draft

Full draft of the National Framework, including references and agreed annexes, ready for structured technical review.

6. Second draft and validation package

Revised draft; comment-response matrix; validation presentation; discussion questions; and structured feedback tools.

7. Final validated Framework

Final Arabic Framework incorporating approved validation and quality-assurance comments; final comment-response matrix; and technical review of the English version prepared by an external translator to verify accuracy and consistency with the final Arabic version.

8. Implementation and communication package

Initial phased implementation plan; results and monitoring framework; list of required secondary tools; executive summary; policy brief; and final presentation.

Note: The proposed allocation totals 60 working days. Except for the inception report and the final deadline, the Consultant shall propose detailed delivery dates in the technical proposal and confirm them in the inception workplan. All deliverables must be completed within three months of the contract start date. Acceptance of each deliverable will depend on written approval by TDH Italy following consultation with the Ministry of Education and the designated technical reviewers.

7. Methodological and Quality Requirements

The Consultant is expected to apply the following requirements throughout the assignment:

  • Use a human-rights-based and social model of disability, consistent with the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.
  • Use respectful, non-stigmatising and consistent terminology in Arabic and English references.
  • Ensure meaningful participation of persons with disabilities and their representative organisations; consultation should not be limited to final-stage endorsement.
  • Differentiate clearly between official data, verified evidence, legal requirements, stakeholder perceptions and the Consultant’s analysis.
  • Reference all sources and avoid unsupported national-level claims or direct replication of another country’s framework.
  • Apply gender, age, protection, safeguarding, conflict-sensitivity and do-no-harm considerations.
  • Develop realistic and phased proposals that acknowledge capacity and resource constraints without reducing the State’s rights-based commitments.
  • Use accessible document structures and provide editable electronic versions of all outputs.
  • Maintain a transparent audit trail through consultation records, decision logs and comment-response matrices.
  • Comply with TDH Italy policies on child safeguarding, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, code of conduct, confidentiality and data protection.

8. Management, Coordination and Review Arrangements

  • The Consultant will be administratively managed by TDH Italy and will work in close technical coordination with the Ministry of Education and the designated national technical group.
  • TDH Italy will facilitate access to available project documents, consultation reports, relevant stakeholders and agreed coordination mechanisms.
  • Policy decisions and matters falling within the mandate of the Ministry of Education will be referred to the Ministry through the agreed coordination structure; the Consultant will not independently determine contested policy positions.
  • All substantive comments will be consolidated through an agreed focal point or review mechanism to minimise contradictory instructions and uncontrolled versioning.
  • The Consultant will submit editable versions of all deliverables and participate in review meetings as required within the agreed level of effort.
  • Where regional or international technical expertise becomes available, the Consultant will coordinate with the expert(s), participate in technical review sessions and address approved comments. Such support will complement, rather than replace, the national drafting process.
  • Any material changes to the scope, number of consultations, travel requirements or deliverables will require prior written agreement between TDH Italy and the Consultant.

9. Duration, Location and Indicative Level of Effort

The assignment is expected to require up to 60 working days over approximately four months. Work will combine home-based document review and drafting with in-person or online meetings, technical working sessions and validation activities. Travel within Syria may be required subject to prior agreement, access, security considerations and applicable TDH Italy procedures.

10. Required Qualifications and Experience

10.1 Education

  • Advanced university degree (PHD, Master’s degree or equivalent) in education, inclusive or special education, education policy and planning, disability studies, social sciences, public policy or another relevant field.

10.2 Professional experience

  • At least eight years of progressively responsible professional experience in education, education policy, system strengthening or a closely related field.
  • At least five years of demonstrated technical experience in inclusive education, disability inclusion or the rights of persons with disabilities, including research, policy or framework development, technical advisory work, system strengthening, or programme design and evaluation.
  • Proven experience in drafting national or institutional strategies, policies, frameworks, standards or implementation plans.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of the Syrian education system, institutional context and relevant national legislation and policy processes.
  • Experience working with ministries, public institutions and multi-stakeholder technical groups.
  • Experience designing, facilitating or analysing participatory consultations, including engagement with organisations of persons with disabilities.
  • Strong experience in evidence synthesis, policy analysis, results frameworks and professional writing skills.
  • Knowledge of international standards and technical guidance on inclusive education and disability rights.
  • Experience in education in emergencies, teacher development, curriculum and assessment, education data, school accessibility or inter-sectoral referral systems is an asset.

10.3 Language and technical skills

  • Excellent written and spoken Arabic, including demonstrated ability to draft complex policy documents clearly and precisely.
  • Good command of written and spoken English sufficient to review technical sources and coordinate with international experts.
  • Strong facilitation, consensus-building, analytical, presentation and document-management skills.
  • Proficiency in standard MS Office and online collaboration tools.

10.4 Core competencies

  • Strategic and systems thinking.
  • Commitment to inclusion, dignity, participation and non-discrimination.
  • Ability to manage diverse and potentially conflicting technical perspectives impartially.
  • Cultural sensitivity, political awareness, discretion and conflict-sensitive judgement.
  • Accuracy, accountability and ability to deliver high-quality work within agreed deadlines.

11. Application Requirements

Applicants should submit:

  • an updated curriculum vitae;
  • a technical proposal demonstrating understanding of the assignment and presenting the proposed methodology, proposed allocation of up to 60 working days and quality-assurance approach;
  • a financial proposal in Euros, with a clear breakdown of the professional fee by number of working days and daily rate. Any other reimbursable costs, if needed, must be listed separately with the relevant assumptions. Payment will be made in New Syrian Pounds using the exchange rate applied by TDH Italy on the payment date;
  • two relevant writing samples in Arabic, preferably a strategy, policy, national framework or comparable analytical document, with the applicant’s authorship role clearly stated;
  • contact details for at least three references; and
  • a declaration of availability during the proposed assignment period of the three contracted months and disclosure of any actual or potential conflict of interest.

12. Evaluation Criteria

Technical proposal - Understanding of the assignment; methodological quality; feasibility of the workplan; stakeholder engagement; and quality assurance 30%

Relevant technical experience - Inclusive education, disability inclusion, education-system strengthening and national policy/framework development - 25%

Contextual and institutional experience - Knowledge of the Syrian education system and experience working with government and multi-stakeholder processes. 10%

Qualifications and writing samples Academic background, analytical capacity and quality/relevance of submitted samples -5%

Financial proposal Cost-effectiveness and clarity of financial assumptions 30%

13. Payment Schedule

Payments will be linked to the satisfactory completion and written acceptance of deliverables. An indicative schedule is provided below and will be confirmed in the contract:

Milestone10%

Acceptance of Deliverable 1: inception report 20%

Acceptance of Deliverables 2 and 3: desk review/gap analysis and consultation synthesis 20%

Acceptance of Deliverables 4 and 5: Framework architecture and first complete draft 20%

Acceptance of Deliverable 6: second draft and validation package 30%

Acceptance of Deliverables 7 and 8: final validated Framework, review of the English translation, and implementation/communication package.

14. Ownership, Confidentiality and Ethical Obligations

  • All materials, data, consultation records, drafts and final products produced under this consultancy will remain the property of TDH Italy and/or the competent national authority, as specified in the contract.
  • The Consultant may not publish, circulate or use assignment materials outside the consultancy without prior written authorisation.
  • All sources must be appropriately acknowledged. Plagiarism, unattributed reproduction and undisclosed use of third-party intellectual property are prohibited.
  • The Consultant must protect confidential and personal information and follow agreed data-protection, consent and safeguarding procedures.
  • The Consultant will be required to sign and comply with TDH Italy’s Ethical Code, Code of Conduct, Child Safeguarding Policy, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse requirements, and other applicable policies.
  • Revisions reasonably required to bring a deliverable into conformity with the approved terms of reference and agreed quality standards are included in the consultancy fee, provided that the agreed scope has not materially changed.

opportunities.title: Finance Coordinator
opportunities.description:
About us

The War Child Alliance is an international non-governmental organization committed to providing psychosocial support, child protection, youth empowerment programming and quality education to the children affected by armed conflict. We implement evidence-based interventions to empower key stakeholders—including governments, educators, caregivers, and communities—to foster children’s wellbeing, education, and self-determination. We work with global teams with team members being based in different locations. War Child is currently operates in: Afghanistan, the Central African Republic, Colombia, DR Congo, Germany, Jordan, Lebanon, the occupied Palestinian territory, South Sudan, Sweden, Syria, Uganda, Ukraine (soon to be registered), and Yemen. We also have offices in the Netherlands and the United Kingdom.
Learn more about War Child and our programmes https://www.warchild.net/

Your mission

​​​​​The Finance Coordinator contributes to the effective and efficient implementation of the accounting processes, systems, financial planning, and reporting for the WC Projects to enable program staff and other stakeholders to implement the Project.
Ensures compliance with WC and donor financial and administrative rules for the files entrusted to him/her for follow-up. Ensure that accounting processes and systems are running effectively and efficiently. Responsible for supporting the Finance Manager in compliance with Local and external donor financial and administrative requirements.

About the role

1. Handling finances – 80%
• Follow up on Partners Periodic Financial Reports and burn rate reports.
• Checking the Partners financial supporting documents eligibility and compliance, and the data recording on the accounting system.
• Ensures that all bookkeeping/financial documents of partners and War Child are compiled and organized according to international auditing standards and donor and WC standards, polices, and guidance.
• Preparing the Partner's financial reports for recording on the WC accounting system.
• Review financial reports from partners in collaboration with the Program Team.
• Follow up with the WC partners and hold regular meetings.
• Supports WC Project Partners on all financial aspects.
• Assesses WC partners capacities in collaboration with the Program team and contributes to training when relevant.
• Manages the Partner Funding Agreement, the payments, and the advances to Partners.
• Monitors WC projects budgets and advises on the allocation of expenses.
• Updates WC projects budgets forecast of expenses in collaboration with the Program staff, and the Procurement and Logistics Senior Officers.
• Provide Senior Program staff with regular monthly financial analysis, highlighting overall challenges and opportunities.
• Review the monthly expenses allocated to the project and update the BFU.
• Drafting the donors financial reports.
• Participates in the monthly Grant review meetings and presents the spending status of grants he/she is following up on.
• Supporting the operations team, program team, and partners in preparations of new budgets and budget reallocations.
• Leading the Audit preparation, during the audit and for the implementation of audit recommendations findings.
• Advises and supports the Finance Manager in maintaining efficient financial workflows, control, and Segregation of Duties.
• Assess and mitigate financial risks, ensuring relevant organizational setup and reliable internal control system.
• Alert key staff on financial risks and responsibilities.

2. Handling Administration – 20%
• Line Manage and Supervises the Finance Officers
• Holding the filing system for the Grants Agreements.
• Holding the filing system for the partners’ Funding Agreements, financial reports, and financial documents.
• Complies with deadlines and reporting dates.

** This position is open for remote working

Your profile

A. Knowledge:

  • BA Degree in Accounting or similar degree
  • 4 to 5 years’ experience in similar positions with an NGO or INGO
  • Knowledge of and experience working on main international humanitarian donor-funded programs
  • Experience working in a consortium and with partners is an added value
  • Experience with training and capacity building on finance and administration

B. Experience & Qualifications:

  • Very strong computer skills, Microsoft office, especially Excel
  • Fluency in spoken and written English and Arabic.
  • Cultural sensitivity
  • Result-oriented
  • Attentive to details and cost-conscious
  • Works well in a small team
  • Flexibility and adaptability
  • Critical thinking and strong analytical skills
  • Excellent management skills, teamwork, and flexibility
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
  • Commitment to training, capacity building, and collaboration with local organizations

Deadline for Applications: 03 August 2026

Safeguarding and Integrity
Our work with children and at-risk adults to keep them safe is the most important thing we do. We are committed to the safeguarding of children and vulnerable adults in all areas of our work. We have zero tolerance for any behaviours and practices that puts children and/or vulnerable adults at risk of abuse and/or harm. All (prospective) employees will be expected to be compliant with and sign up to our Child Safeguarding policy, our Code of Conduct and PSEA: Adults at Risk Policy. You can find the Child Safeguarding and Adults at Risk policy here: Integrity & Safeguarding - Home

Justice, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (JEDI) and Belonging (DEIB)
We value diversity and inclusion and are committed to ensuring that all our people and job applicants are treated fairly, irrespective of where, what or whom they were born, or of other characteristics. We want to offer a safe and inclusive workplace where all our people, especially those who are currently marginalised or underrepresented, can be themselves at work. If you have any questions about our commitment to Justice, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (JEDI) and Belonging (DEIB) do get in touch: JEDI.team@warchild.net

opportunities.title: Learning and Adaptive Management Consultancy for Advancing Adaptation through Resilient mobility And Natural capital (AARAN) Project
opportunities.description:
BRCiS Consortium

Learning and Adaptive Management Consultancy for Advancing Adaptation through Resilient mobility And Natural capital (AARAN) Project

Terms of Reference

  1. Background

Building Resilient Communities in Somalia (BRCiS) is a Consortium of national and international organizations – Action Against Hunger (ACF), Concern Worldwide (Concern), GREDO, the International Rescue Committee (IRC), KAALO, Save the Children, and Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) as lead agency. BRCiS’ objective is to work across the humanitarian-development divide, supporting marginalized communities in disaster-prone, rural Somalia to become more resilient to shocks and stressed, including as a result of climate change. BRCiS approach is contextually adaptive, focused on the specific shocks, needs, and priorities of individual communities. BRCiS was established in 2013 and is now implementing projects funded by multiple humanitarian and development donors in more than ten regions of Somalia1.

2. Program Background

The Advancing Adaptation through Resilient mobility And Natural capital (AARAN) project is a three-year, FCDO-funded initiative under the Somalia Humanitarian and Resilience Building in Somalia (HARBS) Programme. Implemented by a consortium of five Members (NRC, Concern Worldwide, GREDO, KAALO, Lifeline Gedo) in partnership with IOM, AARAN targets approximately half-million Somalis across 15 districts in five federal Member States (Jubaland, Puntland, Galmudug, Hirshabelle and Southwest). The project integrates the complementary strengths of the BRCiS and Danwadaag into a single operational model centered on climate adaptation across rural-urban corridors.

AARAN’s Theory of Change (ToC) posits that supporting more climate-resilient systems will directly reduce the severity of humanitarian needs and forced displacement in Somalia. This impact is achieved when institutions and marginalised communities, including Displacement-Affected Communities (DACs), drive inclusive, locally-led, climate-adaptive solutions to climate-related shocks and stressors (Outcome). The ToC is operationalized through six interconnected Technical Workstreams (Outputs 1-6), each led by a designated Workstream Lead:

Table 1: AARAN Outputs and Workstream

Workstream, Focus Area, Lead Agency

Output 1- Housing, land and Property (HLP) Rights & Legal Identity- NRC

Output 2 - Ecosystem & Natural Resource Management- BRCiS Consortium Management Unit (CMU)

Output 3- Market Systems & Livelihoods- GREDO (with Concern Worldwide technical support on Self-help groups)

Output 4- Early Warning & Early Action (EWEA)- Concern Worldwide

Output 5- Durable Solutions & Urban Planning- Danwadaag Consortium Leadership Team (CLT)

Output 6- Evidence, Learning, and Adaptation- BRCiS CMU (with support of this learning partner)

Output 6 serves as the central coordination and learning platform of the project, responsible for ensuring that learning is not a siloed activity but a continuous, participatory process that drives strategic adaptation.

AARAN recognizes that meaningful learning and adaptive management cannot happen in isolation. The project operates with a prioritized Learning Ecosystem comprising diverse actors who should continuously coordinate closely, jointly identify learning priorities, and collectively reflect on evidence to inform adaptations. This ecosystem includes:

  1. Internal Consortium Structures:
    • Technical Workstream Leads (Outputs 1-6): Responsible for generating thematic evidence and identifying operational learning needs within their technical domains while Workstream 6 is the overall responsible workstream to oversee and manage the learning agenda by working as the bridge between the learning and adaptive management structure commissioned under this ToR and other Consortium structures.
    • Programme Management Group (PMG): Comprising senior technical leads from each implementing Partners, the PMG holds strategic oversight and decision-making authority for adaptive management.
    • MEAL Working Group: Provides technical rigor on monitoring, evaluation, and learning methodologies, supporting carrying out learning exercises in the field, ensuring data credibility and harmonization across the Consortium.
    • Finance Working Group: Ensures that proposed adaptations including value for money are fiscally viable, aligned with FCDO compliance, and can be implemented within existing budget and forecasting timelines.
    • Project Steering Committee (PSC): Provides governance-level oversight, including senior representation from Member organizations, and approves major strategic adaptations.
  2. Dedicated Learning & Evidence Partners:
    • AARAN Resilience & Impact Measurement Consultancy: Responsible for project resilience and impact measurement through baseline, routine community engagement and endline measurements. Their longitudinal data and routine community engagement is a critical input to the Learning Agenda.
    • FCDO Independent HARBS MEL Provider: Ensures AARAN’s adaptive management evidence, outcome harvesting, and learning products inform portfolio-wide measurement and coherence.
    • AARAN Learning and Adaptive Management Consultancy: This serves as the project's dedicated Learning Partner, tasked with operationalizing a dynamic, participatory Learning Agenda that evolves with the project's context and stakeholder priorities. In this capacity, the Learning Partner also functions as the Ecosystem Convenor, responsible for ensuring the learning ecosystem functions efficiently, facilitating coordination among all actors, and support translating evidence into actionable adaptations. Beyond curating this live framework, the partner leads targeted thematic learning exercises, synthesizes multi-source evidence into actionable insights
  3. Government & National Stakeholders:
    • Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) & Federal Member States (FMS): Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) & Federal Member States (FMS): Including the National Centre for Rural Development and Durable Solutions (NCRDS), Ministries of Environment & Climate Change (MoECC), Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA), National Identification & Registration Authority (NIRA), Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation (MOAI), Ministry of Livestock, Forestry and Range (MoLFR), Ministry of Planning, Investment and Economic Development (MoPIED) and Durable Solutions Technical Working Groups (DSTWGs). These actors are both partners in implementation and primary audiences for learning products aimed at influencing national policy and planning (e.g., Somalia’s National Adaptation Plan 2026-2030, the National Solutions Pathways Action Plan (NSPAC, 2024–2029), and National Transformation Plan (NTP 2025-2029) specially Pillar 4 of this framework on Environment and Climate Resilience.
  4. External Resilience & Peer Actors:
    • Somalia Cash Consortium, NGO Consort research and Working Group, WFP, FAO and similar actors: As peer resilience implementers, these actors are key for sharing cross-programme learning, avoiding duplication of research, and collectively influencing the broader Somalia resilience and climate adaptation evidence base.
  5. Target Communities & Local Actors:
    • Displacement-Affected Communities (DACs), Community Resilience Committees (CRCs), DAC Fora, Self-Help Groups (SHGs), Community Resilience Extension Workers (CREWs), etc: These are the key project participants and primary sources of experiential knowledge. Their feedback, lived experiences, and observed behavioural changes are essential data points for validating or challenging project assumptions.

It is important to note that BRCiS has already established a comprehensive Collaboration, Learning, and Adaptation (CLA) and Knowledge Management strategy, grounded in the USAID CLA approach. These strategies have been progressively operationalized across the Consortium, providing a solid foundation for this assignment. The AARAN Learning Agenda will build upon and refine this existing CLA framework, contextualizing it for the specific priorities of the AARAN project (rural-urban corridors, climate adaptation, and durable solutions). The Learning Partner will build upon and refine existing strategies rather than develop new frameworks from inception.

3. Structure of the Assignment, Objectives and Deliverables

This Terms of Reference is structured into two complementary lots, each with specific requirements and terms of engagement. Interested consulting firms are expected to submit technical and financial proposals for both lots, as the Consortium intends to engage a single partner to deliver the full scope of work, ensuring coherence and integration across the learning function.

  • Lot 1: Learning Ecosystem Coordination, Learning Agenda Stewardship & Adaptive Management
  • Lot 2: Thematic Learning Production & Dissemination

The Learning Partner will:

  • Facilitate systematic reflection and coordination across the learning ecosystem.
  • Steward and continuously update the AARAN Learning Agenda as a living document.
  • Conduct targeted technical and thematic learning exercises, produce high-quality learning products and syntheses and support strategic dissemination to influence policy, programming, and the broader resilience and climate adaptation evidence base in Somalia

4. Lot 1: Learning Ecosystem Coordination, Learning Agenda Stewardship & Adaptive Management

4.1 Objective: To operationalize and steward the AARAN Learning Agenda as a dynamic, participatory framework that captures evolving learning priorities, and to facilitate effective coordination and adaptive management across the AARAN learning ecosystem.

4.2 Scope of Work: The Learning Partner will:

  • Update and Steward the Learning Agenda: Engage with project stakeholders to update and refine the existing BRCiS Learning Agenda, identifying 3–4 priority thematic areas with particular attention to rural-urban dynamics linking natural ecosystems, markets and livelihoods, social interaction, and mobility—themes that hold potential influence on the wider resilience, climate adaptation, and durable solutions system architecture in Somalia. For each priority theme, the consultant will define learning questions, responsible stakeholders, workplans, and expected products.
  • Facilitate Bi-Annual Internal Coordination, Learning, and Adaptive Management Events: Convene Workstream Leads, PMG, MEAL and Finance Working Groups, and CMU for reflection sessions to review progress against the Learning Agenda, assess evidence produced, and identify gaps. The Learning Partner’s participation in these sessions will be virtual/remote and will not include in-person travel. In preparation for these sessions, the Learning Partner will compile and synthesize learning products from across the Learning Ecosystem once every six months, producing concise briefs with key recommendations for adaptive management. Additionally, these sessions may serve as a forum to identify and propose specific thematic learning exercises for consideration under Lot 2, where a demonstrated need exists and internal capacity is insufficient to address the identified learning priority. Proposals emerging from these sessions will be subject to the standard pitch and approval process outlined in Section 5.2
  • Facilitate Annual External Learning Events: Convene representatives of the broader learning ecosystem including government counterparts, peer agencies, FCDO, and community representatives to participate in systematic reflection, identify synergies, and translate collective learning into concrete programmatic adaptations.

4.3 Deliverables

The timelines and frequencies specified in Table 2 are provisional and provided as indicative guidelines to assist applicants in developing their proposals. Final deliverable schedules, including specific dates and sequencing, will be mutually agreed upon and formalized during the inception phase following the consultant's onboarding.

Table 2: Lot 1 deliverables

  1. Deliverable: Inception Report (detailed workplan, methodology, stakeholder engagement strategy)

    Description: Comprehensive workplan detailing methodology, stakeholder engagement strategy, risk mitigation measures, and a phased implementation schedule for both lots.

    Timeline and Frequency: September 2026 (Once)

2. Deliverable: Updated AARAN Learning Agenda (priority themes, questions, methodology matrix, operational plan)

Description: Refined learning agenda articulating 3–4 priority thematic areas, corresponding learning questions, methodological approaches, responsible stakeholders, and operational plans.

Timeline and Frequency: October 2026 (Once)

3. Deliverable: Bi-Annual Synthesis of Learning Products with Adaptive Management Recommendations

Description: Consolidated synthesis of learning products generated across the Consortium, accompanied by actionable adaptive management recommendations for internal decision-making

Timeline and Frequency: Bi-annually (5 cycles): March 2027, September 2027, March 2028, September 2028, March 2029

4. Deliverable: Annual External Learning Event Report and Synthesis

Description: Comprehensive report and synthesis documenting key discussions, emerging insights, and collective recommendations from the annual external learning convening

Timeline and Frequency: Annually (3 events): May 2027, May 2028, May 2029

5. Deliverable: End-of-Project Learning Synthesis (cumulative report on key themes, adaptation case studies, and recommendations)

Description: Cumulative final report distilling key thematic findings, documented adaptation case studies, and forward-looking recommendations to inform future resilience and climate adaptation programming in Somalia

Timeline and Frequency: July 2029

opportunities.title: Remote Climate Consultancy to Strengthen Climate Adaptation Programme Positioning and Readiness for Future Climate Funding
opportunities.description:
Background

Concern recognises climate change as a significant driver of poverty, inequality and humanitarian need. Concern's Climate Change Adaptation (CCA) Policy (2026–2035) and Organisational Strategy commit the organisation to ensuring all programmes are climate-sensitive, while strengthening climate adaptation and resilience where climate risks are a significant driver of vulnerability. Concern also aims to strengthen its capacity to secure climate funding to support locally led adaptation and resilience-building efforts.

Many Concern country programmes are already delivering interventions that contribute to climate adaptation—including resilient livelihoods, disaster risk reduction, climate-informed health and nutrition, WASH and natural resource management. However, these programmes are not always explicitly designed or positioned as climate adaptation programmes, limiting opportunities to access dedicated climate funding.

This consultancy will support four selected country programmes to strengthen climate adaptation thinking, programme conceptualisation and programme positioning for future climate funding. Through facilitated workshops, technical coaching and programme design support, the consultant will help country teams identify climate adaptation opportunities within existing programmes, strengthen programme logic using appropriate design tools, and develop practical recommendations to improve readiness for future climate funding opportunities.

For the purpose of this consultancy, climate funding refers to dedicated climate finance mechanism, as well as institutional and foundation led donor opportunities where climate adaptation and resilience are central programme objectives.

Concern will select four priority countries before the consultancy begins. The consultancy will focus on Foundation and Emerging Readiness country programmes where targeted support is expected to strengthen climate adaptation thinking, programme conceptualisation and future readiness for climate funding.

Purpose and objective

This consultancy will support four countries to develop and strengthen programme designs and interventions in order to pre-position for climate funding, through a combination of facilitated reflection, programme review, workshops, targeted technical coaching, training and practical recommendations. The consultancy will support country teams to identify priority programme concepts and strengthen programme logic for future funding opportunities.

Methodology and core support

  1. Programme review and climate adaptation opportunities

The consultant will work with each selected country programme to reviewing existing programmes, identify interventions and good practices with relevance to climate adaptation and resilience, and explore opportunities to strengthen climate adaptation thinking and future climate funding potential. This process will help country teams identify and prioritise programme areas with the greatest potential for future development.

The consultant will:

  • Review existing programme experience, strategic priorities and emerging ideas.
  • Identify interventions and good practices that contribute to climate adaptation and resilience
  • Facilitate discussion to identify opportunities to strengthen climate adaptation thinking across existing programmes and prioritise those with the greatest potential for future climate funding

2. Programme conceptualisation and positioning

Building on the programme review, the consultant will support country teams to strengthen programme design, articulate a clearer climate adaptation rationale and improve programme positioning for future climate funding opportunities. Through facilitated workshops, targeted coaching and practical technical guidance, the consultancy will strengthen country teams’ capacity to apply climate adaptation concepts and programme design approaches beyond the consultancy.

The consultant will:

  • facilitated workshops and programme discussions
  • provide targeted coaching, technical advice and practical learning on climate adaptation programme design
  • support programme conceptualisation using appropriate programme design tools (e.g. objective trees, theories of change or results chains)
  • strengthen programme logic, climate adaptation framing and programme positioning.

3. Recommendations and roadmap

The consultant will work with each country team to translate the outputs of the consultancy into practical recommendations and a clear roadmap for strengthening programme quality and future readiness for climate funding beyond the consultancy period.

The consultant will:

  • Provide practical recommendations to strengthen climate adaptation approaches and programme positioning, specific to the local context
  • Identify priority programme concepts for future development
  • Identify future climate funding pathways, in collaboration with the Climate and DRR Unit and Fundraising where appropriate
  • Develop a practical roadmap outlining priority next steps for each country team.

The consultancy will be delivered in close collaboration with the Climate and DRR Unit and Fundraising teams. Where possible, activities will be co-facilitated with members of the Climate and DRR Unit to strengthen internal capacity. Throughout the consultancy, the consultant will capture and document practical approaches, programme design tools and decision-making processes that can be adapted and reused across Concern's wider climate adaptation portfolio.

Scope of work / Key deliverables

The consultant is expected to:

  • Deliver tailored workshops and programme conceptualisation sessions for four country programmes.
  • Review existing programmes and identify interventions, approaches and good practices with relevance to climate adaptation and resilience.
  • Support country teams to strengthen programme conceptualisation and programme design using appropriate tools (e.g. objective trees, theories of change, results chains or other programme design approaches).
  • Strengthen programme logic, climate adaptation framing and programme positioning for future climate funding opportunities.
  • Produce country-specific recommendations and roadmaps outlining priority programme concepts, actions and next steps to strengthen climate adaptation programming and readiness for future climate funding.
  • Work with the Climate and DRR Unit and Fundraising teams, where appropriate, to validate programme positioning and identify priority funding pathways.
  • Facilitate a final learning workshop with participating country teams, the Climate and DRR Unit and Fundraising to share lessons learned and recommendations.
