  • Flexible Leave Time – Between vacation days, personal leave days, and holidays, you have ample opportunities to take time off when you need it.

Alight is an Equal Opportunity Employer offering employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, citizenship, physical or mental disability, or protected veteran status. Alight complies with all applicable laws governing nondiscrimination in employment.

opportunities.title: Programme Development Manager, Syria
opportunities.description:
Programme Development Manager, Syria

The starting salary package for this position is £54,544 GBP / approx. $73,000 USD including all allowances.

This is an unaccompanied post.

About MAG:

MAG (Mines Advisory Group) is an international humanitarian organisation based in Manchester, UK, and working in 32 countries. We remove landmines and unexploded ordnance to release safe and productive land for communities, and work to reduce the threat of armed violence by supporting governments to safely manage weapons and ammunition. In 1997, MAG was a co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize for our work campaigning for the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention.

About the role:

Reporting to the Country Director, the Programme Development Manager plays a leading role in developing our evidence-based programme strategy, quality management, and impact. You will ensure that our work in Syria is needs-driven and results-based as well as remaining closely monitored and funded in timely and appropriate ways. You will work in close collaboration with our programme team in Syria, the regional management unit, and MAG’s global support teams, to develop and adapt our forward-looking operational and funding development strategy. You will act as a key representative of MAG’s Syria programme to ensure that MAG is recognised for its leadership and coordination in humanitarian mine action to donors, peer organisations, partners, humanitarian fora, and coordination bodies. You will foster crosscutting initiatives to enhance diversity, integrity, inclusiveness, and accountability within our programme teams, and will ultimately take responsibility for programme development and implementation. This is a challenging and varied role which offers the opportunity to effect meaningful change and grow our lifesaving work in Syria.

About the Syria programme:

MAG has been responding to the Syria crisis since 2013, working to support development by finding and destroying the explosive remnants of war so that communities can raise their families and pursue their livelihoods in a safe and secure environment, free from fear of death or injury.

Requirements:

You will be an experienced humanitarian manager with significant relevant experience in programme quality management and community inclusion. You should have excellent people management skills, with experience mentoring and supporting staff both directly and remotely and proven capacity to work on safeguarding related matters. You should have a sound understanding of the humanitarian, development, and mine action sectors, with significant experience developing, coordinating, managing, monitoring, and evaluating a range of programmes ideally within the mine action sector. Experience working in the Middle East is essential, particularly working with a range of humanitarian actors including national authorities, and local and international organisations.

Fluency in English is essential, and Arabic language skills would be highly advantageous.

We’re looking for someone with:

  • Experience in programme quality management and community inclusion
  • Experience working with a range of humanitarian actors, including national authorities, and local and international organisations
  • Broad understanding of the humanitarian, development, triple nexus and where possible mine action sectors
  • Some understanding of Mine Action activities undertaken by MAG

Please note that as part of MAG's commitment to safeguarding, this post is subject to background checks before an offer of employment is confirmed. For more information on MAG’s approach to safeguarding and background checks on our website**.**

MAG is committed to the principles of diversity, equality and inclusion. If you think you would be suited to one of our roles we would welcome your application regardless of your background. We strive to provide an inclusive and supportive working environment where all employees feel respected and supported in fulfilling their potential.

Benefits:

  • Renumeration Package: £54,544 per annum including basic salary and all allowances and this increases with service.
  • Accommodation: MAG will provide accommodation in-country.
  • Leave: We recognise our staff work hard and need the appropriate time out to stay motivated. You'll have a minimum of eight weeks out of the programme per year.
  • Flights: MAG provides four international flights home per year.
  • Insurance: Internationally contracted, programme based staff are automatically covered by MAG's comprehensive insurance package including: Personal accident and medical expenses insurance; Death by natural causes insurance and access to 24-hour medical assistance.

Org. Setting and Reporting

This position is located in the Crisis Response Division (CRD) in the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). OCHA is part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA also ensures there is a framework within which each actor can contribute to the overall response efforts. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention and facilitate sustainable solutions. This Recruit from Roster (RfR) is being advertised for the position of Humanitarian Affairs Officer / Head of Sub-Office in Sittwe, Myanmar. Under the overall supervision of the Head of Office, OCHA Myanmar, the incumbent reports to the Deputy Head of Office for Field Coordination.

Responsibilities

Within delegated authority, the Humanitarian Affairs Officer / Head of Sub-Office will be responsible for the following duties: • Manages day-to-day operations of OCHA Rakhine, while monitors, analyzes and reports on humanitarian developments, disaster relief/management or emergency situations in assigned country/area. • Organizes and prepares studies on humanitarian, emergency relief and related issues; organizes follow-up work, including interagency technical review meetings to support policy development work and decision-making on important issues overseeing the OCHA Rakhine team • Drafts and prepares regular situation papers/reports highlighting relevant operational factors affecting the humanitarian situation and response efforts. • Prepares or contributes to the preparation of various written reports, documents and communications, e.g. drafts sections of studies, background papers, policy guidelines, parliamentary documents, briefings, case studies, presentations, correspondence, etc. • Assists in the preparation, implementation and monitoring of the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) • Ensures appropriate monitoring and reporting mechanisms; provides information and advice on a range of related issues • Reviews and provides advice on policy issues related to safeguarding humanitarian principles and ensuring the effective delivery of humanitarian assistance. • Partners with other humanitarian agencies to plan and evaluate humanitarian and emergency assistance programmes and help ensure that latest findings, lessons learned, policy guidelines, etc. are incorporated into these activities, including gender-related considerations • Provides substantial support to sector/cluster working groups as required and facilitate exchange on cross cutting issues • Establishes and maintains contacts with authorities, other UN, non-governmental organizations, diplomatic missions, media, etc. • Supports advocacy initiatives on issues impacting humanitarian needs and response efforts through the collection of information, liaison with humanitarian partners, government officials, the media, etc • Manages the production of appeals for international assistance; ensures the proper use and spending of donor contributions channeled through OCHA. • Undertakes and provides support to technical assistance and other field missions, e.g. participates in field trips to undertake in-depth reviews of specific country coordination mechanisms. • Organizes and participates in work groups, meetings, conferences, consultations with other agencies and partners on humanitarian and emergency relief-related matters. • Performs other duties as required.

Competencies

• PROFESSIONALISM: Knowledge of a range of humanitarian assistance, emergency relief and related human rights issues, including approaches and techniques to address difficult problems. Analytical capacity and in particular the ability to analyze and articulate the humanitarian dimension of issues which require a coordinated UN response. Ability to identify issues and judgment in applying technical expertise to resolve a wide range of problems. Ability to conduct research, including ability to evaluate and integrate information from a variety of sources and assess impact on the humanitarian rights situation in assigned country/area. Ability to work under extreme pressure, on occasion in a highly stressful environment (e.g. civil strife, natural disasters and human misery); ability to provide guidance to new/junior staff. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Able to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. • TEAMWORK: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings • PLANNING & ORGANIZING: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently.

Education

Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in political science, social science, public administration, international studies, economics, engineering, earth sciences or a related field. A first-level university degree in combination with an additional two (2) years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Work Experience

A minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian affairs, emergency preparedness, crisis/emergency relief management, rehabilitation, development, or other related area is required. Experience supervising a team in a humanitarian context is required. Experience negotiating humanitarian access in a complex emergency setting with state and non-state actors is required Humanitarian experience in the field (actual setting where a mission and/or project is being implemented) in emergency situations (complex emergency or natural disaster) is required. Experience representing a UN agency, NGO or similar organization at sub-national level is desirable

Languages

English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required.

Assessment

Evaluation of qualified candidates may include an assessment exercise which may be followed by a competency-based interview.

Special Notice

opportunities.title: Program Specialist – Localization (Consultant)
opportunities.description:
A. About Asian Disaster Preparedness Center

ADPC is an autonomous international organization established for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes with a vision of safer communities and sustainable development through disaster risk reduction and climate resilience in Asia and the Pacific. Established in 1986 as a technical capacity-building center, ADPC has grown and expanded its role to serve scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes. ADPC employs a wide range of professional expertise typically required for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR).

ADPC develops and implements cross-sectoral projects/programs on the strategic themes of Risk Knowledge and Geoinformatics, Policy and Institutional System, Effective Localization for Resilience, Climate Services, Resilient Planning and Implementation, Preparedness and Anticipatory Action, Nature based Solutions, Financing for Resilience, Resilient Recovery, Food and Water Security, Disaster Risk Finance Insurance, Health Risk Management, Urban & Infrastructure Resilience, Private Sector Engagement, and ADPC Knowledge Academy. Our strategic themes are complemented and underpinned by the cross-cutting themes of gender equality and social inclusion, disaster and climate innovations, and regional and transboundary cooperation.

Through its work, ADPC supports the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the New Urban Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, the agenda defined at the World Humanitarian Summit in 2016, and other relevant international frameworks.

For details, please refer to the ADPC website at http://www.adpc.net/

B. Department Introduction:

The Preparedness and Climate Action (PCA) Department of ADPC advances ADPC Strategy 2030 by strengthening disaster preparedness, anticipatory action, emergency response, resilient recovery, and climate resilience across Asia and the Pacific. The department works with governments, national and local institutions, civil society organizations, volunteer networks, the private sector, communities, and other traditional and non-traditional actors to promote inclusive, locally led, and whole-of-society approaches to disaster risk management. In line with ADPC’s strategic priorities, PCA supports countries and communities in developing and operationalizing preparedness, response, recovery, and climate action frameworks, plans, systems, and capacities before, during, and after disasters. It also promotes localization, gender equality and social inclusion, innovation, regional cooperation, knowledge exchange, and partnerships to ensure that disaster preparedness and climate action are practical, evidence-informed, sustainable, and responsive to the needs of at-risk communities.

C. Statement of Intent:

ADPC is implementing Phase 3 of the Asian Preparedness Partnership (APP), a multi-stakeholder localization partnership launched in 2016 in response to the World Humanitarian Summit’s call to shift power to national and local actors in disaster preparedness and response. APP Phase 3 is aligned with ADPC Strategy 2030 and the ADPC Strategic Action Plan 2026-2030 which identifies localization as a priority area of action for strengthening disaster risk reduction, preparedness, response, recovery, and climate resilience across Asia and the Pacific. Through APP, ADPC advances this localization priority by strengthening nationally owned, and regionally supported multi-stakeholder partnerships that bring together government, civil society, the private sector, and other local actors to lead, plan, finance, implement, and sustain locally led preparedness and resilience actions. The APP has been supported by the Gates Foundation since its inception in 2016.

APP operates in seven countries: Cambodia, Lao PDR, Nepal, Pakistan, the Philippines, Myanmar, and Sri Lanka. Each country has established a National Preparedness Partnership (NPP) comprising government, civil society networks, and the private sector, with engagement and cooperation from ADPC. Phase 3 focuses on ensuring the sustainability of NPPs and the regional partnership beyond the project duration, as well as developing localization models based on the implementation of initiatives supported by the Asian Disaster Readiness Fund (ADRF).

To support the implementation of APP Phase 3, ADPC is seeking to engage a Program Specialist – Localization (Consultant). The incumbent will manage the implementation of the Asian Preparedness Partnership Phase 3 (APP3) during its life through 31 July 2027. The Consultant will be responsible for ensuring the timely completion of all APP3 outputs and contractual deliverables while leading the programme's sustainability and institutionalization agenda. This includes supporting the sustainability of APP, National Preparedness Partnerships (NPPs), documenting and synthesizing localization models and good practices, advancing the operationalization of the Asian Disaster Readiness Fund (ADRF), and preparing programme legacy and knowledge products.

The Consultant will undertake these responsibilities while ensuring compliance with donor requirements, quality standards, monitoring and reporting obligations, and effective knowledge management throughout the programme close-out period.

Note: It is not the intent of this ToR to cover every aspect of the position requirements, rather to highlight the most important areas of personal and joint responsibilities.

D. Responsibilities and Tasks:

The position will provide technical, operational, and administrative support to ensure the timely delivery of programme activities and outputs, including activities implemented through APP and ADPC Strategy 2030’s localization priority area of action, as reflected in the Strategic Action Plan 2026–2030.

1. Completion of APP3 Delivery

  • Coordinate implementation of all activities as per the workplan and monitor progress against agreed milestones.
  • Ensure timely completion of all contractual deliverables, reporting obligations and programme close-out requirements.
  • Coordinate implementation across participating countries to ensure consistency, quality and timely delivery of regional and country-level outputs.
  • Support planning and delivery of regional meetings, APPRSC processes, policy dialogues, and other project deliverables.
  • Ensure compliance with donor requirements, organizational policies, and reporting obligations.

2. Technical Programme Support

  • Support sustainability planning and institutionalization of National Preparedness Partnerships across APP3 Project countries : Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Philippines and Sri Lanka and promoting locally led disaster preparedness and resilience.

  • Coordinate the documentation, analysis and dissemination of localization models, good practices and lessons emerging from APP implementation across participating countries.

  • Lead the preparation of the ADRF Strategy and Operationalization Document, including governance arrangements, partnership approaches, capitalization options and implementation roadmap until the life of the Project.

  • Facilitate the development of regional synthesis reports, knowledge products, technical briefs and communication materials highlighting programme achievements and lessons learned.

  • Ensure all project documentation, knowledge assets and technical resources are completed, quality assured and archived before programme closure.

  • Organize strategic events included in the work plan until 31 July 2027.

    3. Monitoring, Reporting, and Quality Assurance

  • Consolidate evidence demonstrating programme outcomes, sustainability achievements and institutional changes across participating countries.

  • Coordinate preparation of the final programme results report and evidence package for donor reporting and organizational learning.

  • Under the supervision of the M&E Lead, ensure all information and data/statistics are collected, updated, maintained, and shared through regular progress reports, program performance monitoring sheets, including the development of data collection tools and templates.

  • Draft project progress reports and technical documentation for management review.

  • Draft and edit technical reports, special reports, and other related program documents.

    4. Gender and Diversity Integration:

  1. Ensure integration of gender into APP3 Project implementation.
  2. Bring together and manage a diverse group of stakeholders and people from different backgrounds, countries, race, religious beliefs, ethnicity, age, gender, physical abilities, political beliefs, and socio-economic status for successful implementation of APP3 Project interventions.

This ToR covers the general responsibilities and representative tasks of this position. Other tasks may be assigned as necessary according to program priorities and needs.

Deliverables

  • All APP3 outputs and contractual deliverables completed in accordance with the approved workplan and donor requirements.
  • Sustainability plans prepared for National Preparedness Partnerships and Regional Platform across participating countries.
  • Regional synthesis report documenting APP localization models, lessons learned and recommendations completed.
  • Progress reports submitted during the project period
  • Final programme report, knowledge products and other documents completed

disseminated and / or archived as appropriate.

E. Reporting Arrangements:

The Consultant will report to the Unit Head, Resilience Building and Localization, under the overall guidance of the PCA Director. The Consultant will work with other Unit Head Project/Program Managers, Specialists, and Coordinators, as necessary.

F. Required Qualifications:

Required Qualifications and Specifications

  • Master's degree in Disaster Management, Emergency Management, Public Health, or related disciplines with substantial experience in the Asia-Pacific region.
  • A minimum of 8 years of professional experience in program management, advocacy, knowledge management, communication, etc., in Disaster Management or a related field, is required; A minimum of 3 years of experience in international organizations or IGO is required.
  • Excellent English language skills, both oral and written, are required.
  • Analytical capacity and the demonstrated ability to process, analyze and synthesize complex, technical information into user-friendly formats and products.
  • Substantial experience assisting in the design, monitoring, and evaluation of disaster preparedness and capacity development programs.
  • Advance knowledge and understanding of current discourse related to disaster risk reduction and humanitarian actions, including the existing disaster risk management systems, policy, and legal framework in the program countries.
  • Demonstrated experience in institutional strengthening, localization, partnership development, knowledge management, and development of regional strategies and technical guidance documents.
  • Proven ability to support the development of high-quality knowledge products, including the development of multimedia products, and provide guidance and training on the development of knowledge products.
  • Communicate effectively in writing to a varied and broad audience in a concise and straightforward manner.
  • High level of competence in writing and editing reports and other technical communications.
  • Ability to work under stress and demanding circumstances.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Self-motivated, proactive, and takes initiative.
  • Demonstrated ability to plan and organize work & time independently.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, team-oriented work style, and experience in working in a multi-cultural environment.
  • Strong networking capacity and understanding of humanitarian and development nexus at local and regional levels.
  • Strong desire to learn, undertake new challenges, must be creative problem-solver and must have self-confidence, willingness to work hard, good sense of humor but with seriousness about the quality and excellence of work.

G. Duty Station:

Bangkok, Thailand, with possible travel to program countries as required.

H. Contract Duration:

September 2026 – July 2027

I. Itinerary:

During official missions outside the duty station, the Consultant will be entitled to local and international travel, daily subsistence allowance, accommodation, and other related travel costs in accordance with ADPC financial policy. Reimbursement of general and administrative expenses related to programme implementation will be subject to prior approval by the respective supervisor identified above.

J. Condition of Payment:

The Consultant will be paid a monthly consultant fee based on the prior experience and salary records. Payment will be made upon submission of monthly timesheets. In addition, the Consultant may be reimbursed for programme-related costs incurred for implementation of programme activities, subject to prior approval in accordance with ADPC’s Authorization and Approval Levels.

K. Mode of Payment:

Payments shall be made through bank transfer, based on monthly timesheets.

opportunities.title: Governance Consultant
opportunities.description:
Governance Consultant

Location: Remote (with participation in online meetings and one in-person workshop)

Duration: 15 Aug – 23 Dec 2026

Application Deadline: 11.08.2026

About SARD

SARD is a regional feminist oral history network working across the Arabic-speaking region to document, preserve, and activate the lived experiences, political agency, and collective memory of feminist actors, grassroots communities, and marginalized groups. Founded in Feb- 2022 by four feminist organizations; Al-Rowat for Studies and Research, Badael, Knowledge Workshop, and Women and Memory Forum. SARD is currently entering a new phase of institutional and governance development.

Purpose of the Consultancy

The consultant will accompany and facilitate SARD members through a participatory governance exploration process that enables informed collective decision-making regarding SARD's future institutional form. The consultant is expected to design and facilitate a feminist process that enables members to critically assess governance alternatives, clarify governance needs, identify institutional implications, and collectively identify the most suitable governance and institutional pathway for SARD.

Scope of Work

The consultant is expected to undertake the following:

Phase I: Governance Assessment

  • Review SARD's current governance arrangements, host modality, and decision-making practices.
  • Conduct interviews and consultations with founding members.
  • Identify strengths, limitations, governance gaps, and future institutional needs.
  • Produce an inception note outlining the proposed methodology and workplan.

Phase II: Governance Exploration

The consultant will:

  • Map and present comparative governance and institutional models relevant to regional and transnational feminist networks, including case studies of governance arrangements adopted by collaborative networks, membership-based organizations, and alliances.
  • Facilitate critical reflection on the opportunities, challenges, and implications of different governance modalities for SARD.

Phase III: Facilitation and Collective Governance Process

The consultant will:

  • Design and facilitate a series of participatory governance discussions with SARD members throughout the consultancy period.
  • Facilitate one two-day in-person governance workshop to deepen collective reflection and dialogue.
  • Guide discussions to ensure meaningful participation, shared understanding, and informed collective deliberation.
  • Document key discussions, emerging reflections, areas of convergence, and outstanding questions throughout the process**.**

Phase IV: Institutional Roadmap

Building on the outcomes of the governance exploration and facilitation process, the consultant will:

  • Synthesize the findings and conclusions emerging from the governance discussions and in-person workshop.
  • Develop a governance roadmap outlining the proposed institutional pathway, institutional arrangements, transition phases, governance milestones, and priority actions.
  • Produce a two-page final consultancy report.

Required Profile and Qualifications

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • Proven track record in designing and facilitating participatory and multi-stakeholder processes.
  • Proven track record in facilitating feminist dialogue, collective reflection, and participatory decision-making processes.
  • Proven track record in supporting regional networks, coalitions, or collaborative initiatives.
  • Experience in organizational governance, institutional development, or organizational transformation processes.
  • Excellent knowledge of the Arabic-speaking region and its civil society/ feminist movements landscape.
  • Strong understanding of feminist facilitation approaches, collective leadership, and participatory governance.
  • Ability to synthesize complex discussions into clear and actionable recommendations.
  • Excellent written and spoken Arabic.

opportunities.title: CONSULTANCY TO CONDUCT A MARKET ASSESSMENT OF ACCREDITED TRAINING INSTITUTIONS AND JOB-READY SKILLS FOR VULNERABLE YOUTH (18–35 YEARS) IN NAIROBI COUN
opportunities.publisher: Center for Domestic Training and Development
opportunities.description:
RMS OF REFERENCE (TOR)
Re-Advertisement
CONSULTANCY TO CONDUCT A MARKET ASSESSMENT OF ACCREDITED TRAINING INSTITUTIONS AND JOB-READY SKILLS FOR VULNERABLE YOUTH (18–35 YEARS) IN NAIROBI COUNTY AND THE THIKA ROAD ECONOMIC CORRIDOR
1. Background;
The Centre for Domestic Training and Development (CDTD) is a Kenyan non-governmental organization committed to advancing decent work, skills development, labour rights, and economic empowerment for vulnerable populations, particularly women, youth, migrant workers, domestic workers, refugees, survivors of trafficking, and host communities. For over two decades, CDTD has championed innovative interventions that improve livelihoods through technical skills development, advocacy, labour mobility, and market-driven employment pathways.
CDTD works closely with industry, employers, development partners and government agencies to ensure that training programmes respond to labour market demand and lead to meaningful employment, entrepreneurship and economic inclusion.
CDTD is implementing the Jenga Ajira Project, an 18-month youth employability initiative targeting vulnerable youth aged 18–35 years across Nairobi County and the Thika Road Economic Corridor. The project seeks to equip young people with market-driven technical and vocational skills while facilitating their transition into internships, apprenticeships, self-employment and decent work opportunities.
To support evidence-based decision-making in selecting suitable training institutions, CDTD seeks to engage an experienced consultant to undertake a comprehensive market survey of accredited learning institutions and job-ready skills within Nairobi and Kiambu (Thika Road Economic Corridor) Counties in close proximity to EAIHM community.
2. Purpose of the Consultancy;
To conduct a comprehensive market assessment of accredited learning institutions offering market-driven, job-ready training programmes in Nairobi and Kiambu (Thika Road Economic Corridor) Counties and provide evidence-based recommendations on institutions that best meet the quality, accreditation, employability and industry linkage requirements of the Jenga Ajira Project.
The consultancy will provide CDTD with a credible, evidence-based market assessment report identifying the most suitable accredited learning institutions and job-ready training programmes in Nairobi and Kiambu (Thika Road Economic Corridor) Counties. The findings will guide strategic partnerships under the Jenga Ajira Project, ensuring selected institutions deliver quality, industry-relevant training with demonstrable pathways to certification, internships, attachments and sustainable employment for vulnerable youth.

3. Objectives of the Assignment;
The consultant shall carry out:
a) Institutional Mapping: Identify and profile accredited learning institutions offering technical, vocational and job-ready training programmes within Nairobi and Kiambu (Thika Road Economic Corridor) Counties.
b) Training Programme Assessment; Assess and compare market-responsive training programmes offered by the institutions, courses, while considering labour market demand and future employment potential.
c) Institutional Capacity Assessment: Evaluate each institution against agreed quality parameters, including:
I.TVETA/ NITA registration and accreditation
II.Relevant examination and certification bodies
III.CBET delivery capacity
IV.Quality of trainers
V.Training infrastructure and equipment
VI.Student support services
VII.Gender responsiveness
VIII.Safeguarding policies
IX.Capacity to support vulnerable youth
X.Graduate tracking mechanisms
XI.Industry engagement
d) Employability Assessment; Assess institutional capacity to:
I.Secure industrial attachments
II.Facilitate internships
III.Coordinate apprenticeships
IV.Link graduates to employment
V.Support entrepreneurship pathways
VI.Demonstrate graduate employment outcomes
e) Training Analysis; By determining;
I.Intake schedules
II.Training duration
III.Examination cycles
IV.Certification timelines
V.Graduation periods
VI.Cost for each course identified
f) Industry Linkages: Assess the strength of partnerships between institutions and employers, industries, companies and sector associations.
4. Scope of Work;
A. Desk Review; Review relevant documentation including:
I.TVETA accredited institution listings
II.NITA (or equivalent) accredited programmes
III.Sector Skills reports
IV.Labour Market Information
V.Employer demand reports
VI.Youth employability studies
B. Field Assessment; Conduct visits to shortlisted institutions within Nairobi and Kiambu (Thika Road Economic Corridor) Counties with responses from;
I.Institution management
II.Trainers
III.Career or industry liaison officers
IV.Current students enrolled
V.Alumni students
VI.Employers and Internship partners
VII.Safeguarding, counsellor and or sexual harassment appointed personnel
C. Verification and Assessment Parameters; The consultant shall verify:
I.Accreditation status
II.Training facilities
III.Workshop equipment
IV.Laboratories
V.Student enrolment
VI.Examination centres
VII.Industry partnerships
VIII.Graduate placement success rate
IX.Internship opportunities
X.Attachment arrangements
XI.Safeguarding policy and compliance measures
5. Methodology;
The consultant shall adopt a mixed-methods approach incorporating: Literature review; Institutional surveys; Key Informant Interviews (KIIs); Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), where appropriate; Observation; Verification; Documentary review; Comparative institutional analysis and Market demand analysis should be properly interrogated to suit the assignment priorities.
6. Expected Deliverables;
a)Deliverable 1: Inception Report and Desk Review literature (within 2 days)
b)Deliverable 2: Comprehensive Market Survey (10 days)
c)Deliverable 4: Stakeholder Validation Meeting (1 day)
d)Deliverable 3: Market survey analysis and report ( 2 days)
7. Consultant Qualifications;
a.Education: Master's degree or higher in one or more of the following: Development Studies, Social Sciences; Entrepreneurship; Higher Education; TVET; Labour Economics; Public Policy; Youth Development and any other relevant field
b.Experience: Minimum 7 years' demonstrated experience in: Labour market assessments; TVET sector research; Skills demand assessments; Youth employability programmes; TVET institutional assessments; Labour market information systems; Market surveys; Education sector research
c.Technical Experience: Demonstrated experience in; Competency-Based Education and Training (CBET); TVETA standards; Skills ecosystem analysis; Youth employment; Industry engagement; TVET quality assurance; Employment pathways; Labour market research methodologies
8. Application documents required;
a)Technical Proposal
b)Financial Proposal
c)Updated CV(s)
d)Copies of academic certificates
e)Professional certificates
f)Valid KRA PIN
g)Tax Compliance Certificate
h)Business registration certificate (where applicable)
i)Company profile (for firms)
j)At least three (3) reference letters from clients confirming successful completion of similar TVET or labour market surveys, skills assessments, or youth employability studies
9. Reporting;
The consultant shall report directly to the Program Officer for Jenga Ajira Project. All deliverables shall be submitted in both Microsoft Word and PDF formats, together with the underlying datasets (Excel or equivalent), assessment tools, and institutional scorecards.

opportunities.title: Senior Finance Lead
opportunities.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

BACKGROUND

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is a leading humanitarian and development organization working in more than 40 countries and 26 U.S. cities to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future.

The IRC has been operating in South Sudan since 1989. Our programs have provided critical Health, Nutrition, Protection and Rule of Law, Child Protection, Education and Economic Wellbeing services in eleven field sites, covering five of the ten states and one administrative area. With two offices in Northern Bahr el Ghazal- NBeG (Aweil East and South), five offices in Unity State (Bentiu, Koch, Mayendit, Ganyliel and Nyal), one in the Ruweng Administrative Area (Jamjang) covering operations in the Ajuong Thok and Pamir Refugee Camps and the host community, one office in Rumbek town covering the whole of Lakes, one office in Maban covering the refugee response and one field office in Central Equatoria (Juba)-urban programming together with the Country office.

Scope of Work

The IRC is seeking a Finance Leader for an upcoming FCDO funding opportunity. The project is intended to help mitigate conflict-driven mortality, morbidity, and protection risks by enabling vulnerable people to access lifesaving, multi-sector humanitarian assistance and protection in a highly constrained operating environment.

The programme is expected to run from October 2026 for 2.5 years.

The Finance Lead serves as a member of the Programme's Senior Management Team and is responsible for overseeing financial management and operations for the programme. The postholder provides leadership necessary to ensure the programme has appropriate financial infrastructure and systems in place to support smooth implementation. Working closely with the Team Leader and Deputy Team Leader, the Finance Lead contributes to the development of strategic and operational plans and is accountable for monitoring delivery against financial plans through comprehensive financial analytical reviews.

The Finance Lead establishes programme finance policies, systems, and procedures, and directs their development, documentation, and implementation. This includes preparing and regularly reviewing the programme financial management manual and ensuring all staff comply with organisational and FCDO requirements. The postholder manages programme finance activities to meet reporting requirements and deadlines, including preparing quarterly accrual reports, expenditure reporting, and projections consolidated across all programme offices. The Finance Lead provides programme staff with monthly actual-to-budget expenditure reports and analysis, facilitating review to support adaptive management.

The Finance Lead directs the preparation of all FCDO financial reports in accordance with accounting, legal, and contractual requirements. The postholder maintains up-to-date knowledge of local government requirements and ensures compliance with tax and other legal regulations, including establishing programme-specific bank accounts with adequate financial controls. Given the programme's use of conditional cash transfers, the postholder works closely with the Cash Programming Technical Lead to ensure robust fiduciary risk management across cash delivery mechanisms.

The Finance Lead holds accountability for finance and programme support staff, including performance management, career progression, and capacity strengthening. The postholder leads recruitment for finance staff and implements training programmes covering accurate expenditure tracking and quarterly forecasting.

In addition, the Finance Lead will oversee financial management across downstream partners and any sub awards, including financial due diligence, partner budgeting support, minimum compliance standards, and routine expenditure verification. The role will strengthen partner finance capacity through coaching and practical tools, ensuring partner reporting is accurate, timely, and consistent across locations.

The Finance Lead will also lead programme assurance, including audit planning and coordination, follow up on findings, and implementation of corrective actions, with a clear focus on internal controls and fraud risk management. The postholder will provide scenario based financial analysis and value for money insights to support senior management decisions and course correction during implementation.

Finance Lead Profile and Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited university in accounting, business administration, commerce, or finance with a recognised professional certificate in accounting such as CPA, or a master's degree in accounting.
  • Minimum of 10 years in a similar financial, compliance, or operational role supporting FCDO accountable grants and other international donor projects in fragile and conflict-affected contexts.
  • Experience with budgeting and financial reporting requirements on multi-million-pound, multi-year FCDO accountable grants.
  • Experience with financial management and reporting on programmes with substantial sub-awards and consortium partners operating across multiple locations.
  • Experience with adaptive management approaches and evidence-based programming is strongly preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of generally accepted accounting practices, financial reporting standards, and financial management processes and procedures.
  • Familiarity with FCDO rules and regulations, particularly related to the management of programme expenditure, forecasting requirements, and fiduciary risk management.
  • Experience with financial oversight of cash transfer programming, including understanding of risks and financial controls required for cash delivery mechanisms, is strongly preferred.
  • Extensive experience with computerised accounting systems, standard spreadsheets, and database programmes.
  • Proven track record of proactively identifying and communicating potential problems and proposing solutions, particularly within complex and high-risk operating environments.
  • Excellent interpersonal communication skills with the ability to interact, partner, and thrive in a diverse environment. Committed to staff training and development and effective at facilitation.
  • Experience managing staff performance and providing additional training or managing performance improvement plans.
  • Fluency in English and Arabic is required. Experience working in Sudan is an advantage.

This position will be contingent on the outcome of the bid.

Equal Opportunity Employer: IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

opportunities.title: Country Representative for South Sudan, based in Juba
opportunities.description:
WHAT IS IMPACT INITIATIVES ?

OUR AIM: IMPACT aims to shape practices and influence policies in humanitarian and development settings, in order to positively impact the lives of people and their communities.

Created in 2010, IMPACT is a Geneva-based NGO and the largest independent data provider in contexts of crisis. We aim to support a range of stakeholders in making better, more informed decisions in humanitarian, stabilisation, and development settings. We believe that a key pathway to better planning and decision-making is direct engagement with local communities.

How do we work?

IMPACT takes an initiative-based approach to structuring our programming. Each initiative has a specific aim, operational model, and portfolio of solutions.

REACH strengthens evidence-based humanitarian decision-making through efficient data collection, management, and analysis - before, during, and after an emergency.

PANDA improves the impact of humanitarian and development interventions through programme design, assessments, and monitoring & evaluation.

AGORA promotes localised and multi-sectoral aid action in support of the recovery and stabilisation of crisis-affected communities, in partnership with local stakeholders

Through our global team of research specialists, on average IMPACT publishes more than 1,700 information products on a yearly basis.

In 2010, IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarters are based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, which particularly allows IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support in its fields of intervention.

We are currently looking for a Country Representative to lead our South Sudan mission, based in Juba

Position: Country Representative

Contract duration: Until September 2027

Location: Juba, South Sudan

Starting Date: September 2026

Application Deadline: 31 August 2026.

COUNTRY PROFILE

South Sudan has faced protracted crisis since gaining independence in 2011, marked by cycles of conflict, political instability, economic volatility, and recurring climate shocks, such as flooding and drought. Humanitarian needs remain vast and complex, driven by displacement, food insecurity, and limited access to basic services. Humanitarian assistance continues to be a lifeline for millions across the country.

IMPACT, through REACH, has been active in South Sudan since 2012, providing timely and reliable data to support humanitarian planning and coordination. The South Sudan team delivers data and analysis that inform both rapid response and long-term resilience efforts. Our work plays a critical role in shaping evidence-based decision-making within one of the most challenging humanitarian contexts in the world.

FUNCTIONS

Under the management of IMPACT’s Regional Coordinator in Geneva, the Country Representative is responsible for representing IMPACT and managing and developing IMPACT’s programmes in South Sudan. S/he leads the IMPACT team to achieve program excellence and ensure the highest level of impact and accountability, while ensuring compliance to IMPACT guidelines, policies and standards across the mission. The CR is in regular contact with HQ, ensuring that organizational risks are promptly and clearly communicated to the Regional Coordinator, the Director of Country Programmes and Operations, and other relevant HQ Senior Management. S/he will promote organizational vision and core values across the mission and will actively link with HQ to contribute to the implementation of IMPACT’s global strategies. In his/her mission, the Country Representative will be hosted by Acted and will fall under the direct responsibility and management of Acted’s Country Director for all Administrative, Security, Logistics and Finance issues. S/he will therefore fully abide by Acted’s Security, HR, Administration and Logistics rules and regulations, and, in coordination with Acted, will ensure that all IMPACT staff abide by them.

RESPONSIBILITIES

The Country Representative responsibilities include the following:

Strategic Leadership

  • Develop and execute an up-to-date Country Strategy aligned with IMPACT’s global objectives and South Sudan’s humanitarian landscape.
  • Identify strategic opportunities, consolidate ongoing initiatives, and explore new programme areas to enhance IMPACT’s value to the aid community.

Programme and Project Management

  • Oversee programme planning, implementation, and evaluation, ensuring all projects meet objectives, timelines, and compliance standards.
  • Facilitate coordination between IMPACT and partner organizations to achieve efficient project delivery and impact.

Fundraising and Donor Engagement

  • Identify and secure funding opportunities in collaboration with HQ and Acted.
  • Lead proposal development and negotiate contracts with donors, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities.

Finance and Budget Oversight

  • Manage project budgets and forecast expenses, ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting to HQ and Acted.
  • Mitigate financial risks and ensure optimal budget utilization.

Human Resources and Team Leadership

  • Guide and develop the IMPACT team, ensuring performance standards, capacity building, and adherence to IMPACT and Acted’s policies.
  • Coordinate with HQ and Acted for transparent recruitment and career management of staff.

External Representation and Coordination

  • Establish and maintain productive relationships with donors, UN agencies, NGOs, and other stakeholders, representing IMPACT’s programmes and strategic interests.
  • Ensure proactive contribution to key humanitarian decision-making forums and promote IMPACT’s programme visibility.

Data Protection and Accountability

  • Uphold strict confidentiality of all data collected and engage with communities respectfully, ensuring awareness of programme objectives and methods.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Academic qualifications: Excellent academic qualifications, including a Master’s degree in a relevant discipline (International Relations, Political Sciences, Social Research, Development Studies, or similar).
  • Management experience: Previous experience in a senior management role in an INGO at field level. Track record in successful management of international and national teams in humanitarian contexts.
  • Familiarity with aid system: Familiarity with the aid system, and the research community.
  • Communication/reporting skills: Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting, including proven experience in contributing to high level presentations/briefings.
  • Years of work experience: At least 5 years of relevant working experience. Any previous experience in South Sudan would be an asset.
  • Research skills: Experience in assessments. M&E, field research, evaluations an asset.
  • Multi-tasking skills: Ability to multitask with tight deadlines in complex environment.
  • Level of independence: A self-starter with a proven ability to work independently.
  • Cross-cultural work environment: Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment.
  • Language skills: Fluency in English required**.**
  • Security environment: Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

  • For this position, salary between 4’620 CHF and 4’680 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 500 USD
    NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in hardship places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
  • Accommodation and food provided in ACTED guesthouse
  • Private pension fund, health insurance, and repatriation assistance (& unemployment insurance for EU citizens)
  • This is not a family duty station
  • Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered
  • R&R after 3 months in country (flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance)
  • Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 23kg and 100kg, depending on the length of the contract
  • Annual leave of 36 days per year

opportunities.title: Technical Consultant for parliamentary conference system installation, and commissioning (Retainer)
opportunities.description:
Overview of position

Our client is an operational arm of the United Nations, supporting the successful implementation of its partners' peacebuilding, humanitarian, and development projects around the world. Mandated as a central resource of the United Nations, our client provides sustainable project management, procurement, and infrastructure services to a wide range of governments, donors, and United Nations organisations.

Our client has been operating in Somalia since 1995, providing implementation and advisory support for various development initiatives in the areas of infrastructure, project management, procurement, and financial services. Based in Mogadishu, the Somalia Country Office is currently implementing projects across Somalia. From delivering high-quality infrastructure for public services to facilitating security sector reform and supporting crisis recovery, our client is an established partner of the Government of Somalia and development partners in the country's path towards reconstruction and state-building.

Somalia Country Office

Since 1995, our client, headquartered in Mogadishu and part of the East and Southern Africa Multi-Country Office (ESAMCO), has been a trusted partner to the Government of Somalia and international donors. Through the provision of project management, infrastructure, procurement, and financial services, the Somalia Country Office (SOCO) plays a critical role in supporting national priorities in health, rule of law, security, transport, and resilience.

The office has delivered impactful infrastructure projects, including the Immigration Headquarters (US$6.8 million), Maritime Police Headquarters (US$3.7 million), and regional hospitals (US$20 million), and leads key national initiatives such as the Joint Police Programme (US$56.4 million). Our client also manages large-scale procurement, including over US$75 million in non-lethal support to security actors. Advisory support to urban resilience and crisis recovery efforts further strengthens institutional capacity through projects valued at US$8.1 million, US$8.8 million, and US$7.4 million. SOCO's integrated approach contributes to sustainable peacebuilding and development outcomes across Somalia.

Project-Specific – Governance Facility

This Terms of Reference (TOR) forms part of the EU Governance Facility for Somalia, implemented by our client and funded by the European Union (EU). The project builds on previous EU support to state-building, democratisation, federalisation, security, and the rule of law in Somalia, and contributes to advancing inclusive governance priorities across the country.

The Governance Facility supports initiatives aimed at strengthening political dialogue, promoting inclusive and credible electoral processes, and responding to emerging governance priorities. Through the mobilisation of technical expertise and operational support, the project contributes to advancing Somalia's inclusive politics agenda and supports key stakeholders involved in governance and democratisation processes.

Role objectives

Pre-Installation Review and Planning

Conduct a detailed technical assessment of the Parliament Chamber, including electrical, networking, and infrastructure readiness. Review and validate supplier technical submissions, including system design, layout, and installation methodology. Verify that proposed equipment and configurations align with project specifications and site conditions. Provide inputs to refine installation plans and ensure feasibility and efficiency. Develop and apply inspection and quality control checklists throughout the installation process. Conduct regular site inspections to verify compliance with technical specifications and international standards. Identify defects, gaps, or non-compliance issues and ensure corrective actions are implemented by the supplier. Validate that all hardware and software components are installed and configured correctly before acceptance.

Quality Assurance

Supervise the supplier during delivery and installation of all conference system components, including microphones, control units, audio processors, amplifiers, speakers, cameras, cabling, and recording systems. Verify that all delivered equipment meets the required specifications, quantities, and quality standards. Ensure proper installation practices, including mounting, cabling, labelling, and equipment safety. Monitor progress against agreed timelines and report any delays or deviations. Develop and apply inspection and quality control checklists throughout the installation process. Conduct regular site inspections to verify compliance with technical specifications and international standards. Identify defects, gaps, or non-compliance issues and ensure corrective actions are implemented by the supplier. Validate that all hardware and software components are installed and configured correctly before acceptance. Oversee configuration of the conference management system, including microphone control, speaker priority, and participant management functions. Ensure proper integration of all system components and compatibility with the existing audiovisual and IT infrastructure. Develop and oversee system testing protocols, including functionality testing and User Acceptance Testing (UAT). Witness and verify testing conducted by the supplier, including audio clarity and microphone functionality, speaker output and system control features, camera tracking and recording functionality, and overall system stability and performance. Ensure all identified issues are resolved prior to final acceptance. Provide formal technical recommendations for system acceptance and commissioning.

Documentation and Reporting

Review and validate all technical documentation provided by the supplier, including system architecture diagrams, equipment layout plans, cabling maps, and operational manuals. Prepare and submit regular progress reports highlighting installation status, risks, and performance. Produce a final installation verification and compliance report.

Training and Capacity Building Oversight

Review and validate the training programme delivered by the supplier. Ensure parliamentary technical staff receive adequate hands-on training on system operation, troubleshooting, and maintenance. Verify the operational readiness of users prior to handover.

Risks, Issues and Stakeholder Coordination

Identify and manage technical and operational risks related to installation and system performance. Maintain a risk and issue log and recommend mitigation measures. Coordinate closely with the Parliamentary Secretariat, technical teams, the supplier, and the Client to ensure smooth implementation. Escalate critical issues to the Client in a timely manner for resolution and decision-making.

Project reporting

The role reports directly to the Client Senior Project Manager.

Key competencies

Develops and implements sustainable business strategies, thinking long term and externally to positively shape our client's organisation. Anticipates and understands the impact and implications of future decisions and activities across different parts of the organisation. (Applicable only for levels ICS-10 and above.)

Treats all individuals with respect, responds sensitively to differences and encourages others to do the same. Upholds organisational and ethical standards, maintains high standards of integrity and trustworthiness, and serves as a role model for diversity, equity and inclusion.

Acts as a positive role model, contributing to a strong team spirit. Collaborates effectively and supports the development of others. For people managers, demonstrates positive leadership by motivating, guiding and inspiring others to succeed, using appropriate leadership styles.

Demonstrates an understanding of the impact of their role on all stakeholders and consistently puts our client's end beneficiaries first. Builds and maintains strong external relationships and acts as a trusted and competent partner where relevant to the role.

Efficiently establishes an appropriate course of action for self and/or others to achieve objectives. Delivers high-quality results through attention to detail and a commitment to excellence. Identifies opportunities and takes the initiative to act on them. Recognises that the responsible use of resources maximises value and impact for our client and its beneficiaries.

Embraces change and remains flexible in a fast-paced environment. Effectively adapts approaches to changing circumstances or requirements. Reflects on experience, learns from it and adjusts behaviour accordingly. Maintains consistent performance under pressure while continually seeking opportunities for improvement.

Evaluates data and options to make logical, pragmatic decisions. Takes an objective and balanced approach, managing calculated risks appropriately. Demonstrates innovation and creativity in solving problems.

Communicates ideas and information clearly, concisely and openly. Considers the needs and perspectives of others in all communications. Actively listens, shares knowledge proactively and manages conflict constructively by finding common ground and fostering collaboration.

Team management

There is no team management under this role

Further information

To be advised

opportunities.title: Request for Proposals: Development of Policy Recommendation for The Transformation of Integrated Access to Justice: Victim Recovery Services Delivery
opportunities.description:
About the Proposal

Program Background

Australia-Indonesia Partnership for Justice Phase 3 (AIPJ3) is a five-year investment by the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to partner with the Government of Indonesia (GOI) to advance its priority law and justice reforms. It aligns with Indonesia’s National Development Plans (Long- Term National Development Plan 2025-2045, Mid-Term National Development Plan 2025-2029) and the Australia-Indonesia Development Partnership Plan 2024-2028.

Building on previous phases, AIPJ3 will support partners to deliver activities against agreed policy priorities, while maintaining the flexibility to respond to emerging needs and opportunities. The program focuses on seven policy priorities that are important to Australia and Indonesia: accountability and transparency, criminal justice reform, preventing violent extremism, transnational crime cooperation, commercial law, access to justice, and women’s leadership.

AIPJ3 will progress the long-term goal of “Strong and accessible justice and security institutions that uphold the rule of law and contribute to stability and prosperity in Indonesia and the region”. With the specific objective of “working in partnership with Indonesia to support effective realisation of justice reforms”, AIPJ3 has the following end-of-program outcomes (EOPOs):

  • EOPO 1: Justice institutions develop and implement policies, plans, budgets and practices that advance the rule of law and economic development in the priority areas of accountability and transparency, criminal and commercial law reform
  • EOPO 2: Justice institutions and partners implement and adapt policies, plans, budgets and practices that contribute to preventing violent extremism and addressing transnational crime
  • EOPO 3: Justice institutions develop and implement policies, plans, budgets and practices that advance equal access to justice for women, children and persons with disabilities
  • EOPO 4: Government of Indonesia, Government of Australia and non-government organisations deepen partnerships in the justice and security sectors for mutual benefit

Access to justice is a fundamental human right whose recognition has been institutionalized at both the international and national levels. More specifically, one of the Priority Activities under the 2025–2029 National Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMN) is the Transformation of Access to Justice, in which the provision of services and the strengthening of access-to-justice policies constitute key development priorities.

In 2021, Indonesia’s Access to Justice Index score was 53.8 out of 100, placing it in the “Moderate” category. Nevertheless, the Recovery from the Impact of Legal Problems variable remained in a “Poor” condition, with 75.1 percent of the population lacking access to recovery services. This issue warrants particular attention, considering that the Government has responded to the need for victims’ rights provision and recovery through various institutions and service mechanisms.

The Witness and Victim Protection Agency (LPSK) carries out functions related to the protection of victims of crime; the Ministry of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection (KPPPA) provides comprehensive support services for women and children who are victims of violence; the National Commission on Violence Against Women (Komnas Perempuan) coordinates a number of service providers; and Regional Governments contribute through various service delivery schemes. However, the existence of multiple actors does not automatically result in a functional and integrated system. From a governance perspective, the provision of recovery services for victims remains fragmented and poorly connected. Services provided by LPSK, KPPPA, Komnas Perempuan, Regional Governments, and other relevant stakeholders are not yet integrated. As a result, victims often submit requests for assistance to multiple institutions, while those institutions remain unaware of one another’s involvement.

Furthermore, the delivery of victim recovery services continues to rely heavily on informal networks without clear standardization. Based on data previously obtained by the Ministry of National Development Planning/Bappenas in West Sumatra, case workers or facilitators often seek assistance from institutions with which they have personal relationships and which they believe have the capacity to provide support. In many cases, such requests cannot be fulfilled, forcing them to seek alternative channels of assistance.

A clear pattern emerges from these conditions: there is currently no integrated mechanism for the provision of victims’ rights and recovery services. As a consequence, victims frequently do not receive services in an optimal manner and, in some cases, receive no services at all. This indicates that, substantively, victim support services remain insufficiently comprehensive. Recovery efforts often fail to address victims’ physical, psychological, economic, and social needs in an integrated manner, resulting in interventions that are neither sustainable nor capable of fully restoring victims’ well-being.

Accordingly, a comprehensive study is needed to map the existing mechanisms for the provision of victims’ rights and recovery services, including the identification of service-providing institutions, service delivery pathways, and existing gaps. The study is expected to generate policy recommendations that will serve as the foundation for the development of a National Integrated Access to Justice Mechanism, particularly by strengthening interconnectivity among service providers and ensuring that no victim falls outside the reach of the system. Ultimately, the resulting policy framework should ensure that victims receive adequate, equitable, and sustainable recovery services.

About DT Global

DT Global is shaping a future where sustainable development and innovation empower individuals, communities, and nations. We work in partnership with local stakeholders to foster inclusive prosperity, social equity, and environmental stewardship. Our global team of 2,500 staff and experts work in over 90 countries to solve complex problems in the peacebuilding, governance, economic development, environment, and human development sectors. With a track record of technical excellence and more than 60 years of international development experience and relationships, we deliver innovative solutions that transform lives.

For more information, please see www.dt-global.com

About the Engagement:

AIPJ3 is seeking a qualified Subcontractor to support Ministry of National Development Planning (Bappenas) to conduct a comprehensive study to map the existing mechanisms for the provision of victims’ rights and recovery services, including the identification of service-providing institutions, service delivery pathways, and existing gaps. The study is expected to generate policy recommendations that will serve as the foundation for the development of a National Integrated Access to Justice Mechanism, particularly by strengthening interconnectivity among service providers and ensuring that no victim falls outside the reach of the system. Ultimately, the resulting policy framework should ensure that victims receive adequate, equitable, and sustainable recovery services. Specifically, the selected organisation is expected to:

  1. Map and analyse the existing mechanisms for victim rights fulfillment and recovery services operated by relevant Ministries and Institutions, including the Indonesia Witness and Victim Protection Agency (LPSK), the Ministry of Women's Empowerment and Children's Protection (KPPPA), The National Commission on Violence against Women (Komnas Perempuan), and regional governments, covering service delivery modalities, target beneficiaries, referral pathways, and budget allocations.
  2. Identify gaps, overlaps, and systemic inefficiencies arising from the fragmented and disconnected implementation of victim recovery services across institutions, including cases where victims fall outside the reach of any service provider.
  3. Develop a blueprint for an Integrated National Mechanism for Access to Justice (Mekanisme Nasional Akses terhadap Keadilan Terpadu) that establishes clear interconnections between existing institutions and service providers, ensuring no victim is left without adequate support.
  4. Formulate actionable policy recommendations on service standardisation, inter-institutional coordination frameworks, and the operationalisation of a comprehensive and sustainable victim recovery system, in alignment with the national development priorities under RPJMN 2025–2029.

Requirement for the Request for Proposals (RFP)

To access the RFP document, please click on the link or copy paste it to access the full proposal requirements for this procurement: https://tinyurl.com/RFP-VictimProtection-ext

opportunities.title: Impact and Accountability Project Officer - DDI Project
opportunities.description:
About CIVICUS

CIVICUS exists to defend people power. As a growing global alliance of over 17,000 members in over 180 countries, we work together to monitor violations of basic civic freedoms, call out the perpetrators of violations and strengthen the power of people to organise by supporting a more accountable, effective and innovative civil society. We strive to promote excluded voices, especially from the global south.

About the Role

The Impact and Accountability Officer work dynamically with the Impact & Accountability (I&A) Cluster and the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) team to design, implement, and strengthen program-specific MEL systems that are robust, adaptive, and aligned with CIVICUS’s Integrated Results Framework.

The role is responsible for leading data-driven performance monitoring, outcome measurement, evaluation, and adaptive management processes across DDI’s global portfolio of projects. Beyond compliance-focused reporting, the I&A officer plays a key role in fostering a culture of learning, accountability, and evidence-informed decision-making.

A central focus of the position is to embed partner-centered learning approaches, facilitate South-South knowledge exchange, and strengthen accountability to constituencies across a diverse and geographically distributed network of civil society actors. Through these efforts, the MEL Officer contributes to improving program effectiveness, capturing impact, and supporting strategic learning across the DDI portfolio.

Key Requirements

  1. A bachelor’s degree or Diploma in Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning, International Development, Development Management, or equivalent. A master’s degree is strongly preferred.
  2. Minimum 5–7 years' professional experience in MEAL concepts and approaches, with at least 2–3 years in a relevant functional area/similar role.
  3. Fluency in English is required; proficiency in French, Spanish, or Arabic is an added advantage.
  4. Proved experience in using result-based and participatory monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) approaches using evaluation methodologies such as Contribution Analysis or Outcome Harvesting;
  5. Excellent IT including skills, including experience with MS Office, especially Excel, PowerBI and Smartsheet.
  6. Commitment to CIVICUS’ vision, mission, values and ways of working.
  7. Familiar with civil society, development and human rights issues; understanding the challenges faced by marginalised citizens and organisations - especially those in the Global South - particularly around data availability, literacy, connectivity, quality etc.
  8. Familiar with online M&E tools and general technology savviness.
  9. Strong analytical and methodological skills to support both qualitative and quantitative research
  10. Demonstrated track record of evaluation and report writing at various levels (donor reporting, project reporting, internal management reporting etc.).
  11. Excellent organisational skills and the ability to meet deadlines.
  12. Excellent writing skills and ability to be concise and clear – providing actionable analysis and recommendations.
  13. Ability to communicate and meaningfully engage with diverse stakeholders, including those not too familiar with M&E.
  14. High degree of self-awareness and the ability to work effectively with multiple teams, across various time zones, many of which are virtual.
  15. Proactive and creative in identifying opportunities for innovative improvements in CIVICUS’ current M&E related systems and processes.
  16. Familiarity with digital democracy themes (e.g., digital rights, algorithmic accountability, gender-based violence, internet freedom, tech governance, Civic Tech Innovation etc).
  17. Learning and M&E knowledge, ideally in the non-profit sector.
  18. Experience with transforming raw monitoring data into compelling visual narratives using tools like PowerBI, Tableau, or interactive graphics to drive both internal learning and public advocacy.
  19. Experience working with historically excluded communities such as rural groups, indigenous peoples, women, youth, and LGBTQI+
