opportunities.title: Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) Manager
opportunities.description:
Description

The Pacific Community (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The Operations & Integration (O&I) collective delivers essential enabling services that support the organisation’s scientific and technical portfolio. Our key functions include corporate services, programme support, partnerships, resource mobilisation, and strategic engagement. These services are coordinated through our regional and satellite offices across the Pacific and Europe. Additionally, the O&I collective leads a dedicated workstream focused on organisational change and transformation to drive continuous improvement and adaptability.

The Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) Manager will oversee the overall responsibility for organisational budgeting, financial analysis, developing sustainable financial models and cost recovery and business partnering with management and support divisions.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

Leadership and coordination

  • Provide proactive leadership in all areas of budget & forecast management. This includes the following: Leading improvements in organisational budgeting practices across the organisation to improve accuracy, relevance and timeliness of financial budgeting and reporting; Developing tools and practices which are relevant and practical at organisational, divisional and program / project levels.
  • Leading financial analysis and development of sustainable financial models:
  • Analysis of income, pipeline and expenditure trends across the organisation.
  • Develop sustainable financial models through management fee, cost recovery or other financial models which meet organisational and donor requirements.

Support to the finance director

  • Annual business planning. This includes thinking strategically of staffing and system requirements required to deliver on plans.
  • Lead responsibility in senior team for audit and Risk Committee responsibilities including writing and presenting papers and coordination
  • Provide advice to the director and perform services in such areas as:
  • Strategic, financial, and organisational reform.
  • Appropriate models for financial sustainability, including economic data analysis.
  • Internal Audit & Risk audit board management.
  • Internal stakeholder relationships
  • Matrix and cross-cutting work programmes.

Support to other areas

  • Leadership on business partnering across management and support functions and shared services approach across science divisions.
  • Ensure the FP&A team meet regularly with all management functions to support their team financial analysis and planning needs.
  • Indirect line management of assigned Divisional Finance Team Leaders as part of shared services approach.
  • Flagships and other new ways of working.
  • Close coordination with the General Accounting Team to:
  • Provide oversight of organisational and divisional reporting.
  • Ensure that accounting and budgeting practices are aligned across the organisation.
  • Delivery of their periodic accounting and reporting requirements, including making strategic recommendations on how services and controls can be improved.
  • Support the Business Improvements & Internal Controls team in:
  • Development and implementation of systems and processes
  • Development of shared services and pooling strategies and activities.
  • Strengthening of internal controls.

Shared Services

  • Actively participate and lead in shared service programs and activities. This includes supporting the finance pooling initiatives to bring about workforce planning.
  • Work collaboratively with divisional finance team leaders and other finance staff towards embedding shared services within divisions.
  • Provide thought leadership in different areas of work.

People Management

  • Creating a team environment that fosters and develops effective working relationships and high performance.
  • Managing service levels to stakeholders and customers in a complex operating environment.
  • Manage staff performance and support training and development.
  • Conduct fair, consistent, timely performance planning and review meetings and encourage open communication to discuss performance.
  • Monitor the performance and workloads of staff members to ensure objectives are met.
  • Supports the health and safety and well-being of employees in the way they manage and monitor the team.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please refer to the online job description.

Key selection criteria

Qualifications

  • Post-graduate degree in accounting, finance or business administration or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

Technical expertise

  • At least 12 years of experience and demonstrated competence in the same field.
  • Demonstrated experience in managing donor or project funded organisations and familiarity with a broad range of donor reporting requirements.
  • Strong analytical ability and demonstrated ability to navigate complex technical issues and to manage financial risk.
  • Experience in developing organisational budgeting systems in large, complex organisations.
  • Sound collaboration and team working skills.
  • Advanced Excel skills.

Language skills

  • Fluency in English.

Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness

  • Knowledge of Pacific Island countries and territories is an advantage

Salary, terms and conditions

Contract Duration – This vacant position is budgeted for 3 years and is subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

Remuneration – The Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) Manager is a band 12 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale with a starting salary range of SDR (special drawing rights) 5,012-6,169 per month, which converts to approximately XPF 723,251-890,185 (USD 6,717-8,267; EUR 6,061-7,460).SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea – SPC provides housing support in Noumea. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

Languages – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

Recruitment principles – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an equal-opportunity employer, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the Pacific Islander. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

opportunities.title: Senior Specialist, Climate Health & WASH
opportunities.country: Lebanon, United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, United States of America
opportunities.description:
Job Overview

The Senior Specialist for Climate Health and WASH is the organization’s focal point for Climate Resilient WASH (CR-WASH) and Climate Sensitive Infectious Disease Prevention within the Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) department. The Senior Specialist works under the leadership of the Environment & Climate Health Global Practice Lead (GPL), to drive progress through leadership of strategic projects, delivering on global strategic priorities, and ensuring the scope, quality and relevance of organizational technical standards. In line with IRC Strategy 100, the Senior Specialists leads delivery of the CR-WASH and water security components of the Health Outcome Strategy, and co-delivers the Infectious Disease Prevention & Control (IDPC) Impact at Scale priority. The Senior Specialist covers a global portfolio including WASH service continuity in the face of climate shocks, water-related disease prevention, WASH in Healthcare facilities, anticipatory action and the water-energy nexus. The Senior Specialist collaborate closely with other Global Specialists, Global Practice Leads, Regional Practice Leads and Health Technical Advisors (TA) to promote technical best practice in CRRD programming. S/he supports high impact strategic business development, strategic and technical relationship management, and technical advocacy at the global level.

Major Responsibilities

Strategic and Technical Delivery (50% LOE)

  • Lead a complex portfolio of strategic projects across CR-WASH, water security, and the water-energy nexus, including anticipatory action and forecast-based response for CR-WASH, WASH systems and finance, and energy access for water and health facilities in fragile and conflict affected settings (FCAS).
  • Drive technical delivery of the IDPC Impact at Scale priority, with a focus on CR-WASH and water-related disease dimensions, including strategy refinement, country prioritization and road map planning, in collaboration with the GPL and others.
  • Provide intensive remote and in-country technical support to Technical Advisors, Regional Practice Leads and Country Program teams, including development of implementation tools and technical guidance and delivery of specialized capacity strengthening, technical advice and coaching for staff and partners for strategic projects.
  • Identify and shape research opportunities in CR-WASH/IDPC, including cost-effectiveness and life-cycle costing, and lead implementation when needed, in collaboration with the GPL, Airbel Impact Lab, and others
  • Collaborate with the Emergency Unit on technical quality strengthening for WASH in Emergencies, review technical guidelines for acute emergency contexts, including cholera outbreak, and technical backstopping as needed, in close partnership with the Emergency WASH Coordinator and others
  • Monitor progress on technical program implementation, including budgets and expenditures, and drive course corrections as needed for strategic projects.
  • Collaborate effectively on shared priorities within the Health Unit and with other Technical Units and Global Practice Areas, including the Climate Resilience Global Practice Area, the Anticipatory Action team, and the Economic Recovery & Development, Protection and Education Technical Units.
  • Support partner and donor engagement for strategic projects as needed.
  • Under the guidance of the GPL, contribute to global strategy and delivery planning for CR-WASH/IDPC as needed.

Technical Quality Strengthening and Organizational Learning (25% LOE)

  • Lead finalization and roll out of the CR-WASH core indicators and Climate Resilient WASH MEAL package and lead ongoing revision of CR-WASH technical guidance and standards as evidence and field practice evolves.
  • Convene and sustain a CR-WASH community of practice for peer exchange across countries and regionals, surfacing field learning and research to inform technical guidance and incorporate into global best practices
  • Synthesis lessons, strengthen technical guidance and capacity and support strategic work on Anticipatory Action for CR-WASH/IDPC, in close coordination with the Anticipatory Action team.
  • Contribute to the development of the Environment & Climate Health technical competency framework and assessment to identify capacity gaps, inform capacity strengthening priorities, and support staff development.
  • Synthesize, adapt, and disseminate relevant technical standards, methodologies, and implementation tools for CR-WASH/IDPC, drawing on evidenced-based best practices and reflecting IRC programming.
  • Provide technical inputs to MEAL tools and methodologies when needed, and support data interpretation and use, including support to regional TAs to analyze relevant technical and program data as needed.
  • Proactively disseminate lessons learned across countries and regions for select strategic projects, ensuring these inform program design and implementation of country-led projects.
  • Contribute to shaping, refining and delivering the Environment & Climate Health Learning Agenda.

External Influence, Relationships and Representation (10% LOE)

  • Collaborate with policymakers, implementing partners, humanitarian responders, and UN agencies to advance guidance, outcomes, research, implementation, and documentation on CR-WASH/IDPC.
  • Represent IRC, as appropriate, in priority external forums, including technical, policy, and advocacy workshops across Health, WASH and Climate domains.
  • Contribute to global prioritization and agenda-setting efforts, ensuring that research, evidence, tools, and resources are being used to advance IRC’s strategy and agendas for FCAS.
  • Work with the Policy and Communications Teams to develop and advocate IRC’s and global policies on CR-WASH/IDPC.

Business Development (15% LOE)

  • Lead strategic business development opportunities in partnership with relevant technical and business development teams and regional and country colleagues.
  • Provide TAs and Country Programs with specialized support on program design in relevant technical areas of CR-WASH and IDPC, on request
  • Service as technical lead on large, complex and high value business development opportunities

Key Working Relationships

  • Position Reports to: Global Practice Lead, Environment & Climate Health
  • Primary Health Care Global Practice Lead and Senior Specialist, Infectious Disease
  • Regional Technical Advisors
  • Other Specialists and Senior Specialists

Key Internal Relationships:

  • Health Unit team members
  • Research and Innovation teams
  • MEAL team
  • Airbel Impact Lab
  • Emergency Unit
  • Policy Solutions, Advocacy Influence, and Systems Change Global Teams
  • Global HQ and AMU
  • Key External Relationships: INGO counterparts, UN agencies, global coordination mechanisms, public and private donors, research networks

Desired Experience and Skills

  • Established or growing recognition as an expert in WASH, water security, environmental management or closely related field, with a minimum of 6-8 years of progressive experience designing and leading programs relevant to Climate Resilient WASH in FCAS and/or across the humanitarian-development nexus.
  • Master’s degree in public health engineering, environmental management and/or related fields or equivalent professional experience required.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and delivering new strategies to advance ambitious goals, with strong ability to connect WASH infrastructure development to service models, sustained operations, financing, policy and systems strengthening.
  • Experience collaborating across health, nutrition, climate resilience and related domains, with ability to clearly communicate the contribution of WASH and water security to health, climate resilience and other outcomes.
  • Knowledge of and ability to use and integrate data, including climate forecasts, epidemiological data, and geo-spatial data to inform program targeting and intervention design; demonstrated ability to use of data and research evidence for programmatic decisions and rigorous analytic skills
  • Strong track record of driving uptake of evidence-based practice, including technical skills in coaching, mentoring, and capacity strengthening
  • Ability to design technical approaches for proposals and identify new business development opportunities
  • Ability to work, manage, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced, highly matrixed environment; outstanding business acumen, critical thinking, problem solving and decision-making skills required
  • Superb inter-personal, written and verbal communication skills with ability to collaborate across countries, cultures, and departments
  • Excellent communication, influencing, and storytelling skills
  • Proficiency in English and French required; knowledge of Spanish or Arabic an asset.
  • Ability to travel globally up to 30% of the time, occasionally on short notice

Compensation (US): ($104K - $120K). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

Info for Job Ads:

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Background:

IRC’s Technical Excellence team is comprised of four teams or sector “Units” which have deep expertise in their respective fields: Education, Economic Recovery and Development, Health, and Violence Prevention and Response, as well as teams which provide measurement and finance/grant management support. Technical teams are also matrixed with a team that focuses on the quality and content of cross-sectoral programming in emergency responses.

IRC’s Technical Excellence teams offer five core services to IRC country programs and the wider organization:

  • Program Design: We support country and regional teams to design state of the art programming, incorporating the best available evidence, cost data, and expertise of what has worked elsewhere, with the knowledge that country teams, partner organizations and our clients bring to the table.
  • Quality Assurance: We partner with our measurement teams to design and drive the use of indicators to measure progress towards outcomes; we partner with regional and country teams to review program delivery progress and help address implementation challenges and adapt interventions to changed circumstances.
  • Business Development: We partner within and outside the IRC to design winning bids and identify winning consortia; we deploy technical expertise in public events and private meetings to position IRC as a partner of choice.
  • Research & Learning: We partner with our research lab to design cutting edge research to fill evidence gaps, and with country teams to learn from implementation such that we continuously improve our future design and delivery.
  • External Influence: We showcase the IRC’s programs, technical insights and learning in order to influence and improve the humanitarian sector’s policy and practice.

Health Unit

IRC’s health programs comprise the largest proportion of its overall program budget and are essential to both IRC emergency response and long-term programming worldwide.

The Health Technical Unit is a dynamic team of more than 70 professionals in Primary Health Care, Sexual and Reproductive Health, Nutrition, Mental Environment & Climate Health and Systems Strengthening. They provide IRC’s 40 plus country offices and emergency response team with world class technical expertise, capacity strengthening and a cross-country view of what works to achieve outcomes in terms of both evidence and practical experience. They also lead a focused research agenda, influencing donor policy to support interventions and innovations proven cost effective to achieve positive change in people’s lives.

Professional Standards
All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

opportunities.title: Design and Delivery of a Product Quality Assurance and Standardization Training for REAP Retail Trading Groups
opportunities.description:
Background and Context

The Response to Education and Protection Needs (REAP) Project is a 27-month humanitarian and development intervention funded by Save the Children Italy and implemented by the Somali Lifeline Organization (SOLO) in partnership with Save the Children International (SCI) and the Relief, Reconstruction and Development Organization (RRDO), running from October 2024 to October 2026 across the Dadaab Refugee Complex, Garissa County, Kenya. Under Output 4.1, the livelihoods component supports adolescent mothers, caregivers and foster parents with enterprise-based livelihood training and start-up capital in the Ifo 1, Ifo 2, Dagahaley and Hagadera settlements.

In May 2026, SOLO commissioned the first round of a planned bi-annual longitudinal REAP Tracer Study — Livelihoods Component, covering 419 respondents through a mixed-methods design combining a structured survey, Key Informant Interviews, Focus Group Discussions, enterprise observation and light-touch market validation. The study found that 99.8 percent of respondents are running a business and that mean monthly profit increased by 167.7 percent since programme entry. It also found that 96.2 percent of all REAP-supported enterprises are concentrated in only two sectors, retail trade (82.6 percent) and livestock (13.6 percent), making retail trade by far the dominant REAP livelihood activity.

Vendor Key Informant Interviews conducted for the study described how this concentration plays out in practice: retail kiosks across Ifo 1, Ifo 2 and Dagahaley overwhelmingly stock the same narrow range of goods, staples such as sugar, rice, oil and flour, alongside soap and small personal care items. Vendors reported that this product homogeneity across competitors made price the primary competitive variable, pushing selling prices and margins down for all sellers in the same market row. The study further found that 64.0 percent of REAP enterprises have no formal or informal market linkage, with most retail groups sourcing stock through informal spot purchases from market intermediaries or Dadaab town wholesalers, with no negotiated pricing, quality assurance, or guaranteed supply relationship. This leaves retail groups competing almost entirely on price within a saturated local market, with no basis to differentiate their goods or access markets beyond the camp economy.

SOLO therefore wishes to engage a qualified consultant or consultancy firm to design and deliver a product quality assurance and standardization training for REAP retail trading groups, so that these groups can move from undifferentiated, price-based competition toward offering quality-assured goods that meet recognized Kenyan standards, building consumer trust and opening access to more competitive markets beyond Dadaab.

Rationale for the Assignment

This assignment responds directly to structural findings of the REAP Tracer Study (Chapters 19 and 23) regarding retail market saturation and the absence of quality or market differentiation among REAP-supported traders:

  • Retail trade dominates REAP enterprises (82.6 percent of all enterprises), and 96.2 percent of enterprises overall are concentrated in retail trade and livestock, creating market saturation and collective vulnerability to the same demand-side shocks.
  • Products are undifferentiated and price is the only competitive lever (Chapter 19 vendor interviews): the emergence of new kiosks selling essentially the same goods has driven downward pressure on prices and margins for all sellers in the same market row.
  • Market competition is the second most cited constraint on applying REAP skills, reported by 63.7 percent of respondents, after capital shortfalls.
  • Market linkages are largely absent (Recommendation 5): 64.0 percent of enterprises have no formal or informal market linkage, and stock is sourced through unverified, informal spot-purchase arrangements rather than structured supplier agreements.
  • A strong group-based foundation already exists to build on (Recommendation 8): 99.3 percent of REAP beneficiaries report group membership (VSLA/cooperative structures), providing a ready platform for collective, group-level quality assurance practice and joint market access.

The tracer study's overarching conclusion is that the programme needs to shift from enterprise entry support toward enterprise incubation, including market linkages and differentiation strategies for existing enterprises, not only diversification into new sectors. A product quality assurance and standardization training, aligned with the frameworks used by Kenya's national quality and trade institutions, offers retail trading groups a practical route to differentiate their goods, build consumer and buyer confidence, and reduce the price-based competition documented in the study.

Purpose and Objectives of the Assignment

Overall Objective

To equip REAP-supported retail trading groups with the practical knowledge, tools and referral pathways needed to source, handle and sell quality-assured goods that meet recognized Kenyan quality and trade standards, specifically those administered by the Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS) and the Kenya National Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KNCCI), so that groups can differentiate from saturated local competition and access more competitive markets.

Specific Objectives

  1. Build practical, group-level understanding of the KEBS quality frameworks most relevant to REAP retail product categories: The Standardization Mark (S-Mark) for locally manufactured goods, the Import Standardization Mark (ISM) for imported stock, and the Diamond Mark of Quality (D-Mark) as a voluntary premium differentiator, including how groups can verify supplier and product compliance and avoid substandard or counterfeit stock.
  2. Train groups on basic product handling, storage, display, labelling and record-keeping practices consistent with recognized quality and consumer-protection standards, building on the existing REAP business skills curriculum.
  3. Orient retail trading groups on KNCCI Garissa Chapter membership, registration and trade facilitation services, and support interested groups to begin the practical steps toward group or cooperative registration and chamber membership as a route to wider market recognition.
  4. Strengthen group-based collective quality assurance practice and joint market linkages, building on the existing 99.3 percent group membership base, so that REAP retail groups can supply quality-differentiated goods collectively to larger markets, including Garissa town wholesalers, aggregators and other buyers.
  5. Equip groups, together with their SOLO, RRDO and SCI coaches and peer mentors, with a simple, low-literacy self-assessment and quality-compliance checklist, and a directory of relevant KEBS and KNCCI contact points, to sustain quality practice after the training ends.

Scope of Work

The consultant(s) will carry out the assignment in five phases:

Phase 1: Inception, Desk Review and Standards Mapping

  • Review the REAP Tracer Study Final Report, existing REAP retail/business skills training content, and relevant KEBS and KNCCI published requirements.
  • Map the KEBS certification schemes and KNCCI membership requirements applicable to REAP retail product categories and to group-based applicants such as VSLAs, cooperatives, and community-based organizations.
  • Submit an inception report with a detailed work plan.

Phase 2: Institutional Engagement

  • Consult with the KEBS regional/county office serving Garissa and with the KNCCI Garissa Chapter to confirm current requirements, fees, and any simplified or group-based pathways available to REAP trading groups.
  • Document findings and any partnership opportunities in an institutional engagement brief.

Phase 3: Curriculum and Tool Development

  • Develop a standardized, low-literacy, Somali-adapted Quality Assurance and Standardization training curriculum and facilitator guide for retail trading groups.
  • Develop a Group Quality Self-Assessment and Compliance Checklist tool, using visual and demonstration-based formats appropriate for the target population.
  • Develop a KEBS/KNCCI referral directory for groups wishing to pursue registration, membership or certification.

Phase 4: Training Delivery

  • Deliver training sessions directly to retail trading groups and their leadership/committees across Ifo 1, Ifo 2, Dagahaley and Host.
  • Co-facilitate with SOLO, RRDO and SCI field staff and peer mentors so the approach can be sustained and reinforced through routine coaching after the assignment ends.
  • Where feasible, facilitate an introductory linkage session between interested groups and KEBS and/or KNCCI representatives.

Phase 5: Reporting and Handover

  • Submit a training report with attendance records, pre/post knowledge assessment results and group feedback.
  • Submit a final report comprising the complete standardized quality assurance package and an institutionalization brief with recommendations for sustaining and scaling the approach, including a possible pathway toward group registration or certification in future REAP cohorts.

Target Participants

  • REAP-supported retail trading groups (VSLA/cooperative-based), prioritized given the 82.6 percent concentration of REAP enterprises in retail trade.

  • Group leaders and committee members responsible for group purchasing, stock and sales decisions.

  • SOLO, RRDO and SCI livelihoods field staff and selected peer mentors, as co-facilitators to sustain the approach through ongoing coaching.

  • Indicative number of groups/participants: 50, drawn from Ifo 1, Ifo 2, Dagahaley and Hagadera settlements.

    Expected Deliverables and Indicative Timeline

    Deliverable and Indicative Timeline

    1.Inception report and work plan, including a mapping of KEBS product/quality certification schemes and KNCCI Garissa Chapter membership requirements applicable to REAP retail product categories and group-based (VSLA/cooperative) applicants:

    Indicative Timeline:

1.Within 5 working days of contract signing

  • 2. Institutional engagement brief documenting outcomes of consultations with the KEBS regional/county office and the KNCCI Garissa Chapter, including confirmed requirements, fees, and any simplified or group-based pathways available to REAP trading groups:

    Indicative Timeline:

  • Week 2

    3. Standardized, low-literacy, Somali-adapted Quality Assurance and Standardization training curriculum and facilitator guide for retail trading groups.

    Indicative Timeline:

  • Week 2

    4.Group Quality Self-Assessment and Compliance Checklist tool, and a KEBS/KNCCI referral directory for groups wishing to pursue registration or certification.

    Indicative Timeline:

    Week 2

    5.Delivery of training sessions to retail trading groups and their leadership across Ifo 1, Ifo 2, Dagahaley and Host, co-facilitated with SOLO, RRDO and SCI field staff and peer mentors.

    Indicative Timeline:

    Week 3-4

    6. Training report with attendance records, pre/post knowledge assessment results, and group feedback

    Indicative Timeline

  • Within 5 working days of training completion.

    7. Final report, including the complete standardized quality assurance package and an institutionalization brief with recommendations for sustaining and scaling the approach, including a pathway toward group registration/certification in future cohorts.

    Indicative Timeline.

  • 5th September 2026

  • Duration, Location and Level of Effort

  • The assignment is expected to require an estimated 15 working days over approximately 4 weeks, combining desk-based work, institutional engagement in Garissa town, and field-based training in Ifo 1, Ifo 2, Dagahaley and Host. SOLO will facilitate access to project sites, groups and relevant contacts; the consultant is responsible for their own travel, accommodation and logistics unless otherwise agreed in the contract.

  • Management and Reporting Arrangements

  • The consultant(s) will report to SOLO's REAP Project Manager, with technical oversight from the MEAL Coordinator, and will coordinate with designated focal points from RRDO and SCI throughout the assignment. All deliverables must be submitted in draft for review and comment before finalization.

  • Consultant Qualifications and Experience

  • Applications are invited from individual consultants, consultant teams, or firms. The proposed team should collectively demonstrate:

  • A relevant degree or professional qualification in quality assurance, trade/standards compliance, enterprise development, or a related field.

  • Demonstrated familiarity with KEBS product certification schemes (Standardization Mark, Import Standardization Mark, Diamond Mark) and/or KNCCI membership, registration and trade facilitation processes.

  • A minimum of 8 years of experience in MSE/SME development, market linkage facilitation, or quality/standards-focused business training.

  • Demonstrated experience developing training materials for low-literacy, refugee, or other vulnerable populations, ideally in Dadaab, other ASAL counties, or comparable humanitarian contexts.

  • Working knowledge of Somali language and Dadaab context, or the capacity to work with qualified Somali-speaking co-facilitators/translators.

  • Strong facilitation skills and experience working with grassroots trading groups, VSLAs or cooperatives.

    General Conditions

  • All materials, curricula, tools and directories produced under this assignment shall remain the intellectual property of SOLO and the REAP consortium and may not be reproduced or used for other purposes without written permission.

  • The consultant(s) will maintain confidentiality of all programme data and beneficiary information accessed during the assignment.

  • SOLO reserves the right to cancel or amend this call for applications at any stage without liability to applicants.

    Safeguarding and Code of Conduct

  • Given that the REAP project works directly with adolescent mothers, caregivers and other vulnerable populations, the selected consultant(s) will be required to sign and comply with SOLO's Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct, including Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) commitments, for the full duration of the assignment.

  • For clarification questions regarding this Terms of Reference, please contact Hussein.abdi@somalilifeline.org*.*

opportunities.title: Palestine Risk & Compliance Senior Officer
opportunities.description:
INTRODUCTION

Join Humanity & Inclusion (HI) as a Palestine Risk & Compliance Senior Officer and contribute to strengthening risk management and compliance across our humanitarian operations in Palestine.
You will support departments in managing risks and strengthening internal controls, coordinate audits, and promote a culture of integrity and accountability.

THE ORGANIZATION

Humanity & Inclusion / Handicap International - co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize- is an independent and impartial organisation working in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. Through our actions on the ground and our advocacy, we respond to the essential needs of vulnerable populations, improve their living conditions and promote respect for their dignity and fundamental rights. HI is present in 56 countries around the world.

Handicap International is an inclusive and equal opportunity employer and particularly welcomes applications from people with disabilities.

Please let us know if you need any special fittings, even during the first consultation.

OBJECTIVE OF THE POSITION:

Under the hierarchical management of the Deputy Country Director of HI Palestine during the establishment phase, and under the hierarchical management of the Regional Compliance Senior Officer beyond January 2027, the Palestine Risk & Compliance Senior Officer is responsible for establishing and operationalising the Risk & Compliance function within HI Palestine.

The position ensures that preventive procedures and internal control mechanisms are properly implemented, enabling HI Palestine to identify, prevent, mitigate and manage risks related to non-compliance with HI's internal rules and policies, applicable legal and administrative obligations, contractual commitments and ethical standards.

The Palestine Risk & Compliance Senior Officer provides mission-wide support and assurance on risk management, compliance, internal controls, audit coordination, due diligence and safeguarding. The position works closely with the Senior Management Team and all departments to strengthen organisational governance, accountability and risk-informed decision-making.

The position is responsible for establishing and structuring the Palestine Risk & Compliance Unit, developing its processes, tools and annual action plan, and ensuring effective coordination between compliance, risk management, safeguarding, audit and other assurance functions.

The scope of intervention covers all HI Palestine activities, projects, shared services, partnerships and operating locations, including remote-management settings.

The Palestine Risk & Compliance Senior Officer is the mission focal point for compliance and the fight against fraud and corruption. The position also ensures that HI staff, partners, suppliers and other relevant stakeholders are aware of applicable institutional policies, ethical standards, prevention measures and internal reporting/alert mechanisms.

The position directly supervises the Safeguarding Officer and ensures effective coordination between safeguarding and the wider Risk & Compliance framework, while respecting the specific technical and confidentiality requirements applicable to safeguarding and investigations.

The position requires a high degree of autonomy, sound judgement and the ability to establish systems and processes in a complex and rapidly evolving operational environment.

Responsibilities/ Missions:

1. Establish and Lead the Palestine Risk & Compliance Unit

Tasks:

  • Establish and operationalise the Risk & Compliance Unit within HI Palestine
  • Define and document the mandate, scope of intervention, roles, responsibilities and interfaces of the Unit with other departments and assurance functions
  • Develop the Unit's annual action plan and priorities based on the mission's risk profile and strategic priorities
  • Develop and institutionalise the Unit's procedures, SOPs, tools, templates and reporting mechanisms
  • Establish clear accountability and coordination mechanisms between risk management, compliance, internal control, safeguarding and audit functions
  • Develop risk-based reporting and escalation mechanisms for high and critical risks
  • Establish regular Risk & Compliance reporting to the Country Director and Senior Management Team
  • Ensure coordination and alignment with the Regional Compliance Senior Officer and the wider HI Compliance function
  • Contribute to the progressive integration of the Palestine Risk & Compliance Unit into the regional Compliance structure

2. Strategy, risk management and steering

Tasks:

  • Understand HI Palestine's strategy and translate it into operational objectives and priorities for the Risk & Compliance function
  • Support the development of the risk register including risk indicators, trigger points and escalation mechanisms for significant and critical risks
  • Support in the identification, analysis and assessment of organisational, operational, programme, financial, legal, regulatory, compliance, safeguarding, partnership, fraud and reputational risks
  • Support the definition of mitigation plans and monitor effectiveness of risk mitigation measures

3. Compliance and internal control

Tasks:

  • Ensure compliance with: HI internal rules, policies, procedures and standards; applicable national and international legal and regulatory requirements; contractual obligations; institutional donor requirements; partnership and consortium agreements; relevant requirements applicable to suppliers and third parties
  • Assess compliance and internal control risks associated with remote-management arrangements
  • Ensure that HI employees are familiar with the standards, procedures and tools required for the proper management of activities and resources
  • Identify control weaknesses and support departments in developing and implementing corrective action plans
  • Conduct risk-based compliance reviews, spot checks and second-level controls across the mission

4. Verification of Legal and Administrative Compliance

Tasks:

  • Ensure that HI Palestine complies with applicable legal, regulatory and administrative obligations required for its operations
  • Monitor key obligations related to registration, permits, authorisations, reporting requirements, labour regulations, taxation and other administrative requirements affecting HI operations in close coordination with the relevant departments (Finance, HR, Logistics)
  • Identify and escalate potential cases of non-compliance to the Country Director and relevant support functions
  • Support departments in implementing corrective measures where compliance gaps are identified.
  • Liaise with HQ, regional support functions and external legal advisers when specialised expertise is required

5. Compliance with contractual obligations and donor requirements and audit coordination

Tasks:

  • Support the Grants Manager, as the lead responsible for donor compliance, in identifying, monitoring and addressing risks related to contractual obligations and donor requirements applicable to institutional grants and other funding agreements
  • Act as the focal point for the coordination of internal and external audits within HI Palestine
  • Coordinate audit preparation, including the collection, organisation and provision of required documentation
  • Facilitate communication between auditors and relevant HI departments
  • Consolidate and coordinate management responses to audit findings and recommendations
  • Maintain a central audit findings and recommendations tracker, including corrective action plans
  • Follow up on the implementation and closure of audit recommendations
  • Ensure that lessons learned from audits inform the Risk & Compliance action plan, internal controls and procedures

6. Partnership and third-party due diligence

Tasks:

  • Establish and strengthen a risk-based due diligence framework for partners, suppliers, contractors, consultants and other relevant third parties
  • Ensure that appropriate due diligence is conducted before and, where relevant, during relationships with third parties
  • Ensure that identified risks are documented and appropriate mitigation measures are established and monitored throughout the duration of partnerships and contractual relationships

7. Focal point for the fight against fraud and corruption

Tasks:

  • Promote awareness of HI's policies relating to integrity, fraud, corruption, conflicts of interest and abuse among HI staff, partners and relevant third parties
  • Receive or facilitate the appropriate referral of reports through HI's established reporting (Ethics Point) and alert mechanisms, while ensuring confidentiality and respect for all individuals involved
  • Contribute, when specifically requested and within the applicable HI framework, to administrative investigations into fraud or abuse under the supervision of authorised HI management or HQ functions
  • Alert the Country Director, Regional Compliance Senior Officer and/or relevant HQ focal points in the event of significant fraud, corruption or integrity risks

8. Safeguarding supervision and oversight

Tasks:

  • Directly supervise and support the Safeguarding Officer and the Palestine Safeguarding focal points in West Bank and Gaza
  • Support the development and implementation of the mission safeguarding action plan
  • Ensure that safeguarding policies, procedures and reporting mechanisms are known and accessible to staff and relevant third parties
  • Support the strengthening of safe, confidential and accessible reporting and referral mechanisms
  • Monitor safeguarding compliance across HI operations and partnerships

Note that this job description must remain flexible; the list of tasks set out above is not exhaustive and is subject to changes resulting from the diversity of Humanity & Inclusion/Handicap International activities to respond to additional tasks or changes as identified by the line and functional managers.

Job Requirements:

Professional skills

  • University degree in audit
  • Minimum 5 years’ experience in audit and compliance,
  • Previous INGO experience is a desirable

Cross-cutting skills

  • Arabic and English are mandatory
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills.
  • Adapting communication and messages to an intercultural environment.
  • Proactive, shows initiative
  • Working as part of a team/network, cooperating.
  • Ability to give and receive constructive feedback, discussing with multi-disciplinary teams, working as part of a network and collaborating.
  • Advance knowledge of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Power Point, Access).
  • Planning, organizing and multitasking skills
  • Strong team player
  • Solution maker
  • Ability to travel to all countries of the programme when required

The initial contract will be for a period of up to 6 months, with the possibility of extension depending on the funds and the performance

PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS:

HI workers must adhere to the values and principles outlined in HI Code of conduct. In accordance with these values, HI operates and enforces policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-fraud, bribery, and corruption.

Handicap International is an equal-opportunity employer and particularly welcomes applications from persons with disabilities

opportunities.title: Community Committee Follow-up Staff Assistant (WFP Project)
opportunities.description:
Job purpose:

Job Location: Idleb

Number of Positions: 2

Contract Duration: 2 months, with no extension

Salary: As per the WFP salary scale

The Community Committee Follow-up Staff is responsible for supporting the establishment, capacity building, and continuous follow-up of community committees within targeted communities under the WFP project. The position ensures effective community participation, strengthens communication channels between the project team and community members, and supports community committees in fulfilling their roles in promoting accountability, transparency, and community engagement

Major Responsibilities:

  1. Community Committee Formation and Coordination
  • Support the identification and establishment of community committees in targeted areas according to project requirements.
  • Coordinate with community leaders and local stakeholders to ensure inclusive and transparent selection of committee members.
  • Ensure representation of different community groups, including women, vulnerable groups, and marginalized individuals where applicable.
  • Maintain updated records of community committee members and related documentation.

2. Community Committee Training and Capacity Building

  • Organize and facilitate orientation and training sessions for community committee members on their roles, responsibilities, and project objectives.
  • Provide guidance on community engagement, accountability mechanisms, feedback channels, and communication procedures.

Knowledge / Qualifications for the Role

Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:

  • Minimum high school diploma.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, Education, Community Development, or related fields.
  • Relevant experience may compensate for educational requirements

Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to facilitate discussions and training sessions.
  • Good understanding of community-based approaches and humanitarian principles.
  • Ability to work effectively with diverse community groups.
  • Good reporting and documentation skills.
  • Ability to work in the field and travel to project locations.
  • Good knowledge of MS Office applications.

Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement

  • 80% field work
  • 20% office based

Physical Requirements

  • Based in NWS

Language Requirements

  • English and Arabic,

opportunities.title: Finance Manager
opportunities.description:
About Qatar Charity

Qatar Charity is a leading international humanitarian and development organization working in numerous countries to support vulnerable communities through sustainable development, humanitarian assistance, education, health, livelihood, and social welfare programs.

Job Purpose

We are seeking a highly qualified Field Financial Manager to join Qatar Charity's international operations. The successful candidate may be assigned to one of Qatar Charity's field offices worldwide and will play a key role in ensuring sound financial management, effective financial control, compliance, and strategic financial planning.

The Field Financial Manager is responsible for providing financial leadership and oversight, supporting decision-making through financial analysis, ensuring compliance with organizational policies and local regulations, and safeguarding the organization's financial resources, assets, and investments.

Key Responsibilities

  • Prepare and manage annual budgets in alignment with strategic objectives and operational plans.
  • Monitor budget implementation and financial performance, providing periodic reports and recommendations.
  • Ensure the accuracy of accounting records and compliance with approved financial policies, accounting standards, and local regulations.
  • Prepare financial statements, annual accounts, and year-end financial closures.
  • Oversee all accounting and financial operations within the field office.
  • Analyze costs, expenditures, operational results, and financial performance against approved plans and budgets.
  • Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports for headquarters, donors, and other stakeholders.
  • Establish and maintain effective financial controls and risk management mechanisms.
  • Ensure implementation of financial directives and procedures issued by headquarters.
  • Coordinate internal and external audits and ensure proper documentation is maintained.
  • Prepare audit files and support audit processes and financial reviews.
  • Oversee inventory management, cash operations, and asset registration.
  • Ensure adequate insurance coverage for office assets and properties where applicable.
  • Review financial obligations, project balances, guarantees, surpluses, and deficits, and recommend corrective actions.
  • Supervise and develop accounting staff within the field office.
  • Participate in procurement and tender committees as required.
  • Support senior management with financial analysis, forecasts, and strategic recommendations.

Qualifications& Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Financial Management, or a related field.
  • Professional certifications such as CPA, CMA, ACCA, CFA, or equivalent are highly desirable.
  • Minimum of 6 years of progressive experience in accounting, finance, or financial management.
  • Excellent English language skills; Arabic, French or any additional languages are an asset.
  • Experience in humanitarian, development, nonprofit, or international organizations is highly preferred.
  • Proven experience in budgeting, financial reporting, financial controls, and audit coordination.
  • Experience working with ERP systems and financial management software.
  • Experience managing multicultural teams and working in complex operational environments is an advantage.
  • Willingness to be assigned to any Qatar Charity field office worldwide.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong financial management and accounting expertise.
  • Budget planning, forecasting, and financial analysis.
  • Knowledge of international accounting standards and financial controls.
  • Risk management and compliance awareness.
  • Strong leadership and team management capabilities.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Effective communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Strong organizational and reporting abilities.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, especially Excel.
  • Experience using ERP and financial management systems.

Additional Information:

  • The selected candidate may be assigned to any Qatar Charity field office worldwide based on organizational needs.
  • The role requires a high degree of flexibility, adaptability, and willingness to work in diverse cultural and operational contexts.

opportunities.title: Senior Liaison Advisor EU - Global Partnerships and Resource Mobilization
opportunities.description:
DanChurchAid (DCA) is seeking an energetic and committed professional with demonstrated experience in building and managing relations and global partnerships and consortia, as well as mobilising resources from institutional donors for international programmes, to join the Global Partnerships and Resource Mobilization (GPRM) Unit based in Copenhagen.

In this role, you will contribute to the development and implementation of DCA's strategy towards European institutions and relevant European platforms. As DCA's focal point in Brussels, you will play a key role in strengthening DCA's position as a credible organisation in its engagement with the European Union and related institutions. The position is designed to contribute directly to increasing EU funding and expanding strategic partnership opportunities for DCA.

You will lead efforts to maintain and further develop DCA's long-term partnership with the EU, both as a lead grant holder and, where relevant, as a consortium partner. You will also support strategic engagement and advocacy initiatives while ensuring that the organisation remains informed of key policy developments, funding opportunities, and budgetary trends within the EU landscape.

opportunities.title: Development of MSF’s Menstrual Health Management (MHM) Toolkit
opportunities.description:
MSF Inclusive Innovation

Development of MSF’s Menstrual Health Management (MHM) Toolkit

Consultancy: Development of Practical MHM Guidance and Information, Education and Communication (IEC)/Health Promotion (HP) Materials for MSF

Background

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, natural disasters, and exclusion from healthcare. Through its Inclusive Innovation team, MSF has been working to strengthen menstrual health management (MHM) support across diverse humanitarian settings.

Menstrual health is more than hygiene, it is fundamentally tied to dignity, health, protection, and participation. Yet in humanitarian contexts, it remains widely overlooked. Periods do not pause in crises, but access to the resources, facilities, and knowledge needed to manage them safely often does. Across many MSF settings, menstruation is highly stigmatised, and women and girls lack access to safe, private facilities and practical information, limiting their ability to move freely and participate fully in daily life.

In response, MSF’s Inclusive Innovation team has taken a holistic and participatory approach to MHM that goes beyond simply providing MHM products to address the full spectrum of needs, including stigma, knowledge, infrastructure, and community dynamics. This work has been grounded in seeking to understand the lived experiences of women and girls.

Since 2018, MSF have implemented 11 MHM projects across eight countries, including the Democratic Republic of Congo, Mali, Sierra Leone, India, Bangladesh, Iraq, Ethiopia, and Bhutan. These projects have explored a range of approaches, including community-based participatory methods, menstrual underwear (MU) distribution, hygiene kit provision, Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WaSH) facility assessments, and health promotion activities. Together, these experiences represent a growing but previously fragmented body of operational knowledge within MSF.

In January 2026, MSF’s Inclusive Innovation team produced the MSF MHM Synthesis Report, a comprehensive consolidation of this body of work. The report brings together qualitative and quantitative insights from across projects to identify common patterns, context-specific differences, and recurring operational challenges. It captures three core areas of learning:

  • MHM knowledge, beliefs, and practices across different communities
  • project outcomes, including the acceptability and feasibility of different approaches
  • operational learnings related to design, implementation, and delivery.

From this analysis, the report presents 44 structured recommendations across five key implementation domain - context, organisational systems, project design, project delivery, and individuals - supported by an evidence confidence framework. While the report provides a strong evidence base, it is primarily a technical and analytical document and is not designed for direct use in implementing integrated MHM interventions as part of MSF operations.

This synthesis serves as the foundation for MSF’s forthcoming MHM Toolkit: a practical, field-oriented resource designed to translate evidence into action. The toolkit is intended to support MSF teams at project and coordination levels to design, adapt, and implement MHM interventions in diverse humanitarian settings.

The toolkit will function as a decision-support and implementation resource, bringing together:

  • Practical guidance for designing and adapting MHM interventions across contexts
  • Step-by-step tools and templates to support implementation and delivery
  • Participatory methods to engage communities and address stigma and social norms
  • Operational tools to support integration across sectors, including health promotion, WaSH, and Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR)

Importantly, the toolkit is not intended to be a static guidance document, but rather a modular, user-centred resource that supports teams to make context-specific decisions and adapt approaches in real time.

While the synthesis report provides evidence, the toolkit is the means of translating that evidence into practice. A central component of the toolkit will be a suite of Health Promotion (HP) and Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) materials that make complex insights accessible, actionable, and relevant for different users and contexts. These materials will play a critical role in supporting community engagement, behaviour change, and the practical delivery of MHM activities.

Objectives

MSF's Inclusive Innovation team is seeking external creative communications support to translate evidence, recommendations, and operational learning detailed in the MSF MHM Synthesis Report into a practical, accessible and engaging suite of Health Promotion (HP) and Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials to be included in the MSF MHM Toolkit.

This requires a thorough review of the synthesis report to identify priority findings and messages, assess their potential for creative communication, and recommend the most appropriate content formats, communication assets, and storytelling techniques to maximise engagement across diverse audiences and operational applications.

The objectives are to:

  1. To review, analyse, and synthesize the findings, recommendations, and operational learning from the MSF MHM Synthesis Report to inform the development of evidence-based resources and guidance.
  2. To identify and prioritise key themes, messages, target audiences, and use cases, and translate complex evidence and operational insights from the MSF MHM Synthesis Report into clear, engaging, context-sensitive HP and IEC materials, and toolkit content.
  3. To develop audience-appropriate materials that meet the needs of MSF frontline and coordination staff, as well as diverse community groups, including women, girls, men, and boys, ensuring relevance, accessibility, and practical applicability.
  4. To produce implementation-ready materials that are suitable for printing in low-resource settings, optimised for digital use, adaptable across multiple operational contexts, and available in a range of accessible formats.

Core language: English (Materials should be created and delivered in formats that allow easy translation into additional languages)

Expected Results/Outcomes:

Our expected production cycles include:

  • Discovery, Creative Direction and Content Planning
  • Prototype Development and Concept Testing
  • Final Asset Production
  • Toolkit Integration and Roll-out Support

Your team will:

  • Have demonstrable experience developing user-centred design and communication materials within humanitarian and global health contexts, including translating complex evidence and operational learning into accessible, audience-appropriate content and visual assets.
  • The proposed team should demonstrate a complementary mix of expertise in creative strategy, health communication, content development, graphic design and illustration, storytelling, and user-centred research and testing. Prior experience in MHM, SRHR, gender, WaSH, or other related technical areas will be considered an asset.
  • Include team members with professional-level English proficiency and demonstrated experience developing materials and facilitating collaboration across multilingual and multicultural environments, including with non-native English speakers.
  • Have strong interpersonal and facilitation skills to work effectively with multidisciplinary teams and develop content that encourages meaningful engagement, reflection, and sustained community interaction.
  • Be skilled in identifying communication opportunities and operational barriers, translating complex evidence into clear, accessible, and audience-appropriate materials that support understanding and practical application.
  • Demonstratable experience in applying scalable, adaptable, and user-centered methodology with clear quality assurance processes to support consistent delivery across all stages of development and production.
  • Demonstrate a strong understanding of the role of communications, health promotion, and community engagement within humanitarian and global health settings, and effectively communicate this value to project teams and stakeholders.
  • Possess excellent communication, engagement, storytelling, and design capabilities and thrive working under pressure in culturally diverse and evolving operational environments.
  • Demonstrate alignment with humanitarian principles and a strong commitment to the values, mission, and operational approach of MSF.

opportunities.title: National Programme Officer NOB Emergency, N'Djamena, Chad (For Chadian nationality only)
opportunities.description:
ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT

The Emergency Officer will play a central role in supporting WFP Chad's emergency preparedness, response, and strategic transition agenda in one of the world's most complex humanitarian environments. Chad continues to face recurrent displacement crises, climate shocks, and chronic food insecurity, while hosting a growing refugee population from neighboring countries. In this context, WFP is implementing a gradual transition from largely status-based assistance towards a vulnerability-driven approach that prioritizes resources according to needs while strengthening pathways towards resilience and self-reliance.

Working under the Emergency Preparedness and Response function, the incumbent will support preparedness planning, emergency response coordination, operational analysis, and partnership engagement across the Country Office and Field Offices. The position requires close collaboration with programme, supply chain, protection, digital solutions, and monitoring teams, as well as with key external stakeholders including UNHCR, IOM, CNARR, government authorities, NGOs, and humanitarian coordination mechanisms.

The Emergency Officer will contribute to ensuring that emergency interventions remain timely, accountable, and evidence-based, while supporting the operationalization of WFP's strategic shift towards vulnerability-based targeting and integrated assistance approaches. This includes supporting emergency assessments, beneficiary targeting and verification processes, digital delivery systems, donor reporting, and coordination efforts that bridge humanitarian response with resilience, livelihoods, and self-reliance opportunities for refugees and vulnerable host communities.

The role requires strong analytical, coordination, and operational skills, as well as the ability to work across multiple functions and partners to support WFP's objective of saving lives today while enabling vulnerable populations to progressively reduce their reliance on humanitarian assistance over time.

JOB PURPOSE

To provide support to policy and programme activities that effectively meet food assistance needs.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES (not all-inclusive, within delegated authority)

  • Lead emergency preparedness and rapid response coordination by supporting the implementation of the Country Office Emergency Preparedness and Response, maintaining minimum preparedness standards, strengthening refugee influx analysis and timely rapid response, and operational coordination with UNCHR and CNARR.
  • Support the delivery of high-quality emergency assistance and programmatic transition efforts by working closely with internal and external stakeholders to ensure effective targeting, beneficiary management, digital delivery systems, and the progressive shift from predominantly status-based assistance to vulnerability-based assistance creating coherent pathways from emergency response to resilience-building/self-reliance solutions for refugees and vulnerable host communities.
  • Contribute to operational analysis, evidence generation, and strategic reporting through needs assessments, operational monitoring, donor reporting, situation reports, and management briefs that support informed decision-making, resource mobilization, and accountability to affected populations and donors.
  • Facilitate coordination across humanitarian and reinforce collaboration with Government by supporting the Food Security cluster Coordination, developing and implementing the collaboration framework and capacity strengthening activities with the CNARR and other relevant government technical services.
  • Contribute towards the development of a wide variety of projects, plans and processes, ensuring alignment with wider programme policies and guidance.
  • Provide project management support to specific and defined programmes and projects of considerable size/complexity, ensuring a coordinated approach with wider programmes that complies with WFP standards and procedures.
  • Develop and coordinate data gathering and monitoring systems ensuring that rigorous quality standards are maintained.
  • Research and analyse a range of policy and operational issues to inform the development of policies, programmes and activities.
  • Contribute to the preparation of accurate and timely reporting on programmes and activities that enable informed decision making and consistency of information presented to stakeholders.
  • Liaise with internal and external counterparts to ensure effective collaboration, monitor ongoing projects and highlight potential risks to project delivery.
  • Support the identification, development and management of potential partnerships to collaborative working leading to improved food assistance packages.
  • Support the capacity building of WFP staff, partners and national government to prepare for and respond to food assistance needs, e.g. through providing inputs into training materials.
  • Guide and supervise more junior staff, acting as a point of referral and supporting them with analysis and queries.
  • Other as required.

DESIRED EXPERIENCES FOR ENTRY INTO THE ROLE

• Have 3 years of professional experience in Programme, especially in emergency area.

•Has deepened technical knowledge through exposure to technical teams.

• Has taken leadership of implementing programmes.

• Has provided input into policy discussions and decisions.

STANDARD MINIMUM ACADEMIC QUALIFICATIONS

Education: Advanced University degree in International Affairs, Economics, Nutrition/Health, Agriculture, Environmental Science, Social Sciences or other field relevant to international development assistance, or First University Degree with additional years of related work experience and/or trainings/courses.

Language: International Professional: Fluency (level C) in French language. Intermediate knowledge (level B) in English
