opportunities.title: Finance Coordinator - Nigeria - M/F
opportunities.description:
ALIMA IN NIGERIA

ALIMA has been present in Nigeria since 2016. Its actions are part of a regional response strategy to health and nutrition emergencies, with a focus on pediatric, maternal-infant, and epidemic interventions. ALIMA is present in North-East Nigeria in Borno State (MMC and Jere LGAs) and in Yobe State (Bade and Karasuwa LGAs) where it provides outpatient and inpatient healthcare and nutrition services for IDPs and host communities. In North-West Nigeria, ALIMA is in Katsina State (Kaita, Batagarawa, and Katsina LGAs) to respond to increased nutritional needs. ALIMA is present in the South-West, in Ondo State (Owo LGA) where teams are treating patients for Lassa fever and conducting research into improved treatment.

In Borno state, ALIMA ensures outpatient and inpatient access to nutrition services, as well as outpatient health care in MMC and Jere LGAs. In 2022, ALIMA delivered 85,925 OPD consultations and treated 9,278 SAM cases without complications at the OTP level. 3,963 deliveries were conducted, and 2,446 mental health consultations were delivered. ALIMA also provided inpatient care for SAM cases with complications within 3 stabilization centres (University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital -UMTH, Gwange II, and Fatima Ali Sherrif - in MMC) and treated 3,386 SAM children with complications.

In Yobe state, ALIMA supports 5 Primary Health Care Centers (PHCCs) - Waro, Jajeri, Jajimaji, K. Garun Guna and K. Galu - since May 2021 for nutrition and health care. ALIMA also provides inpatient care for SAM cases with complications within its 40 beds stabilization center located in Gashua General Hospital, Bade LGA. ALIMA also support hospitalization for children under five in Jajimaji. In 2022, ALIMA delivered 53,196 OPD consultations and treated 4,722 SAM children. 2,036 deliveries were conducted, and 976 mental health consultations were delivered.

In Katsina state, ALIMA ensures since August 2021 the provision of outpatient and inpatient nutrition and healthcare services for children under 5. ALIMA currently delivers OPD consultations, and supports the ambulatory management and referral of Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) cases in 5 Primary Health Care Centers (PHCCs) in Kaita LGA: Dankama, Sabon Birni (Ba’awa ward), Dankaba, Zabakau (Gafiya ward), Matsai. ALIMA also ensures inpatient healthcare and provides care for SAM cases with complications within its 110 beds stabilisation centre located in Kaita CHC. In 2022, ALIMA treated 2,171 SAM cases with complications at the ITFC level and 29,239 SAM cases without complications at the OTP level. ALIMA also delivered 36,851 OPD consultations for children under 5, while 4,906 were hospitalized at the inpatient department of Kaita CHC.

In Ondo State, ALIMA has been supporting the NCDC and the State Ministry of Health with case management, active case detection, patient triage, public awareness campaigns, and reinforcement of the Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) measures among health workers in the different hospital structures of Ondo State. In addition to prevention and case management, ALIMA is currently participating in the coordination of several studies to better understand the disease, including an observational cohort study (LASCOPE) to describe the clinical, biological course, management and outcomes of hospitalized patients with a diagnosis of confirmed Lassa fever and a phase II clinical trial (SAFARI) to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Favipiravir.

MISSION AND OBJECTIVES

The Financial Coordinator will serve as the safeguarding authority for the finance department, responsible for defining and implementing the strategic direction of the department to support operational goals. This role encompasses overseeing the proper management of ALIMA's resources within the mission, ensuring accurate accounting practices, and monitoring mission budgets. The Financial Coordinator will play a crucial role as a management controller, facilitating financial planning and treasury security. Furthermore, the incumbent will be responsible for timely reporting to both headquarters and donors, ensuring transparency and compliance with financial regulations.

TASKS & RESPONSABILITIES

Main tasks:

  • The FINCO contributes to the definition of the Strategy of the mission with the Coordination of Team.
  • The FINCO applies, reinforces and supervises the respect of the procedures and tools of Alima in the mission, in order to secure the resources & improve the quality of the management of the missions, in order to allow better operations for our beneficiaries.
  • He/She supervises and guarantees a proper accounting for the mission, with SAGA Software with the support of deputy finance coordinator.
  • He/She defines the procedures of treasury management for the mission to secure the resources of Alima.
  • He/She provides to the mission and HQ, a good visibility and risks on budget of the mission, with regular follow-up of the budgets, and consolidate the planning of expenses with the projects & coordination.
  • He/She is in charge to built and follow up the Mission Budget of ALIMA Nigeria and the allocation table with the support of deputy finance coordinator
  • He/She realises the budget propal for Donors and the financial report to Donors, in respect of Donors procedures and ALIMA’s requirements.
  • He/She recruits, managed and supervised the finance team of the mission.
  • He takes actions for the prevention of Fraud & Corruption, alerts HQ on the risks on resources in the missions and is in charge of internal control.
  • He/ She plans and organizes audit preparation, manages with the support of the deputy finance coordinator he will implement training needs, and participates in training administrative staff (accounting assistants and base administrators) in accounting data entry and procedures (use of accounts, use of SAGA software, cash management, etc.)
  • He/She supervises the deputy finance coordinator, and provides capacity building.

PROTECTION OF BENEFICIARIES AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS

Level 3: The incumbent is responsible for the application of HR processes and may be required to conduct field visits. She/he. He/she may therefore be in contact with children and/or vulnerable adults. Therefore, a criminal record check or the presentation of a certificate of good conduct will be required. In situations where the impossibility of providing a criminal record or a certificate of good conduct is established, a declaration of honour will be requested.

EXPERIENCES & COMPETENCES

Experiences:

  • University degree in finance, administration, and human resources
  • Minimum 5 years experience in Finance management
  • Experience in a similar position for at least 1 year.
  • Experience with medical international NGO is an asset.
  • Team management and supervision skills.
  • Knowledge of Donors and experience in Financial Reports.
  • Perfect knowledge of MS Office packages, especially Excel.
  • Knowledge of Saga (Finance software) is appreciated

Qualities required:

  • Rigorous, autonomous, and organized
  • Adapting Capacities and Proactivity
  • Ability to work in a multicultural context
  • Risk Alert, and good communication

Languages:

  • English is mandatory
  • French is an asset

CONDITIONS

Contract term: contract under French law, 12 months

Position to be filled: ASAP

Salary: Competitive Compensation: Depending on experience, along with a per diem of USD 20.

Comprehensive Travel Support: We cover all travel costs between your country of origin and the mission location.

Accommodation costs are fully covered to ensure your comfort while you work.

Health Benefits: Enjoy peace of mind with our health coverage that includes not only you but also your dependents residing in your home country. Medical coverage starts from your first day of contract and extends for one month after your departure from the mission country.

Regular Breaks: After every three months of service, you are entitled to a paid break of 7 working days back in your home country. ALIMA covers your travel expenses up to 1500 Euros, allowing you to rest and reconnect with your loved ones without financial worry.

opportunities.title: Consultancy Opportunity: Mediation Skills Training for Female Youth in Mogadishu, Somalia.
opportunities.description:
Background

The American Friends Service Committee is a Quaker organization that includes people of various faiths who are committed to social justice, peace, and humanitarian service. Guided by the Quaker belief in the divine light of each person, AFSC works with communities and partners worldwide to challenge unjust systems and promote lasting peace. AFSC has more than 100 years of experience building peace in communities worldwide and works in the following ways: bridging and convening, community organizing and civil society strengthening, advocacy, research, and analysis. It seeks to change situations and systems that lead to violence. Much of AFSC's work includes support to opportunities for dialogue and capacity building led by the affected communities.

About the Somalia Program

AFSC believes that young people can positively transform the prevailing context of violent conflicts in Somalia into more secure, productive, and just places. Consequently, AFSC is implementing a peacebuilding program in Somalia targeting the youth, with the approach of empowering them with peacebuilding, leadership, and advocacy skills.

In Somalia, AFSC works in Mogadishu, Kismayu, Bosaso and Dadaab Refugee Camp in Kenya that hosts 97% refugees of Somalia origin.

Young women in Mogadishu are increasingly called upon to prevent and resolve conflicts within their families, peer groups, and communities, yet often lack adequate knowledge and skills in mediation and safe spaces to practice them. AFSC therefore seeks to engage a qualified consultant to train 20 female youth in Mogadishu on mediation skills while strengthening their capacity to prevent, manage, and peacefully resolve conflict in their community.

Overall Objective

To equip 20 female youth trained in Alternative to Violence Program (AVP) in Mogadishu with practical mediation skills and strengthen their capacity to prevent, manage, and peacefully resolve conflicts within their families and communities.

Specific Objectives

The consultant is expected to:

  • Develop training materials, and a facilitation plan tailored to the Mogadishu context and the needs of young women.
  • Conduct a five-day, in-person training for 20 female youth in Mogadishu on mediation skills.
  • Provide participants with handouts, case studies, tools, and templates for future reference.
  • Submit a comprehensive training report including outcomes, lessons learned, and recommendations.

Scope of Assignment

The consultant is expected to train on mediation covering aspects including and not limited to:

  • Introduction to conflict, conflict analysis, and conflict dynamics.
  • Principles, approaches, and stages of mediation.
  • Core mediation skills ; active listening, neutrality, reframing, and negotiation.
  • The role of young women as mediators and peace agents within families and communities.

opportunities.title: Outreach and Engagement Advisor
opportunities.description:
Description

The Pacific Community (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The Strategic Communications, Outreach and Engagement Unit is a central function under the Office of the Director-General, which is responsible for driving a strategic, integrated and contemporary approaches to communications and storytelling that drives impact across our organisation and externally. The team provides central coordination, development of effective systems and processes, coordination of strategic and Pacific-led storytelling approaches, policies, procedures and impact-based communication actions. A central aim of this role will be to ensure culturally sensitive storytelling including capturing of Pacific-led and owned stories of impact and preservation of cultural storytelling in line with Pacific cultures and practices. A central aim of the division is achieving visibility of SPC’s results – achieved in collaboration with our members and development partners – through improved media engagement and coordination within SPC.

The role – Outreach and Engagement Advisor will be central to the strategic engagement, outreach and implementation of effective strategic communications practices internal and external to SPC across gender equality. The role will also support integrated and organisational wide gender equality coordination and work with internal systems and teams to strengthen the translation of policy to action.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

Engagement strategy design, implementation and strategic content to translate for SPC staff, partners and members in coordinated and integrated manners

  • Lead the development of the internal SPC engagement strategy with key partners (OneSPC, SPL, SCOE, WIL and O&I) ensuring change process and systems are translated into accessible, practical and innovative tools.
  • Drive meaningful engagement sessions with incentivised actions to increase engagement in partnership with OneSPC teams and partners across SPC in dynamic ways.
  • Demonstrate results show impact in improved engagement and understanding of the value and expected behaviours of SPC staff, vendors, partners and members and better understanding of policy in action around gender and integrated areas of work including the change management approaches underway in SPC.

Effective information development and dissemination through best practice design, strategic communications, outreach and engagement

  • Lead the development of best-practice dissemination channels including a quarterly Internal and Member’s Circular distribution with OneSPC, Director SCOE and Executive Office.
  • Implement the SPC Ambassador program in partnership with SCOE Outreach & Engagement team for staff including development of products, training and support in integrated and OneSPC focused manners.
  • Review and set clear standards for all SPC communications information internally to better inform action, understanding and engagement.
  • Manage the WIL and Gender Flagship digital web pages and content alongside SCOE team broadly and digital teams where needed.

Internal coordination and outreach between operations and integration and science and capability teams broadly

  • Coordinate, develop and disseminate inputs and elevation of gender equality and WIL content in digital and best practice ways across and alongside the broader practitioners and teams in SPC across all internal communications actions.
  • Lead the development of quarterly internal reports on SPC online and outreach performance for pivoting and learning purposes including use of pulse surveys through Culture Amp coordination.
  • Ensure key communications focal point for content development for internal communications and internal gender equality and WIL work in line with member direction and organisational institutional strengthening.
  • Lead the coordination of bringing together learning practices and sessions to ensure outreach and engagement of changing policies, behaviours, sensitisation of SOPs such as the Domestic Violence policy and wellbeing focal points is anchored by this role collectively with respective internal teams.

Data visualisation

  • Lead the coordination of using existing internal systems work with the Online Community Officer and Communications teams to support development of visual templates, in-house training packages using SPC’s Learning Management System, using Shorthand and other tools to promote understanding by our audiences (internal and external).
  • Ensure coordination of matrix line management team to ensure all documents are saved in appropriate folders for knowledge management, processes of change are captured, and all images and content is loaded to appropriate locations for auditing and use purposes.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please refer to the online job description.

Key selection criteria

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in communications, engagement, media, graphic design or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

Technical expertise

  • At least 7 years of professional experience in strategic communications, development, or related area, with a strong focus on integration, digital and outreach tools and engagement.
  • Experience in digital analytics tools to track performance on internal and external platforms.
  • Excellent interpersonal and cross-cultural communications, outreach and engagement skills working across integrated and diverse teams.
  • Must be creative and tech-savvy.
  • Must be a passionate innovator that is adept to leveraging best-practice strategic engagement and relationships to drive engagement and growth internally and externally to SPC.

Language skills

  • Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage.

Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness

  • Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

Salary, terms and conditions

Contract Duration – Until 31 July 2029 – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

Remuneration – The Outreach and Engagement Advisor is a band 10 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 2,703‒3,379 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 8,354–10,442 (USD 3,623-4,528; EUR 3,269-4,086). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva – SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

Languages – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

Recruitment principles – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an equal-opportunity employer, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the Pacific Islander. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

opportunities.title: Logistics Officer (M/F) – Syria Technical Assistance Hub [Team Europe Initiative]
opportunities.description:
Mission Description

As part of a Team Europe Initiative (TEI), bringing together the European Commission and five European bilateral cooperation agencies, the Technical Assistance (TA) Hub will support the Syrian government to reinforce institutional systems and capacities. The TA Hub will serve as a central entry point for TA requests, linking the priorities expressed by the Syrian government with the relevant expertise, in coordination and complementarity with other actors and initiatives. The TA Hub is designed as a fully demand-driven mechanism to facilitate and coordinate access to Technical Assistance.

The Logistics Officer of the Team Europe Initiative (TEI) Technical Assistance Hub for Syria, will ensure the efficient management of logistics and office operations to support the implementation of the project. Working within the Project Management Unit and Expertise France/GIZ support services, the Logistics Officer will facilitate the smooth delivery of project activities by overseeing procurement processes, office administration, transportation, and logistical arrangements in compliance with Expertise France/GIZ procedures.

Main Responsibilities

The responsibilities of the Logistics Officer will include:

  • Managing project procurement processes, including requesting quotations, collecting and verifying mandatory supporting documentation, and monitoring the validity of contracts related to office operations and project activities, in coordination with Expertise France support services;
  • Providing logistical support for the implementation of Technical Assistance Plans (TAPs), including the procurement of goods and services required for project activities, as well as travel booking;
  • Supporting the establishment and day-to-day management of the project office, including utilities, maintenance, lease management, office supplies, and service providers;
  • Coordinating vehicle rental, transportation, and travel logistics to ensure the efficient movement of project staff, experts, and visitors;
  • Maintaining logistics records and ensure compliance with Expertise France/GIZ administrative and procurement procedures;
  • Liaising with internal support services and external service providers to ensure the timely delivery of logistical and operational support;
  • Contributing to the smooth functioning of the Project Management Unit by providing day-to-day operational and logistical assistance as required;
  • Assisting the National Operations Security Coordinator in refining, operationalising, and implementing secure mission arrangements, in coordination with any provider, ensuring that all field missions are planned and conducted in accordance with established security procedures.

Qualifications & experience

Profile

  • Bachelor's degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Procurement, or another relevant field;
  • At least 3 years of professional experience in logistics, procurement, administration, or operations support, preferably with an international organisation, NGO, or donor-funded project;
  • Strong command of Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and Word;
  • Demonstrated experience in procurement processes, supplier management, contract follow-up, and office administration;
  • Experience in organising travel, transportation, and logistical arrangements for staff, consultants, and project activities;
  • Good knowledge of logistics and procurement procedures of international organisations;
  • Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines;
  • Excellent interpersonal and coordination skills, with the ability to work effectively with a wide range of national and international stakeholders;
  • Fluency in Arabic and English (written and spoken).

Desirable qualifications (optional criteria):

  • Previous experience with EU-funded projects or European agencies;
  • Knowledge of French would be an asset;

Context and project description

The Team Europe Initiative (TEI) Technical Assistance Hub project

Funded by the European Union, as well as several EU Member States, the TA Hub is a Team Europe Initiative aiming at providing technical assistance to the Syrian government (national and subnational institutions), upon their demand, within the framework of the reconstruction of Syria and its institutions. The project will be co-implemented by a consortium composed of 5 European cooperation agencies: GIZ, Expertise France, AICS, the British Council and ENABEL.

About Expertise France

Expertise France is France’s public agency and interministerial actor in charge of international technical cooperation. As a subsidiary of Agence Française de Développement Group (AFD Group), it designs and implements projects that sustainably strengthen public policies in developing and emerging countries. Expertise France works in key areas of development: governance, security, climate change, health, education, and more. Alongside its partners, it contributes to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Expertise France in Syria

Expertise France has been working in Syria since 2013 within the framework of stabilization programs, focusing on areas outside of direct control from the former Syrian regime. In line with the humanitarian-development nexus, Expertise France’s action seeks to create the conditions for stabilization, economic recovery, and community resilience. The overall objective of Expertise France’s program in Syria has been to strengthen human security and affected communities’ resilience by improving livelihoods and preparedness. Since January 2025, Expertise France is committed to scaling up its activities across the Syrian territory, supporting the reconstruction and recovery, in coordination and collaboration with the Government of Syria.

Further information

  • Type of contract: 12 month fixed-term local consulting contract local employment contract (renewable)
  • Starting date: September 2026
  • Remuneration: according to EF salary grid and profile

opportunities.description:
Position Information

  • VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/123
  • Position Title: National Technical Consultant to support the Personal Status Department in MOIM on records replications.
  • Duty Station: Beirut
  • Duration: 6 months (without exceeding 15 working days per month)
  • Vacancy Date of Issue: 27 July 2026
  • Vacancy Closure Date: 03 August 2026
  • National or International consultancy: National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1pWDc2D45gg931NcaisgWjJOIAnETTrEy/view

BACKGROUND

UNDP has been working closely with the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities (MoIM) to strengthen the capacity and efficiency of key public institutions responsible for delivering essential services to citizens. As one of the core public service providers, the Directorate General of Personal Status (DGPS) plays a critical role in ensuring citizens’ access to civil registration and identity-related services, which are fundamental to legal identity, protection, and access to public services.

In light of the multiple crises affecting Lebanon, including the impact of the recent conflict, the demand for timely and accessible civil registration services has significantly increased. At the same time, several Personal Status Departments have faced operational challenges, including increased workloads, damaged infrastructure, and limited administrative capacity. Strengthening the Directorate’s operational capacity is therefore essential to ensure the continuity and quality of service delivery.

As part of its support to the MoIM, UNDP is assisting the Directorate General of Personal Status in enhancing its operational efficiency and improving service delivery through targeted technical assistance. To support these efforts, UNDP is seeking a National Technical Consultant to provide technical and administrative support to the Directorate in processing, organizing, verifying, and managing civil registration data and related records, thereby contributing to more efficient, accurate, and citizen-centred service delivery across the Personal Status Departments.

SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES, AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK

Under the supervision of the Senior Project Officer and the Director General of Personal Status, the consultant will be responsible for:

  • Organizing and reviewing civil registration files and supporting documentation to ensure completeness and compliance with the Directorate’s requirements.
  • Coordinating with relevant departments within the Directorate General of Personal Status and other concerned government entities to follow up on missing documentation and verify records, as required.
  • Entering, updating, and validating civil registration data in the Directorate’s electronic database while ensuring data accuracy and consistency.
  • Supporting the processing, tracking, and archiving of civil registration records and related administrative documentation.
  • Identifying, reporting, and following up on data inconsistencies and technical issues affecting the electronic database, and coordinating with the relevant technical teams to facilitate their resolution.
  • Preparing periodic progress updates on data-entry activities, file processing, and operational challenges to support informed decision-making and efficient workflow management.

EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities, noting that the total duration should not exceed six months, with no more than 15 working days per month.

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

  • The consultant will work under the overall guidance of the Governance and Rule of Law Chief Technical Advisor/Project Officer.
  • The title rights, copyrights, and all other rights of whatsoever nature in any material produced under the provisions of this Terms of Reference will be vested exclusively in UNDP. UNDP has full ownership of the activity and its final product. Accordingly, any public mention of the activity, including through social media, should clearly state such ownership. In addition, any public appearance related to the activity should be coordinated with and approved by UNDP.

UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely, thorough, and transparent manner. UNDP will also be responsible for providing the necessary clarifications and facilitating the work.

The consultant shall rely on his/her own means of communication and shall commute between the place of residence and the duty station at his/her own expense.

DURATION OF WORK

The assigned duration of this consultancy is six months, with 15 working days per month.

The assignment is expected to commence immediately and must be completed no later than 30 March 2027.

The time required to review, comment on, and approve deliverables and outputs is five working days.

DUTY STATION

The assignment is based at the Personal Status Department at the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities in Beirut, with occasional meetings at UNDP offices, if required.

STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Education

· A High-School degree is required
· At least 2 years of relevant experience in working with the Personal status Department

Language: Fluency in Arabic and English.

“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.

opportunities.title: Partnership Development Advisor
opportunities.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
opportunities.description:
Manchester, UK

Starting salary for this position is £41,628 per annum (plus contributory pension)

About MAG:

MAG (Mines Advisory Group) is an international humanitarian organisation based in Manchester, UK, and working in 32 countries. We remove landmines and unexploded ordnance to release safe and productive land for communities, and work to reduce the threat of armed violence by supporting governments to safely manage weapons and ammunition. In 1997, MAG was a co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize for our work campaigning for the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention.

Build partnerships that expand humanitarian impact:

MAG is seeking a Partnerships Development Advisor to help grow our reach, influence and funding through innovative partnerships that connect Humanitarian Mine Action and Armed Violence Reduction with wider humanitarian, development and peacebuilding efforts. You will work with our country programme teams to identify and develop strategic collaborations with organisations whose expertise complements MAG's work, creating new opportunities for impact and sustainable growth. You will support teams across the organisation to scope opportunities, engage potential partners, design joint interventions and develop high-quality collaborative proposals.

Working closely with the Contracts Director and Partner Delivery & Assurance Advisor, you will help shape MAG's strategic approach to partnership development and ensure opportunities are translated into effective and impactful programmes. Success in this role will be measured through the growth of high-value partnerships, increased joint programming and proposal development, access to new funding opportunities and stronger engagement beyond the Humanitarian Mine Action and Armed Violence Reduction sectors. If you are a relationship builder with a strategic mindset and a passion for creating partnerships that deliver meaningful change, we would love to hear from you.

Please note that as part of MAG's commitment to safeguarding, this post is subject to background checks before an offer of employment is confirmed. For more information on MAG’s approach to safeguarding and background checks on our website**.**

MAG is committed to the principles of diversity, equality and inclusion. If you think you would be suited to one of our roles we would welcome your application regardless of your background. We strive to provide an inclusive and supportive working environment where all employees feel respected and supported in fulfilling their potential.

About you:

You will be a partnership development expert, with a strong understanding of key trends in humanitarianism and development and the practical implementation of project delivery within these contexts. You should be a strong communicator, able to collaborate with and influence stakeholders across a range of functions and build strong working relationships both internally and externally. You should be positive and solution-focused, with experience developing practical guidance, tools and resources to support partnership development across programmes. You will be highly self-motivated, able to work autonomously and take initiative, with significant experience of developing tenders, bids and proposals. Ultimately you should be interested in and committed to MAG’s humanitarian mandate and able to represent our work and key issues with authority in order to effectively advance our mission, vision, and values. Fluency in English is essential, and fluency in a relevant second language would be advantageous.

We’re looking for someone with:

  • Proven experience of strategic partnership identification and development.
  • Proven experience of developing practical guidance, tools and resources to support partnership development across programmes.
  • Proven experience of managing programme/project activity implemented with local or international partners across humanitarian, development, and/or peacebuilding sectors.
  • Experience of developing tenders, bids and proposals.

Benefits and Further Information:

  • Salary: £41,628 per annum and this increases with service.
  • Pension: MAG has a salary sacrifice group personal pension plan in place, and matches employee’s contributions up to 5%.
  • Leave: We recognise our staff work hard and need the appropriate time out to stay motivated. Annual Leave starts at five weeks each year and increases with service to six weeks. We also offer paid sick leave, and the amount of the entitlement increases with service. Once you’ve been with MAG for two years, you’re entitled to 13 weeks. MAG also has policies on compassionate leave, flexible working and family leave, including maternity, paternity, adoption and surrogacy leave.

opportunities.description:
• Place: Tawila/Nyala - Sudan
  • Starting date: 15th September 2026;
  • Duration of contract: 5 months;
  • Closing date for applications: 16th August 2026.

Humanity & Inclusion presentation

Humanity & Inclusion is an independent and impartial aid organisation working in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. The organisation works alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations, taking action and bearing witness in order to respond to their essential needs, improve their living conditions and promote respect for their dignity and fundamental rights.

Since its creation in 1982, HI has run development & humanitarian projects in more than 55 countries and responded to numerous emergencies. Today, we have a budget of approximately 200 million euros, with 4,000 employees worldwide

At Handicap International-Humanity & Inclusion, we truly believe in the importance of inclusion and diversity within our organisation. This is why we are engaged to a disability policy to encourage the inclusion and integration of people with disabilities.

Please indicate if you require any special accommodation, even at the first interview. For more information about the organisation.

JOB CONTEXT:

Since April 2023, Sudan has been facing an unprecedented humanitarian crisis, fueled by the conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). Armed conflict, attacks on civilians, population displacements, malnutrition, epidemics and climate shocks have left 30.4 million people, or nearly two-thirds of Sudan's population (+23% compared to 2024), including 16 million children, in urgent need of humanitarian assistance (OCHA, HRP 2025). The conflict has displaced more than 12 million people, making it the largest displacement crisis in the world. The situation is particularly dire for people living in areas of active conflict, including Darfur, one of the most affected regions in Sudan, where nearly 80% of the population (meaning 30.4 million people1) is in need of humanitarian assistance (OCHA, HRP 2025).

Since January 2024, HI has been responding to Sudan’s crisis. HI’s joint multisectorial response in Gedaref State, implemented with a Sudanese partner NGO, is already providing physical and functional rehabilitation services in healthcare centers and at community level, as well as MHPSS services, including individual and group counselling. HI is further engaged at the humanitarian coordination level to mainstream disability inclusion throughout the humanitarian response.

HI is scaling up its response from both geographic and modalities/sectorial perspectives. In particular, HI has deployed emergency response teams in Darfur, to setup its operations and initiate its response in the western parts of Sudan, since December 2024. Activities are implemented in Darfur since January 2025 in Basic needs (Wash and FSL), and assessment in other sectors are being conducted. The advertised vacancy is to be part of that team.

Atlas Logistique (AL) is an operational unit of HI, which has been supporting humanitarian actors since 1993. Atlas Logistique facilitates, optimizes and accelerates the delivery of aid in emergency situations and chronic crisis contexts. Our mission is to open up humanitarian space to the most hard-to-reach populations and to optimize humanitarian supply chains. AL’s operations focus around four key sectors: shared transport and storage platforms, medical logistics, logistics capacity building and light civil access engineering, both in the preparation and response phases of emergencies. These all contribute to HI-AL's position as a key player in humanitarian access.

After a phase of initial diagnosis to understand the logistical needs of the humanitarian community in Darfur, AL is launching operations in Darfur focusing on storage, transportation and capacity building activities.

YOUR MISSION:

Reporting to the Operations Manager, the “AL Project Manager” supports the Atlas Logistique teams on the operational planning, implementation and monitoring of HI/AL’s operational strategy. This position englobes the storage and transportation components of the project as well as Capacity Building. To do so, the Atlas Logistique PM supports his/her team to ensure optimal quality, effectiveness and impact of the implemented project and to contribute to the sound management and effective functioning of the organization in Darfur.

In this framework, the main missions are:

Mission 1: Operational implementation

  1. Ensures project implementation, in collaboration with the relevant departments and in line with general standards and procedures:
  • Ensures the planning of activities and establishes action plans;
  • Ensures Budget forecast and follow-up;
  • Ensures that activities are implemented in line with the project reference documents and the allocated budget;
  • Manages expenditures and ensures a follow up of budget lines for his/her activities;
  • Ensures that activities are implemented according to internal quality and technical standards and, if necessary, proposes adjustment or improvements to help meet objectives;
  • Follows procedures to develop new partnerships with user organizations ;
  • Ensures the effective implementation and follow up of institutional policies (PSEAH, mandatory cross-cutting approaches, etc.) on his/her project;
  • Coordinates and collaborates with relevant internal services, especially logistics, HR, finance and technical departments;
    1. Ensures project data management:
  • Ensures that the appropriate data collection and management tools are in place on the project, in line with applicable standards;
  • Ensures that data related to the project is collected and compiled in the project database;
  • Carries out regular verifications and makes any necessary corrections in the activity database.
    1. Ensures project reporting:
  • Monitors the achievement of results and indicators, as per the logical framework;
  • Is in charge of producing the appropriate reporting tools ;
  • Reports regularly to the line manager;
  • Contributes to writing reports for the funding agencies when relevant;
  • Guarantees the proper archiving of information and documentation regarding the project.

Mission 2. Expertise: Logistics services to humanitarian actors

  1. Ensures that the project is implemented in compliance with technical and operational frameworks as well as local/international regulations regarding provision of storage and transport services to other humanitarian stakeholders and smooth running of operations:

  • Ensures that the activities implemented comply with HI/AL and external applicable technical norms and standards;

  • Monitors and improves storage tools and processes (database, SoPs,…) , and ensures their effectiveness in close coordination with his/her superiors and relevant other departments of HI/AL;

  • Ensures project’s staff benefit from technical training upon needs, and that technical briefings/capacity-building of partner organization staffs upon needs in order to smoothen interactions with HI/AL and ensure optimal provision of services;

  • Ensures the quality and relevance of project activities implemented, in particular the quality of services provided to partner organizations;

  • Ensures technical learning from projects by drawing on lessons learned and good practices;

  • Makes sure HQ and Field technical specialists/resources get the information they require and collaborates with other HI/AL technical departments when necessary;

  • Adjusts the project activities’ implementation to technical monitoring or audit recommendations, if applicable.

    1. Fosters and maintains smooth relationships with partner organizations and other relevant stakeholders involved in the project.

Mission 3. Management

Manager as a role model: embody HI's values daily and be a role model and contribute to the development of his or her staff.

  • Line-manages the Atlas Logistique Team (sets individual objectives, assesses individual performance, contributes towards the professional & career development of his/her team members, monitors competences);
    • Organizes and leads regular team meetings;
    • Manages the recruitment and selection of new team members/open positions;
    • Ensures strict application and respect of the program’s Internal Regulations by the project team.

Mission 4. Influence & Communication:

  • Represents HI/AL in relevant coordination bodies, contributes to HI’s external influence by participating in relevant networks ;
  • Communicates on evolutions of the project to partners and external stakeholders as much as relevant.

Mission 5. Strategy & business development:

  • Provides inputs to contribute to the design of the program’s overall operational strategy
  • Contributes to the design of project proposals for the continuity or expansion of the project, or for the development of new projects upon request.

YOUR PROFILE:

  • You have minimum 3 years of experience in project management
  • You have experience in volatile contexts security-wise
  • You have experience in logistics programming in an NGO
  • You have proven project management skills, including admin, budget, reporting, team management

opportunities.title: Consultant: Guidelines for Religious Counsellors on Rehabilitation and Reintegration of Individuals Exposed to Violent Extremism
opportunities.description:
Terms of Reference (TOR): Consultant

Development of Community Based Guidelines on Rehabilitation, Reintegration, and Empowerment of Individuals Exposed to Violent Extremism for Religious Counsellors.

Overview

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) is a dynamic, international non-governmental organisation. NP works with people affected by violence to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP). NP works to reduce and prevent violence, protect civilians in countries affected by violent conflict and its aftermath, and help transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

Background

Indonesia continues to strengthen a comprehensive approach to preventing and countering violent extremism conducive to terrorism. Beyond security measures and law enforcement, these efforts require sustainable rehabilitation and social reintegration for individuals who have previously been exposed to violent extremist ideologies.

In practice, however, the reintegration process continues to face several challenges, including limited inter-agency coordination, the absence of well-established community-based support mechanisms, and the need to strengthen the capacity of local actors involved in facilitating successful reintegration.

The Government of Indonesia reaffirmed its commitment through Presidential Regulation No. 8 of 2026 on the National Action Plan for Preventing and Countering Violent Extremism Conducive to Terrorism (RAN PE) 2026–2029, which emphasizes a whole of government and multi-stakeholder approach to prevention efforts. Within this framework, the Ministry of Religious Affairs plays a strategic role through the promotion of religious moderation, religious counselling services, and strengthened social cohesion, in line with Presidential Regulation No. 58 of 2023 on Strengthening Religious Moderation.

Through the RECONNECT (Reintegration through Religious and Community Counsellor Empowerment & Trust-Building) Programme, Nurani Perdamaian Indonesia (NPID), in collaboration with the Ministry of Religious Affairs and cross-sector strategic partners, seeks to strengthen the role of Religious Counsellors and community actors in supporting safe, inclusive, and sustainable rehabilitation and social reintegration. The programme includes capacity building for Religious Counsellors, the development of practical guidance for community-based assistance, and the strengthening of reintegration risk monitoring mechanisms integrated within the Ministry of Religious Affairs' system.

The Policy Dialogue and Stakeholder Dialogue conducted in June 2026 identified several critical gaps, including:

  • the absence of operational guidelines and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for Religious Counsellors supporting former terrorism offenders;
  • the lack of a strong institutional mandate within the Ministry of Religious Affairs to formally assign such responsibilities;
  • insufficient capacity of Religious Counsellors on issues related to violent extremism, deradicalisation, needs assessment, and community-based case support;
  • rehabilitation approaches that remain largely security-oriented and need to be expanded to address social, psychological, economic, family, and community dimensions; and
  • the absence of an integrated and sustainable economic empowerment model for former
    terrorism offenders.

As a follow-up to the recommendations generated through these dialogue processes, it is necessary to develop a comprehensive Guideline on the Rehabilitation, Reintegration, and Empowerment of Former Terrorism Offenders, which will serve as the primary technical reference for Religious Counsellors and relevant stakeholders in implementing community-based reintegration support.

To achieve this, NPID, through the RECONNECT Programme, seeks to engage an experienced Preventing and Countering Violent Extremism (PCVE) Consultant o develop the guideline using a comprehensive, participatory, and evidence-based approach.

Objective

To develop a practical and context-specific Guideline on the Rehabilitation, Reintegration, and Empowerment of Former Terrorism Offenders that will serve as a reference for Religious Counsellors and relevant stakeholders in supporting inclusive, sustainable, community based, and cross sectoral rehabilitation and social reintegration processes, in line with RANPE 2026–2029 and Presidential Regulation No. 58 of 2023 on Strengthening Religious Moderation.

Scope of Work

The Consultant will be responsible for:

  • Conducting a desk review of relevant policies, regulations, guidelines, and good practices related to the rehabilitation, reintegration, and empowerment of former terrorism offenders, including RAN PE 2026–2029 and Presidential Regulation No. 58 of 2023.
  • Mapping the roles, institutional mandates, and capacities of Religious Counsellors in supporting the rehabilitation and social reintegration of Individuals Exposed to Violent Extremism, including identifying institutional strengthening needs.
  • Develop a practical guideline (Do's and Don'ts) for Religious Counsellors (Penyuluh Agama) that provides operational guidance on community based rehabilitation and social reintegration of Individuals Exposed to Violent Extremism including roles and responsibilities community engagement approaches cross sector coordination, and referral mechanisms with relevant government agencies (zakat institutions and Islamic philanthropic organisations) to support holistic reintegration, including economic empowerment.
  • Finalising the guideline based on feedback relevant to the RECONNECT Programme team.

Duration

The assignment will last 30 working days.

  • Week 1 — Initial consultation with the RECONNECT team, collection of relevant documents, preparation of the Inception Report, desk review of policies, regulations, existing guidelines, and findings from the Policy Dialogue and Stakeholder Dialogue. Deliverables: Inception Report and Desk Review Summary
  • Week 2 — Consolidation and analysis of evidence, stakeholder inputs, and reference materials, identification of key thematic areas, institutional gaps, and operational needs for Religious Counsellors. Deliverable: Evidence and Analysis Summary
  • Week 3 — Development of the first draft of the Guideline, including roles and responsibilities, Do's and Don'ts, referral pathways, community engagement approaches, and cross-sector coordination mechanisms. Deliverable: First Draft of the Guideline
  • Week 4 — Presentation of the draft to the RECONNECT team and the Ministry of Religious Affairs; incorporation of comments and revisions, finalisation and submission of the Guideline.
    Deliverables: Meeting Report, Revised Draft, and Final Guideline

Consultant Criteria

  • A minimum of a Master's degree with at least five (5) years of relevant professional experience, or a Bachelor's degree with at least seven (7) years of relevant experience in Preventing and Countering Violent Extremism (PCVE).
  • Demonstrated experience in developing technical guidelines, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), or case management frameworks, preferably related to the rehabilitation and reintegration of former terrorism offenders or deradicalisation programmes.
  • Strong understanding of the institutional context of the Ministry of Religious Affairs, the role of Religious Counsellors, and issues related to religious moderation and social cohesion will be considered an advantage.
  • Experienced in collaborating with ministries and government institutions.
  • Excellent communication and report writing skills in Bahasa Indonesia.
  • Demonstrated ability to complete assignments within agreed timelines.
  • Individual consultants may apply independently or as part of a consulting team.

Application Requirements

  • Updated Curriculum Vitae (CV);
  • Cover Letter explaining how the applicant meets the required qualifications;
  • A brief Technical Proposal (maximum three pages) outlining the proposed methodology and the preliminary structure (outline) of the guideline;
  • For team applications, the proposal should clearly specify the names, roles, and expertise of each team member;
  • Samples of previously developed technical guidelines, SOPs, or case management frameworks.

Selection Process

  • Administrative screening based on the completeness and relevance of the submitted application documents;
  • Interviews (if required) to assess the consultant's methodological approach and readiness to undertake the assignment;
  • Shortlisted candidates may be invited to present their technical proposals;
  • The final selection will be based on the overall technical quality, relevant experience, and demonstrated suitability for this Terms of Reference.

Honorarium and Payment Terms

  • The Consultant will receive a lump sum professional fee of IDR 23,000,000 (Twenty Three Million Indonesian Rupiah), inclusive of all applicable costs, including taxes, transportation, communication, logistics, and other related expenses.
  • Payments will be made based on the completion of agreed milestone deliverables.

SPECIAL NOTICE

Nonviolent Peaceforce is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against based on disability.

Nonviolent Peaceforce acknowledges the duty of care to safeguard and promote the welfare of employees, contractors, volunteers, interns, communities we work with, and other stakeholders and is committed to ensuring safeguarding practice reflects statutory responsibilities and government guidance and complies with best practices in the Humanitarian and Development sector. NP expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We prioritise ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. NP also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

NO FEE

We never ask for payment as part of our selection process, and we always contact candidates via our corporate accounts and platforms. If you are approached for payment, this is likely to be fraudulent. Please check whether the role you are interested in is posted here on our website.

opportunities.title: Health Advisor - Roving
opportunities.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
opportunities.description:
Hours: You will be required to work the hours as are necessary for the proper discharge of the duties with the notional requirement being 35 hours per working week. Work will normally be undertaken in office hours, Monday to Friday, but weekend and evening working will be required

Remuneration: Up to £42,440 GBP gross per annual (dependent on experience)

Duration: 12 months, with the possibility of extension subject to funding

Location: Manchester, UK (hybrid working available), with an expectation of up to 80% international travel/deployment as required by UK-Med. (Open to candidates based in the UK or internationally, with a preference for UK-based candidates due to operational considerations.)

We are seeking a Medical Doctor with expertise and experience in international humanitarian responses, conflict and/or disasters to provide expert technical leadership across UK-Med’s growing portfolio of emergency health programmes.

UK-Med is a frontline humanitarian medical NGO, delivering life-saving healthcare in emergencies and strengthening health systems in some of the world’s most challenging environments. As a key partner of the UK Emergency Medical Team (UK EMT), we work closely with the UK Government, WHO, Ministries of Health and international partners to respond rapidly when crises strike.

This is a unique opportunity for a highly experienced humanitarian clinician who is passionate about emergency response and willing to deploy internationally in support of UK-Med’s operations. Our teams have responded to some of the world's most complex humanitarian crises, including conflicts, disease outbreaks, natural disasters and public health emergencies. Current and recent programmes have included conflict responses in Ukraine, Gaza and Sudan, as well as support to Ebola preparedness and response activities in DRC, and disaster responses in countries including Venezuela.

The successful candidate will play a key role in shaping humanitarian health programmes, providing technical expertise, supporting programme design and strategy, contributing to funding proposals and deploying overseas to provide leadership to multidisciplinary health teams when required.

You will bring significant experience in emergency and humanitarian health, strong technical credibility and the ability to work effectively with health authorities, WHO and international partners in complex and fast-moving environments. Join us and be part of a passionate, purpose-driven organisation making a real difference where healthcare is needed most.

We offer a competitive salary and benefits package, a supportive and collaborative working environment, and the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to humanitarian health outcomes worldwide. UK-Med is a dynamic and ambitious organisation with a dedicated team of staff, volunteers and Register members committed to delivering high-quality healthcare where it is needed most.

opportunities.description:
Starting Date / Initial Contract Details

September 2026, 24 months maximum

Role Summary

The Finance Project Manager (FPM) oversees the financial management of the country programme, ensuring accuracy, compliance, and strong stewardship of resources. The FPM supports decision-making by providing timely financial insights and ensures donor and organisational requirements are met. The role reports to the Programme Development Coordinator (PDC), who is part of the Country Senior Leadership Team, ensuring close alignment between financial management and programme strategy.

Project Overview

The Lebanon programme works across the country, including in the Bekaa Valley and Beirut Mount Lebanon. Medair supports both Syrian refugees and Lebanese communities with projects in Health, Mental Health, Shelter, Basic Assistance and GIS Mapping.

Workplace & Conditions

Field based position in Beirut, Lebanon. Take a look at Medair’s work in Lebanon.

Responsibilities:

  • Manage finance and accounting functions for the country programme, ensuring appropriate transaction processing, financial liquidity, budget adherence, transparent processes, and compliance with Medair and donor guidelines. Understand programme needs and ensure timely support to facilitate achievement of programme objectives
  • Support budget holders in preparation and development of budgets, spend forecasting and ongoing grant monitoring. Provide training to staff on Finance systems and processes.
  • Ensure financial activities and processes are implemented in line with Medair, donor, country, and international regulations and procedures. Review, develop and implement systems to improve transparency. Ensure adequate anti-fraud procedures are in place to detect and prevent loss or fraud. Carry-out regular inspections and spot-checks to ensure appropriate use of resources.
  • Line-manage designated team members; ensure effective communication, performance management, capacity building, and a supportive, transparent and inclusive work environment. Support the team to work together effectively, modelling Medair’s values. Provide matrix management to field finance staff.
  • Ensure compliance with host government tax requirements, submitting any related required reporting. Prepare for, manage and support internal and external field financial audits, providing all information.

Qualifications, Experience & Technical Competencies:

  • University degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration or a related field
  • Professional certification in accounting or finance (e.g. ACCA, CPA, CIMA or equivalent)
  • Proficient in English (spoken and written); Arabic desirable
  • Relevant professional experience in financial management, including budgeting, reporting and accounting

Behavioural Skills

  • Strong servant leadership skills with a consultative management style
  • Creative, open-minded, flexible, self-learner, with good understanding of cross-cultural issues
  • Capacity to work under pressure and manage personal stress levels, self-motivated, proactive
  • Able to oversee multiple tasks, prioritizing, delegating, and seeking advice as required
  • Attention to detail and clear communication that establishes clarity to leadership and the wider team on budgets, procedures, and other matters.

Team Spiritual Life

Reflect the values of Medair with team members, local staff, people we serve, and external contacts. Work, live, and pray together in our Christian faith-based teams. Fully contribute to a rich spiritual team life, including team devotion, prayer, and words of encouragement.

Before you apply

Please ensure you are fully aware of the:

  1. Medair organisational values.
  2. Medair is committed to safeguarding the protection of beneficiaries, volunteers, staff and partners, and particularly children. Therefore, we do not employ staff whose background we understand to be unsuitable for working with children. Medair staff are required to give the utmost respect to, and comply with,Medair’s accountability policies and best practices.
  3. Medair Relief & Recovery Orientation Course (ROC) (which forms part of the recruitment selection process for field positions).
