Consultants' Expertise

The Consultants should demonstrate strong experience in feminist research, baseline studies, context and needs analysis, MEAL, GBV and TFGBV, digital safety, survivor-centred approaches, qualitative and quantitative data collection, and working with feminist CSOs, WROs and movement actors across African contexts. A working knowledge of the specific country they are applying for is a requirement.

Required Qualifications

  • A minimum of a Master’s degree in social sciences, gender studies, development studies, monitoring and evaluation, public policy, human rights, digital rights, research methods or another relevant field.
  • At least five years of demonstrated experience conducting baseline studies, context analyses, evaluations, feminist research or applied research in development, human rights, gender justice or digital rights contexts.
  • Strong technical knowledge of gender-based violence, technology-facilitated gender-based violence, digital safety, survivor-centred approaches and feminist ethical research principles.
  • Proven experience using qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis methods, including key informant interviews, focus group discussions, surveys, desk reviews and indicator-based baseline measurement.
  • Demonstrated experience working with feminist CSOs, women’s rights organisations, movement actors, community-based organisations or human rights defenders in African contexts.
  • Excellent analytical, writing and reporting skills, with the ability to produce clear, evidence-based and consolidation-ready reports in English or French, depending on the assigned country context.
  • Strong knowledge of the assigned country’s legal, policy, social and digital rights context, including actors and referral systems relevant to TFGBV prevention and response.
  • Ability to work independently, meet tight deadlines and coordinate effectively with UAF-Africa and consortium partners.

opportunities.title: Rewards and Organization Development Specialist
opportunities.description:
MSF Eastern Africa is looking for a Rewards and Organization Development Specialist

Do your skills and experience not precisely match the requirements? At MSF EA, we strive to create a safe, diverse and inclusive workplace, recognizing the need to increase access to professional opportunities for historically underrepresented groups. If you're interested in this position but your experience doesn't align perfectly with the selection criteria, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the ideal candidate for this or other positions.

Firmly committed to safeguarding patients, community members, staff, and all those in contact with the organization from all forms of abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), we will take all necessary steps, through rigorous vetting processes, to ensure that confirmed perpetrators of abuse do not join the organization.

For this position, contact level with patients and children is categorized as Low Risk and will be monitored with this in regard.

Introduction

Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) is an international independent medical humanitarian organisation that provides assistance to people affected by conflicts, epidemics, and natural or human-made disasters and excluded from healthcare. We provide this assistance without discrimination, irrespective of race, religion, creed or political affiliation.

About MSF Eastern Africa

MSF Eastern Africa is the regional institutional office of MSF. It focuses on representation and networking, recruiting and supporting staff from the region, communications and fundraising, as well as working on other dossiers of importance to MSF such as Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI), Data Protection, mutualization, training, medical operational support and environmental health.

Rationale/Objective for Position

The Rewards and Organization Development Specialist is responsible for developing and executing MSF EA and Ubuntu job evaluation, rewards, organization design, workforce planning, workforce analytics, competency, performance management, and related organization effectiveness strategies, frameworks and initiatives that contribute to equitable, sustainable and effective total rewards, organizational structures and capacities.

This position will be hierarchically and functionally accountable to the Rewards and Organization Development Manager.

Tasks & Responsibilities

Rewards & Organization Development Strategy

  • Implement, monitor, and contribute to the periodic review of rewards & organization development strategies, ensuring alignment with the organization's strategic plan, P&C strategy, workforce priorities, and operational objectives.

Rewards Governance, Compliance & Policy

  • Develop, implement and promote the consistent application of reward policies, procedures, governance frameworks, and operational guidelines.
  • Monitor and ensure reward policies and practices comply with applicable employment legislation, taxation requirements, donor obligations, internal policies, and MSF governance standards.
  • Maintain accurate, confidential, and auditable reward records, documentation, and governance files.
  • Review and update reward policies, procedures, templates, and guidance materials to reflect organizational and legislative changes.
  • Represent MSF EA and Ubuntu in MSF regional and global platforms on rewards, contributing to the development of global policies, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement of reward practices.

Job Design & Evaluation

  • Conduct job analysis and role profiling to ensure roles are accurately documented and aligned with organizational requirements.
  • Develop, review, and maintain job descriptions, job profiles, and role documentation across the organization.
  • Conduct job evaluation exercises using approved methodologies and facilitate evaluation panels where required. Ensure consistent application of job evaluation principles and governance across the organization.
  • Prepare job evaluation documentation, grading recommendations, and evaluation reports. Maintain job evaluation records, grading structures, and job architecture documentation.

Market Benchmarking, Compensation & Pay Structures

  • Design, implement and periodically review compensation structures, salary scales and remuneration frameworks.
  • Conduct benchmarking analyses comparing the organization's compensation practices and pay positioning with relevant humanitarian, NGO, and regional labour markets.
  • Participate in salary surveys by collecting, validating, analyzing, and submitting organizational reward data.
  • Analyze salary structures, grading distributions, remuneration trends, workforce costs, and internal pay equity.
  • Carry out annual salary review processes, salary adjustments, and remuneration initiatives in accordance with market data, organizational affordability, and internal equity.
  • Maintain compensation databases, salary structures, grading records, and remuneration documentation to ensure accuracy and integrity.

Organization Design

  • Develop and implement the organization’s design frameworks, methodologies, principles and governance.
  • Conduct organization-wide reviews, diagnostics, benchmarking and continuous improvement of organizational structures, layers, spans of control, reporting relationships, governance arrangements, and operating models that support organizational strategy and operational effectiveness.
  • Maintain organization charts, documentation and repositories.

Workforce Planning

  • Develop and implement the organization's workforce planning frameworks and methodologies, to ensure workforce capacity and composition aligns with current and future organizational needs.
  • Conduct workforce planning analyses and modelling to inform unit capacity and planning decisions.
  • Develop workforce planning dashboards, forecasts, scenarios and recommendations informed by unit plans and workforce analytics.
  • Maintain workforce planning data and documentation.

Workforce Analytics & Reporting

  • Collect, validate, analyze, and interpret organizational, workforce, reward, and employee data from multiple sources.
  • Carry out rewards and organization development related employee engagement surveys, pulse surveys, listening sessions, focus groups, and other employee feedback mechanisms. Analyze employee data to identify organizational trends, strengths, and improvement opportunities.
  • Develop dashboards, scorecards, diagnostics that support evidence-based organizational and reward decision-making.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness of reward and organization development indicators and initiatives using qualitative and quantitative methodologies.
  • Prepare regular reports on workforce metrics, remuneration trends, grading outcomes, employee experience, and other rewards and organization development metrics.

Organization Effectiveness, Transformation & Change/Project Management

  • Execute rewards and organization development transformation projects/ initiatives across the organization, that strengthen organizational effectiveness, capacity, and agility.
  • Prepare and maintain project plans, stakeholder engagement plans, communication materials, implementation guides, and governance documentations.
  • Conduct change readiness assessments and identify organizational risks and mitigation strategies.
  • Monitor implementation progress, employee adoption, project milestones, risks, issues, and dependencies throughout organizational change initiatives.
  • Conduct post-implementation reviews and document lessons learned to inform continuous improvement.
  • Conduct research on emerging trends, innovations, and best practices in rewards and organization development, and prepare recommendations.

Development of Competency Framework

  • Design, develop, and periodically review the organization's competency framework, ensuring competencies support organizational strategy, leadership expectations, culture, and MSF values.
  • Define core leadership, managerial, technical, and functional competencies across all job families.
  • Conduct competency mapping for new and existing roles and update job descriptions.
  • Maintain the organization's competency framework and libraries’ documentation and associated reference materials.

Development of Performance Management Framework

  • Design, develop, and periodically review the organization's performance management framework, ensuring alignment with MSF's strategic objectives, values, and people strategy.
  • Develop the performance management philosophy, principles, components, policies, and governance mechanisms that promote consistency, fairness, accountability, and employee development.
  • Maintain performance management policies, guidelines, templates, standards, and supporting documentation.

Other Responsibilities

  • Integrate EDI & Safeguarding aspects in area of work responsibility, including policies and practices.
  • Recognize, respond, and document any form of abuse or inappropriate behavior and alert the safeguarding unit of any suspected potential abuse.
  • Proactively participate in the individual performance management process including objective setting, performance monitoring and performance evaluation.

Qualifications

Education

  • A Bachelor’s degree in Human Resource Management, Business Studies, Psychology, Humanities, Organization Development or an equivalent qualification from a recognized institution.
  • Knowledge of MS Office Tools (PPT, Excel).
  • Fluency in English is required, and knowledge of French and a third language is an added advantage.

Experience

  • At least three (3) years’ experience working in a P&C role, with significant experience specifically on rewards and compensation management, organization design, workforce planning, workforce analytics, organization development, change management, competency and performance management.
  • Experience working with Hay and other grading methodology/tools is an advantage.
  • Experience executing complex cross-functional projects and organizational transformation initiatives.
  • Previous experience with MSF or other humanitarian NGOs is an added advantage.

Competencies

  • Technical Competencies
    • Excellent organizational skills with demonstrated ability to execute projects on time.
    • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with ability translating complex data into actionable recommendations.
    • Ability to interact effectively at all levels in a complex international organization through excellent communication, negotiation, and conflict management skills.
    • Strong facilitation and presentation skills.
  • Behavioral/General Competencies
    • Ability to work independently and with minimal supervision.
    • Ability to work across diverse cultural, regulatory, and operational contexts.
    • Commitment to delivering high-quality work and achieving measurable outcomes.
    • Flexible, resilient, and able to adapt to fast-changing environments.
    • Commitment to MSF’s Principles.
    • Ethics: High ethical standards and a commitment to protecting the data of individuals and furthering MSF mandate.

Conditions and Benefits:

  • Job Location: MSF Eastern Africa office in Nairobi (Kenya).
  • Contract: 5-Months, full-time contract/ etc.
  • Start date: ASAP.
  • Salary: An annual salary of EUR 23,296 at HQ Grade 7 based on a full-time appointment with an annual increment of 2% every year up to a maximum of 10 years.
  • Work-life balance financial benefit; ranging between EUR 247 to 295/month based on individual & administrative status. This amount may be used to cover accommodation and utilities, transportation, etc.
  • Other benefits include; 25 days of annual leave, Employer Pension contribution and medical insurance cover (staff and family) based on MSF EA terms/conditions.

opportunities.title: Humanitarian Affairs Officer / Programme Officer, P3
opportunities.publisher: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
opportunities.description:
Job Opening ID: 281968
Job Network : Political, Peace and Humanitarian
Job Family : Humanitarian Affairs
Category and Level : Professional and Higher Categories, P-3
Recruitment Type : Temporary Opportunities
Duty Station : BANGUI
Department/Office : Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
Date Posted : Jul 31, 2026
Deadline : Aug 14, 2026

Org. Setting and Reporting

This position is located in the Crisis Response Division (CRD), Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). OCHA is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA also ensures there is a framework within which each actor can contribute to the overall response efforts. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate for the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention; and facilitate sustainable solutions. This temporary job opening is being advertised for the position of Humanitarian Affairs Officer / Programme Officer (P-3), based in Bangui, Central African Republic (CAR). Under the overall supervision of the Head of Office (HoO), OCHA CAR, and the direct supervision of the Head of the Humanitarian Financing Unit/Fund Manager, the incumbent supports the management and oversight of the Central African Humanitarian Fund (CAR HF) and contributes to the effective delivery of humanitarian financing in support of humanitarian priorities in the country.

Responsibilities

Within delegated authority, the Humanitarian Affairs Officer / Programme Officer will be responsible for the following duties: • Fund Management and Coordination: - Under the supervision of Pooled Fund Manager, support and advise the HoO on the overall management of the Country-Based Pooled Fund (CBPF) and Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) vis-à-vis the humanitarian context (i.e., priorities and critical needs). - Ensure the overall administration of the Fund and liaise as necessary with relevant OCHA HQ sections as instructed by the Pooled Fund Manager. - Support and implement standardized policy in line with HQ guidance and decisions. - Manage and supervise Fund-related monitoring officers. - Manage fund allocation processes ensuring necessary coordination with relevant counterparts in line with the Terms of Reference and/or allocation guidelines (i.e., Review and/or Advisory Boards, cluster or sector leads, humanitarian organizations, and OCHA). - Liaise with NGOs, UN partners as well as clusters and OCHA field offices to follow-up on project progress and overall Fund progress. - Conduct periodic field visits to promote the knowledge and support the appropriate use of the Fund in line with its Terms of Reference, field visits should focus on key actors (i.e. OCHA field colleagues, recipient organizations, local governments, communities). - Ensure proper communication and support during the allocation process to all stakeholders. - Liaise with and provide necessary support to recipient organizations of the Fund throughout the life-cycle of the projects, promoting coherence between humanitarian needs and response. - Advise the Pooled Fund Manager on measures to mitigate foreseeable operational risks. - Ensure recipient organizations compliance with financial rules applicable to the Fund. - Ensure coordination and information exchange with humanitarian partners aiming to promote coordinated and complementary use of funds. • Monitoring, Reporting and Evaluation: - Ensure compliance with monitoring and reporting requirements in place for the Fund. - Systematically provide information on project status to the Pooled Fund Manager. - Ensure timely overall project reporting, including acting as the lead for the pooled fund annual report exercise. - Assist in the preparation of evaluations or other research activities and studies in consultation with relevant HQ sections. • Analysis, communications and public information: - Research, analyze and present humanitarian financing information, in particular funding trends and requirements, gathered from diverse sources. - Assist in policy development, including the review and analysis of humanitarian issues and funding trends at the country level, ensuring proper coordination with relevant HQ sections. - In collaboration with other OCHA units and field offices, as well as with support from relevant OCHA HQ sections, document and disseminate results, best practices and results of the Fund across internal and broader audiences through information and communication products/pieces (i.e., bulletins, feature stories, photographs/videos, websites, etc.). - Liaise with OCHA field offices and recipient organizations in order to disseminate full information on Fund activities. - Perform other duties as assigned by the Pooled Fund Manager.

Competencies

PROFESSIONALISM : Knowledge and understanding of humanitarian assistance, emergency relief and related humanitarian issues, including humanitarian financing and Country-Based Pooled Fund management. Ability to identify issues, analyze and participate in the resolution of issues and problems. Ability to conduct independent research and analysis and apply sound judgment in the context of assigned responsibilities. Ability to evaluate information from a variety of sources and assess its impact on humanitarian programming and funding decisions. Ability to work under pressure, including in highly stressful environments associated with humanitarian emergencies. Demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. COMMUNICATION : Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify and promotes two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match the audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. PLANNING AND ORGANIZING : Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amounts of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently.

Education

An advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in political science, social science, international studies, public administration, economics, development studies, business administration, engineering, earth sciences or a related field is required. A first-level university degree in combination with two (2) additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Work Experience

A minimum of (5) five years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian affairs, emergency preparedness, crisis/emergency relief management, rehabilitation, development, or other related area is required. Experience in programme or project management, monitoring and evaluation, grants management, or humanitarian coordination is required. Experience in humanitarian financing, including grant management, fund allocations, project monitoring, donor reporting or pooled fund management is desirable. Experience working with a Country-Based Pooled Fund (CBPF) or a comparable multi-donor humanitarian financing mechanism is desirable. Experience within the UN Common System or other international organization is desirable. Experience supporting capacity strengthening of national and local humanitarian organizations is desirable. Experience in the West and Central Africa region is desirable.

Languages

English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English and French are required. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult https://languages.un.org for details).

Assessment

The evaluation of qualified candidates may include an assessment exercise which may be followed by a competency-based interview.

Special Notice

This position is temporarily available until 31 December 2026. If the selected candidate is a staff member from the United Nations Secretariat, the selection will be administered as a temporary assignment. The selected candidate may be required to travel within the Central African Republic in support of monitoring, coordination, capacity-building and other programme-related activities. While this temporary assignment may provide the successful applicant with an opportunity to gain new work experience, the selection for this position is for a limited period and has no bearing on the future incumbency of the post. Subject to the funding source of the position, the eligibility for this temporary job opening may be limited to candidates based at the duty station. This temporary job opening may be limited to “internal candidates,” who have been recruited through a competitive examination administered according to staff rule 4.16 or staff selection process including the review of a central review body established according to staff rule 4.15. Staff members of the United Nations common system organizations who will reach the mandatory age of separation or retirement within the duration of the current temporary need period are not eligible to apply. Submitting an application or selection for the current temporary job opening does not delay or increase the mandatory age of separation. Retirees above the mandatory age of separation who wish to be considered for the current temporary job opening must indicate the reason for their last separation as "retirement." Such retirees shall not be employed by the Organization, unless (a) the operational requirements of the Organization cannot be met by staff members who are qualified and available to perform the required functions; and (b) the proposed employment would not adversely affect the career development or redeployment opportunities of other staff members and represents both a cost-effective and operationally sound solution to meet the needs of the service. Pursuant to section 7.11 of ST/AI/2012/2/Rev.1, candidates recruited through the young professionals programme who have not served for a minimum of two years in the position of their initial assignment are not eligible to apply to this position.

United Nations Considerations

According to article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. Candidates will not be considered for employment with the United Nations if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. The term “sexual exploitation” means any actual or attempted abuse of a position of vulnerability, differential power, or trust, for sexual purposes, including, but not limited to, profiting monetarily, socially or politically from the sexual exploitation of another. The term “sexual abuse” means the actual or threatened physical intrusion of a sexual nature, whether by force or under unequal or coercive conditions. The term “sexual harassment” means any unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature that might reasonably be expected or be perceived to cause offence or humiliation, when such conduct interferes with work, is made a condition of employment or creates an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment, and when the gravity of the conduct warrants the termination of the perpetrator’s working relationship. Candidates who have committed crimes other than minor traffic offences may not be considered for employment. Due regard will be paid to the importance of recruiting the staff on as wide a geographical basis as possible. The United Nations places no restrictions on the eligibility of men and women to participate in any capacity and under conditions of equality in its principal and subsidiary organs. The United Nations Secretariat is a non-smoking environment. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. By accepting a letter of appointment, staff members are subject to the authority of the Secretary-General, who may assign them to any of the activities or offices of the United Nations in accordance with staff regulation 1.2 (c). Further, staff members in the Professional and higher category up to and including the D-2 level and the Field Service category are normally required to move periodically to discharge functions in different duty stations under conditions established in ST/AI/2023/3 on Mobility, as may be amended or revised. This condition of service applies to all position specific job openings and does not apply to temporary positions. Applicants are urged to carefully follow all instructions available in the online recruitment platform, inspira, and to refer to the Applicant Guide by clicking on “Manuals” in the “Help” tile of the inspira account-holder homepage. The evaluation of applicants will be conducted on the basis of the information submitted in the application according to the evaluation criteria of the job opening and the applicable internal legislations of the United Nations including the Charter of the United Nations, resolutions of the General Assembly, the Staff Regulations and Rules, administrative issuances and guidelines. Applicants must provide complete and accurate information pertaining to their personal profile and qualifications according to the instructions provided in inspira to be considered for the current job opening. No amendment, addition, deletion, revision or modification shall be made to applications that have been submitted. Candidates under serious consideration for selection will be subject to reference checks to verify the information provided in the application. All external candidates recruited in accordance with section ‎2.2 (a) of ST/AI/2025/3 for a fixed term appointment without limitation and all external candidates recruited in accordance with section 2.2. (c) of ST/AI/2025/3 for a fixed term appointment limited to the entity are subject to an initial probationary period of one year under a fixed-term appointment. Job openings advertised on the Careers Portal will be removed at 11:59 p.m. (New York time) on the deadline date.

No Fee

THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING). THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CONCERN ITSELF WITH INFORMATION ON APPLICANTS’ BANK ACCOUNTS.

opportunities.title: Travel and Contracting Officer_Kigali
opportunities.description:
MSF Eastern Africa is looking for a Travel and Contracting Officer

Do your skills and experience not precisely match the requirements? At MSF EA, we strive to create a safe, diverse and inclusive workplace, recognizing the need to increase access to professional opportunities for historically underrepresented groups. If you're interested in this position but your experience doesn't align perfectly with the selection criteria, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the ideal candidate for this or other positions.

Firmly committed to safeguarding patients, community members, staff, and all those in contact with the organization from all forms of abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), we will take all necessary steps, through rigorous vetting processes, to ensure that confirmed perpetrators of abuse do not join the organization.

For this position, contact level with patients and children is categorized as Low Risk and will be monitored with this in regard.

Introduction

Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) is an international independent medical humanitarian organisation that provides assistance to people affected by conflicts, epidemics, and natural or human-made disasters and excluded from healthcare. We provide this assistance without discrimination, irrespective of race, religion, creed or political affiliation.

About MSF Eastern Africa

MSF Eastern Africa is the regional institutional office of MSF. It focuses on representation and networking, recruiting and supporting staff from the region, communications and fundraising, as well as working on other dossiers of importance to MSF such as Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI), Data Protection, mutualization, training, medical operational support and environmental health.

Rationale/Objective for Position

The Travel and Contracting Officer is responsible for coordinating the MSF EA office and intersection cross administration and travel tasks and ensuring effective and efficient administrative services for all areas related to staff travel, transit management and NCR contracting at the Eastern Africa Office.

This position will be hierarchically and functionally accountable to the Travel and Mobile Staff Deployment Team Leader.

Tasks & Responsibilities

Administrative processes & support

  • Collaborate with the Travel and Mobile Staff Deployment Team Leader to initiate and draft a travel and movement policy and ensure implementation on the same.
  • Act as the reference point for all movement and travel -related issues for Eastern Africa Office.
  • Act as the focal point for staff regarding non-Kenyan staff administration.
  • Maintain proactive, effective communication, and good collaborations with the Regional Protocol office (RPO).
  • Ensure accurate and updated information for deployment through the EAS travel tool, or local external service providers. Link with the MSF Sections and OC travel focal points for specific travel requirements.
  • Initiate the processing and follow up of Work Permit/Passes/Cards for all Non- Kenyan employees based in EA office.
  • Provide administrative support for any medical interventions in Nairobi and the region with the support of the Staff Health Officer and other colleagues involved.
  • Respond to teams regarding potential incidences, validity of travel fares, and business trips.
  • Review of local accommodation and hotel requirements with the support of the Finance/facilities to ensure specification of administrative needs is considered.
  • Ensure clear communication regarding administrative requirements for travel (visas,) and together with Staff Health officer, vaccines and checkup.
  • Coordinate preparation of administrative documents for work permits and follow up with the protocol/regional representative’s office.
  • Give support in organizations of training and events including providing administrative papers such as introductory letters from employers required by any Embassy.
  • Act as support for visas and administrative procedures for employees traveling to the programs.
  • Create a network with embassies (as and when) that we mostly deal with and establish an updated contact list for the same.
  • Support the proximity management initiatives by providing punctual information on Kenyan/other staff movements to facilitate meetings/briefings and follow up in collaboration with the career management.
  • Assist in the organization of team events, meetings, and activities.
  • Support Talent Management team in communication, administrative requirements for travel and movement (vaccination/health checks/briefings/other) and contact with program staff contracted and managed by the office.
  • Provide input during review/update of People Services policies & procedures and disseminate relevant information to all staff where needed.
  • Prepare handover documents and reports for follow up during absence.
  • Ensure administrative work plans are updated and followed regularly with the supervisor.
  • Support in the management of critical incidents as/when required

Management and Organization of Deployment Movements for all staff based at the EA Office

  • Coordinate flight bookings and hotels for staff.
  • Provide support and information regarding visas to the respective employees.
  • Prepare and send travel documents.
  • Coordinate proper filing of non-Kenyan documents for / work permit/passes/cards.
  • Maintain and manage accurate data and information relate to all movements/ travels.
  • Authorize travel expenses such as per diem forms for EA staff and visitors and flights.

Contract Management

  • Provide on point briefing and debriefing of mobile staff to mobile staff and managers on contracting procedures, documentation requirements, timelines, and administrative processes.
  • Support onboarding and offboarding activities by coordinating travel, documentation, accommodation, and other administrative arrangements for mobile staff.
  • Liaise with People and Culture, Finance and Services, operational centers, and partner sections to facilitate timely processing, approval, and implementation of contracts.
  • Maintain up-to-date contract records, trackers, and monitoring tools, and proactively follow up on contract expiries and pending actions.
  • Coordinate end-to-end administration of NCR mobile staff contracts and decentralized offices, including preparation, amendments, renewals, extensions, and closure of contracts.
  • Legal documentation handling including work permits, social security registration, and NIE acquisition for international staff.

Other Responsibilities

  • Integrate EDI & Safeguarding aspects in area of work responsibility, including policies and practices.
  • Recognize, respond, and document any form of abuse or inappropriate behavior and alert the safeguarding unit of any suspected potential abuse.
  • Proactively participate in the individual performance management process including objective setting, performance monitoring and performance evaluation.
  • Recognize and reinforce strong performance in supervisees; identify and encourage improvement where needed; and ensure quality and timely performance management process is carried out for supervisees.

Qualifications

Education

  • A Bachelor’s degree in Human Resource, Administration, Tourism, or an equivalent qualification from a recognized institution.
  • Knowledge of MS Office Tools (PPT, Excel).
  • Fluency in English is required, and knowledge of French and a third language is an added advantage.

Experience

  • At least two (2) years' experience in a similar job, preferable in the non-profit making sector.
  • Experience in the touristic sector (travel agency, airline, coordination of events, visas and work permit management).
  • Previous experience with MSF or other humanitarian NGOs is an added advantage.

Competencies

  • Technical Competencies
    • Excellent IT Skills
    • Web/internet navigation skills.
  • Behavioral/General Competencies
    • Commitment to MSF’s Principles
    • Cross-cultural Awareness
    • Strategic Vision
    • Results and Quality Orientation
    • Service Orientation
    • Planning and Organizing
    • Initiative and Innovation
    • High level of flexibility.
    • Strong communication skills.
    • Ethics: High ethical standards and a commitment to protecting the data of individuals and furthering MSF mandate

Languages

  • Working proficiency in English and French is mandatory

Conditions and Benefits:

  • Job Location: Kigali (Rwanda)
  • Contract: Open-ended, Full-time, contract.
  • Start date: ASAP.
  • Salary: An annual salary of EUR 18,476 at HQ Grade 6 based on a full-time appointment with an annual increment of 2% every year up to a maximum of 10 years.
  • Work-life balance financial benefit; ranging between EUR 247 to 295/month based on individual & administrative status. This amount may be used to cover accommodation and utilities, transportation, etc.
  • Other benefits include; 25 days of annual leave, Employer Pension contribution and medical insurance cover (staff and family) based on MSF EA terms/conditions.

opportunities.title: Licensed AI Trainer – Design and deliver a tailored AI training program for the National Trade Help Desk team
opportunities.description:
Position Information

  • VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/125
  • Position Title: Licensed AI Trainer – Design and deliver a tailored AI training program for the National Trade Help Desk team
  • Duty Station: Chamber of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture of Beirut and Mount Lebanon in Beirut
  • Duration: 2 months (without exceeding 13 working days per month)
  • Vacancy Date of Issue: 29 July 2026
  • Vacancy Closure Date: 05 August 2026
  • National or International consultancy: National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow the below link:

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1WFlDKy33_DdDyq5MnGKq5bwb5yKhrVEO/view

BACKGROUND

The Women’s Economic Empowerment (WEE) Through Advancing Women-Led Enterprises in Lebanon is a new project funded by the Government of Canada for a period of 3.5 years. The project aims at supporting gender-responsive job creation and helping generate economic opportunities for women-led micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) across various productive sectors with high growth potential. Through this objective, the project will foster the economic security, stability and prosperity of women entrepreneurs and women-led MSMEs in Lebanon.

The project includes three main components:

Component 1: Ensuring that government institutions are more responsive to women’s needs through processes that are more conducive to doing business.

Component 2: Ensuring that women-led MSMEs have access to the financial resources needed to grow and remain sustainable.

Component 3: Ensuring that women-led MSMEs receive the necessary technical support to increase their access to local and international markets.

The project was developed in response to the multiple crises that have affected Lebanon, particularly the financial crisis, which has hindered the ability of MSMEs in general, and women-led MSMEs in particular, to access the financing needed to grow. With the collapse of the banking system and the resulting depletion of all sources of financing, access to finance is considered one of the biggest impediments preventing MSMEs, particularly women-led MSMEs, from developing and taking their businesses to the next level.

This has compounded the existing barriers faced by women entrepreneurs, including stringent collateral requirements, high interest rates, complex documentation processes, sub-optimal financial literacy and the absence of market information.

In light of the current situation and the ongoing conflict, and based on consultations held with WEE project beneficiaries, it became clear that MSMEs, particularly women-led and women-owned MSMEs, require more targeted, timely and practical support to:

  • Access market information;
  • Understand export requirements;
  • Identify opportunities; and
  • Navigate the increasingly complex trade environment.

Many MSMEs continue to face challenges related to limited access to accurate information, changing regulations, weak market intelligence and limited capacity to assess export readiness and comply with market requirements.

To respond to these needs, the project will strengthen the capacity of the National Trade Help Desk (NTHD) team through dedicated Artificial Intelligence (AI) training sessions. These sessions will equip the NTHD team with practical tools and methods to use AI more effectively in:

  • Trade intelligence;
  • Market research;
  • Regulatory and compliance checks;
  • HS code classification; and
  • The preparation of clear advisory outputs for MSMEs.

The training will also support the team in improving the quality, speed and consistency of the services provided through the Help Desk.

By building these capacities, the NTHD will be better positioned to provide MSMEs with more responsive, reliable and tailored support, helping them identify new market opportunities, understand export procedures and make more informed business decisions.

This will directly contribute to the WEE project’s objective of improving access to technical support and strengthening the competitiveness and market access of women-led enterprises in Lebanon.

This Terms of Reference (TOR) outlines the scope of work, qualifications and expected deliverables for the AI Trainer, who will be responsible for:

  • Designing the training content;
  • Developing the supporting tools and materials; and
  • Delivering the AI training sessions for the National Trade Help Desk team.

The Trainer will ensure that the sessions are practical, context-specific and tailored to the day-to-day functions of the NTHD, with a focus on strengthening the team’s capacity to use AI tools responsibly and effectively in trade intelligence, market research, regulatory and compliance research, HS code classification and MSME advisory services.

SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK

UNDP is seeking the services of a licensed AI Trainer to design and deliver a tailored Training of Trainers (ToT) programme for the National Trade Help Desk team, consisting of 16 members.

The training will aim to strengthen the team’s capacity to understand, use and transfer practical AI applications that can support:

  • Trade intelligence;
  • Market research;
  • Regulatory and compliance research;
  • HS code classification; and
  • MSME advisory services.

Under this consultancy, the Consultant will be requested to deliver four training sessions covering key AI concepts, practical tools, applied use cases and responsible AI practices relevant to the work of the National Trade Help Desk.

The training should be practical, hands-on and adapted to the day-to-day functions of Help Desk officers, enabling participants to use AI tools more effectively while ensuring accuracy, verification, data protection and accountability.

Training Modules

The modules should cover the following areas:

Introduction to Artificial Intelligence

Understanding what AI is, what it is not, its key limitations and the main types of AI failure modes that users should be aware of when applying AI tools in professional settings.

Using AI as a Main Assistant for NTHD Tasks

Practical use of AI models to support the daily work of the National Trade Help Desk, including research, drafting, analysis, summarization, content preparation and responding to MSME inquiries.

Overview of AI Tools and Platforms

Introduction to different AI tools, platforms and applications relevant to trade support services, including guidance on which tools are most appropriate for specific Help Desk tasks.

Creating an AI-Powered Workspace

Guidance on how to create and organize a dedicated AI-powered workspace to support NTHD operations, workflows, knowledge management and internal coordination.

Supporting MSMEs Through AI-Assisted Services

Practical approaches for using AI to support MSMEs with market information, export readiness, regulatory guidance, product classification and the preparation of clear advisory outputs.

Prompt Engineering Fundamentals

Application of structured prompt-engineering techniques to improve the quality, accuracy, relevance and consistency of AI-generated outputs, with a focus on trade-related tasks.

Creating AI Assistants

Development of prototype AI assistants tailored to selected NTHD workflows, such as:

  • Responding to inquiries;
  • Preparing export briefs;
  • Supporting HS code classification; and
  • Producing MSME guidance notes.

Verifying and Fact-Checking AI-Generated Information

Application of a repeatable verification process to review AI-generated outputs, validate information against reliable sources and support findings with primary-source references.

Use of Trade-Specific AI Tools

Practical use of AI-supported trade tools and resources to prepare verified export briefs, market snapshots, regulatory summaries and other trade-related outputs.

HS Code Classification with AI

Use of AI tools to support the classification of Lebanese products while cross-checking results against verified customs, tariff and product-classification databases.

Market Intelligence and Trade Data Analysis

Development of repeatable workflows for producing sourced, structured and verifiable market-intelligence briefs, including information on:

  • Demand trends;
  • Competitors;
  • Import requirements; and
  • Potential opportunities.

Trade Regulations and Compliance Research

Use of AI to support research on export requirements, technical regulations, standards, documentation, labelling, certification and compliance procedures, with clear references to official sources.

Communicating Findings Clearly to MSMEs

Converting technical trade, market and regulatory information into concise, practical and MSME-friendly outputs, such as:

  • One-page briefs;
  • Checklists;
  • Frequently asked questions; and
  • Guidance notes.

In addition, the training should include modules on:

  • Data privacy;
  • AI governance;
  • AI ethics; and
  • Facilitation techniques.

These modules should enable trainers to deliver the basic concepts effectively and support MSMEs in applying AI tools responsibly and practically.

Evaluation and Expected Outcomes

The Consultant will be required to design a pre- and post-training assessment to measure participants’ knowledge, skills and confidence before and after the four-session AI training programme.

The Consultant should analyse the results and provide a short assessment report showing the level of improvement achieved by participants, including:

  • Clear before-and-after results;
  • Key observations; and
  • Recommendations for further capacity strengthening.

Upon completion of the training programme, participants should be able to:

  • Assist Lebanese MSMEs with trade and export-related requests and inquiries more efficiently and with greater confidence.
  • Use ChatGPT as their main AI assistant for daily National Trade Help Desk tasks, building on the team’s existing familiarity with the tool.
  • Apply a repeatable verification protocol to ensure that AI-supported outputs are accurate, reliable and supported by primary-source citations.
  • Conduct HS code classification, market-intelligence research and trade-regulation lookups using ChatGPT in combination with ITC trade tools and other reliable sources.
  • Translate technical export findings into clear, practical and MSME-ready one-page briefs in Arabic and English.
  • Build and use personal AI assistants tailored to their own Help Desk workflows.
  • Apply data privacy, security, AI governance and ethics principles to all AI-supported Help Desk activities.
  • Train and coach junior staff within their respective entities using the same tools, methods and materials, enabling them to act confidently as internal trainers.

The Consultant will also be responsible for preparing and sharing all training materials with the NTHD team, including:

  • Presentations;
  • Handouts;
  • Practical exercises;
  • Templates;
  • Checklists;
  • Sample prompts;
  • Verification guides; and
  • Any other tools needed to support the team’s continued use of AI after the training.

EXPECTED DELIVERABLES

The Consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities, noting that the total duration should not exceed two months, without exceeding 13 working days per month.

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

  • The work is expected to start upon contract signature.
  • The Consultant will work under the overall guidance of the UNDP WEE Project Manager, in close coordination with the UNDP team.
  • The Consultant will rely on his or her own means of communication and transportation.
  • Transportation and communication fees for the Consultant should be included in the financial offer.
  • The title rights, copyrights and all other rights of whatsoever nature in any material produced under the provisions of this TOR will be vested exclusively in UNDP.
  • UNDP has full ownership of the activity and its final product. Therefore, any public mention, including through social media, about the activity should clearly state that ownership.
  • Any public appearance related to the activity should be coordinated with and approved by UNDP.
  • In the event of any delay, the Consultant will inform UNDP promptly so that decisions and remedial action may be taken accordingly.
  • Delays that affect the flow of collaborative work and the delivery of outputs on schedule may lead to termination of the contract.
  • Should UNDP deem it necessary, it reserves the right to commission additional inputs, reviews or revisions as needed to ensure the quality and relevance of the work.

DURATION OF WORK

The assigned duration for this consultancy is two months, without exceeding 13 working days per month.

The mission is expected to commence on 1 August 2026 and be completed by 1 October 2026.

The time required to review, comment on and approve deliverables and outputs is five working days.

DUTY STATION

The four sessions will be delivered at the Chamber of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture of Beirut and Mount Lebanon in Beirut.

STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Education

  • Master’s degree in business administration, Management, Economics, International Trade, Digital Transformation, Artificial Intelligence, or any other relevant field, with a recognized certification as an AI Trainer
  • At least 10 years of relevant professional experience, including demonstrated experience in AI integration for business operations, export promotion, trade support services, MSME advisory, or related areas.

Language: Fluency in Arabic and English ( written and spoken)

“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.
