opportunities.title: Technical Support: Climate-Smart Agriculture and Conservation Agriculture-Based Sustainable Intensification (CSA/CASI)
opportunities.description:
1. Overview

The Development Fund (DF) works to combat hunger and poverty, guided by its vision of a sustainable and just world. DF supports and strengthens small-holder farmers facing the growing challenges of climate change, including extreme weather and increasingly difficult farming conditions. Each year, DF reaches approximately half a million people across Africa, Asia, and Central America.

The CRRC programme strengthens climate resilience and improved food security across 38 kebeles in Tigray, Amhara, and Oromia. It supports CSA/CASI; biodiversity; post-harvest and livestock management; economic empowerment; community-led land and water management; energy-efficient technologies; and producer-led value chain development and inclusive government service delivery. It builds on lessons learnt from the Climate Adaptation and Rural Development Phase II (CARD II) Programme and the Scaling Conservation Agriculture-Based Sustainable Intensification (SCASI) Project. The programme is implemented through civil society organisations (CSOs) in close collaboration with government authorities.

2. Assignment Overview and Objective

  • Applications are sought from organisations legally registered to work in Ethiopia
  • The Assignment will begin on 1st September 2026 or as soon after as possible
  • The Assignment will be completed no later than 31 December 2028
  • The budget for the assignment will not exceed Norwegian Kroner nine-hundred and fifty-one thousand, seven-hundred and sixty (NOK 951,760)
  • The assignment will be conducted, in its entirety, in Ethiopia

The objective of the assignment is to enhance the implementation effectiveness of the CRRC programme and in-turn ensure long-term sustainability of programme impacts, through tailored technical support interventions that address identified knowledge and skills gaps in Climate-Smart Agriculture and Conservation Agriculture-Based Sustainable Intensification (CSA/CASI).

Such technical support will be provided to CRRC programme partner staff, strengthening their capacity to effectively implement, monitor, and scale CSA/CASI technologies and practices across diverse agroecological contexts.

These interventions and approaches proposed by the applying organisation are expected to enhance the technical competencies of implementing partners, strengthen cross-learning and collaboration, and contribute to the successful delivery and sustainability of the CRRC Programme.

3. Applicants’ Required Qualifications, Knowledge and Experience

  • Be a globally leading research and science-based organisation focused on developing climate resilient crop varieties and agricultural practices including CASI and CSA.
  • Have extensive experience working with key Ethiopian crops including but not limited to teff and wheat.
  • Have more than ten years of experience supporting agricultural development in Ethiopia
  • Be familiar with Norwegian government support for agriculture and civil society through Norad.
  • Have strong familiarity with the Norad funded CARD and SCASI programmes in Ethiopia
  • Be experienced in providing direct technical support to local organisations working in CASI/CSA in Ethiopia.

4. Reporting and Supervision

The technical support organisation will report to DF and work closely with CRRC partners.

opportunities.title: Regional Development Manager - PIROPS (H/F/X)
opportunities.description:
Building on its unique expertise in supporting Red Cross and Red Crescent National Societies in small island states around the world, the International Operations Department (DOI) of the French Red Cross reopened the Preparedness and Response Platform for the Pacific (PIROPS) at the end of 2024, with its office based in New Caledonia.

PIROPS implements a broad range of humanitarian programmes across the Pacific, including a large-scale disaster preparedness programme in Fiji and Vanuatu (the 3 Oceans Project, funded by the Agence Française de Développement - AFD). It also provides rapid emergency response support at the request of Pacific Red Cross National Societies and develops disaster risk reduction initiatives throughout the region.

PIROPS is recognised as a strategic humanitarian actor in the Pacific region by national and local authorities, as well as by the components of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. It works closely with the Territorial Delegation of the French Red Cross in New Caledonia (DTNC).

Since its reopening, PIROPS has benefited from funding from AFD, CDCS (Center of Crisis of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs), as well as private partners. As it enters a new phase of development, PIROPS seeks to build on the experience gained over the past two years to strengthen its regional positioning, mobilise new funding opportunities and implement its long-term strategy in support of Pacific National Societies.

Poste

Main Duties and Responsibilities

Reporting to the Head of Delegation, the Regional Development Manager is responsible for strengthening PIROPS' strategic positioning across the Pacific region. The position focuses on developing partnerships, identifying funding opportunities, structuring PIROPS' programme portfolio and leading resource mobilisation efforts in line with the organisation's international priorities and the strategy of national societies.

Partnership development
- Strengthen PIROPS' understanding of the priorities, challenges and strategies of key regional stakeholders, particularly members of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement.
- Actively position PIROPS as a key actor within regional technical networks.
- Foster coordination and collaboration with Movement partners and other humanitarian actors.
- Maintain and further develop strong, strategic and effective partnerships with existing institutional and operational partners.

Strategic development
- Identify needs and opportunities to support the development of PIROPS projects and translate them into strategic orientations and development plans.
- Prepare positioning papers, presentations, concept notes, project proposals and other strategic documents.
- Develop standard project concepts that respond to regional priorities.
- Design and development of programmes that respond to the priorities of Pacific National Societies, in close coordination with the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement.
- Ensure all proposals are aligned with PIROPS' strategic priorities and those of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement.

Resource Mobilisation
- Monitor donor trends and identify relevant funding opportunities.
- Develop and maintain a mapping of institutional donors and funding partners.
- Design and implement donor engagement strategies.
- Lead the preparation and submission of funding applications and project proposals.

Representation and visibility
- Strengthen PIROPS' visibility and positioning among humanitarian, institutional and regional stakeholders.
- Identify opportunities to promote PIROPS during regional events, conferences and technical forums.
- Represent PIROPS in relevant regional meetings, conferences, forums, working groups and events.

Reporting Line
- Reports directly to the Head of Delegation (N+1).
- The Regional Development Manager has no direct management responsibilities.

Functional Relationships
- PIROPS programme teams.
- Technical advisors and the Partnership Department at French Red Cross headquarters.
- Regional partners, donors and other key stakeholders.

Date de prise de poste souhaitée

September 2026

Expériences / Formation: Required Skills and Knowledge

  • Significant experience in the humanitarian and/or international development sector.
  • Excellent interpersonal and networking skills.
  • Full professional proficiency in English (working knowledge of French would be considered as an asset).
  • Strong knowledge of donors and funding mechanisms.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills.
  • Strong analytical, strategic thinking and synthesis skills.
  • Excellent command of IT tools (office software).
  • Good knowledge of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement.
  • Good understanding of the Pacific regional context, including key humanitarian challenges and stakeholders.
  • Strong representation and advocacy skills, with the ability to confidently engage in high-level meetings, workshops and public events.

Informations pratiques liées au poste

The position is based in Suva, Fiji, with frequent travel throughout the Pacific region.

opportunities.title: Field Security Officer
opportunities.description:
Overview of position

OVERVIEW OF POSITION

The Field Security Officer (FSO) provides practical, field-based security support to enable safe and sustained programme delivery in Libya.

Operating in a fragmented and fluid environment, the role requires the ability to interpret evolving conditions, assess risk in context, and translate this into clear, actionable guidance for operational teams.

The FSO supports country teams through risk analysis, movement advisory, incident response, and engagement with relevant security counterparts, while ensuring alignment with CTG’s global risk approach. The role is embedded within operations and contributes directly to planning and delivery, rather than functioning as an administrative or compliance layer.

The FSO contributes to CTG’s Duty of Care by strengthening staff awareness, supporting disciplined incident management, and helping ensure that security considerations are applied in a way that is proportionate, practical, and operationally relevant.

Role objectives

Risk Analysis & Context Monitoring

  • Monitor and interpret the evolving security environment in Libya, including political, armed actor, and community-level dynamics, and other factors shaping access and operational risk
  • Identify emerging patterns, behavioral indicators, and shifts in risk posture
  • Produce concise, decision-oriented updates highlighting what is changing and the operational implications

Operational Support & Movement Advisory

  • Advise on staff and consultant movements, including routes, timings, posture, and contingency measures
  • Support operational teams in adapting plans based on real-time conditions
  • Ensure movement guidance reflects actual field dynamics and constraints

Briefings & Awareness

  • Deliver clear, context-specific security briefings and inductions
  • Promote situational awareness and practical risk ownership among staff
  • Tailor messaging to reflect behavioural patterns and sensitivities in the operating environment

Incident Management & Escalation

  • Support immediate response to security incidents, including information gathering and coordination
  • Ensure disciplined escalation and clear communication during incidents
  • Contribute to After Action Reviews, focusing on root causes, operational impact, and lessons learned

Stakeholder Engagement & Security Interfaces

  • Maintain working-level relationships with relevant security counterparts, including client security structures (e.g. IOM), UNDSS, and other coordination platforms as required
  • Support coordination with client security teams during movements, incidents, and operational planning
  • Provide insight into how formal and informal dynamics may affect access, posture, and delivery
  • Ensure engagement remains practical, focused on enabling operations, and aligned with CTG’s role and responsibilities

Security Planning & Documentation

  • Support the development and maintenance of practical security procedures, annexes, and guidance aligned with CTG standards
  • Ensure documentation reflects operational realities and is usable by field teams
  • Contribute to simplifying processes where they create unnecessary operational friction

Capacity Support & Continuous Improvement

  • Provide ongoing support and coaching to staff on security awareness and practical application
  • Identify recurring issues, gaps, or inefficiencies and propose improvements
  • Contribute to strengthening how security is applied operationally, not just documented

Project reporting

The role reports operationally to the Regional Operations Manager and has a functional/technical reporting line to the Global Risk Director.

Key competencies

- Strong contextual judgement and situational awareness.

- Ability to build trust with diverse stakeholders in sensitive environments.

- Demonstrated experience drafting and operationalising security procedures and SOPs in complex environments.

- Ability to support and structure security responses during incidents, including first-hour actions and coordination.

- Strong judgement in dynamic environments, with the ability to translate risk analysis into practical guidance.

Team management

This role does not have team management responsibilities

Further information

Travel Requirements: This role requires occasional travel to field locations, including remote or challenging environments. The role will as well require flexibilityto work irregular hours and provide support in emergency situations, including weekends and holidays.

CV Submission: Please note that CV's and application should be submitted in English language.

Female candidates are encouraged to apply

opportunities.title: Regional Communications and Visibility Officer
opportunities.description:
Background:
The International Rescue Committee responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, IRC offers life-saving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in more than 40 countries and in 22 U.S. cities, IRC restores safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted by conflict or disaster. IRC leads the way from harm to home.

Program Background:

The IRC's MENA Early Childhood Development (ECD) portfolio builds on over seven years of programming, starting with the Ahlan Simsim and Play to Learn initiatives, launched in 2018. These initiatives reached millions of children and caregivers with ECD services, generated a library of high-quality ECD content, and established a resource bank of proven program models. Partnerships with Ministries of Education, Health, and Social Development produced co-designed programs that are now embedded within government services across the region.

The portfolio today spans multiple grants and donors across the MENA region, with an overarching aim of supporting the youngest children and their caregivers — particularly those affected by crisis and conflict — with high-quality, scalable, and sustainable interventions. Interventions target children directly and through their caregivers and communities. The portfolio also strengthens the capacity of the ECD workforce — including teachers, multi-sector facilitators, and health workers — advances national systems and policy through advocacy efforts, and delivers innovative digital technology solutions. The IRC works alongside key public and private stakeholders across health, protection, education, and economic recovery and development to co-design and expand partner-led interventions. For more information on the IRC's ECD work in the region, visit: https://www.rescue.org/ahlansimsim.

The MENA regional ECD team manages core regional grants, supports country programs on country-specific awards, and actively contributes to business development efforts to expand programming reach, deepen impact, and mobilize resources from a growing base of public and private donors. The team also supports country programs in program quality and fidelity, content development, research and monitoring, policy, advocacy and communications, project and financial management, and digital technology solutions.

Position Summary:

Reporting to the Regional Policy, Advocacy and Communications Lead, the Communications & Visibility Officer will support the implementation of the regional ECD portfolio communications and visibility activities across the MENA region. The role will contribute to storytelling, content collection, visibility materials, event coverage, communications products, and coordination with country, regional, and global communications colleagues. The Communications & Visibility Officer will serve as a central coordination point for communications and visibility efforts across the MENA ECD portfolio country programs, ensuring the timely collection, development, management, and dissemination of high-quality content that showcases program impact, learning, and achievements, in close coordination with country program communication leads.

The Communications & Visibility Officer will play a key role in ensuring high-quality documentation of program activities, capturing impact stories from children, caregivers and communities, maintaining communications assets, and supporting the production of donor-facing and public-facing communications materials.

Specific Responsibilities:
The Communications and Visibility Officer will support the planning, coordination, and implementation of communications and visibility activities across the regional ECD portfolio. The role will work closely with country teams, regional colleagues, partners, and external service providers to strengthen storytelling, visibility, content management, and communications products that showcase program impact, learning, and achievements.

Content Development and Storytelling

  • Draft and edit blogs, human-interest stories, case studies, newsletters, talking points, press releases, and media materials in English and Arabic.
  • Adapt communications content for digital and social media channels.

Content Collection and Asset Management

  • Coordinate collection of photos, videos, testimonials, and other assets from country teams and partners, including through field visits and event attendance, ensuring timely submission against donor and content calendars.
  • Maintain organized, tagged archives in Brandfolder (the IRC content library) and other content management platforms for reporting, donor engagement, and future use.

Country and Regional Communications Coordination

  • Serve as the primary coordination point between the regional ECD portfolio team and country communications focal points, supporting them in identifying communications opportunities, in close coordination with IRC’s regional Polic, Advocacy and Communications team and relevant global communications team.
  • Facilitate sharing of products and lessons learned across country, regional, and global teams, and identify opportunities to amplify regional ECD portfolio achievements.

Visibility, Branding and Vendor Management

  • Ensure safeguarding, consent, and IRC/donor branding compliance across all communications materials and assets, coordinating sign-off on branded items as needed.
  • Act as day-to-day focal point for communications, photography, videography, and content production vendors, including external consultants and agencies, tracking deliverables, timelines, and quality standards.
  • Support visibility activities across regional and country programs, including event communications packages and on-site visibility support.

Reporting and Administrative Support

  • Maintain communications trackers, content calendars, and visibility monitoring tools, and support donor and project reporting requirements.
  • Provide day-to-day communications support to the Regional Policy, Advocacy and Communications Lead and the wider regional ECD portfolio team.

Supervisory Responsibilities: None.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in communications, Journalism, Media, Marketing, International Development or a related field; previous experience in an NGO in a similar role is a plus.
  • Minimum 4 years of professional experience in communications, media, public relations, storytelling, journalism, or related fields.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Arabic is required required.
  • Strong storytelling and case study writing and editing skills, with the ability to identify strong stories and adapt communication style to different audiences.
  • Experience collecting and developing human-interest stories, interviews and beneficiary testimonials.
  • Experience coordinating communications activities across multiple stakeholders and locations.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • Experience working with photography, videography and content management processes; knowledge of Adobe Creative Suite (Premiere Pro, Illustrator, Photoshop, and InDesign) is highly desirable.
  • Familiarity with, Brandfolder, Box, SharePoint or similar content management systems.
  • Experience in humanitarian, development, education or early childhood development programs is highly desirable.
  • Work-related travel within the MENA region (Jordan, Lebanon, Syria), up to 30%, is expected.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience working with humanitarian, development, education, early childhood development, or donor-funded programs.
  • Experience coordinating communications activities across multiple countries or regional programs is highly desirable.
  • Photography, videography, content editing, or multimedia production experience is an asset.

Reporting Line
The Communications and Visibility Officer reports directly to the Regional Policy, Advocacy and Communications Lead for the regional ECD Portfolio, with a technical reporting line to the regional Content and Digital Specialist, and works closely with the country program teams, regional and global communications colleagues, implementing partners, and external communications service providers.

Duration
12 months, with possibility of extension subject to funding and performance.

Working Environment

  • Standard office work environment
  • Significant travel across MENA required
  • Position is based in Amman, Jordan.

Professional Standards
IRC and IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in the IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti Workplace Harassment, Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.Gender Equality: IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances.

Diversity and Inclusion: at IRC MENA, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work.

IRC is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive, respectful and safe work environment where all persons are treated fairly, with dignity and respect. In keeping with our core values of Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality, IRC strives to maintain a work environment built on mutual respect in which all individuals treat each other professionally, and free of bias, prejudice, and harassment. IRC expressly prohibits and will not tolerate discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or bullying of IRC Persons in any work setting. All IRC staff, wherever they are located, are accountable for creating an environment free of discrimination, harassment, bullying, and retaliation.

opportunities.title: MHPSS Expert - East Africa
opportunities.description:
MiCT is calling for proposals for a freelance Arabic and/or English speaking MHPSS expert or organisation that can provide psychosocial support in the framework of its program “MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices 2026-2027” in East Africa, funded by the German Federal Foreign Office. This is a freelance position running from August 2026 - June 2027.MiCT invites interested and qualified persons to submit proposals by 17.08.2026.

About MiCT:

Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT) is a non-profit organisation delivering expert media services in complex and challenging contexts with passion, precision, and agility.

Through collaborative work with partners, MiCT fosters transparent, inclusive, and fair dialogue supporting resilient societies. Operating across three continents and 15 countries, MiCT facilitates journalist training, media content production, research, monitoring, and supports the financial sustainability of media partners.

About the Project:

Since 2022, the MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices has supported at-risk journalists and media professionals from conflict regions, enabling them to continue their essential work in safety. The programme is part of the Hannah Arendt Initiative and a member of the Journalists in Distress Network. It offers stipends, security and equipment support, (mental) health services, legal aid, relocation, and professional development through regional hubs.

Description of the role:

To support Fellows who face immediate psychological trauma and mental health issues, MiCT is looking for a MHPSS expert to provide individual and group psychosocial support sessions online/offline for media makers in East Africa. Organisations and individuals are welcome to apply.

Application Requirements:

Successful applicants should be able to provide proof of the following:

  • Proven psychosocial counselling qualifications
  • In-depth knowledge of trauma related support preferred
  • Experience analysing and coordinating MHPSS needs
  • Availability to provide group therapy sessions online
  • Experience working with journalists and people in active crisis and conflict regions preferred
  • Counselling available in Arabic and/or English language preferred
  • Working knowledge of English is required.

opportunities.title: Program Support & Development Officer
opportunities.description:
WORK CONTEXT

CESVI is a secular and independent humanitarian organization founded in Bergamo in 1985, operating in over 20 countries around the world to support the most vulnerable populations in achieving their aspirations and sustainable development while respecting human rights. Guided by the ideals of social justice, CESVI works to improve the well-being of people living in poverty or affected by war, natural disasters, and environmental catastrophes.

CESVI global strategy has the objectives of expanding and improving its humanitarian work; strengthening its interventions in the areas of Protection, Production Chains and Income Generation, and Climate Impact Response; and deepening its commitment to people, partners, donors, and society.

To develop and consolidate this strategy, the International Programmes Department is analysing the different funding opportunities offered by institutional, national, and international donors, as well as private entities such as foundations and companies.

Participation in calls for proposals is therefore expanding rapidly, creating a need to strengthen project design activities with dedicated and competent staff.

JOB DESCRIPTION

The collaboration will start in September 2026.

The position is home-based with frequent field missions (at least 50% of the time).

The Program Support & Development Officer (PSDO) will report to CESVI’s Head of International Department. He/She will contribute to the development of new project proposals in CESVI’s countries of operation. He/she will also support the management and supervision of ongoing CESVI projects in strategic operational contexts.

The PSDO manages and coordinates the project design process (with the internal team and relevant partners) and ensures adherence to deadlines and compliance with donor requirements.

The PSDO will also work closely with other units within the International Programs Department during the project design and the implementation phase.

This collaboration will facilitate coordination between the PSDO, the CESVI teams in the field, and the other CESVI units typically involved in project design and supervision.

More specifically, the tasks assigned to the PSDO are:

  • Develop and draft project proposals for major Italian and international donors. In particular, ECHO, INTPA, AICS, and major U.S. and European government agencies, in both development and emergency contexts.
  • Oversee the entire project design process in collaboration with the department team: developing the project concept, defining the logical framework, drafting and revising texts, preparing the budget, establishing the monitoring (and evaluation) plan, and finalizing project documents in accordance with the guidelines provided by donors.
  • Conduct field missions to foreign countries at the request of the International Programmes Department team to carry out the project design process, including need assessments.
  • Prepare the formal documentation to be submitted with the project proposal.
  • The Program Support & Development Officer will actively support, through field missions, the set-up and the supervision of ongoing selected strategic projects, contributing to the achievement of projects’ objectives and indicators. The position will also contribute to the preparation of intermediate and final narrative reports.

Essential Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree with training/specialization in Project Cycle Management (PCM).
  • At least 3 years of prior experience in designing multisectoral international cooperation projects, both for emergency response and development.
  • In-depth knowledge of project proposal writing methodologies (PCM, Logical Framework, Theory of Change) and all phases of project design and project cycle management: identifying and analyzing calls for proposals, conducting context and needs analyses and need assessments, assessing and coordinating (potential) partners during the project development phases; defining the intervention logic; drafting project documents; budget preparation; development of the monitoring plan; ensuring compliance with requirements and submission of the proposal to the donor; ability to produce timely project narrative and financial reports
  • Proven experience in project design for major institutional donors in foreign cooperation—both international and national, and in both emergency and development contexts—such as ECHO, INTPA, AICS, and major U.S. and European government agencies.
  • Excellent command of Italian and English, both written and spoken, with particular expertise in project design terminology. Spanish knowledge is considered a plus
  • Solid skills in developing highly complex project budgets
  • Excellent organizational and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent ability to carry out project design activities
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines
  • Flexibility and independence
  • Proactivity and autonomy
  • Availability to travel abroad for project design assignments
  • Excellent interpersonal and intercultural communication skills, and the ability to work effectively within a team spread across different countries and with colleagues from diverse sociocultural backgrounds
  • Excellent knowledge of the Office suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and of internet browsing and communication tools
  • Proficiency in using the main online communication platforms (Microsoft Teams, Zoom, GMeet, etc.)

Desirable Requirements

  • Previous project design and project management experience in the areas of the environment, entrepreneurial development, job creation in agricultural and non-agricultural supply chains, and the protection of women and children.
  • Knowledge of and experience using the main SMART assessment tools (Google Forms, Kobo, NEAT+) are considered preferred skills, as is proficiency in less common digital platforms and software related to project design.
  • Knowledge of languages other than English and Italian (particularly French and Spanish) will be valued.
  • Previous experience in writing and presenting project proposals to companies and/or grant-making foundations.

SAFEGUARDING

CESVI has a zero-tolerance approach to any harm to, or exploitation of, a child or a vulnerable adult by any of our staff, related persons or partners.

CESVI commitment to being a safe organization begins with the staff recruitment process which includes meticulous checks, such as criminal records checks or check disclosure of previous convictions, to ensure children and vulnerable people are safeguarded and abuse is prevented. Safeguarding checks are part of the selection process performance.

HEALTH SAFEGUARDING

CESVI pays particular attention to safeguarding the health of all the human resources of the Organisation. Therefore, in order to protect its staff, an assessment of their suitability for the position in each mission is carried out before departure. Such assessment is done by the Occupational Doctor of the Organisation.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, therefore early applications are strongly encouraged.

Due to the high volume of applications received, we are unable to respond to all candidates. Only those shortlisted and contacted for an initial interview will be updated on the status of their application.

WE OFFER

  • Contract duration: 6 months, renewable
  • Salary range: € 2.300 - € 2.500 gross per month
  • Insurance coverage

opportunities.title: National Consultant – Sustainable Local Governance and Social Stability Consultant
opportunities.description:
• VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/132
  • Position Title: National Consultant – Sustainable Local Governance and Social Stability Consultant
  • Duty Station: Field-based in Tripoli and the assigned districts, with occasional visits to the UNDP North Office in Tripoli as required.
  • Duration: 30 working days within a four-month period
  • Vacancy Date of Issue: 04 August 2026
  • Vacancy Closure Date: 11 August 2026
  • National or International consultancy: National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1gOrUIKyxgB1XfHPi8mP9nNYcgyAE2PB4/view?usp=drive_link

Background

Lebanon continues to face unprecedented and overlapping crises that have significantly affected social cohesion, public trust, and local governance structures. Tripoli, Lebanon’s second-largest city and one of its most vulnerable urban centers, has been particularly affected by rising socio-economic pressures, weakened municipal capacities, unemployment, and recurring inter- and intra-community tensions. These challenges are compounded by longstanding historical divisions, uneven development, and declining confidence in public institutions.

In response, UNDP, in partnership with UNICEF and IOM, is implementing the “Tripoli Peace Initiative: Safeguarding Stability in Lebanon,” funded by the United Nations Peacebuilding Fund (PBF). The project aims to strengthen social stability in Tripoli by addressing the root causes of tensions through inclusive local development, participatory governance, youth engagement, and community-based peacebuilding processes.

As part of the project, UNDP’s Peacebuilding Project, through its local implementing partner NAHNOO, conducted a comprehensive Conflict Analysis by the end of 2025. The analysis assessed local conflict dynamics, social-cohesion challenges, governance gaps, and emerging drivers of tension in Tripoli. Its purpose was to inform conflict-sensitive programming, strengthen local stability mechanisms, and support inclusive and sustainable community-engagement processes.

Building on the findings, consultations, and stakeholder engagement conducted through the Conflict Analysis, the Municipality of Tripoli recognized the importance of moving towards a practical and sustainable next phase focused on strengthening participatory local governance and institutionalized community-representation mechanisms.

In this context, UNDP seeks to recruit a National Consultant to conduct a participatory and conflict-sensitive assessment and develop a practical governance framework and implementation methodology for establishing neighborhood-based representative structures in Tripoli.

Scope of work, responsibilities and description of the proposed analytical work

The overall objective of the consultancy is to support the Municipality of Tripoli in developing:

  1. A revised, evidence-based classification and division of neighborhoods and localities within Tripoli Municipality, based on social, demographic, geographic, governance, and conflict-sensitivity considerations.
  2. A proposed methodology for establishing representative neighborhood committees through locally endorsed community-election processes.

The proposed neighborhood committees are envisioned as sustainable social-stability and participatory-governance mechanisms formally linked to the municipality. They will support improved coordination between communities, the municipality, donors, and development actors while strengthening legitimacy, representation, accountability, and social cohesion at the neighborhood level.

Under the supervision of the Local Peacebuilding Coordinator in the North and the Peacebuilding Project Manager, the Consultant will undertake the following tasks:

Review and analysis of existing resources and context

  • Conduct a desk review of existing resources related to Tripoli’s governance, urban divisions, social dynamics, local conflict drivers, and participatory mechanisms.
  • Review and analyze the findings of the Conflict Analysis Report.
  • Identify and document the principal criteria and considerations for redefining and classifying neighborhoods and localities in Tripoli.
  • Consider geographic boundaries, demographic characteristics, community identities, social-cohesion dynamics, municipal service coverage, governance arrangements, and conflict-sensitivity factors.

Stakeholder consultations and participatory mapping

  • Conduct consultations with municipal officials, Mokhtars, civil society organizations, youth and women representatives, community representatives, and other local actors.
  • Conduct participatory discussions and mapping exercises to validate existing neighborhood boundaries and identify community-representation structures.
  • Analyze local-governance dynamics and social-cohesion and tension-related considerations relevant to neighborhood classification and committee formation.
  • Submit a summary report documenting the consultations, key findings, and recommendations.

Development of the neighborhood-classification framework

  • Develop an evidence-based and conflict-sensitive framework for classifying and dividing neighborhoods and localities within Tripoli Municipality.
  • Develop proposed classification criteria, supporting rationale, neighborhood profiles, and recommendations for municipal adoption and future updates.
  • Produce a proposed neighborhood-classification map and accompanying methodology.
  • Document the recommended boundaries, classification process, data sources, stakeholder-validation process, and justification for the proposed divisions.

Development of the neighborhood-committee methodology

  • Develop a practical and conflict-sensitive methodology for establishing representative neighborhood committees.
  • Take into consideration the applicable legal and institutional framework governing municipalities and community-representation mechanisms in Lebanon.
  • Propose the committees’ governance structure, composition, community-election process, institutional linkages with the municipality, and implementation arrangements.
  • Develop implementation recommendations and a phased roadmap for operationalization.

Final report and presentation

  • Submit a final consolidated report containing the finalized neighborhood-classification framework and neighborhood-committee methodology.
  • Facilitate a validation workshop or presentation with relevant stakeholders.
  • Incorporate stakeholder and UNDP feedback into the final outputs.

The Consultant is expected to adopt a participatory, conflict-sensitive, and evidence-based methodology combining desk review, stakeholder mapping, Key Informant Interviews, Focus Group Discussions, participatory mapping exercises, governance analysis, and conflict-sensitivity analysis.

The Consultant shall build on the completed Conflict Analysis and avoid duplicating previously conducted assessments.

Expected outputs and deliverables

The consultancy consists of 30 working days distributed over four months. The Consultant is expected to complete the following deliverables:

Deliverable 1: Inception report – 5 working days

The Consultant shall submit an inception report including:

  • The proposed methodology and analytical framework.
  • A detailed work plan and timeline.
  • Stakeholder mapping and engagement approach.
  • Proposed data-collection methods and tools.
  • Key milestones and expected outputs.
  • A basic risk assessment and mitigation measures.
  • A quality-assurance approach.

The deliverable is expected during the first month following contract signature and represents 15% of the total contract value.

Deliverable 2: Stakeholder consultation and participatory mapping report – 15 working days

The Consultant shall conduct a participatory consultation process with relevant stakeholders and submit a comprehensive report documenting:

  • The consultation methodology and stakeholder-engagement process.
  • Key findings from consultations.
  • Participatory mapping results.
  • Existing neighborhood boundaries and community-representation structures.
  • Local-governance and conflict-sensitive considerations.
  • Recommendations to inform the neighborhood-classification framework and committee-formation methodology.

The deliverable is expected during the second month following contract signature and represents 45% of the total contract value.

Deliverable 3: Draft neighborhood-classification framework and neighborhood-committee formation methodology – 5 working days

The Consultant shall submit:

  • A draft evidence-based and conflict-sensitive neighborhood-classification framework.
  • Proposed classification criteria and supporting analysis.
  • Neighborhood profiles and a draft neighborhood-classification map.
  • A draft methodology for establishing representative neighborhood committees.
  • A proposed governance structure and committee composition.
  • A proposed community-election process.
  • Institutional linkages with the Municipality of Tripoli.
  • Implementation arrangements and a phased roadmap.

The deliverable is expected during the third month following contract signature and represents 20% of the total contract value.

Deliverable 4: Final report and validation workshop outputs – 5 working days

The Consultant shall:

  • Facilitate a validation workshop with relevant stakeholders.
  • Present the draft neighborhood-classification framework and committee-formation methodology.
  • Incorporate feedback received during the validation process.
  • Submit a final consolidated report containing the finalized framework, methodology, key findings, and recommendations for municipal adoption and implementation.

The deliverable is expected during the fourth month following contract signature and represents 20% of the total contract value.

All deliverables shall be submitted in one original hard copy and one electronic copy, preferably in Microsoft Word format where applicable.

Institutional arrangements

  • The Consultant will work under the supervision of the Local Peacebuilding Coordinator in the North and the Peacebuilding Project Manager.
  • UNDP will provide the Consultant with the necessary guidance in a timely, thorough, and transparent manner.
  • UNDP will provide clarifications and facilitate the work as required.
  • The Consultant shall maintain regular and consistent field presence throughout the assignment.
  • The Consultant shall properly document stakeholder consultations and field activities.
  • The Consultant shall triangulate data sources and validate findings before finalization.
  • The Consultant shall ensure compliance with data-protection, confidentiality, and ethical standards.
  • All transportation and site-logistics costs must be included in the Consultant’s financial offer and daily rate.

Duration of work

The total duration of the consultancy is four months, comprising a maximum of 30 working days.

The assignment will be implemented through the following phases:

  • Phase 1: Inception – desk review, methodology development, stakeholder mapping, and work-plan submission.
  • Phase 2: Consultations – stakeholder consultations and participatory mapping.
  • Phase 3: Classification and methodology – preparation of the draft neighborhood-classification framework and neighborhood-committee formation methodology.
  • Phase 4: Final reporting and validation – validation workshop and submission of the final report.

The Consultant shall submit a revised and detailed project work plan within one week of contract signature. Once approved, the work plan will form the basis for monitoring progress and performance.

Duty station

The Consultant will be field-based in Tripoli and the assigned districts, with occasional visits to the UNDP North Office in Tripoli as required.

Regular and consistent field presence is required throughout the assignment to conduct data collection, stakeholder consultations, participatory discussions, and validation activities.

STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Education

A Master’s degree in urban planning, governance, political science, peace and conflict studies, sociology, public administration, anthropology, or a related field.

Experience

  • A minimum of ten years of relevant proven experience in local development, urban planning, local governance, and peacebuilding.
  • Proven experience conducting at least three relevant projects or assignments in urban planning, local governance, conflict prevention, or social stability is required.
  • Demonstrated experience in participatory governance assessments, stakeholder consultations, neighborhood classification, conflict-sensitive programming, or community-representation processes is desirable.

Language

Fluency in English and Arabic is required.

The selected Consultant must be covered by valid health insurance and personal accident insurance for the duration of the assignment. Insurance may be provided by the individual or the company, with any related costs deducted from the Consultant’s remuneration, as applicable.

opportunities.title: Project Coordinator (m/f/d) Syria
opportunities.description:
KfW Banking Group

KfW, a public law institution under German law, is supporting the German Federal Government to achieve its goals in development policy and international development cooperation for more than 60 years. In this regard, KfW is both an experienced bank and a development institution with financing expertise, an expert knowledge of development policy and many years of national and international experience. On behalf of the German Federal Government, and primarily the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), KfW finances and supports projects that mainly involve public sector players in developing countries and emerging economies – from their conception and execution to monitoring their success. KfW’s goal is to help our partner countries fight poverty, maintain peace, protect the environment and the climate, and shape globalization in an appropriate way. More than 900 staff at its head office in Frankfurt, Germany and about 440 specialists in more than 64 local offices worldwide cooperate with partners all over the world.

In Syria, KfW currently finances projects mainly in the following sectors: basic infrastructure, employment creation, health, agriculture, water/wastewater, WASH, education, private sector development, good governance, social cohesion.

KfW Office Syria

The KfW Office Syria is currently re-established and is operational as of August 2026. The KfW Office will be a small, dynamic set-up actively supporting KfW’s interests and the German Government’s development cooperation in Syria.

The Syria office covers various aspects of KfW’s engagement in the country. The principal purposes of the Country Office is to strengthen the effectiveness of German Development Cooperation (GDC) in general, and in particular the Financial Cooperation (FC) with Syria; strengthen the visibility of development policy and the positioning of GDC in the international donor community; and to intensify the contact with partner institutions and project executing agencies with regard to a more effective, efficient and rapid implementation as well as identifying the potential for development and promotional loans as well as mandates.

In this respect, an expert in Project Coordination is sought for the office in Damascus for an initial period of two years with the possibility of an extension.

Starting date: November 2026

Duration: 24 months, full-time position

Location: Damascus and Syria

Main duties & responsibilities

The project coordinator focuses on supporting projects and programs in the infrastructure sector including rehabilitation of basic infrastructure, employment creation, health, agriculture, water/wastewater, WASH, education, private sector development, good governance, social cohesion. In addition, the project coordinator is expected to liaise with governmental institutions and entities across Syria. Furthermore, the project coordinator is expected to assist in PR-related matters.

The project coordinator shall implement all tasks according to KfW regulations and guidelines in a way that ensures smooth running of daily office and project affairs and timely adherence to logistic requirements. High flexibility according to arising needs is required in organizing daily work. Moreover, a strong sense of proactivity and of being responsible for the respective tasks contributing to the functioning of the office in Damascus is expected.

Project Coordination:

  • support and advise the Peace and Security Sector Team and the Country Director of KfW Office Syria in the preparation and implementation of respective projects and programs;
  • monitor and report on relevant developments in the sectors of basic infrastructure, employment creation, health, agriculture, water/wastewater, WASH, education, private sector development, good governance, social cohesion including financial sector and initiatives of other donors;
  • facilitate signing of financing agreements and disbursement processes
  • prepare assessments and analysis related to (potential) project executing agencies and peace and conflict aspects;
  • attend donor and partner related meetings in close coordination with the Country Director of KfW Office Syria and the Peace and Security Sector Team;
  • facilitate communication between the Syrian Government and the project executing agencies;
  • explore and identify new project/program opportunities based on a do-no-harm-approach and new partnerships in the above mentioned sectors as well as additional sectors;
  • undertake project preparation and project management tasks in the sector in close coordination with the respective sector team/s at HQ and the Country Director;
  • monitor projects and programs under implementation, undertake regular site visits to the projects all over Syria, and draft monitoring reports;
  • review, comment on and contribute to project proposals and progress;
  • support other local KfW colleagues in their work, if and when required;
  • Support and accompany missions from KfW HQ (arranging meetings, coordination of in-country field visits with partner organizations, etc.).

PR & Liaison:

  • PR assistance: daily screening of newspapers and compiling relevant news and headlines into a press overview; prepare and regularly update PR materials on projects and KfW’s work in Syria;
  • Liaison with Government of Syria and implementing partners: establish regular contact to relevant GoS institutions and liaise on matters pertinent to project implementation (in close coordination with the Country Director);
  • Translation: act as translator if and when required by the Country Director and visiting missions.

Required Competencies & Skills

  • Master level degree in economics, political/social sciences or related fields;
  • Fluency in English, Arabic (speaking/writing);
  • German language is not required but would be an asset, wanting to learn German would be a plus;
  • A minimum of 3 to 5 (but preferably more) years of significant working experience with bi-or multilateral agencies, donors, international institutions or a large international NGO;
  • Profound understanding of the infrastructure and finance sector in Syria;
  • Computer literacy in excel, accounting software, online banking and the like and an affinity to database management and other systems that could increase the efficiency of our current systems;
  • Proven ability to build and manage successful relationships and to establish a business network;
  • Experience in the coordination of complex projects, especially infrastructure projects in Syria would be an additional asset;
  • Demonstrated understanding of international development cooperation, strategies and projects (incl. gender mainstreaming and gender-related challenges, do-no-harm approaches, peace-and conflict assessments, climate change);
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, intercultural competence;
  • Willingness to work in teams and pro-active work attitude
  • Willingness to travel in-country and abroad according to requirements.

opportunities.title: Finance Intern for DCA South Sudan Country Office
opportunities.description:
DanChurchAid (DCA) is an International Non-Governmental Organisation with headquarters in Copenhagen, Denmark. The organisation was founded in 1922, and have country offices in 19 countries across Africa, the Middle East, Ukraine, and Asia.

DCA is working with local partners in South Sudan and the Regions to assist the poorest of the poor with a focus on protection, combating hunger, working for peace and conflict mitigation and the safe removal of explosive remnants of war (EWR).

The Finance Intern will provide temporary administrative and operational support to the Finance Department to ensure the timely execution of finance activities and facilitate the increasing number of internal and external audit requests. The intern will assist in organizing finance documentation, retrieving vouchers, scanning supporting documents, and maintaining proper records to strengthen audit readiness and overall departmental efficiency. This position is also a key one to guarantee a harmonization of processes and policies within all organization of DCA in South Sudan.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Retrieving payment vouchers and supporting documentation for internal and external audit requests.
  • Scanning, filing, and electronically archiving finance documents in accordance with DCA filing standards.
  • Organizing physical and electronic finance records to ensure easy retrieval.
  • Assisting in the preparation and compilation of audit documentation.
  • Supporting month-end filing and documentation processes.
  • Assisting with data entry and updating finance trackers when required.
  • Supporting the Finance Team with administrative tasks, including photocopying, printing, and document organization.
  • Ensuring finance documents are complete, properly labeled, and filed in the appropriate locations.
  • Performing any other finance-related administrative duties assigned by the Senior Finance Officer.

Expected Deliverables

  • Audit documents retrieved and shared within agreed timelines.
  • Finance vouchers scanned and filed accurately.
  • Physical and electronic finance records are maintained in an organized manner.
  • Timely support provided for ongoing audit assignments.
  • Improved efficiency in finance document management and retrieval.

Education

  • Diploma or bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • Partial Professional qualification is an added advantage.

Technical Skills

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and basic financial systems
  • Strong numerical and analytical skills
  • Knowledge of financial controls and accounting procedures

Core Competencies

  • High level of integrity and accountability
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy
  • Good organizational and time management skills
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines
  • Teamwork and collaboration

What can DCA offer you:

This position is Three (3) months as Intern to be based in DCA South Sudan Country Office Juba.

DCA promotes equal opportunity in terms of gender, race/ethnicity and belief and encourages all qualified and interested candidates to apply.

Expected starting date: September 1, 2026

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, race, religion, sexual orientation, abilities or ethnic affiliation are encouraged to apply for the vacancy. DCA conducts background check as part of the recruitment process. It is a prerequisite that you can pass this check and maintain this status throughout your employment with us. Everyone applying for a job with DCA must be ready to comply with our Code of Conduct, Staff Policy on Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment and our Child Safeguarding Policy.

opportunities.title: Community Manager East Africa - Arabic
opportunities.description:
MiCT is calling for proposals for a freelance Arabic speaking Community manager in the framework of its program “MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices 2026-2027”, funded by the German Federal Foreign Office. This is a freelance position running from August 2026 - June 2027 to be based in Nairobi, Kenya. The total number of working days will run up to 120, the exact number will depend on project implementation. MiCT invites interested and qualified persons to submit proposals by 16.08.2026.

About MiCT

Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT) is a non-profit organisation delivering expert media services in complex and challenging contexts with passion, precision, and agility.

Through collaborative work with partners, MiCT fosters transparent, inclusive, and fair dialogue supporting resilient societies. Operating across three continents and 15 countries, MiCT facilitates journalist training, media content production, research, monitoring, and supports the financial sustainability of media partners.

About the Project:

Since 2022, the MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices has supported at-risk journalists and media professionals from conflict regions, enabling them to continue their essential work in safety. The programme is part of the Hannah Arendt Initiative and a member of the Journalists in Distress Network. It offers stipends, security and equipment support, (mental) health services, legal aid, relocation, and professional development through regional hubs.

Description of the role

To support the Fellows from Sudan and East Africa, MiCT is looking for a Community manager to support project implementation on a freelance basis:

Tasks include, but are not limited to:

  • Organise the onboarding of all Fellows, including needs/interest assessment and introducing exiled fellows to the host countries’ environment.
  • Identify suitable project partners and experts to accompany the fellowship based on the interest assessment.
  • Set up and moderate various social media channels for the fellow community.
  • Function as the main point of contact for fellows for all programme elements, from personal support to finance.
  • Oversee community development and support for Fellows.
  • Coordinating and supporting the productions of fellow journalists in exile if they are able to during the duration of the entire Fellowship.
  • Close coordination with local partners in-country and in exile.
  • Available for regular meetings with Fellows and the MiCT headquarter team in Berlin.

4. Application Requirements

Successful applicants should be able to provide proof of the following:

  • Experience working with journalists in crisis and conflict contexts
  • Thorough understanding of the global media landscape, particularly in Sudan and its neighbouring countries, preferred
  • Fluency in Arabic and English is required
  • Experience communicating under stressful conditions
  • Familiarity with discourse around exile and crisis journalism, media freedom and critical, non-discriminatory development communication
  • Proven experience organising media related events and trainings required
  • Journalistic experience preferred
  • Flexibility and teamwork
  • The position requires availability in Nairobi, Kenya for 3 months per half year

opportunities.publisher: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
opportunities.description:
Job Opening ID: 281947

Category and Level : Professional and Higher Categories, P-3
Recruitment Type : Temporary Opportunities
Duty Station : NEW YORK

Deadline : Aug 6, 2026

Org. Setting and Reporting

This position is located in the Human Resources Section, Executive Office of the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). The post will be located in New York. OCHA is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA also ensures there is a framework within which each actor can contribute to the overall response efforts. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention and facilitate sustainable solutions. This temporary job opening is being advertised for the position of Human Resources Officer located in New York. The incumbent will report to the Human Resources Officer/Team Lead, Talent Acquisition and Outreach Management in Istanbul, Türkiye.

Responsibilities

Within delegated authority, the Human Resources Officer will be responsible for the following duties: General • Provides advice and support to managers and staff on human resources related matters. • Prepares special reports and participates and/or leads special human resources project. • Keeps abreast of developments in various areas of human resources. Recruitment and placement • Identifies upcoming vacancies in coordination with client offices. • Prepares vacancy announcements, reviews applications, and provides a short-list to those offices. • Arranges and conducts interviews to select candidates. • Reviews recommendation on the selection of candidate by client offices. • Serves as ex-officio in appointment and promotion bodies, examinations boards, and prepares and presents cases to these bodies. Prepares data and statistics using Inspira and existing dashboard for reporting purposes for client offices. • Monitors and evaluates recruitment and placement related activities of client offices, and recommends changes or corrections related to procedures to these offices. • Supervises and monitors the work of the Human Resources Assistants in carrying out all human resources activities. • Support the Junior Professional Officer (JPO) programme including liaising with the relevant stakeholders. • Prepares data and statistics using Inspira and existing dashboard for reporting purposes for client offices. • Supports the Head of Unit by monitoring recruitment status. • Provides advice on staff selection system in accordance with internal policies and in line with relevant rules and regulations. Other duties • Prepares in coordination with offices classification of jobs in Professional and General Service and related categories as needed. • Provides guidance to programme managers on the application of classification policies and procedures. • Assists in preparing staffing related policy papers, position papers and briefing notes on issues related to examinations and tests. • Collects and analyzes data to identify trends or patterns and provide insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods to enable data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting. • Performs other duties as required

Competencies

• PROFESSIONALISM: Knowledge of human resources policies, practices and procedures and ability to apply them in an organizational setting. Ability to identify issues, formulate opinions, make conclusions and recommendations. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Able to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. • PLANNING AND ORGANIZING: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. • CLIENT ORIENTATION: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be “clients” and seeks to see things from clients’ point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients’ needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients’ environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client.

Education

Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in human resources management, business or public administration, social sciences, education or related area. A first-level university degree in combination with qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Work Experience

A minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in human resources management, administration or related area is required. Experience in recruitment and talent sourcing, including screening of applications, is required. Experience with Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems or People Soft platforms, such as Inspira or equivalent is required. Experience in organizing outreach activities, events or campaigns, including digital engagement and stakeholder co-ordination is desirable. Experience in providing advice and guidance on human resources policies related to recruitment is desirable. Experience in working in the UN Common System or comparable international organizations is desirable.

Languages

English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. French is desirable.

Assessment

Evaluation of qualified candidates may include an assessment exercise which may be followed by competency-based interview.

Special Notice

This position is temporarily available for 6 months. If the selected candidate is a staff member from the United Nations Secretariat, the selection will be administered as a temporary assignment. While this temporary assignment may provide the successful applicant with an opportunity to gain new work experience, the selection for this position is for a limited period and has no bearing on the future incumbency of the post. Subject to the funding source of the position, the eligibility for this temporary job opening may be limited to candidates based at the duty station. This temporary job opening may be limited to “internal candidates,” who have been recruited through a competitive examination administered according to staff rule 4.16 or staff selection process including the review of a central review body established according to staff rule 4.15. Staff members of the United Nations common system organizations who will reach the mandatory age of separation or retirement within the duration of the current temporary need period are not eligible to apply. Submitting an application or selection for the current temporary job opening does not delay or increase the mandatory age of separation. Retirees above the mandatory age of separation who wish to be considered for the current temporary job opening must indicate the reason for their last separation as "retirement." Such retirees shall not be employed by the Organization, unless (a) the operational requirements of the Organization cannot be met by staff members who are qualified and available to perform the required functions; and (b) the proposed employment would not adversely affect the career development or redeployment opportunities of other staff members and represents both a cost-effective and operationally sound solution to meet the needs of the service. Pursuant to section 7.11 of ST/AI/2012/2/Rev.1, candidates recruited through the young professionals programme who have not served for a minimum of two years in the position of their initial assignment are not eligible to apply to this position.

United Nations Considerations

According to article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. Candidates will not be considered for employment with the United Nations if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. The term “sexual exploitation” means any actual or attempted abuse of a position of vulnerability, differential power, or trust, for sexual purposes, including, but not limited to, profiting monetarily, socially or politically from the sexual exploitation of another. The term “sexual abuse” means the actual or threatened physical intrusion of a sexual nature, whether by force or under unequal or coercive conditions. The term “sexual harassment” means any unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature that might reasonably be expected or be perceived to cause offence or humiliation, when such conduct interferes with work, is made a condition of employment or creates an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment, and when the gravity of the conduct warrants the termination of the perpetrator’s working relationship. About CIVICUS

CIVICUS exists to defend people power. As a growing global alliance of over 17,000 members in over 180 countries, we work together to monitor violations of basic civic freedoms, call out the perpetrators of violations and strengthen the power of people to organise by supporting a more accountable, effective and innovative civil society. We strive to promote excluded voices, especially from the global south.

About the Role

The Head of Finance provides strategic and operational leadership for CIVICUS’ financial management. The role combines strategic thinking and hands on delivery and requires a leader who can thrive in a dynamic mission driven and solutions focussed environment with high levels of accountability and transparency.

The Head of Finance is responsible for managing CIVICUS’s finance team, organisational financial strategy, budgeting and planning, financial reporting, audit management, risk oversight and compliance with funder, statutory, and regulatory requirements. The role encompasses mentoring and supervising finance staff, ensuring robust financial systems and controls are in place, and providing high-quality financial insights to support effective programme delivery and organisational decision making.

Working closely the Chief Operations Officer (COO) the Head of Finance is responsible for embedding sound financial management across the organisation, ensuring stewardship, accountability, transparency and long-term financial sustainability.

Key Requirements

  • A recognised professional qualified accountant (ACCA, CPA, CIMA, CIPFA or equivalent) with at least seven years post qualification experience, including at least 3 years in a Head of Finance role.
  • Senior level experience in a finance leadership role within an organisation of similar scale and complexity.
  • Strong written and verbal English skills.
  • Experience in the non-profit sector.
  • Extensive experience in establishing and administering financial processes for restricted donor funding within the not for profit sector.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of institutional donor regulations and financial compliance standards, including those of the European Union, US Foundations and European government agencies.
  • Ability to analyse, evaluate, and summarise financial records for accuracy and compliance with procedures, rules, and regulations, while effectively communicating financial information to non-financial team member in a clear and understandable manner.
  • Extensive experience in creating and leading training interventions for non-finance teams to enhance organisation financial management and adherence to financial standards.
  • Proven ability to build and lead high-performing, geographically dispersed teams by empowering employees, delegating responsibilities effectively, clearly defining roles, and promoting individual and team accountability.
  • Sound understanding of human rights and social justice principles.
  • Proven experience in driving innovation through the implementation of automated financial systems, process improvements, and technology solutions to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and financial reporting.
  • Knowledge of one or more UN languages other than English is desirable.
