opportunities.description:
Programme Finance Manager

Manchester, UK

Starting salary for this position is £41,628 per annum (plus contributory pension)

About MAG:

MAG (Mines Advisory Group) is an international humanitarian organisation based in Manchester, UK, and working in 32 countries. We remove landmines and unexploded ordnance to release safe and productive land for communities, and work to reduce the threat of armed violence by supporting governments to safely manage weapons and ammunition. In 1997, MAG was a co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize for our work campaigning for the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention.

About the role:

Reporting to the Head of Programme Finance, you will provide effective financial business partnering to MAG’s Regional and Country Programmes, Strategic Partnerships team and other key internal and external stakeholders. You will ensure the delivery of high quality financial information and support across multi-regional and multi-country activities, enabling informed decision making, strengthening ways of working and supporting the effective financial management of MAG’s multi-country contracts. You will work with your key stakeholders to ensure that contracts deliver value for money and remain compliant with donor and statutory requirements. This role is a key enabler to MAG’s global operations, ensuring that we can deliver on our mission to save lives, ease suffering and enable sustainable development.

Please note that as part of MAG's commitment to safeguarding, this post is subject to background checks before an offer of employment is confirmed. For more information on MAG’s approach to safeguarding and background checks on our website**.**

MAG is committed to the principles of diversity, equality and inclusion. If you think you would be suited to one of our roles we would welcome your application regardless of your background. We strive to provide an inclusive and supportive working environment where all employees feel respected and supported in fulfilling their potential.

About you:

You will be a finance professional with significant experience in either commercial or NGO environments, including preparation of business planning in complex scenarios and multiple currencies. You should be curious and risk aware, with strong analytical and evaluation skills, the ability to gather information from diverse sources tactfully and convert findings into detailed, actionable solutions. You will be a strong communicator over a range of mediums, able to engage stakeholders from varied backgrounds in a clear and constructive way. You should have strong experience of using mid-range accounting systems and reporting tools (e.g. PS Financials, Sage, SUN etc.), and advanced knowledge of of Microsoft Excel and database reporting tools to add value to business processes and reporting. You will be skilled in proactive problem-solving and have an innovative and solution-oriented approach, along with the flexibility to travel to remote and insecure locations at short notice.

We’re looking for someone with:

  • Strong experience of financial management, analysis and reporting
  • Advanced analytical and problem solving skills
  • Effective financial business partnering and stakeholder management skills
  • Experience managing multi-country, donor-funded contracts or complex grants

Benefits and Further Information:

  • Salary: £41,628 per annum and this increases with service.
  • Pension: MAG has a salary sacrifice group personal pension plan in place, and matches employee’s contributions up to 5%.
  • Leave: We recognise our staff work hard and need the appropriate time out to stay motivated. Annual Leave starts at five weeks each year and increases with service to six weeks. We also offer paid sick leave, and the amount of the entitlement increases with service. Once you’ve been with MAG for two years, you’re entitled to 13 weeks. MAG also has policies on compassionate leave, flexible working and family leave, including maternity, paternity, adoption and surrogacy leave.
  • Insurance: MAG provides personal accident insurance and life assurance to all staff, as well as medical and repatriation insurance for any period spent overseas whilst working for MAG.
  • Professional Subscriptions: MAG will pay for the cost of your annual subscription/membership fee for one professional body in certain circumstances.
  • Employee Assistance Programme: MAG offers free access to Health Assured, a service providing 24/7 confidential support and expert advice on a wide range of issues.

This role is based in the UK, therefore, a pre-existing right to work in the UK is a requirement and MAG will not be able to sponsor visa applications. Please note that if you have not declared your right to work in the UK on your application, we will not be able to consider you for this role.

We are happy to receive flexible working and job share requests in your application. If you are applying with an existing job share partner email us at recruitment@maginternational.org for further guidance.

opportunities.title: Project Outcome Harvest Writers
opportunities.description:
BACKGROUND INFORMATION ON PLAN INTERNATIONAL

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation that advances children’s rights and equality for girls.

We believe in the power and potential of every child, but this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion, and discrimination, and it is girls who are most affected. Working together with children, young people, our supporters, and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges facing girls and all vulnerable children.

We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood, and we enable children to prepare for – and respond to – crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national, and global levels using our reach, experience, and knowledge.

We have been building powerful partnerships for children for over 80 years and are now active in more than 75 countries.

Read more about Plan International's Global Strategy: 100 Million Reasons at https://plan-international.org/strategy

OBJECTIVE

The objective of this assignment is to conduct a comprehensive outcome harvesting exercise and develop high-quality written documentation that captures, validates, and presents the key outcomes, lessons learned, sustainability considerations, and contributions of the Education in Emergencies project implemented in Borno State.

The assignment will identify and document verifiable intended and unintended outcomes, including observable changes in behaviours, practices, relationships, systems, actions, and decision-making among children, adolescents, caregivers, teachers, community structures, partners, and government actors.

Drawing on evidence from Focus Group Discussions, Key Informant Interviews, direct observations, programme data, project documentation, and stakeholder reflections, the Consultant will analyse the project’s contribution to observed changes and produce clear, evidence-based, and human-centred written products that support donor reporting, accountability, learning, advocacy, visibility, and future programming.

SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES

The Consultant will be expected to:

  • Identify and document verifiable intended and unintended outcomes emerging from the project, including changes in behaviours, practices, actions, relationships, systems, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Gather, review, and synthesise evidence through Focus Group Discussions, Key Informant Interviews, direct observations, programme data, project reports, and relevant documentation to substantiate identified outcomes.
  • Analyse the project’s contribution to observed changes, including key enabling factors, implementation processes, contextual influences, stakeholder roles, and external factors that supported or limited progress.
  • Document measurable and credible non-measurable results, programme achievements, participant experiences, and evidence of change across key project components, including access to education, teaching and learning, learner retention and transition, protective learning environments, and community engagement.
  • Capture lessons learned, promising practices, challenges, sustainability considerations, and influencing actions to inform adaptive management, accountability, future programming, proposal development, and strategic decision-making.
  • Translate technical findings, programme evidence, and outcome harvesting insights into clear, compelling, accessible, and audience-appropriate written products for both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Develop high-quality narratives, case studies, outcome stories, learning products, and documentation materials that reflect the voices, experiences, resilience, and perspectives of children, adolescents, teachers, caregivers, community members, partners, and government stakeholders. This should detail who changed in what way, when and where the change took place, and how Plan International contributed to that outcome.
  • Ensure that all documentation is ethical, evidence-based, and in line with Plan International Nigeria’s safeguarding, informed consent, child protection, inclusion, confidentiality, and representation standards.
  • Ensure the outcome harvest aligns with Plan International’s Global Outcome Harvest Guidance.

SCOPE OF WORK

Working closely with Plan International Nigeria’s Brand and Communications team, MERL team, programme team, implementing partner, and relevant stakeholders, the Consultant will be responsible for conducting a comprehensive outcome harvesting exercise and developing high-quality written documentation from the Education in Emergencies project implemented in Borno State.

The assignment will include:

  • Participating in inception and briefing meetings with Plan International Nigeria, CASFOD, MERL, programme, and communications teams to clarify expectations, methodology, timelines, documentation priorities, ethical requirements, safeguarding considerations, and approval processes.
  • Reviewing relevant project documents, including proposals, reports, results frameworks, activity reports, monitoring data, previous documentation, communication materials, and other evidence sources to understand the project design, implementation approach, target groups, and expected outcomes.
  • Developing an outcome harvesting plan, including proposed outcome areas, data collection approach, stakeholder categories, tools, interview guides, validation process, field schedule, and documentation structure.
  • Identifying and documenting intended and unintended outcomes emerging from the project, including observable changes in behaviours, practices, relationships, systems, actions, decision-making, learning access, teaching approaches, learner retention, transition, community engagement, and protective learning environments.
  • Conducting Focus Group Discussions, Key Informant Interviews, direct observations, and other appropriate documentation activities with substantiators, including children, adolescents, teachers, caregivers, school leaders, community structures, government stakeholders, implementing partners, and project staff.
  • Gathering and triangulating evidence from stakeholder testimonies, programme data, field observations, project reports, and relevant documentation to substantiate identified outcomes and strengthen the credibility of findings.
  • Analysing the project’s contribution to observed changes, including key enabling factors, implementation processes, stakeholder roles, contextual influences, challenges, and external factors that supported or limited progress.
  • Documenting project achievements, measurable and credible non-measurable results, lessons learned, promising practices, sustainability considerations, challenges, innovations, and influencing actions to support accountability, learning, adaptive management, and future programming.
  • Developing clear, compelling, evidence-based, and human-centred written products, including outcome stories, success stories, case studies, learning briefs, participant narratives, and other agreed documentation outputs.
  • Ensuring that all written products reflect the dignity, voices, experiences, resilience, and perspectives of children, adolescents, teachers, caregivers, community members, partners, and government stakeholders reached or engaged through the project.
  • Working closely with the Brand and Communications team to ensure that all narratives are clear, audience-appropriate, ethically framed, and suitable for donor reporting, advocacy, visibility, stakeholder engagement, knowledge management, digital communication, and institutional learning.
  • Incorporating consolidated feedback from Plan International Nigeria, CASFOD, MERL, programme, and relevant review teams in a timely and professional manner.
  • Ensuring that all documentation processes and final outputs comply with Plan International Nigeria’s safeguarding, child protection, informed consent, confidentiality, inclusion, ethical storytelling, representation, and data protection standards.
  • Submitting all final approved outputs in agreed editable formats, including clean and tracked-change versions where applicable, together with organised supporting materials, interview notes, outcome records, references, captions, and other relevant documentation files.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Working in close coordination with the Project Team, CASFOD, and Plan International Nigeria’s MERL, Brand, and Communications teams, the Consultant will:

  • Participate in desk review of relevant project documents, including proposals, reports, monitoring data, activity records, previous documentation, and existing evidence to inform outcome identification and documentation priorities.
  • Participate in pre-field briefing sessions to align on the outcome harvesting objectives, methodology, data collection tools, stakeholder mapping, safeguarding protocols, informed consent procedures, timelines, and expected outputs.
  • Develop and apply an appropriate sampling approach for selecting Focus Group Discussion and Key Informant Interview participants, ensuring representation across gender, age, disability, location, and stakeholder categories.
  • Conduct field visits to targeted communities in Damboa, Kala Balge, and Mobbar LGAs to collect primary data through Focus Group Discussions, Key Informant Interviews, direct observations, and other appropriate participatory methods.
  • Engage relevant stakeholders, including teachers, school administrators, adolescent learners, caregivers, community members, education authorities, community structures, implementing partners, project staff, and other relevant actors, ensuring informed consent and safeguarding compliance at all stages.
  • Identify and document verifiable intended and unintended outcomes, clearly capturing changes in behaviours, practices, actions, relationships, systems, decision-making, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Ensure each documented outcome clearly reflects who changed, what changed, when and where the change occurred, why the change is significant, and how the project contributed to the observed change.
  • Gather and organise credible evidence to substantiate documented outcomes, drawing from stakeholder testimonies, programme monitoring data, field observations, project reports, and other relevant sources.
  • Triangulate qualitative findings with available programme data, including indicators, activity reports, monitoring records, and other documented evidence, to strengthen the credibility and accuracy of the outcome findings.
  • Ensure documented outcomes are evidence-based, well-structured, and substantiated through at least two credible sources, where feasible, with clear articulation of outcome significance, lessons learned, sustainability considerations, enabling factors, challenges, and influencing actions.
  • Analyse the project’s contribution to observed changes, including the role of project interventions, stakeholder actions, contextual factors, partnerships, community engagement, and other factors that supported or limited progress.
  • Collaborate with the MERL, Programme, Brand, and Communications teams to ensure consistency, quality assurance, and alignment between documented outcomes, supporting evidence, visual materials, and final communication products.
  • Develop clear, compelling, evidence-based, and human-centred written outputs, including documented outcomes, outcome stories, success stories, case studies, learning products, and analytical summaries, as agreed.
  • Submit documented outcomes, analytical outputs, and draft written products for review, and incorporate consolidated feedback within agreed timelines to ensure quality, accuracy, completeness, and alignment with Plan International Nigeria’s standards.
  • Ensure all documentation processes and final outputs comply with Plan International Nigeria’s safeguarding, child protection, informed consent, confidentiality, inclusion, ethical storytelling, representation, data protection standards and Plan International’s Global Outcome Harvest Guidance.

DELIVERABLES

The consultant (writer) will be expected to provide the following:

  • A comprehensive Outcome Harvesting Report documenting verifiable intended and unintended outcomes, including clear articulation of who changed, what changed, when and where the change occurred, the project’s contribution, supporting evidence, and the significance of each outcome.
  • Structured outcome documentation organised by location, including Damboa, Kala Balge, and Mobbar LGAs, and by thematic or project component, with analysis of changes in behaviours, practices, actions, relationships, systems, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Synthesised findings from Focus Group Discussions, Key Informant Interviews, direct observations, programme data, and relevant project documentation, including participant quotes, testimonial extracts, and narrative details aligned with safeguarding, informed consent, confidentiality, and ethical storytelling requirements.
  • An outcome evidence matrix or dataset, where applicable, showing outcome statements, sources of verification, key actors, supporting evidence, data type, and validation status for each documented outcome.
  • A detailed section on lessons learned, promising practices, sustainability considerations, challenges, enabling factors, and influencing actions, highlighting implications for future programming, policy engagement, adaptive management, and institutional learning.
  • A consolidated written report or narrative portfolio presenting key achievements, outcome-level changes, stakeholder perspectives, implementation insights, lessons learned, sustainability considerations, and programme impact in a clear, coherent, and audience-appropriate format.
  • Final written outputs organised by location, theme, project component, story type, and intended use, and submitted in agreed editable formats.
  • Clean and tracked-change versions of written outputs, where revisions have been made, to support review and approval processes.
  • A clean and organised repository of all final products, supporting notes, evidence references, captions, quotes, outcome records, and approved narrative materials.
  • Written confirmation that all outputs have been developed in compliance with Plan International’s safeguarding, informed consent, confidentiality, child protection, inclusion, data protection, ethical representation standards and outcome harvest guidance.

FORMAT & QUALITY

All deliverables must:

  • Be submitted in Microsoft Word or Google Docs, with clean formatting, clear structure, appropriate headings, and high editorial standards in tone, grammar, flow, and readability.
  • Be clear, evidence-based, well-organised, and suitable for both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Accurately reflect validated outcome harvesting findings, programme evidence, stakeholder perspectives, participant experiences, and approved project data.
  • Align with Plan International Nigeria’s brand voice, tone, messaging standards, and editorial quality expectations.
  • Comply fully with Plan International Nigeria’s safeguarding, child protection, informed consent, confidentiality, inclusion, ethical storytelling, representation, and data protection standards.
  • Present children, adolescents, girls, caregivers, teachers, community members, and other stakeholders with dignity, agency, respect, and contextual accuracy.
  • Avoid stereotypes, exaggeration, sensationalism, deficit-based language, or any framing that may expose participants or communities to harm, stigma, or misrepresentation.
  • Ensure that participant voices, quotes, testimonials, and case details are used responsibly and only in line with approved consent and safeguarding requirements.
  • Clearly distinguish between validated evidence, stakeholder perspectives, interpretation, and analysis.
  • Be submitted in both clean and tracked-change versions where revisions are required, and in final approved formats agreed with Plan International Nigeria.

QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE

Consultant/Vendor Qualification and Experience

  • An advanced degree in Communications, Journalism, Development Studies, Social Sciences, International Development, or a related field.
  • A minimum of 5–7 years of professional experience in writing, editing, qualitative documentation, storytelling, or knowledge product development within humanitarian or development programming contexts.
  • Demonstrated experience in outcome harvesting, qualitative evaluation, developing high-quality success stories, impact narratives, case studies, learning documents, and advocacy-oriented content for donor-funded projects.
  • Strong understanding of adolescent and youth participation, gender equality, child and youth rights, social and behaviour change programming, and humanitarian response in fragile or conflict-affected settings.
  • Proven experience documenting human-centred stories and translating technical programme information into compelling and accessible narratives.
  • Strong qualitative interviewing, synthesis, editing, and storytelling skills.
  • Experience working with international NGOs, UN agencies, development partners, or donor-funded projects.
  • Solid understanding of safeguarding, Protection from Sexual Harassment, Exploitation, and Abuse (PSHEA), informed consent, confidentiality, ethical storytelling, and child protection standards.
  • Demonstrated experience working in North-East Nigeria or similar humanitarian and security-sensitive environments.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English; knowledge of Hausa or other relevant local languages will be considered an added advantage.

Applicants must submit at least two (2) verifiable samples of high-quality documentation of outcome harvests, success stories, and lessons learned previously developed in similar contexts.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND EQUIPMENT

The Editor and writer Consultant must demonstrate:

Skills:

  • Strong expertise in qualitative documentation, storytelling, knowledge product development, and evidence synthesis.
  • Excellent writing, editing, and narrative development skills with the ability to produce compelling, technically sound, and audience-appropriate content.
  • Ability to translate complex programme evidence and field experiences into accessible and engaging communication materials.
  • Strong understanding of humanitarian programming, adolescent participation, gender-transformative approaches, and ethical representation standards.
  • Strong interpersonal, facilitation, and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to deliver quality outputs within agreed timelines.

Equipment

  • A reliable computer system capable of handling data analysis, report writing, and design of high-quality documents.
  • Access to relevant data analysis and documentation tools, such as Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and qualitative analysis software where necessary.
  • Professional writer and editing and layout software (e.g., Adobe InDesign or similar) for producing visually appealing and publication-ready reports.
  • Adequate data storage and backup systems to ensure safe and secure management of all collected data and documentation materials.
  • Reliable internet connectivity and communication tools to support virtual coordination, data transfer, and timely submission of deliverables.
  • Ability to provide secure digital transfer of all project outputs, including reports, datasets, and supporting materials, to the project team

PERFORMANCE METRICS & PAYMENT BASIS

The Consultant’s work will be assessed based on:

  • Number of outcomes validated
  • Quality of outcome statements and strength of evidence
  • Timeliness of delivery
  • High-quality, clear, and well-organised success stories
  • Documentation of success stories and lessons learned
  • Success stories and case studies show real experiences of learners and communities
  • Adherence to ethical and consent protocols
  • Completeness of documentation

QUANTIFICATION OF WORK:

The Consultant will be required to conduct outcome harvesting and provide high-quality writing, editing, and documentation support for the ECHO HIP 2024 Education in Emergencies project across Kala Balge, Mobbar, and Damboa LGAs in Borno State.

The assignment will focus on documenting verifiable intended and unintended outcomes emerging from the project, including changes in behaviours, practices, actions, relationships, systems, learning access, teaching approaches, learner retention and transition, community engagement, and protective learning environments.

The scope of work will include the collection, validation, synthesis, analysis, writing, editing, and finalisation of outcome documentation, success stories, outcome stories, case studies, impact narratives, participant quotes, lessons learned, sustainability considerations, evidence matrices, and supporting narrative materials.

All outputs should be suitable for donor reporting, accountability, advocacy, visibility, stakeholder engagement, knowledge sharing, institutional learning, future programming, and digital communication purposes.

The final number, type, and structure of written outputs will be agreed with Plan International Nigeria during the inception and briefing phase, based on approved documentation priorities, field schedules, available evidence, safeguarding considerations, and communication needs.

Payment will be made upon satisfactory delivery and approval of all agreed outputs, including required revisions, supporting materials, evidence documentation, and organised files in the agreed formats.

Assignment-specific briefs, outcome harvesting tools, story leads, interview guides, or additional guidance may be issued by Plan International Nigeria where necessary to further define activity-specific documentation requirements.

SUPERVISION AND REPORTING

The consultant will report to the Brand and Communications team and work closely with the Project Manager, MERL Officer, Project Officer, and other relevant project team members to ensure that all design outputs are contextually accurate, aligned with the approved content, and responsive to programme objectives.

The consultant will be responsible for maintaining regular communication with the assigned focal persons throughout the assignment and for incorporating feedback received during the review and approval process.

All design outputs, source files, and final materials produced under this contract shall remain the exclusive intellectual property of Plan International Nigeria. The consultant may not reuse, reproduce, publish, or distribute any material developed under this assignment without prior written approval from Plan International.

Interested Consultants may access the full details of this call, including all relevant annexes, through the link below: https://tinyurl.com/4syxjt5j

opportunities.title: Wildlife & Community Development Expert with national experience
opportunities.description:
Ref: 003
Position Title: Wildlife & Community Development Expert with national experience
Status: Consultant
Number of Days: 360 (over a period of 18 months)
Location: Tanzania, Ruvuma

About Landesa

Grounded in the knowledge that having legal rights to land is a foundation for prosperity and opportunity, Landesa partners with governments and local organizations to ensure that those experiencing the most extreme forms of poverty have secure rights over the land they steward. Founded as the Rural Development Institute in 1967, Landesa has helped more than 100 million families living in poverty gain legal control over their land. With secure land rights, these families can eat better, earn more, educate their children, practice conservation, and achieve dignity for generations. For additional information, visit the Landesa website at www.landesa.org.

Landesa is seeking a highly qualified Wildlife & Community Development Expert with national experience for an anticipated 18-months GIZ program that aims to improve the management of Human Wildlife Conflict by key actors in Tanzania. The project’s main geographical scope is the Ruvuma Landscape/ including 42 villages of the Districts of Liwale, Namtumbo, and Tunduru. The project also aims to strengthen the capacity for steering and coordination of the Wildlife Division of the Ministry for Natural Resources and Tourism, and the institutions involved in managing HWC, including the Tanzania Wildlife Management Authority (TAWA), Tanzania National Parks (TANAPA), Tanzania Forest Services Agency (TFS), Districts councils and Hotspot Villages.
The contractor will be responsible for the implementation of one District land use plan, 15 village land use planning (LUP) and community action plans, developing the organizational structure, curricula and materials, as well as piloting 30 clubs, for the revival of the Malihai Club (environmental conservation clubs in schools and colleges) and strengthening the outreach programs of Tanzania Wildlife Management Authority and Tanzania National Parks Authority (concept development, materials and support to implementation of pilot in 30 villages) of the institutions involved in wildlife management.

The vacancy is limited to candidates living in Tanzania. The position is contingent upon receipt of donor funding.

Availability: The Wildlife & Community Development Expert with national experience should start work on November 1st 2026.

Tasks of the Expert:
•
Strengthen collaboration working closely with districts natural resource, and land use planning team to engage communities in participatory land use planning, ensure integration of key priority conservation area into district and village land use plans, and guide the demarcation of land adjacent to community and protected areas, ensuring the HWC aspects are deeply considered during the process and implementation.
•
Provide technical advice on coexistence measures in farming and pastoral communities, districts and relevant authorities during the LUP and CAP processes and implementation.
•
Promote conservation-linked livelihoods through implementation of Community Action Plans (CAPs) with a focus on improving community livelihoods, linking conservation with income-generating activities.
•
Technical advice on HWC and biodiversity conservation, conservation issues, sustainable land use, and human-wildlife coexistence supporting the revitalization of Malihai Clubs and the outreach programs of TAWA and TANAPA, including content development, training ToTs, and facilitating pilot in selected schools to ensure long-term sustainability.

Qualifications of the Expert:
•
Education/training: University degree (e.g. master’s or equivalent) in either wildlife biology or management, rural development, Community Development or Natural Resource management.
•
Language: Knowledge of English C1, C1 in Swahili.
•
General professional experience: 3 years of professional experience on Wildlife and Natural resource conservation projects. 2 years of professional experience on Community development project in rural setting.
•
Specific professional experience: 5 years of professional experience in human wildlife conflict management projects in Tanzania. 4 years of professional experience in community outreach or environmental awareness programs related to HWC and wildlife management. 2 years of professional experience on working with local governments, traditional authorities (3 out of 10).
•
Professional experience in the country/ region of assignment: 9 years of professional experience in Tanzania of which 5 years in rural communities in Tanzania.

Soft Skills
•
A deep commitment to the mission of a better, safer future for the world’s poorest people through secure access to land.
•
Strong problem-solving.
•
Strong oral presentation skills and an ability to think on one's feet when defending policy recommendations.
•
Familiarity with concepts that can be applied to rural development.
•
Ability to develop concrete work plans and manage elements so that work is performed according to agreed-upon budgets and plans.
•
Ability to manage documents and correspondence, track, and report on project labor, and carry out other administrative tasks efficiently, routinely, and in conformance with Landesa standards and procedures.
•
Ability to work collaboratively with a range of people at all levels, including those from host country governmental and non-governmental organizations, and other counterparts, clients, and funders.
•
Ability to demonstrate cross-cultural sensitivity, tact, and poise.
•
Ability to lead and work collaboratively as a member of teams, regardless of role within the team, through consensus building, communication, and leadership.
•
Ability to make and use distinctions as to types, frequency, tenor, and levels of communication, depending upon the circumstances and audience.
•
Legal right to work in the country of assignment.

Physical and Environmental Conditions
This position does not require unusual demands for physical effort. Work environment involves everyday risks or discomforts that require normal safety precautions typical of places such as offices, meeting or training rooms, residences, or commercial vehicles, e.g., use of safe workplace practices with office equipment, and/or avoidance of trips and falls, and observance of fire regulations and traffic signals.

Work Environment and Working Conditions for Travelers to Developing Countries
While performing the duties of this job, the employee may be exposed to working conditions and hazards that are prevalent for the location and/or country of assignment. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Work is primarily performed indoors, with some potential for exposure to safety and health hazards related to electronics work. The employee may be required to travel overseas and domestically. When traveling in a developing country, the employee may be exposed to: Physical Hazards (illnesses, noise, extreme temperatures, wet or humid climates, etc.) Road Hazards (unfinished/dirt roads, potholes, traffic-related accidents, etc.), and Atmospheric Conditions (odors, dust, fumes, smog, etc.).

Additional Comments
The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. Reasonable accommodation may be provided in appropriate circumstances to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this job.

opportunities.title: Recrutement d'un consultant national (Togo) pour l'évaluation finale externe du Programme SSF
opportunities.description:
1. Description du programme

Le « Programme de promotion des structures sociales visant à mettre en place des structures durables pour des soins de santé inclusifs et à permettre aux groupes socialement marginalisés et économiquement défavorisés de participer au développement social et économique du pays (Togo) » (Programme SSF) est cofinancé par le Ministère fédéral allemand de la Coopération économique et du Développement (BMZ) et par CBM à travers le mécanisme de financement des structures sociales (Social Structure Funding – SSF). Le SSF est une initiative du BMZ visant à financer des programmes de développement à long terme tout en cherchant à influencer les politiques et stratégies de développement au niveau national. Cette initiative contribue au renforcement des structures sociales afin de répondre efficacement aux besoins et aux contraintes des populations vulnérables. À l'instar d'autres organisations allemandes actives au Togo, le Bureau Pays de CBM au Togo a bénéficié de cette opportunité de financement pour contribuer au renforcement des structures sociales locales. Ce soutien vise à améliorer l'accès à des services de soins oculaires de qualité, à promouvoir l'éducation inclusive des enfants présentant une déficience visuelle et à autonomiser les personnes en situation de handicap visuel grâce à la formation professionnelle et à l'accès à l'emploi. Pour cette première phase, le programme est mis en œuvre sous la coordination du Bureau Pays de CBM, en collaboration avec trois organisations partenaires, à savoir le PNSO, la CNT/EPT et la FETAPH, chacune apportant son expertise propre pour promouvoir la santé oculaire, l'éducation inclusive et l'emploi inclusif des personnes présentant une déficience visuelle au Togo. Cette mise en œuvre se déploie aux niveaux macro (national), méso (régional) et micro (communautés, individus), comme suit :

  • Au niveau macro, le programme SSF vise à mener un travail de plaidoyer pour améliorer la perception du public à l'égard des personnes en situation de handicap et à assurer une meilleure prise en compte de leurs besoins et contraintes spécifiques dans les politiques et stratégies transversales.
  • Au niveau méso, le programme SSF vise à améliorer la participation et l'implication des structures régionales et étatiques d'appui, ainsi qu'à renforcer les systèmes d'éducation et de santé inclusifs, en leur fournissant les ressources nécessaires à la mise en œuvre des mesures prévues par l'État au titre de la Stratégie de Santé Oculaire (2019–2023) et du Plan Sectoriel de l'Éducation (2020–2030).
  • Au niveau micro, le programme SSF vise à mettre en place des structures sociales telles que des groupes d'entraide de personnes présentant une déficience visuelle (en particulier les jeunes) et de leurs aidants, des comités de parents/enseignants et d'autres groupes sociaux d'entraide, qui assureront le suivi de la qualité de l'éducation dans les écoles et du fonctionnement des services de conseil et de réadaptation, et qui soutiendront les personnes présentant une déficience (visuelle) et leurs familles à travers des activités génératrices de revenus (AGR) dans le Grand Lomé et la région Maritime.

Pour la phase actuelle (2024–2026), le programme SSF est mis en œuvre dans le Grand Lomé et la région Maritime, ciblant 176 750 personnes présentant une déficience visuelle en tant que bénéficiaires finaux, à travers l'atteinte de quatre objectifs spécifiques :

  • Objectif 1 : Des structures de dépistage et de traitement des maladies oculaires sont disponibles dans toutes les préfectures, en particulier dans le Grand Lomé et la région Maritime.
  • Objectif 2 : Les services de réadaptation et les structures d'appui sont accessibles à toutes les personnes présentant une déficience visuelle.
  • Objectif 3 : Les possibilités éducatives pour les personnes en situation de handicap (visuel) sont améliorées dans le Grand Lomé et la région Maritime.
  • Objectif 4 : Les personnes en situation de handicap (visuel) ont un accès sans obstacle à des opportunités adaptées de formation professionnelle et d'emploi.

Objectif de l'évaluation et utilisation prévue

La présente évaluation finale vise à fournir une appréciation indépendante et fondée sur des données probantes de la performance et des résultats du Programme SSF cofinancé par le Ministère fédéral de la Coopération économique et du Développement (BMZ) et Christian Blind Mission (CBM). L'évaluation examinera la mesure dans laquelle le programme a atteint les objectifs visés et produit des résultats conformes au cadre de projet approuvé et à l'accord contractuel. Plus précisément, l'évaluation devra :

  • Apprécier la pertinence, la cohérence, l'efficacité, l'efficience, l'impact et la durabilité du programme SSF ;
  • Mesurer les progrès accomplis vers les effets (outcomes) et les objectifs ;
  • Examiner, dans la mesure du possible, l'égalité de genre, l'inclusion du handicap, la durabilité environnementale et les droits humains ;
  • Identifier les bonnes pratiques, les innovations, les défis et les leçons apprises ;
  • Formuler des recommandations opérationnelles.

Les conclusions de cette évaluation serviront à la redevabilité, à l'apprentissage et à la prise de décision par CBM, le BMZ et les partenaires de mise en œuvre (PNSO, CNT/EPT et FETAPH). Elle fournira une appréciation indépendante de la performance, des résultats et de l'utilisation des ressources du Programme SSF. L'évaluation alimentera les exigences de reddition de comptes aux bailleurs et renforcera la transparence à l'égard des parties prenantes et des bénéficiaires. Elle produira des leçons apprises fondées sur des données probantes, des bonnes pratiques et des recommandations opérationnelles pour améliorer la programmation future. Les résultats orienteront également les ajustements stratégiques des interventions en matière de santé oculaire inclusive, d'éducation et d'inclusion socio-économique des personnes présentant une déficience visuelle au Togo.

2. Champ de l'évaluation

L'évaluation couvrira la période de mise en œuvre du programme allant du 1er janvier 2024 au 30 septembre 2026. Elle couvrira également les deux régions d'intervention (le Grand Lomé et la région Maritime).

3. Public cible et apprentissage

L'évaluation finale s'adresse à diverses parties prenantes, notamment :

  • Les bailleurs (BMZ, CBM) ;
  • Les organisations partenaires (PNSO, CNT/EPT, FETAPH) ;
  • Les Ministères de la Santé, de l'Éducation, de la Solidarité, du Commerce et de la Jeunesse ;
  • Les conseils municipaux et communes (autorités locales) ;
  • Les districts sanitaires, hôpitaux et directions préfectorales de la santé ;
  • Les écoles, directions régionales de l'éducation, inspections du préscolaire et du primaire, la Direction des Examens, Concours et Certifications (DECC) ;
  • L'Institut des Aveugles de Togoville, le Centre Polyvalent Saint-Augustin de Lomé ;
  • Les Chambres de métiers, centres d'apprentissage ou de formation, autres structures de formation technique ou d'apprentissage.

Les résultats de l'évaluation serviront à des fins de redevabilité vis-à-vis des bénéficiaires et des bailleurs de l'intervention, et à tirer des leçons de sa mise en œuvre. Plus précisément, les résultats de l'évaluation permettront à CBM et aux trois (3) organisations partenaires de comprendre l'impact de l'intervention sur les groupes cibles, en particulier les personnes présentant une déficience visuelle dans les deux (2) régions d'intervention, sur la période couverte par l'étude.

D'autres parties prenantes de l'intervention, telles que les ministères clés, les autorités locales ou les partenaires techniques et financiers (PTF) actifs dans les mêmes secteurs, pourront aussi utiliser les résultats de l'évaluation pour enrichir leur apprentissage des bonnes pratiques à prendre en compte au bénéfice des personnes présentant une déficience visuelle en matière de soins oculaires, d'éducation inclusive et d'accès à la formation, à des sources de revenus ou à des emplois décents. Pour ce qui est de l'organisation contractante, CBM, les résultats de l'évaluation seront utilisés dans le cadre de la reddition de comptes au BMZ. Les résultats orienteront également sa future collaboration avec les autorités locales en vue d'établir des services de santé oculaire, des services éducatifs et des sources de revenus durables et de qualité, inclusifs et accessibles, pour les groupes cibles au regard des trois (3) axes thématiques. Les résultats permettront en outre à CBM de renforcer sa collaboration avec le BMZ dans la mise en œuvre des programmes bénéficiant du financement SSF. À des fins d'inclusion et d'accessibilité, en particulier pour les personnes présentant une déficience visuelle, l'équipe de consultants chargée de l'évaluation veillera à ce que le rapport soit rédigé dans un langage clair et accessible.

Questions d'évaluation

A. PERTINENCE – Le programme était-il sur la bonne voie ?

  • Dans quelle mesure et comment le Programme SSF a-t-il adapté ses stratégies de mise en œuvre, ses activités et son ciblage en cours d'exécution en réponse à l'évolution des conditions contextuelles affectant les bénéficiaires et les parties prenantes, et comment ces adaptations ont-elles influencé l'atteinte des résultats ?

B. COHÉRENCE – Dans quelle mesure le programme s'inscrit-il dans le contexte national et international plus large ?

  • Dans quelle mesure la logique d'intervention du programme était-elle cohérente et plausible pour relier les activités, les produits, les effets et les changements de long terme visés ?

C. EFFICACITÉ – Le programme a-t-il atteint ses objectifs ?

  • Dans quelle mesure le Programme SSF a-t-il atteint les produits et effets visés, et quelle contribution a-t-il apportée aux changements au sein des groupes ciblés et dans les zones géographiques d'intervention, au regard des trois (3) axes thématiques :
    • la prévention des maladies oculaires et l'amélioration de l'accès à des services de soins oculaires de qualité pour les femmes, les hommes et les enfants présentant une déficience visuelle ;
    • l'amélioration de l'accès à une éducation inclusive et de qualité pour les enfants présentant une déficience visuelle ;
    • l'amélioration de l'accès à la formation professionnelle, aux opportunités génératrices de revenus et à un emploi décent pour les jeunes et les adultes présentant une déficience visuelle.
  • Dans quelle mesure le modèle de partenariat entre CBM, le PNSO, la CNT/EPT et la FETAPH a-t-il été efficace pour atteindre les objectifs de l'intervention ?

D. EFFICIENCE – Dans quelle mesure les ressources ont-elles été planifiées et utilisées ?

  • Dans quelle mesure les ressources allouées (financières, humaines et matérielles) ont-elles été utilisées de manière efficiente, appropriée, respectueuse des délais et équitable pour atteindre les résultats visés ?

E. IMPACT – Quelle différence le programme a-t-il produite ?

  • Dans quelle mesure l'intervention a-t-elle généré des effets positifs ou négatifs, intentionnels ou non, sur les bénéficiaires, leurs ménages, leurs communautés et les institutions concernées, en particulier au regard de la santé oculaire, de l'éducation inclusive, de l'employabilité, des moyens de subsistance, de la participation sociale et du bien-être ?
  • Quelles données probantes attestent d'un impact émergent et de la probabilité d'un impact à plus long terme ?

F. DURABILITÉ – Les bénéfices seront-ils durables ?

  • Dans quelle mesure le programme SSF a-t-il mis en place un cadre multisectoriel intégré et efficace (« structure sociale intégrée ») pour la fourniture de soins oculaires et d'un accompagnement éducatif et socioprofessionnel aux enfants et aux jeunes présentant une déficience visuelle ?

G. Protection des enfants et des adultes vulnérables

  • Dans quelle mesure les aspects liés à la sauvegarde des enfants et des adultes à risque ont-ils été pris en compte, et comment les mécanismes correspondants ont-ils été établis, utilisés et respectés ?

H. Égalité et inclusion / égalité de genre

Dans quelle mesure le projet a-t-il promu et mis en œuvre les droits des personnes en situation de handicap, en particulier celles présentant une déficience visuelle, à une santé oculaire de qualité, à une éducation et une formation inclusives, ainsi qu'à l'accès à des moyens de subsistance et à des emplois décents ? Comment ces droits se traduisent-ils parmi ces bénéficiaires, y compris les hommes et les femmes, les garçons et les filles ?

Méthodologie

Cette évaluation nécessitera le recours à des méthodes participatives pour la collecte et l'analyse de données quantitatives et qualitatives.

Il revient au consultant (e) ou cabinet de consultant de proposer une méthodologie qui permettra d'évaluer l'ensemble des composantes du projet en accord avec les critères d'évaluation.

Aucune théorie du changement formelle ni étude de faisabilité n'ayant été élaborée avant la mise en œuvre du programme, l'équipe d'évaluation devra, le cas échéant, reconstituer la logique d'intervention du programme à partir de la documentation disponible et des consultations des parties prenantes. L'équipe d'évaluation devra apprécier la cohérence et la plausibilité de cette logique d'intervention ainsi que la mesure dans laquelle la conception et le ciblage du programme étaient adaptés au contexte et aux besoins des bénéficiaires visés.
L'équipe d'évaluation proposera une stratégie d'échantillonnage assurant une représentation adéquate des femmes, des hommes, des filles et des garçons présentant une déficience visuelle, des aidants, des prestataires de services, des acteurs étatiques et des organisations partenaires.

Le rapport final devra présenter les bonnes pratiques, les innovations, les facteurs clés de succès, les défis et les leçons apprises - y compris ce qui a fonctionné, ce qui n'a pas fonctionné, pour qui, dans quelles circonstances et pourquoi - et formuler des recommandations opérationnelles pour les interventions futures.

Profil du consultant principal. Le consultant principal doit justifier d'une expérience avérée dans la conduite d'évaluations de programmes dans les domaines de la santé publique, de l'éducation inclusive et de l'accès à l'emploi pour les groupes vulnérables tels que les personnes en situation de handicap, ou tout autre domaine similaire. Il/elle doit satisfaire aux exigences suivantes :

  • Formation supérieure (minimum Bac+5) en sciences sociales (sociologie, anthropologie, etc.), santé publique, éducation, gestion de programmes de développement, suivi et évaluation ;
  • Connaissances avérées dans les domaines du handicap, de la santé oculaire, de l'éducation inclusive et de l'emploi des groupes vulnérables ;
  • Expérience de plus de 08 ans dans la conduite d'évaluations et la capitalisation de programmes financés par des bailleurs internationaux (BMZ, GIZ, UE) ;
  • Avoir mené des évaluations (au moins trois) de programmes/actions dans des domaines identiques ou similaires à l'action à évaluer ;
  • Bonne maîtrise du cadre de résultats, des approches d'évaluation participatives et des outils de prise en compte des questions de handicap et d'intégration du genre et des groupes vulnérables dans le cycle de programme ;
  • Excellente maîtrise du français, de la rédaction de rapports et de l'outil informatique (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, SPSS, etc.) ;
  • La maîtrise de l'anglais et d'une ou plusieurs langues locales (mina, éwé) constituerait un atout.

Livrables

Le rapport doit être soumis en français, dans le format standard des rapports d'évaluation de CBM, avec au moins un résumé en français et en anglais (3 pages max.).

  • Le rapport de démarrage est soumis 10 jours après réception de l'ensemble de la documentation de base et signature du contrat. Le rapport de démarrage devra comprendre une matrice d'évaluation reliant les questions d'évaluation, les indicateurs, les sources d'information, les méthodes de collecte de données et les approches analytiques. L'objet de ce rapport est de garantir que l'évaluation couvre les éléments les plus critiques de l'exercice, en particulier la pertinence et la robustesse de la méthodologie à utiliser, ainsi que la représentation du genre, du handicap et de la diversité et la participation des différents groupes sociaux en vue d'une analyse inclusive des besoins.
  • Le rapport de démarrage offre l'occasion à l'organisation et à l'équipe d'évaluation de s'assurer d'une compréhension commune de l'évaluation et de clarifier leurs attentes dès le départ. Le rapport devra rendre compte de la revue documentaire réalisée par l'équipe d'évaluation et des lacunes que le travail de terrain permettra de combler. Il devra également refléter les possibilités de participation des personnes en situation de handicap à l'élaboration de la méthodologie ainsi qu'au processus de collecte et d'analyse des données.
  • Le projet de rapport final doit être soumis au plus tard 14 jours après la phase de terrain.
  • Le rapport d'évaluation final (en français), d'un maximum de 30 pages de texte (+ annexes), sera examiné par CBM et ses organisations partenaires et devra intégrer les commentaires reçus.
  • Le rapport doit comporter un résumé de deux (02) à trois (03) pages maximum en français et en anglais, qui pourra être utilisé à des fins de publication (par exemple sur les sites internet de CBM).
  • Tous les documents de référence, y compris les questionnaires, les bases de données, etc., devront figurer en annexe. La confidentialité des données devra être garantie à toutes les étapes, et les noms des répondants ou toute autre information permettant de les identifier (adresse, numéros de téléphone) ne devront pas apparaître sur les questionnaires remplis.
  • Un (1) atelier devra être organisé pour la présentation et la validation du rapport final.

L'évaluation devra se conformer aux normes éthiques internationalement reconnues, notamment la participation volontaire, le consentement éclairé, la confidentialité, la protection des données, la sauvegarde et le principe de ne pas nuire (do-no-harm).

Calendrier de l'évaluation

L'évaluation devra se dérouler du 1er septembre au 15 novembre 2026.

Les candidat (e) s doivent donc proposer un calendrier de conduite de l'évaluation.

opportunities.title: Consultancy to Facilitate the Review and Revision of the Oxfam in Africa (OiA) Strategy 2025 2030
opportunities.description:
Oxfam in Africa (OiA) adopted its Strategy 2025 2030 under the vision "An Africa Without Inequality," anchored in Ubuntu. The Strategy provides the overarching strategic direction for Country Offices, the SAF Cluster, the AU Liaison Office, and
engagement with African-based Affiliates and other stakeholders. It advances OiA's work on Just Economies, Accountable and Inclusive Governance, Climate Justice, Gender Justice and Humanitarian Action, while aligning with the Oxfam Global Strategic Framework (GSF) 2020 2030, Horizon II and the Confederation's transformation
agenda.

Since its adoption, both the external operating environment and OiA itself have evolved significantly. Across Africa, protracted conflicts, humanitarian crises, climate shocks, shrinking civic space, widening inequalities, governance challenges and declining development and humanitarian funding have increased the need for greater strategic
focus, organizational agility and more effective prioritization of limited resources.

Internally, OiA has undergone structural and operational changes to strengthen sustainability, collaboration and organizational effectiveness, generating important implementation experience and lessons after approximately eighteen months of Strategy implementation.

At the Confederation level, implementation of the Transformation Design is commencing, while development of the next phase of the Global Strategic Framework (Horizon III) is expected during FY2027 2028. Although both processes will shape Oxfam's future strategic direction, they are not yet sufficiently advanced to guide immediate strategic adjustments within OiA.

Accordingly, OiA will undertake a light, focused and evidence-informed strategic recalibration in response to its evolving organizational context and the outcomes of its recent change process. Rather than comprehensively redesigning the Strategy, the review will identify the strategic adjustments needed to strengthen its relevance, focus, feasibility and implementation within OiA's current organizational capacity and resource realities. This recalibration is intended to address OiA's immediate strategic needs while recognizing that a more comprehensive strategic review may be undertaken once the Oxfam Confederation's transformation processes and Horizon III are completed.

opportunities.title: ICT Cloud Officer
opportunities.description:
MSF Eastern Africa is looking for an ICT Cloud Officer

Do your skills and experience not precisely match the requirements? At MSF EA, we strive to create a safe, diverse and inclusive workplace, recognizing the need to increase access to professional opportunities for historically underrepresented groups. If you're interested in this position but your experience doesn't align perfectly with the selection criteria, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the ideal candidate for this or other positions.

Firmly committed to safeguarding patients, community members, staff, and all those in contact with the organization from all forms of abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), we will take all necessary steps, through rigorous vetting processes, to ensure that confirmed perpetrators of abuse do not join the organization.

For this position, contact level with patients and children is categorized as Low Risk and will be monitored with this in regard.

Introduction

Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) is an international independent medical humanitarian organisation that provides assistance to people affected by conflicts, epidemics, and natural or human-made disasters and excluded from healthcare. We provide this assistance without discrimination, irrespective of race, religion, creed or political affiliation.

About MSF Eastern Africa

MSF Eastern Africa is the regional institutional office of MSF. It focuses on representation and networking, recruiting and supporting staff from the region, communications and fundraising, as well as working on other dossiers of importance to MSF such as Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI), Data Protection, mutualization, training, medical operational support and environmental health.

Rationale/Objective for Position

Design, deploy, and maintain MS-Cloud infrastructure to ensure secure, resilient, and scalable ICT services across MSF Eastern Africa and Ubuntu operations. Provide expert-level support and contribute to strategic modernization of network and systems architecture.

This position will be hierarchically and functionally accountable to the IT Infrastructure & Operations Specialist.

Tasks & Responsibilities

  • Lead the design and implementation of hybrid cloud infrastructure, ensuring alignment with organizational needs and security standards.
  • Manage Microsoft cloud including Azure, Exchange Online/M365, and Windows Server components.
  • Develop and maintain technical documentation, procedures, and configuration standards for cloud systems and networks.
  • Ensure robust backup, disaster recovery, and system hardening practices.
  • Collaborates to long-term networking strategy and cloud migration roadmap in collaboration with ICT leadership.
  • Support in virtualization platforms (VMware, Hyper-V etc) and DevOps tools (Terraform, Ansible, Docker).
  • Implement proactive monitoring and alerting systems to detect and resolve cloud infrastructure issues before service impact.
  • Conduct regular security audits and vulnerability assessments to ensure compliance with MSF ICT policies and external frameworks as CIS & NIST.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams and other MSF entities to integrate cloud-native solutions and enhance operational efficiency.
  • Resource optimization: regularly review recommendations (Azure Advisor, ...) related to VMs’ sizing and avoid over- or under-provisioning.
  • Continuous Improvement: Proactively make suggestions to increase efficiency and reduce overhead.
  • Incident Management: investigate and resolve incidents and alerts.
  • Monitor cloud infrastructure health, resource quotas and log to ensure optimal performance.
  • Manage and support the deployment and configuration of azure virtual machines, virtual networks, load balancing, and scaling solutions.
  • Collaborate with the applications team to deploy, install, and support HQ and field applications.
  • Develop and maintain PowerShell Scripts to automate routine tasks and improve operational efficiency.

Qualifications

Education

  • Degree in Computer Science or related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Certifications; Microsoft Azure Administrator Associate, Azure Network Engineer Associate, Microsoft Azure Solutions Architect Expert (Plus).

Experience

  • Minimum 5 years in network and ICT cloud infrastructure roles
  • Language; English (required)
  • Knowledge
    • Expertise in networking (TCP/IP, VLANs, DNS, IPsec)
    • Cloud platforms (Azure etc)
    • Microsoft systems (M365, Azure AD, Intune)
    • Virtualization (VMware, Hyper-V etc)
    • Backup/storage (Veeam, HP 3PAR etc)
    • Linux, DevOps tools, IaaC
    • Basic database administration (asset)

Competencies

  • Strong troubleshooting and organizational skills, autonomous and collaborative mindset, adaptable to change, and willingness to work outside office hours when needed.
  • Knowledge of Azure DevOps is desirable.

Conditions and Benefits:

  • Job Location: MSF Eastern Africa office in Nairobi (Kenya)
  • Contract: Open-ended Full-time contract.
  • Start date: ASAP.
  • Salary: An annual salary of EUR 23,296 at HQ Grade 7 based on a full-time appointment with an annual increment of 2% every year up to a maximum of 10 years.
  • Work-life balance financial benefit; ranging between EUR 247 to 295/month based on individual & administrative status. This amount may be used to cover accommodation and utilities, transportation, etc.
  • Other benefits include; 25 days of annual leave, Employer Pension contribution and medical insurance cover (staff and family) based on MSF EA terms/conditions.

opportunities.title: Request for proposal production agency for success story development Mzazi Hodari III programme
opportunities.description:
Request for Proposal

Production Agency for Success Story Development

Mzazi Hodari III Programme – Tanzania

July 2026

Assignment Summary

Item Description

Client - Girl Effect Tanzania

Assignment - Success Story Production Agency

Procurement Method - Open Competitive Procurement

Contract Type - Consultancy Services

Location - Arusha, Tanzania

Reporting To - Creative Director, Girl Effect Tanzania

Contract Duration - August 2026 – May 2027

Deliverables - Three multimedia success stories

Proposal Type - Technical and Financial Proposals submitted separately

Who We Are

Girl Effect is an international non-profit organisation that creates media, technology and behaviour change interventions that equip adolescent girls and young women with the knowledge, confidence and skills to improve their health, education and livelihoods.

In Tanzania, Girl Effect delivers programmes through its youth brand Tujibebe, which uses radio, social media, digital platforms and community engagement to promote positive health, parenting and behaviour change.

This consultancy supports the Mzazi Hodari III programme, which promotes responsive caregiving, early childhood development and positive parenting behaviours among young parents and caregivers.

Background

Mzazi Hodari III is a one-year extension programme designed to improve nurturing care practices for children under three years by encouraging:

  • Early initiation of breastfeeding
  • Exclusive breastfeeding
  • Responsive caregiving
  • Positive parenting practices
  • Appropriate health-seeking behaviour
  • Improved child nutrition

As the programme concludes, Girl Effect seeks to document programme impact through compelling multimedia success stories demonstrating behavioural change among programme participants and showcasing the effectiveness of the programme's Social and Behaviour Change (SBC) approach.

Assignment Objective

Girl Effect Tanzania seeks to engage a qualified Production Agency to conceptualise, film, edit and deliver three high-quality success story products that demonstrate the impact of the Mzazi Hodari III programme.

The agency will work closely with Girl Effect's Creative Team throughout pre-production, production and post-production to ensure all deliverables align with Girl Effect's creative, safeguarding and brand standards.

What You’ll Do

Mzazi Hodari III is a one-year extension project focused on improving children’s health by encouraging responsive caregiving, early breastfeeding, and promoting positive parenting behaviors through media content across radio, social media, IVR, and on-the-ground interventions.

The goal of Mzazi Hodari III is to increase knowledge and practices around nurturing care for children under three, particularly in areas like early breastfeeding, responsive caregiving, and child health care. We aim to:

  • Improve knowledge about health-seeking behaviors among adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) who are non-caregivers.
  • Shift perceptions by highlighting the positive outcomes associated with good health practices.
  • Increase self-efficacy among AGYW to engage confidently in caregiving and health-related decisions.

Deliverables

The successful agency will produce the following outputs:

Deliverable Description

Becoming Mzazi Hodari 2-minute documentary following three young parents

SBC in Action Written success story and accompanying short social media reel

60 Seconds of Impact One-minute donor-focused impact video

Behind-the-scenes Footage Raw footage and photography

Raw Video Files All original production files

Final Edited Assets High-resolution versions suitable for digital distribution

Girl Effect Responsibilities

Girl Effect will:

  • Provide programme background and creative brief.
  • Facilitate introductions to beneficiaries and partners.
  • Coordinate safeguarding onboarding.
  • Provide brand guidelines.
  • Supply monitoring and evaluation results.
  • Review and approve all creative outputs.
  • Coordinate final dissemination.

Who You Are

Essential

The agency should demonstrate:

  • Minimum four years' experience in professional video production.
  • Proven experience producing documentaries or success stories.
  • Strong storytelling capability.
  • Experience filming in community settings.
  • Professional filming and audio equipment.
  • Capacity to operate in Arusha and surrounding regions.

Desirable

Preference will be given to agencies with:

  • Experience working with NGOs or development partners.
  • Experience producing behaviour change communication content.
  • Knowledge of safeguarding and ethical storytelling.
  • Strong understanding of Tanzanian cultural contexts.

Assignment Schedule

  • Phase 1: Creative briefing and pre-production
  • Phase 2: First production shoot ("Before")
  • Phase 3: Second production shoot ("After")
  • Phase 4: Editing and review
  • Phase 5: Final delivery of all assets

Detailed production dates will be agreed during contract inception.

Proposal Submission

Interested agencies should submit:

Technical Proposal (Maximum 5 Pages)

The proposal should include:

  • Understanding of the assignment.
  • Proposed creative approach.
  • Production methodology.
  • Workplan and timeline.
  • Team structure.
  • Relevant experience.
  • Links to previous documentary or impact storytelling work.
  • Three client references.

Financial Proposal

Submitted separately and including:

  • Professional fees.
  • Pre-production costs.
  • Production costs.
  • Post-production costs.
  • Travel and logistics.
  • Applicable taxes.
  • Any assumptions or exclusions.

Evaluation Criteria

The criteria against which proposals will be evaluated are listed below.

Criteria Weight

Relevant Organisational Experience - 35%

Creative Approach & Methodology - 25%

Previous Work & References - 10%

Proposed Team - 10%

Financial Proposal / Value for Money - 20%

Commercial Terms

  • The successful agency will enter into Girl Effect's standard consultancy agreement.
  • All deliverables produced under this assignment shall become the intellectual property of Girl Effect.
  • Payment shall be linked to satisfactory completion of agreed deliverables.
  • All applicable taxes should be quoted separately.
  • The agency must comply with Girl Effect's safeguarding, confidentiality and data protection requirements.

Procurement Timetable

Activity Date

RFP Issued - 27 July 2026

Proposal Submission Deadline - 3 August 2026

Evaluation - Early August 2026

Contract Award - Early August 2026

Project Commencement - Mid-August 2026

Final Delivery - May 2027
