opportunities.title: Architectural Planning, Spatial Design, and Cost Estimation for the Proposed Immersive Learning Center within SIDM (now SIDR), Odisha
opportunities.description:
A. About the Asian Disaster Preparedness Center:

The Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) is an autonomous international organization established for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes with a vision of safer communities and sustainable development through disaster risk reduction and climate resilience in Asia and the Pacific. Established in 1986 as a technical capacity-building center, ADPC has grown and diversified its expertise across social and physical sciences, envisioning safer communities and sustainable development through disaster risk reduction. Being an autonomous international organization governed by the Board of Trustees. It supports sustainable solutions for disaster risk reduction across a broad range of specialist areas, with a wide range of professional expertise from atmospheric scientists to social scientists with experiences from all levels of engagement typically required for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR) effectively.

ADPC’s Strategy 2030 guides the organization in providing comprehensive risk reduction support to countries and communities in Asia and the Pacific with various programs being implemented under 15 strategic themes by three departments, namely the Preparedness and Climate Actions, Risk Analytics and Climate Services, and Risk Governance and Financing. In addition to these, ADPC also works on three cross-cutting themes: Gender and Diversity, Innovation, and Regional and Transboundary Cooperation through permanent working committees. These activities are supported by proactive individual departments of Finance, Human Resources, and Administration. ADPC recognizes the importance of examining the linkages between disaster risk management, poverty reduction, gender equality, sustainability, rights-based approaches, climate change, and regional cooperation.

For details, please refer to the ADPC website at http://www.adpc.net.

B. Department Introduction

The Preparedness and Climate Action (PCA) Department of ADPC focuses on enhancing the preparedness and response management capacities of governments, response organizations, volunteers, non-governmental organizations, the private sector, communities, and other traditional and non-traditional actors of the Disaster Risk Management Ecosystem. It also strives to strengthen the capacity of institutions and at-risk communities for faster and more efficient disaster recovery. The department works with the above-stated actors to ensure that the regional, national, sub-national, and local disaster preparedness, response, and recovery frameworks and implementation plans are in place well before disaster strikes.

C.Statement of Intent

The Institutional Strengthening through Preparedness and Inclusive Response in India (INSPIRE) Program is a collaborative initiative by the Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC), the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), and state institutions in Odisha, Gujarat, and Kerala. The program aims to enhance institutional systems for disaster preparedness and climate action at the national and state levels, while contributing to regional cooperation in the Bay of Bengal.

Through INSPIRE, ADPC works closely with national and state-level stakeholders to promote risk-informed planning, strengthen local capacities, and support sustainable disaster management practices. The program focuses on advancing institutional leadership and technical capacities within strategic government institutions, enabling them to play a central role in managing disasters and responding to climate shocks. It also fosters the development of innovative, data-driven solutions and promotes cross-learning through structured regional collaboration.

As part of the programme, the Odisha State Disaster Management Authority (OSDMA) is exploring the establishment of an Immersive Learning Centre (ILC) within the State Institute of Disaster Resilience (SIDR). The proposed facility is envisioned as a technology-enabled experiential learning environment to strengthen disaster preparedness, applied learning, and simulation-based training. The facility should provide a flexible learning environment that can be expanded over time and serve as a model for future immersive learning facilities in disaster management institutions.

ADPC seeks to engage an Architect/Planner to translate this concept into an implementable architectural proposal. The assignment will develop the Functional Design Brief, prepare concept design options, develop the preferred option to schematic design level, and prepare indicative cost estimates and a preliminary Bill of Quantities to support Government decision-making and subsequent detailed design.

This assignment includes concept planning, schematic architectural design, preliminary specifications, indicative cost estimates, and preliminary Bills of Quantities for planning and budgeting purposes. It excludes detailed engineering design, structural design, MEP design, tender documentation, and construction supervision.

The Consultant will work closely with ADPC and OSDMA throughout the assignment.

D.Expected Outputs:

The Consultant shall deliver a structured set of architectural planning, concept design, and preliminary cost estimation outputs to support the proposed Immersive Learning Center (ILC) within SIDM, Odisha. All outputs shall be aligned with the concept inputs, consultations, functional requirements, and institutional directions provided by ADPC and OSDMA.

The Consultant shall deliver the following outputs:

  1. Inception Report and Functional Design Brief:

The Consultant shall prepare an Inception Report and Functional Design Brief that establishes a common understanding of the assignment, confirms the approach and work plan, and translates stakeholder requirements into a clear functional and spatial brief to guide the architectural design process. The output shall include:

  • methodology and workplan;
    • stakeholder consultation plan;
    • review of available background information;
    • benchmarking of relevant facilities;
    • functional and spatial requirements;
    • planning assumptions; and
    • Functional Design Brief

2. Concept Design Options:

The Consultant shall develop concept design options that translate the Functional Design Brief into practical architectural solutions for consideration by ADPC and OSDMA. The options should demonstrate alternative approaches to spatial organisation, functionality, and user experience and support the selection of a preferred concept for further development. The output shall include:

  • up to two concept design options;
  • functional zoning;
  • indicative layouts;
  • area statement;
  • design rationale; and
  • recommendation of a preferred option

3. Schematic Architectural Design Package:

Based on the preferred concept approved by ADPC and OSDMA, the Consultant shall prepare a Schematic Architectural Design Package that develops the selected option to a level sufficient for institutional review, budgeting, and subsequent detailed design. The output shall include:

  • site integration plan;
    • dimensioned floor plans;
    • area statement and space schedule;
    • key sections and elevations, where required;
    • indicative 3D views;
    • design notes; and
    • phased implementation approach, where applicable

4. Cost Estimate and Preliminary Bill of Quantities:

The Consultant shall prepare an indicative cost estimate and preliminary Bill of Quantities for the approved schematic design to support budgeting, planning, and investment decision-making. The cost estimate shall clearly identify assumptions and exclusions and shall not be considered a detailed engineering estimate. The output shall include:

  • indicative cost estimate;
    • preliminary Bill of Quantities;
    • major cost categories; and
    • assumptions and exclusions

5. Final Report and Presentation Package:

The Consultant shall consolidate all approved outputs into a final report and presentation package suitable for submission to ADPC and OSDMA. The final submission shall provide a coherent record of the assignment, document the recommended design solution, and support subsequent stages of project development. The output shall include:

  • final report;
    • presentation slides;
    • editable drawings;
    • CAD files, where applicable;
    • Excel cost estimate and BoQ; and
    • PDF versions of all outputs.

Close-out Support: The Consultant shall provide close-out support after completion of the main technical deliverables. This support shall be provided on an as-needed basis to assist ADPC and OSDMA in responding to final clarifications, compiling submission materials, addressing comments, and supporting the handover of editable files and final documentation.

E. Scope of Work/Responsibilities and Tasks:

Task 1. Preparation of the Functional Design Brief

The Consultant shall:

  • review background documents, available drawings, and relevant information provided by ADPC and OSDMA;
  • undertake consultations with ADPC, OSDMA, and other relevant stakeholders;
  • review relevant national and international examples of immersive learning and simulation facilities;
  • define the functional and spatial requirements for the proposed ILC; and
  • Prepare the Functional Design Brief to guide concept development.

Task 2. Development of Concept Design Options

The Consultant shall:

  • develop up to two concept design options;
  • prepare concept layouts and presentation materials;
  • present the options to ADPC and OSDMA;
  • revise the options based on comments received; and
  • support selection of the preferred option.

Task 3. Preparation of the Schematic Architectural Design Package

The Consultant shall:

  • prepare schematic architectural drawings for the approved option;
  • prepare area schedules, key sections, and supporting design notes;
  • identify interface requirements for building services, AV/IT systems, and immersive learning technologies;
  • propose practical measures to improve energy efficiency, reduce resource consumption, minimize maintenance requirements, promote the use of locally available materials where feasible, and reduce lifecycle costs through appropriate architectural and planning solutions; and
  • Prepare documentation suitable for institutional review and budgeting.

Task 4. Cost Estimation and Final Documentation

The Consultant shall:

  • prepare an indicative cost estimate;
  • prepare a preliminary Bill of Quantities;
  • clearly state assumptions and exclusions;
  • prepare the draft and final reports;
  • incorporate comments received from ADPC and OSDMA; and
  • Submit all reports, drawings, and editable files.

F. Reporting Principles:

The Consultant will report directly to the Unit Head, Resilience Building and Localization Unit at ADPC and will work under the technical guidance of ADPC in close coordination with OSDMA. ADPC will provide technical guidance, facilitate stakeholder consultations, coordinate review meetings, and provide comments on all deliverables. OSDMA will facilitate site access, consultations, and review of the proposed design options.

The Consultant is expected to lead the key consultation and review meetings so as to understand client needs directly and respond appropriately through the design process.

All costs related to consultations, stakeholder meetings, and workshops will be managed separately by ADPC. Travel undertaken by the Consultant in the delivery of this assignment shall be covered by ADPC upon prior written approval and in accordance with ADPC policy.

This is a lump-sum consultancy assignment.

G.Minimum Qualifications:

The assignment shall be undertaken by an Individual Consultant / Lead Architect or Planner with demonstrated architectural planning and cost-estimation capability. The Consultant may draw on drafting, visualization, quantity estimation, or specialist technical support as required, while remaining fully responsible for the quality, coherence, and timely delivery of all outputs.

The architect/planner should have demonstrated experience in strong architectural planning and cost estimation capability, with:

  • minimum 10 years of relevant professional experience;
  • demonstrated experience in architectural design and planning of institutional, educational, training, or experiential learning facilities;
  • demonstrated ability to translate functional and operational requirements into spatial concepts and planning outputs;
  • experience in preparation of cost estimates and bills of quantities;
  • experience in the development of concept-level architectural packages for institutional decision-making;
  • experience in working with government agencies or large institutions;

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in immersive learning centers, simulation-based environments, or analogous training facilities is desirable;
  • Experience in disaster management, emergency training, or related facilities is desirable;
  • Prior experience in India or South Asia is preferred.

H. Duty Station: Home-based, with missions to Bhubaneswar and other relevant locations as required.

I. Contract Duration: The Contract will be for a period of 6 months between August 2026 – January 2027.

J. Deliverable: The work shall be carried out during the contract period from August 2026 to January 2027, as per the following indicative timelines. The consultant will be home-based, with travel to Bhubaneshwar, as approved by ADPC.

Deliverable 1 : Submission and approval of the Inception Report and Functional Design Brief

Timeline : By 31 August 2026

Deliverable 2 : Submission and approval of the Concept Design Options, including functional zoning, indicative layouts, area statement, design rationale, and recommended preferred option

Timeline : By 15 September 2026

Deliverable 3 : Submission of the Schematic Architectural Design Package, including site integration plan, dimensioned floor plans, area statement and space schedule, key sections/elevations where required, indicative 3D views, design notes, phased implementation approach where applicable, indicative cost estimate, preliminary Bill of Quantities, major cost categories, and assumptions and exclusions

Timeline : By 30 September 2026

Deliverable 4 : Submission and approval of the Final Report and Presentation Package, including final report, presentation slides, editable drawings, CAD files where applicable, Excel cost estimate and BoQ, and PDF versions of all outputs

Timeline : By 30 November 2026

Deliverable 5: Close-out support for up to five working days, including final clarifications, minor revisions, handover support, and response to ADPC/OSDMA queries, as requested

Timeline : Up to 5 working days available until 31 January 2027

K. Payment Terms:

  • Payments will be released upon submission and formal approval of agreed deliverables by ADPC.
  • The Consultant shall address and incorporate all comments required for approval of each milestone.
  • ADPC reserves the right to withhold approval of deliverables that do not meet the required technical, presentation, and reporting standards until satisfactory revisions are completed.
  • All deliverables shall be submitted in:
    • Editable formats (AutoCAD, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, CAD, or equivalent formats where applicable)
    • PDF versions for institutional review and documentation purposes
  • All design outputs shall be professionally formatted and suitable for technical review and institutional presentation. All outputs shall include, where applicable:
    • Annotated diagrams
    • Concept layouts and zoning plans
    • Functional descriptions
    • Schematic representations
    • Presentation-ready graphics
    • Supporting technical notes and recommendations

L. Itinerary:

All costs related to travel to field locations as required, including transportation, accommodation, and per diem, shall be covered by ADPC as per policy.

In addition, all costs related to approved consultations, review meetings, workshops, and validation sessions will be managed separately by ADPC in accordance with organizational procedures.

M. Payment Mode:

Payment shall be made through bank transfer based on satisfactory delivery of agreed outputs.

N. Selection Method:

The candidate will be selected in accordance with ADPC’s recruitment process and policy guidelines.

opportunities.title: Program Development Consultant
opportunities.description:
Project HOPE is an international NGO of more than 1,000 engaged employees and hundreds of volunteers who work in more than 25 countries, responding to the world’s most pressing global health challenges. Throughout our 60-year legacy, Project HOPE has treated millions of patients and provided more than $3 billion worth of medicines to local health care organizations around the world. We have helped build hundreds of health programs from the ground up and responded to humanitarian crises worldwide.

Code of Conduct

It is our shared responsibility and obligation to treat each other with respect, take affirmative steps to prevent matters involving Sexual Exploitation & Abuse and Trafficking in Persons, and to disclose all potential and actual violations of our Code of Conduct, which may include Conflicts of Interest, Fraud, Corruption, Discrimination or Harassment. Together we can reinforce a culture of respect, integrity, accountability, and transparency.

Background

Project HOPE seeks a highly qualified consultant to serve as the lead technical writer and program development advisor for the development of a Statement of Interest (SOI) in response to the U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy (GHSD) Annual Program Statement (APS): Advancing Global Health (Funding Opportunity Number: DFOP0017890), Addendum I: Innovations in Population-Based Surveys and Surveillance.

The Addendum invites organizations to propose innovative approaches that strengthen population-based surveys, routine surveillance systems, and epidemiologic data collection methodologies in low- and middle-income countries. The opportunity emphasizes cost-effective, sustainable, country-owned surveillance systems that improve the timely generation and use of population health data across priority health areas, including HIV, tuberculosis, malaria, neglected tropical diseases, nutrition, and emerging public health threats.

Through this consultancy, Project HOPE intends to develop a competitive SOI that advances innovative surveillance and survey approaches aligned with the Department of State's objectives related to global health security, country ownership, sustainability, data quality, interoperability, and evidence-based decision-making. The consultant will provide strategic technical leadership, facilitate program design discussions, coordinate technical contributions from internal and external stakeholders, support consortium development, and develop the complete Statement of Interest (SOI) package.

Reference Documents

  • Grants.gov Opportunity Announcement: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/363057
  • U.S. Department of State APS: Advancing Global Health (DFOP0017890)
  • Addendum I: Innovations in Population-Based Surveys and Surveillance

The consultant will provide strategic technical leadership, facilitate program design and proposal development discussions, coordinate technical inputs from Project HOPE and prospective consortium partners, and develop the complete SOI narrative for submission by September 15, 2026. The period of performance will begin upon execution of the agreement and continue through the SOI submission deadline.

Specific Objectives:

  1. Lead technical program design and development of Project HOPE's SOI in response to GHSD Addendum I.
  2. Develop a competitive technical approach aligned with the objectives, guiding principles, and evaluation considerations outlined in the APS and Addendum.
  3. Collaborate with Project HOPE staff and partners to refine project strategy, implementation approach, anticipated outcomes, and consortium roles.
  4. Provide strategic recommendations regarding consortium composition, partner roles, and complementary technical expertise.
  5. Draft and revise the complete SOI narrative, incorporating feedback from Project HOPE and consortium partners.
  6. Participate in planning meetings and technical discussions throughout the SOI development process.
  7. Support final quality assurance of the submission to ensure responsiveness, clarity, and compliance with APS requirements.

Position Requirements

The consultant should demonstrate the following

  • Advanced degree (Master's or higher) in Public Health, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Global Health, Health Systems, Infectious Diseases, International Development, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience designing, implementing, or evaluating global health surveillance systems, population-based surveys, epidemiological studies, or public health research programs.
  • Demonstrated experience leading the development of successful U.S. Government-funded proposals, concept notes, statements of interest, or applications for agencies such as USAID, CDC, NIH, PEPFAR, Department of State, or other major international donors.
  • Strong technical knowledge of population-based surveys, surveillance systems, monitoring and evaluation, epidemiology, health information systems, and data use for decision making.
  • Demonstrated experience working with multi-country or regional global health programs in low- and middle-income countries.
  • Excellent technical writing, analytical, and communication skills, including experience synthesizing complex technical information into concise, compelling proposal narratives.
  • Proven ability to facilitate collaborative design processes involving multiple stakeholders, technical experts, and consortium partners.
  • Ability to work independently and meet aggressive deadlines within a fast-paced proposal development environment.

Duration of Consultancy

The consultancy is expected to be completed over approximately 8-10 weeks, beginning upon contract execution and concluding following submission of the Statement of Interest on September 15, 2026.

Notice to applicants: Project HOPE does not conduct direct solicitation/recruitment via email. Project HOPE never asks job applicants for payment or financial information at any stage of the recruitment process. Project HOPE will never send you a third-party check and ask you to cash it. If you have been recruited via email, please contact Compliance@projecthope.org

Due to the substantial number of inquiries, we receive, only candidates who have met the required experience & qualifications for this position will be considered. No phone calls please. However, since we are active around the world in the field of public health, we may wish to retain your CV in our database for other/future opportunities, unless you direct us otherwise.

Thank you very much for your interest in Project HOPE and this exciting project opportunity.

opportunities.title: Senior Communications Officer
opportunities.country: Kenya, United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
opportunities.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Programme Scope:

IRC is seeking a Senior Communications Officer to lead the communications function of the What Works to Prevent Violence - Impact at Scale Programme (What Works II) - a global flagship seven-year Programme funded by the UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) to improve prevention and response to violence against women and girls. The What Works II Programme is located within the Violence Prevention and Response Unit (VPRU) at the International Rescue Committee. The consortium delivering the What Works II Programme includes five partners: IRC, Raising Voices, CARE International UK, SD Direct and SAMYA/ Breakthrough. The Programme builds on the success of its predecessor (What Works I) to produce evidence of what works to prevent violence and communicate it to decision-makers and a range of different audiences to influence a more effective, scaled-up global response to end VAWG.

Job Summary:

The Senior Communications Officer will lead and deliver the programme’s communications function, shape its narrative, and strengthen high-impact communications in support of this global flagship initiative. Working closely with the External Engagement and Influencing (EEI) pillar, the role will build the programme’s external and internal communications capacity and support advocacy and influencing efforts that engage key stakeholders and build shared agendas across the wider VAWG prevention field. The role will be responsible for translating research findings and programme evidence into clear, audience-specific messages and formats (such as policy briefs, reports, presentations, and media content) and strategically disseminating to policy makers, implementers, funders, and other stakeholders in order to influence policy, inform practice, secure funding, and build broader awareness and support for GBV prevention efforts. The role will supervise a social media and Digital Officer.

Responsibilities:

  • Communication for advocacy and influencing
    • Serve as the key communications link between the implementation and research consortia, coordinating on products and publications, and delivering the programme’s evidence dissemination strategy.
    • Lead the synthesis and translation of evidence from the grants and studies into easily accessible, engaging, and user-friendly formats for the consortium, VAWG prevention stakeholders, related sectors (e.g. education, climate, humanitarian response), donors, media, and the public.
    • Coordinate with the EEI team, grant managers, and technical advisors to respond to information requests, gather material, and identify trends and highlights for donor visibility products and reporting.
    • Support the planning, delivery, and visibility of What Works II events and conferences (virtual and in person), including briefing packages and visibility materials for high-level visits and donor engagements.
  • Narrative development & strategic messaging
    • Develop communication frameworks and forge strategic partnerships around the release of major communication products, events, commemorations, and milestones.
    • Translate complex technical documents into clear and compelling narratives for external stakeholders.
    • Support policy-related communications as needed.
    • Support programme leadership in developing speaking notes, keynote presentations, thought leadership content, opinion pieces, and strategic messaging.
  • Issues management & crisis communications
    • Lead crisis preparedness and response planning, including the development of crisis communication frameworks, playbooks, and escalation protocols.
    • Provide strategic guidance during sensitive or high-profile situations involving media, regulatory, operational, or reputational risks.
    • Partner with internal stakeholders to develop messaging and stakeholder communications during critical events.
    • Identify opportunities to strengthen programme positioning and proactively work with programme leadership to manage reputational risks.
  • Producing and managing multimedia and communications content
    • Produce multimedia and communications content tailored to political, academic, and activist audiences.
    • Lead internal communications priorities, including producing and disseminating the quarterly newsletter.
    • Source photography, case studies, and field evidence; identify photography opportunities; support the hiring of freelance photographers and videographers, ensuring adherence to informed-consent principles; manage content-collection shoots as needed.
    • Produce or project-manage graphic design and formatting support for donor and public-facing materials (reports, briefs, templates).
    • Ensure that all materials adhere to the What Works II Programmes branding requirements and applicable donor requirements.
    • Compile digital media metrics and communications achievements for quarterly donor reporting.

Line Management:

  • Supervise the Social Media and Digital Officer, with oversight of:
    • Social media management (X/Twitter, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Facebook).
    • What Works II website management.

Requirements:

  • A bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, English, public relations or another related field from an accredited university.
  • Experience in, or familiarity with development and/or humanitarian programming and operating in an emergency context.
  • Willingness and ability to travel to visit field-sites and document findings.
  • Knowledge of/experience with graphic design and social media photography, and videography.
  • Fluent written and spoken English required. Knowledge of French or Arabic an added advantage.

Experience:

  • A minimum of 6-8 years of professional experience in a similar role.
  • Experience in a communications role and demonstrate experience of developing public/ audience facing documents/ content.
  • Experience of using social media for communications and advocacy
  • Excellent IT skills, including Advanced Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and SharePoint. Including experience with communication related AI packages.
  • Experience working with quantitative and digital metrics data (desirable)
  • Experience of using digital analytics tools and good analytical skills
  • Excellent organizational skills
  • Proven ability to manage a heavy and fluctuating workload
  • Proven ability to manage conflicting demands of a large cross-organizational team
  • Proven ability to prioritize own workload
  • Proven experience in organization of events/workshops
  • Results orientated
  • Knowledge or experience working in donor funded programmes

Working Environment:

Standard office work environment on a hybrid basis, with periodic travel to the field to visit programme activities or events.

This is a hybrid position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.

This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in United Kingdom and Kenya.

Compensation: (Pay Rate: £52,210-£61,999/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

Equal Opportunity Employer: IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

opportunities.title: IT Project Manager (TIC Single Data Entry)
opportunities.description:
We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.

Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.

Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.
We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.
MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centres.

Context:

The Single Data Entry (SDE) project is a transformational initiative led by MSF to significantly improve the quality and efficiency of supply chain data entry in stock management processes (cargo reception, order preparation, stock count) across multiple operational centres (OC). The solution being developed revolves around a mobile application leveraging QR codes and AI-powered OCR technologies to automate data capture and integrate with MSF’s existing supply chain systems. The project team is looking for an application manager to bring technical expertise and a capacity to coordinate with IT organizations across OCs to execute its test & deployment strategy and define the support model.

Mission:

The IT Project Manager is pivotal in developing and implementing the SDE solution to meet high standards and integrate smoothly with existing systems and stock management tools. Responsible for the successful delivery of IT solutions supporting the SDE program, this role ensures both business,

functional and technical requirements are efficiently met. The IT Project Manager will work closely with diverse stakeholders to develop and implement tailored solutions, ensuring these are delivered on time, within budget, and aligned with strategic objectives. In this role, you will provide technical leadership within the SDE core team, manage the product development, and collaborate with technical experts from the four cosponsoring Operational Centers (OCs) of the SDE program.

We are seeking an experienced IT Project Manager with a robust background in software development and a proven track record in leading mobile application projects. Join us at Médecins Sans Frontières and contribute your expertise!

Occasional travel to the field or the Geneva Office can be expected.

Scope of responsibilities

  • Collaborate with IT working groups from co-sponsoring OCs to ensure building a viable, maintainable and deployable solution
  • Lead end-to-end planning and delivery of the product development project
  • Collaborate and build relationship with suppliers to enable project success
  • Monitor project progress and performance, identify variances, and drive corrective actions to keep delivery on track.
  • Identify, assess and manage risks, issues, blockers and dependencies, including escalation where needed.
  • Ensure readiness and support go-live of the solution in MSF missions
  • Coordinate testing, defect resolution, environment readiness, release planning and go-live activities, in collaboration with the Deployment Manager.
  • Promote adherence to quality standards, security requirements, compliance needs, and operational readiness expectations.
  • Lead workshop and activities to define the operating model and ensure successful transition to business-as-usual after implementation

opportunities.title: Final Project Evaluation of the UNESCO Project “AI Ready Flemish Public Administration”
opportunities.publisher: UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
opportunities.description:
The UNESCO Science Sector is seeking an evaluation team to conduct the final evaluation of the "AI Ready Flemish Public Administration" project, funded by the European Commission's Directorate-General for Structural Reform Support (DG REFORM) through the EU's Technical Support Instrument (TSI).

The main purpose of the evaluation is to generate findings and recommendations on the project's results in supporting the European Commission's efforts to enhance the AI readiness of the Flemish public administration. The evaluation will provide accountability for the use of resources and the results achieved by assessing the project's performance against its original objectives, while also capturing lessons learned to inform future EU–UNESCO initiatives in the field of AI readiness.

The evaluation will assess the project's achievements to date, identifying what has been effective, under what conditions, and in which contexts, as well as its contributions to the implementation of ethical AI policies and its potential for long-term impact. It will cover all project components, outcomes, activities across the beneficiary entities, and knowledge products. In addition, it will examine the main challenges encountered during project implementation, as well as the project's governance and management arrangements. The evaluation period will cover October 2024 to September 2026.

opportunities.title: Volunteer Advocacy and Communications Officer
opportunities.description:
Project Description

I Have Rights provides legal information to asylum seekers on the island of Samos, prepares applicants for their asylum interviews, holds legal information workshops, appeals procedures for rejected applicants and accompanies applicants to interviews. As a political organisation, I Have Rights speaks out about the situation on Samos and actively advocates for policy and practice reforms that are responsible for human rights violations in both Samos and Europe.

The organisation on Samos consists of a project coordinator, a Greek lawyer, one senior case worker, one to two volunteer case workers and one volunteer responsible for communications and advocacy. The remote team consists of the board members, interpreters and various volunteers of the Task Forces. The organisation aims towards flat hierarchies; the structures are still evolving, and we would like to welcome you to play an active role in shaping the project.

I Have Rights is committed to safeguarding the well-being of everyone we work with. Team members are expected to uphold our policies, including our Code of Conduct, and adhere to the 'do no harm' principle in all their actions. You can find our policies here.

Detailed information on the project can be found at: www.ihaverights.eu.

Role & Responsibilities

  • Working with the Legal and Team Coordinator to implement our advocacy and communications work

  • Drafting of reports and briefings

  • Networking with stakeholders to achieve our goals

opportunities.title: Impact and Accountability Officer-EU Projects
opportunities.description:
About CIVICUS

CIVICUS exists to defend people power. As a growing global alliance of over 17,000 members in over 180 countries, we work together to monitor violations of basic civic freedoms, call out the perpetrators of violations and strengthen the power of people to organise by supporting a more accountable, effective and innovative civil society. We strive to promote excluded voices, especially from the global south.

About the Role

The Impact & Accountability Officer for European Union (EU) projects collaborate closely with the I&A Cluster Lead, the Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) focal person at Hivos, and other Consortium members. The incumbent contributes to the development and execution of a comprehensive MEAL System tailored to meet EU grant management standards for both the EU System for an Enabling Environment for Civil Society (EU SEE) and the Strengthening Global CSO Umbrella Organisations projects (SGUO). The role also involves ensuring that the MEAL systems are fully aligned with CIVICUS' Integrated Results Framework.

In addition to overseeing the implementation of effective data-driven decision-making processes within CIVICUS and its partner organizations, the I&A Officer is responsible for leading the adoption of advanced data analytics, automation, and robust data science techniques to enhance the quality, efficiency, and predictive value of MEAL activities. The role holder will promote data literacy, Knowledge Management, Learning, and Adaptive Management initiatives among consortium members, CIVICUS Networks and partners. The role holder is responsible for ensuring that CIVICUS' organizational learning and constituency accountability practices are embedded in project implementation to foster a culture of continuous improvement and transparency.

Key Requirements

  1. A bachelor’s degree or Diploma in Monitoring, Evaluation, Economics Accountability and Learning, Statistics, Data Science, Computer Science, International Development, Development Management, or equivalent. A master’s degree is strongly preferred.
  2. Minimum of 5 years' professional experience in MEAL, with at least 3 years supporting European Union (EU)/European Commission (EC) or other major institutional donor-funded projects.
  3. Fluency in English is required; proficiency in French, Spanish, or Arabic is an added advantage.
  4. Strong knowledge of EU grant management requirements, donor compliance, reporting standards, and Results-Oriented Monitoring (ROM) principles.
  5. Demonstrated expertise in results-based and participatory MEL approaches, including methodologies such as Outcome Harvesting, Contribution Analysis and Contribution Analysis, Most Significant Change, and mixed-methods research approaches.
  6. Strong analytical and quantitative research skills, with proficiency in data analysis software such as SPSS, STATA, R, SurveyCTO, KoboToolbox, Power BI, SmartSheets, and advanced Microsoft Excel.
  7. Proven experience managing evaluations, coordinating donors and organizational reporting, and translating evidence into actionable recommendations.
  8. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with diverse stakeholders and communicate complex data in an accessible manner.
  9. Solid understanding of civil society, human rights, and international development, including the challenges faced by marginalized and historically excluded communities.
  10. Experience applying qualitative data analysis techniques, including the analysis of large volumes of textual and feedback data, with knowledge of GIS/geospatial analysis considered an advantage.
  11. Strong organizational, project management, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively across multicultural, virtual, and cross-time-zone teams.
  12. Experience working with historically excluded communities such as rural groups, indigenous peoples, women, youth, and LGBTQI+.
  13. Experience with geospatial analysis (GIS) for mapping civic space trends or project coverage.
  14. Familiarity with data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR) and ethical data management practices in the context of civil society data.

opportunities.title: Education Officer
opportunities.description:
Details

Mission and objectives

Le Bureau de pays de l’UNICEF au Maroc accompagne le Gouvernement dans la mise en œuvre des priorités nationales en matière d’éducation, avec un accent particulier sur l’équité, l’inclusion, la qualité des apprentissages, la prévention du décrochage scolaire, le préscolaire, l’éducation non formelle et le développement des compétences des enfants et des adolescents. Dans ce cadre, la Section Education travaille en étroite collaboration avec le Ministère de l’Éducation Nationale, du Préscolaire et des Sports, aux niveaux central et territorial au travers d’un partenariat avec 5 AREFs, ainsi qu’avec le Ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication lorsque les interventions concernent les parcours éducatifs, l’épanouissement, l’engagement et les compétences des adolescents et des jeunes. Le/la Volontaire des Nations Unies apportera un appui programmatique, technique et de coordination à la Section Education afin de renforcer le suivi des activités, la consolidation des résultats, la documentation des bonnes pratiques et la cohérence des interventions avec les priorités nationales et le programme de coopération de l’UNICEF.

Context

Appuyer la mise en œuvre, le suivi et la coordination des programmes Education de l’UNICEF au Maroc, en appui aux priorités nationales visant l’amélioration de l’accès, de la qualité, de l’équité et de l’inclusion dans l’éducation. L’affectation contribuera plus particulièrement au suivi des initiatives menées avec le Ministère de l’Éducation Nationale, du Préscolaire et des Sports, ainsi qu’aux actions conjointes avec le Ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication lorsqu’elles contribuent aux objectifs éducatifs, au développement des compétences et à la continuité des parcours d’apprentissage des enfants et des adolescents.

Task description

Sous la supervision directe de la Spécialiste Education, le/la Volontaire des Nations Unies effectuera les tâches suivantes : • Appuyer la coordination opérationnelle et programmatique avec le Ministère de l’Éducation Nationale, du Préscolaire et des Sports, notamment pour le suivi des activités inscrites dans les plans de travail et cadres de coopération convenus avec l’UNICEF ; • Contribuer à la coordination avec le Ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication pour les initiatives liées à l’épanouissement, aux compétences de vie, à l’engagement des adolescents et des jeunes et à la continuité des parcours d’apprentissage ; • Assurer le suivi régulier de la mise en œuvre des activités Education, y compris la col-lecte et la consolidation des informations auprès des partenaires, des prestataires et des équipes régionales, selon les besoins ; • Contribuer à la préparation, la revue et la consolidation des rapports de mise en œuvre, comptes rendus de réunions, notes de suivi, tableaux de bord et documents de synthèse relatifs aux programmes Education ; • Appuyer la revue, la finalisation et l’organisation des outils, guides, supports de formation et documents techniques produits dans le cadre des interventions Education ; • Soutenir la documentation, la capitalisation et la valorisation des initiatives mises en œuvre, en coordination avec les équipes Communication, Plaidoyer, Suivi évaluation et Partenariats de l’UNICEF ; • Contribuer à l’organisation de réunions, ateliers, missions de terrain et consultations avec les partenaires institutionnels, les acteurs territoriaux, les enfants, les adolescents, les jeunes et les communautés, selon les besoins du programme ; • Effectuer toute autre tâche pertinente demandée par la superviseure, en lien avec les priorités de la Section Education. Résultats attendus : • Le suivi des activités Education est renforcé et les informations relatives à leur mise en œuvre sont consolidées de manière régulière. • Les rapports, notes de suivi, comptes rendus et documents de synthèse relatifs aux pro-grammes Education sont préparés, revus ou consolidés dans les délais requis. • La coordination avec le Ministère de l’Éducation Nationale, du Préscolaire et des Sports et, le cas échéant, avec le Ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication, est fa-cilitée et documentée. • Les outils, guides, supports de formation et documents techniques produits dans le cadre des interventions Education sont organisés, revus et finalisés selon les besoins. • Les bonnes pratiques, leçons apprises et résultats des initiatives Education sont documentés et valorisés en coordination avec les équipes concernées de l’UNICEF.

Eligibility criteria

Age

18 - 80

Required experience

3 years

Nationality

Candidate must be a national, legal resident or hold refugee status in the country of assignment.

Assignment requirements

Relevant experience

3 years

Languages

Arabic, Level: Fluent, Required French, Level: Fluent, Required English, Level: Fluent, Desirable

Required education level

Bachelor's degree in Diplôme universitaire en éducation, sciences de l’éducation, sciences sociales, développement international, politiques publiques, gestion de projet ou tout autre domaine pertinent.

Competencies and values

• Établir et entretenir des partenariats • Cultiver la conscience de soi et démontrer un sens de l’éthique • S’atteler à obtenir des résultats tangibles • Innover et épouser le changement • Gérer l’ambiguïté et la complexité • Penser et agir de manière stratégique • Travailler de façon collaborative

Skills and experience

 Au minimum 3 ans d’expérience dans la gestion, la coordination, le suivi ou l’appui à des programmes/projets dans le domaine de l’éducation, du développement de l’enfant, de l’inclusion, de la formation ou du développement des compétences.  Expérience de travail avec des partenaires institutionnels, notamment les ministères, administrations publiques, académies régionales, organisations de la société civile ou agences des Nations Unies.  Bonnes capacités rédactionnelles (développement de projets et rapports) en arabe, en français ; l’anglais est un atout majeur.  Communication interpersonnelle et aisance dans le travail avec les partenaires institution-nels, les acteurs éducatifs, les enfants, les adolescents et les jeunes.  Capacité à s’adapter à différents interlocuteurs et à travailler dans des environnements complexes  Bonne maîtrise des outils informatiques, notamment Microsoft Office, courrier électro-nique, internet et outils collaboratifs. Une expérience dans l’utilisation de tableaux de bord, d’outils de suivi ou de logiciels de mise en page/Canva serait un atout.  Avoir un intérêt à servir les enfants, pour le volontariat comme un mécanisme durable de développement et pour le système des Nations Unies.

Area(s) of expertise

Disability, other social inclusion aspects, Project management, programme development, strategy, General and specialised medicine

Living conditions and remarks

Le Maroc est un pays à revenu intermédiaire comptant une population d’environ 38 millions d’habitants. Au cours de la dernière décennie, le pays a connu d’importantes transitions politiques, institutionnelles et démographiques. Le climat à Rabat et dans les zones côtières est doux, avec des étés chauds et des hivers courts, humides et pluvieux. Bien que l’arabe soit la langue officielle, le français est largement parlé par une grande partie de la population. Des logements (appartements, studios, villas) sont disponibles à des prix raisonnables. Les services bancaires, les transports, les soins de santé et les moyens de communication sont facilement accessibles. Les transports publics, notamment le réseau ferroviaire (qui bénéficie d’un bon niveau de sécurité), sont abordables et relient les principaux centres urbains du pays. Les taxis sont largement disponibles dans les grandes villes telles que Casablanca et Rabat. Ces villes offrent également une variété d’activités culturelles et de loisirs, notamment des cinémas, des restaurants, ainsi que des possibilités de shopping dans des boutiques modernes ou dans les souks, marchés traditionnels en plein air où les vendeurs proposent une large gamme de produits artisanaux locaux. La cuisine marocaine jouit d’une reconnaissance internationale auprès des amateurs de gastronomie. Toutes les commodités occidentales (produits alimentaires, vêtements, restaurants, etc.) sont disponibles dans les grandes villes. Étant donné qu’il s’agit d’une mission de Volontaire des Nations Unies (VNU) national, le/la Volontaire des Nations Unies sera responsable de l’organisation de son propre logement ainsi que de ses autres besoins essentiels liés à la vie quotidienne.

Les VNU nationaux bénéficient d’une couverture d’assurance conformément aux dispositions applicables. Conditions de service 1. Avant le début de l’affectation Allocation forfaitaire d’entrée (Entry Lump Sum) : 350 USD Indemnité de réinstallation (Relocation Allowance) : 175 USD au début et à la fin de l’affectation, lorsque le lieu d’affectation est situé en dehors de la distance raisonnable de déplacement domicile-travail, conformément à la détermination de l’UNV. 2. Pendant l’affectation Allocation mensuelle de subsistance du Volontaire (VLA) : 13 179,16 MAD par mois. Apprentissage et développement des compétences : Accès aux ressources d’apprentissage et de développement professionnel proposées par l’UNV. Congé annuel : 2,5 jours par mois de service. Assurance : Une couverture complète couvrant les soins de santé, l’assurance vie et les actes malveillants pour le/la Volontaire des Nations Unies, ainsi qu’une couverture médicale pour jusqu’à trois personnes à charge éligibles. Les critères détaillés d’éligibilité sont précisés dans les Conditions de Service de l’UNV.

opportunities.title: Assessment Specialist - Analysis for Afghanistan, based in Mazar-i- Sharif
opportunities.description:
BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organization manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis, GIS and remote sensing. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO with headquarters based in Paris and presence in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, which allows IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support in its fields of intervention.

We are currently looking for an Assessment Specialist to contribute to cross-cutting analysis and thematic priorities.

Department: IMPACT

Position: Assessment Specialist - Analysis

Contract duration: 6 months (extension possible depending on funding)

Starting Date: 28 June 2026

Location: Mazar-i-Sharif, Afghanistan (with travel to Kabul and other locations).

COUNTRY PROFILE

The humanitarian response in Afghanistan remains one of the largest in the world, with 21.9 million people identified as in need of assistance in the 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan. The country is particularly vulnerable to climate change, with drought conditions affecting agriculture and livelihoods. Natural disasters, including flooding and earthquakes, remain prevalent – often causing displacement, damaging and destroying shelter and services, and disrupting livelihoods. Conflict remains a risk, with recent increase in conflict activity between Afghanistan and Pakistan. With millions of refugees in neighbouring countries, including Iran and Pakistan, forced return of refugees is also a driver of needs in the country.

Alongside this, since the De facto Authorities took control of the government in 2021, a range of restrictive policies have significantly restricted the rights of women and girls in society – leading to increased marginalisation and protection risks. The economic situation remains poor and authorities lack resources to run effective public services, with reliance on humanitarian assistance. As the USA was a major aid donor in Afghanistan, their withdrawal of all aid funding had a significant effect, for example on the closures of health centres. With political positioning of donor governments restricting a full development approach, a basic human needs response is increasingly complementing the humanitarian response across Afghanistan.

Against this backdrop, IMPACT Initiatives is planning a range of research activities to support an evidence- and needs-based humanitarian response. The Assessment Specialist will work to provide timely analysis from these products, provide longitudinal and cross-research analysis in line with thematic priorities, contribute to global analysis products, and combine IMPACT research with secondary data analysis for enhanced analysis products.

POSITION PROFILE

IMPACT Initiatives in Afghanistan is recruiting an Assessment Specialist to support its work in promoting evidence-based decisions across the aid response in Afghanistan (both humanitarian and basic human needs).

The candidate will perform a range of analysis tasks both supporting research units and teams, leading on certain research projects, and supporting IMPACT in developing thematic expertise through cross-cutting analysis, longitudinal analysis, and combining IMPACT data with secondary data sources.

This may involve both short-term and longer-term initiatives, ensuring that analysis from key research products is provided in a timely fashion, for example geographic or thematic briefs from the Multi-Sector Needs Assessment.

The Assessment Specialist will be required to engage within the aid architecture to both guide the initiation of analysis products and to disseminate effectively to a range of stakeholders.

RESPONSIBILITIES

The Assessment Specialist’s responsibilities will include:

DEVELOPMENT AND DELIVERY OF ANALYSIS PRODUCTS

  • Map opportunities within the response for analysis products to guide policy and programme decision-making.
  • Work with Research Units and Teams, and Field Teams, to identify opportunities for analysis from IMPACT’s research portfolio and provide support to or lead the process to deliver timely analysis briefs following data collection.
  • Identify opportunities for longitudinal analysis or analysis linking multiple IMPACT research products, in particular in-line with thematic priorities outlined in the country strategy.
  • Contribute to longer-term analysis pieces designed to inform strategic decision-making within the aid response.
  • Ensure that IMPACT Afghanistan effectively contributes to IMPACT global analysis products.

DEVELOPMENT OF RESEARCH PRODUCTS

  • Where identified by the (Deputy) Country Representative, support research design for IMPACT research products to link findings to identified research priorities.
  • Lead the development of primary data collection research cycles as necessary designed to support specific analysis products or timely analysis in response to changes in context (including sudden onset shocks).

CAPACITY STRENGTHENING

  • Work with national staff within the research units and teams to identify staff with potential to develop analysis skills and provide on-the-job training opportunities for them to develop skills (in alignment with line managers).
  • As required, support IMPACT capacity strengthening activities for Afghan organizations, as included in funded projects.

EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT

  • In coordination with the (Deputy) Country Representative, represent IMPACT/REACH with donors, partners, and the wider aid community in Afghanistan.
  • Engage with operational stakeholders in the aid response to determine where additional analysis could support their work and ensure effective dissemination.
  • Support IMPACT dissemination events as required, through producing presentations, summary briefs, or meeting reports.

STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION

  • Under the guidance of the (Deputy) Country Representative, support the development of the team workplan, including engagement and involvement with various technical and coordination forums;
  • Work with key clusters, partner organizations and working groups to understand the various relevant information gaps within Afghanistan and identify how and what analysis could fill these gaps.
  • Contribute to the development and implementation of the REACH Afghanistan country strategy, including coordinating with the heads of other research and analysis units and teams;
  • Develop and implement dissemination strategies to strengthen the impact of analysis products;

The Assessment Specialist will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Work experience Demonstratable relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as programme management, evaluation and assessments;
  • Research skills Excellent quantitative and qualitative research design, data collection, and data analysis experience required;
  • Analysis skills – Demonstratable ability to analyse a range of complex datasets and produce compelling analysis in multiple formats.
  • Familiarity with aid system Good understanding of the aid system and the research community. Prior experience with humanitarian coordination forums preferred;
  • Experience of work with climate change and/or gender issues is desirable, whether from a research, analysis, or programmatic perspective;
  • Experience in geographical region Past experience in the region/supporting is desirable;
  • Communication/reporting skills Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting, presenting, and reviewing;
  • Cross-cultural work environment Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility and work independently;
  • Academic qualifications A Master’s degree in a relevant discipline is preferred. However, significant relevant work experience can be considered.
  • Software skills Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software an asset
  • Security environment Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment.
  • Language skills Fluency in English required, competency in Dari or Pashto is an asset.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

  • For this position, salary between 3’050€ and 3’100 monthly before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
  • Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
  • Affiliation to French Social security (CFE) + health Complementary (Mobility Benefits) + Repatriation assistance (SOS International) + Private Pension Fund.
  • Flight tickets every six months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
  • R&R after eight weeks, flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance
  • Contribution to the transportation of luggage: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
  • Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
  • Predeparture induction - three days at IMPACT Initiatives’ HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training (depending on previous inductions and security trainings taken);
  • IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff, and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

opportunities.title: Senior Information Management Officer for OPT, based in Amman
opportunities.description:
BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. We are currently looking for an Information Management Officer (IMO) to support our team in the occupied Palestinian territory (oPt):

Position: Senior Information Management Officer (IMO) Site Management Cluster

Contract duration: 9 months

Starting Date: 24 August 2026

Location: Amman, Jordan

COUNTRY PROFILE

The humanitarian situation in the occupied Palestinian territories (oPt) has reached dire levels, particularly in the Gaza Strip, where ongoing hostilities have resulted in mass displacement, the collapse of basic services, and a near-total breakdown of civilian infrastructure. With 2.1 million people affected, access to food, water, healthcare, and shelter remains critically limited. The scale of destruction and access constraints have created an environment where humanitarian needs far exceed available resources. At the same time, rising tensions and violence in the West Bank have severely impacted freedom of movement, livelihoods, and overall humanitarian conditions.

In response, IMPACT Initiatives is implementing a range of activities to support a needs-based, evidence-driven humanitarian response. This includes multi-sectoral household assessments, displacement site mapping, and market assessments across Gaza to inform coordination, operational planning, and strategic decision-making.

POSITION PROFILE

Under the supervision of IMPACT’s Research Manager, the Senior Information Management Officer (SIMO) will lead on the aggregation of service and infrastructure mapping from response partners across the Gaza Strip. In coordination with Acted, UNDP and UN Habitat, the SIMO will be responsible for identifying valuable service and infrastructure data from local, national and international actors as well as UN Agencies in order to provide a comprehensive overview of ongoing humanitarian programming across the Strip. This role offers a unique opportunity to directly contribute to the response’s effectiveness by supporting evidence-based planning and coordination. The IMO is expected to engage independently with partners and be confident articulating objectives to a range of audiences. The position requires strong technical skills in data management and analysis, excellent coordination and communication abilities, and a flexible, solutions-oriented mindset. An interest in humanitarian coordination and contextual developments in oPt is strongly preferred.

RESPONSIBILITIES

The Senior Information Management Officer’s responsibilities include:

Co-ordination and planning

  • Engage clusters, INGOs, NNGOs and CSOs to generate support and buy in for the service and infrastructure mapping
  • Generate an understanding of the information landscape within oPt actors, identifying which organisation or cluster has data on which services and infrastructure
  • Engage other coordinating bodies such as OCHA and act as IMPACT focal point across early recovering information management discussions
  • Promote the use of inter-operable technologies among partners;
  • Provide information outputs in the local language wherever feasible.
  • Receive data from partner organisations

Data quality control

  • Generate sectoral specific data quality standards, working with information management officers in partner organisations to understand sector specific data quality requirements and document them
  • Generate data quality scripts to assess incoming data for quality issues
  • Generate shared data standards, including naming, data formatting and data taxonomies (for the standard naming of e.g. health care facility types across organizations)
  • Generate data quality key performance indicators
  • Work with partner organisations to address issues with the data they have provided
  • Promote data quality standards across partner organisations and build a culture of data integrity and accuracy within the response.

Data visualization

  • Visualise the GIS and structured data shared by partners in a dashboard (using common data visualsation tools, e.g. R Shiny or PowerBI)
  • Ensure coherent style and design across the dashboard
  • Facilitate analysis through the dashboard user interface
  • Collaborate with UN Habitat, Acted and UNDP to ensure data visualisations align to their needs

The Information Management Officer will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners, or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Excellent academic qualifications, including a Master’s degree in relevant discipline (such maths and statistics, information science, geography), or an equivalent combination of relevant training and experience in humanitarian related activities in disaster or conflict situation;
  • 4 years of relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as information management, GIS, monitoring and evaluation, research design and analysis, etc.;
  • Sound judgment and emotional intelligence in high-pressure or sensitive situations. Possesses strong interpersonal awareness and the ability to respond constructively to feedback and shifting priorities;
  • Knowledge of the humanitarian community, specifically with regards to inter-agency coordination;
  • Experience in the context of partnership building and consensual decision-making;
  • Proven ability to conceptualize, develop, plan monitor and evaluate IM in relation to programming, as well as to teach skills and build team capacity;
  • Excellent writing, communication and negotiation skills; ability to prepare clear and concise reports;
  • Understanding of different data collection methodologies and their strengths and weaknesses, to be able to assess quality/reliability of secondary sources and to advice on potential areas of improvement;
  • Ability to compile, triangulate and holistically analyse diverse and large datasets;
  • Experience with handling confidential and sensitive data and demonstrated;
  • Ability to work effectively and harmoniously in a team and in the inter-agency context with colleagues from a variety of cultures and professional backgrounds;
  • Resilience, stress tolerance and ability to work under difficult conditions;
  • Fluently spoken and written English is mandatory. Arabic an asset;
  • Data capture and analysis :
  • MS Excel (Essential) : Ability to create macros; Strong knowledge of statistical, conditional, and text-based functions;
  • Web Design (Asset): HTML, PHP, ASP; Basic understanding of web-based applications
  • Mapping (Essential) : ArcGIS, QGIS, Understanding of geospatial data management, analysis, and map making processess.
  • Data programming (essential): R, Python, ability to write data cleaning and analysis pipeline scripts, GitHub or version control experience an asset.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

  • For this position, salary between 2’580 CHF and 2’640 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
  • Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
  • Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance.
  • Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
  • Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
  • Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
  • Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training;
  • IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.
