opportunities.title: Research Manager - Economy, Markets & Livelihoods for Afghanistan, based in Kabul
opportunities.description:
BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis, GIS and remote sensing. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO with headquarters based in Paris and presence in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, which allows IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support in its fields of intervention.

We are currently looking for a Research Manager to scope out and set-up a new Research Team focussing on the Economy, Markets, and Livelihoods

Department: IMPACT

Position: Research Manager

Contract duration: 5 months

Starting Date: ASAP

Location: Kabul, Afghanistan

COUNTRY PROFILE

The humanitarian response in Afghanistan remains one of the largest in the world, with 21.9 million people identified as in need of assistance in the 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan. The country is particularly vulnerable to climate change, with drought conditions affecting agriculture and livelihoods. Natural disasters, including flooding and earthquakes, remain prevalent – often causing displacement, damaging and destroying shelter and services, and disrupting livelihoods. Conflict remains a risk, with recent increase in conflict activity between Afghanistan and Pakistan. With millions of refugees in neighbouring countries, including Iran and Pakistan, forced return of refugees is also a driver of needs in the country.

Alongside this, since the De facto Authorities took control of the government in 2021, a range of restrictive policies have significantly restricted the rights of women and girls in society – leading to increased marginalisation and protection risks. The economic situation remains poor and authorities lack resources to run effective public services, with reliance on humanitarian assistance. As the USA was a major aid donor in Afghanistan, their withdrawal of all aid funding had a significant effect, for example on the closures of health centres. With political positioning of donor governments restricting a full development approach, a basic human needs response is increasingly complementing the humanitarian response across Afghanistan.

Against this backdrop, IMPACT Initiatives is planning a range of research activities to support an evidence- and needs-based humanitarian response. The IMPACT Deputy Country Representative (DCR) supports the Country Representative (CR) in overseeing programme strategy and implementation internally, as well as external representation of IMPACT.

POSITION PROFILE

Following the development of our new Country Strategy, IMPACT Afghanistan is planning to establish a new research team with the aim of providing relevant information to humanitarian and basic human needs stakeholders linked to the economy, markets and livelihoods in Afghanistan.

IMPACT Afghanistan is therefore seeking an experienced Research Manager with knowledge of assessment and analysis, to scope out a programme of work for this new team, through internal and external consultations. The Research Manager will be responsible for drafting concept notes and research ToRs that can be used to solicit funding for the start-up of the team.

The Research Manager will be responsible for building an understanding of the relevant aid strategies existing in Afghanistan and identifying relevant data and research gaps that could be filled. This will involve connections with international and national NGOs (including members of Cash Consortium of Afghanistan), the UN, and donors. The Research Manager will review existing research in Afghanistan (including the MSNA and Joint Market Monitoring Initiative) and also connect across IMPACT to understand similar research being conducted elsewhere that could be adapted for the Afghanistan context.

RESPONSIBILITIES

The Research Manager’s responsibilities will include:

CONTEXTUAL UNDERSTANDING

  • Assess relevant strategic, analytical, and operational documents to develop an understanding of the current priorities relating to the economy, markets and livelihoods for the aid response in Afghanistan.
  • Mapping existing IMPACT data, other research, and other relevant information sources to understand relevant areas for potential assessment and research.
  • Connecting with national and international NGOs, UN colleagues, and the donor community to understand their priorities and to identify where IMPACT research could support their programmes and strategies.
  • Provide SMT and other staff members with key updates from these efforts.

DEPARTMENT STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT

  • Engage with IMPACT colleagues in HQ and in other country programmes to identify existing assessment and research tools that could be adapted for Afghanistan.
  • Develop a series of concept notes that can be shared with prospective partners or donors, to seek funding for the set-up for the new team.
  • Develop/draft relevant research ToRs, enabling technical discussion and approval of potential research projects.
  • Develop a light-touch team strategy that could subsequently be further developed based on the eventual set-up and staffing of research activities.
  • Coordinate with staff in the Cash Consortium of Afghanistan to identify potential assessment and research opportunities for the future of the Consortium.

RESEARCH MANAGEMENT

  • As necessary, support the Humanitarian Coordination and Monitoring Unit in the delivery of research and analysis linked to Joint Market Monitoring Initiative and the Cash Consortium of Afghanistan.
  • As required, work with the cross-cutting analysis team to support the develop of analysis products linked to the economy, markets, and livelihoods, which can better position IMPACT Afghanistan in this thematic field.

The Research Manager will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Work experience Demonstratable relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as programme management, evaluation and assessments. Experience working with development responses is an advantage;
  • Thematic experience Able to showcase experience in working with economy and market data in an aid environment’
  • Research skills Excellent quantitative and qualitative research design, data collection, and data analysis experience required;
  • Familiarity with aid system Good understanding of the aid system and the research community.
  • Management experience Demonstrated team management skills, including remote management;
  • Experience in geographical region Past experience in the region/supporting is desirable;
  • Communication/reporting skills Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting and reviewing;
  • Cross-cultural work environment Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility and work independently;
  • Academic qualifications A Master’s degree in a relevant discipline is preferred. However, significant relevant work experience can be considered.
  • Software skills Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software an asset
  • Security environment Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment.
  • Language skills Fluency in English required, competency in Dari or Pashto is an asset.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

  • For this position, salary between 3’050€ and 3’100 monthly before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
  • Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
  • Affiliation to French Social security (CFE) + health Complementary (Mobility Benefits) + Repatriation assistance (SOS International) + Private Pension Fund.
  • Flight tickets every six months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
  • R&R after eight weeks, flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance
  • Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
  • Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
  • Predeparture induction - three days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training (depending on previous inductions and security trainings taken);
  • IMPACT prioritises the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

opportunities.title: MEAL Officer (Syria - Latakia)
opportunities.description:
Job Title: MEAL Officer

Job location: Syria – Lattakia

Reports to: MEAL Coordinator

Jobe Style : Full Time

JOB SUMMARY

The primary responsibility of the MEAL Officer is to support MEAL Coordinator to implement the MEAL plans and ensure implementation of robust system and to provide real time analytics to guide the quality of the program and implementation.

MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Working under direct supervision of MEAL Coordinator:

- Contribute to the development of the MEAL framework.

- Contribute to the design and development of new tools as required (questionnaires, Satisfaction Survey, Pre-Post tests- Checklists…etc) which are needed to assess all projects aspects and measuring all planned indicators.

- Contribute to building the capacity of the MEAL department.

- Conduct field visits to monitor projects activities via observation and stakeholders’ interviews.

- Maintain and compile a lesson learned database and share these lessons with the program team in timely manner.

- Work with MEAL Coordinator to ensure MEAL Management Information System are used for all MEAL activities.

- Contribute towards all MEAL reports including needs assessment.. etc.

- Ensure compliance for all MEAL participants and beneficiaries of the projects in terms of data privacy, informed and signed consent and data protection.

- Ensure all relevant MEAL inputs are collected according to specified means of verification in timely manner.

- Oversee the implementation and effectiveness of UITYD’s CFM, ensuring it is accessible, transparent, and responsive.

- Manage and document complaints and feedback, ensuring prompt response and resolution in coordination with relevant departments.

- Analyze complaints and feedback data to provide insights for program improvement.

QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS

should have the following skills, education, and experience:

- Bachelor’s degree in social sciences, computer science, engineering, Development Studies, or a related

field.

- Minimum of 2-3 years of experience in accountability, MEAL, or related roles within the humanitarian

sector.

- Knowledge of and demonstrated practical experience MEAL methodologies (particularly appropriate quantitative and qualitative research methods) data analyst and report writing.

- Advanced skills with MS office and Power Bi.

- Experience designing applications/forms with Kobo.

- Experience in managing complaints and feedback mechanisms and engaging with affected populations.

- Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to facilitate discussions and gather

community insights.

- Ability to analyze feedback trends and produce reports for program improvement.

- Ability to write a report with English.

- Native Arabic speaker with intermediate English proficiency.

ABOUT UITYD

- UITYD is a local medical non-profit organization Co-funded by Med Global and multiple donors; it registered in Turkey in the year 2020, working on the front lines of crisis relief in Syria and Turkey to alleviate suffering and save lives, It provides health services and rebuilding healthcare to people in need and supports doctors and medical professionals by provides professional and educational pieces of training to physicians, and delivers medicine and medical supplies to hospitals and vulnerable families, including refugees and displaced persons, in disaster and underserved regions and offers assistance to people based on need, irrespective of race, religion, gender, or political affiliation, UITYD is composed of medical and public health volunteers of diverse backgrounds.

CODE OF CONDUCT

- UITYD Code of Conduct reflects the profession’s core set of beliefs and values of care, respect, trust, and integrity. These beliefs and values are fundamental to UITYD employees, volunteers, interns, consultants, and contractors to guide their practice and conduct. The Code is organized into categories, as follows:

- 2. Always act with fairness, honesty, integrity, and openness; respect the opinions of others and treat all with equality and dignity without regard to gender, race, color, creed, ancestry, place of origin, political beliefs, religion, marital status, disability, age, or sexual orientation.

- 3. Provide a positive and valued experience for those receiving service within and outside UITYD.

CHILD PROTECTION POLICY

Child abuse in all forms is unacceptable to UITYD, which recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. UITYD is committed to ensuring a child-safe environment and is applying a zero-tolerance approach towards any kind of child abuse and exploitation.

DISCRIMINATION, ABUSE, AND HARASSMENT POLICY

UITYD provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and expressly prohibits and will not tolerate any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (sexual or otherwise), based upon race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, gender, age, marital status, citizenship status, disability, or military status. UITYD employees and related personnel must under no circumstances take part in any form of discrimination, harassment, or abuse (physical, sexual or verbal), intimidation or exploitation, or in any other way infringe the rights of others inside or outside the organization.

opportunities.title: Programme Management Officer, Human Settlements (Readvertisment)
opportunities.description:
(READVERTISMENT: Candidates who have previously applied do not need to reapply)

Functional title: Programme Management Officer, Human Settlements

Duty station of assignment: Istanbul, Türkiye

Contract modality: International ICA

Grade: IICA-3 equivalent

Duration of assignment: 1 year (with possibility of extension)

Closing date for applications: 11 May 2026

Background

The United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) is the United Nations agency mandated by UN General Assembly to promote socially and environmentally sustainable towns and cities with the goal of providing adequate shelter for all. UN-Habitat is a focal agency for the New Urban Agenda's monitoring and implementation. It supports with all partners the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), in particular, Goal 11 of "Making cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable". With its Headquarter in Nairobi, Kenya, UN-Habitat's Regional Programme Division has its Regional Office for Eastern Europe and Central Asia (ROEECA) in Istanbul, Türkiye. ROEECA engages with over 24 countries in Eastern Europe, Western Balkan, Caucasus and Central Asia.

The position is located in ROEECA's Istanbul office. The Programme Management Officer will play a key role in regional programme development, resource mobilization, partnership building and strategic engagement across Eastern Europe and Central Asia. The Programme Management Officer typically oversees a small number of personnel in the region.

Duties and main responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of the Regional Director, the incumbent is responsible for the following duties::

  • Coordinates regional policy and programme development, including the review and analysis of issues and trends, preparation of evaluations, research activities and strategic studies.
  • Develops, implements and evaluates assigned programmes/projects, etc. in close collaboration with UN-Habitat country offices and with United Nations Resident Coordinator offices and partners, as relevant.
  • Collaborates internally with relevant divisions and externally with partners to strengthen resource mobilization, strategic partnerships, portfolio development and donor engagement. Leads project formulation and approvals, monitors programme implementation, identifies issues, initiates corrective actions and ensures timely follow-up.
  • Leads and/or participates in large, complex field missions, including provision of guidance to external consultants, government officials and other parties and drafting mission summaries, etc. in close collaboration with UN-Habitat country offices.
  • Coordinates activities related to budget funding (programme/project preparation and submissions, progress reports, financial statements, etc.) and prepares related documents/reports (pledging, work programme, programme budget, etc.);
  • Researches, analyzes and presents information gathered from diverse sources and generates survey initiatives; designs data collection tools; reviews, analyzes and interprets responses, identifies problems/issues and prepares conclusions relevant to the implementation of the strategic plan within ROEECA, portfolio, thematic focus, and relevant country programming in the context of Common Country Analysis and Cooperation Framework engagements.
  • Organizes and prepares written outputs, e.g. draft background papers, analysis, sections of reports and studies, inputs to publications, etc., both with a regional or sub-regional level or country-focused, as required.
  • Provides substantive backstopping to regional and relevant country-focused consultative and other meetings, conferences, etc., to include proposing agenda topics, identifying participants, preparation of documents and presentations, etc.
  • Leads regional programme development, outreach and partnership initiatives, including engagement with donors, development partners and other strategic stakeholders.
  • Performs other duties as required..

Competencies

Professionalism: Knowledge in the project management cycle and of project lifetimes, from resource mobilization and inception to implementation, evaluation and audit. Ability to identify issues, analyze and participate in the resolution of issues/problems. Ability to conduct data collection using various methods. Conceptual analytical and evaluative skills to conduct independent research and analysis, including familiarity with and experience in the use of various research sources, including electronic sources on the internet, intranet and other databases. Ability to apply judgment in the context of assignments given, plan own work and manage conflicting priorities. The ability to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Planning and Organising: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. Client Orientation: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be "clients" and seeks to see things from clients' point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients' needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients' environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client.

Required Skills and Experience

Education

  • Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in business or public administration, urban development, urban planning, housing studies, development studies, urban environment management studies or a related field.
  • A first-level university degree in combination with two (2) additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.
  • Successful completion of both degree and non-degree programs in data analytics, business analytics or data science programs is desirable.

Experience

  • A minimum of seven years of progressively responsible and international experience in project or programme management in the areas of human settlements development and urban development in relevant developing countries is required.
  • A minimum of four (4) years of responsible and relevant experience as a senior project manager in an international development organization is desirable.
  • Experience in resource mobilization and donor coordination in three (3) or more related areas (slum upgrading, housing, basic services delivery and environmental upgrading, humanitarian response and climate action) in relevant developing countries is desirable.
  • Experience in programme management and partnership development in Eastern Europe and Central Asia is desirable.
  • Experience in contributing to organizational strategic planning relevant to the implementation of the New Urban Agenda is desirable.
  • A minimum of two (2) years or more of experience in data analytics or related area is desirable.

Language

  • English and French are the working language of the United Nations Secretariat. For this position, fluency in English is required. Knowledge of another official UN language is desirable. NOTE: "fluency equals a rating of "fluent" in all four areas (read, write, speak, understand) and " Knowledge of" equals a rating of " confident" in two of the four areas.

opportunities.title: Deputy Finance Director
opportunities.description:
Qui sommes-nous ?

La mission de Maries Stopes International est « enfants par choix et non par hasard » ; organisation spécialisée dans les droits de la santé de la reproduction, nous agissons à travers nos canaux d’offres de service pour renforcer l’offre de planning familial au Niger.

Au Niger, le taux de prévalence contraceptive est très bas (12%) et stagnant tandis que le taux de fertilité demeure élevé (7,6). Sous l’invitation du Ministère de la Santé du Niger pour participer à la mise en œuvre du Plan d’action 2020-2030 pour la planification familiale au Niger, Marie Stopes International Niger a vu le jour en 2014. MSI Niger est rapidement devenu l’un des prestataires de services de santé sexuelle et reproductive (SSR) et de planification familiale les plus importants au Niger. L’organisation est en constante expansion grâce aux multiples bailleurs de fonds qui reconnaissent la qualité des services rendus par MSI

La Fonction

Sous la supervision de la Directrice Financière, il/elle contribue à la bonne gestion financière de l’organisation et à la mise en œuvre de sa stratégie financière. Il/elle veille à la bonne application des procédures et assure le suivi des activités liées à la comptabilité générale et analytique, à la trésorerie, à la fiscalité, au contrôle de gestion et au contrôle budgétaire.

Sous cette supervision, ses principales missions sont les suivantes :

Responsabilités Principales

  1. Appui dans Stratégie et Gestion d’équipe
  • Élaborer le budget annuel en cohérence avec la stratégie de MSI Niger.
  • Superviser la comptabilité générale et analytique, la trésorerie, la fiscalité, le contrôle de gestion et le suivi budgétaire.
  • Contribuer à la planification stratégique annuelle et aux initiatives de développement de MSI Niger.
  • Promouvoir un environnement de travail éthique, respectueux et orienté vers la performance.
  • Renforcer la collaboration interne, appuyer la résolution des problèmes et favoriser une prise de décision inclusive.
  • Collaborer avec l’équipe régionale des finances sur les projets d’amélioration des systèmes financiers.
  • Superviser l’équipe finance, organiser la répartition des tâches, suivre les plans de travail et appuyer le développement professionnel des collaborateurs.
  • Instaurer une culture de gestion transparente, responsable et professionnelle.
  • Appuyer la Direction dans l’élaboration des plans de financement et la validation des besoins de financement externe.
  1. Appui dans la Gestion Financière et Comptable
  • Garantir une comptabilité conforme aux normes locales, aux exigences des bailleurs et aux procédures MSI Global.
  • Assurer une utilisation transparente des ressources financières grâce à des contrôles internes efficaces sur la paie, les caisses, les banques, les stocks et les immobilisations.
  • Piloter la gestion des risques financiers et proposer des mesures de mitigation adaptées.
  • Gérer la trésorerie des programmes et préparer les demandes de fonds auprès du siège et des bailleurs locaux.
  • Suivre les obligations fiscales nationales, évaluer leur impact sur MSI Niger et recommander les mesures nécessaires.
  • Vérifier et valider les journaux comptables avant leur enregistrement dans le système.
  • Contrôler la codification des transactions intercompagnies avec Londres et les autres pays de la région avant la clôture mensuelle.
  • Analyser les comptes de bilan avant chaque clôture et s’assurer que les soldes sont justifiés et correctement documentés.
  • Préparer les reportings comptables mensuels pour le siège dans les délais requis.
  • Mettre en place un calendrier de clôture mensuelle et annuelle, avec une répartition claire des tâches de l’équipe finance.
  • Organiser des revues mensuelles avec l’équipe de direction pour analyser les tendances financières et les points d’attention.
  • Garantir un archivage sécurisé, systématique et conforme à la réglementation locale ainsi qu’aux contrats de subvention.
  • Suivre le recouvrement des créances auprès des débiteurs.
  • Assurer le règlement des factures fournisseurs, des prestations de service et des avances autorisées.
  • Partager mensuellement les analyses de performance financière avec les départements concernés, en mettant en évidence les points nécessitant un suivi.
  • Élaborer, en consultation avec le Conseiller Régional des Finances, le manuel des procédures financières, former les équipes à son utilisation et assurer sa mise à jour régulière.
  1. Contribution à la Gestion des Projets et Rapportages
  • Mettre en place des mécanismes de suivi des dépenses par rapport aux activités planifiées et proposer les ajustements nécessaires avec les gestionnaires de programme.
  • Maintenir les outils de suivi budgétaire, notamment les prévisions RH et l’analyse des coûts indirects de fonctionnement.
  • Préparer chaque mois une analyse détaillée des dépenses programmatiques par bailleur pour l’équipe de direction.
  • Vérifier l’éligibilité des dépenses imputées au regard des budgets et accords de financement, puis proposer les actions correctives nécessaires.
  • Préparer les rapports financiers aux bailleurs dans les délais et conformément aux engagements contractuels.
  • Élaborer le budget annuel avec les équipes programmes et actualiser les prévisions sur une base mensuelle et trimestrielle.
  • Appuyer les équipes programmes et New Business dans la préparation des budgets pour les nouvelles propositions de financement.
  1. Appui aux Audits
  • Coordonner les audits internes et externes en facilitant les échanges entre les auditeurs et les équipes concernées.
  • Préparer, avec l’équipe régionale des finances, les réponses de la direction aux recommandations d’audit.
  • Suivre la mise en œuvre des recommandations d’audit dans les délais convenus.
  1. Appui au contrôle interne
    • Actualiser et appliquer les systèmes, procédures et politiques de gestion financière conformément aux normes nationales, internationales et MSI.
    • Suivre les contrôles internes liés aux caisses, aux stocks, aux immobilisations et aux autres actifs.
    • Identifier les faiblesses du contrôle interne et proposer des mesures correctives adaptées.
    • Diffuser les politiques, procédures et outils financiers auprès des cadres de MSI Niger.
    • Réaliser des visites périodiques de contrôle dans les centres de prestation de services.
  2. Gestion administrative
    • Veiller à la conformité des accords de MSI avec la réglementation nationale.
    • S’assurer du respect des obligations légales applicables à MSI Niger.
    • Garantir l’application des procédures administratives et financières.

Competence et Experience (souhaitées)

  • Au moins sept ans d’expérience en gestion financière, dont trois ans dans un rôle de supervision, idéalement dans une ONG ou une organisation internationale.
  • Diplôme Bac+4/5 en finance, comptabilité, audit, gestion ou domaine équivalent.
  • Expérience dans la gestion financière de projets financés par des bailleurs institutionnels.
  • Bonne maîtrise du suivi budgétaire, du reporting financier et des règles de conformité.
  • Bonne expérience en contrôle interne, audit et gestion des risques financiers.
  • Capacité à analyser les données financières et à formuler des recommandations claires.
  • Expérience en gestion d’équipe, coaching et développement des compétences.
  • Maîtrise d’Excel et bonne connaissance des outils Microsoft Office.
  • La connaissance de logiciels comptables tels que SUN, SAGE ou Infor est un atout.
  • Maîtrise du français requise ; une bonne capacité de travail en anglais est souhaitée.

Qualifications Personnelles

Fort engagement pour la mission de MSI et les droits en santé sexuelle et reproductive.

  • Bonne capacité de communication, d’écoute et de négociation.
  • Sens de l’initiative, des responsabilités et de la confidentialité.
  • Bonne organisation, rigueur et respect des délais.
  • Capacité à travailler en équipe et à collaborer avec différents services.
  • Ouverture à l’apprentissage et au développement professionnel.
  • Respect du choix des clients et engagement pro-choix.
  • Autorisation légale de travailler au Niger

Comportement du membre d’équipe Travailler à l'unisson au sein de MSI

  • Vous contribuez à utiliser et partager des données et des preuves exactes pour améliorer la compréhension, la connaissance et la prise de décisions à travers MSI, nous permettant ainsi d'optimiser notre capacité à influencer les autres.
  • Vous partagez les connaissances, l'expertise et les ressources appropriées pour renforcer l'esprit d'équipe et éviter la duplication des efforts.
  • Vous travaillez activement au sein d'une équipe, fournissant soutien aux collègues et faisant preuve de flexibilité, équité, compréhension et respect pour toutes les personnes et cultures.

Vous faites preuve de courage, d'authenticité et d'intégrité

  • Vous assumez la responsabilité des décisions que vous prenez et des comportements que vous adoptez.
  • Vous êtes courageux, doté d’un esprit critique et prêt à prendre des risques de manière appropriée et maitrisée.

Développement et croissance

  • Vous êtes ouvert à la critique afin d'avoir une plus grande conscience de vous et en fournissez de même aux autres d'une manière qui les pousse à être encore plus efficaces.
  • Vous gérez votre développement de carrière, ce qui inclut la mise à jour régulière de vos connaissances et compétences.

Atteindre l'excellence, toujours

  • Vous vous efforcez à toujours satisfaire et dépasser les attentes, en plaçant les clients au centre de tout, et prenez des mesures plus intelligentes et plus efficaces pour accomplir votre tâche.
  • Vous construisez et maintenez des relations de travail efficaces à long terme avec toutes les parties prenantes et êtes un véritable ambassadeur de MSI.

Leadership (cadres et responsables hiérarchiques uniquement)

  • Vous inspirez les individus et les équipes, par le biais d'un leadership adapté aux situations, en offrant une orientation claire.
  • Vous cherchez et offrez des options qui motivent les membres de l'équipe, contribuant ainsià développer les compétences et le potentiel tout en renforçant les talents et assurant la relève.
  • Vous êtes au courant des derniers développements dans notre secteur, faisant preuve de connaissances stratégiques de nos clients et de nos activités et vous encouragez ceci au sein de votre équipe.
  • Vous formulez une vision de l'avenir qui inspire et stimule les autres
  • Conduite par une mission : Avec un engagement inébranlable, nous existons pour donner l’autonomie aux femmes et aux hommes d’avoir des enfants par choix conscient et non par surprise.
  • Centré sur le client : Nous sommes passionnés de nos clients et consacrons nos efforts à l’atteinte de nos objectifs avec la plus haute performance
  • Redevabilité : Nous assumons la responsabilité de toutes nos actions pour assurer la durabilité et l'impact croissant.
  • Courageux : Nous recrutons et gérons les talents, hautement motivé et courageux, promptes à relever des défis, et à prendre des décisions difficiles

Pour postuler, veuillez envoyer votre dossier de candidature (lettre de motivation (max 2 pages) et CV (max 4 pages) avec 3 personnes de références des employeurs précédents de préférence) au plus tard le 31 juillet 2026, avec en objet la mention « Candidature au poste de DEPUTY FINANCE DIRECTOR » à l’adresse électronique Recrutement.Niger@mariestopes.org

MSI Niger analysera les dossiers de candidature au fur et à mesure de leur réception et se réserve le droit de pourvoir le poste avant la date de clôture de la publication si une personne remplissant les conditions du poste est identifiée.

Tout candidat pour un poste au sein de MSI doit avoir un fort engagement en faveur des droits sexuels et reproductifs. Seuls les candidats présélectionnés seront contactés

opportunities.title: External Evaluation Consultant - Project OPPORTUNITY ESF+
opportunities.description:
International Rescue Committee Poland (IRC Poland) is seeking an External Evaluation Consultant to conduct the final independent evaluation of the project:

"OPPORTUNITY: Fostering Economic and Social Wellbeing of Ukrainian Refugees in Poland and Germany through Opportunity Self-Employment Social Innovation Model" (ESF-SI-2024-UA-01-0071).

The project is funded by the European Social Fund Plus (ESF+) Social Innovation+ Initiative and implemented by IRC Poland together with partners from Poland, Germany and Lithuania.

Scope of the assignment

The selected consultant will be responsible for:

  • conducting a desk review of project documentation;
  • developing the evaluation methodology;
  • carrying out remote interviews and/or focus group discussions with consortium partners and key stakeholders;
  • analysing qualitative and quantitative data;
  • preparing the final External Evaluator Report based on the OECD-DAC evaluation criteria.

The assignment will be fully remote and implemented between July and September 2026.

Required qualifications

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • an advanced university degree in social sciences, economics, development studies, evaluation or a related field;
  • at least three years of experience in evaluating EU-funded and/or humanitarian and development projects;
  • proven experience in applying the OECD-DAC evaluation criteria;
  • expertise in qualitative and quantitative research methods;
  • excellent command of English;
  • experience in refugee, migration, entrepreneurship or economic recovery programmes will be considered a strong asset.

opportunities.title: Project Manager
opportunities.description:
Location: Syria /Aleppo or Homs
Employment Type: Full-time Employment Contract
Reports to: Programme Director
Expected Start Date: ASAP
Application Deadline: 20.07.2026

About SYCAC

SYCAC is a non-governmental and non-profit civil society organization established in Türkiye in 2012. The organization works to support conflict-affected and displaced communities through humanitarian action, early recovery, peacebuilding, social cohesion, empowerment of marginalized groups, and strengthening the capacities of local actors and community initiatives.

Purpose of the Position

SYCAC is seeking to recruit a Project Manager to lead the overall implementation of the project and ensure the successful delivery of all project activities in accordance with approved work plans, timelines, quality standards, and organizational policies.

The Project Manager will be responsible for the day-to-day management of the project, supervision of the project team, coordination across programme, operations, finance, and MEAL functions, and maintaining effective collaboration with local partners and relevant stakeholders. The role also ensures the integration of conflict sensitivity, safeguarding, and risk management throughout the project lifecycle.

Scope of Work

The Project Manager will lead and oversee the following areas:

General Management and Coordination

  • Lead the operational planning and overall coordination of project activities.
  • Develop and monitor periodic work plans and implementation schedules.
  • Supervise the project team and oversee day-to-day implementation.
  • Ensure effective coordination between programme, operations, finance, and administrative functions.
  • Organize regular project meetings and maintain effective internal communication.
  • This position requires regular travel between the target governorates, in accordance with project needs.

Project Implementation

  • Oversee the implementation of project activities across the target governorates.
  • Ensure activities are delivered according to approved plans, timelines, and quality standards.
  • Monitor project progress against agreed indicators and outputs.
  • Address implementation challenges and introduce corrective actions when necessary.
  • Ensure the efficient utilization of project resources.

Partnership Management

  • Oversee collaboration with local civil society organizations and project partners.
  • Ensure the quality of partnership implementation and compliance with agreed standards.
  • Build and maintain productive relationships with local stakeholders and relevant authorities.
  • Represent SYCAC in coordination meetings and relevant events when required.

Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning

  • Oversee the implementation of the project's MEAL framework.
  • Review monitoring data and use findings to improve project performance.
  • Ensure lessons learned and best practices are documented.
  • Supervise evaluations and studies conducted under the project.

Risk Management and Safeguarding

  • Monitor the security and operational context in project areas.
  • Identify project risks and ensure appropriate mitigation measures are implemented.
  • Ensure the application of conflict sensitivity and Do No Harm principles.
  • Ensure compliance with safeguarding policies, the Code of Conduct, and organizational procedures.

Financial and Administrative Management

  • Monitor project budget implementation in coordination with the Finance team.
  • Review financial reports and expenditure against approved budgets.
  • Ensure compliance with organizational financial and administrative procedures.
  • Contribute to budget revisions and operational planning when required.

Key Responsibilities Project Management

Team Management

Coordination and Representation

Reporting and Documentation

  • Prepare and review periodic and final project reports.

Required QualificationsEducation

Professional Experience

Technical Skills

Leadership and Personal Competencies

opportunities.title: Field Project Officer
opportunities.description:
SYCAC Organization

Position: Field Project Officer
Location: Syria – Aleppo, Idlib, Hama, Homs, Tartous
Number of Posts: 5 (one per governorate)
Start Date: ASAP
Application Closing Date: 20 July 2026

About SYCAC

SYCAC is a non-profit, non-governmental civil society organization established in Turkey in 2012. It aims to increase civic spaces to play an active role in peace processes and early recovery of communities by empowering, protecting, and building community capacities, as well as enhancing the leadership role of women and marginalized groups, to achieve communities that embrace the principle of democracy and human rights.

Job Purpose

SYCAC is seeking five Field Project Officers to support a community-based project that strengthens civil society partnerships and promotes peaceful coexistence in Syria. Each officer will be based in one of five governorates (Aleppo, Idlib, Hama, Homs, or Tartous) and will serve as the primary field-level focal point for engagement with community-based organizations (CBOs), local communities, and relevant stakeholders, ensuring activities are implemented in a timely, high-quality, and conflict-sensitive manner.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the main point of contact for CBOs in the assigned governorate, supporting them from selection through initiative completion, including guidance on planning, implementation, and documentation.
  • Identify capacity gaps and escalate issues to the Project Manager and Partnership & Grants Coordinator.
  • Support CBOs in applying conflict sensitivity, safeguarding, and Do No Harm principles.
  • Organize and co-facilitate trainings, workshops, and learning sessions, coordinating with Field Operations Officers on logistics.
  • Conduct regular field visits and document participation, feedback, and outcomes.
  • Support the Field M&E Assistant with data collection, beneficiary registration, and documentation.
  • Submit timely field reports to the Project Manager on progress, challenges, contextual developments, and lessons learned.
  • Maintaining constructive relationships with local authorities and community stakeholders, while coordinating—where appropriate—with relevant bodies at the governorate level.
  • Ensure complaint and feedback mechanisms are accessible at all activities.
  • Apply safeguarding standards in all field interactions, ensuring the inclusion of women, youth, and marginalized groups, and promptly report any safeguarding concerns to the Project Manager.
  • Commit to SYCAC's Code of Conduct, child protection policy, and PSEA (prevention of sexual exploitation and harassment) standards.

Required Qualifications

  • University degree in social sciences, development studies, peacebuilding, community development, or a related field; equivalent professional experience may substitute for a formal degree.
  • Minimum 2 years of field experience implementing projects with NGOs or civil society organizations, including direct work with community-based or grassroots groups.
  • Experience in peacebuilding, social cohesion, or community engagement programming is an advantage, particularly in post-conflict or fragile settings in Syria.
  • Familiarity with the social and community context of the assigned governorate is strongly preferred.
  • Sound understanding of conflict sensitivity and Do No Harm principles, with the ability to facilitate community meetings and trainings.
  • Basic monitoring and documentation skills, and proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel).
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with sensitivity to gender, diversity, and inclusion.
  • Arabic: required (native or fluent); English: basic to intermediate.

opportunities.title: MEAL Officer (Syria - Homs)
opportunities.description:
Job Title: MEAL Officer

Job location: Syria – Homs

Reports to: Senior MEAL Officer

Job Style: Full Time

JOB SUMMARY

The primary responsibility of the MEAL Officer is to support MEAL Coordinator to implement the MEAL plans and ensure implementation of robust system and to provide real time analytics to guide the quality of the program and implementation.

MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Working under direct supervision of Senior MEAL Officer:

- Contribute to the development of the MEAL framework.

- Contribute to the design and development of new tools as required (questionnaires, Satisfaction Survey, Pre-Post tests- Checklists…etc) which are needed to assess all projects aspects and measuring all planned indicators.

- Contribute to building the capacity of the MEAL department.

- Conduct field visits to monitor projects activities via observation and stakeholders’ interviews.

- Maintain and compile a lesson learned database and share these lessons with the program team in timely manner.

- Work with MEAL Coordinator to ensure MEAL Management Information System are used for all MEAL activities.

- Contribute towards all MEAL reports including needs assessment.. etc.

- Ensure compliance for all MEAL participants and beneficiaries of the projects in terms of data privacy, informed and signed consent and data protection.

- Ensure all relevant MEAL inputs are collected according to specified means of verification in timely manner.

- Oversee the implementation and effectiveness of UITYD’s CFM, ensuring it is accessible, transparent, and responsive.

- Manage and document complaints and feedback, ensuring prompt response and resolution in coordination with relevant departments.

- Analyze complaints and feedback data to provide insights for program improvement.

QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS

should have the following skills, education, and experience:

- Bachelor’s degree in social sciences, computer science, engineering, Development Studies, or a related

field.

- Minimum of 2-3 years of experience in accountability, MEAL, or related roles within the humanitarian

sector.

- Knowledge of and demonstrated practical experience MEAL methodologies (particularly appropriate quantitative and qualitative research methods) data analyst and report writing.

- Advanced skills with MS office and Power Bi.

- Experience designing applications/forms with Kobo.

- Experience in managing complaints and feedback mechanisms and engaging with affected populations.

- Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to facilitate discussions and gather

community insights.

- Ability to analyze feedback trends and produce reports for program improvement.

- Ability to write a report with English.

- Native Arabic speaker with intermediate English proficiency.

ABOUT UITYD

UITYD is a local medical non-profit organization Co-funded by Med Global and multiple donors; it registered in Turkey in the year 2020, working on the front lines of crisis relief in Syria and Turkey to alleviate suffering and save lives, It provides health services and rebuilding healthcare to people in need and supports doctors and medical professionals by provides professional and educational pieces of training to physicians, and delivers medicine and medical supplies to hospitals and vulnerable families, including refugees and displaced persons, in disaster and underserved regions and offers assistance to people based on need, irrespective of race, religion, gender, or political affiliation, UITYD is composed of medical and public health volunteers of diverse backgrounds.

CODE OF CONDUCT

UITYD Code of Conduct reflects the profession’s core set of beliefs and values of care, respect, trust, and integrity. These beliefs and values are fundamental to UITYD employees, volunteers, interns, consultants, and contractors to guide their practice and conduct. The Code is organized into categories, as follows:

Always act with fairness, honesty, integrity, and openness; respect the opinions of others and treat all with equality and dignity without regard to gender, race, color, creed, ancestry, place of origin, political beliefs, religion, marital status, disability, age, or sexual orientation.

Provide a positive and valued experience for those receiving service within and outside UITYD.

CHILD PROTECTION POLICY

Child abuse in all forms is unacceptable to UITYD, which recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. UITYD is committed to ensuring a child-safe environment and is applying a zero-tolerance approach towards any kind of child abuse and exploitation.

DISCRIMINATION, ABUSE AND HARASSMENT POLICY

UITYD provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and expressly prohibits and will not tolerate any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (sexual or otherwise), based upon race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, gender, age, marital status, citizenship status, disability, or military status. UITYD employees and related personnel must under no circumstances take part in any form of discrimination, harassment, or abuse (physical, sexual or verbal), intimidation or exploitation, or in any other way infringe the rights of others inside or outside the organization.

Note :

1. Due to urgent hiring needs, we may begin conducting interviews while the job posting is still active.

2. We strongly encourage women to apply for this role

opportunities.title: Grants Financial Manager
opportunities.description:
Starting Date / Initial Contract Details

July 2026. Full-time, 6-12 months

Role Summary

The Grants Financial Manager will support Senior Management with financial analysis and data to support timely and effective decision making. They will collaborate closely with the Global Support Office Finance Partner, Field Finance Manager and Senior Management in DR Congo to ensure sound financial management of grants, effective cost coverage, and accurate spend forecasting. The Grants manager will also support the budgeting and financial reporting processes, ensuring accuracy and eligibility.

Project Overview

Medair is significantly scaling up its programming in DR Congo in response to the recent Ebola outbreak. Medair is implementing specific pillars of the response to the outbreak, including Infection Prevention control, Case Management, Surveillance, Risk Communication and Community Engagement and Mental Health/ Psychosocial Support.

Workplace & Conditions

Kinshasa, DRC, with regular travel to Ituri and Nord Kivu Provinces.

Responsibilities:

• Establish/ maintain appropriate systems and procedures to ensure compliance with donor contracts. Know donor regulations and advise on eligibility of expenses, budget flexibility & spending deviations. Check financial reports.

• Maintain an overview of all ongoing grants and ensure costs are allocated accurately and appropriately to maximise cost coverage whilst ensuring appropriateness and eligibility of costs. Conduct regular reviews and corrective action.

• Work with the Finance Partner to ensure regular updates to cost coverage calculations and availability of financial information to enable timely and sound financial decision-making by Senior Management.

• Support country leadership in financial analyses. Provide the right data to support decision making on staffing, equipment, fleet, etc. This includes developing or maintaining the right tools such as staff or fleet matrix.

• Support teams with budgeting, asking relevant questions to check/ prompt inclusion of easily overlooked costs. Work with teams to ensure accurate spend forecasting and cash need projections, keeping the Finance manager informed.

• Monitor grant spending on a monthly basis, communicating with relevant programme managers on any under/ over spend and working with them to agree appropriate corrective actions to bring spending in line with approved budgets.

Qualifications, Experience & Technical Competencies:

• Financial diploma or e.g. certificate in business administration and/ or accounting/book- keeping/ related

• 3-5 years minimum experience post qualification

• Proficiency in French language, written and spoken

• Proficiency in using Excel spreadsheets

• Overseas experience in relief work with an NGO, ideally in finance or grant management

Behavioural Skills

• Strong servant leadership skills; able to coach and support other staff members.

• Strong numeracy skills and attention to detail combined with ability to see the big picture.

• Good communication and interpersonal skills; able to maintain and develop relationships with stakeholders.

• Creative, solution-oriented, flexible, with good understanding of cross-cultural issues.

• Organised and able to prioritise. Capacity to work under pressure to meet tight deadlines and manage personal stress levels.

Team Spiritual Life

Reflect the values of Medair with team members, local staff, people we serve, and external contacts. Work, live, and pray together in our Christian faith-based teams. Fully contribute to a rich spiritual team life, including team devotion, prayer, and words of encouragement.

opportunities.title: Field Security Officer
opportunities.description:
Overview of position

The Field Security Officer (FSO) supports the safe and effective delivery of CTG operations in Haiti by providing contextual security analysis, movement advice, incident response, and practical risk guidance

The role monitors the operating environment, assesses the operational impact of security developments, supports informed decision-making, and contributes to CTG's Duty of Care through timely advice, coordination, and field-based security support.

Role objectives

Risk Analysis & Context Monitoring

  • Analyse security developments, including armed group activity, civil unrest, access constraints and local security trends, assessing their relevance to CTG activities.
  • Identify emerging risks, movement restrictions and changes in the operating environment, providing recommendations to inform planning and decision-making.
  • Produce concise security reporting focused on operational implications, risks and required actions.

Operational Support & Movement Advisory

  • Provide advice on staff and consultant movements, including routes, timings, communications, contingency measures and security considerations.
  • Monitor conditions affecting travel and access, adjusting movement guidance based on security developments, road conditions and local constraints.
  • Coordinate with relevant personnel and client counterparts to facilitate safe movement and activity planning.

Briefings & Awareness

  • Deliver clear, context-specific security briefings and inductions
  • Promote situational awareness and practical risk ownership among staff
  • Tailor messaging to reflect behavioural patterns, access sensitivities, and cultural and community dynamics in the operating environment

Incident Management & Escalation

  • Support immediate response to security incidents, including information gathering and coordination
  • Ensure disciplined escalation and clear communication during incidents
  • Contribute to After Action Reviews, focusing on root causes, operational impact, and lessons learned

Stakeholder Engagement & Security Interfaces

  • Maintain working-level relationships with relevant security counterparts, including client security structures, UNDSS, security coordination forums, local authorities, and other relevant stakeholders as required
  • Support coordination with client security teams during movements, incidents, and operational planning
  • Provide insight into how formal and informal dynamics, including local power structures and access constraints, may affect posture and delivery
  • Ensure engagement remains practical, focused on enabling operations, and aligned with CTG’s role and responsibilities

Security Planning & Documentatio

  • Support the development and maintenance of practical security procedures, annexes, and guidance aligned with CTG standards
  • Ensure documentation reflects operational realities and is usable by field teams
  • Contribute to simplifying processes where they create unnecessary operational friction

Capacity Support & Continuous Improvement

  • Provide ongoing support and coaching to staff on security awareness and practical application
  • Identify recurring issues, gaps, or inefficiencies and propose improvements
  • Contribute to strengthening how security is applied operationally, not just documented

Project reporting

This position reports operationally to the Regional Director - Asia, with a functional dotted-line to the Global Risk Director.

Key competencies

Education

  • University degree or equivalent professional experience in a relevant field (e.g. security management, international relations, humanitarian operations, risk advisory, or related disciplines)

Experience

  • 3-5 years’ experience in security, access, risk advisory, or operational support roles in complex, fragile, or conflict-affected environments, preferably including Haiti, the Caribbean, Francophone contexts, or comparable high-risk urban settings.
  • Proven ability to operate in complex stakeholder environments, including coordination with local authorities, community actors, clients, and international partners
  • Experience contributing to incident response and operational decision-making under pressure, with sound judgement and discretion
  • Experience supporting movement planning, incident response, and security coordination in environments affected by armed violence, access restrictions, civil unrest, or kidnapping risk is desirable.

Languages:

  • Good command of English written and spoken
  • French and/or Haitian Creole required; fluency in both is strongly desirable

Competencies:

  • Strong contextual judgement and situational awareness.
  • Ability to build trust with diverse stakeholders in sensitive environments.
  • Demonstrated experience drafting and operationalising security procedures and SOPs in complex environments.
  • Ability to support and structure security responses during incidents, including first-hour actions and coordination.
  • Strong judgement in dynamic environments, with the ability to translate risk analysis into practical guidance.

Travel Requirements: This role requires travel within Haiti, including to field locations and areas where access may be constrained by security conditions, infrastructure limitations, or operational need. The role also requires flexibility to work irregular hours and provide support in emergency situations, including weekends and holidays.

Team management

This role does not have team management responsibilities

Further information

  • Female candidates are encouraged to apply.
  • Candidates must have the right to work in Haiti.

opportunities.title: Request for Proposals (RFP) The Gambia CROP-H Project
opportunities.description:
Request for Proposals
Midterm Evaluation - CROP-H Project: The Gambia,
USDA/FAS/FFPR PROJECT | FCC-685-2017/026-00-A
Organization: Shelter For Life International
Country: The Gambia
Project: Shelter For Life International
Project dates: 2023 - 2028
Donor: USDA/FAS Food for Progress
RFP Number: RFP-5502-0726
Date of RFP: July 3, 2026
Due date: August 3, 2026, 5:00 PM CDT

1. Introduction
Shelter for Life International (SFL) is an international, faith-based, relief and development organization with more than 30 years of experience providing sustainable development and humanitarian assistance to post-conflict countries around the world. We are currently operational in Afghanistan, Senegal, and The Gambia.
SFL is issuing this Request for Proposals (RFP) to conduct a Midterm Evaluation of its Cultivating Resilient and Optimal Production – Horticulture (CROP-H) Project in The Gambia.
Summary of RFP Schedule
Release of Request for Proposal
July 3, 2026
Questions Due by email / confirmation of interest
July 15, 2026
Proposals Due
August 3, 2026
Conclusion of Selection Process
August 14, 2026
Contract Letter Issued
August 14, 2026
Note: SFL reserves the right to modify this schedule as needed. All parties will be notified of any changes by email.

2. General Instructions to Offerors
Offerors wishing to respond to this Request for Proposals (RFP) TOR must submit proposals in accordance with the following instructions:
1. Offerors must review all instructions and specifications contained in the RFP. Failure to do so will be at the offeror’s risk. Issuance of this RFP in no way obligates Shelter For Life to award a contract.
2. Offerors will not be reimbursed for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of their proposal, and SLF shall in no case be responsible or liable for these costs.
3. Submission to SFL of a proposal in response to this RFP does not constitute an offer but indicates the offeror’s agreement to the terms and conditions of this RFP and any attachments. SFL reserves the right not to evaluate a non-responsive or incomplete proposal.

Submission Requirements:
Proposal Submission Deadlines: Proposals must be received no later than the date and time indicated on the cover page of this RFP. Late submissions will not be accepted; however, SFL may request additional documentation after the bid deadline, which will not count against the offeror. SFL will review all submitted proposals and may conduct in-person or remote interviews with offerors under consideration. Proposals must be submitted via e-mail to info@shelter.org, with the subject line of “CROP-H Midterm Evaluation”, and the company or organization name.
Full version of the RFP can be found here: Request-for-Proposals-RFP-CROP-H-Midterm-Evaluation-The-Gambia.pdf

Proposal Structure and Required Documentation:
Offerors must submit two sets of proposals in separate files and labeled clearly: 1. Technical Proposal and 2. Cost Proposal.
Submissions must be in English. Each proposal should be typed in 12-point Arial or Times New Roman font and single-spaced. All pages must be numbered, and the RFP reference number and name of the company or organization must be included on each page. The proposal submission should include each of the following sections in the specific order listed below:

Technical Proposal:
The technical proposal shall include:

Section 1: Organization Information:
The offeror shall list the legal name and authorized contact, including address, phone number, and email proof of registration (attach the copy of registration certificate). Briefly describe the organization's or company’s history, vision/objectives, legal/registration status, and structure. This section should also state the legal status in The Gambia, if applicable.

Section 2: Analysis and Proposed Approaches/Methodologies:
Describe the underlying assumptions, conditions, and constraints that will inform the offeror’s approach and guiding principles to this midterm evaluation. Describe the proposed approaches and methodologies for addressing evaluation questions. Describe the proposed sampling methods for data collection.
This section should include information on how both quantitative and qualitative data will be collected, compiled, and analyzed, including the software to be used and the analytical approach taken (e.g., whether inductive or deductive coding be used for qualitative analysis). The perceived risks need to be explained and proposed actions to mitigate them. This should also outline any ethical considerations, including issues of consent and plans for protecting human subjects.

Section 3: Work Plan:
The offeror is to propose an activity-based work plan consistent with the timeline, technical approach, and methodology. It should highlight key activities of these TOR that will be completed during the midterm evaluation and which the offeror is encouraged to expand upon. The work plan should be in the Gantt chart style.

opportunities.title: Protection Officer (2 positions, Ukrainian Nationals Only)
opportunities.description:
Job Title: Protection Officer (2 positions, Ukrainian Nationals Only)

Department: Programming

Division: Programme Implementation

Duty Station: Mykolaiv, Ukraine

Line Manager: Team Leader

Line Management Responsibility: N/A

Position Type: Full-time

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) is a dynamic, international non-governmental organisation. We work with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP). We work to reduce violence, protect civilians in countries affected by violent conflict and its aftermath, and help transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

Overview:

NP first established a presence in Ukraine in 2014/2015 working on peacebuilding and conflict mediation. NP has had a sustained presence in Ukraine since April 2022. NP occupies a unique space in the protection response in Ukraine; simultaneously providing direct protection to at-risk civilians and providing hands-on support to front-line volunteer collectives to directly contribute to the sustainability and safety of their actions.

Job Summary:

The role of the Protection Officer (PO) is to support the implementation of civilian protection and violence-prevention programming for those affected by conflict.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Provide support for the day-to-day implementation of project activities in accordance with the agreed work plans and log-frames.
  • Support and assist the Team Leader (TL) in the engagement and relationship building with local humanitarian NGOs, community-based organizations, local authorities and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Support and assist the TL in the crafting and development of work/activity plans and budget forecasting.
  • Conduct and facilitate community meetings and dialogues in the project areas.
  • Support and assist the TL and team in conducting and facilitating training and seminars for community and project partners, for example, Civilian Protection – Early Warning and Early Response (CP-EWER), International Humanitarian Law (IHL), Human Rights Law (HRL), Child Protection (CP), Gender Based Violence (GBV).
  • Support in providing protective accompaniment to civilians exposed to vulnerabilities, particularly the elderly and people with special needs.
  • Support and assist, monitor, verify and report incidents of violence and civilian displacement.
  • In collaboration with the NP Partnerships Department, contribute to monitoring the implementation of sub-grants provided to NP local partners including: support alignment of activities against the agreed-upon objectives, planning and budget, and in accordance with the humanitarian standards. Where requested, provide direct feedback to partners.
  • Regularly monitor the provision and the availability of humanitarian services to civilians in need, and conduct referrals, when necessary.

Qualifications:

  • University degree in a related field (Social Science, Development Studies, etc.).
  • Interest in peacebuilding, conflict transformation, and civilian protection and human rights. Practical experience in these fields is highly desirable.
  • Qualifications or commensurate practical experience in peacebuilding, conflict transformation or nonviolent peacekeeping (preferred).
  • At least 2 years relevant work experience in civilian/humanitarian/child protection and human rights.
  • NGO/humanitarian work.
  • Post-conflict/conflict area experience.
  • Experience in community organizing/mobilization.

Skills and Competencies:

  • Understanding civil protection and human rights frameworks.
  • Understanding of conflict dynamics in Ukraine.
  • Understanding of humanitarian and DO NO HARM principles.
  • Knowledge and understanding of peacemaking, peacekeeping, peacebuilding and social cohesion concepts.
  • Experience in project implementation and Grants Cycle Management processes.
  • Analytical and report writing skills.
  • Ability to gather information and analyze data from multiple sources and present combined/concise thematic inputs and factual reports meeting the deadlines.
  • Demonstrable problem solving skills and creative thinking around mitigating risks to enable project implementation.
  • Willing and able to work as a member of a team, with people of diverse backgrounds, different genders, and views, at the same time staying impartial and objective.
  • Able to communicate in oral and written, and able to work with documents in English, as well as Ukrainian.
  • Experience in working with Windows applications, including Microsoft Office.

opportunities.title: WASH Project Manager DR Congo Bunia
opportunities.description:
Contexte

Le Conseil Norvégien pour les Réfugiés (NRC) est une Organisation Internationale Non Gouvernementale d’origine norvégienne, présente dans plus de 25 pays du monde. Il œuvre en République Démocratique du Congo depuis l’année 2001. Ses programmes sont focalisés dans les secteurs d’Education, Urgence, Protection et Médiation Humanitaire, Abris, Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène (WASH), et l’Information, Conseil, et Assistance Légale (ICLA) en faveur des populations contraintes au déplacement.

Ituri est une province de l’est de la République Démocratique du Congo. Elle est plus au nord et partage ses frontières avec l’Ouganda et le Soudan du Sud.

Le contexte sécuritaire est l’un des plus critiques du pays. Une quinzaine d’acteurs armés sont encore opérationnels dans la province. Il s’agit des Groupes armés locaux (CODECO, Zaire, FPIC, FRPI, Maï-Maï…) et un acteur international ADF qui est connu pour provenir de l’Ouganda voisin.

L’Area office de NRC en Ituri est composé d’une soixantaine de staffs. Les projets mis en œuvre adressent les questions des secteurs : d’Éducation, Réponse Rapide aux Mouvements de Population (RRMP), Protection contre les violences, Abris, Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène (WASH), et l’Information, Conseil, et Assistance Légale (ICLA).

Ce que nous recherchons :

Le Manager de Projet WASH a la charge de mettre en œuvre plusieurs projets ambitieux dans une zone complexe et dynamique. Il devra être en mesure de tirer des leçons, d'établir des bonnes pratiques pour contribuer au développement du programme, en intégrant les considérations de Programmation Intégrée, de Programmation Sûre et Inclusive, et de sensibilités environnementales, entre autres. Il aura sous son management l’équipe WASH de l’Ituri.

Ce que vous ferez :

  • Promouvoir les droits des personnes touchées par le déplacement conformément à la stratégie de plaidoyer.
  • Effectuer des revues mensuelles sur l'avancement du projet, y compris les progrès par rapport aux objectifs, aux indicateurs, aux activités ainsi qu'au budget par rapport aux réalités, rendre compte au responsable de zone et de secteur de l'avancement du projet.
  • Travailler en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe Monitoring, Evidence and Learning (MEL), pour soutenir le suivi continu de la mise en œuvre du projet, de la qualité, de la mesure de tous les indicateurs ainsi que garantir que les mécanismes de redevabilité (mécanisme de plaintes et de retour d'information du NRC) soient mis en place, régulièrement évalués, connus et effectivement utilisés par les bénéficiaires.
  • Concevoir, planifier et piloter les évaluations des besoins WASH ainsi que les études de référence (baseline, endline), les évaluations intermédiaires et finales et contribuer activement au suivi-évaluation des projets, notamment au suivi des indicateurs, en étroite collaboration avec les équipes programme, le département MEL et le spécialiste WASH.
  • Assurer la préparation et de la livraison en temps voulu des plans détaillés de mise en oeuvre des projets, d'approvisionnement et de dépenses budgétaires tout en veillant à ce que les objectifs non atteints soient identifiés et atténués en temps opportun.
  • Contribuer à l'analyse de la situation, à l'identification des besoins et participer activement à l'élaboration d'une stratégie conformément aux ambitions mondiales de NRC.
  • Veiller à la mise en place des systèmes durables garantissant le fonctionnement et l’entretien à long terme des infrastructures d’eau, d’assainissement et d’hygiène, y compris par la formation des acteurs concernés.
  • Promouvoir les synergies entre les secteurs WASH, Abri, Éducation, ICLA, Réponse Rapide et autres axes éventuels de NRC, afin de favoriser une approche intégrée et cohérente.
  • Veiller à la coordination des activités WASH avec les actions des autres organisations.

Compétences professionnelles:

  • Expérience professionnelle de 5 ans minimum dans un poste similaire.
  • Expérience professionnelle antérieure dans des contextes complexes et instables.
  • 5 années d’études universitaires en Génie Hydraulique, Génie Rural, Génie Civil ou tout autre domaine pertinent et/ou une expérience minimale de 7 années dans des postes similaires si le niveau d’études est inférieur.
  • Excellentes maitrises du français.
  • Bonne maitrise de l’anglais souhaitable.
  • Maitrise de l’utilisation des logiciels de dessins techniques (tels que AutoCAD, ArchiCAD, Revit Architecture, Sketchup, etc.), de calculs hydrauliques et de structure (tels que Epanet, WaterGEMS, Robot SA, Revit Structure, etc.). La maitrise des SIG (QGiS, ArcGIS, ou autre) est un atout

Compétences Professionnelles Spécifiques

  • Bonne connaissance du contexte de l’Est de la RDC
  • Aptitude à travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes terrain et intersectorielles.
  • Excellentes compétences en communication, représentation, flexibilité et négociation.
