opportunities.title: Senior Development Officer
opportunities.description:
POSITION TITLE: Senior Development Officer

LOCATION: Remote, USA (specific states listed below); Washington DC; or Geneva, Switzerland. Must possess valid work authorization.

SALARY RANGE: $75,000-$90,000 (12.5% increase applies in Switzerland)

DEADLINE: The priority application deadline is July 6, 2026. Applications submitted after that may not be reviewed

SUMMARY DESCRIPTION:

The Center for International Environmental Law (CIEL) uses the power of law to protect the environment, promote human rights, and ensure a just and sustainable society. We work at the intersection of environmental protection and human rights, across sectors and borders, and in close collaboration with global partners and local communities to defend the right to a healthy planet.

The Senior Development Officer plays a critical role in advancing CIEL’s ambitious fundraising agenda by building new relationships with foundation and government funders, composing grant proposals and reports, and working with program and finance staff across the organization to advance fundraising strategy.

The Senior Development Officer will draft and refine grant narrative content for a robust (primarily foundation-based) portfolio throughout the entire grant life-cycle, including prospecting, developing proposals, monitoring progress on grant awards, reporting, and renewals. The Senior Development Officer will craft high quality, accurate, and persuasive proposals and reports and ensure all proposal and reporting requirements are met.

This position will work closely with Leadership and Program staff to develop and sharpen strategies and clearly and compellingly convey CIEL’s work and impact for both general operating and project grants. The successful Senior Development Officer will contribute to the growth and retention of funding by collaborating with program staff to steward current funders while also identifying and cultivating new foundation prospects. They will maintain a funder portfolio, keeping many projects moving at once, and balancing numerous priorities and emerging opportunities while meeting firm deadlines.

This position will require excellent writing ability, capacity to receive and integrate written and verbal feedback, strategic thinking, and deep commitment to CIEL’s mission, values, and goals. This position is included in the CIEL staff unit of the Washington Baltimore News Guild union.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Grant Writing (60%)

  • Develop and write compelling, substantive, outcomes-oriented, grant proposals and reports, collaborating across programs to develop project narratives, objectives, and deliverables that are aligned with CIEL’s mission, strategic priorities, and capabilities.
  • Coordinate with the finance department to meet grant budgeting and reporting deadlines.
  • Collaborate with relevant staff to align donor interest with grant deliverables, distill relevant material for proposals and reports, coordinate the drafting processes and review loops, and deliver high-quality, timely final products to foundation and government funders.
  • Ensure compliance with all relevant internal and external deadlines and standards.

Portfolio Management (35%)

  • Maintain a portfolio of institutional donors, working in collaboration with Leadership and program staff to grow these relationships and maximize funding potential.
  • Identify new prospects and create engagement strategies to cultivate foundations donors and secure additional support.
  • Ensure timely submission of proposal, renewal, and reporting requirements for current and potential grants (both project-based and general operating support)
  • Contribute to and support processes and procedures that improve the efficiency of the development team and its interactions with the rest of the organization.
  • Update records and information within CRM system.
  • Organize all grant files according to established protocols.

Administration (5%)

  • Maintain timesheets and submit them on time.
  • Meet periodically as requested, with supervisor and other team members.
  • Participate in weekly staff and team meetings and other organizational activities, including an annual staff performance evaluation.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Minimum Qualifications:

  • At least 5 years of professional experience in an institutional development/fundraising role.
  • Proven experience securing grants in mid to upper six-figure range and managing a portfolio of grants with competing deadlines.
  • Strong grant writing skills including past experience with grants for projects and general operating support.
  • Ability to understand and interpret grant budgets.
  • Exceptional communication skills and attention to detail, including the ability to articulate complex subject matter clearly and compellingly both in writing and verbally.
  • Ability to successfully work on multiple priorities concurrently, including having strong planning and organizational skills, and ability to work well under pressure.
  • Ability to work and communicate effectively with people of different backgrounds, lived experiences, and communication styles.
  • Sound judgment in handling confidential donor information.
  • Ability to work both independently and in close coordination with a team.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Experience with CRM maintenance and use, such as Blackbaud products.
  • Experience in an organization with offices in multiple countries.
  • Past experience in a remote work environment.
  • Comfort leading meetings to discuss complex strategies and impact with managers across teams.
  • Experience with Google Suite (including Docs and Sheets) and Asana project management software.
  • Project management experience.

opportunities.title: Project Assistant, UNHCR Livelihood (Greater Cairo)
opportunities.description:
THE ORGANISATION

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation/charity/non-profit that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child but know this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination. And it is girls who are most affected.

Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge.

For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries.

We won’t stop until we are all equal.

Plan International started working in Egypt in 1981 and has a presence in ten of the 27 governorates in which the country including Greater Cairo, Alexandria, Giza, Beheira, Kalyoubia, Damietta, Qena, Assuit and Sohag. Plan international Egypt implements programmes designed to enable communities to improve the lives of the most marginalised children and their families. Plan Egypt’s Country Strategy focuses on five strategic objectives.

Through a five-interconnected, gender transformative and context-fit country objectives, PIE intends along with the various stakeholders at all levels to continue delivering positive and transformative changes so that “Children, especially girls, and young people grow up in an enabling environment, realizing their rights and contributing in both development and humanitarian settings as active agents of change”.

THE OPPORTUNITY

You will follow up and monitor the project at the PU level, while ensuring a seamless integration and quality of deliverables in line with the Country Strategy. Further, you will design, implement, monitor and report the progress of project activities in line with detailed implementation plan. You will be the link between the target beneficiaries and all stakeholders critical to the project success.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Monitor and coordinate project implementation with partners, ensuring plans, timelines, and indicators are met.
  • Facilitate planning, reflection, and coordination meetings to strengthen teamwork and adapt implementation as needed.
  • Produce accurate progress and donor reports, interpreting data to inform initiatives and communicate lessons learned.
  • Ensure compliance with gender equality, child protection, safeguarding, and security policies in all activities.
  • Support government stakeholders and partners for quality, timely delivery of agreed activities.
  • Manage and monitor project budgets, advances, and expenditures in line with objectives.
  • Supervise field activities to ensure alignment with donor regulations and organizational policies.
  • Foster collaboration and strong relationships with partners for effective project outcomes.
  • Plan International has a robust global policy for Safeguarding and Gender Equality and Inclusion standards, ensuring staff and associates within your scope strictly comply with these principles and guidelines.
  • You will be trusted to take on additional assignments within the scope of work as assigned by your supervisor on need basis.

What we are looking for:

  • Someone with a bachelor's degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies or similar field.
  • Should have 3-5 years of experience with a proven record of success at a similar level preferably in an INGO sector.
  • Someone with proven experiences and ability to coordinate and collaborate with different civil society and Community based organization.
  • Someone experienced in planning, conducting, and facilitating trainings/workshops.
  • Should have previous experience working on projects that promote gender equality.
  • Someone knowledgeable on gender sensitive approaches and the ability to apply them in project implementation and beneficiary engagement.
  • Should have understanding of basic gender and protection principles within humanitarian and development programs.
  • Someone familiar with safeguarding, protection, and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) principles.
  • Someone experienced in supporting livelihood, economic empowerment, entrepreneurship, or employability initiatives that promote women's participation and access to economic opportunities.

Please respond to the requirements of this role in your cover letter.
Only applications in English language will be accepted.

Location: On site working and the role is based at Greater Cairo

Reports to: Project Coordinator

Job Grade: Hay Level 11

Vacancy advert closing Date: 3rd July 2026

Contract end date: 31st December 2026

This vacancy is open to Egypt nationals only.

Equality, diversity and inclusion is at the very heart of everything that Plan International stands for.

We want Plan International to reflect the diversity of the communities we work with, offering equal opportunities to everyone regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation.

Plan International is based on a culture of inclusivity and we strive to create a workplace environment that ensures every team, in every office, in every country, is rich in diverse people, thoughts, and ideas.

We foster an organisational culture that embraces our commitment to racial justice, gender equality, girls’ rights and inclusion.

Plan International believes that in a world where children face so many threats of harm, it is our duty to ensure that we, as an organisation, do everything we can to keep children safe. This means that we have particular responsibilities to children that we come into contact with and we must not contribute in any way to harming or placing children at risk.

A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with Plan International's Safeguarding Children and Young People policy. Plan International also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this scheme we will request information from applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

Disclaimer: Plan International is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate applicants on any basis. We also do not charge Job seekers any fees at any point of the recruitment process.

opportunities.title: Technical Expert to Support the Development of the Compendium of Best Practices on Disaster Management: Commemorating 20 Years of AADMER(Consultancy)
opportunities.description:
Position Title : Technical Expert to Support the Development of the Compendium of Best Practices on Disaster Management: Commemorating 20 Years of ASEAN Agreement on Disaster Management and Emergency Response (AADMER)
Duty Station : Home-based
Duration of Contract : 11 months (with possibility of extension)
Type of Appointment : Consultancy
Estimated Start Date : July 2026 or as soon as possible

Organizational Context

The International Organization for Migration (IOM), through its Deployment Roster, is seeking to identify qualified technical experts to support the development of the Compendium of Best Practices on Disaster Management: Commemorating 20 Years of AADMER.

The Deployment Roster is a global mechanism through which pre-vetted experts are identified and mobilized to support humanitarian and development operations. Selected candidates may be considered for current and future deployment opportunities.

Objective of the Consultancy

This consultancy will support the development of a strategic knowledge product documenting ASEAN’s progress, best practices, and key lessons in disaster management at both the regional and national levels over the past two decades.

The Compendium will consolidate contributions from ASEAN Member States, ASEAN entities, UN agencies, development partners, academia, and other relevant stakeholders, to capture the region’s collective knowledge and experience in disaster management. It will also identify key lessons, emerging opportunities, and actionable recommendations to strengthen regional coordination, institutional resilience, and future disaster management efforts across ASEAN.

The technical expert will undertake a desk review, develop the Compendium outline, consolidate stakeholder contributions, and prepare draft and final versions of the Compendium for review and finalization.

opportunities.title: ESC Refugees Welcome Project Assistant
opportunities.description:
Refugees Welcome España (Refugiados Bienvenidos) is a non-profit association that promotes a Culture of Welcome through housing solutions for displaced people (applicants for International Protection, refugees, migrants, etc.). Its objective is to create stories of intercultural coexistence based on horizontality, equality, and mutual respect, facilitating access to decent housing and promoting social inclusion. It is part of the international Refugees Welcome network, present in 12 countries, and develops projects in different territories across Spain, including Barcelona, Rubí, Sant Cugat del Vallès, Sabadell, Valldoreix, and other municipalities in Catalonia.

As an ESC volunteer at RW, the main focus will be to provide operational, administrative, and documentary support to the Project Officer in managing the organization’s projects in Catalonia. Your role will be to support the monitoring, data collection, and reporting of projects, contributing to the success of the initiatives promoting a Culture of Welcome and decent housing for displaced people.

We are looking for someone who wants to gain experience in administration and project management, documentation, and event management.

Main tasks

  • Support in the collection, organization, and filing of invoices, receipts, and financial documentation required for Justification Reports (public and private).
  • Collaborate in the preliminary drafting and review of intermediate and final technical reports under the supervision of the Project Officer.
  • Maintain the digital and physical archive of the projects organized (entering operational and impact data, indicators, calls for proposals databases, forms, correction requests, etc.).
  • Assist in the search for information and documentation required for the preparation of new funding proposals and grants.
  • Enter operational and impact data reported by other departments to ensure project indicators are up to date.
  • Help prepare materials, meeting minutes, and presentations for the spaces in which the organization participates.
  • Support, facilitate, and participate in the organization and implementation of events, activities, and training/workshops, manage logistics, and present the project when necessary.
  • Participate in ESC activities (organizing team-building activities, awareness-raising in schools, etc.).
  • Provide support to the rest of the team when needed and actively participate in the general activities of the organization.

Requirements

  • A sociable, proactive person with a vocation for helping others; comfortable initiating contact with unknown people and networking.
  • Independent and creative, with the ability to contribute ideas, find new ways of doing things, and suggest improvements.
  • Proactivity and teamwork orientation.
  • Good level of Spanish.
  • Flexibility in working hours (to attend activities on Saturdays or events in the afternoons/evenings during the week). Overtime will always be compensated.
  • Previous experience as a volunteer in third-sector organizations.
  • Ability to manage deadlines, plan ahead, and anticipate problems.
  • Familiarity with software tools and interest in learning to use new systems such as Slack, Airtable, and Notion.
  • Writing skills (for example, writing engaging texts for event promotion and communicating with different key stakeholders).
  • Enthusiasm and commitment to promoting diversity and social inclusion.
  • Feminist and intersectional perspective.

Nice to have

  • University degree or higher vocational training in Social Sciences (Social Work, Cooperation, Political Science, Sociology), Project Management, Administration, or similar.
  • Knowledge of administrative project management or grant support in the third sector (NGOs/Associations).
  • Interest in the field of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI).
  • Interest in migration, refugees, and asylum.
  • Knowledge of other languages (Catalan, English, Darija, French, etc.).

Eligibility criteria

To participate in the European Solidarity Corps (ESC) volunteering program, it is mandatory to meet the following criteria:

  • Be between 18 and 30 years old.
  • Be a resident of the EU or one of the partner countries mentioned (neighboring countries of the EU).
  • Be available for 12 months.
  • Not have previously participated in a long-term ESC volunteering program.

What do we offer?

Our volunteering program is funded by the European Commission through the European Solidarity Corps program. This means that the volunteering includes:

  • Travel expenses coverage: Up to the limits established in the distance calculator of the Erasmus+ Guide from the volunteer’s region of residence to our center.
  • Free accommodation (shared room): Provided in the center of Barcelona. The apartment is fully equipped (kitchen, bathrooms, washing machine, Wi-Fi, etc.).
  • Monthly allowance (pocket money): €330 per month.
  • Health insurance: Henner.
  • Free language courses: Online

opportunities.title: Risk Communications and Community Engagement (RCCE) Officer
opportunities.description:
Background:
L’International Rescue Committee (IRC) est l’une des principales organisations humanitaires mondiales d’aide d’urgence et de développement. Depuis plus de 80 ans, l’IRC est à l’avant-garde des initiatives humanitaires pour aider les personnes déplacées par les guerres, les persécutions et les conflits armés, en fournissant un soutien vital pour les aider à survivre et à reconstruire leur vie. L’Unité de Préparation et de Réponse aux Urgences (EPRU) de l’IRC dirige les activités mondiales de préparation et de réponse aux urgences, avec pour mission de répondre aux besoins immédiats de survie et de réduire la souffrance des populations affectées par les conflits ou les catastrophes lors de la phase aiguë des urgences.

Contexte:
Le 15 mai 2026, le Ministère de la Santé de la République Démocratique du Congo a déclaré la 17ᵉ épidémie de la Maladie à Virus Ebola (MVE) du pays, après confirmation de cas causés par l’espèce virale Bundibugyo (BDBV) dans la province de l’Ituri. La transmission initiale a été détectée dans et autour des zones de santé de Mongbwalu, Rwampara et Bunia. Le 17 mai 2026, l’OMS a évalué l’épidémie comme une Urgence de Santé Publique de Portée Internationale (USPPI) en raison du risque de propagation régionale et d’un environnement opérationnel difficile. L’IRC se prépare à soutenir la réponse à l’épidémie en Ituri et au Nord-Kivu par un appui aux structures de soins de santé primaires, notamment le dépistage et l’isolement de cas de MVE, le renforcement de la prévention et du contrôle des infections (PCI), des activités RCCE communautaires ainsi que des activités de protection. Au début du mois de juin 2026, l’épidémie s’est étendue à 25 zones de santé en Ituri, au Nord-Kivu et au Sud-Kivu, avec 488 cas confirmés et 86 décès. La souche non-Zaïre (Bundibugyo) limite l’efficacité des vaccins disponibles, renforçant ainsi l’importance cruciale des approches PCI et communautaires. La méfiance des communautés, alimentée par les conflits armés, la stigmatisation et la précarité socio-économique, a conduit à des incidents sécuritaires contre les équipes de réponse. Le/La Chargé(e) RCCE travaillera dans cet environnement de terrain complexe et en évolution rapide, nécessitant une forte conscience contextuelle, de la flexibilité et le respect des protocoles de programmation sécurisée et de PCI en tout temps.

Portée du travail:
Sous la supervision du Gestionnaire RCCE en Ituri, le/la Chargé(e) RCCE aura pour rôle principal de mettre en œuvre et de superviser les activités RCCE dans un certain nombre de sites dédés (qui seront définis) en Ituri, et d’agir en tant que point focal RCCE pour cette zone. Il/elle fera partie des équipes mobiles de l’IRC, composées de personnel de santé, PCI/WASH, RCCE et protection, déployées pour soutenir la réponse à l’épidémie dans les structures de santé et les communautés affectées. Il/elle rendra compte au Gestionnaire RCCE, tout en maintenant une coordination étroite avec les autres départements de l’IRC travaillant dans le lieu qui lui a été assigné.

Roles et responsabilités

1.Communication de risques et engagement communautaire (RCCE)

  • Agir en tant que point focal pour les activités RCCE au sein des équipes mobiles de l’IRC
  • Soutenir les évaluations et évaluations RCCE, notamment en réalisant et/ou en mettant à jour les cartographies des parties prenantes
  • Mener des consultations avec les publics cibles sur leurs besoins et préférences en matière d’information, adapter les messages et identifier les canaux de communication sur la base de ces consultations
  • Compiler et maintenir à jour les informations et messages dans les langue(s) locale(s) à l’intention des bénéficiaires (ex. femmes, hommes, filles et garçons vivant avec ou sans handicap, etc.) et des communautés utilisés pour les activités, notamment des messages de sensibilisation à la santé, des informations sur la réduction des risques et l’accès aux services essentiels non spécifiques à la santé, ainsi que des informations sur les adaptations et modifications des services de l’IRC, etc.
  • Planifier et conduire des séances de sensibilisation auprès des publics cibles identifiés
  • En collaboration avec l’équipe Responsabilité envers les Clients & Redevabilité / MEAL de l’IRC, collecter les retours et réactions des communautés et y répondre
  • Avec le soutien du Gestionnaire RCCE et d’autres membres pertinents de l’équipe IRC, adapter les messages en fonction des besoins et des réactions recueillis auprès de la communauté, et répondre aux recommandations et préoccupations de celle-ci

2. Planification, rapportage et tâches administratives

  • Élaborer et soumettre des plans hebdomadaires, ainsi que des PR et budgets pour planifier et mettre en œuvre correctement les activités du programme
  • Préparer et soumettre des rapports d’activité hebdomadaires au Gestionnaire RCCE
  • Renseigner tous les outils de rapport, de suivi et d’évaluation pertinents pour les activités menées
  • Classer et archiver tous les documents et correspondances importants liés au projet et aux activités
  • Contribuer aux rapports hebdomadaires et mensuels, en mettant en évidence les défis, les opportunités et les progrès réalisés

3. Coordination et représentation

  • Se tenir informé(e) des développements dans la communauté et dans les zones environnantes susceptibles d’affecter les activités RCCE
  • Signaler au superviseur toute préoccupation, tendance et mise à jour RCCE dans la communauté et les zones environnantes
  • Maintenir de bonnes relations avec les partenaires de l’IRC, les ONG locales et internationales, les acteurs et autorités gouvernementaux, les leaders communautaires, les communautés locales, etc.

4. Sauvegarde, protection transversale et PCI

  • Respecter et soutenir activement les mesures PCI, telles que définies par l’équipe de santé pour les services concernés
  • Respecter les principes de protection transversale et de la sauvegarde
  • Promouvoir et respecter les principes, objectifs et code de conduite de l’IRC
  • Collaborer avec le personnel de protection et de santé pour assurer des références sécurisées et adaptées aux services de protection et de santé

5. Autre

  • Se comporter professionnellement et personnellement d’une manière qui valorise l’image de l’IRC et ne compromet pas sa mission humanitaire
  • Si nécessaire, assurer la traduction et l’interprétation lors de réunions, formations et/ou de documents pour aider le personnel expatrié à comprendre
  • S’acquitter de toute autre tâche demandée par son/sa superviseur(e) pour assurer la réalisation du programme

Profil requis

  • Diplôme dans un domaine pertinent tel que la Santé Publique, la Promotion de la Santé, les Sciences Sociales et Comportementales, la Communication, le Travail Social, la Psychologie, l’Anthropologie, la Sociologie, l’Éducation, ou un domaine connexe
  • Au moins 2 ans d’expérience professionnelle dans la communication sur les risques, l’engagement communautaire et le travail avec des personnes ou des communautés vulnérables
  • Expérience dans l’engagement communautaire – notamment la conception et la diffusion de messages clés ; l’écoute des membres de la communauté et la recherche de solutions ; le travail avec des populations diverses et la facilitation de sessions de renforcement des capacités
  • Une expérience antérieure dans la réponse à une épidémie d’Ebola est un atout majeur
  • Maîtrise de la communication bidirectionnelle avec les clients et les communautés
  • Expérience au sein d’une ONG nationale et/ou internationale ; une expérience avec l’IRC et une connaissance des systèmes et procédures de l’IRC sont souhaitées
  • Expérience de travail sur le terrain dans un contexte d’urgence
  • Volonté de penser et de travailler dans une perspective transversale
  • Capacité à rédiger des rapports clairs et concis
  • Bonnes compétences en planification et en organisation, et capacité à formuler des recommandations d’amélioration
  • Créatif(ve) et innovant(e), flexible et doté(e) d’un bon réseau
  • Positif(ve), très motivé(e), avec de solides compétences interpersonnelles
  • Attitude positive et professionnelle, notamment la capacité à bien travailler en équipe
  • Disponible à travailler sous pression et dans un environnement instable et dynamique
  • Maîtrise de l’outil informatique, notamment Microsoft Word et Excel
  • La maîtrise du français et des langues locales de l’Ituri est requise ; l’anglais est un avantage

opportunities.title: Grant Writing and Proposal Development Services “International Rescue Committee Poland” Foundation
opportunities.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) Poland invites qualified individual consultants and companies to submit proposals for the provision of grant writing and project development services under a Framework Agreement.

Background

IRC Poland seeks to strengthen its capacity to identify funding opportunities, develop high-quality project concepts, and prepare competitive funding applications for institutional, governmental, multilateral, private foundation, and corporate donors.

Through this procurement process, IRC intends to establish a pool of experienced grant writers and project development specialists who can provide flexible, timely, and high-quality support across humanitarian, integration, recovery, and development programming.

The Framework Agreement will be non-exclusive. IRC may engage one or multiple service providers depending on the nature, complexity, language requirements, technical expertise, and timelines of individual assignments.

The agreement does not guarantee any minimum volume or value of work. Assignments will be commissioned on an as-needed basis throughout the duration of the agreement.

Scope of Services

Selected consultants and/or companies may be requested to support various stages of the fundraising and project development process, including but not limited to:

  • Analysis of donor guidelines, funding opportunities, and grant calls;
  • Support in assessing funding opportunities and go/no-go decision-making processes;
  • Collaboration with technical, programmatic, MEAL, Grants, Partnerships, and Finance teams in project design;
  • Preparation, drafting, editing, and formatting of concept notes, Expressions of Interest (EOIs), grant proposals, annexes, and full applications;
  • Development of logframes, theories of change, workplans, and results frameworks;
  • Preparation of budget narratives and ensuring consistency between technical and financial sections;
  • Coordination and consolidation of inputs from multiple stakeholders;
  • Quality assurance reviews of application packages;
  • Technical editing, proofreading, and finalization of submission packages;
  • Incorporation of internal and donor feedback into application documents;
  • Strategic advice related to donor engagement, positioning, and fundraising.

One of the first confirmed funding opportunities expected under this Framework Agreement is the CERV Daphne Call.

Required Qualifications

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • Proven experience in preparing successful applications under programmes such as CERV, FERS/FSE+, and other national or regional funding schemes in Poland;
  • Strong knowledge of EU Funding & Tenders Portal, SOWA, and MEWA systems;
  • Excellent proposal writing and project design skills;
  • Understanding of EU and national funding regulations, budgeting principles, and eligibility requirements;
  • Experience in preparing donor-compliant budgets and supporting financial documentation;
  • Ability to effectively utilize AI-based tools while ensuring confidentiality and donor compliance;
  • Excellent written and spoken Polish and English;

Experience in the fields of human rights, migration, labour market integration, humanitarian assistance, and gender-based violence prevention will be considered an asset.

Interested applicants must submit a complete proposal package including the following documents:
