opportunities.title: Development of a set of Global Guidelines to protect boys affected by sexual exploitation and abuse
opportunities.description:
ECPAT International is a global network of organisations working together for the elimination of the sexual exploitation of children (SEC) in all its manifestations i.e., exploitation of children in prostitution, online child sexual exploitation, sale and trafficking of children for sexual purposes, sexual exploitation of children in travel and tourism and some forms of child, early and forced marriage. The ECPAT Network currently consists of 141 member organisations working at national and local levels in 113 countries.

The ECPAT International Secretariat coordinates the global work of the organisation and is based in Bangkok, Thailand. The Secretariat designs and implements global and regional level programmes, and undertakes programming, advocacy and research and facilitates a range of network initiatives.

Context of Consultancy

The ECPAT Global Boys Initiative (GBI) has conducted a series of 17 case studies collecting and documenting practices of organizations supporting boys at risk or victims and survivors of sexual exploitation and abuse https://ecpat.org/global-boys-initiative/

These case studies – with others currently in development- document practices, challenges and lessons emerging from different contexts, and highlight how services and protection responses can better take into account the specific experiences of boys. They serve as practical, locally-led examples for civil society organisations and practitioners seeking to better understand how boys are affected, how to design and implement prevention and response activities, and what resources are needed.

Across these diverse contexts, one key learning consistently emerges: despite significant differences between countries and regions, many of the challenges faced are very similar. These include stigma surrounding boys’ experiences of sexual abuse and exploitation, legal and policy barriers that limit recognition and access to protection, and investigation and response mechanisms that are often not gender-sensitive. In many contexts, these factors contribute to underreporting, limited access to services, and responses that do not fully take into account boys’ specific experiences and needs.

This work of documentation has been strongly collaborative with each local organisation and its staff, from design to review and validation of the content and final product. This process has allowed the ECPAT GBI to build knowledge that is grounded in the experience and expertise of practitioners working directly with boys and communities, while also aligning with the expertise, strategic priorities and resources of the Global Alliance for the Protection of Boys from Sexual Violence (GAPB), linking practice-based evidence with technical guidance and funding streams (OAK Boys and Carlson Family Foundation) supporting this work.

The next step, in line with the collaborative spirit of the programme, is to translate this collective learning into a set of Global Guidelines validated by practitioners, experts and other relevant stakeholders during a global event. Building on the insights generated through the case studies, available research and evidence, these Global Guidelines will aim to consolidate practical knowledge that can support organisations, service providers and policy actors in strengthening their approaches to preventing and responding to sexual abuse and exploitation against boys.

The development of the Global Guidelines will culminate in the 2027 ECPAT Global Boys Summit (GBS), which will bring together the partner practitioners from the case studies, members of the GAPB, donors and child protection agencies to validate and refine the document and discuss pathways for its implementation, uptake and dissemination.

Key Objective of The Assignment

As part of this assignment, the selected consultant will build on the learning from the ECPAT Global Boys Initiative series of case studies in working with boys affected by sexual exploitation and abuse to develop the content of the Global Guidelines, and will be required to:

  • Conduct a series of online consultations with relevant stakeholders (from local civil society organisations to international agencies) to define the content, needs to be addressed and format of the Global Guidelines;
  • Draft, review inputs and consolidate inputs from the series of case studies, survey findings and online consultations to develop the Global Guidelines;
  • Support the design of the methodology for the 2027 ECPAT Global Boys Summit and suggest sessions to help participants work on, review and validate the content and format of the Global Guidelines;
  • Support the facilitation of the 2027 ECPAT Global Boys Summit for the review and validation work, and support the creation of a dissemination and uptake plan;
  • Integrate the final inputs after the Summit and finalise the content of the Global Guidelines and the dissemination plan.

Key Deliverables

  • Summary note of the online consultations, outlining the preferences of involved stakeholders in terms of content, format and needs;
  • First draft of the Global Guidelines (including findings of the online survey and the online consultations) for review;
  • Design of a suggested methodology for the 2027 ECPAT Global Boys Summit, which includes format of the sessions for technical review and discussions for dissemination and uptake;
  • Attendance and Co-facilitation of the Summit and note-taking of key inputs and action items;
  • Final content of the Global Guidelines and supporting dissemination plan.

Timeline

This consultancy requires an estimated number of 30 working days – to be defined according to the suggested methodology – within the period 24 May 2026-mid-March 2027.

Consultant Profile

The consultant needs to have:

  • Demonstrated experience including work on similar assignments, including in developing tools for the protection of children against sexual violence and case management tools and programmes;
  • Proven knowledge and previous experience with children’s rights, child protection, or gender equity issues;
  • Experience in facilitating workshops and/or multi-stakeholder consultations;
  • Strong analytical and writing skills, with the ability to translate complex inputs into practical guidance;
  • Understanding of and commitment to the ECPAT International values;
  • Advanced ability to work in English (ability to work in Arabic, French or Spanish would be an asset);
  • Demonstrated ability to take initiative and work independently and within the established deadline;
  • Availability to participate in the 2027 ECPAT Global Boys Summit (in person) – location to be yet confirmed;
  • High ethical standards and commitment to human rights and feminist principles.

Additional Information

  • This is a home-based position using their own equipment.
  • The Consultant is expected to act at all times in a manner consistent with the values of ECPAT International and in compliance with the organisation’s policies and procedures including Safeguarding Policies and the Code of Conduct.
  • The maximum budget available for this assignment is 11,000 USD. ECPAT will cover travel and related costs separately.

Our Commitment

  • As ECPAT’s International Secretariat we recognise that our strength lies in the diversity of the people who make up our global network, staff, volunteers and consultants. We are committed to being an inclusive workplace where people of all backgrounds and cultures can strive and be themselves. This means we will challenge ourselves to do better and to continue learning, to create and maintain a working environment steeped in respect, tolerance, safety, and where all parties are valued equally.
  • As a child-focused organisation, ECPAT has a strong commitment to child safeguarding and rigorous procedures, and the successful candidate will be required to sign our 2 codes of conduct.

Fixed term | 6 months | ASAP

Convergences

Founded in 2008, Convergences is a multi-stakeholder platform for reflection, mobilisation and advocacy that promotes a just transition by fostering reflection, action and the co-creation of innovative, high-impact partnerships.

Paris headquarters coordinates global interventions and facilitates the animation and development of a global ecosystem of stakeholders committed to the 3ZERO vision, notably through Convergences and the 3ZERO House activities.

Convergences was co-founded by Acted. For over 30 years, Acted has been working alongside the most vulnerable communities to respond to humanitarian, environmental and development crises. Operating in over 40 countries, the organisation pursues a three-pronged mandate covering humanitarian, environmental and development work, and champions the vision of a 3ZERO world: Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon, Zero Poverty.

Acted ACTED - Convergences

Under the supervision of the Executive Director, the Officer in Charge of International Development is responsible for driving the expansion, structuring, and implementation of Convergences’ international activities, with a strong focus on international forums, partnerships, and fundraising.

The Officer will ensure the coherence, quality, and impact of Convergences’ international initiatives, working closely with headquarters teams, Acted country teams, and external partners.

This is a high-responsibility position equivalent to a managerial level, requiring full ownership of projects and a strong capacity to operate independently in complex and evolving environments.

The position is HQ-based requiring close collaboration with Acted’s global network and teams, as well as international multi-stakeholder ecosystems (NGOs, public sector, private sector, academia). It includes frequent interaction with high-level partners and speakers. Regular travel may be required.

  • Generate innovative ideas for new formats, geographies, and partnerships
  • Support the development of new initiatives (e.g. 3ZERO ecosystem, thematic platforms, international alliances)

Any other tasks as assigned by the Line Manager.

Expected skills and qualifications

This position requires a highly autonomous and proactive professional, able to thrive in a fast-moving and
sometimes uncertain environment:

• Self-starter with the ability to initiate, structure, and drive projects independently
• Highly autonomous with strong ownership and accountability
• Rigorous and detail-oriented, ensuring high-quality delivery
• Strong organisational, prioritisation, and multitasking skills; able to manage multiple topics simultaneously
• Dynamic, adaptable, and able to deliver results in fast-paced, high-pressure and volatile environments
• Creative and innovative, with intellectual curiosity and the ability to generate new ideas, formats,and partnerships
• Action- and solution-oriented, with strong problem-solving skills
• Strong interpersonal and diplomatic skills, with the ability to engage and collaborate with diverse stakeholders (internal and external)
• Proven ability to manage complex, multi-stakeholder projects end-to-end
• Strong experience in international development, partnerships, or event-driven ecosystems
• Experience in fundraising, proposal development, and donor engagement
• Excellent understanding of global development, sustainability, and multi-actor dialogue dynamics
• Excellent writing and summarising skills in French and English
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office (PowerPoint, Excel, Word)
• Proficiency in digital and communication tools (social media, web publishing such as WordPress, and basic graphic/video editing tools including Adobe Suite)
• Master’s degree in political science, international relations, communication, project management, sustainable development, social and solidarity economy, or equivalent
• Strong interest in climate, social, and sustainable development issues, and international cooperation
• Ability to take initiative while knowing when to seek clarification

Terms of reference

For more information about the position, click here .

Conditions

ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT

This job is part of Chad Country Office (CO). They report to the Country Director, or more senior Operational Information Management & Performance Reporting Officer or designate.

Job holders operate with a high degree of independence, are likely involved in activities and analytical work of a high complexity and contribute to Operational Information Management and Performance Reporting improvement.

JOB PURPOSE

To support all Operational Information Management and Performance Reporting (OIM & PR) activities and contribute to the establishment and presentation of standard and consistent operating picture of WFP operations and associated results that facilitate informed and timely decision-making at all levels throughout the organisation.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES (not all-inclusive, within delegated authority)

Typically, have three years or more of postgraduate professional experience in a relevant field of work, with a background and interest in international humanitarian development.

Knowledge & Skills:

  • Strong written and oral communication skills, including substantive analysis and report writing skills.
  • Able to supervise and support more junior and/or less experienced members of the team.

Language:

Fluency (level C) in English language. Intermediate knowledge (level B/C) French

opportunities.title: Consultant to Train Social Media Influencers in Sokoto and Bauchi States
opportunities.description:
BACKGROUND INFORMATION ON PLAN INTERNATIONAL

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation that advances children’s rights and equality for girls.

We believe in the power and potential of every child yet too often, this potential is suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion, and discrimination. And its girls are among those most affected. By working together with children, young people, our supporters, and partners, we strive to create a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges facing girls and all vulnerable children.

We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood. And we enable children to prepare for, and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge.

We have been building powerful partnerships for children for over 85 years, and are now active in more than 80 countries.

Read more about Plan International's Nigeria’s Country Strategy to empower 20 million girls in Nigeria to take action and drive change at https://plan-international.org/nigeria/

BACKGROUND/CONTEXT

At Plan International Nigeria, strategic visibility is a core component of how we advance programme outcomes, strengthen stakeholder engagement, while reinforcing our commitment to sustainable, people-centered impact. In the context of of Social and Behaviour Change Communication (SBCC), visibility helps amplify evidence-based interventions that influence attitudes, challenge harmful social and gender norms, and promote positive behaviours among adolescents, young people, and communities.

As digital platforms continue to shape opinions and behaviours, social media has become an increasingly important channel for development communication, particularly among young people. In Northern Nigeria, especially in Bauchi and Sokoto States, platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, and WhatsApp play a growing role in how information is consumed and shared. However, communication in these contexts must be culturally sensitive, locally relevant, and accessible, including the use of Hausa and simplified English where appropriate.

Under the Global Affairs Canada (GAC)-funded Aspire project, Plan International Nigeria is implementing interventions that advance girls’ rights, education, protection, and empowerment. As part of the project’s SBCC strategy, there is a need to strengthen the capacity of selected social media influencers in Bauchi and Sokoto States to serve as credible digital advocates for approved project messaging. Leveraging trusted local influencers, particularly micro-influencers with strong community ties, can significantly enhance message reach, strengthen credibility, and support positive social and behaviour change outcomes.

To support this objective, Plan International Nigeria seeks to engage a qualified consultant with strong technical and creative expertise to train identified social media influencers across the two intervention states (Bauchi and Sokoto) on effective content creation and social media management for social media, while ensuring alignment with Plan International’s approved messaging, safeguarding standards, brand requirements, and communication dos and don’ts.

This engagement is intended to support the development of digital content that will;

  • Promote positive sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) behaviours
  • Challenge harmful social and gender norms
  • Encourage positive masculinity
  • Increase awareness and utilisation of Adolescent Corners as safe, confidential, and adolescent-friendly service delivery points

PURPOSE OF THE CONSULTANCY:

The purpose of this consultancy is to strengthen the capacity of selected social media influencers in Bauchi and Sokoto States to communicate Aspire Project messages accurately, responsibly, and effectively across digital platforms. The consultant will design and deliver a structured training and mentoring process that equips influencers with the practical skills, content development tools, and strategic understanding required to produce high-quality, culturally relevant, and audience-appropriate digital content aligned with Plan International Nigeria’s communication priorities.

The consultancy is expected to contribute to the following outcomes:

  • strengthened influencer understanding of Plan International Nigeria’s mandate, tone, safeguarding commitments, and campaign priorities
  • improved message discipline, with influencers able to communicate agreed key messages clearly, accurately, and consistently across platforms
  • responsible storytelling that reflects dignity, informed consent, and do-no-harm principles, especially when featuring children, survivors, or vulnerable communities
  • stronger content quality, including improved structure, clarity, visual quality, captions, and calls to action aligned with campaign objectives
  • increased ability to translate complex issues such as girls’ rights, education, protection, and Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) into simple, audience-friendly messages without misinformation or harmful framing

The Brand and Communications team will remain closely engaged throughout the process to provide guidance on messaging alignment, quality assurance, and overall communication coherence.

This consultancy will also support the development of digital content that:

  • promotes adolescents’ and young people’s knowledge of Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR)
  • encourages positive attitudes and behaviours related to SRHR
  • increases awareness and utilisation of Adolescent Corners as safe, confidential, and adolescent-friendly service delivery points in Bauchi and Sokoto States

All content developed under this engagement must resonate with a wide range of audiences, including adolescents, young people, donors, partners, programme participants, and the general public, while clearly reflecting Plan International Nigeria’s values. The assignment must adhere to ethical, safeguarding, and child protection standards, and contribute to stronger SBCC visibility, advocacy, and stakeholder engagement under the Aspire Project.

RECOMMENDED TRAINING SCOPE

The consultant will design and deliver a practical, context-responsive training programme for selected social media influencers in Bauchi and Sokoto States. The training should equip participants with the knowledge, tools, and applied skills required to create accurate,engaging, and audience-appropriate content that aligns with Aspire Project priorities and Plan International Nigeria’s brand and communication standards. At the minimum, the training should cover the following areas;

  • Plan International Nigeria brand and communication essentials: organisational voice and tone, visual standards, logo and brand use, and clear guidance on what is permissible and not permissible in public-facing content
  • Messaging architecture and message discipline: approved key messages, message hierarchy, what to say and what not to say, audience segmentation, and call-to-action framing to ensure clarity, consistency, and alignment across platforms
  • Narrative framing and content strategy: storytelling approaches that work across formats such as reels, carousels, threads, and short-form videos, including how to develop strong hooks, structure content effectively, and drive purposeful engagement
  • Digital storytelling for behaviour change: how to translate themes such as girls’ rights, education, protection, positive masculinity, and Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) into relatable, audience-friendly content that supports positive social and behaviour change
  • Safeguarding and do-no-harm principles: informed consent, privacy, safe and dignified representation of children and communities, management of sensitive topics, and escalation protocols where necessary
  • Accuracy and misinformation management: fact-checking basics, avoiding misquotes, preserving context integrity, source discipline, and reducing the risk of misinformation or harmful framing when communicating sensitive issues
  • Content creation and production skills: practical guidance on scripting, caption writing, filming and editing basics, short-form video production, subtitling, accessible design, and inclusive language
  • Audience engagement and community management: comment moderation, responding to sensitive questions, handling backlash, identifying harmful narratives, and applying appropriate referral pathways where required
  • Content planning and campaign delivery: campaign calendar alignment, posting cadence, content sequencing, creative direction interpretation, and approval or review checkpoints
  • Practical application: development of draft scripts, captions, sample posts, short-form video concepts, and mini content plans linked to ASPIRE Project priorities

To support measurement of training effectiveness and post-training performance, the training should also include a social media analytics and performance tracking component, covering:

  • introduction to key platform metrics and what they mean
  • how to track performance by post and by platform
  • how to assess whether content is meeting communication objectives
  • basic interpretation of analytics to improve future content decisions
  • use of a simple reporting template to track reach, impressions, engagement, video views, completion rate, audience growth, and audience feedback themes

Overall, the training should be practical, output-oriented, and tailored to the digital realities of Bauchi and Sokoto States, with a clear focus on strengthening message quality, content effectiveness, responsible storytelling, and measurable behaviour-change communication outcomes.

POST-TRAINING OUTCOMES AND MEASUREMENT

To ensure that the training leads to measurable improvements in content dissemination and quality, the consultant will establish a practical post-training performance and reporting approach.

Following the training, influencers should be able to:

  • develop and implement content dissemination plans aligned with campaign priorities
  • create and publish content that reflects agreed messaging and quality standards
  • track and report content performance consistently across platforms
  • demonstrate improved confidence and competence in digital advocacy, storytelling, and responsible audience engagement

The consultant will:

  • guide influencers to develop a post-training content dissemination plan, including platforms, timelines, content formats, and intended audiences
  • provide simple analytics reporting template to be used consistently by all influencers
  • ensure that the following minimum indicators are captured for each post, where applicable:
  • reach/impressions
  • engagements, including likes, comments, shares, and saves
  • video views and completion rate
  • link clicks/click-through rate, where links are used
  • audience growth during the campaign period
  • top-performing content type and key audience feedback themes

Reporting cadence:

  • weekly reporting during the campaign activation period
  • one consolidated endline summary at the close of the activation cycle

The consultant will also support the compilation of influencer reports into a summary dashboard or report showing:

  • Total content produced and published
  • Total reach and engagement across influencers
  • compliance with approved messaging, brand, and safeguarding expectations
  • level of message penetration across published content
  • key lessons learned and recommendations for future influencer engagement cycles

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Consultant Responsibilities

The consultant will be responsible for the end-to-end design, delivery, mentoring, and reporting of the influencer training and content development process under the Aspire Project. The role is expected to strengthen the capacity of selected social media influencers to serve as credible digital advocates who can communicate project messages effectively, responsibly, and in ways that support Social and Behaviour Change Communication (SBCC) outcomes.

Specifically, the consultant will:

  • Design the training approach: develop the training agenda, methodology, session materials, and facilitation tools in alignment with Plan International Nigeria’s communication standards, safeguarding expectations, and the Aspire Project objectives.
  • Deliver technical training: facilitate practical sessions on digital advocacy, message discipline, narrative framing, content strategy, responsible storytelling, platform-specific content creation, audience engagement, and content planning.
  • Strengthen message delivery: build influencers’ capacity to communicate approved ASPIRE key messages clearly, accurately, and consistently across digital platforms, while adapting content to audience needs and platform formats.
  • Promote responsible content creation: ensure that influencers are guided to produce content that is culturally sensitive, audience-appropriate, and reflective of dignity, informed consent, and do-no-harm principles, particularly when addressing sensitive issues or featuring vulnerable groups.
  • Enhance content production skills: strengthen influencers’ practical skills in scripting, caption writing, short-form video production, filming, editing, subtitling, and the development of engaging digital content, with particular emphasis on platforms such as TikTok and Instagram Reels.
  • Lead practical content development: facilitate hands-on exercises and support influencers to produce draft scripts, captions, sample posts, short-form video concepts, and mini content plans aligned with campaign priorities.
  • Provide tools and templates: develop and share participant resource packs, including key messages, content guidance, do’s and don’ts, sample content formats, and simple analytics reporting templates to support consistent content production and performance tracking.
  • Strengthen engagement and misinformation response: guide influencers on comment moderation, audience interaction, managing backlash, responding to sensitive questions, and addressing misinformation or harmful narratives in ways that protect message integrity and audience trust.
  • Ensure quality and alignment: ensure that all training content and influencer outputs remain evidence-informed, contextually relevant, and aligned with Plan International Nigeria’s voice, values, and communication expectations.
  • Support behaviour change objectives: ensure that the training and subsequent influencer content contribute to promoting adolescents’ and young people’s knowledge of Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR), encouraging positive attitudes and behaviours related to SRHR, and increasing awareness and utilisation of Adolescent Corners as safe, confidential, and adolescent-friendly service delivery points in Bauchi and Sokoto States.
  • Mentor influencers post-training: provide post-training mentoring and technical guidance to strengthen application of learning, improve content quality, and support influencers during the activation phase.
  • Document and report results: submit a post-training report capturing participation, training outcomes, practical outputs developed, key risks or issues identified, lessons learned, recommendations, and next steps.

The consultant will ensure that all content developed by the trained influencers resonates with a wide range of audiences, including adolescents, young people, donors, partners, programme participants, and the general public, while clearly reflecting Plan International Nigeria’s values. All processes and outputs under this assignment must adhere to ethical, safeguarding, and child protection standards and contribute to strengthened SBCC visibility, advocacy, and stakeholder engagement under the Aspire Project.

DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

Total duration: 20 working days including travel days (10 days in Bauchi (3 days training, 2 days report writing and 5 days mentoring) and 10days in Sokoto ((3 days training, 2 days report writing and 5 days mentoring))

A detailed implementation schedule will be agreed with Plan International Nigeria prior to commencement of the assignment.

COORDINATION AND REPORTING

The consultant will report to the Project Manager, Aspire Project, and work closely with the Brand and Communications team at Plan International Nigeria.

Throughout the assignment, the consultant will work closely with the Brand and Communications team and relevant programme staff to ensure that all training materials, practical outputs, and influencer-generated content align with Plan International Nigeria’s approved messaging, brand, and communication standards.

The consultant will ensure that all content created and shared by the social media influencers aligns with the Aspire project’s SBCC 13 thematic areas, which are:

  1. The Right of Adolescent Girls and Young Women (AGYWs) to make informed choices concerning sexual activity and say no when they mean no
  2. Prevention against sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse.
  3. Building confidence among (AGYWs) to seek Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) services including Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Services (MPHSS) at the adolescents’ Friendly Centers.
  4. Create awareness on the availability of (SRHR) services including Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Services (MHPSS) at the adolescents Friendly Centres
  5. Promote joint inclusive decision making among spouses in child spacing and when to have children.
  6. Promote spousal communication in relation to accessing Child Spacing Services.
  7. Discouraging Child Early and Forced Marriage
  8. Creating awareness on proper management of menstrual hygiene
  9. Promoting positive spousal support during pregnancy, labor and after delivery including birth preparedness.
  10. Promote positive masculinity among adolescent boys and male community members.
  11. Promote positive health provider attitudes towards (AGYWs) including those with disabilities and almajiris.
  12. Promote safe spaces for (AGYWs) in school environment including increased access to SRHS information and services, availability of Sexual and Gender Based Violence (SGBV) prevention mechanisms (policies/guidelines and reporting channels)
  13. Portraying the impacts of Village Savings and Loans Association (VSLA Adashen Gata) among older adolescents and women

In addition, the consultant will ensure that all training content aligns with Plan International Nigeria’s strategic priorities and thematic focus areas, including:

  • Gender Equality
    • Child Rights and Protection
      • Education
      • Health and Nutrition
      • Youth Empowerment
      • Livelihoods and Economic Inclusion

CONSULTANT QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The consultant/vendor must demonstrate the following qualifications and experience:

  • proven experience in digital communications, social media strategy, or influencer engagement in Nigeria

  • strong understanding of the socio-cultural context of Northern Nigeria, particularly Bauchi and Sokoto States

  • demonstrated experience working with youth influencers, content creators, or digital advocates

  • strong knowledge of major digital platforms, especially TikTok and Instagram, including short-form video trends and audience engagement approaches

  • fluency in English, with Hausa proficiency considered a strong advantage

  • prior experience working with NGOs, development projects, or social impact initiatives, particularly those focused on gender, youth, education, protection, or SRHR.

  • demonstrated ability to work independently, manage multiple deliverables, and meet agreed timelines while adhering to quality, safeguarding, and ethical standards.

    CONTRACT & PAYMENT TERMS

  • Please note that, if successful, Plan International’s standard terms of payment are within 30 days after the receipt of the invoice, or after acceptance of the Goods/Services/Works, if later.

    Additional information, along with all relevant annexes, can be accessed through this link: https://tinyurl.com/c3avapr3

opportunities.title: Project Officer – AI and Emerging Technologies
opportunities.description:
The Centre for Humanitarian Dialogue (HD) is a private diplomacy organisation founded on the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence. Its mission is to help prevent, mitigate and resolve armed conflict through dialogue and mediation. HD operates in more than 40 countries with more than 300 staff. HD is currently looking for a:

Project Officer – AI and Emerging Technologies

Location: Flexible (Central European Time, or nearby time-zone, preferred)

Starting date: 1 June 2026

Full-time

AI is reshaping the risk landscape for international security. Diplomacy is still adjusting. HD helps close that gap – and is looking for a key team member.

HD’s AI and Emerging Technologies programme (AIET) convenes officials, technologists and experts from around the world in discreet, outcome-oriented dialogues that complement formal diplomatic and multilateral processes on AI governance. Where formal channels are constrained, HD creates the space for frank, practical conversations that help address risks.

The programme has two main areas of work: an established dialogue track on military applications of AI and a growing track on civilian advanced AI (‘frontier AI’), convening governments, AI labs and technical experts on the governance challenges posed by advanced AI. Both tracks aim to support and facilitate the adoption of pragmatic and effective national and international measures to address high-priority risks posed by AI for international security, stability and conflict dynamics.

As Project Officer you will support the operations and activities of the AIET programme, covering both tracks. You will work within HD’s Digital Conflict Directorate, which comprises four programmes: cyber diplomacy; social media and conflict mediation; AI and emerging technologies; and outer space.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and run project activities on military AI and advanced AI:
    • Organize and facilitate dialogues, consultations and other diplomatic outreach on military AI and advanced AI (drafting meeting agendas, liaising with participants, facilitating key sessions where relevant and co-developing background materials and outcome papers)
    • Monitor, research and analyse key developments in AI and international security, and translate them into programme insights, for example on military AI – decision-support systems and autonomous systems – and on advanced AI –accidental and deliberate misuse risks (e.g. impact on critical infrastructure, CBRN-related).
  • Build relationships and represent HD’s AIET team
    • Develop and maintain links with relevant experts in governments, AI companies, expert communities, partner organisations, donors and multilateral bodies
    • Represent HD at meetings and in engagements with officials and experts on AI
    • Collaborate with HD country teams and regional offices on region-specific diplomatic activities.
  • Contribute to donor relations, reporting and strategic development of the AIET programme
    • Ensure projects are implemented and reported on in a timely manner, drafting project reports as required
    • Draft project documents and concept notes
    • Contribute to fundraising efforts and donor relations
    • Contribute to the strategic planning for the AI team and the Digital Conflict Directorate

You might be the right person for this role if you:

  • Have at least 4-5 years’ experience working in AI policy and/or peace and conflict, disarmament, diplomacy, technology policy or a closely related area
  • Bring subject matter expertise on military applications of AI and/or advanced AI safety, including familiarity with key government positions and international governance initiatives
  • Have an existing network in the AI governance space - including governments, AI companies, experts or multilateral bodies
  • Hold a relevant Master’s degree (e.g. peace and conflict studies, international relations, technology policy or related field)
  • Are comfortable operating in varied diplomatic settings and engaging with a range of interlocutors with political astuteness
  • Write and communicate excellently
  • Thrive in a small, entrepreneurial team working on fast-moving and high-stakes issues
  • Are an excellent English speaker; other languages are an asset.
