opportunities.title: Consultant to Design and Develop the Air4Laos Mobile Application
opportunities.description:
Purpose and Objectives:

The Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) is an autonomous international organization that works to build the resilience of people and institutions to disasters and climate change impacts in Asia and the Pacific.

Under the U.S.-Thailand-Laos Cooperation on Transboundary Haze Management, SERVIR Southeast Asia has co-developed Air4Laos with the Lao PDR Ministry of Agriculture and Environment (MAE) - a web-based platform integrating satellite-derived PM2.5 estimates, ground station measurements, forecasts, and fire hotspot information for Lao PDR. Following provincial training and community demonstration events in Vientiane Capital, Luang Prabang, and Champasak, participants consistently requested a mobile version of the tool to make air quality information accessible to the general public on smartphones.

ADPC therefore seeks a qualified consultant to design and develop a native mobile application for Air4Laos, with a Lao-English bilingual interface, in accordance with the Air4Laos Mobile App Feature List attached to this ToR as Annex A, which forms an integral part of this assignment. The application will consume data from the existing Air4Laos backend services; apart from the notification and alerting services required under this assignment, no new data processing infrastructure is required.

Measurable objectives include:

  1. Deliver a complete UI/UX design for the Air4Laos mobile application covering the four core screens, notifications, and settings, consistent with the Feature List at Annex A
  2. Develop a fully functional mobile application for Android and iOS covering the Home, Map, Statistics, and News screens with the features specified at Annex A
  3. Implement the Notifications and Alerts module, including threshold-triggered bad-air alerts based on the official Lao PDR air quality standard
  4. Deliver the settings and supporting features, including the Lao-English bilingual interface, home-screen widget, and low-bandwidth operation
  5. Complete publication to the application stores, documentation, and full source code transfer to ADPC

Expected Outputs: The consultant shall deliver the following specific and measurable outputs:

  1. UI/UX design package covering the Home, Map, Statistics, and News screens, the Notifications and Alerts flow, and the Settings screen, including navigation flow and design assets.
  2. Functional beta build of the Air4Laos mobile application for Android and iOS, installable for testing by the ADPC team.
  3. Completed Air4Laos mobile application for Android and iOS, integrated with the existing Air4Laos backend services and tested on representative devices, comprising:
    • Home screen - current PM2.5 reading for the user's location with colour-coded health recommendation and practical action icons; data source label switching dynamically between the NASA GEOS-5 model and the nearest ground station; temperature, wind speed, and rainfall; 3-day forecast at 3-hour intervals; 24-48 hour historical trend graph; last data update timestamp; location search by village, district, and province; multiple saved locations; share function; news and alert banner; and unit and standard toggle
    • Map screen - toggle between the satellite-derived spatial PM2.5 layer and ground-station point data; colour-coded PM2.5 index legend; zoom-to-my-location function; search by village, district, and province; and data source credits (MAE, SERVIR SEA, NASA GEOS-5)
    • Statistics screen - ranking of villages, districts, and provinces by PM2.5 from highest to lowest; ranking level toggle (district within province, province within country); default to the user's own location; ranking date and time; and colour-coded index legend
    • News screen - localized news feed on haze and PM2.5 filtered to Lao PDR, including relevant Thailand-side coverage; and an educational content library explaining PM2.5, its health effects, and the causes of haze, presented separately from news headlines
  4. Notifications and Alerts module, comprising the bad-air push notification triggered when PM2.5 crosses into an unhealthy category under the official Lao PDR air quality standard; adjustable alert sensitivity; independent alerts for each saved location; daily digest notification; next-day forecast alert; fire and hotspot proximity alert using existing satellite hotspot detection data; SOP-trigger advisory for designated local officials, tied to the project's standard operating protocol thresholds; and an alert history log.
  5. Settings and supporting features, comprising the Lao-English bilingual interface; home-screen widget for Android and iOS showing live PM2.5 without opening the application; selector for units and for the air quality standard applied (Lao PDR and US EPA); feedback button on each screen; and offline and low-bandwidth operation suitable for rural provinces.
  6. Publication of the application to Google Play and the Apple App Store on behalf of ADPC, using ADPC-owned developer accounts, including build files, signing configuration, store listing assets, and deployment instructions.
  7. User manual and administrator manual, in English, covering installation, operation, configuration, and troubleshooting.
  8. Complete source code transferred to the ADPC repository, with commented code, dependency documentation, and build instructions - by 30 September 2026.

All outputs will be documented in English and shared in digital format compatible with ADPC systems. The application interface shall support both Lao and English. All features shall conform to the Air4Laos Mobile App Feature List at Annex A, with the exception of the user-submitted haze and visibility reporting function and the SMS-based alert fallback, which are excluded from the scope of this assignment.

Responsibilities and Tasks: The consultant shall be responsible for the following tasks:

Design

  • Design the UI/UX of the Air4Laos mobile application in accordance with the Feature List at Annex A, adapting the My Air reference design to the Lao PDR context
  • Design the Lao-English bilingual interface and coordinate with ADPC on Lao-language content and terminology

Development

  • Lead the front-end and back-end development of the mobile application for both Android and iOS
  • Integrate the application with existing Air4Laos data services, including satellite-derived PM2.5 estimates, ground station observations, forecasts, and fire hotspot data
  • Implement location search and multiple saved locations at village, district, and province levels
  • Implement the historical trend graph, share function, and the selector for units and air quality standard (Lao PDR and US EPA)
  • Develop the home-screen widget for both Android and iOS
  • Ensure the application operates reliably under low-bandwidth conditions typical of rural Lao PDR, including appropriate caching and offline behavior

Notifications and alerts

  • Develop and configure the push notification service for PM2.5 threshold alerts based on the official Lao PDR air quality standard, with adjustable sensitivity and independent settings for each saved location
  • Implement the daily digest notification, next-day forecast alert, and fire and hotspot proximity alert
  • Implement the SOP-trigger advisory for designated local officials, including the access control required to restrict it to authorized users
  • Implement the alert history log

Testing, deployment, and handover

  • Provide support on code versioning and code maintenance in the ADPC GitHub repository
  • Troubleshoot bugs and errors during the development and testing cycles
  • Conduct testing on representative Android and iOS devices and address feedback from ADPC review
  • Publish the application to Google Play and the Apple App Store on behalf of ADPC, using ADPC-owned developer accounts
  • Prepare user and administrator manuals and hand over the complete source code to ADPC

Working Principles: The consultant will report to the Air Quality Thematic Lead, SERVIR Southeast Asia, ADPC.

Qualifications: The consultant should possess the following minimal competencies:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Geo-informatics, Remote Sensing, or a related field
  • At least 3 years of professional experience in mobile application development, with a demonstrated portfolio of published applications
  • Proven experience developing map-based or geospatial mobile applications
  • Proficiency in cross-platform mobile development frameworks (e.g., Flutter, React Native) or native Android and iOS development
  • Experience integrating mobile applications with REST APIs and geospatial web services
  • Experience implementing push notification services (e.g., Firebase Cloud Messaging), including threshold-triggered and scheduled notifications
  • Experience developing home-screen widgets for Android and iOS
  • Experience building offline-capable or low-bandwidth-tolerant mobile applications, including local caching strategies
  • Experience implementing multilingual interfaces and localization
  • Ability to design and develop UI/UX for mobile applications, with good understanding of typography and colour theory
  • Demonstrated experience with application store submission and release processes for both Google Play and the Apple App Store
  • Ability to work with Lao-language content and to coordinate on translation and localization
  • Working knowledge of relational database models such as PostgreSQL and MySQL
  • Basic understanding of satellite remote sensing and air quality data is an advantage
  • Professional experience in the Lower Mekong region desired
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English

Duty Station: Home-based.

Duration: The contract will be for a period of 2 months between August 2026- September 2026.

Itinerary: There is no travel expected on this consultancy.

Condition of payment: Payment will be phased and based on completion and acceptance of deliverables as follows:

Phase 1 - Inception and Design:

  • Kick-off meeting (virtual), review of the Feature List at Annex A and the reference UI design, and confirmation of the technical approach

Phase 2 - Development:

  • Development of the four core screens, backend integration, the Notifications and Alerts module, and the settings and supporting features

Phase 3 - Testing and Refinement:

  • ADPC review and device testing, with iterative correction of defects and refinement of the user interface

Phase 4 - Publication and Handover:

  • Preparation of store listings, submission, and release on Google Play and the Apple App Store on behalf of ADPC

Payment Schedule:

  1. Acceptance of the UI/UX design package for the Air4Laos mobile application - 40%
  2. Acceptance of the completed Air4Laos mobile application for Android and iOS, including the Notifications and Alerts module and the settings and supporting features - 40%
  3. Acceptance of the user and administrator manuals, publication to the application stores, and source code transfer - 20%

Selection Method: The consultant will be selected in accordance with ADPC’s recruitment process.

opportunities.title: RESPONSABLE FINANCE
opportunities.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Rattaché·e au Responsable de Département Finance, votre mission principale consistera à assurer la gestion comptable et financière de la base dans le respect des procédures définies pour la mission et du cadre de gestion ACF
Plus spécifiquement, vos missions seront les suivantes :
Assurer la comptabilité de la base
Assurer et animer la gestion de la trésorerie
Mettre en oeuvre et assurer le suivi de la collaboration et la coordination financière et budgétaire avec les partenaires de la mission
Encadrer et accompagner l'équipe Finance de la base.

Profile :

Vous êtes titulaires d'un diplôme de niveau Bac+2/3 en finance et/ou gestion, vous justifiez d'une expérience professionnelle d'au moins 2 ans sur un poste similaire dont au moins une année sur le terrain au sein d'une ONG internationale.
Vous avez une bonne connaissance de la budgétisation bailleurs, de gestion financière, vous connaissez le logiciel SAGA et vous avez une bonne maîtrise d'Excel.
Vous avez d'excellentes aptitudes au travail d'équipe et la capacité d'établir de bonnes relations tant en interne qu'en externe.
Vous avez une parfaite maitrise du français et des notions d'anglais.
Une précédente expérience avec ACF est un atout et une connaissance du pays est un plus.

Conditions d'emploi

La vaccination contre le Mpox est recommandée pour les salarié·e·s qui se rendent dans le pays.
Contrat à durée déterminée d'usage de droit français : 6 mois
Salaire mensuel brut : de 2332 euros à 2676 euros en fonction de l'expérience, incluant 13ème mois
Remboursement assurance retraite pour les citoyens non français : 16% du salaire mensuel brut
Augmentation du salaire de base : 6% tous les 12 mois de contrat continu
Per diem et frais de vie mensuels : 1105$ nets, versés sur le terrain
Allocation contexte mensuelle : 450euros
Allocation enfant : 1500euros par an et par enfant présent dans le pays d'origine (plafond de 6000euros/an)
Transport et logement : Prise en charge des déplacements et logement collectif
Couverture Médicale : 100% de la prise en charge des cotisations santé et assurance rapatriement, de vos frais médicaux et ce jusqu'à 1 mois après la fin de votre contrat
Dispositifs de maintien de salaire (maladie, maternité, paternité)Congés et RnR : 25 jours par an de CP et 20 RnR par an ; prise en charge du billet avec plafond pour se rendre sur la zone de break choisie, et 215euros d'indemnité forfaitaire par RnR
Accompagnement et formation
Suivi et accompagnement parcours professionnel
Accès illimité et gratuit à plateforme d'e-learning Talentsoft
Conditions particulières : déplacements à prévoir en Région Ituri, Drodro, Mongbwalu, Jiba, Lita

Fixed term contract: 4 months, from 21/09/2026

PUI around the world

With its 40 years of experience, Première Urgence Internationale :

  • Supports close to 6 millions beneficiaries
  • With more than 100 millions € yearly budget
  • Present in 22 countries, on 5 continents

Thanks to the work and commitment of :

  • More than 2000 national staffs
  • Around 200 expatriates from 45 different nationalities
  • And 90 employees at HQ

PUI works in 10 areas of intervention and distinguishes itself by the implementation of an integrated approach in its response. This method aims to identify and understand the needs of all those affected by a crisis. Our teams come together to bring a rapid global response to the basic needs of populations affected by humanitarian crises to help them regain independence and dignity.

Learn more on our history, our values, our areas of intervention.

What about the Deputy Country Director for Programs ?

As Deputy Country Director for Programs (DCD-P) you will be responsible for the implementation of the programs across the different bases, ensuring the steering and the development of a pertinent, appropriate and technically sound program strategy. For this purpose, you will be responsible for :

  • Programs: You will be in charge of program implementation, ensuring that programs progress in accordance with PUI charter and complying with internal technical guidelines and contractual procedures. You will be responsible for the follow up of programs achievement at mission level. You will be in charge of challenging Bases on quality need for improvement.
  • Development/Strategy: You will lead the needs and gaps analysis, and suggest new operations according to the needs identified in direct coordination with the Field and Technical Coordinators. You will lead the donor mapping to develop the fundraising strategy.
  • Human resources: You will manage directly the Technical Coordination Team, and ensure that the Field Coordinators and Deputy Field Coordinators are properly supported by them.
  • Representation: By delegation from the Head of Mission, you will ensure and coordinate PUI’s representation at national level among partners, donors and authorities. You will participate in technical forums (Working groups).
  • Coordination: You will ensure effective interaction between the Technical Coordination Team and the bases. You will also ensure that the technical coordination department is properly liaising with the support coordinators.
  • Logistics, administrative and financial monitoring: You will be involved in direct collaboration with the Technical Coordinators in the global oversight of links between the technical coordination department and logistics, HR and administrative departments. You will guarantee that the implementation of all activities is done while respecting all internal and external logistics and administrative frames.

The challenges that await you

  • Fundraising to ensure the programmatic continuity of both operational bases
  • Answer to the humanitarian crisis generated by the double earthquake in June 2026.

What you will need to succeed

  • Training: You hold a Master’s degree in a field related to Project Management, international development and/or social sciences. Training in Public Health / Protection / Livelihood and/or Shelter will be valued.
  • Experience: Strengthened by minimum 4 years managing multi-sectorial humanitarian projects (among which at least 2 years in coordination position) and strong experience in project management, you also have experience in assessing needs and developing proposals, in external representation and in team management. You already worked with Première Urgence Internationale? It would be a definite asset!
  • Skills: You master project management and team management, you demonstrate strong knowledge in donor requirements and expectations, particularly ECHO, BHA, WFP, UNHCR, CDCS, AFD and BPRM, you also have excellent writing skills (especially for proposals and reporting).
  • Qualities: You have strong leadership skills and ability to make decisions, a sense of analysis (discernment, pragmatism) and synthesis. You are a good negotiator and communicator, both in writing and orally. You demonstrate organization skills, rigor, flexibility, and capacity to remain calm and level-headed.
  • Languages: Spanish and English have no secrets for you! All the better, they are both mandatory for this position. If you speak French also, it would be a definite asset.

A word from the manager

« Join our team to be part of PUI humanitarian response and help design and implement integrated activities to address Venezuela’s complex and multi layered crisis! »

PUI will offer you

  • Status : Cadre with a Fixed-Term Contract
  • Monthly Gross Income : 2 970,00 – 3 330,00 EUR depending on your experience in International Solidarity + 50€ per semester of seniority with PUI
  • Insurance including medical coverage and complementary healthcare, 24/24 assistance and repatriation
  • Housing in individual accommodation
  • Daily Living Expenses (« Per Diem »)
  • Paid Leaves Policy: 5 weeks of paid leaves per year + return ticket every 6 months
  • Break Policy: in addition to paid leaves mentioned above, 1 R&R of 5 working days + break allowance (frequency liked with the duration of contract)

Our commitments

PUI is committed to preventing all forms of inappropriate behavior in the workplace, including harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity, and financial misconduct, while promoting the well-being of children and adults with whom PUI interacts.
PUI expects all employees to fulfill their professional duties and responsibilities in accordance with PUI’s Ethical Framework. All employees will receive appropriate training and commit to promoting, disseminating, and upholding the principles set forth in its Ethical Charter.
The holder of this position may potentially have access to personal data concerning children and vulnerable adults as part of their work (Category 2 in the safe recruitment risk classification). Consequently, all recruitments will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate background checks, which include criminal record and counter-terrorism financing checks.
Première Urgence Internationale considers the diversity of nationalities, genders, beliefs, backgrounds, and statuses within its Human Resources as a major asset for its humanitarian work. The organization is therefore committed to strictly upholding the principle of non-discrimination throughout its recruitment process.
We are dedicated to ensuring diversity and gender equality within our organization and strongly encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply.
Please note that Première Urgence Internationale shall not in any case request a financial contribution for administrative costs related to recruitment. Any such information would be fraudulent, please disregard it.

Early applications are encouraged, as we may close the process earlier than the deadline mentioned above if a suitable candidate is identified.

You recognize yourself in this profile and you adhere to our commitments? You feel ready to take up the challenge and to join PUI great family?

opportunities.title: Coordinateur.rice Finance et RH - MSF OCP Pool des Urgences F/H
opportunities.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

En collaboration avec la Cellule des Urgences et le chef de mission, le Coordinateur Finances et RH organise la gestion qualitative du personnel (national et international), supervise la gestion financière et veille à l’exactitude, au respect des délais et à l’intégrité de celle-ci. Il.elle veille à l’exhaustivité et à l’exactitude des rapports budgétaires et financiers pour la mission et au respect des politiques et procédures MSF en matière de finances, d’administration et de ressources humaines, de manière à réaliser avec efficacité les objectifs de la mission et à garder un strict contrôle sur l’allocation des ressources. Membre de l'équipe de coordination, il effectue de fréquentes visites sur les terrains afin de mesurer la bonne adéquation entre les moyens humains et financiers et les activités. Nous recherchons 2 profils dont 1 à dominante RH et 1 à dominante Finance.

Principales responsabilités

  • Être un membre actif de l’équipe de coordination de la mission et contribuer à la définition de ses objectifs et de ses plans stratégiques.
  • En tant que membre de l’équipe de coordination et en étroite collaboration avec elle et les responsables de terrain, définir et mettre en place la structure organisationnelle de la mission, élaborer les organigrammes et les descriptifs de postes, déterminer les différents niveaux de responsabilités et de délégation de pouvoirs, afin d’assurer la mise en œuvre efficace de la stratégie de la mission et d’établir une organisation génératrice de valeur.
  • En collaboration avec l’équipe de coordination, et les responsables terrain planifier les besoins opérationnels et budgétaires des RH afin de s’assurer de disposer à la fois des ressources humaines et des capacités nécessaires à la mission
  • Aider l’équipe de coordination lors des processus de recrutement, s’assurer d’une gestion cohérente des procédures administratives et juridiques dans l’ensemble de la mission (recrutement, fin de contrat, paiement des impôts nationaux et locaux, bonne tenue des dossiers du personnel, gestion des heures supplémentaires, etc.) de manière à répondre aux besoins en ressources de manière appropriée et en accord avec les principes de safeguarding
  • Aider l’équipe de coordination à déterminer les besoins de formation en fonction des exigences opérationnelles, à évaluer les performances du personnel et à mettre en œuvre les plans d’actions destinés à améliorer les capacités des membres du personnel et leur contribution aux objectifs de la mission.
  • Définir et coordonner la mise en place sur le terrain, conformément aux pratiques MSF et aux réglementations locales, vérifier mensuellement le calcul des salaires et des impôts, élaborer une politique de rémunération juste de manière à assurer l’équité en interne, la compétitivité voulue et la conformité juridique.
  • Coordonner la mise en œuvre, conformément aux politiques MSF, des politiques de L&D.
  • Définir et coordonner la politique de communication interne, en collaboration avec toutes les équipes de coordination sur le terrain, organiser les réunions du personnel et promouvoir les valeurs et la vision de MSF afin de renforcer l’engagement et la participation active du personnel et son adhésion aux valeurs de l’organisation.
  • Coordonner la mise en œuvre de l’ensemble des procédures et protocoles administratifs locaux, organiser des réunions d’information régulières avec tout le personnel, participer de manière systématique aux briefings de tous les coordinateurs et gestionnaires concernés (nationaux et internationaux), superviser les processus administratifs pour le personnel expatrié, gérer les conflits qui surviennent de manière à garantir le respect du droit du travail et améliorer l’image de leur employeur.
  • Coordonner, en étroite coopération avec les services médicaux, la mise en œuvre des protocoles de sûreté, de sécurité et médicaux afin d’assurer des conditions de travail saines et sans risque tant au personnel de la capitale qu’à celui du terrain.
  • Actif support aux managers dans la résolution des conflits entre membres du personnel (national et expatrié).
  • Coordonner la mise en place du logiciel Homere, y compris la préparation de la paie (en se conformant à la réglementation locale en matière de charges sociales et de paiement des impôts).
  • Produire et coordonner le budget annuel de la mission, de la façon la plus précise et la plus réaliste, avec les détenteurs de budget et en cohérence avec le plan opérationnel annuel, mettre à jour le budget tout au long de l’exercice budgétaire, s’assurer que les moyens sont adaptés et proportionnés, anticiper les changements et les défis et planifier en conséquence.
  • Assurer, de manière régulière, le suivi des dépenses par rapport au budget, analyser les écarts et décider des mesures correctrices si nécessaire.
  • Produire des indicateurs réguliers et appropriés permettant de mesurer la situation financière de la mission, produire des analyses de coûts pertinentes et les diffuser.
  • Coordonner et assurer avec efficience la gestion de la trésorerie, y compris l’ensemble de la comptabilité de la mission, de façon à assurer en permanence le bon déroulement des opérations et à maîtriser de la meilleure façon possible les risques de sécurité. Ceci implique, entre autres, de définir les niveaux minimums d’argent liquide nécessaire, d’anticiper les sorties de fonds prévues, de gérer les comptes bancaires locaux et les transferts de fonds, de gérer les contacts avec les banques et/ou les autres institutions financières au niveau de la mission ainsi que de contrôler le paiement des fournisseurs et des salaires du personnel.
  • Assurer la mise en œuvre et le respect des politiques et lignes directrices MSF, veiller à leur conformité avec les exigences locales et le cadre juridique du pays, concevoir ou adapter des politiques et des procédures locales pertinentes et des outils pour optimiser la gestion des ressources financières de la mission.
  • Former et encadrer le personnel financier de la mission sur tous les points relatifs à la comptabilité, aux finances et au budget ; sensibiliser les membres clés de la direction comme les coordinateurs, les détenteurs de budget et les gestionnaires concernés aux risques financiers et à l’étendue de leurs responsabilités en la matière.
  • Définir la stratégie financière de la mission avec le CdM ou le coordinateur des urgences, en évaluer les risques et les moyens de les atténuer, mettre en place une organisation adaptée et un système de contrôle interne fiable de manière à s’acquitter de toutes les obligations financières tout en veillant à ce que l’éthique financière soit respectée en permanence au sein de la mission.
  • Vérifier que les procédures administratives relatives à la fiscalité et au paiement des charges sociales sont bien suivies et se conformer à l’environnement juridique du pays.

Profil recherché

Expérience : Diplôme universitaire requis, de préférence en économie, finance ou gestion des ressources humaines.

Minimum de 2 ans d’expérience professionnelle dans une fonction similaire au sein d’une ONG internationale.

Atout : Expérience préalable au sein d’autres ONG médicales.

Souhaité : Expérience de travail dans des interventions d’urgence

Compétences :

  • Capacité démontrée à identifier les priorités et à mettre en place des plans d’action pertinents en adéquation directe avec la stratégie opérationnelle/médicale.
  • Solides compétences en leadership et en organisation.
  • Compétences en négociation, communication et reporting.
  • Flexibilité et capacité à travailler sous pression.
  • Capacité à former, mobiliser et encadrer du personnel international et national.
  • Orientation qualité et résultats.
  • Compétences analytiques et de planification.
  • Vision stratégique.
  • Orientation service, travail d’équipe et coopération.

Langues :

Très bonne connaissance du français (B2 minimum) et de l’anglais (B2 minimum)

La connaissance d’autres langues comme l'arabe est un plus

Conditions d'emploi

  • Poste terrain avec visites au siège à Paris.
  • CDD de 12 mois à temps plein.
  • Poste terrain, rémunération niveau 13 selon la grille de salaires terrain MSF et en fonction de l’ancienneté et de l’expérience pertinente pour ce poste.
  • Assurance santé, frais de transports, d'hébergement et de subsistance (perdiem) pris en charge par MSF
  • Contrat spécifique Urgences : Comprenant une prime de fin de mission et des congés supplémentaires rémunérés, selon la politique de break MSF contrat urgences

Poste à pourvoir : dès que possible

A MSF, nous valorisons la diversité et cherchons à avoir un environnement de travail inclusif et accessible. Nous encourageons toutes les personnes qui possèdent les qualifications requises à postuler, indépendamment de leur origine ethnique, nationale ou culturelle, de leur âge, de leur sexe, de leur orientation sexuelle, de leurs convictions, de leur handicap ou d'autres aspects de leur identité.

Date limite de dépôt de candidatures12 août 2026

opportunities.title: Logistics Officer, Kismayo (Somalia Nationals Only)
opportunities.description:
Organizational Profile

Founded in 1991, Secours Islamique France (SIF) is a national and international solidarity NGO that has worked in France and around the world for over 30 years. SIF acts wherever there are humanitarian and social needs, delivering emergency relief, development programs and advocacy campaigns without proselytism or discrimination.

The SIF Kenya & Somalia Mission was registered in 2012 and currently implements humanitarian and development programs in Education and Child Welfare, Food Security and Livelihoods, and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) across Kenya and Somalia.

Job Summary

SIF is seeking a proactive and detail-oriented Logistics Officer to manage overall logistics operations in Kismayo, supporting SIF operations, programs and staff in Kismayo and Mogadishu. Reporting directly to the Field Coordinator, Kismayo Base, the successful candidate will ensure logistics activities comply with Somalia regulations, SIF procedures and donor guidelines.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Procurement: Manage all Kismayo and Mogadishu office procurement, purchasing requests and supplier contracts in line with SIF and donor procedures.
  • Stock Management: Oversee inventories, storage, asset/equipment tracking and Goods Received Notes.
  • Fleet Management: Coordinate vehicles, drivers, travel and accommodation bookings, and vehicle maintenance and safety equipment.
  • Premises Management: Ensure office, guesthouse and warehouse facilities are functional, secure and well maintained.
  • Team Supervision: Supervise drivers and, where applicable, guards, ensuring compliance with SIF procedures and safety standards.
  • Reporting: Prepare and submit timely Monthly Logistics Reports (MLR) and support procurement planning.

Requirements:

  • University degree in Procurement, Logistics or Business Administration.
  • At least 3 years of relevant NGO experience.
  • Professional certification in procurement/supply chain is preferred.
  • Prior experience managing teams and building staff capacity.
  • Proactive, honest, and highly organized, with strong planning, time-management and problem-solving skills.
  • Able to work under adverse, quickly changing conditions in a cross-cultural environment with minimal supervision.
  • Fluency in written and spoken English and Somali is required.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word.

Safeguarding: This position involves direct and regular contact with children (Child Safeguarding Level 2) and is subject to criminal record checks and professional reference checks. The successful candidate will be required to comply with SIF's Child Safeguarding Policy and the Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH) Policy.

opportunities.title: Advisor, Debris & Rubble Management – Venezuela Earthquake Response
opportunities.description:
Job Purpose:

CORE (Community Organized Relief Effort) is a crisis response organization that brings immediate aid and recovery to underserved communities across the globe. Our mission is simple: save lives and strengthen communities impacted by or vulnerable to crisis. Wherever the crisis is and whenever people are in need, we are there. CORE’s ability to impact communities is directly emboldened by each member of our staff and leadership. CORE is seeking a short-term Debris & Rubble Advisor to shape how CORE clears and reuses earthquake rubble across the impacted areas of Venezuela. This is an investigative, front-loaded advisory role: the Advisor maps CORE’s options, defines the scopes of work CORE could take on—directly, on contract, or as pilots—and produces an actionable debris and rubble removal strategy the team can move on. The Advisor writes in English and engages coordination bodies and authorities in Spanish to determine the authorizations, permits, and approvals required for each scope of work. This is a strategy and planning role; it does not involve directing field crews or operating equipment. This is a short-term, fixed-term consultancy of approximately 2–4 weeks. The role requires in-country deployment to the impacted areas of Venezuela for the contract period; international/expat candidates are welcome. The position may require mobilization on short notice.

Main Responsibilities:

Strategy & Planning

  • Produce a full debris & rubble removal strategy for the earthquake-impacted areas of Venezuela, differentiated by setting (urban, peri-urban, rural, and peri-rural) and by level of impact.
  • Develop a 6–12 month plan with defined scopes of work—laying out the rubble-removal scopes CORE could take on (direct implementation, contract, and/or pilot), with indicative sequencing, resourcing, equipment/labor mix, and cost drivers.

Options, Feasibility & Authorizations

  • Assess the mechanisms available—large-scale contracts, cash-for-work/casual labor, and heavy-equipment (mechanized) debris removal—and, for each, the authorizations, permits, and coordination requirements.
  • Scope heavy-equipment debris removal as a core clearance mechanism—the machinery mix (e.g., excavators, skid steers, loaders, dump trucks), how it is contracted or mobilized, output/throughput and cost drivers, disposal haulage, and site-safety requirements—and where it complements labor-based clearance.
  • Engage coordination bodies and authorities in Spanish (national, state, municipal, and military as relevant) to confirm what CORE needs for each specific scope of work.
  • Ground the strategy in field realities: debris volumes, disposal/dump-site options, road access, and hazardous materials (e.g., asbestos).

Recycling & Reuse (value-add)

  • Assess where rubble recycling and reuse of undamaged cinderblock and materials can feed into the plan—feasibility, quality, and how it plugs into the scopes of work.

Concept Notes & Inputs

  • As the investigation surfaces fundable activities, package findings into technical inputs CORE can drop into concept notes and proposals.

Coordination & Handover

  • Work closely with the Response Team Lead, engaged engineers, and local partners; coordinate with humanitarian clusters and government/military bodies to avoid duplication.
  • Hand over a clear, implementable strategy and set of scopes of work the team can execute.

Scope and Travel:

  • Supervises: N/A (advisory role); works alongside the Response Team Lead, engaged engineers, and local partner staff.
  • Requires in-country deployment to the impacted areas of Venezuela for the contract period (approx. 2–4 weeks); may require travel within Venezuela based on operational needs.
  • Must be able to drive and hold a valid driver’s license.
  • Must be able to mobilize on short notice; must have a current passport valid for international travel.

Qualifications:

  • Relevant experience in humanitarian debris/rubble management, disaster recovery, engineering, construction, or a related field—earthquake experience ideal.
  • A bachelor’s degree is welcomed but not required—equivalent professional experience, including work in disaster-affected or crisis settings, is strongly valued.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop implementable strategies and scopes of work in emergency or high-pressure settings.
  • Commitment to CORE’s mission and a strong understanding of the challenges faced by crisis-impacted populations.

Experience:

  • Disaster debris/rubble management, ideally earthquake-specific.
  • Writing implementable plans and scopes of work, and contributing to concept notes and proposals for donors.
  • Contract-based and/or labor-based (cash-for-work) debris approaches, and heavy-equipment debris removal (e.g., excavators, skid steers, loaders, dump trucks). • Rubble recycling / material reuse (a plus).
  • Coordinating with government, military, and humanitarian coordination bodies.
  • Prior work in Venezuela, Latin America, or similar operating environments (a plus).

Skills & Competencies:

  • Fully bilingual (English and Spanish) required—English for the written strategy, plans, and concept-note inputs; Spanish for engaging authorities and coordination bodies.
  • Strong strategic and analytical skills; able to weigh options and set realistic, defensible scopes of work, targets, and cost drivers.
  • Working knowledge of debris/clearance operations—including heavy-equipment debris removal—site safety, and hazardous-material awareness (e.g., asbestos).
  • Familiarity with rubble recycling / material reuse and disposal considerations (a plus).
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office; strong writing and documentation skills.
  • Ability to work independently, mobilize quickly, and adapt in dynamic environments.
  • Valid driver’s license and able to drive in-country.
  • Preferred but not required: knowledge of cash-for-work program design, procurement/contracting for clearance, and coordinating with authorities on permits and authorizations.

opportunities.title: Venezuela - Project Manager - Respuesta de Emergencia Terremoto (Nacional)
opportunities.description:
Acerca de COOPI

COOPI Cooperazione Internazionale es una ONG laica e independiente, fundada en Milán en 1965. Lleva a cabo proyectos de desarrollo para contribuir a la lucha contra las desigualdades y programas de emergencia para apoyar a las personas afectadas por desastres naturales o conflictos. Actualmente, COOPI está presente en 33 países de África, Oriente Medio, América Latina y Caribe.

Desde 2019 COOPI establece una presencia en Venezuela, y a partir de julio de 2020, inicia un programa regional que se implementa en asociación con organizaciones venezolanas y en coordinación con instituciones locales e internacionales, en el marco de los planes de respuesta vigentes. En los últimos años COOPI ha ampliado sus intervenciones y actualmente ejecuta proyectos con diferentes donantes en Caracas, Sucre, Delta Amacuro y Bolivar, en protección (GBV, trata y tráfico de personas), salud sexual reproductiva, WASH (agua, saneamiento e higiene), alimentación escolar y fortalecimiento institucional.

Tras los sismos ocurridos el pasado 24 de junio, las comunidades afectadas enfrentan graves vulnerabilidades, entre ellas la pérdida de documentación esencial y el aumento de riesgos asociados a la protección de derechos humanos, con especial énfasis en la niñez y personas en situación de vulnerabilidad. COOPI ejecuta un proyecto de respuesta humanitaria integral enfocado en el fortalecimiento del entorno protector, la gestión de casos y la asistencia legal especializada en las regiones priorizadas de Caracas, Miranda y La Guaira.

Objetivo/descripción del puesto

El/la Jefe/a de Proyecto estará implementando un proyecto que se centrará en la respuesta en protección y WASH en tres campamentos temporales que hospeda personas afectada por los recientes terremotos.

Bajo la supervisión de la Coordinación Pais y de Programas, el/la Project Manager asumirá la responsabilidad técnica, operativa y financiera del proyecto de respuesta de emergencia. Se encargará de liderar un equipo multidisciplinar para asegurar que las actividades de WASH y Protección se ejecuten con altos estándares de calidad, dentro del cronograma establecido y respetando los principios humanitarios, en un entorno de ritmo acelerado y alta presión.

Para esta posición se dará prioridad a perfiles nacionales.

Responsabilidades y Funciones Principales

  1. Gestión Operativa y Planificación de la Respuesta:
  • Liderar la planificación detallada, ejecución y monitoreo de todas las actividades del proyecto en los tres albergues de Distrito Capital, Miranda y La Guaira.
  • Coordinar de manera integral junto al personal técnico las líneas de trabajo de WASH (rehabilitación de sistemas de agua, distribución de insumos) y Protección (espacios seguros, rutas de derivación, sensibilización).
  • Asegurar el cumplimiento de los cronogramas de trabajo de emergencia, adaptando las estrategias de forma ágil frente a los cambios constantes en el terreno.
  1. Gestión Financiera y Administrativa
  • Junto al personal administrativo, monitorear y gestionar el presupuesto del proyecto garantizando la eficiencia de los recursos.
  • Junto al personal de logística, velar por que todos los procesos de adquisición y logística vinculados al proyecto cumplan estrictamente con los procedimientos de COOPI y los donantes.
  1. Liderazgo y Gestión de Equipos
  • Supervisar, guiar y apoyar técnicamente al personal del proyecto y coordinar el trabajo técnico con el equipo de WASH y Protección
  • Fomentar un ambiente de trabajo colaborativo y de apoyo mutuo, priorizando el bienestar y la seguridad del equipo bajo condiciones de alto estrés.
  1. Coordinación, Representación y Alianzas
  • Representar a COOPI en los espacios de coordinación local y técnica pertinentes.
  • Mantener una estrecha articulación con las autoridades locales, líderes comunitarios, administradores de los albergues y otros actores humanitarios presentes en el área de intervención.
  1. Monitoreo, Evaluación y Reportes
  • Coordinar con el equipo de Monitoreo y Evaluación (M&E) para el levantamiento de datos en tiempo real, encuestas de satisfacción de beneficiarios y mecanismos de quejas y retroalimentación.
  • Redactar informes internos y externos (mensuales, intermedios y finales) con narrativa técnica precisa y análisis de desafíos en el contexto de emergencia.

Perfil deseado

ESENCIALES

  • Título profesional universitario en Ciencias Sociales, Ingeniería Civil/Saneamiento, Cooperación Internacional, Ayuda Humanitaria o áreas afines.
  • Experiencia demostrada de al menos 3 a 5 años en la gestión de proyectos de respuesta humanitaria de emergencia en contextos de crisis o desastres naturales.
  • Experiencia previa de trabajo en Venezuela, con un profundo entendimiento del contexto social, político y operativo local, así como de los desafíos logísticos específicos del país.
  • Experiencia técnica comprobable coordinando proyectos multisectoriales que involucren componentes de WASH y Protección (o sectores afines de respuesta inmediata).
  • Capacidad comprobada para gestionar múltiples flujos de trabajo simultáneamente bajo presión y con plazos estrictos.
  • Capacidad para liderar evaluaciones rápidas de necesidades en el terreno y adaptar las intervenciones de manera oportuna.
  • Deseable haber trabajado con organizaciones no gubernamentales especialistas en VBG y/o TdP en contextos de emergencia.
  • Comprensión y conocimiento de la situación local y de las dinámicas comunitarias.
  • Respeto de la Visión y Misión de COOPI y de su carta de valores.
  • Disponibilidad para viajar dentro del área designada.
  • Sensibilidad hacia el género y la diversidad.
  • Manejo de herramientas informáticas (sistema operativo Microsoft Windows) y ofimáticas (Microsoft Office: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).
  • Disponibilidad inmediata.
  • Nacionalidad venezolana o permiso de residencia en el país.

DESEABLES

  • Formación complementaria específica en WASH en emergencias y/o Protección/Garantía de Derechos Humanos es altamente valorada.
  • Experiencia previa de trabajo con ONG internacionales y con procedimientos para el manejo de fondos de donantes institucionales (agencias de Naciones Unidas, Unión Europea).
  • Experiencia de trabajo en consorcio y en la articulación con socios locales y contrapartes institucionales.

opportunities.title: RFP - Financial Management System Supply, Implementation Customization, Training & Suppor
opportunities.description:
NEAR (Network for Empowered Aid Response), hosted by Adeso, invites qualified vendors to submit proposals for the supply, implementation, customization, training, and ongoing support of a cloud-based Financial Management System. The selected solution will strengthen NEAR's financial management, budgeting, donor compliance, reporting, and operational efficiency while supporting the organisation's continued growth and transition to independence.

NEAR is seeking experienced vendors with demonstrated expertise in implementing financial management systems for international NGOs and complex, multi-country, multi-donor environments. The proposed solution should support multi-project, multi-currency and multi-entity financial management, provide robust reporting and analytics, integrate with other enterprise systems, and include implementation, data migration, training, and ongoing technical support.

opportunities.title: Finance & Operations Management para proyectos coejecutados en Venezuela
opportunities.publisher: Plan International Latin America and the Caribbean
opportunities.description:
1. Introducción y contexto
PLAN International, Inc. – Hub Regional para las Américas requiere contratar una consultoría individual para fortalecer la gestión financiera, operativa, administrativa y de cumplimiento de los proyectos coejecutados en Venezuela, en el marco de la respuesta humanitaria y de la operación regional en el país.
La consultoría se concibe como un mecanismo temporal de seis (6) meses, bajo prestación de servicios profesionales, para aportar capacidad técnica inmediata y especializada. A diferencia de una posición fija, la relación se regirá por productos, reportes y resultados aprobados por PLAN International, sin generar relación laboral ni beneficios asociados a personal de planta.
La persona consultora estará basada en Venezuela y deberá contar con experiencia comprobada en el sector de organizaciones internacionales no gubernamentales (INGO), gestión financiera de proyectos, cumplimiento de donantes, control interno, compras/logística y respuesta humanitaria.

2. Justificación de la contratación
La ejecución de proyectos en Venezuela requiere un soporte integrado de finanzas y operaciones que asegure continuidad operativa, uso adecuado de fondos, trazabilidad documental y cumplimiento con políticas institucionales, requerimientos de donantes y normativa aplicable.
•
Asegurar planificación financiera, seguimiento presupuestario y reportes oportunos para la toma de decisiones.
•
Fortalecer controles internos, segregación de funciones, custodia de recursos y soporte documental audit-ready.
PLAN International
Hub Regional para las Américas
Términos de referencia para contratación de consultoría – PLAN International, Región de las Américas
•
Acompañar la gestión financiera de socios locales, incluyendo revisión de liquidaciones, evidencias y capacidades administrativas.
•
Coordinar requerimientos operativos, logísticos, compras, pagos y apoyo administrativo necesarios para la respuesta.
•
Mitigar riesgos fiduciarios, legales, fiscales, reputacionales, de fraude, soborno y uso indebido de fondos en un contexto activo de emergencia.

3. Objetivo general
Brindar soporte técnico y operativo especializado para asegurar que los proyectos ejecutados en Venezuela cuenten con una gestión financiera, administrativa, logística y de cumplimiento sólida, oportuna y alineada con los estándares de PLAN International y de los donantes.

4. Objetivos específicos
1.
Implementar y monitorear procesos de planificación financiera, seguimiento presupuestario, análisis de variaciones, proyecciones y reportes periódicos para los proyectos en Venezuela.
2.
Asegurar que los controles internos, documentación de soporte, rutas de aprobación, matrices de autoridad y segregación de funciones funcionen de manera efectiva.
3.
Apoyar la gestión de socios implementadores, incluyendo revisión financiera, liquidaciones, planes de fortalecimiento de capacidades y seguimiento a hallazgos.
4.
Coordinar necesidades de operaciones, adquisiciones, logística, inventarios, activos, pagos y apoyo administrativo en estrecha coordinación con el equipo de Supply Chain y Finanzas regional.
5.
Contribuir a la preparación de auditorías, revisiones de donantes, spot checks, cierres mensuales y reportes financieros de calidad.
6.
Asegurar que la respuesta humanitaria cuente con procesos ágiles pero controlados, documentados y auditables.

5. Alcance de trabajo y principales responsabilidades Área Responsabilidades principales Planificación financiera y presupuestaria
Preparar y actualizar presupuestos, forecasts, burn rate, análisis de variaciones, proyecciones de caja y recomendaciones para decisiones de gestión. Reportes financieros y asesoría
Consolidar información financiera de proyectos, preparar reportes internos y de donantes, alertar sobre riesgos de sobre/sub-ejecución y proponer acciones correctivas. Gestión de grants y cumplimiento de donantes
Verificar elegibilidad de gastos, documentación requerida, codificación presupuestaria, cumplimiento de acuerdos, condiciones de donantes y trazabilidad de costos. Contabilidad, pagos y tesorería
Apoyar el registro oportuno y correcto de transacciones, solicitudes de pago, conciliaciones, controles de caja, manejo de anticipos y respaldo documental. Control interno, riesgo y auditoría
Mantener controles efectivos, identificar riesgos fiduciarios, documentar hallazgos, dar seguimiento a acciones correctivas y facilitar auditorías o revisiones. Supply Chain, compras y logística
Coordinar requerimientos de adquisiciones, logística, servicios, activos e inventarios en línea con políticas, procesos y coordinación con Supply Chain regional/local. Operaciones y respuesta humanitaria
Apoyar la puesta en marcha de procedimientos operativos, protocolos de emergencia, mecanismos de coordinación y soluciones prácticas para continuidad operacional.
PLAN International
Hub Regional para las Américas
Términos de referencia para contratación de consultoría – PLAN International, Región de las Américas
Gestión documental y aprendizaje
Mantener repositorios organizados, evidencia de aprobaciones, minutas, reportes, matrices de seguimiento y lecciones aprendidas para auditoría y continuidad.

6. Perfil requerido
La persona consultora deberá demostrar experiencia, independencia técnica, juicio profesional y capacidad para operar en contextos complejos, con orientación a resultados y cumplimiento.
•
Título universitario en Finanzas, Contabilidad, Administración, Economía, Operaciones, Logística o carrera afín. Maestría o certificación profesional en finanzas, auditoría, gestión de proyectos o supply chain será valorada.
•
Experiencia mínima de ocho (8) años en gestión financiera, operativa, administrativa o de grants, idealmente en organizaciones internacionales, cooperación o sector humanitario.
•
Experiencia comprobada con INGOs, donantes institucionales, socios locales y entornos de respuesta humanitaria.
•
Conocimiento sólido de presupuestos, control interno, conciliaciones, análisis financiero, reportes de donantes, auditoría y documentación de soporte.
•
Experiencia en compras/logística, coordinación de proveedores, activos, inventarios, pagos y servicios operativos será altamente valorada.
•
Conocimiento del contexto venezolano y capacidad de operar de forma presencial en coordinación con equipos regionales y socios.
•
Dominio avanzado de Excel y herramientas financieras; experiencia con SAP u otros sistemas financieros institucionales será deseable.
•
Excelente redacción en español; inglés funcional/profesional deseable para coordinación regional y documentación institucional.
•
Capacidad para trabajar bajo presión, priorizar, resolver problemas, comunicar alertas tempranas y mantener criterio de cumplimiento.

7. Competencias clave
•
Pensamiento financiero y operativo aplicado a contextos humanitarios.
•
Rigor en control interno, documentación, cumplimiento y trazabilidad.
•
Orientación a resultados, análisis crítico y solución práctica de problemas.
•
Capacidad de coordinación con equipos multiculturales, socios locales, finanzas, programas y supply chain.
•
Comunicación clara, profesional y ejecutiva para reportar riesgos, decisiones y avances.
•
Integridad, confidencialidad, independencia profesional y compromiso con los valores de PLAN International.

8. Honorarios y forma de pago
El valor indicativo de la consultoría será de USD 3,200 a USD 3,600 mensuales, sujeto a evaluación del perfil seleccionado, disponibilidad presupuestaria y aprobación interna de PLAN International.
•
El monto incluirá honorarios profesionales, costos administrativos e impuestos que correspondan a la persona consultora, salvo que el contrato indique algo diferente.
•
Los pagos se realizarán mensualmente contra entrega y aprobación del informe mensual de actividades/productos y la factura o recibo correspondiente.
•
Los costos de viaje, alojamiento, viáticos, comunicaciones u otros gastos operativos no estarán incluidos en los honorarios, salvo aprobación previa y por escrito de PLAN International.
•
PLAN International podrá retener o requerir ajustes al pago si los productos no cumplen con el estándar esperado o si la documentación de soporte es insuficiente.
PLAN International
Hub Regional para las Américas
Términos de referencia para contratación de consultoría – PLAN International, Región de las Américas

9. Supervisión y coordinación
La consultoría será supervisada por PLAN International – Hub Regional para las Américas a través del liderazgo regional de Finanzas y Operaciones, en coordinación con el equipo de Respuesta Humanitaria, Supply Chain, Programas y otros puntos focales designados por ROA.
•
La persona consultora deberá participar en reuniones de seguimiento según se requiera.
•
Toda gestión logística o de compras deberá coordinarse estrechamente con Supply Chain para evitar riesgos administrativos, duplicidades o compromisos no autorizados.
•
Las decisiones financieras, compromisos contractuales, pagos y aprobaciones deberán respetar la matriz de autoridad y los procedimientos aplicables.
•
La persona consultora no podrá comprometer legal o financieramente a PLAN International sin autorización expresa.

10. Condiciones administrativas
•
La consultoría tendrá una duración de seis (6) meses calendario a partir de la fecha establecida en el contrato.
•
La prestación de servicios se realizará principalmente desde Venezuela, con coordinación remota con ROA y posibles desplazamientos internos o internacionales según necesidad y aprobación previa.
•
La relación contractual será de consultoría independiente; no constituye relación laboral ni genera prestaciones, beneficios laborales, seguridad social, vacaciones o indemnizaciones laborales.
•
La persona consultora deberá cumplir con requisitos administrativos, fiscales, bancarios y de debida diligencia establecidos por PLAN International antes de la firma del contrato.
•
El/la consultor(a) deberá mantener disponibilidad razonable para atender prioridades de la respuesta humanitaria y reportar oportunamente cualquier conflicto de interés, limitación operativa o riesgo de cumplimiento.

11. Ética, salvaguarda y cumplimiento
La persona consultora deberá actuar en coherencia con los valores, políticas y estándares de PLAN International, incluyendo salvaguarda de niños, niñas y jóvenes, género e inclusión, prevención de fraude, soborno y corrupción, protección de datos, confidencialidad, conflicto de interés y código de conducta para no miembros del personal.
•
Cumplir y promover la Política Global de Salvaguarda de PLAN International y reportar cualquier preocupación por los canales establecidos.
•
Garantizar trato digno, seguro, inclusivo y no discriminatorio en todas las interacciones con comunidades, socios, proveedores y personal.
•
Mantener confidencialidad sobre información financiera, de socios, beneficiarios, proveedores, personal y documentación institucional.
•
Proteger datos personales y documentación sensible, limitando su uso exclusivamente al propósito de la consultoría.
•
Cumplir con estándares anticorrupción, antisoborno, antiterrorismo y sanciones aplicables a PLAN International y sus donantes.

12. Presentación y evaluación de candidaturas
Las personas interesadas deberán presentar, según sea requerido por PLAN International, su hoja de vida actualizada, propuesta económica mensual, disponibilidad, referencias relevantes y evidencia de experiencia similar en INGOs, respuesta humanitaria, finanzas, grants y operaciones. Criterio de evaluación Peso indicativo Experiencia en finanzas, grants, operaciones y control interno en INGOs / cooperación
30% Experiencia en respuesta humanitaria y/o contexto Venezuela 25%

PLAN International Hub Regional para las Américas
Términos de referencia para contratación de consultoría – PLAN International, Región de las Américas
Capacidad técnica en reportes, presupuestos, auditoría, socios y cumplimiento 20% Disponibilidad, idioma, habilidades de coordinación y comunicación ejecutiva 15% Propuesta económica dentro del rango y razonabilidad del costo 10%

opportunities.title: Refugee Info Editorial Officer
opportunities.description:
Background

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 50 countries, the IRC aims to restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure.

The IRC in Italy provides essential safety, empowerment, education, livelihood and health services to migrants, refugees and asylum seekers. Our programs operate across Italy, including in Trieste, Milan, Rome, Turin and various locations in Sicily and Calabria, with a strong focus on supporting the most vulnerable populations, such as women and children.

Position Summary

The Editorial Officer will be a key member of the Refugee.Info Italy project team. Refugee.Info offers asylum-seekers, refugees, and migrants in Italy accurate, timely, and useful information on legal rights, essential procedures, and services. Based on a peer to peer approach, we generate and disseminate information based on communities' needs, equipping people to make informed decisions on the issues that matter most to them. As part of the Refugee.Info Italy team, the Editorial Officer will lead the platform's editorial line, drive the information campaign on the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, track legal procedures and services relevant to refugees and migrants in Italy, produce and update multimedia content, produce analytics and maintain the Refugee.Info Italy Facebook page and website.

Responsibilities:

Content creation and editorial line

  • Develop bespoke, engaging multimedia content for Refugee.Info Italy digital platforms, applying Signpost editorial standards (client-centred framing, rights stated as entitlements, clear next steps).
  • Lead the creation and implementation of the information campaign on the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, including the dedicated site section and related content.
  • Work with the R.I. Project Manager and the R.I. Moderation Lead and moderators to identify information needs, develop and implement an editorial calendar, and plan ads campaigns.
  • Research training opportunities, courses, and initiatives relevant to migrants and refugees for publication on Refugee.Info channels.
  • Under the supervision of the R.I. Project Manager, manage and maintain the website and social media channels of Refugee.Info Italy.
  • Build audiences for ads, promote content through ads campaigns, and maintain a solid online presence.
  • Coordinate with the Signpost technical and development team to ensure the smooth operation and development of Refugee.Info platforms.
  • Participate in R.I., IRC Italy and Signpost team meetings.

Social Media and Web Analyst

  • Analyse Refugee.Info social media growth, engagement, and audience behaviour using analytical tools, and keep editorial teams updated.
  • Produce quarterly KPIs reports, monitor web and social media KPIs, flag critical issues, and recommend improvements to the R.I. editorial teams' digital and marketing strategy.
  • Monitor Google Analytics, Zendesk Explore, and Meta/Facebook analytics data to draw insights.

Requirements:

  • Degree in communication, development communication, social sciences, law, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated written and oral communication skills.
  • High proficiency in technology and software (Microsoft Office Suite, Adobe Professional, Google products, social media platforms).
  • Proficiency in infographic software and/or experience in graphic design.
  • At least 2 years of experience in the field of asylum and migration, media and communications, preferably with an NGO.
  • Knowledge of services, procedures, and legal frameworks relevant to the migration and asylum context in Italy.
  • Excellent command of Italian and English, both spoken and written.
  • Strong collaborator with effective interpersonal and analytical skills, able to work seamlessly across cultures and organizational units.
  • Analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Genuine commitment to migration, asylum, and protection issues.
  • Ability to work remotely as part of a multicultural team distributed across Italy.

IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability.

This position is expected to end on August 23, 2027.

Compensation: (Annual Compensation: €14,400). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

opportunities.title: AVRR Project Assistant (Outreach) - Sicily
opportunities.description:
Organizational Context and Scope

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations, and as the leading UN agency in the field of migration, works closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

Under the general supervision of the Director, Coordination Office for the Mediterranean and Chief of Mission in Italy and Malta, the coordination of the Senior Programme Associate (Migration) and the direct supervision of the Project Coordinator, the incumbent will be responsible for assisting in the implementation of the AVRR counselling and activities related to the project Training, Assistance and Territorial Support for the Efficiency of Assisted Voluntary Returns.

Responsibilities and Accountabilities

  • Support in establishing close contacts with the local stakeholders dealing with migrants and migration management (municipalities, local entities, NGOs, diaspora groups, etc.) in order to support them in providing AVRR information/counselling to migrants and strengthen national AVRR referral mechanisms;
  • Provide AVRR information sessions and tailor-made counselling to all Third Country Nationals (TCNs) potentially interested in returning to their CoOS;
  • Submit AVRR applications through the online system of the Ministry of Interior to the Prefectures competent for the migrants’ place of residence, and keep in good order all the documents related to each potential returnee, securing the appropriate caseload filing;
  • Disseminate the AVRR information material in close coordination with the Project Coordinator;
  • Support migrants in filling in the AVRR application and forward the complete files to the IOM AVRR Team, securing if necessary, the issuance of travel documents by the consulates;
  • Maintain close coordination with Police Headquarters (Questure), Immigration Offices and Prefectures to facilitate the assessment and authorization process of migrants eligible for AVRR assistance.
  • Assist in organizing transportation of medical and non-medical cases, including taking necessary contacts with the local medical facility and personnel to obtain the necessary medical documentation as requested by the IOM AVRR Doctor;
  • Collect and compile information relevant for statistical reporting and migrant profiling, and contribute to the identification, development and dissemination of success stories and testimonies related to AVRR beneficiaries and project activities.
  • Perform other tasks related to the execution of the project, as assigned by the supervisor.

Required Qualifications and Experience

EDUCATION

  • University degree in International Relations, Law, Social, Political or Economic Sciences, Social Work, Migration or Development Studies, Psychology, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or
  • High School diploma, with four years of relevant professional experience.

EXPERIENCE

  • At least two years of working experience in the migration sector;
  • Experience providing direct assistance to migrant populations, also in vulnerable situations;
  • Proven working experience in dealing with the Italian institutions at central and local level, civic society, and diaspora groups;
  • Experience working in a multicultural team;
  • Previous working experience in AVRR counselling is considered an asset.

SKILLS

  • Excellent organizational and communication skills;
  • Personal commitment, efficiency and drive for results;
  • Ability to multi-task, prioritize and work independently;
  • Ability to work under pressure;
  • Demonstrated proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, Access and PowerPoint as well as Outlook is required.

Languages
IOM’s official languages are English, French, and Spanish.

REQUIRED

For this position, fluency in Italian and English is required (oral and written).

DESIRABLE

Another foreign language is considered an asset.

Competencies

The incumbent is expected to demonstrate the following values and competencies:

VALUES - All IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.

Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.

Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.

Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.

Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

CORE COMPETENCIES - Behavioural indicators – Level 1

Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.

Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.

Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.

Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.

Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

opportunities.title: Chief Financial Officer
opportunities.description:
The Center for International Environmental Law (CIEL) uses the power of law to protect the environment, promote human rights, and ensure a just and sustainable society. We work at the intersection of environmental protection and human rights, across sectors and borders, and in close collaboration with global partners and local communities.

As a member of CIEL’s executive team, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) plays a critical role in advancing CIEL’s mission and strategy through effective financial oversight, strategic planning, and inclusive team leadership. The CFO will work with our Board and leadership to ensure fiscal integrity, and will partner with program and development staff to sustain and grow our organizational impact.

The CFO is responsible for providing senior oversight and support across financial planning, reporting, forecasting, and business partnering activities, whilst managing our finance team of 5. The CFO works closely with the CEO, COO, the Board, and in collaboration with other senior organizational leaders based globally, to make sound decisions regarding the financial health of CIEL, and balance strategic and operational priorities. We are seeking a leader who is as comfortable diving into the detail and explaining technical and financial concepts with ease and clarity as they are developing and presenting a strategic forecast. Comfortable with financial reporting and complexity in a global organization with entities registered in Washington DC and Geneva, Switzerland, the CFO will work across cultures, jurisdictions, and time zones.

This is a great opportunity to join a dynamic and passionate team. You will work to ensure CIEL has the financial systems, processes, reporting and strategy in place to ensure our fiscal health, thereby enabling the delivery of high-impact campaigns that protect people and the planet.

CONTRACT: This role is available as either a full-time or fractional (part-time/contract) engagement, dependent on candidate fit and business needs. We are open to discussing the structure and time commitment that works best for the right person.

DEADLINE: 9am ET, Monday, August 3, 2026

LOCATION: Remote, Northeast USA (specific states listed below) or Washington DC (hybrid/flexible), preferred. Must possess valid US work authorization.

SALARY RANGE: $170,000-$200,000 depending on qualifications

Read the full job description and application instructions in the position profile. This search is being led by SCHC Advisors.
