opportunities.title: Procurement Officer- Job Reference NBI /EDO/001/2026
opportunities.description:
The Nile Basin Initiative [NBI] is an intergovernmental partnership of the riparian States of the Nile comprising Burundi, Democratic Republic of Congo, Egypt, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda. It was established in 1999 as a Transitional Mechanism by the Council of Ministers on Water Affairs to foster cooperation and sustainable development of the Nile River for the benefit of the 10 countries. The NBI shared vision is to achieve “sustainable socio-economic development through the equitable utilization of, and benefit from, the common Nile Basin water resources”. NBI has three Centres: NBI SEC based in Entebbe, Uganda, NELSAP-CU based in Kigali, Rwanda and ENTRO based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

NBI Secretariat intends to a hire highly qualified and competent professional for the following position that will fall vacant by end of financial year 2025/2026.

  • Procurement Officer- Job Reference NBI /EDO/001/2026

The above are regional recruitment position to be based at the NBI Secretariat at Entebbe in Uganda and suitably qualified candidates from NBI Member States are encouraged to apply. Full Job Descriptions can be downloaded here.

Duty Station.

The Employees will be based at NBI Secretariat in Entebbe Uganda with possible travel within or out of the Basin Countries as may be deemed necessary by the Employer.

Period of Service

This is a Regional Position with an employment duration (term) of Six (6) years whose annual contracts are renewable based on satisfactory performance, availability of funds and need for the services.

opportunities.title: Business Development and Reporting Coordinator
opportunities.description:
Job Title: Business Development & Reporting Coordinator

Work Location: Damascus, Aleppo, or Qamishli.

Contract end date/duration: ASAP

Contract renewable based on Budget and Performance

*This Position is open for Syrian National Only

Position Summary

The Business Development and Reporting Coordinator (BDRC) supports the organization Syria’s resource mobilization and donor engagement efforts by coordinating proposal development, reporting processes, and handover of approved grants to implementing teams. The BDRC is a central pillar in the organization Syria's internal coordination and has a critical role in grant management functions, together with finances and the program team. Working under the supervision of the Business Development and Reporting Manager (BDRM), the BDRC ensures the timely delivery of high-quality donor submissions, effective design and internal coordination. The role plays a key part in maintaining donor and the organization members trust as well as in strengthening the organization’s financial sustainability, reputation and program.

This role requires strong coordination and organizational skills, excellent writing and editing abilities, and the capacity to build and maintain positive, productive relationships across teams and departments. The ideal candidate will thrive under pressure, delivering high-quality outputs within tight and shifting deadlines. S/he will demonstrate initiative, creativity, and a collaborative spirit — able to troubleshoot challenges in proposal development or reporting, foster positive teamwork, and contribute to a culture of learning and excellence that strengthens the organization’s Syria’s program and credibility with donors.

The employee is also required to;

1. Remain aware of and comply with safety and security regulations/procedures and bear responsibility for personal safety and security while under contract.

2. Comply with the organization Policies which includes but not limited to Safeguarding Policy, Code of Conduct and other organizational and HR policies.

3. The organizations has a zero-tolerance approach towards sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, and child abuse towards any person including our staff, representatives, partners, programme participants and members of the community where we work. We expect all staff, partners and related personnel to share this commitment by understanding, abiding by and working within the organization International Safeguarding Policy and related framework at all times whilst representing the organization.

4. Depending on specific role and responsibilities, may be requested to comply with the terms of additional policies, guidelines and related regulations, as and when necessary.

Key Responsibilities

1. Proposal Development and Coordination: 35%

In order to expand and diversify the organization’s funding base and support the organization in ensuring it responds to humanitarian needs and advances its strategic priorities:

  • Support the design and preparation of high-quality proposals in collaboration with program, MEAL, finance, technical teams, safeguarding, the organization members, and when appropriate partners.
  • Develop and maintain proposal development timelines, templates, and markers.
  • Arrange project design meetings and ensure the promotion of quality and coherent programs in line with the organization Syria's strategy.
  • Ensure all proposal components (narrative, logframe, budget) are reviewed and formatted according to donor guidelines.
  • Coordinate internal inputs, reviews, and sign-offs before submission, ensuring quality improvements.
  • Where necessary, support carrying out competitors analysis, SWOTs, and identification of Unique Selling Point for new opportunities.
  • Maintain positive, productive, and strong relations with the organization members during proposal development.

2. Donor Reporting and Donor Relationship Support: 30%

Ensure the organization Syria’s Business Development efforts are sustained by keeping the donor informed on project progress and proper grant management:

  • Track donor reporting deadlines and ensure timely submission of accurate reports.
  • Liaise with program, MEAL teams, and if necessary partners, to compile data, success stories, and lessons learned.
  • Review reports for compliance with donor templates, language, and branding requirements.
  • Flag to manager variances to project approved, as identified in reporting or BvA meetings.
  • In case of variances, in coordination with the BDRM, support the program team and organization member in identifying solutions during implementation that can be satisfactory for the donor.
  • If requested, support the preparation of the organization members or donor visits to active projects, and collect lessons learnt for future programming.

3. Internal Coordination and Grant Kick-Offs: 15%

Ensure the program and support teams have the information necessary to start the grant implementation:

  • Organize and document grant kick-off meetings to ensure roles, deliverables, and donor requirements are clear.
  • Participate in regular Budget Versus Actual (BVA) meetings with program and finance teams to identify variances that should be flagged to the donor or could harm the organization’s reputation or future grants.
  • Facilitate effective communication between departments to resolve design and implementation issues affecting fundraising or donor relations.

4. Filing, Documentation, and Information Management: 15%

  • Maintain an organized and up-to-date filing system for proposals, contracts, reports, and donor correspondence.
  • Ensure key grant documents are accessible to relevant staff.
  • Support preparation of briefing materials and summaries for leadership or donor meetings.
  • Support the preparation of donor materials as requested by manager.
  • Maintain an updated program and reporting tracker.

5. OTHER RESPONSIBILITIES AS ASSIGNED 5 %

Required Qualification, Skills and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (Social Sciences, Development Studies, Public Administration, Business Administration, or related field) or equivalent combination of education and work experience.
  • At least 3 years of professional experience in proposal development
  • At least 2 years of experience in donor reporting
  • Experience in multi-sectoral program coordination in the humanitarian or development sector.
  • Strong writing and editing skills with attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Critical spirit and ability to anticipate donor questions and address those prior to submission.
  • Proven experience coordinating accoss departments (i.e. programs, finance, MEAL, etc) to gather inputs.
  • Excellent English skills (writing and oral).
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills. Ability to meet tight deadlines and manage multiple priorities, keeping a positive attitude.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and familiarity with digital filing and knowledge management systems.

Desired:

  • Master’s degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, Humanitarian Affairs, or related fields.
  • Certification or training in proposal development, PSEA, safeguarding.
  • Relevant emergency management training (e.g., HEAT).
  • Experience working with international humanitarian organizations.
  • Experience working in the Syria crisis response or other complex humanitarian contexts.
  • Proven track record of successful proposal development for institutional donors (e.g., OCHA, ECHO, GFFO).
  • Understanding of donor regulations.
  • Arabic fluency
  • Familiarity with cross-cutting themes (i.e gender equality, climate resilience, safeguarding).
  • Experience coordinating grant kick-off or close-out meetings.
  • Basic skills in data analysis or visualization (Power BI, Excel dashboards, etc.).
  • Emotional intelligence to effectively work with other team members in a fruitful and positive manner.

Safeguarding Commitments

The organization has a zero-tolerance approach toward sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, and child abuse. We will carefully examine allegations and investigate, and take appropriate disciplinary action where this is needed, taking into consideration the rights and interests of the survivor, consistent with the organization’s survivor-centred approach. We make very clear that sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, and child abuse in any form, perpetrated by our staff, partners or other related personnel, towards anyone, will not be tolerated.

We provide equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, handicap, disability, or marital status.

opportunities.title: Fundraising and Project Co-Coordinator (f/m/d)
opportunities.description:
Initial Commitment:. 9 months (40h/week), possibility for renewal

Location: Ioannina, Greece

Preferred Starting Date: first week of July

About the Organization and the Project (Community Center in Ioannina, Greece)

Be Aware And Share (BAAS) is an independent non-profit organization that supports people in need and contributes to social inclusion. Founded in 2015 in Basel, Switzerland, BAAS is primarily engaging in working with people on the move in Europe. At the moment, the organization is mainly focusing on supporting people on the move at its Community Center in Ioannina, Greece. The multi-storey building offers various services and activities such as a free clothes shop, hot meals distribution, a safe space for women, language courses. a creative atelier and various social activities, among others. BAAS also carries out awareness-raising and information actions in Switzerland. All activities by BAAS are financed exclusively by donations. BAAS is a politically independent organization.

Job description

We are looking for a motivated individual with a hands-on mentality, who is able to work individually and as part of an international, multicultural team. The right candidate will be organized and professional, with strong attention to detail.

The ideal candidate will be culturally aware, able to identify with BAAS’ mission on the ground and will use their personal drive to support the services offered in our Community Center in Ioannina, at the same time co-managing the volunteer team. Additionally, an integral part of the position will be to maintain our existing fundraising efforts as well as help to strategize and deliver new ones.

The Fundraising and Project Co-Coordinator will be cooperating and working closely with the other Project Co-Coordinators and the Project Director on-site.

This position reports to the Project Director.

Key Responsibilities

Project Coordination

  • Co-coordinate activities and services offered at the Community Center
  • Contribute to the strategic-decision development of the Community Center
  • Procurement for the Community Center
  • Distribution of the Community Center’s services such as Free Shop items, Diapers, Pads, etc.
  • Implementation of the project in accordance with project guidelines and policies, as those are developed at the organizational level
  • Management of the volunteer team, along with the other Coordinators
  • Attend the team-coordination meeting with the Project Director and the other Coordinators
  • Attend the different coordination meetings with the project’s volunteers, the various working groups, the Board and active members.

Fundraising Coordination

  • Development and implementation of the BAAS fundraising strategy
  • Drafting and submission of grant applications (narrative and financial part); grant management, including narrative and financial reporting
  • Acquire new institutional donors and maintain existing partnerships
  • Maintain ongoing fundraising efforts and foster relationships with private donors
  • Co-author project reports & annual reports for donors
  • Various administrative tasks (excel sheets, statistics).

Key skills and experience

Required:**

  • Previous experience working in a non-profit and/or humanitarian setting
  • Experience in (project) coordination and/or volunteer management
  • Comfortable with developing narrative donor applications and reports under minimal supervision
  • Comfortable with managing project budgets for donors
  • Proficiency in written and spoken English and German
  • Strong writing and editing skills with attention to detail
  • Strong overall computer skills with very good knowledge of MS Office
  • Excellent interpersonal & communication skills
  • Ability to manage multiple and competing priorities, as well as meet pressing deadlines
  • Alignment with the values of BAAS and the project’s objectives
  • Culturally sensitive

Desirable:

  • Driver’s license category B, manual transmission and willingness to drive in Greece
  • Knowledge of context-related languages such as, Arabic, Farsi or Greek
  • Previous grants and/or financial management experience
  • Experienced working with people on the move
  • Previous experience in the NGO/humanitarian sector in Greece

**We are aware that most candidates are less likely to apply to jobs if they do not meet every single qualification. Even if your experience and/or skills do not align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, but you feel you meet the majority of the required skills and criteria, we still encourage you to apply.

What we offer

  • Employment through the BAAS Greek entity; monthly net salary of 792.42 €
  • Single room in a shared accommodation is provided
  • Wide scope for independent work structure
  • Access to diverse networks and partnerships
  • Comprehensive training and introduction to the Community Center and the organization
  • The opportunity to take on a responsible position in a committed and dynamic team and to make an important contribution to the realization of the BAAS project in Greece.

opportunities.title: Grants Finance Officer
opportunities.description:
The Centre for Humanitarian Dialogue (HD) is a private diplomacy organisation founded on the principles of humanity, impartiality and independence. Its mission is to help prevent, mitigate, and resolve armed conflict through dialogue and mediation.

Are you a detail-oriented finance professional passionate about making an impact through donor-funded programs? We’re looking for a Grants Finance Officer to ensure financial integrity, compliance, and strategic insight across our global grant portfolio.

Grants Finance Officer (100%)

Remote work from Europe, Asia or in any other HD offices

Starting date: As soon as possible

The position is embedded in HD’s Finance team and works in close cooperation with the External Relations team, under the supervision of the Finance Planning and Reporting Manager.

The ER team combines donor relations and fundraising with external communications function

works to ensure that HD’s income meets the organisation’s needs.

This is more than a finance role, it’s a chance to support global programs that make a real difference, while ensuring compliance, and strategic alignment.

Working with the External Relations team (70%), the main responsibilities of the Grants Finance Officer are:

  • Prepare, compile, monitor, and report on budgets for multi-regional, multi-project donor grants
  • Ensure full compliance with donor financial reporting, audit, and contractual requirement
  • Act as the go-to finance contact for regional teams — guiding them through grant compliance and resolving discrepancies
  • Manage Fund Cards in Business Central and maintain a central repository of financial & contractual resources
  • Support internal/external audits, revenue forecasting, and KPI dashboards using HD’s BI tools
  • Review donor agreements for financial feasibility and flag high-risk clauses
  • Ensure IATI compliance for relevant grants

In addition, the Grants Finance Officer will be assisting the Global Finance Planning and Reporting Function (FP&R) translating complex financial data into clear, actionable insights for stakeholders across the organization (30%).

Working closely with regional and cross-functional teams, the role will design and deliver reporting solutions that are not only accurate and efficient, but also intuitive, reliable, and tightly aligned with our strategic goals:

  • Support designing & implementation of financial planning and implementation platform.
  • Optimizing existing tools and platforms through automation, standardization, and better visualization.
  • Building dynamic dashboards to provide finance insights to relevant internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ensuring FP&R tools are intuitive, reliable, and strategically aligned — so decisions are data-driven and confident.

The successful candidate should meet the following criteria:

  • Recognised or working towards an accounting/finance qualification (CIMA, ACCA, CPA or similar)
  • Experience in grant financial management — ideally in the not-for-profit sector is an asset
  • Strong skills in budgeting, financial monitoring, and donor reporting
  • Familiarity with EU/European sovereign donors is a plus
  • Experience with Workday Adaptive Planning, Jet Analytics, Jet Reports, or Business Central is a bonus
  • Professional fluency in English — French, Arabic, or Mandarin is an asset

The ideal candidate should be:

  • A collaborative team player who thrives in cross-regional, remote environments
  • Highly organised, proactive, and able to juggle multiple priorities with tight deadlines
  • A clear communicator — able to explain complex financial concepts to non-financial colleagues
  • Detail-oriented, solution-driven, and committed to continuous improvement

opportunities.title: PARTNERSHIP & COMMUNICATION OFFICER, SOUTH EAST ASIA F/M
opportunities.description:
THE MERIEUX FOUNDATION

The Mérieux Foundation has been working in the field of global health since its creation in 1967. With a public utility status, it specialises in the fight against infectious diseases, particularly among vulnerable populations in resource-limited countries.

Our mission is divided into four priority objectives:

  • Increase access to diagnosis for vulnerable populations
  • Strengthen applied research in the field and the development of collaborative programmes,
  • Develop knowledge sharing and public health initiatives,
  • Take action for mothers and children through a comprehensive approach to health.

We operate directly in more than 25 countries in Asia, Asia, the Middle East and the Indian Ocean, working closely with local actors, which allows us to adapt our programmes and actions to the realities on the ground and the needs of the populations.

Joining us means becoming part of a team of nearly 150 employees in 16 countries, united by common values: international solidarity, commitment, expertise and collaboration.

For more information about Fondation Mérieux in Asia please visit our website: Our projects – Fondation Mérieux

GENERAL MISSION

The Regional Partnerships & Communication Officer contributes to the development and visibility of the Fondation Mérieux’s activities in Asia.

He or she supports the mobilisation of financial and strategic partnerships for the implementation and scaling up of projects in the region. The officer maintains regular contact with technical and financial partners in Asia, actively identifies funding opportunities, and contributes to the preparation of project proposals and donor reporting.

In addition, the officer contributes to the communication and visibility of the Foundation’s activities in Asia, by supporting the development of communication materials, promoting project results and strengthening engagement with partners, donors and regional stakeholders.

MAIN ACTIVITIES AND TASKS

All activities will be carried out under the supervision of the Asia Regional Director, and in close collaboration with:

  • the country teams in Asia
  • the Partnerships Division – Medical & Expertise Department at headquarters
  • the Communication team at headquarters

Depending on the nature of the projects, the officer may collaborate with country office managers, project teams and technical experts.

Define and monitor the regional partnership strategy

  • Develop and oversee the partnership and resource mobilisation strategy for Asia, aligned with Fondation Mérieux’s priorities.
  • Identify regional funding needs with country teams and headquarters.
  • Monitor donor priorities and funding opportunities.
  • Adjust the strategy based on emerging opportunities and country needs.

Identify and secure funding

  • Proactively identify and pursue national, regional, and international funding opportunities.
  • Map donors and partners and prepare country-specific profiles in collaboration with headquarters.

Strengthen communication and visibility

  • Support the development of communication materials (project briefs, success stories, presentations, donor briefs).
  • Contribute content showcasing project results and impact.
  • Coordinate with headquarters to ensure consistent messaging and branding.
  • Promote project visibility through events & publications

Coordinate concept notes and proposals

  • Coordinate the preparation of concept notes and proposals with country teams, partners, and headquarters.
  • Ensure quality and compliance with donor and Foundation standards.
  • Manage timely submission of proposals.
  • Review new opportunities and submit them for internal validation.

PROFILE & QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master’s degree (or equivalent) in political science, international development, international relations, public health, project management, or a related field.
  • At least 3 years of experience in a similar role within an international organisation or NGO.
  • Demonstrated experience in fundraising and donor relations.
  • Good knowledge of donors and funding mechanisms in global health and development, particularly in Asia.
  • International experience, preferably in Asia or in multicultural environments.

Required Skills

  • Strong project management skills (project cycle, logical framework, proposal writing, reporting).
  • Excellent analytical, writing, and communication skills in English (spoken and written).
  • Ability to develop communication materials and support visibility and partner engagement.

Languages

  • Fluent English required.
  • French is an asset.
  • Khmer, Lao, or Thai would be an advantage.

Personal Qualities

  • Adaptable and flexible.
  • Proactive, autonomous, and detail-oriented.
  • Strong team player with good negotiation skills.

TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT

- Working hours: full-time (40 hours/week);

- Health insurance for the employee and their dependents.
- Compensation package:

  • 13th month pro-rated to time worked (paid in December);
    • 8% target bonus calculated on annual salary (eligibility after nine (09) months of attendance during the calendar year and paid in April).

Description:

Handicap International is an independent and impartial international aid organisation working in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. Working alongside persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups, our action and testimony are focused on responding to their essential needs, improving their living conditions and promoting respect for their dignity and their fundamental rights.

In this region, we cover the full manadte of HI – emergency, Armed reduction violence and development - with strong focus on continuum and resilience. There are 5 main sectors of intervention: rehabilitation, education, early child development, BaNEREI (basic needs, economic recovery and economic inclusion) and armed violence reduction. Inclusion Humanitarian Action is both crosscutting within main sectors and sometimes a standalone intervention.

OBJECTIVE OF THE POSITION:

Under the management the Regional HR Manager, the Regional Senior HR Officer fosters a positive workplace culture, drives engagement and retention initiatives, follow up and resolve staff concerns. Mission 3: Operational HR Implementation

  • Ensures archiving processes meet compliance, quality standards and respect of legal context with a focus on continuous improvement.

3.2 Contributes to the quality of personnel administration for HI staff present in his/her geographical area

  • Follow up on the performance appraisal process for staff within the geographical area of intervention.
  • Implementation of sourcing process in his/her geographical area (e.g. interventions in training centres, trade fairs, professional social networks etc.)
  • Onboarding of new arrival and liaison with BDDI team for international staff.

Mission 4: Emergency preparedness and response

Mission 5: Ensure gap coverage and replacement during absence

  • The Regional HR Senior Officer covers the absence of the Regional HRM and the country HR Manager when needed.

Note that this job description must remain flexible; the list of tasks set out above is not exhaustive and is subject to changes resulting from the diversity of Humanity & Inclusion/Handicap International activities to respond to additional tasks or changes as identified by the line and functional managers.

THE SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE:

opportunities.title: Individual Consultant Education Sector Programming Data Analyst System Capacity Grant (SCG)
opportunities.publisher: UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
opportunities.description:
Terms of Reference

OVERVIEW OF THE FUNCTIONS OF THE POST

  1. BACKGROUND

Under the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) System Capacity Grant (SCG) for Myanmar, United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) Myanmar Antenna Office is implementing a multi-year programme to strengthen the resilience and effectiveness of Myanmar’s education sector through improved planning, coordination, financing, monitoring, and evidence generation.

The SCG is structured around the following outcomes:

  • Outcome 1: Improved quality and equity in Myanmar’s education through the effective use of an evidence-based framework that addresses key challenges, promotes gender and inclusivity, and adapts to emerging needs arising from ongoing socio-political instability.
  • Outcome 2: Enhanced sector coordination and improved resource allocation efficiency, leading to increased financial support for Myanmar’s education.
  • Outcome 3: Evidence-based decision-making in strategic policy and program development through the generation of data and evidence on educational outcomes and progress.

In alignment with Outcome 3, and due to the dual shocks of COVID-19 and political conflict, Myanmar has been heavily affected in terms of educational development with severe consequences on access, quality, and learning systems. In order to take stock of donor and implementing partner delivery, UNESCO requires analytical work on education programming, the availability of education data in Myanmar, and the current funding landscape in the Myanmar education sector.

  1. PURPOSE of the ASSIGNMENT

The objective of this assignment is to strengthen the existing education programme dataset and dashboard by collating updated programmatic data from partners, cleaning and organizing the data, and producing descriptive analysis. Based on the updated dataset, the assignment will generate analytical products, including graphs, data visualizations, thematic summaries, and mapping of education data and data gaps.

  1. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Supervisory arrangements:

The Individual Consultant shall perform the tasks under the overall authority of the Regional Director of the UNESCO Regional Office in Bangkok and Office for UN Coordination in Asia and the Pacific, and the direct supervision of the Head of the UNESCO Antenna Office in Yangon, working closely with the UNESCO Education Team. The Individual consultant’s responsibilities include the following:

  1. Meet with the UNESCO education team to understand the approach and scope of the work, agree on the methodology and objectives of the analytical tasks, how to interpret the data, map out relevant additional data sources, and report on data gaps.
    1. Draft the methodologies for analysis and develop a practical workplan for delivery based on the activities and deliverable milestones.
    2. Design data gathering templates for updating datasets with new breakdowns and verifying data for consistency.
    3. Produce graphs and data visualizations (inter alia, budget flow charts, spatial visualizations, thematic graph visualizations, infographics, etc.) under UNESCO guidance.
    4. Produce a mapping of additional data sources (program data) and collate data gaps required for further analytical products on education sector monitoring.
    5. Conduct descriptive analysis on Myanmar education sector programming and funding, with assistance and guidance from UNESCO.
    6. Finalize analytical products into a single report with a focus on education sector programming and the funding landscape.

In line with UNESCO's overall gender mainstreaming strategy, the Individual Consultant is expected to integrate a gender perspective in all activities and apply gender analysis and mainstreaming concepts whenever feasible.

TRAVEL:

The Individual Specialist will be based in Yangon (Homebase) during the contract period. No travel outside Yangon is anticipated.

  1. TIMETABLE AND DELIVERABLES

Deliverables

The individual specialist will submit the following deliverables within the designated timeline. All deliverables must be submitted with original, editable files, as well as high-resolution versions of final products (if applicable) to UNESCO. The assigned tasks must be submitted by the following deadlines.

Deliverables

Deadline

Deliverable 1: Submit an Inception Report, including suggested methodological approaches, analytical products proposed, potential data gaps, and a detailed workplan by 31 July 2026.

Deliverable 2: Submit first drafts of agreed analytical products, such as graphs, spatial/thematic data visualizations, and thematic analyses of program data by 15 August 2026.

Deliverable 3: Submit finalized analytical products (in agreed layout), the final single report, the policy brief, editable data templates, and the related user guide by 31 August 2026.

COMPETENCIES (Core / Managerial)

Accountability (C)

Innovation (C)

Knowledge sharing and continuous improvement (C)

Planning and organizing (C)

Teamwork (C)

Results focus (C)

For detailed information, please consult the UNESCO Competency Framework

  1. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Education

  • Advanced university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in economics, social sciences, development, statistics, educational sciences, or other related discipline.

Work Experience

  • Minimum 5 years of relevant professional experience in managing quantitative data sets and the use of different data sources.
  • Demonstrated competency with developing and producing quantitative analysis for policy-level requirements, preferably in a development and/or education context.

Skills/Competencies

  • Mastery of Power BI and MS Excel /or similar advanced data visualization/business intelligence tools is required to complete the tasks.
  • High-level technical expertise and capacity to analyze and visualize quantitative data and manage quantitative data sets.
  • Ability to provide visualizations which are comprehensible, attractive, and demonstrate analytical insights from data.
  • Ability to evaluate the reliability of data sources for analytical use and monitoring purposes.
  • Ability to write analytical policy text based on data analysis findings and produce high-quality content on tight deadlines.
  • Excellent planning, organizational, and communication skills.

Languages

  • Excellent knowledge of spoken and written English and Myanmar.

DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS

Work Experience

  • Experience collaborating with service providers, consultants, or multidisciplinary teams.
  • Familiarity with the Myanmar education and/or development context.
  • Prior experience working with an INGO and/or UN organization is preferred

Location: Damascus

Job description

GIZ has been operating in Syria since 1976. It has thus established valuable contacts in civil society and garnered experience that is now crucial for supporting the country. From 2013 onwards, it worked without government involvement with the assistance of local non-governmental organisations. Despite the difficult conditions, GIZ has consistently contributed to improving people’s living conditions.

In view of the developments since December 2024, which have led Syria into a decisive phase of transformation, GIZ plans to reopen its Country Office in Damascus in 2026. It is currently implementing projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Federal Foreign Office (FFO), with co-financing from the European Union and other donors. From 2026, the portfolio is planned to be expanded by several new projects.

The “Syria TVET and Employment Promotion Project” (STEP) aims to strengthen the employment prospects of Syrians in close cooperation with the private sector. This includes policy advice on the realignment of vocational training and employment strategies at national level, technical and organizational advice for vocational schools and training centers and cooperating companies. Furthermore, the STEP project focuses on the development of inclusive and efficient labor market services based on partnerships with local and foreign companies for rapid labour market integration.

Your tasks

  • Designing and overlooking conflict-sensitive, inclusive and gender-sensitive employment promotion measures with the local private sector
  • Setting up concrete co-implemented projects with local Syrian companies across all geographies of Syria
  • Overseeing development partnerships with the local private sector, incl. providing information and advice to companies, coordinating a call for proposal and overseeing the co-implementation of employment-oriented partnerships with GIZ
  • Liaising with chambers of industry, associations and individual companies in different governorates
  • Liaising with private sector networks and initiatives in Syria

  • Coordinating with other development or humanitarian actors providing short-term qualification measures

  • Where appropriate and reasonable, performing additional tasks upon request of the management

opportunities.title: Junior Modernisation Officer – Data and Reporting
opportunities.publisher: International Centre for Migration Policy Development
opportunities.description:
Functional Overview

The Junior Modernisation Officer (Data and Reporting) supports the implementation and maintenance of structured data processes across projects within ICMPD’s Mediterranean region, contributing to reliable and consistent data inputs for reporting, dashboards, and knowledge products.

Working under the supervision of the Modernisation Officer, and in coordination with project teams and relevant stakeholders, the role assists in the collection, structuring, and updating of project data in line with predefined standards, tools, and reporting requirements.

The position supports the application of shared data workflows, including the use of databases, reporting templates, and ETL processes, ensuring that data is processed, documented, and maintained consistently. The role also assists in coordinating with project focal points to validate data inputs and ensure their usability for project outputs.

Key Results

Support to Data Structuring and Management: Structured datasets are maintained and updated in line with predefined schemas, data dictionaries, and validation rules, contributing to consistency and traceability across projects. Support is provided to the organisation and documentation of data structures used across projects, ensuring that data is clearly defined, accessible, and aligned with reporting and operational requirements.

Support to Data Processing and ETL Workflows: ETL processes (extract, transform, load, refresh) are executed in line with defined workflows and procedures, ensuring that data is processed accurately and consistently. Issues related to data processing are identified and flagged for follow-up, contributing to the reliability and repeatability of data workflows. Support to Data Validation and Coordination: Coordination with project focal points is supported to collect, validate, and update data inputs in line with agreed definitions and reporting requirements. Data inconsistencies and gaps are identified and communicated to relevant stakeholders, supporting timely resolution and improved data quality.

Support to Reporting and Data Use: Shared databases, reporting templates, and data pipelines are applied to support dashboards and knowledge products. Data is structured and prepared to facilitate its use in reporting, automation, and integration into digital tools, in line with project and donor requirements.

Required Expertise

▪ Analytical thinking with the ability to understand data requirements and support structured data processing and reporting.

▪ Working knowledge of data tools and systems (e.g. spreadsheets, databases, reporting templates), with the ability to apply them in operational contexts.

▪ Basic understanding of data processing workflows, including ETL processes and data validation principles.

▪ Ability to follow predefined data standards, templates, and procedures to ensure consistency and accuracy.

▪ Attention to detail, including the ability to identify inconsistencies and data quality issues.

▪ Ability to coordinate with multiple stakeholders and follow up on data inputs in a timely manner.

▪ Ability to communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

▪ Ability to work in an international and multi-stakeholder environment, maintaining effective working relationships.

Qualifications, Experience and Language Skills

▪ Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field. A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent) with two additional years of relevant work experience may be accepted in lieu of the Master’s degree.

▪ Minimum of 1 year of relevant professional experience in data, reporting, or project support functions, preferably in an international context.

▪ Good drafting, coordination and organisational skills.

▪ Proficiency in (verbal/written) English, proficiency in French and Arabic required. ▪ Proficiency in the use of standard IT tools.

Job Title: Liaison Officer

Job location: Khartoum / Port Sudan / as applicable

Reports to: Country Director (with dotted line to Operations)

JOB SUMMARY

The Liaison Officer will facilitate MedGlobal Sudan’s operational access and compliance by managing relationships with government authorities, supporting visa and permit processes, and ensuring smooth coordination for staff movement and official documentation.

MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Government Liaison and Representation

• Serve as primary focal point with government authorities, including the Humanitarian Aid Commission (HAC)

• Maintain regular communication with relevant ministries and local authorities

• Support registration, permits, and compliance requirements for MedGlobal operations

• Represent MedGlobal in administrative and coordination meetings as required

2. Visas, Residency, and Documentation

• Manage visa applications, renewals, and residency permits for international staff

• Ensure timely processing and follow-up with relevant authorities

• Maintain an updated database of all staff documentation (visas, permits, IDs)

• Advise teams on entry requirements and regulatory procedures

3. Access and Movement Facilitation

• Coordinate travel permits and movement clearances for staff and visitors

• Support access negotiations where required in coordination with security and programme teams

• Ensure all movements are compliant with national regulations.

4. Airport Reception and Facilitation

• Coordinate airport pick-up, reception, and departure procedures for international staff and visitors

• Facilitate customs clearance for personnel and, where required, small consignments.

• Act as focal point for resolving entry/exit issues at airports.

5. Coordination and Internal Support

• Work closely with operations, HR, and security teams to ensure alignment on access and compliance matters

• Provide regular updates on regulatory changes affecting operations

• Support documentation and communication required for partnerships and agreements

Temporary Responsibilities (Liaison Support)

• Support visa processing and residency permit applications in coordination with relevant authorities

• Maintain communication with the Humanitarian Aid Commission (HAC) on administrative and access-related matters

• Facilitate travel clearances, permits, and official documentation as required

• Coordinate airport reception and facilitation for international staff, including arrivals and departures

• Liaise with relevant government entities to support operational access and compliance

QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS

Should have the following skills, education, and experience:

• Bachelor’s degree in public administration, law, political science, or related field

• Minimum 3–5 years of experience in liaison, government relations, or administration (INGO experience preferred)

• Strong understanding of Sudan administrative systems and regulatory environment

• Proven ability to manage government relationships and navigate bureaucracy

• Strong communication and negotiation skills

• High level of discretion and professionalism

• Ability to work under pressure and resolve issues quickly

• Excellent organizational and documentation skills

• Fluency in Arabic and English required

Key Working Relationships

• Internal: Country Director, Operations, HR, Security, Programme teams

• External: Government authorities, including Humanitarian Aid Commission (HAC), immigration offices, airport authorities, and partner organizations

Important Note

This role is critical to ensuring operational continuity in a complex and evolving context. The Liaison Officer must maintain strict neutrality, uphold MedGlobal’s policies, and ensure all engagements with authorities are transparent and compliant

ABOUT MEDGLOBAL

MedGlobal is a global humanitarian non-profit organization providing medical and health education services to people in need, including refugees and displaced persons, in disaster and underserved regions. The organization is composed of medical and public health professionals of diverse backgrounds.

CODE OF CONDUCT

MedGlobal Code of Conduct reflects the profession’s core set of beliefs and values of care, respect, trust, and integrity. These beliefs and values are fundamental to MedGlobal employees, volunteers, interns, consultants, and contractors to guide their practice and conduct. The Code is organized into categories, as follows:

• Always act with fairness, honesty, integrity, and openness; respect the opinions of others and treat all with equality and dignity without regard to gender, race, color, creed, ancestry, place of origin, political beliefs, religion, marital status, disability, age, or sexual orientation.

• Provide a positive and valued experience for those receiving service within and outside MedGlobal.

CHILD PROTECTION POLICY

Child abuse in all forms is unacceptable to MedGlobal, which recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. MedGlobal is committed to ensuring a child-safe environment and is applying a zero-tolerance approach towards any kind of child abuse and exploitation.

DISCRIMINATION, ABUSE AND HARASSMENT POLICY

MedGlobal provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and expressly prohibits and will not tolerate any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (sexual or otherwise), based upon race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, gender, age, marital status, citizenship status, disability, or military status. MedGlobal employees and related personnel must under no circumstances take part in any form of discrimination, harassment, or abuse (physical, sexual or verbal), intimidation or exploitation, or in any other way infringe the rights of others inside or outside the organization.

opportunities.title: Power BI & Power Platform Developer (MEL Data Officer)
opportunities.description:
The MEL Data Science Officer is part of the Global MEL team, strengthening Orbis’s MEL systems through data engineering, analytics, automation, and governance. The Officer supports data integration across systems and countries to enable timely insights.

Orbis is an international nonprofit delivering sight-saving programs in over 200 countries and territories worldwide so that individuals, families, and communities can thrive.

The MEL Data Science Officer supports Orbis’s global MEL function by designing and maintaining data pipelines, automated reporting systems, and analytical solutions that enhance MEL data quality, accessibility, and interoperability. This role builds standardized data models, maintains Dataverse structures, implements ETL processes, and develops Power BI dashboards that support monitoring, reporting and performance analysis across Orbis’s global programs.

The Officer collaborates with MEL teams, program teams and the IS/IT unit to ensure that MEL data systems are reliable, efficient, and aligned with global reporting requirements. This role does not supervise staff but provides high-level technical support, training and troubleshooting to MEL stakeholders globally.

opportunities.title: Crisis Management Advisor
opportunities.description:
Description

The Pacific Community (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The role – the Crisis Management Advisor will strengthen SPC’s organisational preparedness, response capability and learning in relation to crises and disruptive events and is prepared for a variety of crisis situations. These can include disasters, pandemics, and civil or political unrest. The role leads the development and implementation of SPC’s crisis management and coordinates preparedness and response activities across SPC offices including contributing to organisational business continuity efforts and transformation programmes.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

Lead the design and implementation of SPC Crisis Management framework and operations to ensure organisational resilience during disruptions

  • Coordinate the development, maintenance, testing, and continuous improvement of SPC’s organisation‑wide crisis management framework, ensuring alignment with the Risk Management Framework, security arrangements, and business continuity planning
  • Establish and maintain clear crisis escalation pathways, roles, decision authorities, and communication protocols consistent with SPC’s risk governance arrangements
  • Coordinate and support Crisis Management Teams (CMTs) through preparedness tools, rosters, playbooks, and guidance, acting as an advisor and coordinator rather than the executive lead during crises
  • Provide strategic and technical advice on security and crisis events with appropriate mitigation measures and response planning through live monitoring and reporting

Support the organisational efforts towards BCP’s and implementation in relation to crisis management

  • Support the organisational functions to develop, update, and test Business Continuity Plan/s (BCPs), ensuring a consistent and risk‑informed approach across SPC
  • Support the coordination of business continuity readiness activities and exercises, tracking maturity, coverage, and follow‑up actions across the organisation
  • Ensure business continuity arrangements are informed by organisational and divisional risk assessments, without assuming executive ownership of BCPs

Crisis Management framework and operational delivery in alignment and reported against organisational wide risk governance, integration and reporting requirements and protocols

  • Contribute crisis‑related risk insights, emerging issues, and incident learnings to SPC’s organisational risk processes, including inputs to the organisations Risk Register where relevant
  • Provide crisis management and preparedness updates to risk governance forums (e.g. SROC - Strategic Risk Oversight Committee, CRGA) as required, supporting effective oversight and decision‑making
  • Ensure crisis management practices align with agreed risk appetite, escalation thresholds, and reporting expectations
  • Support to ongoing relationships with embassies, consulates, government agencies, and NGOs and partners for coordinated crisis response where appropriate

Provide for Learning and Continuous Improvement

  • Coordinate after action reviews following crises or significant disruptions, ensuring lessons learned are documented, tracked, and actioned
  • Embed learning into crisis management, business continuity, and risk management practices, and support organisational learning across divisions

Strengthened Capability Building, Advisory Support

  • Design and coordinate crisis management and business continuity training, simulations, and exercises in collaboration with HR, security, and risk functions
  • Advise managers, directors, and risk champions on crisis preparedness and risk-based decision making in high uncertainty contexts
  • Promote a consistent organisational narrative on crisis readiness, proportionality, and stewardship, aligned with SPC values
  • Provide crisis management leadership and operational coherence

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please refer to the online job description.

Key selection criteria

Qualifications

  • Postgraduate degree in Emergency Management, Security/Risk Management, or a related field, or equivalent body of knowledge and experience

Technical expertise

  • At least 10 years of professional demonstrated experience, including 5 years at a senior advisory or coordination level in emergency management, or organisational resilience
  • Demonstrated experience in crisis management, security, business continuity, and/or enterprise risk management in complex or multi country organisations
  • Strong understanding of governance, escalation, and accountability in high risk or crisis environments
  • Experience supporting (rather than owning) executive level decision making during incidents or crises
  • Proven experience conducting risk assessments, business impact analyses, scenario planning or organisational readiness reviews
  • Proven track record in multi-stakeholder engagement, including government agencies, international organisations, and NGOs

Language skills

  • Fluency in English and French

Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness

  • Knowledge of Pacific Island countries and territories is an advantage

Salary, terms and conditions

Contract Duration – This vacant position is budgeted for 3 years and is subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

Remuneration – The Crisis Management Advisor is a band 11 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale.

For a Noumea based position – a starting salary range of SDR (special drawing rights) 4,397-5,400 per month, which converts to approximately XPF 634,433-779,190 (USD 5,892-7,236; EUR 5,317-6,530). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia.

For a Suva based position – a starting salary range of 3,245‒4,057 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 10,028–12,535 (USD 4,349–5,436; EUR 3,924–4,905). Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea or Suva – SPC provides a housing allowance (or subsidised housing in Noumea). Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

Languages – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

Recruitment principles – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an equal-opportunity employer, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will begiven to the Pacific Islander. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

GOAL's areas of operations include but not limited to Aleppo, Idleb and Lattakia Governorates, and is expanding to new governorates in Syria. opportunities.title: Advocacy Officer (fixed term - 8 months)
opportunities.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
opportunities.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

The Global Advocacy & Influence Department is a dynamic team that uses the power of IRC’s ideas to solve the biggest challenges facing IRC’s clients. From the drivers of conflict to the needs displaced people, the team partners with politicians, policy makers and civil society to bring these solutions to life. We take pride in being solutions-oriented and creative. We are precise in our tactics, and messages. We lead change year over year, knowing that system change takes dedicated focus while maintaining the flexibility to respond to emerging needs. Finally, we are collaborative, working not only with programs, strategy, research and innovation, and communications teams across the IRC, but also externally, constantly seeking to new ideas and perspectives from others in the humanitarian sector and beyond.

The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

IRC UK
IRC UK is part of the IRC global network, which has its global headquarters in New York. Our team in the UK works to raise profile, deliver policy and practice change, and increase funding to help restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Since 2021, IRC UK has also provided integration services directly to refugees in England.

In Europe, the IRC also has offices in Berlin, Bonn, Brussels, Geneva and Stockholm.

Job Overview

As the Advocacy Officer, you are responsible for building the profile, influence and credibility of IRC’s work with UK politicians, political parties and opinion formers on our humanitarian and development issues. You will be delivering our influence strategies and identifying strategic lobbying opportunities and enabling colleagues to exploit them fully through the use of innovative and creative tactics that help IRC stand out in a crowded arena. You will support building critical strategic relationships to help deliver on IRC’s objectives in parliament. You will contribute fresh insights and analysis to inform IRC’s influence approaches, tactics, and messages.

Major Responsibilities:

  • Advocacy Strategy: Support in delivering advocacy strategies, collaborating with the Advocacy Manager, policy leads, public advocacy and communications colleagues, to advance IRC’s key advocacy objectives.
  • Political and policy monitoring: Analyse and report on relevant political and policy trends and regularly communicate across external relations teams. Expand IRC’s political reach by tracking and analysing shifting government positions, individuals engaging on our issues, and the politics around our issues. Track political processes and profile opportunities / events; including bills, select committee inquiries, and other parliamentary and political developments.
  • Stakeholder management: Building and maintaining relationships with a core group of political champions in and around Westminster, whilst raising IRC’s profile and awareness of our positions on key issues among a wider political audience in order to increase our ability to deliver policy change.
  • Political engagement: Developing and providing regular written or oral briefings to MPs, Peers, government officials, and other decision makers on key policies and campaigns. Producing specific asks to parliamentarians on a regular basis – parliamentary questions, debate contributions etc.
  • Communications: Provide market and audience expertise to communications team to craft public advocacy in the UK. Support team in developing communications strategy and develop materials for advocacy targets, including digital/social content and take actions.
  • Teamwork: Support a positive team culture by acting openly and collaboratively, supporting colleagues in their work and sharing credit with others where appropriate.
  • Steward Gender Equality, Diversity and Inclusion: both in the culture of IRC, as well as in the policy solutions we develop and the ways we wield influence.

Key Working Relationships:

Position reports to: Advocacy Manager

Internal contacts: Policy and Advocacy colleagues, Communications, Technical Excellence leads; International Programs leads, External Relations Department

External contacts: Parliamentarians, government officials, key opinion formers, think tanks and sector colleagues in the UK.

Job Requirements:

Work experience:

  • Experience in delivering advocacy strategies in the UK. 2 years + of experience working on development and humanitarian issues.

Demonstrated skills and competencies:

  • Proven success in delivering successful strategies that influence/impact on legislative and executive policy.
  • Good understanding of relevant the UK’s political structures and processes, and familiar with leverage points within these institutions that can be targeted to achieve policy change objectives.
  • Ability to innovatively and creatively apply influencing techniques and tactics to consistently make IRC stand out from the crowd in Westminster, Whitehall and with other key international stakeholders.
  • Knowledge of development and humanitarian issues in the UK.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate and collaborate successfully with parliamentarians and colleagues in the humanitarian and development fields.
  • Strong writing skills and the ability to translate sophisticated material and data into coherent narratives that resonate with policymakers.
  • Experience of developing effective working relationships with colleagues, and working collaboratively in multi-disciplinary project teams.
  • Ability to work quickly against deadlines.
  • Initiative and ability to work independently on fast-paced issues, and balance competing demands.

opportunities.title: MHPSS Officer
opportunities.description:
Danish Red Cross (DRC) is looking for an experienced Mental Health and Psychosocial support (MHPSS) professional to be seconded to the IFRC headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.

MHPSS Officer

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest volunteer-based humanitarian network. The IFRC is served by a Secretariat based in Geneva, with regional and country offices throughout the world.

Along with Red Cross Red Crescent (RCRC) National Societies and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the IFRC is part of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. The overall aim of the IFRC is to inspire, encourage, facilitate, and promote humanitarian activities by National Societies to prevent and alleviate human suffering and thereby contributing to the maintenance and promotion of human dignity and peace in the world.

The IFRC is committed to scaling up and addressing the Mental Health and Psychosocial support needs at all times including due to the consequences of armed conflicts, natural disasters and other emergencies. The MHPSS Officer will work in close collaboration with the IFRC Health and Care Department and the Movement MHPSS hub, supporting the Lead, Health Security and Community Resilience (IFRC Secretariat MHPSS Focal Point), primarily to ensure that the overall strategic direction and operationalisation of MHPSS initiatives are achieved and well-coordinated internally with RCRC National Societies, relevant IFRC departments and teams, ICRC and externally with WHO and other key actors.

The MHPSS officer reports to the Global Lead, Health Security and Resilience Team in the IFRC Health and Care Department.

Key responsibilities include

  • Strengthen global and regional IFRC emergency response systems, including National Societies and IFRC preparedness initiatives, in close collaboration with the Movement MHPSS hub and IFRC Regional Offices.
  • Manage the global IFRC MHPSS roster, including calls for applications if needed.
  • Facilitate the integration of MHPSS into emergency responses by providing guidance documents and conducting webinars for IFRC cluster/country delegations.
  • Map and regularly update the status of MHPSS work across National Societies (NS) and IFRC offices.
  • In close collaboration with NS, identify priorities, achievements, challenges, needs, and opportunities to strengthen their programmes and services.
  • Collaborate with IFRC regional colleagues and the MHPSS Hub to harmonise MHPSS guidance and approaches, ensuring consistency across regions and facilitate capacity strengthening of NS staff and volunteers to develop, implement, and scale MHPSS programs effectively at the community levels.
  • Provide technical support to IFRC Regional MHPSS colleagues and National Societies’ programmes and services to support piloting, implementation, and scaling up MHPSS interventions.
  • Contribute to identifying and engaging with potential donors and partners for resource mobilization and preparing project proposals and documents for IFRC and NS.
  • Participate and contribute to emergency Task Force meetings in Geneva for MHPSS related components in different emergencies.
  • Strengthen close professional partnerships with, and position IFRC among, key stakeholders in MHPSS at global and international levels.
  • Liaise with the IFRC representatives to the UN providing information on MHPSS to ensure MHPSS is on the global agenda and promote the Movement as a key player within MHPSS and other internal and external bodies/partners promoting the Movement MHPSS.

Experience and qualifications

  • Relevant academic degree in psychology or psychiatry or Master’s degree in public health or other relevant disciplines.
  • A minimum of 7 years of relevant experience in implementing MHPSS programmes in a humanitarian organisation.
  • Strong experience of working in a large humanitarian organisation with multi-actor coordination experience.
  • Strong knowledge of RCRC Movement MHPSS capacities, policies, tools, and practices.
  • A minimum of 5 years mission/field-based experience in disaster/post-disaster environments, preferably from multiple regions; previous IFRC deployments desirable.
  • Excellent communication, coordination as well as networking and facilitation skills.
  • Proven experience of building the capacity of local partners, including training skills.
  • Extensive knowledge of public mental health and Psychosocial approaches and Integrated MHPSS interventions models in promotion/prevention and treatments at primary and secondary health care level.
  • Emergency roster development and management experience preferred.
  • Fluency in English, and good command of another IFRC official language (Arabic, French, Spanish)

Employment Conditions

The position is based in Geneva, Switzerland and is initially for 12 months with the possibility of extension. The starting date is 1 August 2026 or as soon thereafter as possible. There is a 3-month probationary period.

The salary including all allowances and pension payment will be between DKK 52,000 and DKK 55,000 per month depending on qualifications and experience.

Travelling is expected for up to 3 months per year upon request of line manager.

The Danish Red Cross is an equal opportunity employer.

Further information

If you have specific questions about the position, please contact zesd@rodekors.dk subject “MHPSS Officer 2026”.

opportunities.description:

Organisation: humedica e.V.

Duty Station / Location: Lebanon, with regional scope including Syria.

The Consultant will be remote based, with regular presence in Lebanon, particularly at humedica’s country office in Zahle, Bekaa Valley, and periodic visits to Syria or relevant regional hubs (e.g. Amman)

Duration & Time Allocation

  • Fixed-term consultancy with an explicitly advisory and exploratory mandate
  • Duration: 3 months with a potential extension
  • Expected availability: 8–10 working days per month, with flexibility depending on agreed deliverables and project phases
  • The assignment is not designed as a permanent role, but as a time-bound engagement supporting strategic decision-making during a transition phase

About humedica / Background of the assignment

humedica e.V. is an international aid organisation based in Kaufbeuren, Germany. Since 1979, the organization has been providing rapid emergency and disaster relief, working in development cooperation and carrying out charitable projects.

The organisation has been active in Lebanon since 2012 and maintains an established country office in Zahle, Bekaa Valley. The office has implemented a range of humanitarian and medical projects and constitutes a key organizational asset with strong contextual knowledge, operational experience and local networks.

In light of changing global humanitarian dynamics, increasing funding constraints and humedica’s ongoing organization-wide strategic process, humedica is reassessing the strategic relevance, added value and future role of its engagement in Lebanon and Syria.

Purpose of the Assignment

The purpose of the consultancy is to provide independent, senior-level advisory support to humedica HQ by:

  • Supporting strategic reflection on humedica’s future footprint and focus in Lebanon and Syria
  • Assessing humedica’s comparative advantage in the regional humanitarian landscape
  • Providing evidence-based input for leadership-level decision-making regarding consolidation, focus or potential reorientation

Key Responsibilities

Strategic & Contextual Analysis

  • Contribute to strategic reflection on the medium- to long-term role of Lebanon as a country office and/or regional hub.
  • Analyse political, conflict and humanitarian dynamics relevant to the region
  • Identify opportunities for regional, cross-border or synergistic approaches between Lebanon and Syria where appropriate.

Regional Mapping & Stakeholder Analysis

  • Conduct a structured mapping of key stakeholders, including national and international NGOs, UN agencies, coordination platforms, donors and consortia.
  • Identify coordination fora and partnerships of strategic relevance for humedica.
  • Analyse alignment between humedica’s capacities and potential collaboration opportunities.

Donor Landscape & Strategic Positioning

  • Identify donor-relevant opportunities aligned with humedica’s strategic priorities.
  • Provide advisory input on strategic positioning, visibility and engagement with donors and partners.

Representation & Liaison (Advisory Capacity)

  • Serve as humedica’s liaison consultant in selected regional or country-level coordination fora

Country Office Engagement & Transition Support

  • Maintain regular presence at humedica’s country office in Zahle to gain in-depth understanding of operations and organisational dynamics.
  • Provide structured, independent feedback to headquarters during a phase of organisational consolidation and transition.
  • Ensure close coordination with and respect for existing country office capacities and institutional knowledge.

Portfolio & Continuity Analysis

  • Analyse current and past humedica projects in Lebanon and Syria.
  • Assess potential for strategic continuity, consolidation, scaling or replication.
  • Identify gaps, limitations and possible areas for thematic or strategic reorientation.
  • Provide evidence-based recommendations on future programmatic directions.

Expected Deliverables

  • Needs-based programmatic options analysis
  • Project build-on and continuity assessment
  • Stakeholder, coordination and funding landscape overview
  • Lebanon–Syria strategic coherence brief
  • Two concise concept notes for potential pilot projects

Required Profile

  • Advanced academic degree in a relevant field (e.g. international relations, humanitarian studies, development).
  • Minimum 10 years of senior-level experience in humanitarian and/or development cooperation.
  • Proven expertise in regional strategy, governance, donor relations and consortium work.
  • Strong understanding of the humanitarian architecture in the MENA region.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in non-executive advisory roles.

Languages

  • Arabic: Excellent (required)
  • English: Professional working proficiency
